en.regest: Jehan Moucher apologises to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the delayed delivery of the imperial letters, which only now arrive due to the illness of the messenger. He explains that the Emperor asks the citizens of St. Gallen to continue their good neighbourhood with the Count of Burgund in accordance with the inheritance contract. The last two instalments of the contract were paid in Zürich.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to their envoys in Baden that they had provided the new letters of union of the cantons with their seal. They had decided, after consultation with the envoys of the King and other cantons, to join the union, even though the 400 francs had not been promised. They ask the envoys to continue negotiating with the royal plenipotentiaries.
en.sender: Burgomaster, Small and Great Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Johann von Watt, Heinrich Locher, Lienhart Keller und Ambrosius Einbörn

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Josef Büttler in an inheritance matter with the widow of his deceased cousin Gregor Kobler. They request the determination of a Diet date, so that Büttler may take possession of his inheritance according to the statutes of St. Gallen and old custom.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Guldi, a glazier from St. Gallen, who is staying in Basel as a journeyman, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to kindly accept his first work, a glass painting with the coat of arms of the city. He asks for leniency for any possible errors, as he is still in training, and promises to make even more effort in the future.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: King Eduard VI. of England thanks the Council of St. Gallen for its friendship and goodwill, which had been reported to him by his confidant Christoph Mont. He reaffirms his friendship, justifies it by the common Christian religion, and asks that his envoy be given credit.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank King Karl I. of England for his goodwill towards the city and the reformed religion. They assure him that in future councils they will uphold the pure doctrine and protect the King's religion. Furthermore, they declare that they know of no plans for an invasion of the kingdom and that they will consult with the Confederates on such proposals.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Karl I. of England

en.regest: Bishop Christoph zu Konstanz asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to earnestly urge the former bailiff of Arbon, Jacob Eisenhut Krum, to settle the outstanding balances that accrued during his administration. Krum has so far evaded the matter with excuses. Should he not appear for a settlement, the Bishop will present the bond and initiate the necessary steps.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Emperor Karl V. for written confirmation to his envoy Wilhelm von Raurach that the city continues to receive the annual honorarium of 400 francs. They refer to the promises of King Franz I. and the practice to date. Should the Emperor not keep his promises, they are not obliged to observe the articles of union.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Emperor Karl V.

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich confirm the receipt of two letters from the Council of St. Gallen, one concerning a transaction between two related persons and one concerning the description of the future Imperial Diet at Augsburg. As they can hold no complete consultation either today or tomorrow, they ask for patience and promise to discuss the important matters soon and to give an answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to extend the date set for 20 July in the inheritance case of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Hans Wilden until 3 August. The bailiff of Kyburg, Hieronymus Thumysen, necessary for the matter, is prevented. Zürich offers to name another date if 3 August does not suit.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Arbogast von Hohen, Council and Captain as well as Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz, reply to a letter of 1. August. They declare themselves willing to remit 50 gulden from a claim of 700 gulden against Herr Othlion, in order to preserve good neighborly relations. They ask St. Gallen to be satisfied with this remission, as they could otherwise have demanded more.
en.sender: Arbogast von Hohen, Council and Captain as well as Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Montprat von Spiegelberg, Statthalter of the Hauptmannschaft, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz, ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information regarding the stay of the weaver's journeyman Jacob Berle in St. Gallen. Berle came to St. Gallen around Michaelmas and remained there until four weeks before Fastnacht. Konstanz asks for confirmation of this stay and whether Berle has set foot there.
en.sender: Hans Montprat von Spiegelberg, Statthalter of the Hauptmannschaft, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the French envoy Morlet had stated in Basel that the royal treasurer would wait in Lyon for the envoys of the Confederates to settle the peace money. Zürich had sent its town clerk to Lyon for 14 March. Furthermore, the Zürichers invite to a general Diet of the Confederates on the same day in Baden im Aargau.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Luzern respond to an inquiry regarding Margaretha Gmünderin. They report that the deceased priest Johannes Hirt bequeathed his estate, which came from alms, by will to the hospital and the poor in Luzern. If the heirs make claims, they would examine them before the court.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Luzern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their Confederate Othmar Kuntz to appear before the Council of Zürich on 30 April. It concerns a dispute with citizens of Zürich over the sale of a half meggis, in which Kuntz allegedly acted dishonestly. Zürich will handle the matter regardless of Kuntz's presence.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The imperial officials of Bregenz ask the Council of St. Gallen to instruct the bailiff Jacob Sauter and other friends of the widow Katharina Schuelmeisterin to hand over her inheritance to the monastery of Hirschtal. The monastery had supported the orphan for twelve years and has now admitted her into the order. The officials refer to the inheritance agreement between Österreich and the Confederation and ask for a written answer.
en.sender: Ludwig von Reischach zum Meggberg, imperial bailiff, and Wolfgang Raming, imperial Amtmann of the lordship of Bregenz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Council of the city of Bern responds to a complaint by the Abbot of St. Gallen regarding his poor, who are accommodated in Bernese hospitals. Bern justifies the care with the Christian commandment of mercy and the increasing number of those in need. The Council asks St. Gallen not to raise complaints, but to show compassion, as God will repay this a hundredfold.
en.sender: Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they had opened the summons of Emperor Karl to the Council, which was addressed to the Confederates, on a day in Baden. The Pope had also summoned the Confederates to the Council. However, nothing had been decided yet, but the matter had been adjourned until the next day.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Bishop Christoph of Konstanz informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that in a case pending before his ecclesiastical court, the taking of evidence in St. Gallen must be carried out by a commissioner appointed by the Consistory. He points out that this is to be done according to old custom and law, and asks the city to permit this.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to provide legal assistance to the empowered brothers and brothers-in-law of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Heinrich Graf, namely Jacob Graf and Heinrich Truber, in a matter of inheritance. They request prompt adjudication and promise reciprocity.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that merchants of St. Gallen fear that their goods on the way via Lindau to Nürnberg might be confiscated by the Landvogt in Schwaben. Lindau rejects these fears as unfounded and asks St. Gallen to reassure its citizens and assure them of the safe use of the road.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The bailiff and Council of Elgg ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to treat their citizen Hans Vogler and his wife, who have an inheritance in St. Gallen, amicably. They point out that the lords of Zürich take only the tenth penny as a deduction from their subjects who draw inheritances from their territory and demand nothing further.
en.sender: The bailiff and Council of Elgg
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Bern report that the masters and Stubengossen of the weavers' guild in Bern have confirmed that the deceased Christian Rütty left behind three legitimate children. These have authorized the citizen of St. Gallen Heinrich Schütz to collect the inheritance of the deceased Katharina Rütty. Bern asks St. Gallen to support Schütz in taking over the estate and to impose only minor costs on him in doing so.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Ratmann and Innigmeister of the Altstadt Magdeburg ask the Inner Council of the city of St. Gallen for a credit of several thousand gulden for a few years. They justify this with the high costs of the siege and the necessity to compensate the citizens. The Magister Johannes Thomas Zentner is sent as messenger, who had honourably left the city of St. Gallen. The city of Magdeburg promises repayment against a document under the city seal.
en.sender: Ratmann and Innigmeister of the Altstadt Magdeburg
en.recipient: Inner Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Several witnesses from Lindau and Roschach report on the armament of the escort men who have escorted a preacher through Roschach. They describe that the men carried guns, pikes, and other weapons, partly only in breeches and jerkins, and led the preacher right among them. Some demand that the authorities intervene against this violent course of action.
en.sender: Jacob Altther, Zist Bachman, Ulrich Bertschi, Thilin Visch, Caspar Broger, Hans Stör, Lienhart Wenig, Jacob Förster, Michel Xerer
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: King Heinrich II. von Frankreich answers the complaint of the Confederates regarding the levying of duties and subsidies on goods, in particular spices and saffron. He explains that, by a new edict, the old, separate levies have been combined into a single «imposition foraine» and even reduced. The previous lower taxation was due to the forbearance of the lessees. As a preliminary measure, he temporarily exempts the merchants of the Confederates from the payment of these levies. Furthermore, he refers to the difficult situation regarding the demand for the moneys of Margrave Albrecht von Brandenburg.
en.recipient: the Confederates

en.regest: Christoph Schorno, Landvogt in the County of Thurgau, complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that their preachers in the County of Thurgau, which lies under his administration, frequently wrote letters back and forth. He says that this causes scandal in the world and that adversity and great ill-will among the people could arise. He asks the St. Gallen authorities to arrange with their preachers that they refrain from such writing back and forth and soliciting, as otherwise trouble could grow from it.
en.sender: Christoph Schorno, Landvogt in the County of Thurgau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the response to the solicitation of the Magdeburgers. Since a common Diet of the Confederates before Easter is not foreseeable, Zürich has handled the matter itself. They will inform the Magdeburgers in writing that they cannot comply with their request and will set out the reasons. Zürich also communicates this decision to Basel and Schaffhausen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nördlingen thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the support in the war against the Elector. They ask for a confidential hearing of a messenger who is to present further matters.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Jakob von Landau, Leinz von Reischach and Hans Joachim von Laubenberg ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant them and their families protection and lodging in the city during the war turmoil. They promise to repay this in equal and greater measure, and ask for a prompt answer.
en.sender: Hans Jakob von Landau, Knight, Leinz von Reischach, Vogt of Bregenz, and Hans Joachim von Laubenberg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the report on the disturbances of some citizens of St. Gallen. They assure them that the citizens of St. Gallen do not intend anything harmful, and offer their help should this be necessary. They ask for immediate notification in the event of further occurrences.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Rathmann and Innungsmeister of the Altenstadt Magdeburg remind the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of their request for tax relief and aid after the siege. They ask that the envoy Johann Thomas Heussener be heard with goodwill and that he be given credit. Furthermore, they thank them for the fifty gulden granted, which they have handed over to the poor.
en.sender: Rathmann and Innungsmeister of the Altenstadt Magdeburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about the negotiations of their Burgomaster Hans Habben with the Burgundians regarding neutrality. Habben reports that the Königin of Frankreich wishes to ratify the neutrality with the Kaiser and König, but the duration lies with the König. Furthermore, Zürich communicates that the König does not wish to disturb the Glaubensverwandten in Frankreich, but considers them Aufrührer, whom he does not tolerate.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have received new news from Basel. They consider it not necessary to convene a common Confederate Diet as long as the situation does not worsen. They report that they have answered Basel accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen that they have forwarded the imperial letter of 23 September 1551 addressed to the Confederates. The Emperor complains therein about the rebellion of Margrave Albrecht von Brandenburg and his alliance with Frankreich. He calls upon the Confederates to punish mercenaries who march against the imperial hereditary lands and to maintain neutrality. Zürich asks St. Gallen to participate in the Confederate Diet taking place in Baden on 20 October.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Sebastian Uriel Appenzeller asks E. E. W. for permission to leave for a certain period without their cost and damage, in order to gather experience and practice. He promises not to commit himself elsewhere and to return immediately if needed. He encloses a list of his debts amounting to 34 florin.
en.recipient: E. E. W.

en.regest: Joachim Gaisberg, a scholarship holder of the city of St. Gallen, asks the Burgomaster for forgiveness for a misunderstood letter. He explains that he will comply with the order to study theology. Since he may not remain in Tübingen, he will return to Basel, where he can be of more use in theology and live more cheaply. He promises to settle the books and expenses every six months and to transmit the register of the books.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Caspar Stetner thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loaned Soma. He asks for patience in the repayment until St. John's Day, as he cannot safely remit the money because of the wars between Nürnberg and the Margrave of Baden. He promises to remit the sum with interest immediately upon improvement of the situation.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen reply to a complaint by merchants of St. Gallen regarding increased duties on linen and Mitbleut. They deny having introduced new levies and explain that the collection of eight pfennig per hundredweight is due to the negligence of former customs officials. The existing order provides for four pfennig in duty and four pfennig in ground rent. Überlingen asks that the complaint be dismissed and the payment made, and offers in return good conveyance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ysny request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to lend them two shuttles, one white and one red. These are necessary for the appraisal of their linen. The shuttles are to be delivered without color and without defect. Ysny promises to return them after use and to show gratitude in other matters.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jost and Mingn Tschudi report to the Landammann and Council of Glarus on the campaign of the Lord of Brisack. They describe the capture of the fortresses Cewaa and Courtemilla, the siege of St. Steffan, and a skirmish with Spanish horsemen. They ask for intercession and promise to convey new news.
en.sender: Jost and Mingn Tschudi of Glarus
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Glarus

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rottwil reply to an inquiry from the Council of St. Gallen regarding a grain purchase. They assure that the citizen of Rottwil Konrad Kromerle did not sell any grain to the town clerk Josef von Schönberg. Kromerle rather acquired 25 Malter and a quarter of grain from the heirs of the deceased bailiff Burkhard von Danneck in Bollingen through a broker. The grain was not rotten, but only somewhat dusty.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen report that the local furrier Joachim Ruedger was convicted of an offense and sentenced to a fine and taken into custody. After paying the fine, he went home without regard to the still outstanding compensation for the victim, with the intention of raising the money from relatives. Überlingen asks St. Gallen to compel Ruedger to fulfill the judgment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of new news from the French royal court. They report on the King's campaign in Picardy, the battle at Solesmes, and the defeat of the imperial troops. Furthermore, they inform them of the conquest of Corsica by the French fleet and the military movements of Margrave Albrecht von Brandenburg, as well as the diplomatic tensions between the Emperor and the Electors.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Joachim Beldi thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a letter and a Vererung. He explains that he has handed over the office of Ammann to Hans Luchs and that the farewell letters remain with the Council until a new Council is elected. This has led to delays, which is why Vogt Vogel could not come to St. Gallen in time. Beldi offers his help and wishes a happy new year.
en.recipient: Burgomaster of St. Gallen

en.regest: Joachim Gaißberg thanks the gentlemen of St. Gallen for the grant of linen to the Patron. He asks for approval of his annual expenses, which he lists in detail, including table money, books, rent, tailor and shoemaker work, as well as living costs. The sum amounts to 20 Kronen and 14 batzen.
en.recipient: Ambrosius Aigen, former Burgomaster; Nikolaus Schwanberg, Säckelmeister; Martin Huxen, Sturmeister of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Wil report to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about an incident: A man from Rapperswil, who lives in Schwyz, sold two half-ellens of linen cloth in Wil, which he allegedly bought from Jacob Zieg in St. Gallen. Since the cloth bore a St. Gallen mark, the men of Wil suspect fraud. They have temporarily detained the cloth and the man and ask St. Gallen for information on whether the man bought a mark in Rapperswil and how the incident came about.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Othmar Blum, court scribe of the St. Gallen city court, announces to Leonhart Becken von Beckenstein that Caspar Todtmund, Ammann of Rorschach, as the authorized representative of Wilhelm Merzen and his mother-in-law Wolfflin, intends to seize the houses and properties of the recipient located in St. Gallen at the market due to outstanding debts. The recipient is requested to appear before the court on 28 May, otherwise proceedings will be conducted according to law.
en.recipient: Leonhart Becken von Beckenstein

en.regest: Katharina Kraeusin, widow of the late Hans Wolff von Bibelspurg, asks the Statthalter, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg to write to the Council of St. Gallen. She fears that she will be disadvantaged by an informal and unauthorized auction of her properties located in St. Gallen by the Rosacher Ammann Kaspar Rathmundt, as the authorized representative of Wilhelm Götz. Her authorized representative Joachim Reitlinger did not accept the power of attorney. She asks for a report on the actions taken so far, so that she and her relatives are not harmed.
en.sender: Katharina Kraeusin, widow of the late Hans Wolff von Bibelspurg
en.recipient: Statthalter, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg

en.regest: Katharina Warrenthin, widow of the deceased Hans Wolf von Bibelsberg, revokes an alleged power of attorney issued under the name of Othmar Blumen, town court bailiff of St. Gallen. Instead, she instructs the citizen of St. Gallen Joachim Wittlinger to appear before the court, to contest the invalid proclamation, and to appeal if necessary. She promises to confirm the actions of her proxy and to hold him harmless.
en.recipient: Joachim Wittlinger

en.regest: Junkher Hans Heinrich von Muggenthal asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to report to him on the matters and their origin mentioned in a letter from his citizen, the widow Katharina Wölfin.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Bern inform St. Gallen that they have examined the charge of customs evasion against Jacob and Nicolaus Kunck. Since the saffron was unmarked, it was confiscated. Bern waives half of the imposed fine of one hundred Kronen, but demands the payment of the remaining fifty Kronen as well as the settlement of the customs debts outstanding for six years.
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Luzern request the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen to support their citizen Niklaus Brunswiler. He claims that his deceased aunt Barbara Brunswilerin made a will in St. Gallen that disinherited his father Balthasar Brunswiler. Niklaus Brunswiler, as the next heir, asks for the annulment of the will and for the assignment of the estate. Luzern requests St. Gallen to hear the case and to help Niklaus Brunswiler obtain his right.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Luzern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hugo Graf zu Montfort und Rotenfels, Herr zu Tettnang und Argen, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct his subject Magdalena Gigerin, widow of the deceased Jakob Schlapfer, to pay the promised sum of money to his subject Claus Beck of Hemmersreith. He refers to the fact that promises made by women in St. Gallen are fulfilled by the city, and asks for neighborly support.
en.sender: Hugo Graf zu Montfort und Rotenfels, Herr zu Tettnang und Argen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report that a considerable number of riders will soon come to Konstanz and that noble gatherings are to take place there, which they assess as a threat by the Five Cantons. They ask St. Gallen to investigate, in the strictest secrecy, the war preparations and intentions in Konstanz and to inform them immediately, so that they can conduct themselves accordingly for the upcoming Diet at Baden.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the convening of a Diet of the Confederates on 10. December in Baden im Aargau. This Diet was set because of difficulties caused by the government of Ensisheim in the purchase of grain. The imperial envoys would inform at this Diet about new tolls and other matters. The Zürichers ask the St. Galleners to transmit their concerns for the Diet.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to forgive the deceased Jacob Fribolt, who had married against the order and thereby forfeited his benefice in the hospital, and to reinstate him in his former status. They justify this with the honorable conduct of Fribolt's father and hope that he will behave in accordance with the order in the future.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, at their request, they have examined two witnesses in Appenzell. These are to testify in a legal dispute between Heinrich Egger and Bartholomäus Riedrer of the St. Gallen monastery on the one hand and Hans Weber and Hans Rüttin of St. Gallen on the other hand, concerning a twenty-pound interest deed. The testimonies were recorded in writing and handed over to the parties.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Town clerk and Council of Bregenz report to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on the examination of the witness Hans Ebnen in the legal dispute between the St. Gallen citizens Jakob Schirmer and Jakob Freywis. Ebnen testified under oath that he was with Jakob Freywis on 25 January 1550 and there spoke with Schirmer about money and a stepfather. He heard nothing of a purchase of war weapons. Bregenz sends the witness testimony and offers further assistance.
en.sender: Town clerk and Council of Bregenz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: B. Bochetel confirms the receipt of a letter of 13 March and promises to advocate for the merchants of St. Gallen in Toulouse, whose rights are to be upheld by the King. He reports on the capture of the fortress Vignac by the Marshal of Brissac and the repulsion of an imperial attack by the captain Ludovic de Birague, whereupon the imperial side will observe the truce.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to ensure the swiftest and most cost-effective settlement of the estate of Gallus Sünder. He was a pensioner in the St. Gallen hospital and has died. His sister, the citizen of Lindau Barbara Sünderin, widow of the deceased Hans Brunnenburger, is the sole heir.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Councils of the city of Augsburg ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to return the letters deposited at St. Gallen to their citizen Wilhelm Gertz. They promise to support Gertz in similar cases in a friendly manner.
en.sender: Councils of the city of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Council messengers of the five cantons Luzern, Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden and Zug ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen again to reimburse the two women Regula Kellerin and Katharina Tästelerin for the costs incurred in their action from the income of the foundation St. Katharina. They refer to the fact that no answer has yet been received and ask for a receipt.
en.sender: Council messengers of the five cantons Luzern, Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden and Zug
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform them in writing whether the St. Gallen Melcher Kern, who had chopped off the right hand of their countryman Konrad Stricker, still possesses assets. They request assistance with Stricker's claim for damages, as Kern has fled to Appenzell and pays nothing.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Josef and Jörg Weibelknecht, fellow citizens of Bern, reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen. They reject the accusation that they had imprisoned their fellow citizen Martin Hochrütiner for a debt of money. They describe how Hochrütiner, as their servant, had borrowed money in their name and embezzled it. After his arrest in Lyon, he had voluntarily transferred his goods to them. They emphasize that they had followed the judgment of the Council of St. Gallen and offer to sell the goods to settle their claim.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information about the wages for master tailors and journeymen working in the Kundhaus. They wish to know whether there is a corresponding ordinance in St. Gallen or how high the earnings are there, in order to examine their own demands for a wage increase.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Sursee ask the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen to support their citizen Franz Schnetzer in asserting an inheritance right to the estate of the recently deceased Simon Gassner in St. Gallen. Schnetzer says that he only learned of the inheritance after the expiration of the fourteen-day period set in the deceased's will. Sursee appeals to the right that an inheritance must remain undivided for a year and a day, and asks for a written answer.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Sursee
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Bern ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to determine whether Mathias Brunner, who is married to Margarethe Fürstenbergerin in Bern, has another wife and a child in St. Gallen. They ask for a prompt answer in order to be able to proceed accordingly with regard to Brunner.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau send Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the statements of the witnesses Ulrich Kuken, Hans Spilman and Adam Brändtlin as well as a copy of a deed of sale. It concerns the inheritance division of the deceased Konrad Kessler and the claims of his son Veit Kessler, who lives in St. Gallen. The witnesses confirm that Veit Kessler received 125 pounds 6 shillings 8 pfennig in the division and sold a house in Aschach.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Margrave Georg Friedrich zu Brandenburg informs the Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen that he has learned of an attack on a merchant of St. Gallen at Gunzenhausen. He regrets the incident, explains that the perpetrators fled into his territory and could not be arrested. He promises to continue the investigations in order to punish the perpetrators and to replace the damage.
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell report that the Appenzeller Michel Uoßer appeared before them with his wife. He declared that he intended to bequeath his property elsewhere after his death and to exclude the wife of his kinsman, whom he referred to as his kinsman and benefactor. The wife earnestly asks that St. Gallen not interpret this as malicious intent against her, but as being influenced by others. Appenzell asks for an amicable clarification.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Christoff Crößer informs Alexander Gierdtz in Lindau that he had only received his letter today. He refers to the agreed payment of 42 and 55 gulden and to the fact that he had been settled with money only, not with a surety. He refuses the sending of the young Vogler and his brother-in-law, as he does not know them. He has already sent a servant and expects an answer or payment within six to eight days, otherwise he will pursue the matter further.
en.recipient: Alexander Gierdtz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizens Otmar and Clement die Horen as well as Rudolf Senn to pay the amounts owed to the friend of the Nürnberg Council, Wilhelm Loffelholz, according to the bonds. The citizens of St. Gallen had unjustifiably blocked Loffelholz's claim through their Weibel. Nürnberg offers to clarify any counterclaims before their court.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Councils and envoys of the XIII cantons ask Margrave Georg Friedrich von Brandenburg to return the stolen goods to a merchant of St. Gallen, who was ambushed and robbed by riders in August at the Erlibach. They refer to the duty of the authorities to secure the imperial roads and threaten countermeasures otherwise.
en.sender: Councils and envoys of the XIII cantons of the Confederation
en.recipient: Georg Friedrich, Margrave of Brandenburg

en.regest: Margrave Georg Friedrich zu Brandenburg answers the complaint of the Confederates about the robbery of merchants of St. Gallen at Gunzenhausen. He regrets the incident, but explains that the open borders of his territory make complete prevention difficult. Since the merchants were not under the escort of Brandenburg, he refuses compensation. He offers to punish the perpetrators if they can be identified.
en.recipient: Councils and envoys of the Confederation at Baden

en.regest: Caspar von Wartenstein, bailiff of Arbon, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the St. Gallen citizen Erasmus Schlumpf the Younger to pay the court costs to the bailiff of the Bishop of Konstanz or to conclude the lawsuit. Schlumpf had not appeared at the court, whereby the costs for the bailiff had increased. Wartenstein appeals to the old custom of neighborhood, according to which judgments were to be enforced in the respective jurisdiction.
en.sender: Caspar von Wartenstein, bailiff of Arbon
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Graf zu Montfort und Rottenschweiler asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help his subject Claus Vogt in the collection of a debt owed to the St. Gallen woman Schläpferin. The Count refers to the poverty of the Vogt and asks for an amicable solution, so that he does not have to plunge his family into misery.
en.sender: Hans Graf zu Montfort und Rottenschweiler, Herr zu Tettnang und Argen
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: The Councils and envoys of the thirteen cantons of the Confederation ask the Margrave of Brandenburg to investigate the outrages by robbers in his territorial sovereignty reported by St. Gallen and Bischofszell. They demand the return of the stolen goods and the securing of the imperial roads, as the victims were robbed despite having a valid safe-conduct and having paid the toll. They refer to the duty of the safe-conduct lord to provide compensation and ask for a written answer.
en.sender: Councils and envoys of the thirteen cantons of the Confederation
en.recipient: Georg Friedrich, Margrave of Brandenburg

en.regest: The Councilors of Margrave Georg Friedrich zu Brandenburg in the house Onoltzbach inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have answered the petition raised by the Confederates in Baden for the damaged citizens of St. Gallen in the absence of the Margrave. They enclose a copy of this answer and declare themselves inclined to friendly services.
en.sender: Councilors of Margrave Georg Friedrich zu Brandenburg in the house Onoltzbach
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the received news and ask for mutual communication of credible events. They convey new news from Schaffhausen about military unrest and muster places in the name of the King of England on the borders of the Confederation. Furthermore, they report on a letter from Rottweil, according to which Herr Niclaus Fryherr zu Pollwiler has accepted twenty hostile Landsknechte and ordered them to Harb for mustering.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Bern thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a letter of the 23rd of the month and the new news contained therein. They express their friendship and readiness for mutual support. Furthermore, they ask them to report new news to them as well and to use their influence and skill in places where the Confederation is in danger.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Glarus thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the report on the damage that King Franz I. suffered in Picardy last month. They ask that they also be informed of all new or occurring matters in the future, and commend themselves to the protection of the Almighty.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Councils and envoys of the thirteen cantons of the Confederation at Baden forward to St. Gallen a copy of a letter from the Councils of Brandenburg. This concerns the robbery and attack on citizens of St. Gallen and other Confederates. The Confederates ask St. Gallen to handle the matter at its own discretion.
en.sender: Councils and envoys of the thirteen cantons of the Confederation at Baden
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Councils and envoys of the thirteen cantons of the Confederation, assembled in Baden, warn the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of military unrest, particularly in the Spychertal near Rotweil, where troops would have gathered. They ask the St. Gallen to equip their citizens with weapons and armor and to inform them of possible threats. On the 23rd of the month, they would assemble in Solothurn.
en.sender: Councils and envoys of the thirteen cantons of the Confederation
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the shoemaker's apprentice Ulrich Hirer to appear before the court of Zürich regarding an insult to their citizen Stephan Walder. Walder had apologized to the apprentice's daughter, upon which the latter had written him an insulting letter. Zürich demands that the apprentice be legally prosecuted.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Graf zu Montfort und Rotenfels, Herr zu Tettnang und Argen, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help his subject Lorenz Bürchlin of Immenstadt in the collection of debts of the deceased Schlapperitzin in St. Gallen. Bürchlin has been imprisoned in St. Gallen because of this claim. The Schlapperitzin had left debts in Italien, which are secured in St. Gallen by bonds and receipts. The Count asks to support Bürchlin in the collection of this claim so that he may be released from imprisonment.
en.sender: Hans Graf zu Montfort und Rotenfels, Herr zu Tettnang und Argen
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Wil ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Rochus Romer, who has been slandered in Bern by Master Hans Maler. They request that Romer be assisted so that he may work again, and that his incurred costs be reimbursed. They ask for a reply to the enclosed missive of the Schultheiss and Council of Bern.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the City Judges to grant legal standing to their town clerk Hans Jakob Joch, who cannot appear in person due to civic business, through his proxy. They request that the submitted documents be read and that the arrest warrant against the defendants be maintained until the judgment is pronounced.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City Judges of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen regarding prohibited coins. They send a copy of their own prohibition, which forbids the circulation of certain Italian and Welsche coins, in particular the new two batzen, as well as Wiener, Nürnberger, Nördlinger and Schwarzkatzenpfennige, and orders penalties for their issuance or mixing with good money. Good Welsche coins remain permissible.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jakob, Landvogt zu Baden im Aargau, asks the Burgomaster of St. Gallen to inform him in writing whether the House of Austria in Österreich, Schwaben and Etschland accepts Landsknechte and whether these are sent to Mailand. He asks for information on where the soldiers would be needed, or at least whether any such are accepted at all.
en.sender: Jakob, Landvogt zu Baden im Aargau
en.recipient: Burgomaster of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter from E. Er. wt. concerning the regulation of the Welsche coinage. They indicate that they have prohibited in Lindau the Welsche Dreier, Löwen, Zehener, as well as all other new, unknown Welsche coins, the Nuremberg Pfennige and Heller, and all Pfennige that are not struck at fourteen for a Patzen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jost Tschudi von Glarus answers a complaint by the St. Gallen Hauptmann Franz Studer. The latter accuses Tschudi of having moved soldiers to march away with false words. Tschudi affirms that he had only encouraged the soldiers to stay with their Hauptleute, as the latter wanted to cut their pay. He rejects the accusations and asks for acquittal.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to proceed legally against the St. Gallen shoemaker Ulrich Furer, who had insulted them, on behalf of their citizen Felix Walder and his son. They ask for a letter of authentication for the lawsuit and promise to stand up for St. Gallen in similar cases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Buchhorn ask the Burgomaster of St. Gallen to convince the merchants of St. Gallen to continue bringing linen and other goods to the Buchhorn Krammarkt. They apologize for the recent delay of the goods by carters, whom they will punish, and promise that the goods will be delivered punctually in the future.
en.recipient: Burgomaster of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizens Anna and Kunigunde Hündlin, who stood before the court against Christoph and Lonckhart Zollikofer, in their judgment. The Zollikofer had rejected the sureties proposed by the Hündlin. Lindau requests that the Zollikofer be instructed to be content with an appropriate bail.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their fellow citizen Elisabetha Huenlin, widow of Jörgen Aichelmüller, in the inheritance of her deceased brother-in-law Hans Huenlin. The inheritance was left in Frankreich and a bill of exchange had been drawn by the St. Gallen Zolligkhouer. A judgment had ordered the surrender of the obligations and the inheritance, but the inheritance has not yet been paid out. Überlingen requests that the Zolligkhouer be moved to fulfill the judgment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Neuenburg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the St. Gallen woman Magdalena Gmainderin, who is having a hip injury treated in Neuenburg by Master Georg the Barber. As she has no money, they ask that her friends and relatives in St. Gallen be urged to provide surety for her. The surety document is to be handed over to Magdalena Rotsch, so that the doctor can be paid.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information on meat prices and weight determinations in St. Gallen. The Konstanzer butchers complain about high prices and low profits. The Konstanzer request a written answer regarding the prices for beef, cow, calf, and lamb meat, the weight of the pound, as well as about privileges such as lungs, livers, or blood sausage.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Anna Ylin, widow of the late Caspar Schlaprigt, residing in Ravensburg, renounces the citizenship granted to her and her children by the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen. She asks for written confirmation of the acceptance and for further favor. The letter was sealed with the seal of the Ravensburg town bailiff Anton Möwenberger.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Bremgarten report to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on the answer of the Bremgartnerin Margaretha Karpfin, who refuses to return to her husband Hans Norden, a blacksmith in St. Gallen. She justifies this by his lack of financial support and a letter in which he refuses to speak with her. They ask St. Gallen to compel Norden to take his wife back and live with her.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Statthalter, bailiff and court of Staufen report to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the tailor's apprentice Lienhart Weber, who comes from St. Gallen and is mentally confused in Staufen. As they see no improvement, they ask the St. Gallen authorities to take Weber to themselves and help him.
en.sender: Statthalter, bailiff and court of Staufen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Statthalter, bailiff and court of Rorschach report to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they had settled and cleared the debts of the St. Gallen citizen Bernhart Weber, who had become unconscious in Rorschach, with the creditors. As Webers' condition is unstable, they had, upon request, accompanied a messenger with him to Basel or as far as necessary. They further offer their services.
en.sender: Statthalter, bailiff and court of Rorschach
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Coignet informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the Royal Lieutenant of Lyon has reported on large sums of money that subjects of St. Gallen had taken out of Lyon. He fears fraud to the detriment of the King and asks the people of St. Gallen, as good friends and allies of the King, to ensure that such transactions are conducted honestly and that no one from St. Gallen lends their name to foreign traders who take money out of the kingdoms.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a nighttime break-in into the writing room of the hospital, in which money was stolen. They ask to inquire with goldsmiths, merchants and inns whether suspicious persons appear with the stolen money, and for a report on their appearance and clothing.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Konrad Engweiler to settle the debts owed to the citizens of Ulm Bartholomäus App and Heinrich Zeller. Engweiler owes App 86 gulden 10 batzen and Zeller 90 gulden 14 batzen for cloth. The claim has been due since 1658. Ulm asks for payment to the Ulm messenger Jörg Zippen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Council of Feldkirch ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information about the local meat ordinance and prices, as the Feldkirch butchers are asking for higher prices due to rising costs. They want to know the prices in St. Gallen in order to make an appropriate increase without burdening the neighboring towns.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Gessler von Uri, Landvogt im Rintal, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to follow the proceedings between Wolf von Salchenried and the Herr von Beckenstein, as decided by the Aacht Orten in Baden. He informs them that he has requested the Herr von Beckenstein to appear in St. Gallen on the next Tuesday after Easter or to send an attorney to legally handle the claim.
en.sender: Johann Gessler von Uri, Landvogt im Rintal
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The bailiff and Council of Bischofszell report that they have arrested a poor man named Ludwig, who was on a list of persons and clothing transmitted by Wil. Ludwig stated that he had been spinning and making Zainlen in the area for two years. He said that he had bought his coat before Christmas from a Failträgerin in St. Gallen. Bischofszell asks St. Gallen to inquire with this woman whether she had sold such a coat, and promises to transmit the answer.
en.sender: The bailiff and Council of Bischofszell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Bichler, Council member of Uri and Landvogt of Rinegg, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he has had a woman from Diepoldsau, who had slandered him, taken into custody and led to Blatten at the Oberried. He asks the St. Gallen authorities to have the executioner Hans come immediately to the Oberried, so that the truth may come to light and the crime be punished. Bichler promises to pay Hans the due reward.
en.sender: Johann Bichler, Council member of Uri and Landvogt of Rinegg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for written information regarding meat prices and valuation in St. Gallen. They wish to know how beef, veal, mutton, and pork, as well as offal and sausages, are valued, whether butchers are allowed to mix offal into the meat, and how much meat per week per butcher is permitted. Lindau wishes to orient itself towards its neighbors in order to adjust the prices for its own butchers.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The bailiff and Council of Bischofszell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send a hangman, as they have taken in a prisoner and needed his statement. They request that the hangman be arranged at their expense for the evening or the next morning.
en.sender: The bailiff and Council of Bischofszell
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Court of the Gotteshaus zu Kreuzlingen send to the Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen the statements of Martin Klaeß, Jörg Mürckh, Ursell Bechterin and Agatha Sennenningin regarding a Compasbrief submitted by Sebastian Görli. It concerns the sale of about a hundred ells of linen in the inn at Kreuzlingen by a man named Hans Seijdler or Keßweijler. The interrogated persons describe the seller and confirm the sale.
en.sender: Ammann and Court of the Gotteshaus zu Kreuzlingen
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Councils of Bischofszell thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for their letter concerning the newly established toll. They have sent their town clerk to Baden, who, however, was prevented from doing so due to other business. They ask for the desired answer and declare themselves ready for neighborly friendship and willingness to serve.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Stadtammann and Council of Feldkirch report that a man, who gave himself out as Hans Müller of St. Gallen, collected alms in Feldkirch and was accused by two men of St. Gallen of having slandered them. The men of Feldkirch took him into custody and determined that he was in fact Stöffel Müller, a former bathhouse servant from St. Gallen. They ask St. Gallen for written information about his person and his conduct.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform them in writing of the names of suspicious persons, as they have the suspicious Martin Häfelin from Suningen in custody. They also inform them of the current meat prices in Konstanz: beef costs 6 Pfennig per pound, mutton 16 Pfennig, as mutton is scarce.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Wangen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizens Hans and Konrad Hüeber as well as their sister Barbara in the collection of an outstanding sum of money from the citizen of St. Gallen Jakob Lotzer. The Hüeber had served the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Klaus Lotzer and are in debt with a considerable sum, which Jakob Lotzer has taken over. Since Barbara is elderly, she urgently needs the money.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Steckborn request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Melchior Baur to assist the widow Barbara Baur and her two young nieces in obtaining their inheritance in Venedig. The nieces are orphans and require care. Baur possesses the inheritance, which does not belong to him alone, and should hand it over to those entitled to it.
en.sender: The Schultheiss and Council of Steckborn
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant safe conduct to the St. Gallen citizens Michel Scherer and Galli Gmuender to appear before the court. The two are said to have withdrawn out of fear of imprisonment due to accusations they consider unjustified, and are now ready to prove their innocence. Zürich asks that the two be heard in their defense and that they be helped so that they are freed from further dangers and punishments.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Einsiedeln ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to introduce their citizens Georg Schüssler and Barbara Rüttermannin to the St. Gallen citizen Otilia Rüttermannin as relatives of hers. Otilia Rüttermannin wishes to make a will and has inquired whether any relatives are still alive. The Einsiedeln authorities ask that the matter be favorably promoted so that the relatives are provided for in the will.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Council of Feldkirch ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant the hospital master a postponement of payment until Martini. The background is a judgment in favor of the widow Elisabeth Eglis against Martin Jäger. Jäger is maintained in the Feldkirch hospital and his goods are to be sold by the appointed guardians in order to settle the debts. The guardians ask for time in order to be able to sell the goods at a good price.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform the Council envoys of Zürich and Luzern that they have been sent in the name of the Confederates to Kreuzlingen to settle disputes with Konstanz. Since the toll increases by Konstanz also concern the Confederation, the St. Gallen ask to hear their advice and to deal with the matter, so that the complaints are mitigated.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Council envoys of the cantons Zürich and Luzern

en.regest: Ammann and Council of Feldkirch request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the bell founder Ulrich N. to appear at the expense of the defendants, the roof tile makers in Feldkirch, and to give information as an expert on a disputed bell. This is to be done to promote the legal dispute between the community of Götzis and the roof tile makers.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to post and proclaim an edict in St. Gallen. It concerns the absent citizen of Lindau, Peter Knecht, whose creditors have sued his wife for outstanding debts. The Lindau authority has inventoried Knecht's assets and set a court day. St. Gallen is to inform its citizens and dependents so that they can participate in the court day.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Glarus thank St. Gallen for the friendly handling of the division of the inheritance of the children of Hans Altman. They declare that they will take no deduction from St. Gallen and request written confirmation of this renunciation. Furthermore, they ask St. Gallen, in view of the small inheritance and the minority of the children, to deal with them graciously.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Melchior Gallati, Landvogt in Ober- und Unterthurgau, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the heirs of the deceased Bernhart Feren, represented by the bailiff Hansli Huber, are asserting claims to inheritances in the city of St. Gallen. He refers to a decision of the seven cantons, according to which subjects, upon presentation of credible documents regarding their urban citizenship, may freely depart without deduction and take possession of their goods. He asks the authorities of St. Gallen to treat the heirs accordingly.
en.sender: Melchior Gallati, Landvogt in Ober- und Unterthurgau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report that the prisoner Martin Schuster from St. Gallen has confessed to stolen linen and other items. Since the prisoner's statement contains more details than the list transmitted by St. Gallen, Lindau requests a review and a report on the further investigations.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Dreyer Pfund zu Zurhaett ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to take up the case of Frau Katharina Welffin and her curators, in particular her son Balthasar Kunzen. They request that the woman be taken under their protection and that messengers be sent to the Lords Insehers of the Eight Cantons to press for the swift execution of the judgments obtained against the Welffin family.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Uri answer the inquiry from St. Gallen as to whether Hans Joachim keeps a household with a woman other than his wife, the Appenzellerin. They confirm that he has a wife in St. Gallen, with whom he resides, and that he has no other woman in Uri, but only earns with his work and behaves honestly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Neuenburg thank for the communication regarding the edict of Ulrich Zölligoffer and the judges of St. Gallen concerning the inheritance of Jörg Kastant. They state that Othmar Kastant of Neuenburg, who presents himself as an heir alongside his sister, owes debts to them and their subjects and has been publicly defamed as a thief. They ask St. Gallen to hold the inheritance of Othmar Kastant until further notice and to report on the status of the inheritance case as well as its debts towards Neuenburg.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen report that the citizen of St. Gallen, Anton Stadler, has fallen into disgrace due to the unlawful purchase of grain. Stadler has always behaved honestly in Schaffhausen and paid up. The Schaffhausen authorities ask St. Gallen to forgive Stadler and to show him grace again.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they had detained the tanner and vagabond Kaspar Summerlang of Memingen for suspicious actions. He stated that he has a stepfather named Matheüs Kruegel of Baltringen, who is about 30 years old, bearded, dressed in linen trousers and a linen jacket, and is wandering about in the Confederation. Lindau asks St. Gallen to keep an eye on this man in order to punish the evil.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Stadtschultheiss and Council of Bregenz report that the weaver Jacob Hüner, called Scheicher, has not settled a debt to the Amtmann Hans Appenzeller, called Müller, for linen. The citizen of Bregenz Bastian Mörlin, called Finck, has paid the sum for Hüner and seized his household goods. Bregenz asks St. Gallen to report in whose name Hüner sold the linen, and requests support in the matter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to post a proclamation. In it, the heirs of the deceased Jacob Zollikofer and Jacob Stauder, who owe money to the Memmingers, are to be called upon to report at a specific date and to present their situation. This is to be done in the interest of the Memmingen creditors.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to prevent their grain-transporting citizens from buying grain from Count zu Tengen during his market visit in Stein am Rhein. This harms the Stein am Rhein market, as the citizens of St. Gallen had previously had free purchase. They ask for a written answer.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen communicate to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen new news from Zürich and Bern as well as the negotiation results of the assembled Electors and Princes of the Holy Roman Empire at Naumburg with the papal legate regarding the Council. They ask for reciprocity in the forwarding of news.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have the edict concerning the bankruptcy of their citizen Michel Halder in St. Gallen publicly proclaimed. Halder has handed over his assets to the creditors. The creditors are to appear on the appointed court day and assert their claims.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the examination of coins that have come to them from the Confederates of Uri. The Bohemian coins were found to be of full value; the thaler are still under examination. Zürich asks Uri to be more careful with the coins in the future, as otherwise they would have to recall them. The four Bohemian coins that the mintmaster Hans Gutenson had previously sent were also confirmed to be of full value.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen reply to the letter of the St. Gallen creditors of Anton Stadler. Stadler has not changed towards the Überlingen authorities and their committee. Since the creditors recognize Stadler's Abschid and right of domicile, the Überlingen authorities set a peremptory court day for 12 August before the city court, at which the creditors can present their claims.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen inform that the court day for the creditors of the imprisoned fellow citizen Anthony Stadler, originally set for 12 August, has been postponed to 26 August at six o'clock in the morning before the city court. Stadler remains in custody until then. Überlingen asks St. Gallen to inform the creditors of this.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen ask the creditors of Anton Stadler in St. Gallen to redeem two interest bonds for 130 gulden, which are pledged there, and to hand over the money to Überlingen. Überlingen has seized the bonds in the course of an arrest and wishes to use them to cover its own arrears, as it has not been fully paid by Stadler. The remaining money is to benefit the other creditors according to city law.
en.recipient: Creditors of Anton Stadler of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Marx Wyszler, who wants to sue Peter Büeler in St. Gallen for 100 gulden. Wyszler already has a judgment and letters with seals, but the payment has so far been prevented. Schaffhausen asks that Wyszler be protected and the payment be promoted.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Landvogt Ilsung to press the customs officers in Gebratzhofen to refrain from collecting import duties and from the seizure of the goods of the merchants of St. Gallen until the conclusion of the negotiations with the government in Innsbruck. This is to be done in accordance with the agreement made in Baden.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: N. Ilsung, imperial councillor and Landvogt in Schwaben

en.regest: The bailiff and Council of Bischofzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant a postponement until after the feast days to their councilor Jacob Scherwiler, who was called upon by St. Gallen to pay a share of the inheritance of his deceased sister. They hope that the matter can be amicably settled through the council office to be appointed.
en.sender: The bailiff and Council of Bischofzell
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Brant, Landvogt of Imensee, Küßnacht and Ardt, confirms to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the receipt of their letter of 10 October 1661. He requests the payment of 210 gulden to the widow and children of the deceased citizen of Imst Cyrillus Clausen Becken, which, according to the judgment of the court of St. Gallen, are to be paid by Caspar Schlapprizi. He refers to the urgent distress of the family.
en.sender: Hans Brant, Landvogt of Imensee, Küßnacht and Ardt
en.recipient: Statthalter, Klein- und Großrat of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen report that the toll collectors and counter-toll collectors of Gebhartszoffen had written to their citizens regarding the payment of tolls, whereupon they had forwarded the toll collectors' answer to the citizens. They hope that the toll collectors will let the trade rest until a Diet of the Confederation. Furthermore, they forward new news from Basel and ask for confidential observation and reporting.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Council of Feldkirch ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the town clerk Christoph Krantzegger and his wife Katharina Carthauserin in the drawing up of a testament by Magdalena Geigerin. Krantzegger hopes to be provided for in the testament of the widow, whom he refers to as his niece.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of the city of Bern warn Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the consequences of violating the prohibition against joining foreign military service. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to admonish their subjects not to enlist, as Bern will otherwise enforce the established penalties. Bern wishes to use its own subjects in an emergency to protect the fatherland.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to permit their fellow citizen Heinrich Ritter to have three measures and weights made. They request that the competent officials examine and mark the pieces according to the city's regulations, so that Appenzell may obtain them for the fee.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Linder, hatmaker, reports to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that his fellow citizens Salomon Vogel and Gall Gmunder owe him debts. He says that he has pursued Vogel legally and has come into prison because of other debtors. Following a petition to the court, he says that he was released from prison without depositing pledges. Both debtors have fled the city. Linder asks for help in order to obtain his property.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Bern inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the withdrawal of Bernese mercenaries to Frankreich. They explain that the city of Lyon had asked for help against the Duke of Guise. Bern had originally wanted to prevent the departure, but the mercenaries withdrew despite the prohibition. Bern asks for understanding and assures that this is not directed against the Confederates.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich confirm the receipt of a letter from St. Gallen, which concerns the new toll arrangement of the imperial commissioners and the Confederates. They ask for patience, as no full Council could be convened due to autumn business and the absence of the Burgomaster. As soon as the Burgomaster has returned, the matter will be discussed and a reply given.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur ask Burgomaster and Council of Zürich to accept the executioner Matern Hyffin of Mülhausen for the office of Frauenfeld. They certify that he is a skilled judge, who has hitherto conducted himself well in the city and is not given to excessive drinking. They hope that he will perform the service to the satisfaction of the people of Zürich.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Hans Joachim Gütenson, Münzmeister zu Uri, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to continue granting him his citizenship and to levy the annual taxes. He refers to the fact that he has hitherto behaved as a citizen and has not deserved any disgrace. He asks for an oral explanation of the reasons for the alleged complaint about his citizenship, so that he may behave accordingly.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a Confederate Diet scheduled for 3 January in Baden. This Diet serves to address disputes between the Five Cantons and Glarus as well as customs and other matters. The St. Gallen are requested, if they have anything to negotiate on these points, to send their messengers there.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Sebastian und Heinrich Zangmeister ask the Stadtpflege, Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to use their influence with their Council for the payment of a debt of 640 gulden 50 kreuzer including interest and costs. They say that in the year 1660 they sold Barchent to Jacob Staud and relatives and undertook to make the payment from the revenues of the Zangmeister in Memingen. Staud, however, kept the 630 gulden paid for himself. The Zangmeister had the money arrested with Leonhart Weiss and request the Council to force Staud to pay.
en.recipient: Stadtpflege, Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Rathgeber of Augsburg ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizens Caspar Zuewyler and Jacob Stauder to make the payment promised to the Zaugmeister brothers Sebastian and Heinrich from the money due to them. The Zaugmeister had previously lent cash to the St. Gallen citizens and are now in danger. Augsburg asks for payment to avoid further disputes and costs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask the Zoller and Murer of Gefertshofen to postpone the new toll for the aforementioned citizens of Schaffhausen until the Diet has brought about a clarification. Should the toll nevertheless be decided upon, the citizens of Schaffhausen undertake to pay it.
en.recipient: Georg Christ Zoller and Erhart Murer of Gefertshofen

en.regest: The Council and the country people of the Majority of Glarus ask the arbitrating cantons to deliberate earnestly before the Diet of the Confederates at Baden on 4 January how they could restore to Glarus its withdrawn rights. They fear that the dispute with the Five Cantons will be prolonged without a solution and that Glarus will remain excluded from the Pünden and the Landfrieden. They demand a friendly answer by honest messengers at the Diet at Baden.
en.sender: The Council and the country people of the Majority of Glarus
en.recipient: The arbitrating cantons

en.regest: Johannes Rorer, pastor of Bernang, and Thomas Hanggelar, former Ammann and guardian, confirm that Hans Graf von Rorschach, now a citizen and resident in St. Gallen, has redeemed and freed the house and courtyard of Ulrich Hugen for one pound four shillings four pfennig. They declare Hans Graf thereby quit and free.
en.recipient: Hans Graf

en.regest: Hanibal Roschacher accuses the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the citizen of St. Gallen Hans Rietzmann owes him 252 gulden and 41 kreuzer for goods and borrowed money. Despite multiple reminders and granted deadlines, Rietzmann has not paid the amount and thereby damaged him. Roschacher asks the city for support in collecting the claim.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel the citizen of St. Gallen Hans Witzigmann to pay a debt of 252 gulden and 41 kreuzer to the citizen of Nürnberg Hanibal Rosenthaler. They refer to a received supplication and ask for support, as the debt is acknowledged.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter from St. Gallen concerning a sack of grain that arrived in Lindau and had been mentioned multiple times by Thomas Pfund. They explain that, according to their grain house regulations, a foreign sack must be set aside to clarify its origin. Since the Kern has been sold and the empty sack was assigned to Martin Maurer, they ask St. Gallen to have the money along with the band mark returned through Pfund.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of the good news of the peace in Frankreich. They enclose a copy of the letter of the French envoy Delacroix, who reports on the end of the civil wars and the return of the troops. Zürich offers to inform St. Gallen of further news and asks for reciprocity.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Stefan Kiedt, bailiff of Bischofzell, informs the court of St. Gallen that, at the request of Hans Allthaler, he has questioned the Ammann of Schönberg, Simon Künzli. It concerns a dispute between Allthaler and Ulrich Flori over the purchase of a debt of 20 gulden that Sebastian Flori owed to the Draeger. Künzli confirms under oath that Allthaler had bought the debt for 16 to 17 1/2 gulden in cash, without any pledge being mentioned.
en.recipient: Town pastor, judge and court of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lüneburg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist the guardians appointed by them for the children of the deceased Lüneburg citizen Ludwig Kitter, namely Hans Hartmann and Jakob Hinderoffer, in the division of the father's estate in St. Gallen. They request a swift and inexpensive settlement so that the children receive their inheritance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Council and the envoys of the Confederation ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant their citizen Anton Stadler free and safe conduct. Stadler has departed from St. Gallen because of his debts and now wishes to settle accounts with his creditors. The Confederates promise to support St. Gallen in similar cases.
en.sender: Council and envoys of the Confederation
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Schultheiss and Council of Bern to inquire with the Obersten and the judge in Inn about the status of the murder of the St. Gallen citizen Sigmund Hoewen in the garrison of Leon. They request Bern to mediate with the Lords of Arberg so that the suspect Ludwig Derin settles amicably with the widow and the children of the murdered man, in order to avoid further costs and legal proceedings.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Bern

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell reply to a letter from St. Gallen regarding interest-bearing bonds pledged by Appenzellers. They ask that the names of the debtors be transmitted in writing or named in person. Appenzell will then ensure that the interest-bearing bonds are redeemed, as this violates the Landssatzung.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
