en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform that Councilor Niklaus Gall wishes to take possession of the estate inherited from his deceased mother-in-law Magdalena Koblerin. They ask St. Gallen to treat Gall neighborly in the withdrawal and to take only the tenth penny, as is customary in Konstanz.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Einsiedeln ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant their citizens Leonhard Eberz and sons the same rights in the estate proceedings of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Hans Ulrich Rüegger as to the locals. Eberz remained indebted to Rüegger in a high sum and fear being disadvantaged in the payment as foreigners. Einsiedeln refers to the previous equal treatment of foreigners and citizens in the Confederation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz report that two large copper Tollen kettles were stolen from the Tollen. They suspect that this was done by foreign itinerant traders and Kesslern, who cast the metal into plates or balls and sell them. They ask St. Gallen to issue a regulation among their citizens that the purchase of such goods is forbidden to such suspicious persons and that they are to be reported.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jörg Abbot of the Monastery of Kreuzlingen asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant his cousin Jacob Appenzeller, who resides in St. Gallen, citizenship for two or three years and to defer it. In the meantime, Appenzeller should not fulfill any other duties than those of a citizen of the city. The Abbot promises to support the city of St. Gallen.
en.sender: Jörg Abbot of the Monastery of Kreuzlingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform them in writing whether they wish to settle the dispute over the tithes, which they had with Appenzell and the Lord of St. Gallen, by legal means. Appenzell has accepted the mediation through an arbitral award, but has received no answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about rumors that the Bishop of Konstanz and the Obrist Jacob Hanibal von Embs are recruiting a regiment of Landsknechte in Eglisau and intend to lead them to Neapel against the Turks. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to inquire about this and report the results to them, in order to jointly counter possible malicious practices.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Landau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to summon the St. Gallen citizen Peter Bäb, called Stainmetzel, as a witness in a legal dispute between the Landsberg citizens Jacob and Hans Spilman, called Schlaig. They ask that his testimony be recorded and sent sealed to Landau so that the proceedings can continue.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank for the letter of 9 June and assure their willingness to do everything that serves the welfare of the Confederation. They share that they had received a letter from the Landvogt of Sargans, which was addressed to the seven cantons and contained a missive of the imperial bailiff of Feldkirch. They send a copy of this letter and ask to be informed about further developments.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Thomas Hauser, citizen of Möskirch, asks the Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizens and residents to settle the loaned sums with interest, according to the two attached principal interest bonds, on the next Bartholomew's Day. He says that he has already satisfied his creditors and can bear no further delays.
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen, in which the latter had requested a report on the butchers' regulations and meat valuation. They send a copy of the regulation of the butchers in the city and land of Zürich, which regulates the prices for various types of meat, the selling rights of the butchers and Küttler, as well as the marketing of offal.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz reply to a letter of 3 July and state that they have newly fixed the meat prices for beef, mutton, and veal as well as offal. They name the respective prices in Hallers, Pfennigs, and Kreuzers. Furthermore, they order that Hungarian oxen, which are slaughtered in Konstanz, are sometimes to be pastured.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the City of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help Herr Ulrich Philipp von der Hohen Saxe with his claim of 5000 gulden plus interest against the estate of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen, Caspar Huber. They refer to an earlier letter and ask that the claim be negotiated according to law and equity and that the creditor be satisfied from the goods left behind.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Council of Feldkirch reply to a letter from the Burgomaster Paul Furtenbach of St. Gallen. They explain that the appointed court day could not be carried out because of the death of the attorney of the plaintiff. The defendant, Frau Zilin, could nevertheless have attended the appointment. As soon as the final brief of the plaintiff is available, a new court day will be appointed. At the request of the defendant, they are ready to determine an appointment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Villingen reply to a letter from St. Gallen of the 6th of the month. It concerns the inheritance of the deceased abbot of Alpersbach, which the St. Gallen citizens Teuber, Hochreutiner and Ruetin claim. Villingen states that the abbot had purchased in Villingen and that the items there were inventoried and removed by order of the Duke of Württemberg. The house had been sold to a citizen of Villingen and conveyed. Villingen rejects the claim of the St. Gallen citizens and refers them to the legal process.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The signatories confirm to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the acceptance of the alliance. They assure that the French Crown will uphold the old privileges of the citizens and merchants of St. Gallen and observe the edicts for the protection of the religion. They ask that no disadvantages be inflicted under the name of the allies, and recommend the continuation of the friendship.
en.sender: Nde la croix, De laubespine, De la croyx, C. de Lymoges
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen about the demand of Count Ulrich von Montfort to refund the money of the St. Gallen Burgomaster Caspar Schlumpf. Lindau declares that, on the basis of Imperial and Circle decrees, it is obliged to return the money, and asks St. Gallen to examine the matter. They will inform the Count through envoys.
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report that Ulrich, Count of Montfort, insists on his demand for the return of the money that a citizen of Lindau from the Lindau Upper Bailiwick had brought to St. Gallen. Lindau will comply with the district decision and return the money. They ask St. Gallen to behave accordingly towards the Count.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for written information regarding the return of the festgeld to the Burgomaster of Lindau, Caspar Schumpff. They learn that two citizens of Lindau in the lordship of Tettnang, despite the return, have had their debts blocked and pledged. Lindau wishes to know how the return was carried out in order to be able to defend its citizens better.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The administrator of the Vogtei and Ämter of Bregenz and Hohenegg reports that Hans Jakob Huser, who is detained in Bregenz, is accused of having celebrated a wedding with Ottilia Schlosser in St. Gallen. Huser denies this and claims to have wandered as a furrier in Tirol and elsewhere for eight years. The authority asks St. Gallen to verify the information and to communicate the result in writing.
en.sender: Administrator of the Vogtei and Ämter of the lordships of Bregenz and Hohenegg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Delacroix informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the envoys of the Confederates will arrive in Solothurn on 12 May. He asks the St. Gallen to send their envoys on that day so that they can ride the dangerous road together. He offers that the envoys can receive their pension in Solothurn.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform that their fellow councillor and banneret Andreas Schmid has passed away. They ask St. Gallen to examine their councillor and bailiff to St. Katharin, Niklaus Jäger, regarding statements made by Jacob Guntper von Küsnach and to communicate the statements in writing.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Hans Hartmann, the guardian of the children of the deceased St. Gallen citizen Ludwig Ritter, in the collection of the inheritance. Hartmann says that he received money from Heinrich Ritter, which the latter, however, retains without sufficient security for interest and principal. Since one child is already married, the inheritance should be assigned to the children and the money securely invested.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ybbs request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admit the cutler Hans Danner, son of a Ybbs citizen, as a fellow citizen. Danner says that he learned the trade for five years in Allkirch near Basel and received a good letter of recommendation there. He wishes to settle in St. Gallen now in order to live better there. The Ybbs citizens assure that Danner is an honest and experienced craftsman.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to detain Margaretha Jännin, who resides there, sister of the deceased citizen of Zürich Jacob Jänni, to take in and raise her brother's three orphaned children. The children have no property, and the previous guardian Barbara Hugin is poor and unable to provide for them.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen not to interpret unfavorably the absence of their citizen Jacob Wortmüller, a farrier, from a court day appointed in St. Gallen. Wortmüller was unable to attend the day for important reasons. The Zürich side asks for amicable treatment and a waiver of the penalty.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to the letter from St. Gallen concerning the prisoner Christian Müller von Ditzingen. They have had it investigated in their lordship of Neuen Ravensburg, where Roggenzell is located, that there is no such dwelling or person there who makes shoe straps. Perhaps the prisoner may have confused the name Amptzell in the lordship of Hans von Steinach, as the names sound similar.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Grangier, appointed by the King to pay the pensions, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of the arrival of the Solothurn treasurer. He asks for the dispatch of two receipts for the old and the new pension of the year 1565, which he will then pay. He points out that in the receipts the treasurer, but he himself as the payer, must be named, and asks for a joint receipt for the first payment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Belliure reports that the royal treasurer has arrived in Solothurn with the money for the pensions. He asks for the dispatch of an envoy to collect the sum. According to the Baden settlement, two pensions are to be paid: the old one for 1563 and the new one for 1566. The receipts must be made out to Jean Grangier, not to the treasurer. In addition, a general receipt for 1565 is to be handed over, so that the old receipt for 1563 can be returned and paid.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss, Burgomaster and Court of Sarnstett ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to deliver the inheritance to the children of the deceased Sarnstett citizen Jering Lichwerken and his wife Anna. They refer to the Landrecht and the Nuremberg and Speyer Constitutions, according to which siblings are considered the next heirs, and ask for a credible inventory.
en.sender: Schultheiss, Burgomaster and Court of Sarnstett
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Stefan Sturm, Master and Council of Straßburg, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel the citizens there, Thomas and Christoph Zollikofer, or their heirs, to give information to the guardians of the widow and children of the deceased Herr von Castanet regarding a sum of 2000 Kronen invested in their name with the Crown of Frankreich. The Zollikofer had received the interest for years, but now it has ceased. Straßburg requests support in clarifying where the principal is located and who has received the interest.
en.sender: Stefan Sturm, Master and Council of Straßburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Burgomaster, Schöffen and Council of Antwerpen to prevent the citizen of St. Gallen Wilhelm Breitenstein from proceeding against the citizen of St. Gallen Hans Liner, who was banished to Antwerpen, and his wife. Liner has waived the disputed inheritance case and arrest. Breitenstein wants to make himself whole from the goods of the fellow councilor of St. Gallen Bartholomäus Schowinger. The St. Gallen ask that their citizens trading in Antwerpen be left undisturbed and that any further claims of Breitenstein be sought before the court of St. Gallen.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster, Schöffen and Council of Antwerpen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Bern warn the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of a threatened invasion by Spanish troops through the Savoyard lands and the County of Burgundy. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to inform them at the next day at Baden how many mercenaries they could provide at Bern's expense in an emergency to protect the common Confederates.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Waldshut ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the four children of Hans Kuckhermann, who are considered the legitimate grandchildren of the sister of the late town parish priest Hans Valentin Furtmüller, in their claim to the inheritance. They promise to bind the heirs to the court in St. Gallen and to ensure the payment of debts.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Heidelberg request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to permit their fellow citizen Matthias Belierin the collection of the inheritance of the deceased Agatha Kulmerin. Belierin, as the nephew of the deceased, is the nearest heir. The two partial administrators appointed in St. Gallen are to hand over the inheritance to him against a receipt. Heidelberg declares itself willing to serve St. Gallen in similar cases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg request Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizens, the heirs of the deceased Bartholomäus Steck, to pay the amount still outstanding after settlement to the citizen of Nürnberg Konrad Buchs. Buchs has already complained that he has received neither payment nor answer.
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The merchants of St. Gallen in Lyon report on the unrest in the city, in which the Catholics would have taken over power, without any blood having been shed so far. The Governor and other gentlemen were striving for order. They ask the merchants in St. Gallen to write to the ambassador in Solothurn, so that he reminds the Governor of the powers granted to him. They send the servant Hans Grillen back with 20 ducats for his maintenance.
en.sender: Caspar Schlapprizi, Joachim Zoli, Sebastian Guldin, Hans Jacob Studer und Caspar Rotmundt Jung
en.recipient: Merchants of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask St. Gallen to inform them in writing which preachers reside in the lower Thurgau, so that these can be called to the Zürich Synodum. They refer to a joint agreement with the Confederates to examine the preachers in Thurgau and Rheintal. Furthermore, they send a copy of a message from Genf concerning the religious unrest in Frankreich.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform that the Confederates, because of the internal disturbances in Frankreich, have decided to send a joint embassy to promote a peaceful settlement. They ask St. Gallen to join this embassy and to communicate their consent in writing.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The administrator of the captaincy, the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the Labhart and Anna Gündelin have ceded to the St. Gallen citizen Adam Kunigslis and his wife the inheritance share due to them. This is done despite a testament that had reserved the estate to the children of the married couple Anna Labhart and Ulrich Schreiber. The people of Konstanz ask the people of St. Gallen to see to it that the estate is not squandered.
en.sender: The administrator of the captaincy, the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Eglisau answer an inquiry from St. Gallen regarding the inheritance of the deceased spouses Peter and Barbara Büttner. They state that the entire inheritance has been converted into money and amounts to 398 florins. The citizen of St. Gallen Andreas Stricker is to receive 33 florins as a sixth of the half of the principal estate. The interest is due only at Pentecost. Stricker is to receive his balance after deduction of the dues.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich communicate to St. Gallen the answer of the French King to the joint letter of the Confederates. The King considers it not necessary to send further envoys and asks that the good will be saved for another occasion. Furthermore, the Zürcher transmit news from Basel about the warlike events in Frankreich, including the capture of the Lord of Tannay and the movement of the troops of the Count of Montmorency.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell report that their countrymen, who trade in yarn, were punished by the weavers' guild at the St. Gallen market for selling, and two of them were summoned before the Council. They ask St. Gallen to protect the Appenzellers from punishment and to communicate the applicable articles in writing so that they can comply with them. Furthermore, they request that the arrest be lifted until a later date.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Villingen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the guardians of the St. Lorenzen-Kirche to return the annual ten shillings, which were endowed from a house in St. Gallen to the Clarisses, to the endower. The endower had endowed the money to the church, but the guardians had no longer paid it out according to the endowment deed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen of 5 June concerning the prisoner Clemens Memwegers. They confirm that Memwegers comes from their land, that he had behaved peacefully there, and that the suspicion of tax evasion is unfounded. They ask for his release.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Chur report that the Chur citizen Heinrich Gantner is begging in St. Gallen and is showing a letter or credential that is unknown to them. They ask St. Gallen to arrest Gantner upon his return and to inform Chur of this. Furthermore, they are to confirm in writing whether Gantner actually carries such a letter with him.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report that their envoys in Baden did not present the complaints of the preachers in the upper Thurgau, as they were advised against delivering messages. They recommend asking the preachers to bring their grievances friendly in the pulpits and to admonish the subjects to attend church. They ask St. Gallen to act accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Loys de Bourbon informs the city of St. Gallen that he will not go into detail about the state of the impoverished kingdom, as the Seneschal of Valtellina, who is acting as messenger, will set this out in detail based on the instructions received. He asks the recipients to give credit to the envoy and commends himself to their favour.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jean Bourset, Council of the King, informs that he has been commissioned by the Duke of Condé to ask the Confederation for support for peace in Frankreich. He asks St. Gallen to send envoys to the French King to discuss the resumption of peace, and invites to a meeting in Basel.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen communicate to the Council of St. Gallen a letter from the Council of Bern dated 17 September 1568. It reports on the military unrest in Frankreich and the request of the French King for 4000 Confederates. Bern keeps its mercenaries at home and intends to appear with force at the Confederate Diet in Baden to prevent the departure. Schaffhausen asks St. Gallen to also send an authorized embassy and to keep the people at home.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jean Henri de Balagny thanks the city of St. Gallen for the received answer and praises its good intention to serve the King and the Prince of Condé. He asks for the continuation of this support and for intercession for the distressed churches in Frankreich. He recommends himself to the favor of the city and offers his services.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Abbot Heinrich von Fischingen asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to permit their citizen Rudolf Mundprathen, preacher at Lustoß, to temporarily serve the vacant benefice at Sirnach, until the monastery finds another preacher.
en.sender: Heinrich, Abbot of the monastery of Fischingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg reply to a letter of 12 October regarding the dispute between the citizen of Nürnberg Hans Ulrich Fitzen and his servant Hans Lochner. They forward the answer of the citizen of St. Gallen Christoph Vischer, who states that the matter concerns only his servant Lochner, who is absent. Lochner has received a copy of the letter and will return soon to settle his affair. The Nurembergers ask that Lochner be excused as an absent person and that he be granted a deadline.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Cardinal-Bishop Mark Sittich of Konstanz complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the St. Gallen hospital master, who no longer pays the interest of 14 quarters of wheat and 14 quarters of barley each, which has been due from time immemorial in the bailiwick of Bischofszell. He asks the city to instruct the hospital master to continue paying the interest.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the Duke of Zweibrücken with his war troops is causing damage in the County of Burgundy and that the Governor is requesting help from the Confederates. They have set a common Confederate Diet for Sunday Cantate, the 8. Mai, and ask St. Gallen to arrange itself accordingly, should it have anything to bring forward.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to permit their town clerk Hans Uetz to commit himself to their service. They request a favorable answer and promise to repay this to St. Gallen and its people.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Stadtpfarrer and Council of Bregenz ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to waive a fine against their fellow citizen Caspar Zillm. He had behaved improperly in St. Gallen. Bregenz will strictly punish him in the future to prevent further outrages. They ask for leniency for reasons of neighborhood.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Christoff Fischer and Hans Scheuffelin respond to a summons directed at them by St. Gallen in the dispute with Hans Fisch. They declare that the matter does not concern them, as they have nothing to do with Fisch. Their servant Hans Lechner lost money, which they would claim from him. They do not intend to sue Fisch and are not willing to submit to a foreign court. If Fisch sues them, he will receive an answer before their authority.
en.recipient: E. H. F. E. W.

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg confirm the receipt of a letter from the Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen concerning the legal case between Hans Lochner and Hans Ulrich Fehrern. They enclose a copy of the report and petition of their citizens Christoph Tucher and Hans Pfintzstein, who speak for Lochner, and declare themselves ready to provide a counter-response.
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg answer a letter from the Council of St. Gallen regarding the citizen of Nürnberg Hans Kolgrer. He had been instructed to sue the citizen of St. Gallen Hans Ulrich Weysen before the latter's authority. The Nurembergers ask for a reply as soon as Kolgrer has returned, in order to forward his report.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the price of corn and oats has risen due to the influx of foreign merchants. They have issued an ordinance that limits the purchase and export. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to point out this regulation to their citizens who are active in the Schaffhausen markets and to warn them not to overstep, as they would otherwise have to expect punishment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the reply concerning the taxation of Wachs and similar goods. They ask that the people of Appenzell may continue to trade duty-free in St. Gallen in order to maintain the neighborly friendship. Should this not be possible, they will adhere to their own opinion and ask the people of St. Gallen to respect this.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a Confederate day set for 16 February in Baden. This is to take place because of a dispute between the cantons of Schwyz and Glarus over the purchase of grain at the St. Gallen weekly market as well as for other reasons. Zürich asks whether St. Gallen wishes to bring anything forward, and requests acknowledgment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ybbs inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have learned of a new linen fulling mill in St. Gallen, which is praised in Ybbs. They ask that their master craftsman, whom they have sent for this purpose, be allowed to inspect the mill in order to improve their own fulling mills.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, at their request, they had assigned to the citizen of St. Gallen Hans Jörg Precht the inheritances of the deceased Eneas Aegidius Precht claimed by Thomas Stettamen and Lenz Widnführer. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to urge Stettamen and the sick Widnführer to accept the matter, and offer their friendly support.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to reconsider the planned new order of the weavers' guild, according to which weavers of St. Gallen should no longer buy yarn from spinners of Appenzell. They warn of the endangerment of the existence of the poor spinners and request a written answer regarding the state of affairs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Luzern inform Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen that the Luzern Schultheiss Josias Helmlin had learned at the Diet in Baden in Aargau that the Zürich Burgomaster von Cham had reported on unrest in the County of Rotenburg. The Confederates had recalled their envoys, as the unrest had been settled. Luzern thanks them for the St. Gallen embassy and promises to fulfill the Confederate duty.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Luzern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Stadtammann and Council of Veltlin request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have the attached edict publicly proclaimed and posted in St. Gallen. It concerns a court day appointed for all who have claims on the property of the citizen of Veltlin Jergen Beringer, so that they appear on the appointed day.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Karl, Margrave of Baden, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publish a summons issued by his marriage judges to the butcher's apprentice Hans Teschler and to post it in suitable places. He also requests that a document to this effect be issued to the messenger. The summons concerns the complaint of Sabina, daughter of Georg Gewinner of Liebenzell, against Teschler.
en.sender: Karl, Margrave of Baden and Hachberg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Councils and envoys of the Confederation forward to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen a letter from the Burgomaster, Guild Masters and Council of Aarau, which concerns the St. Gallen citizen Hans Linder and his wife. They ask that the letter, together with the attached copies, be handed over to Linder so that he may verify the contents therein.
en.sender: Councils and envoys of the Confederation
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform that their citizen Heinrich Murer has fallen into debt due to poor management and his house has been seized by creditors. They ask St. Gallen to instruct their citizens who have claims against Murer to appear in Zürich on 25 July to assert their claims before the consulting Councils.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the dispute with the Appenzellers of Spycher regarding church attendance and residence. Since the negotiations of 28 August failed, they ask St. Gallen to urge their envoys to give a better answer and to set a new date before Christmas to settle the dispute amicably.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the convening of a Diet of the Confederates on 12. January 1579 in Baden. On this day, the envoys of the cantons, including those of St. Gallen, are to appear regarding the alliance relations with Graubünden and other matters. Zürich asks St. Gallen to instruct its envoys accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the envoy of the Duke of Savoyen at the recent Baden Diet extended the deadline for the release of the Swiss toll by a further year until All Saints' Day. They ask the merchants of St. Gallen to make use of this deadline.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a final oral or written answer in the long-standing dispute over the church attendance and the mooring places of the Appenzellers at the Spicher in St. Gallen. They refer to the position of the Appenzellers, which is based on their letters and seals, and ask for an amicable settlement to avoid future tensions.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rorschach ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizens, who use the Rorschach market for the purchase of grain, to refrain from exchanging good coin for prohibited bad coin. The merchants of St. Gallen exchange coins in Konstanz and bring the bad coin to Rorschach, which harms the market and the city. Rorschach wishes to avoid penalties and asks for neighborly consideration.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg reply to a letter from Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, which concerns the heirs of the deceased Lienhard Henseler, their guardian, as well as Doctor Abraham Mäntzlin and the citizen of Ravensburg Bernhart Henseler. They cannot answer the matter immediately, but will summon Bernhart Henseler to hear his report and then give an answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen concerning an arrest that the Lindau Doctor Abraham Murgel and his brother-in-law Bernhard Haintzler in Ravensburg are supposed to have placed on the assets of the daughter of the deceased Leinhard Haintzler. Murgel denies having placed such an arrest and states that he will appear in St. Gallen in about two weeks to report there.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rottweil request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have their citizens Urban Schwartz, Hans Lander and Jos Lederlin in kind command and to help them, together with their citizen Josua Schwartz, to their trusted money, so that they can feel the benefit of the aforementioned letter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen reply to an inquiry from the St. Gallen town clerk. They confirm that the purchase of houses is customary in Memmingen, and state that the town clerk Ulrich Sporer has been commissioned to report, in his own name, on the state of the grain and wine markets. They ask for suggestions on how these reports could be transmitted weekly and without mistrust.
en.recipient: Caspar Schlumpf, Burgomaster of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen concerning the abandoned daughter of the deceased Chancellor Leonhard Häusler. The citizen of St. Gallen, Doctor Abraham Mergel, and his brother-in-law Bernhard Häusler had been on their way to St. Gallen, but were prevented from doing so by a storm on Lake Constance and flooded bridges in Bregenz. They ask Lindau to answer St. Gallen that they intend to call upon the guardians of the daughter to hand over her property and take over the administration.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg reply to a letter of 21 November 1669 concerning their citizen Bernhard Henseler. He has declared that he has not carried out an arrest. In order to avoid a dispute between the Prelate of St. Gallen and Ravensburg, Henseler and his brother-in-law, Doctor Abraham Mühel, have agreed to render an account to the newly appointed bailiff and to hand over the properties. They ask St. Gallen to accept this.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the introduction of regulations against the pre-purchase of cattle, in particular of calves, in order to lower the high prices. They forbid their citizens the pre-purchase and the resale to other cantons, so that the butchers can slaughter the animals themselves. They ask for consideration of this measure.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rottwil inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have been informed about the inquiry sent by St. Gallen from the two letters of St. Gallen by Melchior Kaufmann. They report on the high inflation, which heavily burdens their poor citizens and subjects as well as the municipal coffers. Since there is no council meeting on the day of the letter, the letter will be dealt with at the next meeting. The answer will be communicated in writing or orally by a citizen of St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rottweil reply to a letter that Melchior Kaufmann had delivered orally. Despite the high prices and the empty granaries, they agree, out of friendship with the Confederates, that St. Gallen can buy two hundred Malter of grain in the Rottweil Kaufhaus.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Anna Maria, Duchess of Württemberg, responds to the request for grain delivery from Württemberg. She communicates that, due to the ongoing price inflation and famine in her principality, she cannot deliver. The Landstände are currently deliberating on the procurement of grain from the Grey Country and other places. Should St. Gallen find grain in the County of Mümpelgart or in Reichenweiler, she will order the delivery there against payment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich transmit to the Council of St. Gallen a copy of the letter of Duchess Anna Maria von Württemberg. She states that, due to the famine in her principality and the ongoing consultations with the Estates of the Land, she cannot supply grain. However, she offers to procure grain in the County of Mümpelgart or the Lordship of Horchweiler for St. Gallen if needed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen reply to a letter of 3 April concerning the Schaffhausen citizen Jacob Schanhowern. They declare that they had known nothing of his marriage to Helena Schowingerin. They have instructed their church officials to reprimand the married couple. Schanhowern has left the city. They forbid their citizen Heinrich Mayer to have dealings with Schanhowern and Schowingerin, and assure that they respect the rights of St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Solothurn answer the inquiry of the St. Gallen citizen Jörg Milling regarding his deceased brother Johann von St. Gallen. They report that he had become a citizen in Solothurn and had died of dropsy in 1570. He had not provided for his brother in his last will, but had only bequeathed something to his sister's daughter Ilsebe. The widow confirms this. The sister's daughter asks for support for her marriage.
en.recipient: Burgomaster, Schöffen and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Erhard Schafhauser, called Irminger, to collect ten gulden from his wife Elisabeth Eggerin. This sum had been bequeathed to him by the deceased sister of the husband, Antonia Zillens. Since the husband has died, Schafhauser wants to collect the money from his wife, who is still alive, and asks for support.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen report on the investigation of the sale of devalued linen from St. Gallen. The Schaffhausen Hans Ziegler has learned that Galli Lingli of Gossau stole the goods from the St. Gallen Blache. The city of Schaffhausen has confiscated the linen and sends a piece as evidence to provide St. Gallen with proof.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Basel answer an inquiry from St. Gallen regarding fruits transferred by the citizens of St. Gallen Ambrosius Schranckenmüller and Jacob Wacker. They report that the two had bought 175 Viernzel of grain in Alltkilch from the Basler Gestiftsschaffner Georg Eckenstein for 4 pounds of Basel coin each. Furthermore, they state that eight Zürich Fiertel correspond to one St. Gallen Viernzel.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Mühlhausen reply to a complaint by St. Gallen regarding the purchase of grain by the citizens of St. Gallen Ambrosius Schirmer and Jacob Wetter. They state that the citizens of St. Gallen had purchased the grain at a price of 62 Sonnenkrone or 6 pounds Stebler per quarter. The high transport costs had, however, wiped out the profit. They praise St. Gallen for its care for the subjects in the difficult time.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter, Regenten und Rat in Oberelsass answer the letter of the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen dated the 18th of the month. They report that they have allowed the St. Gallen citizens Ambrosius Schwarzen and Jakob Platter to purchase a quantity of grain despite the high grain prices and the lack of supplies. They inform that the prices in Wittenheim have been four pounds for a quarter of barley and five pounds for a quarter of wheat and that five half Konstanzer quarters make up a quarter.
en.sender: Statthalter, Regenten und Rat in Oberelsass
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen reply to a letter of 21 May. They regret the execution of Gossauer Gall Kunz for the theft of linen. They report that they have partially recovered the stolen linen, which had been sold in St. Gallen, including 14.5 ells that the wife of Christoph vom Rüdts had bought. However, the bailiff of Rynow refuses to hand it over. Schaffhausen proposes that stolen goods among the Confederates be returned without compensation, and asks for St. Gallen's consent to a corresponding agreement.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report that they have learned from Bern that expelled co-religionists from Besançon are asking for help. They forward drafts of letters to the Governor of Burgundy, the Parliament of Dole, and the city of Besançon, to end the persecution on account of faith. They ask St. Gallen for its opinion on whether the letters should be sent in the name of the Evangelical cantons.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich reply to a letter from St. Gallen concerning an intercession by the city of Bern for the evangelical citizens of Bistanz. They inform that they have returned the transmitted copies to Bern and Schaffhausen. They are willing that Bern submit the intercession in the name of the evangelical cities, but ask that some words in the conclusion be softened. If necessary, the envoys of the evangelical cities could continue negotiations at the next Baden annual account. They recommend that St. Gallen empower their council messenger accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Bailiff, Burgomaster and Council of Horwyl request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send the estate of the deceased citizen of Horwyl, Job Ungeltzer, which is kept in St. Gallen, to the widow and her three children. They request a report on the extent of the estate, so that the widow may receive the usufruct and the children the ownership in accordance with the Württemberg provincial law.
en.sender: Bailiff, Burgomaster and Council of Horwyl
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell reply to the complaint of the butchers of St. Gallen regarding the sale of meat after sworn appraisal. They lament the usury and the distress of the poor, which is exacerbated by such practices. Appenzell has its own sworn appraisers, who may sell the meat according to the appraisal. In the land of Appenzell, however, it is not customary to have appraisers in every hamlet, but the meat is sold according to the parish. They ask for understanding of this practice.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the day of the envoys of the Confederates, scheduled for the Sunday after All Saints' Day, has been moved to the last Sunday of the month of September because of the high price of fruits. They invite the citizens of St. Gallen to participate on this day in Baden im Ergolz at the inn, in order to jointly consult on measures against the high prices.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admit their citizen and master tanner Matheus Salb into their city. They justify this by stating that the tanning trade in Memmingen is overfull, whereas there is a shortage of tanners in St. Gallen. They assure that Salb has hitherto behaved honestly and uprightly, and ask for a favorable answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Caspar Allgäuer, the father of the goldsmith's apprentice Michel Allgäuer, to settle the debts of his son towards the citizens of Zürich Bechinger, Bruner, Oßwald, Nock and Geßinger. The citizens of Zürich had already repeatedly requested the father in writing to make payment, but this had remained unsuccessful.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a Confederate Diet scheduled for 10 February in Baden. They ask to be informed whether St. Gallen has anything to negotiate there, and offer their services.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Hans Christoph Krol. He wishes to sell the properties of his wife in order to invest the money at interest, and to demand back the interest bonds. His brothers-in-law, the citizens of St. Gallen Sigmund and Sebastian Zollikofer, have however placed a seizure and refuse to hand over the bonds. Lindau requests St. Gallen to instruct the Zollikofer to lift the seizure and to hand over the bonds.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen, in which a day for a double Landrat before Easter had been requested. They communicate that they will not hold a Landrat before Easter, as according to their custom only matters referred by the small Council are dealt with before a double Landrat. They can therefore make no reasoned decision. Should urgent matters exist, they set a day for the small Council.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Councils and envoys of the X cantons ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene with Duke Friedrich von Zweibrücken on behalf of the imprisoned Thomas Büttenset. He says that he was arrested for false coinage and sentenced to 5000 gulden. The Confederates request that Councilor Lienhart Keller be instructed to approach the Duke so that Thomas Büttenset may be released from custody and the oath.
en.sender: Councils and envoys of the X cantons
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Katharina Heroltin, widow of the late Johannes Buchenstein von und zu Rummelsberg, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan of 1200 gulden for one to three years against surety and interest. She justifies this by stating that her son Thomas Vautenfer von Sonnenberg, mint master at Rappoltsweiler, was punished and imprisoned by Elector Johann von der Pfalz for minting offenses. She fears further disadvantages if the fine is not paid, and hopes for the help of the city, as her late husband was a citizen there.
en.sender: Katharina Heroltin, widow of the late Johannes Buchenstein von und zu Rummelsberg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the transmission of the testament of the deceased Catharina von Wilerin, widow of the deceased Ulrich Fuchs, as well as for 60 pounds. They inform that the niece Rachel Klenzpergerin has died, but has left behind three living children. Zürich offers to hand over the money to the children so that it is used for their benefit, and asks for confirmation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter from the St. Gallen, concerning the Zollighofer and the Lindau citizen Christoph Kroll. They communicate that Kroll is willing to hear the intended Raitung. They will assign him a person from their circle, as desired. They ask for the designation of a convenient date so that they can make the assignment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Ratsgeber of the city of Augsburg reply to a letter of the 7th of the month, which concerned Ulrich Reich. They say that they had inquired with Veit Holers daughter, Philipp Stuetleber and Hans Holler. Ulrich Reich had presented himself as a Wittiber with good properties, but nothing further had been discussed regarding the marriage. The statements had been taken as joking talk.
en.sender: Ratsgeber of the city of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The bailiff and Council of Bischofszell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizens Jakob and Hans Spindler as well as Johann Stud Zimmermann in asserting an inheritance right to the estate of the deceased woman in Roschach. They present a document stating that grandchildren can inherit under city law, and ask for a favorable and inexpensive handling.
en.sender: The bailiff and Council of Bischofszell
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they had sent their fellow councillor Caspar Bollen to the appointed Diet in the matter of the citizens of St. Gallen Sebastian and Sigmund Halbischofer and the citizen of Lindau Hans Christoph Kölin. He is commissioned to attend the Diet and to do everything that serves the amicable settlement of the matter. They ask that Bollen be given the same trust as to themselves.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report that Hans, the son of the deceased citizen of Lindau Ludwig Ritter, has presented them with the power of attorney of his sister Anna, who lives in Venedig, in order to take over her estate. Since the estate is located in St. Gallen, they ask for consent so that Hans may receive the money.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Wilhelm Graf zu Zimmern asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help him in procuring gold or imperial coins in the value of a thousand or more gulden against three batzen. He asks whether the citizens of St. Gallen could mediate this for him or whether they themselves would be willing to arrange the exchange. He promises to thank them for it.
en.sender: Wilhelm Graf und Herr zu Zimmern
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the Schlumpf heirs, the children of the late Burgomaster Sebastian Schlumpf, in the inheritance matter concerning their aunt Elisabeth Schlumpf. The guardians of the children, Wolf Krinner and Wolf Kramer, have requested an intercession with the Council of the city of St. Gallen so that the children can receive their inheritance.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ludwig Tschudi, Landvogt in Thurgau, replies to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen regarding Barbara Kilchmannin. He explains that he cannot admit the Kilchmannin, as the inheritance law of St. Gallen does not agree with that of Thurgau. He asks the Council not to force the Kilchmannin to her inheritance, but to grant her what is due to her according to equity.
en.sender: Ludwig Tschudi von Glarus, Landvogt in Ober- and Unterthurgau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admit the counsel Joachim Brashperger, whom they have appointed, for their fellow citizen and cannon founder Anton Schmeltz, who must appear before the court on the coming Thursday due to a violation of a regulation from the last fair. They ask for favorable treatment and for the counsel to be heard.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the heirs of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen, Madlena Koblerin, to execute her will. The heirs of St. Gallen had not answered the inquiries of the heirs of the testatrix. Konstanz demands that the citizens of St. Gallen or their representatives appear in Konstanz on 22 November to read and fulfill the will.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter from St. Gallen regarding a Diet against their citizen Hans Hanser, called Rider, and Peter Buben. Since Rider is ill, nothing can be undertaken. They ask the St. Gallen to instruct their citizens to be patient, to keep the deposited mortgage deeds longer as security and to collect the interest from the outstanding principal debt, until the situation changes.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz report that they have received the St. Gallen response to their letter regarding the estate of the deceased Magdalena Kobler. They have summoned the appointed bailiff Hans von Wattensheim and the heirs Hans Jürgen Kobler, who request to be put in possession of the inheritance. A day has been set for 13 December on which the St. Gallen party can present their objections. If they do not come, justice will be granted to the citizens of Konstanz.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter of 19 December concerning their citizen Hans Huser. They announce that Huser, despite the assignment of the interest deeds by the court of St. Gallen, cannot be moved to a settlement with Peter Buben. As they cannot accomplish anything with him, they ask St. Gallen to discuss the matter itself, so that Huser does not suffer damage unjustly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Stadtmann and Council of Feldkirch ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to keep their two Altmänner, Paul Furttenbach and Christoph Bockh, who were placed in arrest due to a debt to the Nuremberg merchants Neronagani, in this arrest. They ask for a written confirmation so that the Altmänner can enjoy the release.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Council of the city of Feldkirch ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have a decree regarding the appointed court day for the creditors of the deceased citizen of Feldkirch, Christa Willis, publicly proclaimed and posted, so that the entitled parties appear and no one can plead ignorance.
en.sender: Ammann and Council of the city of Feldkirch
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The bailiff and officials of the lordships of Bregenz and Hohenegg ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to proceed justly in a legal dispute between their colleague in office, Hans Dietz of Wolfurt, and the St. Gallen citizen Laurenz Kitzinger over a vineyard in Balgach. They request the friendly promotion of the matter so that the poor man may find peace.
en.sender: The bailiff and officials of the lordships of Bregenz and Hohenegg
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ehingen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to read and post a public edict concerning the peremptory court day for the creditor Hans Hueber. They ask that the debtor Hans Vethern and other creditors be informed of the date so that they can appear legally.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Council of the city of Augsburg requests the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to examine the witness Caspar von Schönbüel, residing in St. Gallen, in a legal dispute between Johann Essler as attorney for Hans Huenlin and Hans Weien. Augsburg forwards the bill of complaint and the counter-questions and asks that the witness's testimony be sealed and sent back to Augsburg.
en.sender: Council of the city of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The letter contains only the salutation to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, without further content, sender, or dating.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to settle the matter of their citizen Anton Schlegler, who had appeared before St. Gallen on 6 November 1572. They ask that his scale and weights as well as the outstanding interest be returned to him, as he needs them for the next Whitsun market in St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz point out to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the deceased Magdalena Kobler, a former resident (Hintersasse), died in Konstanz and made her will there. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to have the heirs and guardians of the children of the deceased Bartholomäus Kobler appear before them in Konstanz on 18 May to accept the will or to raise objections. They request a written reply within fourteen days.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Wil request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant free and safe conduct to their countryman and fellow councilor Walther von Roll as well as his brother-in-law, the St. Gallen citizen Jakob Krom. Krom has been imprisoned on account of unfounded accusations and has not been able to defend himself. Wil asks for a friendly reply.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Wangen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the citizens of St. Gallen Tobler and co-relatives to pay the still outstanding 100 gulden for purchased white linen. The Toblers had refused to transfer the amount to the creditors of the deceased factor Simon Kitzschenberg and claimed to have settled the matter with an earlier repayment of a loan to their father. Wangen demands the payment in order to avoid further costs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Ratgeber of Augsburg reply to a letter from St. Gallen concerning Katharina Hofstetterin and the son of Mathes Mandl. They state that they consider the son of Mandl to be illegitimate and do not recognize the marriage with Hofstetterin. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to regulate the maintenance of the legitimate child or to involve Hofstetterin in the maintenance to the extent of one third, and request a reply.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Anna Mamendorferin answers a letter from the Council of St. Gallen to her husband Martin Mamendorfer. She complains about his unfaithfulness and the impoverishment he has caused her and her children. She refuses to take over the common child, as she already has two children from him and he acknowledges the child as his father. She asks the Augsburg authorities not to give the child to her.
en.recipient: City Government, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz refer to the dispute over the testament of the deceased Magdalena Koblerin. They complain that the people of St. Gallen had not observed the appointed date to confirm the testament or to bring forward objections. Since the deceased had resided in Konstanz and died there, the law of that place applies. They request a written answer and offer an amicable settlement.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Council and the envoys of the seven cantons ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to protect the Thurgau Jacob Götz von Hefen in his inheritance right. Götz says that after the death of his wife Barbara Engnerin he received an inheritance share from Katharina Vewillerin in St. Gallen, but that it was taken away from him again because of a legal dispute over the applicable legal order (St. Gallen or Thurgau). The Confederates request that Götz be allowed to keep the share he acquired according to the inheritance law of St. Gallen and that the enjoyment of it not be denied to him.
en.sender: Council and envoys of the seven cantons
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm reply to the letter of 8 June. They confirm that the gunsmith Thomas Schelz from Aistett had cast ten pieces of guns and five Jungstlinge for the armoury. The pieces had been inspected and found to be in good condition. Ulm shares the costs for the manufacture and equipment of the guns and refers to the attached slip.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen ask the bailiff and Council of Bischofszell to confirm and keep in force the testament of the deceased Stoffel Suter. The children of Suter, who are the subsequent heirs, fear that their grandfather's inheritance will be taken away by the mother's current husband or the guardian. St. Gallen supports the children, as they are citizens, and requests Bischofszell to support the guardian and his lord, so that the bequest remains effective.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Bailiff and Council of Bischofszell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publish an edict concerning a court day for the local citizen Daniel Wieland, who has been expelled due to debts, in St. Gallen. The court day is set for 14 August. Lindau requests the proclamation so that the creditors, including the citizens of St. Gallen Caspar Schlumpf and Caspar Herren, appear and cannot plead ignorance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publish the attached edict concerning the appointed court day for the creditors of the deceased citizen of Lindau, Joachim Rorschach, in case it may concern citizens or dependents of St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz request the Statthalter of the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen not to hinder the heirs of the deceased citizen's wife of Konstanz, Magdalena Kobler, in the execution of her testament. They refer to their city law and ask for a written answer. An amicable settlement between the parties is welcome to them.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Statthalter of the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the widow Barbara Strub, née Schalckhen, in her inheritance matter. She has already received 100 gulden from her siblings, but wants a further 900 gulden from the estate of her deceased brother Hans Strub located in St. Gallen. Since her guardian is unavailable, they have commissioned Konrad Hutter and her son Hans Jakob Schalckhen to settle the matter. Schaffhausen asks for a friendly reply and support.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their fellow citizens Quorath Merzholz and Hans Muolr to hand over the 41 gulden and 28 kreuzer owed to the deceased Memmingen citizen Alexander Beßlin immediately to the Memmingen city amman Hans Keller. The debtors have already deposited the money in St. Gallen. Memmingen promises to assist the citizens of St. Gallen in similar cases as well.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Bern inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the arrival of the French envoy Boisrigault. He reports that the King of Frankreich intends to march to Mailand with a great army and to cross the pass on 20 August. He asks the Confederates for help and troops. Bern requests St. Gallen to inform itself and to trust the King, but not the papal intrigues.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz confirm the receipt of a letter along with a counter-report concerning the testament and the estate of the deceased Anna, widow of the deceased Bartholomäus Kobler, as well as the affairs of the widow and children of the deceased Michael Kobler. Since some of those affected are not present, they say that they cannot answer the counter-report immediately. They promise to send an answer upon their arrival.
en.recipient: Statthalter of the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Baden request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have the mother of the St. Gallen citizen Bastian Schlaprecht settle the debt of 50 gulden that her son had incurred with her innkeeper Hans Aberle. They point out that Schlaprecht is a single man and that the mother does not owe the debt, but request amicable payment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Glarus confirm, at the request of the shoemaker Michel Bürgers, that his wife Agatha Landoltin is a woman of Glarus of good repute. They certify that Michel behaved honestly during his stay in Glarus. They ask St. Gallen to treat the couple kindly and not to punish him because he has married a non-St. Gallen woman.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Ratsbeisitzer of the city of Augsburg request the Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen to examine the citizen Johann von Vonwil in the process concerning the inheritance of the deceased Felix Hürlin. They refer to a letter of 10 March and a submitted supplication and ask that the testimony regarding the submitted questions be transmitted.
en.sender: Ratsbeisitzer of the city of Augsburg
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Jakob Strub to pay out the promised 300 gulden from the inheritance of his deceased brother Hans Strub to the widow of Heinrich Schalk, Kümbath Strub. The widow is poor and has only small children. Schaffhausen asks for quick payment without further delay.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain and Council of the city of Konstanz reply to a letter of 8 August regarding the testament of the deceased Magdalena Kobler. They communicate that the parties of St. Gallen are ready to settle the matter amicably. To avoid costs and unrest, they propose an amicable negotiation. They name Johann Montbraten von Spiegelberg, Hans Jacob Egenroth and Christoph Schultheiss as mediators and propose 29 September in Rorschach or Buchhorn as the place and date.
en.sender: Captain and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Statthalter of the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they do not allow dough cakes, Kromer, and similar goods to be publicly sold at their weekly markets and high feast days. They ask the St. Gallen citizens to prevent their potters, vintners, and bakers from trading on these days. For the annual market on 19 September (St. Matthew's Day), the Appenzellers are permitted to attend.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have an edict concerning the appointed court day for the citizen Jakob Hager of St. Gallen published and posted in suitable places, so that no one may claim ignorance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ulrich Graf zu Montfort und Rotenfels informs that his subject and citizen of Tettnang, Melcher Tischmacher, intends to have some Büchsen cast and fitted. He asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help his subject with this work as a priority and to promote him, so that he may profit from the prescribed work.
en.sender: Ulrich Graf zu Montfort und Rotenfels
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Henry, King of Poland, informs the Confederates of his departure for Poland and thanks them for the support by Swiss mercenaries in the Polish succession war. He offers his friendship and asks for the maintenance of the good relations with the Crown of Frankreich. In a postscript, he mentions that he met the French envoy Belliere, who reported to him on the good attitude of the Confederates, and instructs him to confirm the friendship.
en.recipient: Communities and Councils of St. Gallen

en.regest: Bellievre informs that he is leaving the kingdom and traveling to Poland. He regrets having had little opportunity so far to reciprocate the kindness and favor shown to him, but assures them of his sincere gratitude and friendship. Since the King has assured him that he will not keep him in Poland for long, he hopes to find the opportunity in the future to render loyal service. He commends himself to their grace and wishes them health and a long life.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Karl IX. von Frankreich thanks the Councils and Communities of St. Gallen for the military assistance rendered and the loyalty of his troops. He assures them of his friendly disposition and asks for the maintenance of good relations. His envoy, the Herr von Hautefort, delivers the words of thanks and will soon return.
en.recipient: Councils and Communities of St. Gallen

en.regest: Bellievre informs that, on the order of the King of Frankreich, he is riding to him. He reports that the Queen and the Duke of Alençon highly value the friendship with the Confederates and rejoice in their well-being. He conveys the King's oral words of thanks for the support thus far. Furthermore, he assures, in the name of the two Queens and the Duke of Alençon, that in times of need faithful help will always be provided. He recommends himself and his brother, who is also writing.
en.recipient: Großmächtige Herren

en.regest: The Statthalter and Council of the city of St. Gallen ask the ambassador in the Confederation to instruct the Governor in Lyon not to hand over the 6000 francs demanded by the heirs of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen, Hans Spindler, to the creditors, but to deposit them with an impartial person or the Governor, until the pending appeal is decided.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the city of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Herr von Hottenfort, imperial councillor, President in the Dauphiné and ambassador in the Confederation in Solothurn

en.regest: The administrator of the captaincy, the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz reply to a letter from the Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen. It concerns 300 Kronen, which Captain Jacob Studer is supposed to have borrowed from the deceased citizen of Konstanz, Basion Bischoff, at unreasonable interest. Hans Hahnborg, bailiff and brother of the widow of Bischoff, who was questioned by Konstanz, denies that Bischoff or his widow had lent money to Studer or other people of St. Gallen. Bischoff had merely lent 500 gulden to the two wine servers of Bischofszell, without the surety of Studer.
en.sender: The administrator of the captaincy, the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hear with goodwill and give credit to their council friend Joachim Unfried, who conveys a friendly solicitation on behalf of the citizen of Lindau Hans Hauser. They promise to serve St. Gallen in similar cases as neighbors.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The administrator of the captaincy, the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to accommodate their town bailiff Hans Jakob Sponholtz in a claim against the St. Gallen citizens Laurentz, Jörg and Lienhart Zöllikofers. The Zöllikofers have not yielded to the town bailiff so far. The city of Konstanz appoints the nobles Hans von Mundelsheim and Nicolaus de Gall as assistants and asks for an amicable settlement, as it concerns a marriage matter.
en.sender: The administrator of the captaincy, the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Statthalter and Council of Schaffhausen decline the request of St. Gallen to have their councilor Hans Konrad Meier act in the appeal case between Benedikt Isolinis and the heirs of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen, Hans Strub, before the Parisian Parliament. They justify this with the necessity of retaining Meier for the city of Schaffhausen, as well as with the endangerment of the Christian religion in Frankreich. They ask that the refusal be received in the best sense.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Hans Dennerer to honor a purchase contract for twenty fuder of wine concluded on 18 February with the Überlingen citizen Hans Ynder. Dennerer had confirmed the purchase and promised payment by Easter as well as delivery, but now wishes to extricate himself from it due to illness. Überlingen requests that Dennerer be compelled to fulfill the contract, otherwise they will proceed legally.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to examine their fellow councillor Felix Schürff in an inheritance matter. Schürff claims the estate of his deceased cousin Barbara Schürffin as the next heir. The citizen of St. Gallen Marx Müller, innkeeper at the Fotten Ochsen, had often visited the deceased and heard his statement that Schürff was the heir. The Zürich side asks for a written answer regarding Müller's statement.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the convocation of a Diet of the Confederation on Sunday Cantate, 9 May, in Baden. This Diet serves the amicable settlement of the dispute between the Eight Old Cantons and Schaffhausen. The Zürichers ask the St. Galleners to behave accordingly and offer their services.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen, which demands the unopened passage of goods from the Frankfurt Fair for its citizens and merchants. Überlingen refuses this, as the St. Gallen merchants had not presented credible documents from the appointed commissioners, as required by the Imperial Resolutions and Mandates. They ask that this refusal not be interpreted as unfriendly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen concerning the citizen of St. Gallen Jörg Melling. They thank them for the information that Melling is to be considered before other creditors in the satisfaction of his creditors, and declare themselves willing to do the same in this regard. However, they refer to outstanding claims of their citizens Dachsen and Schmerer against the citizen of St. Gallen Salomon Locher, as well as to a bond of the Morellen to the citizen of St. Gallen Lisch. They ask for further information on the status of these cases.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ludwig Tschudi, Landvogt of Ober- and Unterthurgau, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to appoint a guardian for the child left behind by David Gütenson von Sonnenberg, if it does not yet have a guardian. The guardian is to bring the child to court at Frauenfeld on the next Monday morning, in order to answer the claim of the Jew Marx there.
