en.sender: Ludwig Tschudi von Glarus, Landvogt of Ober- and Unterthurgau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Hans Donnerer to honor the wine purchase concluded with their citizen Hans Mader or to set a final court day. Mader has hitherto waited for the fulfillment of the contract, as Donnerer had not appeared. Überlingen asks for mutual support in similar cases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen remind Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of their letter of 22 March concerning a wine purchase by their citizen Hans Madres against the fellow citizen of St. Gallen Hans Wenderer. Since they had not yet received an answer and their citizen asks for help in settling the dispute, they again request the St. Gallen authorities to inform them how Wenderer intends to behave.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich hand over to the envoys of the thirteen cantons the letters of credence and the instruction of the envoy of the Prince of Condé, as the Baden Diet had ended before his arrival. They ask for the examination of the proposals contained therein for peace in Frankreich and propose a joint Confederate Diet for the consultation of suitable means.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Envoys of the thirteen cantons of the Confederation

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about a letter from the three Grey Leagues, which describes three types of false Kronen. They warn the St. Gallen, who are endangered because of their large gold and silver trade, and send a copy of the letter. Furthermore, they report that Josua von Salis and a «der Carlin» were active in Zürich under the pretext of alchemy, but after the fraud was discovered, they had to leave the city.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landsammann and Council of Appenzell reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen. They assure that the delay of the conference is not motivated by neighborly considerations, and promise to determine the place and day for a meeting after the Diet at Baden. Furthermore, they report that they had forbidden throughout the land that foreign salt merchants sell salt; this may only be sold to their own citizens and to the St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about the convening of a Diet of the Confederates in Baden on 8 August 1574. There, Bern, Basel, Schaffhausen, and Zürich decided to send envoys to the French king to end the shedding of blood in Frankreich. The other cantons wanted to give notice only on 17 August. Zürich asks St. Gallen whether it also wishes to send envoys and requests an answer.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Arbon inform Josua Kessler, town clerk of St. Gallen, about the departure of the Kuebler. They ask for the return of the transmitted missive and state that they will let the matter rest for the time being.
en.recipient: Josua Kessler, town clerk of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Frankfurt ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizen Paulus Baldenburger, saddler, in the inheritance of his deceased brother, Doctor Jacob Baldenburger. They request lenient treatment regarding the succession tax and a swift settlement of the inheritance without a protracted process.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to read and post an edict regarding the appointed court day for the creditors of the citizen of Ravensburg Matthes Reichen and his wife Anna Oeßerin, so that the creditors in St. Gallen can assert their claims.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lützelkirch request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publish and beat a public edict in the city. Therein, the creditors of the deceased citizen and dyer of Lützelkirch, Benedikt Züchelin, are called upon to appear before the Council of Lützelkirch on 10 February to assert their claims.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to give preference to their citizen Peter Füßli, the bell founder, over others in the casting of two new bells. They refer to his good work and his humble request to complete the work.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a dispute between their citizen Michel Huldin, as bailiff of the widow Regula Schwytzerin, and the citizen of St. Gallen Lienhart Widerkehr. Widerkehr says that he has taken over the property of the Schwytzerin for 1200 gulden, but is of the opinion that the Schwytzerin and her children may not move out without prior release. Zürich has confirmed in writing to Widerkehr that the law of the city of St. Gallen applies, and asks for mutual support.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about an agreement with the Landvogt in the Rintal and the Lord of St. Gallen. This states that each party is to warn its subjects on the Kienmünze whether they accept foreign coins or not. Appenzell has issued a proclamation that the small coin (16 to 1 batzen) prohibited by Lindau is not to be taken or given out at a higher price. Appenzell points out that citizens of St. Gallen claim that Appenzell has prohibited the coin, which is false. Appenzell asks St. Gallen to note this.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to detain the furrier Hans Jakob Krantz, who expects a penalty in Konstanz for misconduct. Krantz had fled after his arrest. The St. Gallen authorities are to persuade him or his relatives to present themselves in Konstanz and serve the penalty, otherwise damage to his trade is threatened.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz thank for the information that the deceased Barbara Zecochin has left an estate in St. Gallen, to which her grandson Michael Schuler has a claim as heir. They ask the authorities of St. Gallen to help the two appointed guardians of the boy, Michael Schumacher and Jakob Schuler, in taking possession of the estate, so that it can be paid out to the minor with minimal costs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to persuade their citizen Jerolmus Weyen to pay the amount stipulated in the written instrument to the citizen of Nürnberg Hans Winckler. Winckler has asserted this claim against Weyen. Nürnberg offers to serve Weyen in similar cases in the future.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Council of Feldkirch ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the creditors of the St. Gallen citizen Jacob Kaga to lift the arrest on twelve pieces of linen. Kaga had purchased the goods on behalf of the Feldkirch citizen Jacob Zoller and handed them over to the latter upon his dismissal as factor. The goods therefore belong to Zoller, not Kaga.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizen Heinrich Scherl in the collection of a claim of 1000 gulden plus interest against the citizens of St. Gallen Ambrosius and Jacob Aigen. Scherl says that he lent the money on credit and is secured by a bond. Since the debt has priority according to old custom, the Nurembergers ask for support in the enforcement.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Masters and Council of Straßburg request the Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the widow and heirs of the Zollikofer to settle with the widow and children of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen, Anton de Faure, over 2000 Kronen plus interest. The sum was invested under the name of the Zollikofer and paid out to them as their own property. Straßburg refers to earlier correspondence and requests an amicable settlement of the dispute.
en.sender: The Masters and Council of Straßburg
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: De Fleury asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for their good will regarding the affairs of Herr Faulbach. He mentions that he feels obliged to them and hopes that they will be helpful to him in this matter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Councils and envoys of the thirteen cantons at Baden to abolish the tolls in Löwen, which violate the perpetual peace. They refer to the fact that Imperial Majesty has handed the matter over to the Confederates. St. Gallen has sent Doctor Melchior Rötmund as an envoy to Löwen to represent the interests of the merchants. The St. Gallen ask the Confederates to support the envoy and to put an end to the complaints of the merchants.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Councils and envoys of the thirteen cantons at Baden

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Freiburg reply to a letter from the citizens of St. Gallen, who had asked them to support the heirs of the deceased Hans Trübner in a claim against some citizens of Lyon and to send Schultheiss Seiler to Lyon. Freiburg declares itself in principle willing, but cannot dispatch the Schultheiss for important reasons. They promise to work towards an amicable settlement at the next Baden court day.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Freiburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inquire with their weighmaster whether citizens of St. Gallen transport large Mengen of lard over the St. Gallen Weighbridge Square and sell it to places other than the market residents of St. Gallen. They demand a written report on the violations of the Appenzell statute found, in order to be able to punish the offenders.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that some Appenzell lard merchants sell their lard in places that are not useful for St. Gallen. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to create an order with their wagon master to prevent smuggling over the Berg and to punish the merchants. Appenzell will in turn proceed against the smugglers.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Brugg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information regarding the estate of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Ulrich Künckler. His widow Magdalena Hübler and her four children, who are growing up in Brugg, are in need. The people of Brugg ask to be informed whether the children are entitled to anything, and offer to send a messenger.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the harvest had turned out poorly and that they wanted to keep prices low. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to warn their citizens so that they do not come to the Schaffhausen market and drive prices up. Schaffhausen will only allow the St. Gallen citizens to buy according to its own granary regulations, otherwise not without punishment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Christoph von Lör and his co-heirs, including Petronella Otten, in the inheritance of their deceased sister Elisabeth von Lör. They request support so that the community of heirs can take possession of the inheritance at low cost.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they are cancelling the annual market after the Konradstag this year due to moving causes. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to inform their citizens of this, so that they do not incur unnecessary costs for visiting the market.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report that the deceased Magdalena Varnbuechlerin left a testament, which they have opened. Since legacies are bequeathed to the family of the deceased Agatha Rütlingerin, they ask St. Gallen to clarify the absence of the children, to deliver a copy of the testament to the guardians, and to inform them in writing whether the heirs raise objections or accept the legacies.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Barbara Moeschli, the sister of the deceased St. Gallen Webers Konrad Moesch, in the inheritance. Since Konrad left no closer heirs, Barbara, as the sister, is the next heir. Appenzell has assigned the court clerk Hans Müller as her assistant and asks St. Gallen to support Barbara and her assistant in the division of the inheritance with the spouse of the deceased.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Heinrich Toman, Landvogt in Ober- and Unterthurgau, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admit his subject Simon Harder, tailor, as a citizen. Harder wishes to settle in St. Gallen and has hitherto behaved honestly. Toman assures that Harder will conduct himself well in the future, and asks for a favorable answer.
en.sender: Heinrich Toman, Landvogt in Ober- and Unterthurgau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen not to allow the creditors of Hans Hiltbrander and his wife to seize or sell the property of the Hiltbrander wife located in St. Gallen. The creditors should only seize the property of the Hiltbrander wife located in Zürich, which they could use for the debt. The Zürich side asks for a written answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell confirm the receipt of a reply from Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen regarding a dispute between Büchsenmachern and the Appenzell Ammann Badman. They declare themselves in agreement with the St. Gallen position and ask for friendly dealings. If the young Zwifel cannot clarify the matter, they refer to earlier letters. They let the matter rest for the time being, in the hope of a soon amicable settlement.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau remind Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of their letter of 28 November 1675. They ask that the citizens of St. Gallen be instructed to declare by next Thursday whether they wish to accept or contest the aforementioned testament. Since the other co-heirs would have accepted the testament, the appointed heirs would otherwise have to be installed immediately.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg reply to the letter of the Council of St. Gallen regarding Hans Kempher, referred to as Endres Glaser. They inquired with his wife, who was still staying in Nürnberg. Since she did not know whether her husband was still alive and had already remarried, she was expelled from the city. Nürnberg wishes to support St. Gallen in proceeding against Kempher.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz reply to an inquiry from the Council of St. Gallen regarding the grandson of Sebastian Wander. They state that neither the child nor its mother had ever received the citizenship of St. Gallen. The child, father Jacob Appenzeller, was placed in the hospital of Konstanz after having been abandoned by the parents. Wander offered the hospital a bond of interest, which the wardens rejected. The child was returned to Wander, who is now to bear the cost of its maintenance.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen, which, following an agreement between the surrounding cities and their hatters, had asked that no foreign hatters be admitted to the weekly markets any longer. Konstanz declares that it knows nothing of such an agreement and has not concluded one of its own either. It allows foreign hatters free access to the market. Regarding the claim that no Konstanzer hatter has recently visited the St. Gallen market, it cannot confirm this. It is ready to continue to admit St. Gallen hatters if the Konstanzer are admitted in St. Gallen. In a postscript, it again asks for a reply to an earlier letter regarding the grandson of the St. Gallen citizen Sebastian Herder, who was in the Konstanzer hospital for the poor.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau hand over to the children of the deceased citizen of Lindau, Aatha Riedlinger, three annuity deeds from the estate of their aunt Magdalena Varnbüler. They ask St. Gallen to hand over these deeds, together with the remaining balance of nine gulden, four pfennig and four denars, after deduction of thirty gulden, against receipt.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The King of Frankreich warns the Confederates against the Duke of Savoyen, who is seeking an alliance with them that would contradict the eternal peace and the existing alliance with Frankreich. He asserts that such aid to Savoyen would be directed against Frankreich, as the King has a claim to the Duke's territories. He asks that his envoy Hautefort be given credence, and assures his friendship.
en.recipient: Burgomasters, Schultheissen, Ammann, Council and Communities of the thirteen cantons of the old alliance in the high German lands

en.regest: King Heinrich von Frankreich asks the Confederates for financial support, as the war costs would have exhausted his finances. He promises to repay the sum and asks for trust in his envoy, Herr von Hautefort, who would explain the matter in more detail.
en.sender: Heinrich, König in Frankreich und Polen
en.recipient: Confederate cantons

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern ask the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen to help their citizen Hans Jakob Steinegger, letter writer, in the collection of an inheritance. This had fallen to his wife Agnes Dietrich from Balthasar Enoch, a member of the St. Gallen. Bern asks for favorable and swift support so that Steinegger may raise the property without great effort.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: De Bellievre reports to the envoys to Solothurn that the young Lord Balthasar von Grissach has returned by order of the King of Frankreich. He communicates that the peace has been concluded and was published in the camps of the Duke and the Prince of Condé as well as in the Parliament and in the city of Paris between 5 and 9 May. He promises to transmit further details as soon as he has received letters from the King.
en.recipient: Envoys to Solothurn

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rottweil ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel their fellow citizen Nazareno Krüner to settle the still outstanding 42 gulden and 40 kreuzer for the purchase of fruits, as he had promised.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to exert influence on their citizen Endris Gullendretter so that he pays the debt judicially awarded to the Ulm saddler Jörg Herdtegen without further delay.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Bellièvre presents to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen letters from the King of Frankreich and asks for support in his distress. He praises the King's gratitude for the financial assistance of the citizens of St. Gallen Zollikoffer and Lyner to the dismissed officers in Lyon. He asks to persuade Zollikoffer and Lyner to grant the officers a respite of five to six months, as the King owes them larger sums and they are to be served from the first payments.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Wattwil inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have taken into custody Jacob Hamer of Wingarten, who is active as a coachman, for theft and made him confess under torture, among other things, to having stolen 80 gulden from Jakob Zilli. As they wish to verify the truth of his statements, they ask the citizens of St. Gallen to question the affected citizens and to report to them in writing.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Nicolaus de Gall the Younger in a legal dispute against the heirs of the deceased Michael Kobler. It concerns 300 gulden bequeathed to the plaintiff by the testator. The defendants dispute the claim and assert that it was waived in a contract. The plaintiff has already submitted a debt acknowledgment and asks for the removal of the burden of proof imposed on him as well as for the payment of the sum.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the Small Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Elector August asks the Schultheiss and Council of St. Gallen to help his armourer Erhardt Ammon and his father Paul Puchner in the collection of 500 Kronen. The money had been handed over to the merchant Niclas Medersachen in St. Gallen for forwarding to Nürnberg, who, however, is said to have become insolvent and fled. The Elector requests support in the pursuit of the debts of Medersachen and his family.
en.sender: August, Duke of Sachsen, Elector and Burggrave of Magdeburg
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich congratulate Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on the new year and inform them that they had received a letter from Wilhelm von Oranien, in which he reports on the peace in the Netherlands and the events in Antwerpen. They ask for a reply.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Council of the city of Augsburg asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to earnestly urge their fellow citizen Melchior Hueber to settle the outstanding debt of 16 florins to the Augsburg goldsmith Martin Feitel. Feitel has not received the payment despite repeated reminders and promises.
en.sender: Council of the city of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Konstanz informs St. Gallen of the statements of the witnesses Hanns Guldin, Melcher Keßler and Martin Sautter. They report on a dispute between the St. Gallen citizen Hans Donderer and a nobleman of Reischach in Allensbach. The witnesses describe that the two, while drunk, argued about military service, the acquisition of grain by the Archduke, and salt. The nobleman had drawn a knife, and the two had agreed to a fight the next day. However, Donderer had departed early. Othmar Kuster could not testify.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell warn the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that citizens of St. Gallen are acquiring properties against the Appenzell land statutes. They ask that the citizens of St. Gallen be kept from buying goods without the consent of Appenzell. Furthermore, they demand the repayment of 30 gulden, which Konrad Gmünder of St. Gallen had claimed from their Seckelmeister for a Salome Fudlerin lodged in St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Councils of the city of Augsburg ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to deal with their citizen Melchior Hutter, so that he pays their citizen Martin Prechtel, goldsmith, beyond his long-standing patience and reminders, and makes him unclaimable. Prechtel had turned to the Augsburg Councils, who now ask for support.
en.sender: Councils of the city of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Ammann, Burgomaster and Council of Markdorf request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the cutler Hans Vogler to hand over the promised 50 gulden to his stepdaughter Magdalena Sprangerin. They submit witness testimonies according to which Vogler and his deceased wife had promised the money to the woman. They ask that Vogler be made to issue the woman with an unassailable certificate.
en.sender: The Ammann, Burgomaster and Council of Markdorf
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Jörg Spranger in taking possession of an inheritance. This had fallen to him from his deceased sister, the St. Gallen woman Brigitta Sprangerin. Spranger had appointed his brother-in-law Kaspar Buchelmann as his proxy. The people of Konstanz point out that in cases of inheritance among siblings they only take the tenth penny as a deduction, and ask for favorable treatment.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to strictly urge their citizens Caspar Scherer and Sebastian Spindler to pay the Memmingers Melchior Funck, Joseph Lochner and Ursula Welchenbergin the outstanding balance of 150 gulden 32 kreuzer 3 heller in linen debts. The debtors had committed to sending the money to the Memmingen weighmaster, but not to the deceased Kisten or his estate.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Nikolaus de Gall the Younger in a legal dispute with the heirs of the family Kobler. They refer to an earlier letter of 28 September 1576 and ask for a quick decision so that the dispute can be settled. They send a copy of the earlier letter with it.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Zoffingen ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant the son of the deceased citizens Heinrich Schalttenbrand and Magdalena König the withdrawal of temporal goods in St. Gallen. They refer to the fact that in Zoffingen a withdrawal of one mark of silver is due for non-citizens, which is reduced in the case of small property. They hope for a friendly treatment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Condensation of the Royal Letter of 16 July 1577, which concerns the peace concluded with the King of Navarra.

Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg answer the second inquiry of St. Gallen regarding the widow of the deceased Lienhard Straub. They say that they had presented the charges to the accused citizen of Nürnberg, Conrad Voger, and his attorney Georg Rießerberger, and received reports. Since the matter rests on a good account and settlement, they say that they had instructed Voger and Rießerberger to carry out the accounting urgently. Should an amicable settlement not be possible, ordinary justice is to be sought at the Bauhandelsgericht, where each person is helped to fair assistance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Councils of the city of Augsburg request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to pay their citizen Martin Bescher. He says that he has submitted a supplication, as he has waited a long time for his claim against the St. Gallen citizen Melchior Fuescher. Augsburg requests St. Gallen to pay Bescher earnestly, so that he is not further chased about or led into unnecessary costs.
en.sender: Councils of the city of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ingolstadt reply to a letter from St. Gallen concerning the deceased citizen Anton Knecht and his stepson Hans Baptist Knecht. The latter says that he had engaged himself to the maiden Wibratha without the knowledge of his stepfather, his mother, and the guardians. Ingolstadt says that it had punished him for this and ordered him to travel to St. Gallen to settle the matter with Wibratha. They ask St. Gallen, if Knecht appears there, to handle the marriage case according to local custom.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a Diet of the Confederates on 12. January 1478 in Baden. This Diet was convened to discuss two disputed matters with Bern, Basel and the merchants. The Zürichers ask the St. Galleners to behave and act accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform their citizen Melchior Rothmund about a court day appointed for the creditors of the deceased citizen of Konstanz, Hans Dächinger. They also ask that the open edict be posted and proclaimed at the usual places, so that no one sees his right curtailed.
en.sender: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Kasimir, Pfalzgraf bei Rhein, Herzog in Bayern, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the church and school servants as well as students who were dismissed by him and who were dismissed because of their confession. He asks that the aid be distributed in an orderly and modest manner so that it benefits those in need, and promises that he will repay them for it.
en.sender: Johann Kasimir, Pfalzgraf bei Rhein, Herzog in Bayern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Leutkirch ask St. Gallen to help the widow Barbara Costanerin in the collection of a debt freed from Hans von Watt. They demand that her claim be considered before other creditors. Furthermore, they ask for clarification on which persons are to conduct the amicable settlement appointed for 12 January, and for information on how St. Gallen treats trusted property in such cases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Reinhard, Pfalzgraf bei Rhein und Herzog in Bayern, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the death of the mint master Jacob Merckh, who had been in the service of the city for eight years. Since Merckh has not rendered an account of his mint work and a considerable sum is to be settled, the Pfalzgraf asks that the estate of the deceased be inventoried and left unchanged until further notice. He demands a copy of the inventory and inquires about the succession.
en.sender: Reinhard, Pfalzgraf bei Rhein und Herzog in Bayern
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Leutkirch ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to postpone the court day scheduled for 27 January regarding the estate of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen, Hug von Watt. The creditors of Leutkirch had not been able to meet the deadline due to the short notice period. They request a written answer as to whether the court day is postponed or a new date is set.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to cancel the court day scheduled for 27 January regarding the claims of Memmingen council friend Hans Waldner against the citizen of St. Gallen Hugo von Watt, and to set a new, timely announced date, as the summons arrived only on the day itself. They also request timely announcement when the money of the citizen of St. Gallen Niclaus Wolnisaat in Genf is dealt with, so that the citizen of Memmingen Veithus Schwartz, who is surety for Wolnisaat, can safeguard his rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inquire with the officials of the hospital which persons from the Appenzell region had stayed in the hospital in St. Gallen and had died there within the last three or four weeks. They ask for a written answer so that they may conduct themselves appropriately towards the deceased.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Neuenburg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the widow of the deceased Hans Bindemann, now the wife of Thomas Sigli, to pay the outstanding debt of 411 Kronen and 12 kreuzer to their citizen Stefan In der Fehr or his authorized representative.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter from St. Gallen concerning the citizen Jacob Öler there, who was a baker's apprentice in Lindau. They say that they had inquired after him but had not been able to find him. His father Konrad Öler had stated that the son had shown himself a few days ago but had departed again the next day. His whereabouts are unknown. Had he been found, they would have dealt with him according to the law of St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau send, upon request, a copy of their goldsmiths' ordinance. They inform that on the same day they have decided on an amendment: goldsmiths may no longer stamp their works themselves. Instead, works of four Lot or more must be inspected by appointed assayers before delivery. At a fineness of 13 1/2 Lot, the town seal is stamped.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of new news from Basel and ask for reciprocity in the forwarding of information. They warn of a threatening danger from a coalition of the Pope, the Emperor, the King of Spanien and other princes, who under the pretext of the Dutch war are gathering troops in Burgundy and on the borders of the Confederation. These powers planned to raid the evangelical cantons of the Confederation and to enforce the Tridentinum. Zürich urgently recommends securing the cities and lands and remaining vigilant.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz send to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the renewed Goldsmiths' Ordinance of the year 1466, as they had requested in their latest letter.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Wendel Pfyffer, Landvogt in Thurgau, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to pay the promised interest to Jacob Vogel of Altnau for a mill he purchased and to return the principal upon redemption. Vogel received the mill from the St. Gallen as a fief and resold it multiple times. Pfyffer threatens to assist officially if this is not observed and asks for a written answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their fellow councilor Hans Waldner in the legal dispute with the dismissed citizen of St. Gallen Georg von Wadt. Waldner has 1547 gulden as trusted property, not as a loan, with von Wadt. Memmingen requests that Waldner be treated like the citizens of St. Gallen and that payment be procured for him.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the danger of a war breaking out. They report that Count Hannibal von Ems intends to hold a muster near Stockach and to recruit two regiments of recruits. They ask for advice on how they should behave and recommend convening a meeting of the Confederates to counter the war effort.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Anton Zöller, acting Ammann of the city, and the judges and verdict speakers of the city court of Lindau inform St. Gallen that, at the request of Rudolf Dietzi from Reinegg, they have examined the witness Wendel Falchen of Lindau. Dietzi had presented a sealed compass letter in which he pursues an undecided right against Gebhard Böschen the Elder, citizen of St. Gallen. The judges of Lindau questioned the witness under oath and recorded the statements in writing. They send the result to St. Gallen.
en.sender: Anton Zöller, acting Ammann of the city, and the judges and verdict speakers of the city court of Lindau
en.recipient: Melchior Reiner, city Ammann, and the judges and verdict speakers of the city court of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Tachau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to issue a new birth certificate to their fellow citizen Nathanael Oberhaeuser, who lost his birth certificate in a city fire on 6 May 1587. They confirm the loss and ask that Oberhaeuser be supported favorably in this and other matters.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg answer the petition of the St. Gallen citizen Rudolf Mundprat against the Nürnberg citizen Hans Roter. Since Roter could not be found and his wife could not indicate his whereabouts, the matter had remained pending for the time being. Mundprat is to observe Roter after his return. In the event of a further petition, justice will be administered.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their Ratvogt Hans Jakob Atzenholz with his claims against the citizens of St. Gallen Lienhart, Lorenz and Jörg Zölligkauer. Atzenholz wishes to demand something on account of his son, who had served the Zölligkauers. The people of Konstanz ask that the citizens of St. Gallen be moved to accede to Atzenholz in his rightful request.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Landammann and Council of Appenzell whether anyone wishes to bring a charge against their prisoner, who had been involved in a crime against Appenzellers in Rüth. As they had not yet received an answer and the perpetrator had left the territory, they were still holding the prisoner. If no one brought a charge, they would release him as innocent.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich answer an inquiry from St. Gallen. They report that the Zürcher Bad Hans Rudolf Suri married the St. Gallen woman Maria Kupferschmidin three years ago, on the condition that he would wait four years. Since Suri has involved himself with another woman, Maria wishes for a divorce. Suri agrees with this and wants to declare the marital promise void.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Joch, Landvogt zu Vry, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant Jacob Vogel and his mother the interest on a water mill. The mill was pledged as security for a debt of 1200 pounds. The citizens of St. Gallen had stopped the interest because the last holder had neglected his fiefs. The Landvogt refers to a previous oral promise by the envoys of St. Gallen and asks for an answer to avoid further disputes.
en.sender: Hans Joch, Landvogt zu Vry in Ober- und Unterthurgau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the papal envoy Felicianus, Bishop of N., has come to Konstanz. They suspect that he is working against the Council of Trient and the Reformed religion. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to pay attention to the envoy's intentions and to inform them of his activities.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the report on the papal legation and the clerical people in the church. They ask for further inquiries into which orders the legation carried, and promise to do everything necessary to prevent harmful practices and to preserve the peace.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Ratsgeber of the city of Augsburg ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to deal with the St. Gallen citizen Jacob Egen so that he immediately pays the outstanding dower of 18 pounds to his citizen Anna Jaisers, widow of the deceased Caspar Jaiser, and secures the future payments. The request is made on the basis of an accompanying supplication by Anna Jaisers.
en.sender: Ratsgeber of the city of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about the amicable settlement with Appenzell through the Abbot of St. Gallen. They ask St. Gallen to ask Appenzell to drop the displeasure over the informal signing of the territorial coat of arms by a St. Gallen glass painter and printer. Both sides are to inform the respective authority in case of disputes, in order to maintain good neighborly relations.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform the Council of St. Gallen about the imprisoned Jacob Perler, who has confessed to having stolen a piece of linen cloth from the St. Gallen Blache. The cloth was found in the stream and handed over to the bailiff of Rorschach. Perler has acknowledged further thefts but has not confessed to any others. The people of Konstanz ask St. Gallen to examine to whom the cloth belonged.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the warning regarding Dutch thaler and request mutual information. They promise to be helpful in the complaint of Jacob Vogel von Altnau against two citizens of St. Gallen. Since the claims of Vogel are unclear, they recommend sending an envoy to the Landvogt in Frauenfeld to clarify the matter and to protect the citizens of St. Gallen from being summoned before a foreign authority.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a Diet of the Confederates, which was convened on 15 November in Baden im Aargau. The occasion is the movements of the French war troops on the borders of Burgundy and Alsace. The Zürichers ask the St. Galleners to join the Diet, if they had anything to negotiate.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Ulrich Philipsen, Freiherr von Hohen-Sax, for help so that his subject Andres Ortner pays the St. Gallen citizen Hans Schlapparici 35 florins plus costs and damage. Ortner had already promised the sum by handshake years ago but did not settle it. The Council asks him to compel Ortner to pay.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Ulrich Philipsen, Freiherr von Hohen-Sax

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they were commissioned at the recent Baden Diet to examine and appraise various foreign thaler. They have had about 40 types examined and send a statement, so that St. Gallen can use it as it pleases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell reply to the letter of St. Gallen regarding the release of the lordship of Bürglen. They note the absence of a specification of the outstanding interest and ask for clarification. Furthermore, they remind them of the contracts with the Abbot of St. Gallen, according to which the properties of St. Gallen located in Appenzell are also to be taken into consideration, and demand their observance. Finally, they report that they had prohibited Holz that the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Jerg Engler had sold to St. Gallen, as it was to be transported through Wald and crops with many horses, which would harm the Appenzellers.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen. They state that they will accept the surrender of the lordship of Bürgen only after payment of the outstanding interest. Regarding the timber sold by Iheri Zingler, they point out that he had renounced the land law without their consent and therefore may not dispose of his property without their will. They offer to inform the buyers of the conditions for the timber supply and ask for neighborly consideration during the three winter months.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their Confederate Hans Jörg Appenzeller to enforce the judgment of 20 September 1579. Appenzeller owes the widow Anna Henßlerin 15 gulden for costs and claims. The sum is due, as the agreed payment deadline has expired. Zürich asks for payment without further delay.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admit the goldsmith Hans Jakob Pellican, son of the deceased Samuel Pellican, into their citizenship. Pellican wishes to settle in St. Gallen, as his craft is strongly competed in Zürich. Zürich requests benevolent treatment of Pellican and his family.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Jauch, Landvogt in Ober- und Niderturgau, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he has permitted the examination of witnesses requested by Jakob Weggen of Altnau in a legal dispute between Weggen and St. Gallen. He says that he has examined the witnesses and handed their statements over to the Confederate councilor in Baden, where St. Gallen may present its plea.
en.sender: Hans Jauch, Council of Uri, Landvogt in Ober- und Niderturgau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell report that they have consulted the Appenzell residents of Spicher. These are willing to pay the agreed interest, but have already paid two interests and are only still indebted with 21 pounds. They ask St. Gallen to grant them a deadline until Candlemas 1481.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten reply to a letter from St. Gallen concerning Jacob Krencker. They point out that a contract with Pollay is not valid and must not impair the rights of the city. They threaten with penalties and the Imperial Ban if Krencker does not appear. They ask St. Gallen to instruct Krencker as well as Caspar Sicken and Thomas Baumgartner to present themselves and to settle amicably.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich forward a copy of a letter from the Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz, to Stein am Rhein. It reports on the gathering of approximately 2000 to 3000 foreign troops in the Krauchwiser Wald. Zürich asks St. Gallen for consideration and assures of the friendship of the Confederates.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell complain to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the lack of coinage and small change as well as the outflow of coinage abroad. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to instruct their citizens to give the Appenzellers current coinage for purchased goods, so that they can provide for their necessities.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to show goodwill in a feudal dispute. Jacob Vogel of Altikon claims that his father sold the Radmühle in Sumerau without knowing of the feudal obligation and is now burdened with 1030 gulden principal. St. Gallen wants to seize the mill as forfeited. Zürich asks that attention be paid to a mild settlement and a bearable honorarium instead of full forfeiture.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Radolfzell reply to the demands of the St. Gallen citizen Nazarius Jäckhen. They declare that they or their citizens would not deny Jäckhen the due right. They ask the St. Gallen to have Jäckhen come to Radolfzell to settle the matter with the citizens there. Regarding the claim against the Radolfzell Dionysius Wilen, who cannot raise the money, the latter is ready to have the costs assessed according to city custom. If Jäckhen does not pay, he will be pledged.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz intend to renew the regulations for their goldsmiths. They ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information on whether goldsmiths there have the right to process their own silver, which does not meet the prescribed standard, without a stamp, but only with their own mark, or whether they must strictly adhere to the standard.
en.sender: Captain of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to detain their citizens, the Zolligkoffer, to settle an outstanding principal debt of 500 gulden to the Memmingen citizen Hans Jacob Schnitzer on the basis of a receipt and indemnification. Schnitzer has lost the principal document and offers a receipt that cancels the claim. However, the Zolligkoffer additionally demand a pledge or surety, which Schnitzer refuses.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich reply to the complaint of the merchants of St. Gallen regarding the increase of duties in the lands of Archduke Ferdinand of Österreich. They have instructed the Landsschreiber of Baden to draft the requested letter to the Archduke without delay. Until the Archduke's reply, no further counsel is to be given. Zürich offers its help to promote the welfare of the Confederation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, on account of the great shortage of grain and the complaints of the poor population, to have the mint masters strike penny and heller coinage. Alternatively, they propose a coin exchange rate. Furthermore, they remind them of a contract whereby citizens of St. Gallen who own Holz or real estate in Appenzell must have this registered in Appenzell or with the people of St. Gallen. Appenzell asks that the registrations be carried out and the lists be transmitted.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Glarus ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to accept and pay for the iron balls delivered in the previous year without order by their countryman Michel Soldi. Soldi cannot ship the balls elsewhere and has suffered damage. Glarus requests an amicable solution so that Soldi may feel the support of the Confederates.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Bern communicate to the Ammann and Council of the Land of Glarus the answer of the French King to the petitions of the twelve cantons. They ask Glarus to send envoys to the Confederate Diet on Reminiscere in Baden, in order to deliberate on the acceptance of the offered sum and other matters.
en.recipient: Ammann and Council of the Land of Glarus

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz report that the wife of the citizen Leonhart Meißlin had placed a child with the bath attendant Hans Wilderer of St. Gallen. Wilderer had departed with a debt of 25 gulden and had not returned. Meißlin had brought the child to St. Gallen to hand it over to Wilderer or his relatives, which, however, failed. The people of St. Gallen had promised to provide for the child if credible proof of paternity is presented. The godparents Katharina Siezin and Heinrich Aberlin have confirmed Wilderer's paternity.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the convocation of a Diet of the Confederation to Baden on 20 May. The occasion is the threat posed by the warlike people around Genf and the intention of the Duke of Savoyen to take the land. Zürich asks for an answer as to whether St. Gallen has anything to bring forward, and assumes that the Diet will not lead to new resolutions.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the dispatch of envoys to the Duke of Savoyen for the removal of war troops. They report that in the Five Cantons five companies would be ready to march over the Gotthard, and that Spanish and Italian war troops would be approaching a Confederation. They ask for mutual communication of news.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The French envoys Mandolot, Bellievre, Haurefort and Fleury send the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the proposals for the renewal of the alliance with Frankreich, which they have presented in Baden. They ask the city to send envoys with full power to Solothurn on 15 July to seal the alliance, and assure their friendship.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Straßburg asks St. Gallen to compel the citizen and resident there, Doctor Albert Plarer, to pay the Straßburg citizen Nathanael Buers 200 gulden principal together with the overdue interest and Marzhal, and to settle his obligation. Buers has made this request, as he finds it difficult to collect the interest from St. Gallen and wishes to invest the capital in Straßburg.
en.sender: Felix von Nüneckhusen, Meister, and the Council of Straßburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Mandelot, Bellièvre, Hautefort and Fleury inform the returned envoys that at the last assembly in Solothurn a decision was made regarding the renewal of the alliance between the King and the Confederates. They ask the envoys to affix their seal to the alliance letters presented to them in French and German as soon as possible.
en.recipient: Envoys of the Confederation

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Solothurn inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the negotiations discussed at the last Diet in Solothurn regarding the renewal of the union between the King and the Confederates. They ask the St. Gallen to support the representatives they sent, Urs Suter and Hans Jacob von Stal, in the sealing of the letters and contracts in German and French.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send an authorized embassy for the Confederate Diet appointed for 30 September in Baden. The occasion is the regulation of the claims between Savoyen, Genf and Bern, as well as the concern for the cooperation of the Reformed cantons. The news is to remain secret until the Diet session.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg reply to a letter of the 22nd of the same month. They state that Barbara Kuenig, the wife of the citizen of St. Gallen Caspar Schuochmacher, would inherit a house and a bond for 80 gulden as the sole heir of her brother Claus Kuenig. Since the death of the brother has not yet been proven, they have allowed Schuochmacher to take over the bond against a guarantee. They have sent Barbara Kuenig back to St. Gallen so that she can provide the guarantee, and ask St. Gallen to facilitate this.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Bern inform that they leave their complaint against the Duke of Savoyen to the sole decision of the twelve cantons, under the condition that they retain the right to choose their own judges if the verdict is not accepted. They ask St. Gallen to urge the five cantons to decide at the next Diet at Baden on the admission of the Welschenlands into the Confederation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to examine their citizen Balthasar Rothmundt under oath regarding how he acquired two horses and carriages auctioned in Solothurn from the Schaffhausen citizen Hans Konrad Gürtler. They demand a written answer concerning the purchase process.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg report that the citizen of St. Gallen Caspar Schumacher and his wife Barbara Küntzin have returned to St. Stephanus to the house of their brother-in-law Klaus Küntzin. Since Schumacher had forcibly opened the door and behaved improperly, he had been imprisoned. The Ravensburgers ask for a written answer whether St. Gallen would guarantee the property of the family, so that Schumacher and his wife can take up the inheritance, provided they take in and provide for two children from the first marriage.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg reply to a letter from St. Gallen concerning Caspar Schuochmacher and his daughter-in-law Barbara Kränzin. They state that they deny the Schuochmacher the surety upon his judgment. Instead, they propose that Barbara Kränzin should invest 100 gulden in a house of her brother Klaus Krantz. The house is to be sold and the surplus over the 100 gulden as well as a bond for 80 gulden principal are to be handed over to her. For this, she must present a deed or surety sealed by St. Gallen. As soon as the sale is completed, St. Gallen or the Schuochmacher is to be informed so that the assets can be handed over.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to lift the arrest imposed by the wagoner Hans Stahel of Konstanz against the Schaffhausen citizen Hans Conrad Hurtter. Stahel had promised Hurtter to assert his claims only before the Schaffhausen city court, but had let his claims against Caspar Kechmundt in St. Gallen be seized. The Schaffhausers ask that Stahel be referred to the Schaffhausen court.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about an insult in the chapel on the Zugerberg, where the bones of those who died 50 years ago had been dug up and a flimsy painting with writing had been put up. Zürich had requested Zug to rebury the bones and to paint over the painting. Zug had carried this out on 16 January after initial unrest. Zürich asks for forgiveness for the delayed notification.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell reply to a complaint by the citizens of St. Gallen regarding the insufficient scales and weights of the Appenzellers. They ask the citizens of St. Gallen to instruct their stewards to give the Appenzellers good weight and measure and to pay the price for purchases. Appenzell has in turn instructed its countrymen to give the citizens of St. Gallen good weight and goods, in order to promote good neighborliness.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the Confederate Diet scheduled for the coming Sunday Oculi in Baden in the Aargau has been cancelled. The reason is that the King of Savoyen can only send his envoys on the Sunday after Quasimodo, 14 April. The Diet has therefore been called off in all the cantons of the Confederation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Rathgeber of the city of Augsburg ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizen David Hagman. He has assigned a debt of 16 gulden to Joachim Krütlinger, who had advanced the money for him. Esaias Hagman refuses to settle the debt. The Rathgeber request that Esaias Hagman be compelled to make immediate payment to Krütlinger.
en.sender: Rathgeber of the city of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, at the request of the St. Gallen, they had heard about the insults by Peter Locher and Hans Kucher. They had released the two from prison and threatened them with the feud. In addition, Andreas Locher and Jakob Buchler had posted bail to have the two brought before the Landrat. Appenzell offers St. Gallen to hold justice against the two, should they not be satisfied with this.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell regret the improper remarks made by their countrymen Jakob Locher and Hans Küngern von Tüffen towards St. Gallen. They have admonished the two and punish them according to their deserts, in order to preserve good neighborly relations. Appenzell asks St. Gallen to inform them in writing what the servants have done, and promises to report on further actions.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Othmar Scheittlin and Joseph Dannenberg answer the accusation that they had left their table and lodging in Basel without permission. They apologize for not having informed the Council of their progress in their studies, as the letters had not arrived. As a reason for the move to Herr Johannes Brandmüller, they cite the lack of study opportunities and the high costs in the previous lodging. With Brandmüller, they say that they had received better support and spiritual instruction. They ask for forgiveness and promise to study diligently in the future.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Syndics and Council of Genf ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to speak quickly to the heirs of the deceased citizen of Genf, Jean Wernet Schmitz, against the citizen of St. Gallen, Jean Taussperger. They request that the heirs not be disadvantaged by delays in the process, but that the money due to them be handed over to them without process formalities.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the Confederate Diet scheduled for 1 September in Baden was postponed at the request of the Duke of Savoyen and his envoys until the Sunday after All Saints' Day. They ask for acknowledgment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Leutkirch request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to proclaim and post an edict in the city regarding the creditors of the citizen Melchior Preißer there. They want the citizen of St. Gallen Michael Kobler and other creditors to appear on the appointed day, present their claims, and protect themselves from ignorance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hand over to their envoys the confessions of the offenders convicted in St. Gallen. In Konstanz, several persons had been arrested at the Kirchweihmarkt who had not yet made incriminating statements. The convicted persons of St. Gallen had named further accomplices, which is why the confessions are needed for the further prosecution in Konstanz.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the sending of the condemnations of two wrongdoers as well as a list of suspicious persons. They communicate that they recently had three thieves hanged, and send the corresponding judgments further, so that St. Gallen may exercise justice against any companions who may have been taken there.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich transmit to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen a copy of a letter from Elector Ludwig of the Palatinate to the Estates belonging to the Augsburg Confession. In it, they are invited to a meeting on 28. Oktober 1583 in Mülhausen (or Freiburg) to deliberate on the defense against papal practices, the situation of the Elector of Köln, and the improvement of the Kammergericht.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Duke Karl Emanuel von Savoyen has cancelled the Diet scheduled for 3 November in Baden due to illness and postponed it to the Sunday after Epiphany next year. Since a fruitful negotiation without the presence of all parties is unlikely, they have informed all parties involved and ask St. Gallen to act accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell remind St. Gallen of the confirmation of the Eternal Peace in the Rintal by the seven cantons. They ask that the citizens of St. Gallen be prevented from disturbing the purchase of the Sommerswand estate by Hans Herr, as this was confirmed by the seven cantons. Appenzell asks for a written answer and warns of further disputes.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform them in writing whether they consider the properties and vineyards that St. Gallen has bought from Hans Heer of St. Margrethen as Appenzell citizens in the Rhine Valley. Appenzell has already declared that the other seven governing cantons of the Rhine Valley consider these properties as their own Rhine Valley and lands for Appenzell and St. Gallen and not for Hans Heer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the mediation in the dispute over the Strömbkoch of the Sieben Orte. They state that they did not wish to oppose the judgment, and emphasize their willingness to promote the will of the Confederates for good neighborly relations.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Marguerite Compagnon, Philippe Compagnon, Antoine Bayet, Louise Compagnon and George Compagnon ask the Consuls of St. Gallen to summon Jean Fit, so that he pays the amounts owed to them from the estate of their father-in-law Konrad Gueminder. They refer to two previous requests and ask for quick payment, as the people of St. Gallen did not pay for goods in Lyon.
en.sender: Marguerite Compagnon, Philippe Compagnon, Antoine Bayet, Louise Compagnon and George Compagnon
en.recipient: Consuls of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admit the tailor Hans Meyer, son of the late preacher Laurenz Meyer of Niederglatt, into their citizenship and to allow him to establish a household and practice his trade. They recommend him as a young man and because of his father, who had long served in the church ministry.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Landammann and Council of Glarus that they have acceded to the request of the five cantons and will hold the Baden annual account on 7 July according to the old calendar. For the annual account beyond the mountains, the envoy will appear in Luzern on the evening of St. John's Day according to the new calendar. Zürich asks Glarus to instruct its messengers accordingly.
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Glarus

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the annual account for Baden in Aargau is to be held on Sunday, 7 March according to the old calendar. They ask the St. Gallen to behave accordingly if they have anything to attend to there.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Gemeiner Rat der drei Pünfte informs the Council envoys of the Acht Orte that the envoys of the five Catholic cantons had urged them at the Diet in Chur to refrain from establishing an evangelical school in their lands. They reject this demand, as they are not accountable to anyone, and ask the Acht Orte for advice on how they should conduct themselves.
en.recipient: Ratsgesandte der Acht Orte

en.regest: The bailiff, town Ammann and Council of Weesen inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they will move and hold their usual fair this year on the day of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross according to the old calendar, that is on 24 August according to the new calendar. They ask the citizens of St. Gallen to take note of this so that they can visit and use the market.
en.sender: The bailiff, town Ammann and Council of Weesen
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the citizen of St. Gallen Melcher Beintz has made an appraisal of real estate in Tüffen, which he considers not to be in his favor. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to instruct their citizens not to purchase or redeem debts in the land of Appenzell, as the land law stipulates that each person shall collect their own debts themselves.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell complain to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that their people, who were in St. Gallen on Saturday, were only allowed to accept 8 batzen at the Corn Exchange for francs that they had bought in the town for 1 gulden 8 batzen. They ask that the francs be accepted again at the original rate, or that it be communicated in writing at what rate they will be accepted in the future.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster, Judges and Council of Steyr reply to an intercession letter of the Council of St. Gallen concerning the deceased Stadtaoman Jakob Straub and his son. They state that the contract was not submitted and ask for forgiveness for the delay. They ask the Council of St. Gallen to negotiate with Straub regarding the 240-florin debt of the clothmakers, so that he settles the debt from other means.
en.sender: Burgomaster, Judges and Council of Steyr
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen concerning Tuffner countrymen who are supposed to have deceived a wife in St. Gallen. They refuse the surrender of the accused for 25 December, as this day is celebrated in Appenzell as Holy Christmas Day according to the new calendar. They offer to bring the persons before the St. Gallen court on another, non-holiday day.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the communication regarding the middle articles to be treated by the merchants at the next Baden Diet concerning the prevention of complaints in the Kingdom of Frankreich. They endorse the articles and promise, through their envoys, to contribute everything possible to their attainment. They ask that, in the first article concerning goods from the Confederation and Germany, the velvets woven in the country and the silks spun there (Filiseli and Galeti) also be mentioned.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Freiburg informs that it will no longer send the St. Gallen envoys to the assembly scheduled for 14 June in Solothurn, in order not to burden the city unnecessarily. Instead, St. Gallen will be informed of the resolution there. Freiburg asks that this not be misunderstood, and assures its attachment as well as its willingness to comply with the will of the city in future cases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich recommend the tailor Hans Meyer, son of the late preacher Laurentz Meyer, and his wife Katharina Högerin to the city of St. Gallen. Meyer says that he married into St. Gallen and practiced his trade there. He asks for admission to the citizenship, as admission to Zürich has been postponed until 24 June. The Zürich side asks St. Gallen to admit the couple.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rottweil request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to deliver the inheritance of the ward of the deceased Rottweil citizen David Merzen. This inheritance was intended for the child by the grandfather, the deceased St. Gallen citizen Josef Merzen, but is still in St. Gallen. The guardians of the child have already requested the handover for a long time, without success. Rottweil asks St. Gallen to arrange the delivery.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich invite Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to a Diet of the Confederates in Baden. This takes place on Sunday, 27 February, in the evening. The occasion is the expiration of the agreed customs arrangement with Österreich as well as other pending matters. The Zürichers offer their support.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant favorable support to the St. Gallen grain dealers at the market and to purchase grain for them in order to lower the rising prices. They have instructed their dealers to agree on a committee and to send only two representatives per market, who are to purchase and share jointly.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen to accommodate the two grain buyers sent by St. Gallen in their purchases at the Überlingen market. The people of St. Gallen have instructed their grain merchants to send only two representatives in order to stabilize prices and to supply their own population.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to dissuade their citizens and citizen women from harassing the Appenzell countrymen because of the new calendar. The Appenzell people have accepted the calendar and ask for peace in order to avoid disputes with other cantons. They expect a written answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The bailiff, Ammann and court of Winfelden ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have their citizens Wäliwall, the Roßler, Master Jakob Keller and Caspar Affolter pay the goods they had lent to the widow of the St. Gallen physician Othmar Keller. The creditors had not been paid by the lords of Gemmingen and the community of Winfelden, as the widow and her children had not returned the lent goods.
en.sender: The bailiff, Ammann and court of Winfelden
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Wyß, bailiff of Grüningen, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the ward Hans Schüffelberg legally in the inheritance dispute with his cousin Jacob Schüffelberg and his heirs. He requests that the paternal relatives have priority over the maternal heirs, even if they are strangers, and asks for a written answer.
en.sender: Johann Wyß, Council of the city of Zürich and bailiff of the lordship of Grüningen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant their citizen Heinrich Wyssen the inheritance of his wife without deduction. They confirm that in Schaffhausen no deduction is levied when the dowry is increased beyond the originally agreed sum, and ask for equal treatment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen reply to an inquiry from the Council of St. Gallen regarding the churchwarden Eusebius Kleber. They ask for patience for the past time and expect that Kleber will present himself in Memmingen within fourteen days. They request the Council of St. Gallen not to hinder Kleber, as his reasons for the absence could be quickly settled. After the settlement, he will return to his church service.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Evangalist Zanin, silk weaver and citizen of Zürich, offers the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to establish silk manufactories (satin, silk, wool) in the city, as he has done in Zürich. He refers to the recommendation of the citizens of St. Gallen Kaspar and Melchior Näff. Zanin asks for a written answer so that he may come to St. Gallen and discuss the matter orally.
en.sender: Evangalist Zanin, silk weaver and citizen of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform town clerk Caspar Kyter of St. Gallen about the answer of the Duke of Savoyen to the grain prohibition.
