They refer to a translation, which will be contained in the next missive. Furthermore, they pass on the excuse of the Confederates of Bern, who claim to have been responsible for the grain prohibition first and not to have hindered the trade.
en.recipient: Caspar Kyter, town clerk of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen, in which the latter accused them of dealing with unauthorized matters. Appenzell declares that they are willing to leave to St. Gallen inheritances in the city of St. Gallen that fall to Appenzell cousins and first cousins, as they do with inheritances in Appenzell that fall to St. Gallen cousins and first cousins. They refer to two cases in which inheritances in St. Gallen were denied to Appenzell citizens, and ask for an amicable settlement. Otherwise, they will stick to their Landrecht.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of the intention to send a troop contingent to support the city of Genf, as it is threatened by troop gatherings in Lyon and in the Breisgau. They emphasize that this does not mean hostility against others, but serves the defense of the ally Genf. Furthermore, they communicate that the Diet of the Confederation has been moved to 2 October old style.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on the banishment of their churchwarden Eusebius Kleber. He says that he composed an insult against the Council of Memmingen and refuses to sign a declaration of submission. Memmingen has therefore banished him from the city. Memmingen asks St. Gallen not to take offense in this matter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell inform that they have decided in an inheritance dispute between the women of St. Gallen Barbara and Balthasar Köchin and the man of Appenzell Georg Kern. According to old land law, uncles and aunts inherit before nephews and nieces. They ask St. Gallen to apply the same law in future cases to avoid disputes.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jerg Volmershoffer, Zoller zu Göttingen, replies to a letter from the Council of 16 September. He states that he is holding a small cask of linen belonging to Sebastian Struben of St. Gallen, because the carrier could not present a valid toll certificate and the goods were not correctly declared. He asks the Council to inform the merchants and to give him instructions so that he can forward the small cask at the next opportunity.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Columban Gsell informs the Vogtfrau Engela Koblerin that a judgment has been rendered, according to which the old letters and seals are in force. The Untermühle must clear its Kennen for the Obermühle and vice versa. In the event of construction work on the Kennen, no party may act without the consent of the other. The costs are to be borne in equal parts according to an account. Gsell requests, in the name of the Schwieger, the return of the letters and seals.
en.recipient: Engela Koblerin

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell reply to a letter from the St. Gallen, in which they complain about a previous answer. They point out that a complete justification of all oral and written negotiations could endanger the friendship. Regarding the submitted document concerning Jörg Bühlwiler, they recall an old case in which Hans Weber, as bailiff of the widow Kuchis, had intervened for Bühlwiler. They ask that future inheritance cases be reported in writing or orally, in order to maintain the neighborhood.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Glarus ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their envoy in the collection of a debt of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Michel Tobler towards the bailiffs of Glarus Hilary Rausch and Wolfgang Blumer. Tobler had promised payment for the purchase of sheep, but drove the animals on without payment. The Glarus authorities now demand the outstanding sum.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the disputes in Müllhausen between the authority and the majority of the citizens regarding the dissolution of the alliance with the Eight Cantons. Since the previous efforts to reach an amicable settlement have failed, they invite to a Diet of the Confederation on 26 March in Baden to seek means to bring the city back to a peaceful civic Wesen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen about the death of the St. Gallen citizen Sebastian Sutter and his wife Anna Oesingerin. Since the wife died last, her morning gift, the household goods, and a child's share fall to her nearest blood relatives. Since these may possibly reside in Schaffhausen, the St. Gallen authorities ask for inquiry and notification, so that the heirs can assert their rights.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the ongoing disputes in Müllhausen. Since the citizenry there refuses to accept impartial justice, and the requests for help from the affected Councils and citizens have remained in vain, Zürich and the other four cantons still in alliance with Müllhausen have decided to assist the appellants in obtaining ordinary justice and to compel the defiant by force. They ask St. Gallen to understand this undertaking.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send their envoys to Baden on 18 June for the upcoming Baden annual account. This is done at the request of the Confederates of Bern, as the common affairs could not be negotiated. It concerns the new religious league of the Catholic cantons as well as alliances with Spanien and others, which would bring about a separation of the Confederation and other dangers.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern inform the Council of Zürich that, after the conquest of Mülhausen, they have decided to meet in Basel on 25 June to deliberate on the treatment of the citizens there. They ask Zürich to write to Glarus and Schaffhausen so that their envoys can arrive in Basel in time.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Niklaus Schelch and his siblings in asserting their inheritance claims from the estate of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Jakob Strub. They request that the inheritance claims be given priority over other creditors and that the heirs be satisfied without cost.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Jacob Gansser in asserting his inheritance rights. Gansser has inherited estates through the death of his daughter, who is from the marriage with Barbara Kapffmänin, sister of the deceased Ammann of St. Gallen Melchior Kapffman. He wishes to receive these from his brother-in-law Kapffman. The Schaffhausen authorities ask for support so that Gansser can receive his inheritance with little effort.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish the edict concerning the scheduled court day for the creditors of the deceased citizen of Lindau, Stephan Löher. In particular, the citizen of St. Gallen, Kaspar Kornleisch, has claims on Löher's estate. This is done so that no one is curtailed in their rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to examine their citizen Hans Beringer in the debt matter between the citizen of Konstanz Loewatj Leuten and the citizen of St. Gallen Melchior Klein. Beringer is not Leuten's servant, but has only acted as an attorney. Konstanz requests the forwarding of the settlement of the matter.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish the attached edict concerning the appointed general court day for the joint debtor Misael Roeschel at the usual places, so that the creditors, including citizens of St. Gallen, can register their claims.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to detain their citizen Jacob Straub to settle the outstanding debt to the citizens of Ulm, Marx and Tobias Neuwernern, or to clarify the matter. The creditors had taken legal action against Straub, but his assets were insufficient. After the death of the fellow citizen Jacob Straub in Steyr, his heirs had committed to payment, but the payment is being delayed. Ulm asks for support to satisfy the creditors.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Josua Buwmann in the collection of a considerable debt from Joseph Mayer. Buwmann wishes to enforce the claim personally and requests support so that he is not hindered. Schaffhausen asks for assistance in the enforcement or in the legal proceedings.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau thank St. Gallen for the warning about false coins, which are identical to the Irner but consist of pure lead. They declare that they will be vigilant in their city to determine the origin and the issuers of such counterfeit coins, and promise to inform St. Gallen immediately. They ask for mutual warning in the event of future occurrences.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The city of Kuttenberg asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for support, as it has fallen into an irreparable misfortune due to a loss. Two senators have been entrusted with an oath to beg for help. Furthermore, it is requested that the attached letters be authenticated and copied. If Johannes Klamperus or his companions fall into the hands of the authorities in St. Gallen, they are to be brought before the court and the city of Kuttenberg informed thereof.
en.sender: Jan Obecnowsky, Primus Prchorury z Kutny Hory, Consul and the other senators of the city of Kuttenberg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell remind Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of a previous agreement, according to which buyers of St. Gallen purchasing farms in Appenzell should satisfy the interest-holders on the pledges before the purchase. Since this has not yet been done, they ask them to instruct their citizens accordingly, in order to avoid disputes and seizures of St. Gallen property in Appenzell.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a meeting of the Confederates in Baden on the Sunday after Epiphany, which serves to regulate the grain trade. Since the new year is being celebrated, the envoys of Zürich will only arrive on the following Tuesday. They ask St. Gallen to take this into account, should there be matters to be negotiated there.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell complain to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the accusation that their countrymen buy up a lot of lard in St. Gallen and export it to the Swabian lands, whereby prices in Appenzell rise and the population is burdened. They ask for a review and promise to make an order if necessary.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish the edict concerning the appointed general court day for the local citizen Andreas Höhn, the shoemaker. This is done so that no one who has claims on Höhn's property and goods is shortchanged.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to persuade the heirs of the deceased Lienhart Zollikofer to a friendly settlement of the inheritance dispute with his brother Jost Zollikofer. Jost has renounced his citizenship and wants to bring the matter before the cantons of Thurgau, which could be detrimental to St. Gallen. Zürich recommends the choice of impartial arbitrators.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Biel warn Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of the danger of a separation of the Confederation as a result of disputes between the leading members. They ask for advice on how the three Pundtsgenossen could intervene between the parties to promote reconciliation. Biel offers its services and asks for a reply.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist the widow Barbara Viserin, daughter of the deceased citizen of Schaffhausen Hans Ritter, in the inheritance of her brother-in-law Sebastian Suter in St. Gallen. The Viser family has proven its kinship with the Suter through old letters and wishes to send a representative to St. Gallen. Schaffhausen asks for the good promotion of the inheritance claims.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Margarethe vom Stein zu Jetingen und Matzensies, guardian of the children of the deceased Jeronimus Oßwald, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant the children their share of the inheritance as co-heirs of the deceased apothecary Mathes Oßwald. She complains that the father's siblings wanted to exclude the orphans from the inheritance, and requests a written answer.
en.sender: Margarethe vom Stein zu Jetingen und Matzensies
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich reply to the inquiry of the five cantons and Appenzell, why the preachers in the Rheintal and Oberthurgau attend the Synod in St. Gallen. They refer to a farewell of 1567, which provided for this arrangement, and ask St. Gallen to give the five cantons a friendly answer, as they could not immediately name the reason for the earlier arrangement.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Council envoys of the five Catholic cantons Luzern, Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden and Zug reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen. They state that they will present the Appenzeller trade to their lords upon their return. Regarding the Synod and the examination of the preachers in St. Gallen, they declare that their lords will no longer permit this in the future. They are pleased that St. Gallen voluntarily agrees to this and promise a friendly disposition.
en.sender: Council envoys of the five Catholic cantons Luzern, Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden and Zug
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The administrators and officials of the Landvogtei Schwaben report that Georg Kern, called Schapperlin, from Eysigelbach, was captured in the Landvogtei Schwaben. He is said to have murdered a woman and stolen a silver chalice in Wolmatingen in the spring with two accomplices. Since one of the accomplices is said to have been captured in St. Gallen and executed by the wheel, they request his judgments and testimonies, insofar as they concern the prisoner, in order to carry out what is due against him.
en.sender: The administrators and officials of the Landvogtei Schwaben
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The administrators and officials of the lordships of Bregenz and Hohenegg ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their colleague in office, Martin Hermann of Lautrach, in the collection of a debt of 204 florins plus costs from the citizen of St. Gallen Jacob Kübler. Hermann says that he sold pigs to Kübler, but the latter does not pay and is in bankruptcy. They request priority for Hermann's claim over other creditors.
en.sender: Administrators and officials of the lordships of Bregenz and Hohenegg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish an edict concerning a scheduled court day for the creditors of the citizen of Lindau Hans Deller, so that no one may be disadvantaged by ignorance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the convening of a Diet of the Confederates by the Confederates of Luzern. They ask to be informed whether St. Gallen has anything to negotiate at this Diet or whether other matters are to be settled at the Diet.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Bern inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about belligerent intentions and troop movements from Piemont and Savoyen on the borders of Switzerland. They explain that they must occupy their cantons with German troops to protect their subjects, but emphasize that they do not intend any hostility. They ask the Confederates for vigilance and promise to stand together in case of emergency.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern thank the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen for the communication of an important, unknown matter concerning the postal service to Spanien, Mailand, and Rom. They now in turn share reports that they received eight days ago, which confirm a deed committed in Frankreich as well as a subsequent armament. They enclose copies of the reports and reaffirm their friendship and loyalty.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern inform the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen about the discovery of a conspiracy against the Confederates, which is connected to foreign war troops on the border. They refer to the treaty of 1564 with Savoyen, which prohibits the stationing of troops, and request the dispatch of Council envoys with full power to an assembly on 19. January 1589 in Baden.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern thank the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen for their letter, in which they had expressed themselves regarding a meeting in Baden and offered the support of the Confederates. They declare themselves in turn ready to help in similar cases according to the manner and duty of the Confederates.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have received the answer of the Duke of Savoyen to the complaint of the Bernese regarding alleged secret practices against Lausanne. They enclose a copy of the concealed missive and ask them to verify it.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The bailiff, Burgomaster and Court of Stuttgart inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have admitted Erasmus Haltmaier, a citizen of St. Gallen, who has married the daughter of the deceased Hans Heppacher, into their citizenship. They ask St. Gallen to support Haltmaier in the collection of his paternal and maternal inheritance in St. Gallen and to issue him a documentary letter regarding his honest birth and his conduct.
en.sender: The bailiff, Burgomaster and Court of Stuttgart
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen that, in response to the city's request to postpone the annual Synodus due to the visitation bans of the five Catholic cantons, they have inquired with Luzern. Luzern has stated that it has forwarded the letter to the other four cantons and is awaiting their response. As the Synodus is imminent, the Zürichers ask for patience until the response of the five cantons is available, and promise to forward it immediately.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Sancy asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen again for financial support for the King, as the current situation would affect the security of all. He refers to the positive answer already given and asks them to believe the envoy Balbany, who will set out the situation of the royal army.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss, Baumeister and Council of Waldshut ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen not to impose more than five percent deduction on the acquisition of real estate by the heirs there of deceased citizens who inherit in Waldshut. They refer to their own practice, whereby in cases of inheritance in Waldshut only three kreuzer per gulden deduction are levied.
en.sender: Schultheiss, Baumeister and Council of Waldshut
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Sillery thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the good answer to the proposals of Henri Balbany. He assures them that His Majesty knows how to value the services of the city. Sillery informs them that he has handed over the obligation for the security of the promised 10'000 ducats to Balbany, so that the latter can withdraw his own commitment. He promises that both the interest and the capital are to be paid on time.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Bern inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the military conflicts with the Duke of Savoyen. They report that the imperial army attacked Savoyen but withdrew, whereupon the Duke restored his power. Bern intends to march out with its banner to protect itself and Genf. They ask St. Gallen for loyal support of the Confederates and promise gratitude.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Biberach ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist the widow Anna Faeüsaßin, wife of the Scherers Melchior Barten, in the collection of compensation for an alleged bodily injury to her children caused by a horse of the St. Gallen N. Zollickofer. They refer to an attached supplication.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern thank St. Gallen for the friendly reply to their report on the plan to march against the Duke of Savoyen under the St. Gallen banner and the protection of the King. They report that the peace negotiations in Wallenstadt had failed, as the opposing side had made unreasonable proposals. A truce exists between the armies, which gives the enemy time to complete their fortifications. Since Bern has expended large sums of money and the duration of the war is uncertain, they ask St. Gallen to lend them Kronen or gulden for one to twenty years with sufficient security and due interest, or to mediate with other persons who would be willing to do so.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell report on a legal dispute between the citizen of St. Gallen Goriuss Färben and the Appenzeller Basten Wyßler. Wyßler has won the main case and demands from his surety Baschon Oegster the reimbursement of the costs. Färben refuses this and accuses Appenzell of having acted against the rights. Appenzell asks St. Gallen to instruct Färben to settle the costs and to relieve Oegster, and demands an answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Thonne Jäck informs Bartholomäus Landmann that he has received his letter, according to which Bartholomäus Boschen wants to sue him. He refers to a judgment and demands that the judgments, witness testimonies, and the cost account be delivered to him in writing. He is willing to settle, otherwise he will sue for the costs. He asks Landmann to inform Boschen of this and not to bother him further until the documents have arrived.
en.recipient: Bartholomäus Landmann zu Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they are transmitting to them a copy of the letter of the newly elected King of Frankreich. The King asks for the continuation of the friendship and the alliance. Zürich declares itself willing to continue to show all willing goodwill and friendship in other matters.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publish an edict concerning a scheduled day of reconciliation and debt for the Lindau subject Wolf Müller in St. Gallen. Müller is indebted to several citizens of St. Gallen, including Caspar Lang, Ulrichen, Josen Herbern, Frau Margretha Hüeterin, and Jergen Balthasar.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen to listen favorably to their envoys, the Noble and Esteemed Hans Escher, and to give him credit, as he brings forward a petition in the name of the city of Zürich. They ask for compliance and offer their services in return.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss, Burgomaster and Council of Basel ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to allow their citizen Thomas Loxart, the bookbinder, to reside in St. Gallen for a time, so that he may settle his business there. Loxart has married in St. Gallen and acquired real estate there. Basel asks for the friendship of the Confederates and offers reciprocity.
en.sender: The Schultheiss, Burgomaster and Council of Basel
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Karl Ludwig, Graf zu Sulz, complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the seizure of his fruits by the gunsmith in Rheineck. He points out that the Seckelmeister is not authorized to act on account of a previous customs dispute over wine or outstanding interest. He asks that the arrest be lifted and the transport enabled, otherwise he will not pursue the fruits further and will revoke the customs exemption for merchants of St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Othmar Betzhart to present himself in Konstanz within eight days regarding an insult to their citizen Hans Koch. Furthermore, they are to urge Betzhart to settle the matters concerning the dwelling of his father-in-law Koch.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about an inquiry by the Confederates to Appenzell regarding the introduction of the new calendar. Appenzell replies that the Äusseren Roden had reintroduced the old calendar. Zürich asks St. Gallen to verify this, as the Äusseren Roden had held the Ratsschlag in St. Gallen, and assures that nothing will happen without their knowledge.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ernst Friedrich, Margrave of Baden, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he grants escort for the Frankfurt fairs only at certain times and places. He warns the merchants of St. Gallen against missing the escort or taking forbidden detours, as he will not provide compensation for any resulting damages. He asks the city to inform and admonish its citizens accordingly.
en.sender: Ernst Friedrich, Margrave of Baden and Hachberg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Georg Allgöwer and his wife Anna Gurtlerin to come to Schaffhausen within one month to settle the guardianship account with their former guardian Jacob Hueniwadel and to pay the owed sum. Allgöwer has not appeared so far despite his pledge.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant citizenship to the goldsmith Hans Jakob Vögel, son of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Hans Ulrich Vögel. Vögel wishes to settle in St. Gallen, is related there, and has property there. Lindau supports the request on behalf of the local Burgomaster Michael Büchser, who is related to Vögel.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Nicolas Brulart de Sillery and Nicolas de Harlay de Sancy confirm that the named merchants of St. Gallen have lent 10'000 Écus to the King of Frankreich. They undertake in the name of the King to repay the capital within two years and to pay interest. The goods of the French Crown serve as security. An earlier, lost bond is no longer valid.
en.sender: Nicolas Brulart de Sillery and Nicolas de Harlay de Sancy
en.recipient: George Salicofer, Jacques Siler, Jacques Salicofer, Daniel Christoph Studor and Jacques Sclaperitz of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster, Council and citizenry of Suhla report on a devastating city fire on 25 April, in which 277 houses, the church, school, town hall and hospital were destroyed. They ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a mild tax to support the reconstruction, as they themselves could not bear the damage.
en.sender: Burgomaster, Council and community leaders together with the whole citizenry of Suhla
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Chamberlain and Council of the city of Regensburg report that Anton Widmann, from Wöbertshofen, called the Küch-Söldtel, is detained in Regensburg. He has confessed to having stolen five silver cups and a brass-bound Weidner from an innkeeper in the St. Gallen Vorstadt about eight days after New Year. He sold the cups in Augsburg. Regensburg asks St. Gallen to verify the statements and to communicate the result in writing.
en.sender: Chamberlain and Council of the city of Regensburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they had executed Jakob Balbierer, who came from the Rheintal, for theft, in particular of linen. On the scaffold, he asked that his youngest child be given to the wife of the St. Gallen citizen Jakob Spregken, Barbara Moßerin. Zürich assigns the child to Moßerin and asks the St. Gallen authorities to instruct Moßerin and her husband to take in the child.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Jakob Balbierer, who was executed for theft in Zürich on 8 July 1590, had confessed, among other things, to having stolen linen on the St. Gallen Bleiche. Since the witness of the St. Gallen letter had not taken over the goods found at the time, the Zürichers now hand over 65 ells of linen along with two shirts to St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publish an edict regarding the cession of the assets of their citizen Ludwig Leyen to his creditors in St. Gallen. Leyen has appointed a day for an amicable settlement or, if this fails, a debt court day. The citizens of St. Gallen might be indebted to him.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their fellow citizen Balthasar Künneggt, belt-maker and merchant, against the citizen of St. Gallen Othmar Bastert, furrier and merchant. Bastert owes Künneggt 31 gulden 30 kreuzer for goods and has promised payment but has not yet made it. Memmingen requests that Bastert be moved to pay.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: King Heinrich of Frankreich and Navarra asks the Confederates to help supply the families of his soldiers serving in Switzerland, as the roads are insecure. He refers to his envoy Heinrich von Sillery, in whom the Confederates are to place their trust. He promises to support the Confederates in similar cases.
en.sender: Heinrich, King of Frankreich and Navarra
en.recipient: the Confederates

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform the town clerk of St. Gallen that the Council Heinrich Thoman has returned from his embassy to Innsbruck. They transmit a copy of the reply from Archduke Ferdinand, who orders the expulsion of the citizens who fled from Mülhausen from his lands. Zürich expects further reports and offers assistance in the further negotiation.
en.recipient: Caspar Ziller, town clerk of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the convocation of a Confederate Diet on 10. January 1491 in Baden. This assembly was set in view of tensions between Schwyz and Glarus over the bailiwicks in the Gaster and the Unten as well as the threat of war. Zürich asks St. Gallen to behave accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Syndics and Council of Genf report to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on the dire straits of their city after the war against Savoyen and Frankreich. They ask for a collection by the pastors of St. Gallen to alleviate the poverty, debts, and the care of the victims of the war, until a peace is concluded.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Council of the city of Augsburg asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizen Bartholome Schüerle, innkeeper in Augsburg. Schüerle has complained in writing about the still unpaid sum of 117 gulden 7 kreuzer, which Melchior Glinzen the Younger and his brother-in-law Christoph Hillinger owe him for their stay in Augsburg. The Council of Augsburg requests the authorities of St. Gallen to compel Glinzen to pay by suitable means.
en.sender: Council of the city of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Ratsboten of the thirteen cantons at the Diet at Baden confirm the receipt of a letter from St. Gallen regarding the inconvenience of the toll increase by officials of Österreich. They have requested the Archduchess of Österreich to remedy this and ask St. Gallen to accept the reply of Hauptmann Melchior Studer. They will inform St. Gallen about the Archduchess's reply at the next Diet.
en.sender: Ratsboten of the thirteen cantons at the Diet at Baden
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The bailiff and Council of the town of Bischofzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene on behalf of the married couple Josua Schürpf and Magdalena Zillerin. Schürpf had sold his house in St. Gallen to his brothers-in-law or their bailiff in order to buy it back. These men are now blocking his access and demanding a compensation. The wife waives such a compensation. Bischofzell requests St. Gallen to instruct the relatives to hand over the property to the married couple.
en.sender: The bailiff and Council of the town of Bischofzell
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Michael Bäldi von Glarus, captain of a regiment of the Confederates, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen in writing for support for the French King. He refers to the approvals of Zürich, Basel and Schaffhausen and asks for equal help, whether by surety or loan in cash, to cover the King's war costs and to repel his enemies.
en.recipient: Burgomaster, lesser and greater Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Brulart thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for their good will and support in the affairs of his Majesty. He asks that the offered sum be delivered in cash or placed on their credit, in order to make the funds available more quickly. Furthermore, he requests that an envoy be sent to the next Diet of Baden or that his intention be communicated, so that he can adapt to it.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The bailiff and Council of the city of Bischofzell remind the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of a protracted inheritance case between the citizens of Bischofzell Franz Lieb and Hans Küfer and the St. Gallen councilor Zacharias Täschener. They ask that the citizens be granted the rights to which they are entitled in the inheritance, as agreed in a previous letter.
en.sender: The bailiff and Council of the city of Bischofzell
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Syndics and Council of Genf thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a voluntary collection and donation in favor of the city, burdened by the war, and its poor. They report that the troops of Quitry and Sancy, after the battle at Monthouz and the capture of Conay and Uian, withdrew due to lack of money and on the order of Marshal d'Omont, in order to wage war in the Bresse. Genf asks that the state continue to be recommended.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Bivillac asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send their envoys to the court day at Baden and to give them full power to negotiate with the allies Zürich, Bern, Basel and Schaffhausen about an intervention in the question of the League. He refers to the intention of the Electors to raise a large army to support the Emperor in order to thwart the plans of the opponents. Bivillac emphasizes that this support also serves their own reputation and the restoration of the rights of the city.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report that they and their Confederates have been requested by the three secular Electors of the Empire to support Emperor Ferdinand II. in his planned march into Frankreich. Bern has already communicated its troop strength. Zürich asks St. Gallen to examine the situation and communicate its opinion in writing or to participate in the deliberations in Bern.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the convocation of a Diet of the Confederates to Baden on the last Sunday of the current month. The occasion is unrest in the grain purchase, disputes with Basel, and tensions in Freiburg. They ask for notification whether St. Gallen has matters for negotiation, and enclose a copy of a letter from Captain Michel Huldreich Glarus from Frankreich.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: A. Sancy regrets that the form of the obligation presented to the St. Gallen citizens is inaccurate, as it does not clearly name the sum. He explains that this was done only to facilitate the collection of the funds and to conceal the individual obligation of a canon. He offers to provide a declaration according to which the city, despite the general obligation, is liable only for 6000 ducats. He asks that the remaining contracts be concluded so as not to delay the important support for the affairs of His Majesty.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landmann and Council of Appenzell reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen concerning the engagement of the St. Gallen citizen Sebastian Jagk with Anna Tuchse. The family Tuchse declares itself willing to dissolve the engagement and return the given penny, without this being a disadvantage. However, they ask that the costs incurred in the inn be settled, while they will bear the costs in the father's house themselves.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that their former prisoner Hans Bignman von Waldkirch was executed the day before for theft. They send, upon request, a copy of his document in which he confesses to numerous thefts, including the theft of linen in St. Gallen.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel their citizen David Zollikoffer to enforce the judgment rendered before Konstanz against their citizen Andreas Olion. Olion had turned to Konstanz with a supplication, as Zollikoffer had not complied with the judgment.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to restrain their citizen David Zollikofer to comply with the judgment imposed on him, which requires him to release the citizen of Konstanz Andreas Klein from the surety for 400 thaler and costs. Klein had released the arrest on the basis of good faith. Konstanz offers reciprocity for future cases.
en.sender: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz report to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have sent the four pieces of linen, which were found with Hans Eigenmann of Waldkirch, who was executed in Konstanz in September 1592, to the St. Gallen bleacher Jakob Schirker. They have instructed Schirker to hand over the linen to the St. Gallen authority.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they consider the transmitted copy of the contract regarding inheritance cases acceptable, provided that the last article is amended in accordance with the attached slip. They request a written answer so that the contract may be sealed and the mutual friendship promoted.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about complaints of merchants of the city regarding tolls in the jurisdiction of the Duke of Savoyen. They request the dispatch of envoys to the Diet of the Confederates on 6 May in Baden, in order to jointly secure the abolition of the tolls there.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz send, at the request of the St. Gallen, the confession of the executed Hilarius Moser von Colmar. Moser had confessed to having committed numerous thefts with accomplices in the region of Basel, Freiburg, Solothurn, Zürich and in the Thurgau, including the stealing of money, clothing, linen and meat. He had also confessed to having stolen a purse in Konstanz in the grain house.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send an expert in the dispute between Georg Geßner and the city of Lindau over powder deliveries. The St. Gallen powder maker is to appear in Lindau on 20 June to examine the disputed powder. Ravensburg covers the travel costs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Sillery informs that he has written to the four cities in order to give the desired assurance that the city is liable only for 6000 écus. He asks that the contracts not yet sealed be sealed. He assures that he will fulfill all duties towards the King, so that the agreed conditions and the sums owed are settled.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Nicolas Brulart informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the contract regarding the joint obligation of the four cities for the affairs of the King is ready for sealing. He says that he has asked the allies for the promised declaration of compensation, which he estimates to be reasonable and willing. He asks that the envoys be granted full power to negotiate with the others on the day of the baths regarding the form of the declaration, in order to satisfy the St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: The Syndics and the Council of Genf report to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on the recent military confrontations with the Duke of Savoyen. They describe how a Savoyen army under the Marquis de Tresson besieged the Fort d'Arve, but withdrew after eight days upon learning that Lesdiguières had advanced into Savoyen. The Savoyen caused considerable damage to the harvest and the houses of the farmers in the process. Genf asks St. Gallen to maintain the previous friendship and support and to provide assistance in the event of a renewed threat.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jörg Freyherr zu Königsegg asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support his serf Caspar Veesen in an inheritance dispute with the citizen of St. Gallen Hans Jörg Hilterwand. Veesen's wife Barbara Oberhauser has been disadvantaged in the division of her father's inheritance. Königsegg requests the authorities of St. Gallen to give Veesen credit and to grant him help and support in all cases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein reply to a complaint by the merchants and shipmen of St. Gallen regarding an alleged new shipping regulation. They reject the accusation, as the shipmen of St. Gallen are not favored in any case. They explain that shipmen of St. Gallen who travel to Stein with goods may also load goods of St. Gallen there. However, they refuse the right to transport goods without their own cargo, in order to protect their own shipmen. They ask for a friendly reply.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein
en.recipient: Abbot Joachim of St. Gallen and Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Basel asks St. Gallen to compel the St. Gallen citizen Lütolf Zollikofer to pay the Basel citizen Martin Eininger the purchase price of 73 Sonnenkronen for a horse. Eininger says that he delivered the horse and is creditworthy towards the St. Gallen citizen. Basel requests official assistance so that Zollikofer pays the outstanding purchase money and makes himself free of legal claim.
en.sender: Niklaus Schultheiss, Burgomaster and Council of the City of Basel
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the City of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau forward a supplication of the heirs of the deceased Josef Küonlin to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen. The heirs complain about the citizen of St. Gallen Hans Peter Graf, who, despite existing contracts and receipts, makes new demands. They ask St. Gallen for protection against foreign courts and for a written confirmation to Lindau that they are willing to submit only to the courts of St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a Confederate Diet in Baden on Tuesday, the 19. März, at which the dismissal of Ballen Pinatelle in Bern is to be discussed. Since some citizens and merchants of St. Gallen are interested in the matter, they invite St. Gallen to send representatives.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Joseph Pappus, Stadtammann, and the judges and verdict speakers of the city court of Lindau ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in a legal dispute between Martin Alther and the brothers Martin and Hans Jürg Brem, to hear the witnesses named by Alther on Thursday and to send the result sealed to Lindau.
en.sender: Joseph Pappus, Stadtammann, and the judges and verdict speakers of the city court of Lindau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Wangen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have appointed a peremptory court day for the creditors of the deceased citizen Kaspar Schnitzer. They ask the St. Gallen to publish and proclaim this court day in their city, so that no one can plead ignorance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they will this time discontinue and not hold the fair in Lindau scheduled for the next Friday and Saturday after Simon and Jude. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to inform their citizens of this, so that they may avoid unnecessary costs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish an edict concerning a scheduled court day regarding the creditors of the citizen of Lindau Hans Jakob Stoffel and his wife. This is to be done so that no one is injured in their rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Bern report that the envoy of the Duke of Lorraine, Sillery, considers a general Baden Tagleistung to be fruitless. They ask St. Gallen to postpone the decision on this matter and invite to a Confederate assembly on 12 January 1595 in Aarau. There, a mission to the French King is to be discussed. Bern expects a compliant answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen reply to a letter of 7 January, in which Rotmundt and his son Heinrich reported their inability to attend a scheduled appointment regarding the inheritance of the deceased Elisabetha Schwalden. They set a new appointment for 3 March at 7 o'clock in the morning in the town hall and invite Rotmundt or a representative.
en.recipient: Melchior Rotmundt, physician and citizen of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the date set for 3 March for Melchior Gilmünden and his son Heinrich has been moved to 3 February. They request attendance at 7 o'clock in the town hall. The outcome depends on attendance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send them an excerpt from the testament of the deceased Joachim Gaißberg. The daughter of the deceased citizen of Lindau, Georg Karg, Maria, was provided for in the testament as a niece of Gaißberg, but has no certain knowledge of it. She asks for information about the bequest in order to act further.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen inform that they have acceded to the request of St. Gallen concerning the inheritance of the deceased Elisabetha Oßwaldin. They had initially wished to settle the dispute peacefully, but as this did not succeed, they confirmed the testament of the deceased after hearing the parties and witnesses. The bequest to Pastor Augustin Vogt and others is to be fulfilled, and the rest of the estate falls to the sister Clara Oßwaldin. Heinrich Rottmund must pay 50 gulden to Hans Konrad Krabeln for costs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform them what the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Joachim Gaisberg bequeathed to their citizen Maria Kropfen, the daughter of the deceased citizen of Lindau Jürgen Kropfen. They request an extract of the will or further information, as they had not received an answer to their earlier letter of 16 March.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the envoys of the Confederates for the settlement of the French debts will meet on 8 August in Bern and from there travel on to King Heinrich IV. They ask St. Gallen to send its envoys accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Masters and Council of Straßburg inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the departed citizen of Straßburg, Othmar Schlaipffer, has presented them with a general writ of passage. He requests to examine seven witnesses against the citizens of St. Gallen and Melchior Rothmann together with his sons. Straßburg sets the 29th of June (old style) at 7 o'clock in the morning in the chancery as the date and time and calls upon the citizens of St. Gallen to appear or to send proxies. Otherwise, proceedings will be conducted without them.
en.sender: The Masters and Council of Straßburg
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have set the appointment intended for the St. Gallen Council's envoy for the coming Tuesday. They ask that the envoy be received on this day, as the matter can no longer be postponed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen inform that their citizen Daniel Schmidt has died. His estate lies partly in St. Gallen. They ask St. Gallen to record the assets there in writing and to transmit them. Furthermore, they request that the heirs be compelled to pay the deduction due to the Schaffhausers, otherwise the shares are to be arrested and prohibited.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their resident Peter Wetlich with the inheritance of his deceased sister Magdalena Wetlichin. Wetlich, a weaver from St. Gallen, has been admitted in Zürich. The community of heirs consists of him and his siblings. Zürich asks for favorable promotion and support in the collection of the share due to him.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to allow the widow Sara Bidermannin, who received 1000 pounds as a life interest from her deceased husband Daniel Schmid, to invest this capital in St. Gallen. They assure that the sum will be secured by a pledge, and request the creation of a corresponding document.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The King of Frankreich asks the envoys of the cantons of Zürich, Bern, Basel, Schaffhausen and St. Gallen for patience regarding the payment of the principal sum of 70'000 écus for three more years. He promises to ratify the obligation and to verify the letters in Paris. The repayment is not to be taken from the 300'000 écus promised annually to the cantons of the League. The outstanding amounts are to be paid by the end of the current year.
en.recipient: Envoys of the cantons of Zürich, Bern, Basel, Schaffhausen and St. Gallen

en.regest: Bellièvre assures the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of his support and reports that he had assisted their envoys. He assures them that the King and his Council had done everything possible to satisfy St. Gallen and the Confederates. He hopes that provision will be made in the future for the payment of the debts.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish an edict concerning the appointed court day for the creditors of the widow of the deceased citizen of Lindau Blasius Sennner. This is done so that interested citizens of St. Gallen may also assert their claims and no one is disadvantaged by ignorance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to name a specific day and place at which both sides could agree on the inheritance cases. They emphasize that they do not intend to impose anything on strangers and foreigners against equity, but to grant everyone their right.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ulrich Friedrich Steinbock, Bruchsneider in Lichtensteig, asks Burgomaster Friedrich of St. Gallen for permission to display the coat of arms and the windows of the city of St. Gallen on his newly built house in Lichtensteig. He justifies this with the high esteem of the city and asks for approval to testify to the friendship of the city.
en.recipient: Friedrich, Burgomaster of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to allow Horatio Meier, whom they have permitted to trade in silk in Bern, to travel through Bern and conduct his business there, as the post messenger who travels every fourteen days from St. Gallen via Murten to Morez. They ask for a favorable answer.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Lorenz Herold, Ammann, judge and pronouncer of judgments of the city court of Kempten, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to make known to his citizens the appointed court day concerning the creditors and debt claims of the deceased citizen of Kempten, Hans Glogglins. He requests that the interested parties appear at the court day and that no one may plead ignorance.
en.sender: Hans Lorenz Herold, Ammann, judge and pronouncer of judgments of the city court of Kempten
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Syndics and Council of Genf declare to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, owing to the continuing harassment by the Duke of Savoyen and the high costs associated with it, they cannot pay the demanded interest in full. They have handed over 400 ducats to Christoph Studer for the first two years and ask for patience regarding the remaining payment, provided the Lord grants a lasting Peace.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to transfer to Lindau the inheritance money of the brothers Daniel and Abraham Stoffel, which lies in St. Gallen and is arrested there. Lindau wishes to accept the money for mutual liquidation and to settle the dispute between the brothers. They promise to let every claimant have fair justice.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Councils and envoys of the thirteen cantons ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to ensure that their citizens and subjects do not sell saltpeter to foreign cantons, but rather deliver it to the authority or their representatives in the Confederation at a reasonable price. This is to be done so that the saltpeter remains in the country and is available in future emergencies.
en.sender: Councils and envoys of the thirteen cantons
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Basel ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in the name of their citizen Lienhart Herzog dem Tuchern, to mediate so that the heirs of the deceased St. Gallen journeyman David N. reimburse him the costs of 11 pounds 15 shillings incurred during his illness and after his death. Herzog had employed the journeyman in his household during the plague in 1594.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen that the communities of Arbon, Horn, Egnach and Roggwyl ask for help, as the Bishop of Konstanz pressures them in religious matters. Zürich proposes to send an embassy to the Bishop together with other cantons to dissuade him from his plan. They ask St. Gallen for its opinion on this proposal.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to restrain their citizen Melchior Rätz to pay the outstanding teaching fee of 44 gulden to the Zürich silk weaver Ambrosius Pflotter. Rätz had committed himself to settle the matter with Pflotter or to appear in Zürich to clarify the matter amicably or legally.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Council of the city of Augsburg asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the guardians of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen, Othmar Schaden, to pay the citizen of Augsburg, Antonius Schin, the outstanding ten gulden. Schaden's guardians had shifted the debt onto the children after Schaden had been imprisoned in Augsburg.
en.sender: Council members of the city of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant citizenship to Heinrich Hüser, the son of the deceased St. Gallen citizen Ulrich Hüser. He says that he has married a woman of St. Gallen and has lived for some time as a resident (Hintersasse) in St. Gallen. Zürich requests a favorable treatment of the petition.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Councils of the city of Augsburg ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel the heirs of the deceased Ottmar Schardt to settle the documented debts of their citizen Hieronymus Manasser. Manasser has turned to the Augsburgers because of this delay, who wish to support him on account of the civic kinship.
en.sender: Councils of the city of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich send Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen a copy of a letter from the Confederates of Luzern. They ask to be informed, through their messenger, of the state of affairs regarding the matter mentioned in Luzern, whether and what there is to it, how the rumor occurred in St. Gallen, and who gave rise to the suspicion and the cause thereof. They ask that this be understood in a good spirit.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Basel request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizen Martin Liniger in the collection of a claim against the St. Gallen citizen Christoph Zolligkoffer. Liniger refers to a judgment of 22. März 1594, according to which he is to be satisfied from future inheritances or services of Zolligkoffer. Since Zolligkoffer has now received inheritances, the Basel authorities request support so that Liniger receives his arrears together with costs and damages.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Council of the city of Arbon report to Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen on their difficult situation in religious and political disputes with the Prince-Bishop of Konstanz. They ask for neighborly support and intercession at the upcoming Diet, in order to avert their damage.
en.sender: Ammann and Council of the city of Arbon
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz reply to the letter of the St. Gallen regarding their citizen Salome Voglerin. They enclose the report of their citizen Hans Jakob Bischoff. He confirms that the testament of the deceased silverware merchant Gall Feßlen, in which 100 gulden were bequeathed to the Voglerin, was later revoked and replaced by a new testament. Furthermore, the Voglerin had already issued a receipt for her inheritance. The Konstanzer ask the St. Gallen to dissuade the Voglerin from her further claims.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report that the miller's boy Hans Ulrich Haimenstein, who gives himself out as a citizen of St. Gallen, started a quarrel at night in Zürich with a young citizen. He was injured but left without paying the medical costs and the sustenance at the barber. The court of Zürich sentenced him and the citizen of St. Gallen to a fine of 50 gulden each. Zürich asks St. Gallen to examine whether Haimenstein resides there and to settle the claims, and for a written answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Neuenburg inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have admitted the local Kirsner Othmar Ratkaerbs as a citizen. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to leave Ratkaerbs what is due to him from his parents and from his father's testament, so that he may set up a household with his wife. They request an answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to an intercession of St. Gallen for their citizen and hospital clerk Martin Althern. They communicate that the principal debtor Hans Ludwig Brem has assigned his assets. Althern has judicially enforced the surety of Brem’s father and brother before the Lindau city court. The matter has been referred to the city court for resolution, in order to secure justice for Althern.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Amsterdam ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admit the young Heinrich Otto Hinderberch, who descends from free, honest parents and citizens of St. Gallen, into the number of their citizens and to grant him the rights of citizenship. Hinderberch wishes to settle in St. Gallen and marry a daughter of a citizen of St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.place: Amstelodam in the County of Holland

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to deliberate on the shortage and the high prices of beef. They propose that the delegated St. Gallen town messenger inform them whether a meeting in Konstanz would be desirable in order to establish equality in the meat supply.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they had detained the citizen Gregorius Haidtman who had left the city. They ask for a precise list of the thefts and frauds mentioned in a St. Gallen document. Furthermore, they ask for information on whether Haidtman had previously received an honest letter of dismissal, which he can no longer produce.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz report that the prisoner Gregor Hartmann has made no incriminating statements. He claims to have escaped from the St. Gallen captivity because the door was open and to have voluntarily surrendered himself again. Furthermore, he accuses the Seiler Konrad Bertel of having taught false dyeing. The St. Gallen are requested to deliver the dyer Sebastian and his responsibility.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The city court of Lindau informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the citizen of Lindau, Peter Krenkel, has sued Magdalena Späth, resident in St. Gallen, widow of the deceased Hans Wager, for a debt of 14 pounds 3 shillings. Since the defendant did not appear despite public proclamation, a peremptory court day was set for 7 April. The Lindauers ask the St. Gallen authorities to inform the defendant of this date and to compel her to appear.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss, Council and Deputies of the Evangelical Religion of Frauenfeld thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the gift of a dwelling to their church officials. They assure their gratitude and their readiness to serve and be useful to St. Gallen in all cases.
en.sender: Schultheiss, Council and Deputies of the Evangelical Religion of Frauenfeld
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Council of Bregenz ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to consider favorably the two sisters of the deceased Barbara Stroelini, Magdalena and Wilhelma, in their inheritance matter. The sisters were passed over in the deceased's last will and testament for unfounded reasons. The Bregenz authorities ask for a written answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain Hans Bürer von Schwyz, bailiff and Council of Bischofszell, informs that the deceased hospital master Villerius Kübler had bought three white thick cloths from strangers in St. Gallen. The cloths had been bleached in St. Gallen, but none had been usable, as they were afflicted with Lügern. Bischofszell asks St. Gallen to investigate who had sold the cloths and to communicate the results.
en.sender: Captain Hans Bürer von Schwyz, bailiff and Council of Bischofszell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Magdalena Spettin, who lives in St. Gallen, to satisfy her creditor Peter Krautschel or to appear before the Lindau city court on 26 May. They refer to two unsuccessful summonses and threaten further measures in case of continued disobedience.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Ybbs report that the widow Barbara Werdenbergin, wife of the former citizen of Ybbs Jacob Cropper, had exposed her three children in the cold before the city. The children had been taken in at the Ybbs hospital. Since Barbara is staying in St. Gallen, the Ybbs authorities ask the St. Gallen authorities to detain her and make her pick up and provide for her children, otherwise they will initiate legal proceedings.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Bistanz to help the citizens of St. Gallen Jörg Zollikoffer, Jacob and Sigmund Zollikoffer, as well as Caspar Scherer. They were swindled out of goods and money by the former Governor of Sargans, Jeronimo de Rossi, called La Fortune. The St. Gallen authorities ask for swift justice and repayment of the damage together with interest from the money deposited with La Fortune.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Bistanz

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to remind their citizen Hans Signer of his oath and to compel him to appear before the Schaffhausen court on 28 September. The heirs of the deceased Schaffhausen citizen Jeremias Stierlin have brought a claim against Signer and Heinrich Prickhart. Signer had obligated himself to submit to the law. Schaffhausen has issued a new judgment and urged the parties to a friendly settlement, which Signer refused.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the city of Schaffhausen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report that Adelheid Rinderknecht, from Fluntern, was forced into marriage by the citizen of St. Gallen, Baschian Teschler, in Straßburg and taken away. Teschler's sister had promised before the Zürich marriage court to present her brother on the court day, which did not happen. Zürich asks St. Gallen to detain Teschler and his sister so that they appear before the Zürich marriage court on 18 September and answer the claim of the Rinderknechtin.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen inform that the court day scheduled for 22 September has been postponed to 27 October due to other business. They ask St. Gallen to compel their citizen Hans Scherer to appear at the hearing, as he has already promised to do, and expect that he will refute his excuse.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Kriegsrat of Zürich reports to the Eerichter of St. Gallen on the examination of witnesses in the marriage dispute between Adelheid Rinderknächtin and Baschion Tischler. The witnesses confirm that Tischler had married the Rinderknächtin and wished to have her church wedding. Since Tischler’s sister had undertaken that he would appear in person in Zürich, the Council asks for acknowledgment.
en.sender: Kriegsrat of the city and territory of Zürich
en.recipient: Eerichter of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Hans Grübler, living in Lyon, in the collection of a claim of 3077 Sonnenkronen against the heirs of the deceased St. Gallen Sebastian Zollikofer. The heirs had deposited their assets in St. Gallen, but it is not enough for all creditors. Zürich refers to the fact that, according to the statutes of St. Gallen, the Confederates are to be served before foreigners, and asks that Grübler be treated accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Radolfzell reply to a letter from St. Gallen dated 14 November. They report that on their markets, corn dealers and merchants had driven up grain prices through dishonest practices, such as buying in large quantities and driving up prices. They had imposed penalties for such violations of the market regulations. They had not yet heard of any citizens of St. Gallen who had participated in such practices. They recommend that all neighbors should instruct their citizens to behave more modestly when buying and not to make markups.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to lend them 200 gulden for half a year. They also request that the building authority Hans Alder and Captain Jost Össlin be supported and that the interest on the already lent 400 gulden be deferred. They justify the request with the high costs for the construction of a new house and the money from Frundsberg not arriving.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Chur request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a report on the conviction and execution of a person for murder, fraud, and arson. They wish to know how the trial proceeded and to which nation the executed person belonged, in order to be better able to guard against the daily increasing wandering people, particularly from the Netherlands.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have acceded to the request of the Confederates of Solothurn for an extension of the day's contribution set for 26 August (old style). The day's contribution was extended until 30 September (old style). Zürich hopes that this extension will not displease St. Gallen and the other Confederates.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Georg Redenhober in the collection of a claim of 56 gulden plus costs. Redenhober says that he sold wine to the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Melchior Hardennrieder and received payment for only a part. The rest remained as a pledge with Hardennrieder. Since the heirs of the deceased were now entitled to inheritances, Redenhober wants to exercise his pledge right.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Solothurn ask Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich to cancel the Tagleistung scheduled for 5 September in Baden and to extend it by one month. They say that they have been informed that the French King in Blois is deliberating on the means for the payments of the Confederation, but that the decision will not arrive before 5 September. Solothurn hopes that the other cantons will agree to the extension.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Solothurn
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to transmit to them the estate of the deceased Veronika Ösenin, a citizen of Zürich, after deduction of table money and costs, along with a list of the dispositions. The heirs, among them Bartli Ösenin, Hans Rüngg and Hans Heinrich Wälti, had complained that Ösenin, as a person under guardianship, had not been entitled to make dispositions in favor of non-heirs. Zürich wants to distribute the estate among the natural heirs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to cause their citizens Jacob and Sigmund Zollikofer to adhere to the contract concluded with the Kempten citizen Martin Buher and not to harass him any further. Kempten will protect the Zollikofer in any potential legal dispute with their imperial and royal freedoms.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to protect the heirs of the deceased citizen Veronica Osterin in their inheritance rights. Her cousin Heinrich Osteri, a shoemaker from Adliswil, claims the estate that the deceased left in St. Gallen, and has led some citizens of St. Gallen to trust him. Zürich points out that Osteri is a disreputable person and that the inheritance is hardly worth anything, and asks that the heirs not be hindered.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
