en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Bern to help their citizen Caspar Toubacher in enforcing a claim against the deceased Bern citizen David Gier. Gier had committed himself before his death to satisfy his creditors and to settle accounts with Toubacher, which he had not done. St. Gallen has sent the councilor Johann Jacob Rüdlinger as support for Toubacher and asks Bern for support so that Toubacher can assert his claim in court.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Bern

en.regest: The sender rebukes the Wachter for the demand of 10 kreuzer for old wine, as he cannot consume the new wine. He complains about the Züllig, who has forced him and his children into his house, takes 2 florins in interest weekly, and harms other honest people. The sender threatens to go to the Burgomaster and refers to the responsibility before God.
en.recipient: Wachter

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to issue a letter of recommendation to the widow Anna Lochin, née Brugger. She wishes to assert the bequest of the recently deceased Elisabetha Bruggerin in the St. Gallen hospital for her children as heirs. The children are the next heirs, as the deceased left no closer relatives.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen David Zollikofer to lift the unauthorized seizure of the trading house balances of the widow and children of the deceased Sigmund Püchler in the Wolfskehle. Zollikofer had only asserted the claim for his factor Peter Püchler from Nürnberg, who does not represent the other Püchlers. Ulm requests the lifting of the seizure and peace for the Püchlers.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the citizens Jakob and Sigmund Zollighofer to comply with the contract concluded with the Kempten citizen Martin Güser and not to obstruct him any further. Kempten threatens otherwise to assert the imperial and royal freedoms.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to Abbot Bernhard on the events concerning Martin Strub. They reject his claim that he was imprisoned and his goods confiscated because of his new Catholic faith. In fact, he had been imprisoned for fraudulent actions towards his parents and relatives. They ask the Abbot to defend them against the false accusations with Cardinal S. Severinae and the Nuncio in Luzern.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Bernhard, Abbot of the Monastery of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ulrich Nagel, Ammann, and the judges of the city court of Lindau request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to summon their citizen Lorenz Zolligkoffer as a witness in a legal dispute between the Lindau schoolmaster Ulrich Loher and the citizens of Wil Caspar Steübler and Rudolf Hoeger. They ask that the witness be examined, his testimony recorded, and the document returned sealed.
en.sender: Ulrich Nagel, Ammann, and the judges of the city court of Lindau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich state that the chancery clerk Moßer of the Prelate of St. Gallen has uttered insulting remarks against the Reformed religion and the Zürich Bible in the inn called zum Rössli in St. Gallen. They ask St. Gallen to set a court day against Moßer and to question witnesses, so that Zürich may sue him before the St. Gallen court for defamation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich invite Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to a Confederate Diet on 21 September 1600 in Baden. The occasion is the military actions between Frankreich and Savoyen as well as the delayed French payments. The envoys are to appear with full power and to deliberate on the pacification of the princes as well as the demand of the Evangelical cities.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform St. Gallen that they have examined two witnesses in the marriage case between Christoph Büchler and Margaretha Atzenholzin. They send the statements of the wife of the Lindau town steward and the daughter of a citizen of Lindau. The witnesses report on visits to Emps and to the St. Gallen fair as well as on the bride's willingness to wait for the groom.
en.recipient: Judges of the marriage case in St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Landvogt of Bischofszell dated 25 September, which refers to a request by Kaspar Schnizer to the St. Gallen citizen Hans Jakob Schölin. Schölin states that he has kept the purchase contract with Schnizer and thereby discharged the obligation. He is ready to have justice done before his ordinary judge. The St. Gallen ask the Landvogt to leave Schölin with this offer and not to impose anything further on him.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt of Bischofszell

en.regest: The bailiff and Council of Bischofzell report that their citizen Jacob Krumenbach has requested written information on how unpaid purchase prices for fruit are handled in St. Gallen. This is necessary because a trial by evidence is pending before the St. Gallen city court in a dispute between Krumenbach and the heirs of the deceased Stofel Rietmann over the purchase of linen, interest, and old debts. Bischofzell forwards Krumenbach's request and reminds them of the previous court order.
en.sender: The bailiff and Council of Bischofzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Hamburg request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their subject Ulrich Bader and his creditors. Bader has been arrested because of a high debt he assumed for the merchants of St. Gallen Hans Heinrich Reiner and Jakob Kirchmann. The creditors had promised payment but did not make it. Hamburg requests that the debtors and their sureties be compelled to fulfill their obligations, otherwise legal steps be enabled.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Hamburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to proceed against Erasmus Messner, chancery clerk of the Abbot of St. Gallen. Messner has evaded a lawsuit for defamatory remarks against the Bible. The men of Zürich ask that Messner be arrested and imprisoned upon entering the territory of St. Gallen, in order to be able to continue the lawsuit.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report that they have received a written reply from the Duke of Savoyen to a letter from Baden. They send a copy of this letter to St. Gallen so that the city can instruct its envoys for the next Baden Diet accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Pfleger, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the creditors of the Hamburg citizen Ulrich Boders. The citizens of St. Gallen Hieronymus Signer, Daniel Zuegermann and Georg Eirrer had guaranteed Boders' debts and pledged their goods. Augsburg requests St. Gallen to compel these citizens to fulfill their obligations towards Boders' attorney-in-fact Melchior Huebvechter.
en.sender: Pfleger, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Elders of the evangelical Church in Lyon ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for financial support. They describe the distress of their community, which has fallen into poverty due to persecution and civil wars. They must buy and build a house of worship, render an account before the authority, which is hostile to their religion, and send envoys to the King. They promise that God will repay the kindness.
en.sender: The Elders of the Church in Lyon
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Duke Heinrich Julius asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hear Doctor Ruetger Rulandt or his representative in a legal matter against three fellow citizens of St. Gallen. He requests that the documents be sent to a university for legal assessment and that a just judgment be rendered.
en.sender: Heinrich Julius, Bishop of Halberstadt and Duke of Braunschweig and Lüneburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Otto Duke of Braunschweig and Lüneburg asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant swift legal aid to the jurist Rutger Rulant and his clients, the Hamburgers, who have a claim against Ulrich Bader of Augsburg. Rulant has offered himself as the authorized representative of the creditors to conduct the case in St. Gallen. The Duke assures that the claim is legitimate and asks that his intercession be made fruitful.
en.sender: Otto Duke of Braunschweig and Lüneburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Margrave Joachim Friedrich zu Brandenburg asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to treat the legal counsel Rutger Ruland, who acts as the authorized representative of a creditor, favorably in an ongoing lawsuit. He refers to the attached letters of introduction and requests that the attorney be helped lawfully in the preliminary and main procedural matters, so that he can exercise his powers and continue the lawsuit.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Frankfurt request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist Doctor of Laws Rutger Ruland, the authorized representative of the guardians of the minor son of the deceased citizen of Frankfurt Rutger Ruland, in the collection of a debt of the citizen of Augsburg Ulrich Bader in St. Gallen. The guardians request advance and promotion so that the ward be paid.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizen and trumpeter Stefan Bältschi. The St. Gallen trumpeter Michel Löw owes Bältschi 8 gulden and 16 schillings for a surety that Bältschi had posted for Löw. Löw also owed Bältschi 2 gulden in horse hire and was supposed to return an old trumpet, which he had refused to do. Zürich asks St. Gallen to compel Löw to pay and to make amends for the honor.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Burgomaster and Council of Wangen that their bleacher Ulrich Wasser had an entire piece of linen stolen on Tuesday evening. They ask the Wangen authorities to conduct inquiries, identify and punish the perpetrator, and return the stolen goods. St. Gallen offers the same assistance in return.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Wangen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg reply to the petition of the wife of the citizen of Nürnberg Jacob Mair. They state that before their court, impartial justice is done to any creditor who liquidates his claim and proves a better legal basis, without favoring locals. They ask St. Gallen to allow Mair to be granted the due right in his lawsuit against the goods of the family Rhiner (Sichmer).
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report that their butchers complain about the low meat tax, as they would have to buy the meat more expensively than in the neighborhood. They ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform them how the meat prices in St. Gallen are set and whether the city grants the butchers a subsidy for good livestock.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send the judgments against convicted criminals as well as a list of the other persons named by them. They wish to better monitor evildoers wandering around in the area and to secure the roads.
en.sender: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to postpone the court day set for 24 July in the marriage case between Johann Aicholtz and Peter Zollikofer. Aicholtz is prevented from attending due to the death of his mother Dorothea and other obstacles. They ask for an extension of two months and the setting of a new date.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Friedrich, Pfalzgraf bei Rhein, Kurfürst und Herzog in Bayern, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist his Landesschreiber Christoph Waldis in the collection of a claim against the heirs of the deceased St. Gallen citizen Gall Stähelin. Waldis had stood surety for Stähelin and settled his debts. The heirs have now received an inheritance and should repay the money advanced. The Kurfürst requests support for the authorized representative Waldis and a written answer.
en.sender: Friedrich, Pfalzgraf bei Rhein, Kurfürst, Herzog in Bayern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: M. de Vic reports that his envoy returned on 16 August and confirmed the King's good will towards St. Gallen regarding the renewal of the alliance and the satisfaction of the demands of the Nation. He asks that envoys with full power be sent to Solothurn on 8 or 9 September to hear the King's intentions. Furthermore, he requests that until the next Diet all persecutions and executions against the Colonels and Captains who served in Frankreich be suspended, so that these can satisfy their creditors.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they consider the Nuntius's proposal for an Inquisition in Mailand a suitable means to avert the complaints of the evangelical merchants. They have decided to send two Council members to Luzern and ask the St. Gallen to also send representatives so that they can consult with the Zürcher in Zürich on 26 September.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Luzern request Burgomaster and Council of Zürich to react to the complaints regarding the Inquisition in Mailand. The papal Nuntius has agreed to hear the complaints and to promote an amicable settlement. Luzern asks Zürich to send some Council members to Luzern to negotiate with the Nuntius and to convey the specific points of complaint. Furthermore, Zürich is asked to inform St. Gallen at the next Diet in Solothurn, so that this city can also send representatives to Luzern.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel their citizen Caspar Hueber to pay the outstanding principal debt, together with interest and costs, to Felicitas Hirthin, a citizen of Memmingen, widow of Jacob Heinrich Stoltzen. They ask for a written answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the negotiations with the papal Nuntius in Luzern. He has promised that the Inquisition in Mailand will no longer harass the Confederates and Zugewandten who trade there in the future. They ask St. Gallen to instruct their own envoys accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Friedrich Graf zu Fürstenberg thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the transmitted letter and the transmitted cask of wine. He explains that the honor was not necessary, as he would rather wish to serve them to a greater extent. He assures them of his good intentions and intends to reciprocate this in the future.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg forward a declaration by the guardians of Katharina Zollikofer to the Council of St. Gallen. The guardians thank them for the appointment of Matthias Schlaipfer as administrator of the assets of the minors. They request the annual payment of 30 florins for taxes and the needs of the minors. They leave the further accusations of the Zollikofer against the guardians to the Council of St. Gallen, as it knows the state of affairs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Glarus thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the support of the evangelical community in Linthal. The latter received 200 silver crowns for the construction of a church and the maintenance of a preacher, which were accepted by Caspar Schlumpf. Glarus offers St. Gallen its services for this favor and asks for mutual friendship.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen congratulate Bishop Johann Georg on his election and ask him, together with the Abbot of St. Gallen, to intervene with the Nuncio in Luzern for the release of the St. Gallen citizen Ludwig Küng, who is imprisoned in Mailand.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Johann Georg, Bishop of Konstanz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Basel ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizen and linen weaver Jakob Küenrodt in the taking possession of an inheritance. This inheritance has fallen to him, alongside other co-heirs, from his deceased cousin Margarethe Synerin. They request that the citizen be kept in good command and that his share of the inheritance be awarded to him without deductions.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Magister Jacob Torhart, who comes from Württemberg and has fallen into disgrace because of his evangelical conviction, has arrived in Zürich. Since the positions in Zürich are filled, they direct Torhart to St. Gallen and ask that he be taken on for school or church service.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizen Michael Lidel. Lidel complains about his fellow citizen of St. Gallen, Jacob Küchen, regarding outstanding payments. Since the debt is clear according to the attached document, the Nurembergers request that Küchen be compelled to pay the delayed arrears.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Genf apologize to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the outstanding payment of a principal sum with interest. They justify the delay with the ongoing conflicts and costs caused by the officials of the Duke of Savoyen, who seeks to bring Genf under his power by cunning and intrigue. They promise to satisfy the creditors at the first opportunity.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Mery de Vic, Councilor of the King and Ambassador in Switzerland, promises the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to transmit to the King the receipt of the Treasurer Claude Doux dated 30 May 1589 for 10'000 gold escudos. He assures that the King, upon his command, will pay out this sum in gold escudos together with interest.
en.sender: Mery de Vic, Sieur de Moran, Councilor of the King and Ambassador in Switzerland
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to investigate the dispute between Ulrich Stocker and his son regarding the maternal estate of the deceased Margaretha Muntpratin. They ask to be informed whether a part of this estate is recorded in the Weissenbuch in St. Gallen, and request copies of any partition proceedings in order to be able to settle the parties accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich grant the Landvogt Adrian Ziegler permission to have the marriage between Lienhart Zollikofer and Sabina Schlumpf, who are related in the third degree, sealed by the church in his administrative jurisdiction. They ask him not to impose fines or monetary penalties, as the bride and groom reside in St. Gallen and were not permitted to marry there.
en.recipient: Landvogt in the Upper and Lower Rhine Valley, Adrian Ziegler

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to pardon the citizens of St. Gallen Leonhart Zollikofer and Sabina Schlumpf, who are married in Zürich, and to readmit them to the citizenship. The marriage was contracted against the St. Gallen statute on degrees of kinship. Zürich refers to the honorable lineages of those involved and asks for a dispensation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Wil to instruct their citizen Gabriel Rauner to dissuade the two butchers Heinrich Tobler and Jacob Rietmann from their claim to three casings. These had been promised by contract to the Wil gold-beater Hans Allgeer. The St. Gallen side asks for the dispute to be settled and offers reciprocity.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Wil

fixed: the model left out the two butchers in every attempt; sentence corrected by hand against the German (14.11.2026)

en.regest: The Kilchgnoßen of the Evangelical Church in Linthal thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a donation to their new church. As a sign of gratitude, they deliver a pair of Gämse from the Freiberg and ask that these be accepted willingly.
en.sender: Kilchgnoßen of the Evangelical Church in Linthal
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Bishop Johann Georg zu Konstanz reproaches the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen because they had arrested the St. Gallen citizen Daniel Schüchermacher and his accomplices despite an existing court proceeding in Bischofszell and an oath sworn in St. Gallen. He demands the release of the arrested Georg Riedtmann and requires that Schüchermacher continue the proceeding in Bischofszell, as the appeal to the Hofgericht remains open.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Burgomaster and Council of Kempten to send them a reliable copy of the testament of the deceased citizen of Kempten, Hans Scherrer. This is necessary, as the widow of the citizen of St. Gallen, Caspar von Büel, Rosina, has left a testament in which she disposes of her estate. Since Scherrer was married to her daughter and had also made a testament, which is unknown to the widow, St. Gallen needs the copy in order to act correctly in the matter.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizen Jacob Weigen in a claim against the Hamburg merchant Ulrich Bader. Weigen says that he delivered water to Bader, which the latter does not pay. Bader has furthermore plunged Weigen into great costs in an arrest matter. Nürnberg asks to arrest the goods of Bader in St. Gallen, so that Weigen can make up for his damage.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nördlingen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizens Hans Zichlinger and Wolfgang Vischer, both tanners, with official help. These have 593 gulden outstanding from the St. Gallen citizen Jacob Küschler for purchased hides. Küschler says that he sold the hides to Konstanz and Zell, although he should have delivered them to Lindau. The Nördlingen request support so that the creditors regain their property.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Hans Heinrich Rüttlinger in the collection of a debt from Hans Rhyner. Rüttlinger had Rhyner forbid the pigs that are pledged to him. The St. Gallen authorities are to support Rüttlinger in the exercise of law so that he may receive payment of his claim and the costs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Luzern request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Sebastian Klöstriger in asserting an inheritance right. Klöstriger is the nephew of the deceased Barbara Nüssin, who had been married in St. Gallen and maintained in the hospital. After the death of her second husband, the citizen of Zürich Jost Meier, Klöstriger had claimed his aunt's estate. The city of Luzern requests the St. Gallen authorities for documentary information about the estate.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Elisabeth Stein, widow of Caspar von Freubel, replies to the letter of the Council of Kempten. She disputes the validity of the testament of her deceased daughter presented by her son-in-law Martin Schmelzen, as it was forced. She appeals to her right to make a free testament and asks the Council of St. Gallen to confirm her testamentary disposition and to reject Schmelzen's objections.
en.sender: Elisabeth Stein, widow of Caspar von Freubel
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to mediate with the relatives of the St. Gallen citizen Christoph Zollikofer. Zollikofer had taken possession of the estate of his brother-in-law Hans Jacob Lamman, who had died in Paris in 1594. Now Zollikofer is being claimed by Hans Stumpfer for a debt of Lamman. The Zürichers ask that the heirs of Lamman be released from this claim, in order to avoid further legal disputes.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizen Hans Wadus in the collection of a claim of 64 florins against the heirs of the deceased Jakob Fritschis. Wadus says that despite earlier intercession he has not yet received any payment and must cease his business. The city of St. Gallen refers to the joint linen trade and asks for superior help so that Wadus may receive his money.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Syndics and the Council of Genf report to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on the failed raid of the Duke of Savoyen on 12 December and the subsequent offensive of the Confederates. They ask for voluntary financial support, as they need funds for the war against Savoyen, Frankreich and Spanien, and promise their services in return.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Bishop Johann Georg of Konstanz answers the St. Gallen submission in the dispute between Georg Riedtmann and Daniel Spichermann over linen. He refers to an old custom, according to which St. Gallen, Appenzell, and Bischofszell may not arrest one another, and orders Riedtmann not to appear before the court in St. Gallen, but to conduct the already pending legal matter in Bischofszell.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report that the Confederation at the Diet in Baden 1602 set a tax of six kreuzer per salt cask on the salt imported from Lindau, in order to cover the costs of an embassy to Innsbruck. They ask St. Gallen to pay the share of the citizens there according to the attached excerpt from the Lindau record.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Wil request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the guild not to hinder the son of their sworn constable Hans Lienberger, called Koch, in his apprenticeship as a cutler. They refer to the honour and office of their constable and request a written or oral answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Chur thank St. Gallen for the receipt of a letter and some false coins, which were found with a market visitor. They ask to be informed if St. Gallen learns anything about the Bishops of Chur, in order to be able to pursue the matter better. The coins, which are similar to the episcopal coinage, were handed over to the Prince-Bishopess and the mint master, who would address St. Gallen directly on this matter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Bishop Johannes of Chur informs that he was informed by the city of St. Gallen about false coins bearing the stamp of his predecessor Petrus. He affirms the integrity of his mint master and asks the citizens of St. Gallen to investigate where the false coins come from and to report the result to him.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report that they have executed Theiß Precher von Lüssingen, who had been convicted as a thief. He is said to have named further accomplices, some of whom would have fled to Switzerland. Lindau sends a list of the wanted persons and asks St. Gallen to keep an eye on them in its territory, to arrest them, and to forward the list to other neighbors.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Arbon report that their Council member Rudolf Baur, who is suing his stepfather Zacharias Küntzer, was insulted and threatened by the latter when he delivered a legal document to him. They ask St. Gallen for support for Baur and for a written statement on the recent negotiations between the cities.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Council of the city of Arbon declare to Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen that they hold the neighborly settlement and the contract concluded between the cities inviolable. They ask for a written answer.
en.sender: Ammann and Council of the city of Arbon
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizen Heinrich Ziegler and his fellow council member Adrian Ziegler in the settlement of the estate of the deceased Maria Zieglerin, widow of the St. Gallen council member Hermann Schlumpf. They request support so that the widow and her children are provided for according to equity and protected in their rights to the bequests of the deceased.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Council of Arbon declare that they did not wish to offend St. Gallen with the letter of 7 June, but to show good neighborliness. A dispute arose between the St. Gallen Council member Rudolf Teüblin and the Arbon resident Zacharias Kienzen. Arbon will uphold its rights in the matter and send St. Gallen the due response.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to make a gift to the Evangelicals in Egolshausen and Rickenbach, who have newly built their chapel. They have supported the construction with a bell and hope that St. Gallen will also donate. They promise to reciprocate in similar cases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Bishop Johann Georg zu Konstanz informs that there are disputes between Rudolf Stürzenacker and the St. Gallen citizen Zacharias Bungen. He holds an existing contract to be inapplicable, as it refers to common lands and debts, not to real estate. He requests the Council of St. Gallen to instruct Bungen to submit to legal proceedings in Arbon, where the disputed property is located. He offers to do the same in similar cases towards St. Gallen citizens.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Adrian Ziegler von Zürich, Landvogt in Rinthall, asks Burgomaster Othmar Rinner of St. Gallen to intercede with town clerk Melchior Huber. He wishes to have his son, who is proficient in Latin and French, admitted to the chancery for one or two years as a discipline. The town clerk has concerns about doing this without the consent of the Council. Ziegler asks Rinner to advocate this to the town clerk or to inform the Council, leaving the decision on the form to the Burgomaster.
en.recipient: Burgomaster Othmar Rinner of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Count von Fuentes, Governor of the Duchy of Mailand, has prohibited the passage of merchants' goods and trade with the Confederates. Since this is regarded as a hostile action, they invite to a joint assembly on 2 October 1603 in Baden to deliberate on the situation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen, in which the latter complains about grievances of the citizens and merchants there caused by the clergy in Thun. Zürich declares itself willing to provide assistance and asks St. Gallen to send an envoy to the Diet of Baden, so that the matter can be discussed jointly with other Protestant cantons.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Konrad Küttlinger. He has a claim of 76 florins against the St. Gallen butcher Hans Kyner, which is based on a debt of the deceased Sebastian Tuchschren. Kyner has not paid Küttlinger, whereupon the latter had a pig seized in Wil. Kyner has freed himself from the arrest and forced Küttlinger to pay the costs, which is why the latter had to provide surety. Zürich asks St. Gallen to move Kyner to pay the principal, interest, and costs and to release the surety in Wil.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm request the City Court of St. Gallen, in the legal dispute concerning the outstanding wages of the deceased Captain Studer, to take into consideration the mother of the Ulm citizen Conrad Neier. As she is poor, she asks for assistance. Ulm requests that the money due to the son be paid to her or to her son, if the latter is still alive.
en.recipient: Stattammann and Urthelsprechern of the City Court of St. Gallen

en.regest: Town clerk and Council of Arbon ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their envoys in the matter concerning the estate of the deceased Hiltbrand. The creditors of the deceased falsely claimed that the silver deposited by the citizens of St. Gallen was his property. Arbon asks for assistance so that the matter is resolved without damage. Furthermore, Arbon promises to treat citizens of St. Gallen in similar cases as its own.
en.sender: Town clerk and Council of Arbon
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Bishop Johann Georg zu Konstanz asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to promote the return of silverware that had been entrusted to the deceased St. Gallen goldsmith Joachim Hilbrand. He refers to the report of the father and council of Arbon and to the fact that the silverware belongs not to the St. Gallers, but to other interested parties. He requests an amicable settlement.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich invite Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to a Diet of the Confederates in Baden, which takes place on 29 January 1604. They ask that envoys with full power be sent to deliberate on the tense situation on the borders, particularly around Genf, and on the French soldier payment, in order to preserve peace and unity in the Confederation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rottach ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to prohibit the issuance and receipt of coins that have been raised above their usual value in the city and at the customs barriers. They demand that trade in grain be handled by the merchants of the city in order to protect the market. They threaten penalties in case of non-compliance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Blasius Zimmermann, Imperial Chief Court and Field Quartermaster at Bregenz, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in the name of Archduke Ferdinand of Österreich, for the sale of saltpeter or powder. He refers to the necessity of supplying the border fortresses against the Turks and promises good payment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admit the Schaffhausen citizen Lienhart Keller and his fiancée, the daughter of the St. Gallen citizen Jakob Wergel, as citizens. The engagement was concluded before the new St. Gallen regulation regarding the dowry for foreigners. Keller cannot raise the new 200 pounds, but has promised the old 50 pounds. Schaffhausen asks that, in the assessment of the marriage, regard be had for the earlier promise.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jakob Füger, Auxiliary Bishop and Cathedral Provost of Konstanz, reminds the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of a letter from the late Bishop Johann Georg dated 14 August 1603. It concerns a dispute between the St. Gallen citizen Zacharias Künzli and the Arbon resident Rudolf Tübben over the refusal to return a pledge. Tübben had asked the Abbey for help. Füger asks the St. Gallen authorities to comply with the earlier letter and to settle the matter amicably, in order to avoid further complaints.
en.sender: Jakob Füger, Auxiliary Bishop and Cathedral Provost of Konstanz, also Dekan and common Chapter of the high Abbey there
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the Diet performance scheduled for the Sunday of Laetare in Baden was cancelled due to the French payments, upon the request of the envoys of the Zehn Orte and with the knowledge of Bern. They ask the St. Gallen to hold back their messengers, and promise to inform them in good time if another Diet performance should be necessary before the annual accounts.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the Confederate Diet scheduled for Sunday Laetare in Baden was cancelled due to the French payments. They set a new Diet for Sunday Jubilate, 29 April, in the evening in Baden, and ask St. Gallen to send its messengers with full power.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jakob Erwert, Bishop and Cathedral Provost of Konstanz, thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the reply to his letter regarding the dispute between Zacharias Vintzler and Jakob Teuber. He proposes to settle the dispute amicably and offers to send a delegation together with the St. Gallen representatives to persuade the parties to reach a settlement.
en.sender: Jakob Erwert, Bishop and Cathedral Provost of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a legal dispute between the citizen of St. Gallen Jacob Scharpf and Lienhardt Keller. Scharpf complained that Keller, as his son-in-law, had promised him 50 florins but had not paid, which would cost Scharpf his citizenship. Keller asked for a postponement until after his death. Schaffhausen ordered Keller to pay Scharpf 50 florins by St. George's Day, and asks St. Gallen to patiently tolerate Scharpf and his wife and to treat them as citizens.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Friedrich Graf zu Fürstenberg for his efforts in a dispute between their citizens Christoph Stümen and Georg Käßler and Jews before the Imperial Council. They ask him to maintain his benevolent will and to contribute with his authority to the swift settlement of the matter.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Friedrich Graf zu Fürstenberg

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of the outer Rode of the Land of Appenzell request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have their citizen Gabriel Gmuer marry the Appenzeller Anna Roderin. Gmuer is said to have fathered a child on her six years ago and promised marriage. Anna Roderin is said to have raised the child to this day and always refused separation from Gmuer. The Appenzellers request that Gmuer be moved to conclude the marriage, otherwise they will take him to court.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the outer Rode of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant their citizen Lienhard Keller and his daughter, who is married to the St. Gallen citizen Jakob Gschwendt, a short grace period to pay the promised 50 gulden. Keller says that he cannot pay the money in cash, but wants to pay in the autumn. The St. Gallen authorities had demanded that the citizenship be cancelled, which Keller does not want. Schaffhausen asks for patience and promises to reciprocate in similar cases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Schultheiss and Council of Wil to inspect the dishonourable linen cloths seized there and in Lindau. Since many linen cloths were stolen from the St. Gallen bleaching grounds this year, the men of Wil are to examine the fabrics and, if they belong to the St. Gallen citizens, hand them over to them. St. Gallen assures that it will return the linen cloths to the rightful owners according to sworn documents.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Wil

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Landvogt Heinrich Clausen to exert influence on the community of St. Margrethe. It is to adhere to the existing contracts and leave the property of the St. Gallen citizen Heinrich Scherer, which he has inherited from his deceased wife, undisturbed, without increasing the tax. The community had already promised this earlier, but now wants to revoke it.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Captain Heinrich Clausen, Landvogt of the lower and upper Rintal

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Wil inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that a Wil bleacher had stolen linen which a man from Wattwil in the County of Toggenburg had sold in Wil and given in Baden for dyeing. The man had been apprehended in Baden. Wil offers to help the bleacher with a letter to the Lords of Baden so that he may recover his property. The eight ells of linen that had remained in Wil would be credited to the bleacher.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report that the Imperial Majesty, in the annual account in Baden, had again requested the Confederates to state their position regarding the House of Österreich and Müllhausen. The eight cantons that had denounced the Confederation to Müllhausen refused to deal with the matter. The evangelical cantons resolved to hold an assembly in Aarau on 29 July to deliberate on the answer to the Emperor and the further course of action. They ask St. Gallen to send a councillor with full power in good time.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the reinforcement of an old land law, according to which interest deeds and promissory notes on Appenzell properties may not be taken out of the land or pledged. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to oblige their citizens to present such deeds to the Landammann within two months, in order to punish violations. Furthermore, the practice of property valuation is restricted in order to protect debtors.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inquire with the deceased Daniel Zolligkofen as to the name of the mason who, three months ago, collected and paid for 800 unburnt bricks. They ask that the mason be summoned and examined under oath as to which Lindau official he first reported to, who gave him the bricks, and what he paid. The answer is to be communicated to the messenger or in writing.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the transmission of a captured boy and his statement. They report that they had inspected the aforementioned places together with the citizens of St. Gallen and the boy and examined the conditions there. The corpses had not been found despite diligent search. Appenzell assures its friendship and readiness for mutual support.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Matheus Wiheloth in the collection of a claim. They refer to a petition by Wiheloth, which they have handed over to the St. Gallen authorities. Lindau asks for favorable support, as the citizen is in urgent need of the money.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The eight Catholic cantons thank St. Gallen for the support with the Pope and the Cardinal in favor of the citizens Schlumpf. They confirm the lifting of the arrest on the goods of the citizens of St. Gallen lying in Italien and hand these over. They promise further friendship of the Confederation and refer for the rest to the royal letters.
en.sender: Schultheiss, Landammann and Council of the eight Catholic cantons, of the Confederation, Luzern, Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden, Zug, Freiburg and Solothurn, also Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admit their citizen Hans Grünenburg, Sporer, to the city, as there is a shortage of craftsmen there. They assure that he lives honestly and masters the craft, and offer surety through three other citizens.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council in the Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to take Magdalena Strickherin, who is married to the citizen of St. Gallen Melchior Falchen, into their favor and grace. They request that she may reside in St. Gallen as a citizen, without her illegitimate birth, since her parents had been banished from Appenzell, working to her detriment.
en.sender: Landammann and Council in the Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Luzern thank for the support of the Herren Schliniger and Römer in Rome. They declare themselves ready to comply with the wish of the Confederates, and advise waiting for the arrival of the Nuntius in order to regulate the matter better. They promise to inform St. Gallen about the arrival, so that the envoys there can be recalled.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Syndics and Council of Genf thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the hospitality shown to the gentlemen Sarasin and Roset during their passage. They offer their services and ask that the friendship be preserved and that support be sought from the Confederate cantons against the daily threats.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich send to St. Gallen the contract of the deceased Captain Alexander Studer regarding the French pay. They ask that the citizen of Zürich, Hans Konrad Koller, who demands 50 Kronen per captain for the mediation, be compensated from the first pay amount.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Bailiff, Ammann and Council of Arbon inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have set a debt day for the creditors of the deceased town clerk Luz Strüßey for 14 June. Since citizens of St. Gallen would have claims against Strüßey, they ask the St. Gallen authorities to notify them so that they can appear at the appointed time.
en.sender: Bailiff, Ammann and Council of Arbon
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizen Christoph Rad. He says that he was unjustly arrested by men of St. Gallen in Reineck and forced to provide bail. Lindau requests that the arrest be lifted and the dispute be adjudicated before the court of St. Gallen.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Caumartin informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he will pay them two outstanding pensions of the King of Frankreich, namely that for 1594 and that for 1618. He assures them of his willingness to serve them in all matters.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The bailiff and Council of Bischofszell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hand over the child of the deceased Lorenz Schayenwiler, who has inherited in St. Gallen, to the St. Gallen almoner Jacob Klingenberg. Klingenberg has hitherto raised the child and is now to administer the inheritance. The heirs of the child demand an account of the administration.
en.sender: The bailiff and Council of Bischofszell
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to redeem and transfer to Zürich the 50 ducats due to their citizen Hans Conrad Koller from the contract of Captain Alexander Studer. Koller has assigned the sum to his creditors. Zürich refers to an earlier letter of 31 December and to the fact that the claims from other contracts have already been settled.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to determine a suitable day, at the earliest the coming Monday or Tuesday. On this day they want to send their Council envoys to St. Gallen to consult on some matters that have occurred, which they could not settle better in any other way, and to discuss everything that serves the good neighborhood.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Ausserrhoden at Appenzell inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that a day for the negotiation of the case of Ulli Lindner, who killed the deceased town clerk Peter Ochs, has been set for 17 May. Lindner is to appear in person. They ask for a free and safe escort for Lindner to and from, so that he is not curtailed in his right.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of Ausserrhoden at Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Thal confirm to St. Gallen that the imperial Archduke has raised the corn and sack toll by three kreuzer Heller per sack. They reject the complaint of the St. Gallen corn merchant Ulrich Zeiger, who had called the increase arbitrary and for private gain. The increase was carried out by the authority of the territorial prince.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rottachzell inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, due to abuses at the weekly corn market, they have agreed on a new regulation with Überlingen. The market is henceforth to begin between 2 and 3 o'clock in the afternoon and to end on Wednesday between 10 and 11 o'clock. They ask St. Gallen to make this ordinance known to the buyers and sellers. In a postscript, they justify the increase in the toll for grain and bleaching with the high construction and material costs for the market operation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about an agreement with Radolfzell regarding the regulation of the weekly corn market. They stipulate that the market is to be held on certain days and at certain times, and prohibit the use of certain coin types as well as the exceeding of the set rates under threat of confiscation.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Hans Scherer to keep his pledge. Scherer has not presented himself for the settlement of accounts with the Schaffhausen citizen Esaias Nünein for seven weeks. The Schaffhausen authorities ask for superior help so that the account can be settled and concluded.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Schaffhausen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Statthalter, bailiff, Schultheiss and Council of Wil inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the arrest of a Long Merchant, who confessed to having committed ten murders with his companions. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to inform them whether the man hanged in Wil the day before or the two suspects detained there know anything about the merchant referred to as Christa Bader from Tirol, or whether further names of the companions from Wien are known.
en.sender: Statthalter, bailiff, Schultheiss and Council of Wil
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their fellow citizen Caspar Harder. Harder wishes to take up the inheritance of his deceased sister-in-law Magdalena Kügel in St. Gallen. The city of Stein asks for favorable treatment, low costs, and swift assistance in the taking up of the inheritance.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Schaffhausen to intervene on behalf of their citizen Hans Keiner. He says that he was threatened by the Stierlischen on an imperial road. Furthermore, the St. Gallen hospital master had the Stierlischen's debt with Keiner seized. St. Gallen demands that the Stierlischen first legally lift the arrest before they take further steps against Keiner.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schaffhausen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen reply to the supplication of their citizen Hans Thainer. They declare that they have no interest in the incident in which the St. Gallen Jerg Thainer was insulted on a free imperial road and that they would punish Jerg for the deed during his lifetime. Since Thainer has surrendered himself, they summon Jerg to them for Wednesday before Bartholomäi, the 22. August, to negotiate the compensation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admit Hans Mörlin Jung, bailiff's son, grandson and brother-in-law of the Ravensburg fellow citizen Hans Mörlin, who has been in their service for about ten years, into citizenship. They certify his honest and diligent conduct and ask for favorable compliance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen address their Confederates in Schaffhausen. They refer to a previous contract between the St. Gallen citizen Hans Rinner and the Schaffhausen resident Niklaus Eubner, whereby both parties had sworn an oath not to pursue the matter judicially any further. They condemn the fact that Schaffhausen has reopened the law and forced Rinner to take an oath to comply with the judgment. This endangers an existing arrest in favor of the St. Gallen creditors. They demand that Schaffhausen maintain the arrest and not force Rinner into the process, otherwise they might not be able to allow him to participate.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen

en.regest: Leonhart Conrad, Stadtammann, and Judges of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly proclaim the assets of the citizen Melcher Lotter there, which lie in St. Gallen. This is done because bankruptcy proceedings have been opened against Lotter and he has debts to the citizens of St. Gallen. The creditors are to follow the procedure.
en.sender: Leonhart Conrad, Stadtammann, and Judges of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Jacob Tugginer, the baker, in the maintenance of a child. Tugginer has been feeding the illegitimate child of the widow Barbara Tugginer, which had returned to him after the death of the father Abraham Wetzel, for five years. Since the mother does not take the child back and the care falls too heavily on Tugginer, the men of Zürich ask for financial support so that Tugginer can keep the child with him.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The eight Catholic cantons request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to allow the subjects of the Abbey of St. Gallen from the old Landschafft to publicly carry the Cross during the annual Cross Procession, as was formerly customary. They refer to the mutual friendship and ask for a positive answer.
en.sender: Schultheissen, Landammann and Council of the eight Catholic cantons of the Confederation
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Bishop Jakob of Konstanz, Lord of the Reichenau and Oening, invites the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen as well as their citizens who hold fiefs of the Stift Konstanz or of the Gotteshaus Reichenau, for the 17th of January to an enfeoffment at Moersburg. He refers to the attached list of fief-holders and reserves his rights.
en.sender: Jakob, Bishop of Konstanz, Lord of the Reichenau and Oening
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Schwyz inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the imprisonment of Don Jeronimo de Sandt Element. He is said to have claimed to have received funds from merchants in Lucca via bills of exchange and passed them on to merchants of St. Gallen, namely Jacob Zoligkoffer. Schwyz asks for information on whether these statements are true, so that they can conduct themselves towards the prisoner.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Glarus reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen, which concerns the Glarus citizen Josef Klerer and his wife as well as the St. Gallen Statthalter Balthasar. Balthasar has declared that he is satisfied with the Glarus Council, but cannot compel Klerer's wife to hand over the lying principal estate, as its household is being managed carelessly. He demands a credible refutation that the estate was applied and consumed, so that it remains findable in the event of inheritance. Glarus asks for the fulfillment of this promise.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their fellow countryman Hans Metzger in the collection of a bequest of 30 florins. Metzger's mother-in-law, the late Königolt Bombgartnerin, had left this bequest to his wife, the natural daughter. The St. Gallen almoners had refused the payment, as the money was due to the almshouse. Schaffhausen requests that Metzger be treated favorably and that the 60 florins be awarded to him without deduction.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur answer the inquiry of St. Gallen regarding the inheritance of the deceased citizen Cicilia Kappler. They have not yet received any further information about the heirs. However, they have caused inquiries to be made and will instruct the heirs to appear on the day mentioned. If this does not happen, they will hand the matter over to St. Gallen without further delay.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell thank St. Gallen for its efforts towards an amicable settlement in the dispute between the St. Gallen citizen Balthasar Ferwer and the Appenzell countryman Bartholomäus Dörig. They confirm the agreements reached and ask St. Gallen to have Dörig immediately delivered the seals, letters, and other items belonging to him, which are still in the possession of Ferwer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Glarus ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admit the 36-year-old, blind and destitute wife of the departed Glarus countryman Melchior Kaufmann into their hospital. The woman has left behind five small children and is in need of support. Glarus requests a reasonable pension and promises to keep the agreed conditions.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to keep the daughter of the deceased citizen of Zürich, Nikolaus Seeholzer, Barbara Seeholzerin, and her husband, the citizen of St. Gallen N. Zollihofer, under their protection. They request that, in the event of violations of the ordinances of St. Gallen, they not proceed strictly, but leave the married couple in grace and honor.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Sigmund Luppin and the judges of the city court of Memmingen inform the court of St. Gallen that they have held a court day in the case of Daniel Dehmen against Ulrich and Gabriel Zelligkhofer. The witnesses were compelled to testify despite resistance. The testimonies and the compass letter are transmitted so that St. Gallen can continue the proceedings.
en.sender: Hans Sigmund Luppin, Ammann, and the judges of the city court of Memmingen
en.recipient: City Judge and Court of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster, Judges and Council of Kembs and Stein ask Burgomaster, Judges and Council of St. Gallen to move the heirs of the deceased merchant Jacob Schlumpf of St. Gallen to a friendly settlement with Caspar Degenner. Degenner says that he concluded a contract with Schlumpf and asks for support. The senders assure that Degenner will keep the contract and refer to a letter from Lorenz Zollikoffer.
en.sender: Burgomaster, Judges and Council of Kembs and Stein
en.recipient: Burgomaster, Judges and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information about a woman named Anna Zieglerin of Mehringen near Ingolstadt, who was arrested in Kempten for the theft of linen. They ask whether the woman had previously been imprisoned in St. Gallen in the autumn and put in the pillory in Rorschach, and request a written answer or communication to their messenger.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen remind the French envoy in the Confederation that he had intended to inform them in writing in March which outstanding payments they could claim. As they have not yet received anything, they ask him to do so now, so that they can receive the payments like the other cantons of the Confederation.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Herr N. Ammann, imperial envoy in Frankreich and Navarra

en.regest: The letter contains only a date line, which states that the document was printed on 24 May 1536.

Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the Council messengers of the eight cantons that govern the Reintal to lift the perpetual ban on sale (Verkaufsverbots) for the estate Ronenschwende in the court Berneggarten. The citizen of St. Gallen Leonhard Zollikofer had to accept the estate from Balthasar Rotmund in order to settle a debt to the Colonel Salati. Since it was a forced transfer and not a voluntary purchase, the St. Gallen authorities request the favor of the Confederates.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Council messengers of the eight cantons that govern the Reintal

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Leutkirch ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to allow their master builder Martin Aepplin to inspect fulling mills, linen presses and laughäusern and to support him in doing so. They plan the construction of a new fulling mill and a linen press to expand their bleachery.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Emperor Rudolf II. for help for the St. Gallen merchants Christoph Küppers, Jörg Käslers and their trading partners. These are in a legal dispute with Jews who disregarded imperial judgments and brought the merchants into distress. The city requests the Emperor to order the enforcement of the already issued imperial decisions, so that the merchants receive their claims.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Rudolf II., Roman Emperor

en.regest: The eight cantons to which the lordship of Rheineck and the Rhine Valley belong, ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admonish their fellow citizen Sigmund Zollikofer not to reverse the sale of his seat Grünenstein to a man from Ravensburg. The buyer has paid for the purchase and has moved in. The sellers have reached an agreement with the Landvogt. The senders fear that otherwise an unusual precedent would be created, which would unsettle the Confederation.
en.sender: The eight cantons to which the lordship of Rheineck and the Rhine Valley belong
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Appenzell request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their fellow citizen, the woman at the Bread Stalls, to leave Hermann Gmunden of Appenzell undisturbed. He had merely claimed to have heard from the land runner Valentin Krensch that the latter belonged to the Wolfshaus at Rhynach. Appenzell emphasizes that Gmunden did not claim this himself, and refers to the existing friendship.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to award the inheritance of the deceased Maria Nidenhuberin to their citizen Leonhart Straub and his siblings. They refer to the fact that the Straubs had taken up the inheritance according to the custom of St. Gallen, and ask for good promotion in this matter.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss, Landrat and citizens of the city of Bern inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the arbitral award rendered in Baden in the dispute with Basel. The majority of the envoys had annulled the Basel work, although Bern had protested. Bern complains of the injustice and asks St. Gallen for support as well as for the dispatch of empowered envoys to Aarau to improve the decision.
en.sender: Schultheiss, Landrat and citizens of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to place the wife of the deceased Melchior Surler under arrest and prohibition, until the citizen of Lindau Jacob Egger receives the outstanding purchase price of 180 gulden for cloths bought at the fair. Lindau refers to the attached supplication of Egger.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The town clerk and Council of Arbon request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hand over the inheritance of the deceased Barbara Gaißbergin, which Martin Struß had inherited in the name of his daughter Anna, to Anna Struß and her husband Lenhardt Breisinger. They enclose sworn testimonies that prove the kinship and the inheritance case, and ask for prompt settlement without further costs.
en.sender: The town clerk and Council of Arbon
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of the Evangelical Religion reply to a petition from Jörg Bäschert, who is seeking a position as schoolmaster in St. Gallen. They explain that they cannot give him the position, as the former schoolmaster is still in office. However, they confirm that Bäschert would be suitable for the position, and recommend him to the Council of St. Gallen.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the Evangelical Religion
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landvogt Diethrich Reding von Schwyz informs that the citizen of St. Gallen Joachim Vetter has been detained because he is supposed to have taken a horse from a man from the Petten Zeller Gericht. Vetter denies the act and claims that the horse was handed over to him by the Spittelknecht zum Ochsen in St. Gallen. He asks for release from detention. The Landvogt requests the authorities of St. Gallen for written information about the facts of the case.
en.sender: Diethrich Reding von Schwyz, Landvogt of the County of Toggenburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Schwyz report that the Schwyz resident Rudolf Bühler and his co-guarantors are accused by Jakob Egger of Lindau over a cheese delivery. Egger claims that the cheeses were damaged and threatens to have the debtors arrested in St. Gallen. The Schwyz residents ask St. Gallen to excuse the debtors and grant them justice, as they are innocent of the damage.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Schultheiss and Council of Frauenfeld that Balthasar Erhart, who comes from Frauenfeld, has been imprisoned in St. Gallen. They ask for a written report on Erhart's conduct in Frauenfeld as well as on the circumstances of his departure from the city, so that they can decide on further steps.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Frauenfeld

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Frauenfeld ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to release the imprisoned Balthasar Egelhart in mercy. Egelhart says that he was formerly a citizen of Frauenfeld, gave up his citizenship and married in Freiburg im Breisgau. He has honest siblings and in-laws in Frauenfeld who are advocating for him. The accusations are minor, and they hope that the imprisonment serves as a warning to him.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to permit the St. Gallen citizen Jacob Alther to take over the parish office in Hundwil. The community of Hundwil had turned to Appenzell after the death of the pastor Hans Jakob Girtanner, as Alther is active there as a clerk and enjoys great popularity. Alther has declared his consent, provided the St. Gallen authorities agree.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information regarding the weaver Mathis Müller. He is said to be detained in Konstanz for theft and to have stated that he comes from Ysne, but that he lived there with his father Jeronimus Müller and his mother. The mother is said to be a widow in St. Gallen. Konstanz requests a report on the origin and conduct of Müller.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the citizen of Arbon, Lienhard Brisinger. They reject the accusation that Brisinger's wife had been excluded from an inheritance. In fact, she had claimed to be the heir of the deceased Maria Weilenhuberin, which was opposed by more closely related citizens of St. Gallen. Since Brisinger could not prove the kinship, the citizens of St. Gallen installed the closer heirs. They emphasize that they had followed their city law and equity.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Stadtammann and Council of Arbon

en.regest: Duke Wilhelm zu Braunschweig und Lüneburg asks the city of St. Gallen not to cause any further delays by objections or arrests in the matter of his councillor Dr. Rütger Rulantt against the debtors of the Buders. He requests that the already confirmed contracts be upheld and that execution be carried out, so that Rulantt does not have to travel in person.
en.sender: Wilhelm Duke zu Braunschweig und Lüneburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster, Schultheiss, Landammann and Council of the city of Gallen

en.regest: The Statthalter and Council of the city of Arbon request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant their resident Leonhard Breusinger the inheritance of his uncle Joachim Wichtberger, which was awarded to him, without further conditions. They refuse to issue a bond, as their right of inheritance has been established by the Confederates and maintained unchanged. They assure that other heirs would also be admitted regardless of their origin, and send along the statements of the witnesses brought forward by Breusinger.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the city of Arbon
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the city of Memmingen to officially compel their fellow citizen Jacob Weninger (Schrenzing) to keep his marriage promise to the woman of St. Gallen Elisabeth Ranhart and her child. The people of St. Gallen ask for this intervention to prevent further misfortune and offer reciprocity.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Memmingen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hand over immediately to the guardians Andreas Hinderofen and Hans Mutschelin, appointed by them, the outstanding 1000 gulden of maternal property with interest for their ward Katharina Zollickhofer. They refer to the previous good cooperation and ask for a written answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Stadtpfarrer and Council of Bregenz ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish an edict concerning the creditors of the deceased Johann Christoph Schnabel von Schönstein. Since some citizens of St. Gallen are involved in the claims of the deceased, this should ensure that no one is curtailed in their rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizens Hans Caspar and Hans Heinrich Lenhart. The citizen of St. Gallen Conrad Rost had stolen the bundle brought along by the son, worth over 50 pounds. The citizens of Zürich ask for compensation for the damage and costs from Rost's assets in St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, on behalf of the widow of David Mantel and her siblings, for the release of their brother Hans Heinrich Küner, who is held captive in Lyon because of debts. They request that the citizen of St. Gallen Georg Zosatz be instructed to revoke his arrest warrant, so that Küner is not re-imprisoned by further creditors and can continue his mining business.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen send a piece of a new Milanese silver coin. Although it is similar in size to the old ducats, it was minted for only one hundred soldis and is therefore one Ort of a gulden less in value. Since the St. Gallen Confederates had brought such coins back from the Milan fair, the St. Gallen authorities ask for the cattle drivers to be warned so that the common man is not harmed.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell thank for the letter concerning the new mile of silver coinage. They assure that they will punish and admonish their citizens who spend this coinage at more than one hundred sold or twenty batzen. Furthermore, they will ensure that such coins are taken back and must be exchanged for good coinage, which would also have happened if complaints had been received.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich reply to a letter from St. Gallen concerning the new sort of Milanese silver coin. They state that this coin was introduced in Zürich two years ago and circulated like other Italian ducats or silver crowns. After examination and valuation as Reichs- and Fussstallertaler, it was publicly struck. In October, it will be issued again alongside the Milanese silver crowns. Zürich warns the population against confusion and asks St. Gallen to act accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant the free seat in St. Gallen to the married couple Jacob Luchman from Sumava and Ursula Klotharin, a former citizen of Lindau, living there. They refer to the attached supplication of the couple and ask for neighborly compliance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to again show grace to their countryman Claus Gruner, who has fallen into disgrace due to improper conduct. They assure that he has behaved honestly and well in Appenzell, and request a friendly reply.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
