en.regest: Syndici und Rat zu Genf ask Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen, in view of their financial difficulties, to be patient and to postpone the payment of the interest. They promise to settle the principal at a more opportune time. In a postscript, they inform that they had paid the Herren Studer and Reins 300 Kronen on good account of the interest.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: The Prince-Bishopric of Konstanz Chancellery and Council request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to urge the witnesses under their authority to present themselves to the commissioner Johann Jakob Langhans appointed by the Hofgericht in the appeal case between Jacob Unnersern and Hans Solern and to testify truthfully.
en.sender: Prince-Bishopric of Konstanz Chancellery and Council
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the Landvogt in Turgau to allow Hans Bornhauser, who comes from Weerstatt and is pledged in the St. Gallen Hospital, to move into the city without deduction or fee. They refer to an old agreement between St. Gallen and the County of Turgau, according to which persons from both sides may pass freely.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Anton Schmid, Council of Uri and Landvogt in Lower and Upper Turgow

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the city of Schaffhausen to exert influence on their citizen Christoph Ried, so that he does not endow his son Johannes only with the dwelling and the wine barrels of his brother-in-law, but also with an appropriate fortune. The citizen of St. Gallen Jakob Wild, who is married to Ried's daughter, fears unequal treatment in comparison to the siblings and asks for mediation.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Schaffhausen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Hans Lochmann and his wife Ursula Zollikhoferin in an inheritance matter. Lochmann's brother-in-law Sigmund Zollickhofer had held the wife's paternal inheritance under his hands but had fallen into debt. Zürich asks that Lochmann and his wife, as the daughter of a citizen of St. Gallen, not be disadvantaged in the settlement of the debts and that they retain their inheritance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Thun report that their citizen Noll Brach, having been abandoned by her children in her advanced age, decided to part with her house and small property and to live with her daughter Elisabeth. As they cannot confirm the contract without the knowledge of the other children, they ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to cite and question the daughter there, Margaretha Singerin, whether she waives the small property or wishes to save it, and they ask for a written answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the warning about foreign troops sighted near Überlingen. They state that they are watching the troops and will act according to the situation. They ask for further reports on similar incidents and promise to do the same on their part.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish the edict concerning the general court day appointed for the deceased citizen of Lindau, Mathias Kaiser. Since some citizens of St. Gallen have claims against Kaiser, this should ensure that no one is curtailed in their rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Duke Wilhelm zu Braunschweig und Lüneburg asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to continue to assist his counsel and proxy Dr. Rüdiger Rueland in a legal case already decided and to bring about the swift execution of the judgment. He says that because the citizens of St. Gallen wanted to prevent the proxy from paying by trickery, Rueland had gone to Frankfurt. The Duke consents to his absence but asks for prompt execution so that the proxy is not detained any longer.
en.sender: Duke Wilhelm zu Braunschweig und Lüneburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform about unrest in the Drei Bünden, where armed groups are gathering. They have sent envoys to Graubünden to lay down arms and to seek a peaceful solution. Because of the danger to the Confederation and foreign troops on the borders, they invite to a Confederate Diet in Baden. They ask St. Gallen to attend the day with empowered envoys.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Richter and Council of the city of Klosterneuburg ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant a letter of release to their fellow citizen Daniel Reuscher, who wishes to move to St. Gallen with his family, and to release him from his civic duties. They promise that Reuscher shall renounce his right in Klosterneuburg in the future if he settles in St. Gallen.
en.sender: Richter and Council of the city of Klosterneuburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Syndics and Council of the city of Genf report to the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich about a warning from the French field marshal von Boisse. He says that he has informed them that Frankreich learns of an imminent siege by the Confederates and offers help. Genf asks Zürich, in accordance with the obligations of the alliance, to work earnestly on the preservation of the status quo, so that they are not attacked by surprise.
en.sender: Syndics and Council of the city of Genf
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Bern inform Burgomaster and Council of Zürich that a letter from the Confederates in Genf has reached them. It is stated therein that the King of Frankreich, through the Lord of Boysse, has threatened the siege of the city of Genf. Genf has requested support from Bern. Bern has promised this and referred the matter to the officials. Bern forwards the letter from Genf addressed to Zürich.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform the cantons of the Confederation that, at their request, they are sending the town clerk Melchior Wildin as an envoy to the pending negotiations. They ask the cantons to grant Wildin their confidence and promise to do everything that may contribute to the promotion of peace, quiet, and unity in the fatherland as well as to the preservation of the status of the cantons.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomasters and Councils of the cantons of the Confederation

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have been informed by Bern and Genf of an impending siege of Genf. They ask the St. Gallen to tell them everything they learn about the situation in Piemont and Turin, as they have their own envoys there. They rely on the friendship of the Confederates and ask for a quick reply.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to excuse their citizen Hans Peter Steiner and to help him with his claim against Gabriel Zollikofer. Steiner says that despite a judgment letter and deadlines, he has not been cited or satisfied. Zürich requests payment of the claim including costs or a secure promise.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The present page contains several French correspondences from the year 1607. It concerns military movements, including the request of Count von Fuentes for passage for troops, rumors of an enterprise against Genf, and the threat to the Waadt by the Italian army. The senders and recipients are not clearly named in the text.
en.recipient: Unbekannt

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Burgomaster and Council of Solothurn that they have received important news from letters of the President de Charier in Genf. Accordingly, there are still about 20'000 Italian soldiers present, who, despite being on leave, would have received other orders. They ask for mutual precaution and support.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Solothurn

en.regest: Alfonso Casale reports that the Governor of Mailand had instructed the returning Landsknechte not to march through the country in order to avoid disturbances. Since the passes are blocked, the troops will now march through the country. He asks for understanding, as he could not have prevented the detour, and assures the friendship of the Catholic Majesty.
en.recipient: Hochgeachte Großmechtige ehrende Herren u. hoch. wt.

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Einsiedeln request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post an edict regarding the debt burden of the deceased citizen of Einsiedeln, Mathias Büchler. Since some citizens of St. Gallen may be creditors, they are to be informed through the publication so that no one is disadvantaged by ignorance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the Landammann and Council of Appenzell to hand over the child Johannes, whom the Appenzell shoemaker Jacob Lieb from Lachen fathered with the woman of St. Gallen Beatrix Cuozelin, to him or his relatives. Beatrix has sworn under oath that Lieb is the father. The people of St. Gallen ask for the upbringing of the child.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: The Council messengers of the four Oberkeiten on Lake Constance report that they have deliberated on the flooding caused by new, inferior coins. They propose to increase the value of Hungarian ducats and coarse silver coins in order to bring them back into circulation. They ask the recipients for their opinion on whether this measure would be advisable or how else the matter could best be resolved.
en.sender: Council messengers of the four Oberkeiten (Abbenzell, St. Gallen, Konstanz, Lindau, Überlingen, Radolfzell)
en.recipient: Administrator of the Hauptmannschaft, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz, Lindau, Überlingen and Radolfzell

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform that, at the request of the Appenzell authorities and the Abbey of St. Gallen, they cannot participate in the coinage question, as they, being an Imperial and Kurfürstentum, may only negotiate through the Electoral coinage commission. They ask St. Gallen to excuse this.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Glarus ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for support for their fellow councillor and Landshauptmann Niklaus Schuler. He says that he bought the castle of Grünenstein in the Rheintal from the citizen of St. Gallen Leonhard Keller, but has not yet paid in full. Keller says that he sold the castle on to Sigmund Zollikoffer, who sold it on again with a profit. The Glarus guardians demand that the castle serve as security for the purchase price and that Zollikoffer is not entitled to sell it before the Glarus parties have been paid. They ask St. Gallen to support this at the appointed court day.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Councils and envoys of the Confederation demand that the city of Chur cease all disputes, in particular regarding prisoners and the condemned, until the arrival of four envoys from Zürich, Luzern, Schwyz and Glarus. They request a sealed safe conduct for these envoys to Ragaz and promise that the envoys will convey the good intentions of the Confederates.
en.sender: Councils and envoys of the Confederation
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Chur

en.regest: The administrator of the captaincy, the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz reply to an inquiry from St. Gallen, Appenzell and the abbot regarding the new coin. They report on the complaints of their subjects concerning the half coin, but cannot yet make a final decision. They ask St. Gallen to inform them how the other neighbors have decided, so that they can follow suit and withdraw the coin.
en.sender: The administrator of the captaincy, the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen reply to the request of St. Gallen, Appenzell, and the abbot for proposals against the new, defective coin types. They state that they wish to wait for the decision of the Imperial Diet on coinage before making a final decision. They ask St. Gallen to inform the superior authorities about this and offer their help.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster, Small and Great Council of the city of Zürich inform the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen about the state of the negotiations with the Three Leagues. They ask that the planned military delay be refrained from and that envoys be sent to Baden on 26 July to seek a peaceful solution.
en.sender: The Burgomaster, Small and Great Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Ammann and Court of Zilschlacht that the subject Ulrich Neumann, called Tibi, has begotten an illegitimate child with the woman of St. Gallen Elisabeth Kiner. The Court has awarded the child to Neumann, but he has not accepted it and has departed. The Kinerin, who can no longer care for the child alone, has asked for intercession. St. Gallen asks Zilschlacht to ensure that the child is accepted and raised by Neumann or his relatives.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Ammann and Court of Zilschlacht

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Sibilla Schuechpriesterin to release the Schaffhausen citizen Sebastian Pfaef from his surety for a wine purchase in the amount of 88 florins towards Hieronymus Wilhelm von Stockhorn and to pay the purchase price. Pfaef had been condemned to pay by the Schaffhausen city court.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Hans Jost to settle the claim of the Schaffhausen citizen Hans Konrad Hüber or to present himself in Schaffhausen as promised. The arrest placed against the wine of the St. Gallen man was lifted after his promise to present himself within eight days, but he did not appear.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Zoffingen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to donate a window with the coat of arms of the city of St. Gallen for their newly built town hall. They refer to the fact that they have already received windows from the thirteen cantons, but that four places are still free. They promise to reciprocate in similar cases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the decision of the Great Council not to separate in the event of a war mobilization of the Confederation, but to march along according to the Baden Agreements, in order to preserve the honor of the Confederation. They ask St. Gallen to declare itself accordingly, and promise to submit further reports as soon as the votes of all the cantons are in.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about the differing moods of the Confederates regarding the impending mobilization for war in the Grisons trade. They invite to a meeting in Baden on 23 August to deliberate on the dispatch of envoys and further measures for the preservation of peace. They ask St. Gallen to send an authorized Council messenger.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Uri inform Burgomaster and Council of Zürich that the Landsgemeinde has resolved not to accept the articles submitted in Baden and not to send Vendlen into the Feld. They plan to occupy the passes near Pünden in order to protect the Confederate bailiwicks and subjects, and have already sent captains and soldiers there.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: King Heinrich von Frankreich asks the Burgomaster and Council of Zürich to bring back the Grauenpünfte for their own good and to restrain them from the misdeeds that have befallen them through their enemies. He praises the good advice that the citizens of Zürich have given to the Grauenpünfte and assures them of his support. He asks for a reply and commends himself to divine care.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Glarus ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant a voluntary donation to the Evangelical citizens of Bilten for the construction of their new church. They say that these citizens were forced to build their own church because access to the Catholic church was denied to them. Glarus supports the request of Bilten and asks St. Gallen for amicable support.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich invite Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to an assembly of the Evangelical cantons and Associated States on 20. September 1607 in Aarau. The occasion is the attitude of the Drei Bünde towards the demands of the Confederates, which, according to reports, are not to be fully accepted but also not entirely rejected. They deliberate on possible steps to preserve the peace and, if necessary, to prevent the approved military mobilization. It is also communicated that the Drei Bünde are to relocate their penal court from Chur to Ilanz and reorganize it.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Hauptleute of the three Bünde of Chur inform the Burgomaster and Council of Zürich that they cannot accept the conditions proposed by the Confederates, as these would contradict their freedoms. They ask Zürich not to interpret the answer unfavorably, and appeal to friendship to settle the disputes through amicable negotiations and to maintain unity.
en.sender: Hauptleute of the three Bünde of Chur
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Reffuge forwards the King's reply to a letter from the city of Zürich. The King praises the good will of the citizens of Zürich for the well-being of the Confederates and for the defense against foreign threats. He asks them to continue using the friendliest means to settle the disturbances, as the Republic is hard to move. He wishes peace upon the Confederates and asks for the support of the citizens of Zürich.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform that the Drei Pünfte do not accept the conditions of the last Diet of Baden, but hold firm to the negotiation with the Confederation. Therefore, the Diet planned for 11 October in Baden is cancelled. Instead, a Diet is set for Sunday, 11 October, in Ragaz, to deliberate on the dispatch of an embassy to the Drei Pünfte. Zürich asks St. Gallen to send an empowered Council envoy, and informs that the Drei Pünfte have been asked for a truce.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Isny request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have their citizen Christoph Büchler participate in an amicable settlement regarding the debts of the deceased Georg Büchler. The heirs Mathias Büchler and Mathias Rist have submitted a proposal whereby the widows and daughters are to be provided for with their goods and a payment of 1000 florins, in order to save the Büchler name and satisfy the creditors.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Richter und Rechtsprecher des Strafgerichts zu Glarus thank the Confederates for their letter of the 27th of the month. They explain that they cannot dissolve the court, as the Councils and Communities of the Lands had decided on the 13th place at Chur to proceed with the appointed Criminal Court in proper form. They ask the Confederates to accept this excuse and to remain in their benevolent disposition.
en.sender: Richter und Rechtsprecher des Strafgerichts zu Glarus
en.recipient: Burgomaster, Schultheiss, Landammann and Council of the cantons and Associated States of the Confederation (Zürich, Bern, Glarus, Basel, Schaffhausen, Appenzell, St. Gallen and Biel)

en.regest: The Häupter der drei Bünde zu Chur thank the Burgomaster and Council of Zürich for their letters of 25 and 26 September. Since the resolution passed there alters the previous conclusions regarding the pending and confused matters, they cannot give a final answer. They will forward the letters to the Councils and communities of the drei Bünde and obtain their written opinion by 14 October. They ask Zürich to recall the envoys already sent until further notice, in order to avoid unnecessary costs.
en.sender: Häupter der drei Bünde zu Chur
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: The Gemeiner Rat der drei Bünde thanks the cantons and the Associated States for their letter and assures them that the city of Chur has acceded to their requests. The previously issued judgments have been annulled, safe conduct has been granted to those affected, and a new, independent criminal court has been appointed, which is conducting proceedings in due form. The requests to send an embassy to supervise the proceedings and to promote peace are politely declined. They ask that trust be placed in the good will of the Confederates.
en.recipient: Zürich, Bern, Glarus, Basel, Schaffhausen, Appenzell, St. Gallen and Biel

en.regest: Ammann and Council of Altstätten ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a written statement regarding a dispute over the Weinguss. The four farms in the upper Rintal had reached an agreement with St. Gallen, but the three farms did not want to carry out the Guss this year. Altstätten wishes to know how St. Gallen views the matter in order to settle the conflict.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the receipt of a letter concerning the absence of the citizens of St. Gallen Hans Lübachers and Jakob Schranngs. Since Schranng was absent on the court day, a final court day was set for 24 October. The St. Gallen are requested to direct both parties to this date so that the judgment in the disputed matter can be heard and executed.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of the city of Zürich report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a response from the Richter and Rechtsprecher of Ilanz to a letter recently addressed to them. They enclose a certified copy so that St. Gallen can appropriately instruct its envoys for the appointed day at Ragatz.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the day of the Drei Bünde scheduled for the Sunday after 21 September in Ragaz was cancelled at their request. They ask St. Gallen to hold back the dispatched Council messenger and promise to act according to the further notice of the Bünde. Furthermore, they ask St. Gallen to inform the abbot of the monastery of St. Gallen of the cancellation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Burgomaster and Council of Schwyz about the increased value of the Hungarian ducats. They report that the abbot of St. Gallen considered a meeting unnecessary, as the ducats had already been assessed. St. Gallen asks whether Schwyz agreed with this opinion or wished for a neighboring meeting, and offers support.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schwyz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizen Bernhard Hürnerwadel. He has a balance of several hundred francs after the dissolution of a business partnership with Hans Heinrich König in Lyon. The citizens of St. Gallen, Peter Felsen and his brothers, had guaranteed the deceased cashier Johann Vnuet. Schaffhausen requests that the Felsen be instructed to settle the balance including costs, so that Hürnerwadel does not have to go to court.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Jakob Anhorn, Landvogt in the lower and upper Rintal, contradicts rumors that he has already sold his wine and demanded high prices. He states that no one has asked him about the hammer price, and asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen not to believe these false reports and not to raise the price thereby.
en.sender: Hans Jakob Anhorn, Landvogt in the lower and upper Rintal
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the three Pünfte have decided on the letters directed to them. They ask St. Gallen to communicate their opinion on this Pünfte business to them, so that they can act accordingly. They hope that the protracted work can soon be brought to an end.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell reply to a letter from the city of St. Gallen dated 11 October concerning Hungarian ducats. They declare themselves willing to accept these coins in the future for two gulden less, as this is already customary with many and the Prelate as well as the neighbors considered it unnecessary. They thank them for the friendly letter and offer themselves for further neighborly correspondence.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Hans Abt to appear before them on 27 November. Abt had committed himself to the plaintiff Hans Konrad Huber to give an explanation, but has not done so yet. Schaffhausen expects that Abt will inform the plaintiff and await the outcome of the legal proceedings.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about the outcome of the negotiations with the seceded Bündner before the criminal court in Ilanz. The persons present had defended themselves and preserved their honour, but had been sentenced to fines. The cases of the Bishop of Chur and a few others were still open. Since no one was complaining any longer, Zürich considered a further joint embassy to the Bündner cantons unnecessary and proposed to let the matter rest for the time being.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Rheinfelden inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the death of the former citizen of St. Gallen, Magdalena Zelligkofferin. Her brother-in-law, the citizen of Rheinfelden Mauritz Bäuthaner, has a claim to the inheritance. He asks for a letter of introduction so that he can assert this claim in St. Gallen. Rheinfelden requests the authorities of St. Gallen to help the citizen in enforcing his right.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Glarus thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for their support in the collection of a tax for the construction of a new church. They promise to support St. Gallen in similar cases likewise in a friendly and confederate manner.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Erasmus Bädinger with the inheritance of his deceased cousin Hans Hörn in St. Gallen. They refer to the inheritance rights of St. Gallen and ask that Bädinger be treated accordingly. In return, they commit to treating citizens of St. Gallen according to the inheritance rights of Konstanz.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to recognize their countrywoman Anna Vetter as the heir of the deceased hospital wine seller Spengler. Anna Vetter is married to Spengler, whose father had promised the marriage. She has carried for him for three years and asks for support in the recognition of her inheritance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten reply to a letter of 16 January, in which St. Gallen inquires about the current coin rate. Kempten reports that the coinage order is unstable, as the prices for ducats and other coins fluctuated strongly. They hope that the Imperial Diet at Regensburg will provide a remedy.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen reply to a letter of 16 January, in which they inform about the valuation of coins for taxes and revenues of the city of Memmingen. They name the rates for Hungarian ducats, silver crowns, Philippsthaler, Reichsthaler and Goldthaler. In commercial transactions, the rates would sometimes be set higher, depending on the agreement of the parties, without anyone being forced.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Wil ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to exert influence on their citizen Ambrosi Ziegler. The citizen of Wil, Hans Heldt, goldsmith, has complained about Ziegler and requested intercession. Heldt has waited a long time for his claim and incurred costs. The citizens of Wil ask that Ziegler be moved to pay the claim, the interest, and the costs, so that Heldt may be satisfied.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm reply to a letter of 16 January, in which they had been asked for information about the value of the gold and silver coin denominations in Ulm. They apologize for the delayed reply and explain that the coin rates have been so unstable for a long time that no fixed value can be established. For the municipal budget, the coin edict of 1559 is applied, but in trade between citizens and foreigners, the coins are valued higher and unequally. They hope for a regulation by the Imperial Diet.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg answer an inquiry from the Council of St. Gallen regarding the valuation of coins. They report that coarse gold and silver coins are frequently exported and exchanged, which is why their value has risen. They have not set an official valuation, but merchants have agreed on their own rates. They hope for a soon coin reform by the Imperial Majesty and leave the further valuation to the discretion of the St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Landammann and Council of Appenzell about the rising rates of Hungarian ducats and other coins, which exceed the fixed valuation. They would have wanted to convene a neighborhood conference of the four Oberkeiten, but refrained from holding it until after Easter, as they hope for a coinage reform at the Imperial Diet in Regensburg. In the meantime, they must accept the rate increases. They send copies of the replies from Nürnberg, Augsburg, Ulm, Memmingen, and Kempten, which also complain about the impossibility of maintaining the order.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen publicly announce that in the legal case between Elsa Müllerin von Immenstadt as plaintiff and Jeremias Gsellen as defendant, they have ordered the defendant to have the evidence for his settlement with the plaintiff taken in the city of Isny according to its custom. He must notify the opposing party of this in good time and deliver the testimony in writing and sealed to St. Gallen.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of their answer to two letters regarding the coin types and the goldsmith Hans Hallen. Hallen rejects the proposal of his brother-in-law Ambrosi Zingler and demands a sure guarantee for the payment. Ulm asks St. Gallen to instruct Zingler from the official side to fulfill Hallen's demand.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen remind Genf of the outstanding debt of 4000 Kronen with interest, which was already called in on 22 January 1605. Since only 500 Kronen have been paid so far and the merchants of the city, to whom the money belongs, are pressing for payment, the St. Gallen authorities urgently request payment of the remaining 3500 Kronen or at least of half of it with interest. They promise in return the return of the main bond and receipts.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Syndics, Burgomaster and Council of Genf

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Landammann and Council of Glarus for the friendly reply to their intercession regarding their citizen Balthasar Rotmund and Herr Obrist Galati. They ask that Rotmund continue to be well commanded. Since the two months appointed by Glarus have elapsed, they request that a specific day be named on which Rotmund or his agents can appear before the court to begin the matter.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Glarus

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizens Caspar Moser and Gabriel Billwiller to pay the citizen of Schaffhausen Heinrich Schlosser 15 florins together with interest. Schlosser says that he paid this sum to Moser as the authorized representative of Billwiller, but has not been paid despite repeated reminders and now wishes to take other measures.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to the letter from Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of the previous day. They declare themselves willing to supply the citizens of St. Gallen with 14'000 roof tiles for the construction of a house at Hof Siebenach against payment. The tiles could be collected in Lindau.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The bailiff and Council of the town of Bischofszell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to show kindness towards Elsbeth Albrin. She has served for years as a caretaker in the hospital in Bischofszell, but is now no longer able to work due to age. The town of Bischofszell could not refuse her request for intercession, as she had conducted herself honorably there. They ask that she be granted the necessary support for her livelihood.
en.sender: The bailiff and Council of the town of Bischofszell
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Statthalter, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz reply to an inquiry from St. Gallen regarding the coinage. They state that they have not so far set a fixed rate for coins in Konstanz, but have adjusted it according to the circumstances. Swiss batzen are accepted at 90 pfennigs of the Konstanz coin, while Lürer pfennigs and other small coins are current. They declare themselves willing to inform St. Gallen in the future about such matters.
en.sender: Captain, Statthalter, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen make public that they have commissioned the former Burgomaster Joachim Reutlinger and the town clerk Melchior Guldin to ask the envoys of the Confederates' Council in Baden for help in several legal disputes. These concern customs complaints in Lyon, robbery cases in Paris and Österreich, as well as an appeal case against the canons of Bischofszell.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Villingen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene for their fellow citizens Conrad Türner and Jeremias Weiß. These had, at the request of the Zolligkhoffer of Sonnenberg, borrowed carriages from Hans Jörg Kechler, which were now seized by the creditors of the Zolligkhoffer. Since the carriages belonged to Kechler, the Villingen request that the carriages be released or that the Zolligkhoffer be forced to return them or pay.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Solothurn ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to restrain their citizens Malchior Lacher, Heinrich Rottmunder, Lienhart and Jakob Koller to pay the outstanding interest, principal and costs from sold bonds to the Solothurn bailiff at Walenstadt. The bailiff had asserted the claims personally, which had led to inconveniences. Solothurn asks for payment in order not to further bother the debtors.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Chur reply to an intervention for their fellow citizen Heinrich Hochstetter. They state that they would gladly provide his brother-in-law Jeremias Bürtzchen with the payment of the remaining 30 gulden bride price for his daughter. However, as Bürtzchen has been in the Confederation for some time to collect a pledged debt instrument, and is furthermore destitute, he can hardly settle the arrears.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Einsiedeln reply to a letter of intercession from St. Gallen regarding the Buflarisch forgery matters. They state that they had not neglected to promote the matter, but that the parties themselves had delayed it through long delays and lengthy submissions. Now a day for the final decision has been set, whereby the matter is to be amicably settled.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform the French ambassador that they had sent their town clerk to collect their shares of the money. They remind him that the late ambassador Vic had promised that, after the repayment of the 70'000 Kronen for which the five cities had stood as guarantors, the outstanding principal of 20'000 Kronen together with interest would also be refunded. Since the 70'000 Kronen have now been settled, they ask for the payment of a considerable sum.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Herr von Refuge, Botschafter des Königs von Frankreich und Navarra

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Glarus ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizens, the Herren Kobelindiger, to settle the legal dispute with the French Wachtmeister Caspar Gallat before the Council of Glarus. Gallat must travel to Frankreich due to a royal command and cannot wait any longer. If the St. Gallen side does not clarify the matter before the Glarus court, they will no longer allow the Glarus envoys in St. Gallen to answer and will continue the proceedings in Frankreich.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Schultheiss and Council of Solothurn to communicate in writing the opinion of their citizens Jost von Arx and Hans Schwallern regarding the measures agreed upon between these, Melchior Ratmund and Heinrich Hans Anton Zili. Since no reply has yet been received, Zili urges a prompt response so that he may act accordingly.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Solothurn

en.regest: Advocate of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz reply to a letter of 27 July regarding the inheritance of the deceased citizen of Konstanz, Jacob Blumer. They state that they had levied the succession tax on property inherited abroad and had also done so in the case of the inheritance of the woman of St. Gallen, Katharina Wächin. They refer to the will of the testator, according to which the property should remain under their protection, and insist on the claim for deduction in order to maintain good neighborly relations.
en.sender: Advocate of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell communicate to St. Gallen the statements of the witnesses Hans Bucher, Hans Hiller and Vetter Kuen. These concern a dispute between Hans Bucher and the deceased Hans Hiller regarding the treatment of a leg injury by the Kolbrenner as well as the payment by the Appenzellers. The statements were taken under oath at the request of Jochel Bucher.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Town clerk and Court of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to question their relative, the butcher Hans Tobler, under oath. It concerns the defamation of the Appenzeller Daniel Schmid for witchcraft. Tobler is to testify whether he and a boy spent the night at Schmid's in Aeschemoß one evening and heard strange things. The testimony is to be sent in writing and sealed to Appenzell.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizens Sophia and Katharina Näffin. These have applied that their sister Elisabeth Näffin, who has married Leonhart Harthausen in St. Gallen, bring back to Ravensburg the maternal inheritance, which she has acquired after the death of the mother. The sisters want to distribute the property in Ravensburg. Ravensburg offers to participate in the distribution.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Baumeister and Council of Bludenz inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the suspension of the market on 22 September (St. Mauritius) at the request of the Archduke of Österreich. They ask the St. Gallen citizens to warn their butchers not to come to Bludenz, as the market is suspended. They point out that the markets in Bludenz will continue as usual on St. Mauritius Day of the old calendar (22 September) and thereafter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Basel ask Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen to help their citizen Jonas Schuowürker in the collection of a debt. Schuowürker says that he has taken on a surety for the former St. Gallen scholarship student Jacob Altherr, which he now wishes to reclaim. Altherr says that he has used the money for himself. Basel asks for official support so that Schuowürker and other creditors are satisfied and the surety is dissolved.
en.sender: Remigius Fäsch, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Basel
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Rector and Regentia of the University of Basel ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to take care of the Basel tailor Jonas Schritzer. He says that he had stood surety for the St. Gallen scholarship student Jacob Althier, who owes him 62 gulden and 6.5 gulden. Althier has not settled the claims despite reminders. Schritzer asks for a directive to the St. Gallen Council so that he can gently persuade Althier to pay.
en.sender: Rector and Regentia of the University of Basel
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Solothurn, at the request of the citizens of Solothurn Joachim and Jörg Wartenhusser, confirm that these are the legitimate sons of the deceased married citizens of Solothurn Martin Wartenhusser and Barbara Bruni. They ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist the brothers in asserting their inheritance claims on the estate of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Othmar Löffler.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Burgomaster of Buchenbach request a fire tax for the citizen Hans Nester, whose house was destroyed by a fire on 8 August. They point out that the Council and the community will support the city in this emergency.
en.sender: The Schultheiss and Burgomaster of Buchenbach
en.recipient: all noble and non-noble, ecclesiastical and secular lords and people

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen remind Appenzell of the agreement on inheritance cases concluded in 1595, which has now expired. They complain that the citizens do not always disclose whether they have relatives in Appenzell, which can lead to errors. They offer to conclude a new, mutually acceptable agreement through Council messengers, and ask for the designation of time and place for the negotiations.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Usseren Rhoden Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Zürich to send them a copy of the new coinage regulation that Zürich has decided upon with other cantons. They wish to adapt their own coinage regulation to that of the Confederates and ask for information on which cantons have adopted the regulation.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich send, upon request, a copy of the coinage agreement discussed in August with several cantons of the Confederation. They report that Luzern, Schwyz, and Glarus accepted the agreement, but Uri and Unterwalden had not yet declared themselves. Zug had abandoned the matter. Since not all seven cantons had consented, the agreement had not yet been publicly published.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Uri report that some of their butchers had informed the St. Gallen hospital master that he may no longer buy cattle in Uri this year, as it is allegedly deficient. They reject this, as there is no cattle shortage in Uri and the buyers are satisfied. They request St. Gallen to question the hospital master where he has these rumors from, and ask for a sealed answer to their bailiff Jakob Muheim.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Andreas Eys, who has lost 60 gulden to the St. Gallen Hans Melchior Deuber. Eys is poor and urgently needs the money. The Ulm authorities ask for support in collecting the debt, whether through amicable negotiation with the debtor's relatives or through the realization of his tailor's tools located in St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Imperial Bailiff, Schultheiss and Council of Wil reply to the inquiry of St. Gallen regarding the prisoner Mathis Müller. They reject his claim to be a resident (Inssasse), as neither he nor his parents have ever been recognized as such. Müller has been imprisoned twice and escaped, most recently on the third attempt. Furthermore, he was imprisoned and questioned in Konstanz, Zürich and Baden. Wil asks St. Gallen to inquire with the aforementioned cantons.
en.sender: Imperial Bailiff, Schultheiss and Council of Wil
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in the context of an imperial commission proceeding between Dr. Friedrich Ziegler and the city of Kempten, to examine the St. Gallen court clerk Gallin Mauren as a witness. They ask for the designation of a date, examination according to the submitted articles, and transmission of the statements under the town seal to Dr. Spengler.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Überlingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Wil request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to report to them in writing whether Mathis Müller, referred to as a Binnensichser, has been imprisoned or expelled in St. Gallen and what offenses he committed there. They need this information in order to be able to proceed against him accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten reply to a letter of 12 July concerning the Kempten citizen Heinrich Hofstetter. They say that on 16 January they gave the order to pay out two gulden to Hofstetter and his wife from his brother-in-law and father Jeremias Kücken as soon as possible and to collect a further ten gulden against receipt.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Council of Feldkirch ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish the edict regarding the appointed general court day for the creditors of the deceased citizen of Feldkirch Mathias Elckhß and his widow. They suspect that Elckhß might also be indebted to citizens of St. Gallen, and ask for this measure so that no one is curtailed in their rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten confirm the receipt of a communication from St. Gallen, according to which the court clerk Gall Maurer is to be proposed and questioned as a witness for Friedrich Kregler. Kempten considers it unnecessary to send its own representatives and asks St. Gallen to transmit the short interrogatories so that the witness is questioned accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen that Cosmus Jagk, who is from St. Gallen and had fled from the monastery of Einsiedeln, was arrested in Wädenswil. He is said to have stated that, after his conversion to the evangelical religion, he had been taken to Italien, where he had killed a companion. Since the abbot of Einsiedeln demands his extradition, Zürich asks St. Gallen for written information regarding Jagk's person and conduct.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Council of Lindau to give them information about the state and the amount of an inheritance that is due to their citizen Caspar Appenzeller and his wife Ursula Schuehlerin. Appenzeller presses for the satisfaction of his claims. The St. Gallen ask Lindau for help in clarifying the matter or for a negative answer, so that Appenzeller can desist from his plan.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Council of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to order their citizen Lorenz Kunz to pay the outstanding 21 batzen back tax to the town clerk of Lindau. Kunz owes this amount because of his mother-in-law Katharina Weberin. Despite two reminders by the town clerk and two letters to the Burgomaster of St. Gallen Othmar Steiner, the payment has not yet been made.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The imperial Regenten in Innsbruck ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to issue a certified copy of the letter from the city of Bludenz from September 1608 to the Montafoner. This letter had warned the Montafoner not to buy cattle there before the first Bludenz cattle market, as otherwise their cattle would be withheld from them on their return.
en.sender: Imperial Majesty and Princely Highness of Österreich etc. President, Regenten and Councillors of the aforementioned Lands
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform them in writing whether the parish priest Heinrich Blasius of Gachnang possesses a debt instrument for 138 gulden, which serves as security for a loan to the Stein am Rhein citizen Jörg Schmid and his wife Barbara Appenzellerin. They further inquire whether the Appenzellerin has any other inherited property, as the parish priest wishes to redeem the instrument upon repayment of the deduction.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Esslingen answer the inquiry of Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen as to who is to be understood under the names «Matthias Büschler und Gebrüder» in the judgments. They explain that the two deceased elder brothers Matthias and David Büschler had always signed their trade letters in this manner. The parties had used this designation in the documents concerning the bankruptcy matter, which is why the consultants had retained it in the title of the judgment. It is exclusively the two deceased brothers who are meant.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Joachim Reuoteinger, Imperial Bailiff, confirms that on 23 July 1608 the estate of the widow Christian von Hallers was divided. Barbara Haller received a bond for 138 gulden 40 kreuzer, which is pledged to Georg Schmid in Stein. This bond is in turn pledged to Balthasar Gaimb, until it is paid, and lies behind the widow Sebastian Suters.

Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen transmit to the Landvogt of Frauenfeld the process against the imprisoned Anton Peter Rauch from the Calancatal. They explain that they had taken over the imprisonment at the request of the subject Ulrich Rainlin. Since the officials had not expressly demanded the surrender of the prisoner before the arrival of the Landvogt, but had wished for a thorough interrogation, they had already carried this out. They ask the Landvogt not to disapprove of the non-surrender of the prisoner, as they had already ascertained the truth.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Balthasar in der Burg, Landvogt of Frauenfeld

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have imprisoned a suspicious and slanderous woman. As they cannot avoid the painful question, they ask the St. Gallen authorities to send their executioner to Appenzell on the same evening, so that they can proceed properly in the matter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landvogt Christof Schorno in the Rheintal for copies of the interrogations and items found belonging to Katharina Müllerin von Urnäsch, who is detained in St. Gallen. They suspect that she was arrested in Altstätten under her predecessor Heinrich Klöser for theft and counterfeit money, but was pardoned. The documents are to be handed over to a messenger.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Christof Schorno, Landvogt of the Rheintal

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on a marriage contract between Hans Hartmann Escher and his wife Cleophea Loderer. They ask for confirmation of the contract by the authority of St. Gallen, as the bride's family agrees with it. The contract regulates the maintenance of the husband and waives the morning gift.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform the Landvogt in Turgau that a woman, Catharina Müllerin, held in custody in St. Gallen, has reported a fuller named Baschen Wepfer at Sirnach as a forger of silver crowns. They ask the Landvogt to arrest the man and search for evidence on his person, and for a written reply, so that they can proceed against the prisoner.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt in Upper and Lower Turgau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to Landvogt Christof Thomas that their merchants, who trade in Italien, are ready to give up the road if the demands of St. Margrethen do not relent, owing to the dispute over tolls. They ask Thomas to persuade the people of St. Margrethen to desist from their plan, in order to preserve the neighborhood.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Christof Thomas, Landvogt in the upper and lower Rintal

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landvogt Christoph Schorno to inquire with the four courts in the Reintal how they intend to handle the wine trade in the future and whether they are willing to reach an amicable settlement with the city. The previous contracts have expired. Schorno is to inform the city in writing so that it can clarify the matter before the ruling cantons.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Christoph Schorno, Landvogt in the Upper and Lower Reintal

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen forward an edict of the city of Nürnberg, according to which certain coin denominations have risen and others have been prohibited. They report that they have warned their merchants and shopkeepers not to continue importing the prohibited denominations. As the annual bleaching season is approaching, they invite the Innere and Äussere Rhoden to a neighboring conference on 10. August to deliberate on the coin question. They ask for a written reply and the return of the edict.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Innere and Äussere Rhoden

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell confirm the receipt of a letter regarding the coinage. They agree with a joint council and send their council messenger on the coming Sunday evening or Monday morning, so that the discussion regarding the coinage can be held as desired.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to the Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes on the decision regarding the amendment of the coinage edict. They say that they had considered the amendment necessary because of the linen trade and to avoid misfortune, but that they would not have carried it out without the knowledge of Appenzell. They ask that the delay that has arisen be viewed with neighborly goodwill, and thank for the honor shown to the St. Gallen town clerk. Furthermore, they send a copy of the already concluded settlement regarding inheritance law and expect their opinion.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the letter of the Landvogt in the Rheintal concerning the wine purchase. They agree that the wine purchase for the current year is to be handled according to the existing letters and seals. For the coming year, they are ready to reach a new understanding. Regarding the day of settlement set for 22 August in St. Margrethe concerning the road toll, they cannot attend and ask that it be postponed by ten to fourteen days.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Christoph Schorno, Landvogt in the Rheintal

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz report to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a dispute between their weavers and dyers. The dyers demand 18 kreuzer for a pound of yarn, which the weavers consider too high. The people of Konstanz ask for information on whether the dyers can dye a heavy pound of yarn (40 Loth) for 18 kreuzer without suffering a loss, and what the prices are in St. Gallen.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the heirs of the deceased Elisabeth von Wattwil to transmit to them the desired copy of her testament. Furthermore, they request that the opening of the testament of their fellow council member Martin Schmelz be postponed by eight or fourteen days, as he is not present and wishes to assert his claims.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Christoffel Schorno, Landvogt in the Rheintal, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the four upper courts of the Rheintal wish to maintain the Weingartenlauf for another year. He asks the city to determine the time, day, and place for future negotiations regarding the Lauf. Furthermore, he announces that on Monday in eight days, negotiations regarding the equality of the Weggeld are to take place in St. Margrethen, and invites the merchants of the city to attend.
en.sender: Christoffel Schorno, Landvogt in the Rheintal
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the city of Zürich dated 28 August 1609 regarding the extension of the inheritance division of the family von Ikonwil and a copy of the testament of the deceased Elisabeth von Ikonwil. They communicate that the heirs and the widow Felin insist on the already determined date because of the autumn season. They ask Zürich to send them the testament of Dr. Schmaltz in a faithful copy, as this could have clarified the matter. In return, they promise to transmit the Ranzow testament.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Zürich

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell thank St. Gallen for the transmission of a draft for an inheritance agreement with the Ausserrhodern. They declare themselves in agreement with the thaler question, but ask for mutual caution against counterfeiting. They wish to postpone the inheritance agreement until a better opportunity, as they cannot negotiate without the consent of the Landleute. Existing agreements remain valid for them.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in the division of the estate of the deceased Elisabeth von Vanbuel, the mother of Melchior Schmeltzen, to take care of the interests of the Kempten guardians. They have commissioned the Kempten master builder Johann Stuefern and the town clerk Zimprecht Satler to safeguard the rights of the Kempten party. The St. Gallen party are to give credence to the Kempten envoys and ensure that Melchior Schmeltzen and his father as well as the Kempten party are not disadvantaged in the division of the inheritance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Smiths' Guild of St. Gallen asks the Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur to detain their citizen Jörg Schellenberg and have him hand over again the apprentice of the St. Gallen goldsmith Gabriel Gänser, or to go himself to St. Gallen to clarify the dispute. The boy has not completed his apprenticeship and left without proper right.
en.sender: Zunftmeister and Geschworene of the Smiths' Guild of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rottweil reply to a letter from E. F. F. E. W. regarding the gold and coarse coin denominations. Since they did not want to set a price on the coins without a general regulation in the Lake Constance district, they remain with the previous value. They ask for neighborly goodwill.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Leutkirch ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their assessor Gabriel Zollikofer in clarifying disputes with the Zollikofers. They request that the matter be promoted so that their town clerk Matthäus Schwanzer, who is assisting Zollikofer, can depart quickly and return to his city.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to consider their fellow citizen and former pastor in Hundwil, Jacob Altherren, with favor. They request that, because of his honest conduct, he be helped to a good position and that the 52 florins advanced to him out of favor be granted to him for some time longer, until he is in a better position.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Eystett inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the citizen and foundryman of Eystett, Meinrad Wilden, departed on 16 June 1609, after the sale of his house, under the pretext of going to collect money. Since he has been missing since then, his wife Walburga asks for information about his whereabouts. If he is staying in St. Gallen, he is to be sent back to his family.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Wil thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the transmission of the town coat of arms along with the accompanying money. They promise to place the coat of arms in a place of honor in their newly built house, and offer their services for future matters.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their subjects Hilarius Metzger and Dorotea Kilchhofferin in the enforcement of their inheritance rights. The two had been summoned before the St. Gallen court to a court day on 27 February, but did not know from whom the inheritance of their deceased mother-in-law, the Fuden-Männin, was being derived. Stein am Rhein requests information on the persons concerned and helpful assistance so that the subjects can safeguard their rights.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Ältere und Geheime des Rats zu Ulm inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about rumors that Spanish troops are being recruited in the Meissn region, which could be led into Germany. They ask to be informed of what St. Gallen knows about this and request that future news regarding recruitment or troop movements that could be dangerous to the German nation be transmitted immediately.
en.sender: Ältere und Geheime des Rats zu Ulm
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landmann and Council of Glarus ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to provisionally release the imprisoned N. Keller. The Glarus citizen Caspar Streuly, who is mediating in the dispute between St. Gallen and citizens of Rüti and Zillis, has traveled away and will return in eight days. Streuly will then personally address the St. Gallen authorities to achieve an amicable settlement.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Council of Wil request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to cite the St. Gallen citizen Zacharias Rungier as a witness in an inheritance dispute between Jacob Töbelin and Georg Struben, to question him, and to send the testimony in writing to Wil. Töbelin says that he sued Struben before the court for a piece of vines, 100 gulden, and household goods, which he considers inherited. Struben claims that it was given to him by Töbelin's deceased wife as dowry. Rungier, the guardian of the widow, knows the circumstances of the division.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Elders and Secretaries of the Council of Ulm thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the reply of 8 March, in which the situation of the troops in the Milanese territory is described. They express their regret at the news and declare their good intentions. They ask that they be informed day and night at their own expense in case of dangerous movements.
en.sender: Elders and Secretaries of the Council of Ulm
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster, Council and citizens of St. Gallen to admit their citizen Jacob Bodmer, the Schärer of Küßnacht, into their citizenship. Bodmer has settled in St. Gallen and applied for citizenship. The Zürichers promise to incur a debt to St. Gallen if the opportunity arises.
en.recipient: Burgomaster, Council and citizens of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask King Heinrich IV. of Frankreich to cause the Schaffhauser Bernhardin Huenervadel to drop the arrests and proceedings he has initiated in Lyon against the citizens of St. Gallen Peter Felsen and brothers. They refer to the oath that Huenervadel has sworn not to issue arrests as long as the proceedings in St. Gallen are pending, as well as to the Perpetual Peace. They request the King to instruct Huenervadel to conduct the legal dispute before the court of St. Gallen.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: King Heinrich IV. of Frankreich and Navarra

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the information regarding a muster ground located between Konstanz and Rottweil, as well as regarding the arrival of Italian horsemen and foreign troops. They suspect that this is not directed against the Confederates, but against the war in Frankreich, but demand vigilance. They ask for further information and inquire whether the Landvogt in the Rheintal is taking precautions at the borders.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Secret Council of Lindau thank for the letter and the information about the danger from French military operations. They declare themselves willing to watch for possible misfortunes for the community and the neighborhood and to inform St. Gallen confidentially if needed. They ask that such neighborly communications also continue in the future.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Secret Council of Lindau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Secret Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Elders and Secretaries of the Council of Ulm thank for the transmitted news and in turn share news about the military situation at Straßburg. They report on the assembly of about 1500 unarmed foreigners, the expected reinforcement by Kurißer, and the mobilization of over 24,000 men by the Protestant Estates. Furthermore, they inform about the blockade of the Rhine passes, the passage of the Sülzer Knechte, and the support of the French King with money and troops under the command of Prince Christian von Anhalt.
en.sender: Elders and Secretaries of the Council of Ulm
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich communicate to the Landammann and Council of Glarus a letter from the vorderösterreichischen government at Ensisheim to the Confederation. They report that they had answered the government, stating that they were inclined towards peace and friendship and upheld the hereditary agreement with the House of Österreich. Since the government demanded nothing further, they rested on the matters procured. They ask Glarus to inform them if it has other concerns.
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Glarus

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Ulm thank St. Gallen for the confidential communication regarding the danger posed by war preparations, muster places, and troop movements. They ask to be informed immediately of any further developments that could endanger their city. Ulm declares itself ready to act in the same manner. Furthermore, they report that the mercenary troops recruited for Strasbourg, located in the Alsace, have not yet determined their route of passage.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Reffuge informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the King of Frankreich has not violated the alliance treaty. If the matter pending in Paris is to be referred to the courts of St. Gallen, they will be given satisfaction. He will write to the King at the first opportunity and forward him the letter of the St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Feldkirch ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to release their fellow citizen Caspar Weinzierl, who is detained because of unconsidered remarks. They point out that the detention already punishes the offense and ask for lenient treatment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to tolerate their countryman, the Master Carpenter Hans Alder, who has been punished and demoted by the carpentry guild because of his work, in his work. They promise to make efforts for St. Gallen in similar cases.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Syndics and Council of Genf hand over to the messenger the remaining 75 ducats according to the receipt. They ask the authorities of St. Gallen to keep them in favorable remembrance and wish them all the best.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landrichter and Council of Trun give St. Gallen a report on the inheritance dispute of the St. Gallen citizen Hans Halder in Thusis. Halder was excluded from the inheritance after several instances and a final judgment of the Bündner legal committee. The Bündner ask St. Gallen to dissuade Halder from further lawsuits, as they would have helped him had the outcome been just.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to restrain their citizen Georg Strauben to fully fulfill the purchase contract concluded with the citizen of Konstanz Johann Rösler for printing supplies or to compensate for the damage caused. Rösler has complained that Strauben, despite promises, has not delivered the agreed items, which endangers his planned book printing press.
en.sender: The Administrator of the Captaincy, the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Lindau that they have learned that approximately 6000 Spanish soldiers are to march through the territory of the Confederation, partly via Sargans, partly via Rorschach and Wil. They ask Lindau to communicate whether it has similar information, and promise to inform them of further developments as well. For further details, they refer to the Guild Master Hans Schlumpf.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Lindau

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Secret Council of Lindau thank St. Gallen for the information regarding the danger posed by the passage of Spanish troops. They report that the troops had been denied the pass after Venedig, not in a hostile manner, but merely to march to Mailand and to pass through the five cantons and the Leventina. They enclose an excerpt from a letter dated 6 June 1610 and promise to report confidentially upon receiving further news.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Secret Council of Lindau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on the influx of soldiers who wish to march to Italien into the Mailändische. They let these pass for the time being, as they do not expect that larger troop gatherings will form in the region. Should, however, larger groups form, they would refuse the passage and divert the soldiers via the lake. Furthermore, Lindau has been reinforced with guards.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the tense situation with the five Catholic cantons regarding the Gachnanger trade. They fear an attack by Spanish troops and the Madruzzische Landsknechte. Since they are already on the defensive, they ask St. Gallen, as co-religionists and fellow confederates, to watch out for them and to provide support if needed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the confidential report on various incidents. They ask the citizens of St. Gallen to continue informing them about similar events, and promise to watch over them faithfully in this regard.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the transmitted reports and confirm their friendship as Confederates. They promise to use the received warnings and to conduct themselves in the ongoing matters in such a way that their peace-loving and honest disposition is recognizable. They declare themselves ready to support St. Gallen in all feasible cases with their loyalty and protection.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform the Council of St. Gallen that they had learned from Schaffhausen and Stein that a letter had been addressed to the abbot of St. Gallen. They ask to be informed whether St. Gallen had received similar reports from Lindau or elsewhere. Such rumors cause them concern. They recommend to the Council of St. Gallen to examine and clarify the matter in order to avoid unrest and misunderstandings.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a nocturnal noise in Bregenz, which was caused by a forester and his companions. They say that these men had called the people to drive off the enemy on the Rhine, which led to panic and shots. Lindau says that it had sent messengers to Bregenz and Fußach to clarify the situation, and now informs that it was a mistake.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen, in which the latter sought their opinion on a recently concluded agreement in connection with the Thurgau wars. The Zürichers see no particular concerns in the agreement and hope that the storm that has arisen will soon subside. Should further conflicts nevertheless occur, the sincere people in Thurgau are ready to stand by Zürich's side as faithful Confederates.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau thank St. Gallen for the confidential communication regarding the military affairs. They assure that they will undertake nothing dangerous against St. Gallen, and report that they had not yet heard anything about the news that two further regiments would be withdrawn for Spanien. They want to clarify this and inform St. Gallen confidentially how the people could otherwise be diverted. Furthermore, they refer to their answer from the previous day.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
