en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen confirm the receipt of two letters from Lindau of 21 and 22 June. They thank them for the neighborly consideration and declare themselves ready to do everything that is useful and conducive to the maintenance of a good and lasting neighborly correspondence.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Lindau

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for its friendly statement regarding the alliance letters and reaffirm their Confederation. They inform about the expected passage of Austrian troops and promise to inform St. Gallen about further developments. Regarding the Gachnang affair, which is being negotiated in Baden, they hope for an amicable settlement.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Appenzell ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to allow their countryman, the coppersmith Jakob Küchleimer, to practice his trade in St. Gallen and sell his goods. They refer to the fact that he learned the trade in St. Gallen and has relatives there. They request that work not be forbidden to him and that previous incidents be interpreted in the best way, so that he may support his children.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have appointed the Landammann Kaspar Giser as envoy to Baden for the new year. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to also send an envoy in order to jointly secure the abolition of the pass. The Appenzell envoy will depart on Friday morning.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the Duke of Bayern has dismissed his war troops recruited for Spanien, except for 1000 musketeers. The remaining 600 soldiers would pass through Lindau gradually. Since the Confederates had settled their disputes and the troops were also allowed to pass through at other places, the Lindauers grant the troops passage over the Gotthard to Welschland.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter from the St. Gallen, in which 600 foot soldiers for Count von Madruz had been requested. They report that it concerns 2000 men who are to be led to Italien. A large number had come on the same day via Buchhorn, Langenargen and Nonnenhorn to Rorschach and had also marched through Lindau. They ask for further developments.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Chur ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a complete report on the offenses and statements of the former citizen of Chur Niklaus Wintrich, who was punished in St. Gallen for his misdeeds. Since contradictory rumors are circulating in Chur, they want to clarify the situation in order to take further measures if necessary and to punish the evil.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen confirm the receipt of a bill of exchange and of 20 gulden. They report that the linen was inspected by the linen measurers and found to be sound. They thank them for the honour shown to their citizens Caspar Schobinger and Bartholomäus Zollikoffer in Lindau and offer in return good neighbourliness and services.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to pardon and forgive the shoemaker Joachim Zolligkhofer, who comes from St. Gallen and has lived in Zürich for six years, for having previously violated the St. Gallen city ordinance. Zolligkhofer wishes to return to his fatherland. Zürich asks for forgiveness and admission, as Zolligkhofer has atoned for his faults through years of exile.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Von Refuge informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he has begun to pay out the general pensions to the other cantons of the Confederation. He sets 25 October as the date on which the envoys of St. Gallen can receive their pensions in the usual manner.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Melchior Goldast von Haimensfeld sends to the Council of the Imperial City of St. Gallen a book with ecclesiastical and secular ordinances of the Empire as well as the library of the deceased citizen of the Council of Nürnberg, Wilbald Pirkheimer. He asks that the survivors of Pirkheimer be taken under the protection of the city, and recommends himself as a faithful friend and servant of the city.
en.recipient: Stattammann, Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Duke Maximilian for the offer to sell grain. They must discontinue the purchase for this occasion, as the prices are high and they hope for a better harvest. For the future, they offer to have the grain delivered to Zell am Untersee, to have it inspected first by their people, and then to act after the most fruitful negotiation.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Maximilian, Duke of Steiermark, Landgrave of Steiermark, Lord of Bappenheim, Hewen and Meußthal

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter of 27 September 1610, in which Berchtold Brümsi had requested a fire tax for the fire in Schänis. They state that a few weeks ago two men from Schänis, who presented documents from Schwyz and Glarus, had requested a fire tax from them. They had fulfilled this request to the best of their ability and thank him for the inquiry.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Berchtold Brümsi zu Berg, bailiff of Gottlieben

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Solothurn ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to explain to their citizen David Liegweiler whether anything is still due to him vis-à-vis the Lords Rotmund and Zollern. Liegweiler has a principal sum unpaid and is burdened with costs. He wishes to travel to St. Gallen to clarify his matter and asks for support. Solothurn asks for a friendly answer to avoid further costs.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Solothurn
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter of intercession from St. Gallen concerning the Lindau citizen Lienhart Loher, who owes the St. Gallen citizen Malcher Müller six silver crowns. Loher has refused payment and promised a counter-statement, which Lindau now forwards. Lindau assures that Loher, who is penniless, will receive justice before the St. Gallen court and fulfill his obligation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a difference between the church ministers of both sides regarding the pastoral care for the Spycherleute. Appenzell declares that the Spycherleute belong to the parish of St. Laurentzen and refuses to draw them into its jurisdiction by force. Since the matter has not yet been sufficiently discussed, Appenzell proposes a friendly conference with learned assistants and has already sent representatives.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Statthalter of the Bürgermeisterthumb and the Council of the city of Basel ask the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen to reject the appointment of Master Ludwig Lucius as rector of the St. Gallen school. Lucius is already intended for a professorship at the Basel Academy. Should Basel be able to fill the position otherwise within two months, they will oblige St. Gallen in this matter.
en.sender: Statthalter of the Bürgermeisterthumb and the Council of the city of Basel
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Landammann and Council of Appenzell that, at the request of the merchants and in agreement with the abbot of St. Gallen, they provisionally recognize the ducats at 2 gulden 16 kreuzer, but only the weighty ones. They ask Appenzell to warn its subjects not to bring new Churer-Behemer coins to St. Gallen, as these are prohibited due to the coinage mandate and to avoid coinage debasement.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern warn the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen of a threatening hostile invasion by the Duke of Savoyen, which is to be directed against the city, the land, and the people, particularly in the Wald. They ask the Confederates to maintain their armaments and, in the event of an attack, to provide the aid agreed upon in the treaty.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell reply to a letter of 22 January. They declare themselves in agreement with the rate of 2 gulden 16 kreuzer for the heavy ducats. Regarding the report on the import of prohibited Chur coinage, they report that their countrymen had obtained it from Hans Ammann Weltein in Fussach. They had had the matter clarified under oath, imposed penalties, and ordered compliance with the coinage edict.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern inform the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen about reports that Duke Karl Emanuel von Savoyen has plans against Genf and the Bernese countryside. They ask the Confederates to arm themselves and to provide assistance in case of emergency. Bern has already stationed troops on the borders and expects an attack. They promise to help St. Gallen in the same case.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Oberster vor Yverdon reports on his journey to Genf, where he spoke with the Lords of La Noue and the Confederates. The Lord of Betune is said to have arrived with 120 evangelical noblemen who wish to serve for six months at their own expense. The Queen has decided to muster 18'000 foot soldiers, 2'000 horses and 6'000 Confederates and intends to proceed to Lyon. The Lord of Lux has orders to relocate the passes in the Lordship of Gex. The bridge at Gresin has been destroyed to hold up the Gauchier. The Royal Procurator from Gex has reported that the Lord de Grand Muttwocher will arrive in Gex with 1'200 horses.
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of the City of Bern

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Hans Ulrich Stadler to pay the outstanding interest and parts of the principal to the citizen of St. Gallen Friedrich Schobinger. This is necessary so that the Basel Martin Luder, to whom the obligation was pledged, can be settled and the obligation redeemed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern thank St. Gallen for the offer of military aid and ask for a waiver of this, as the absence of the citizens would endanger trade transactions in Savoyen, Piemont, and Mailand. Instead, Bern offers 600 silver crowns monthly. Bern also informs about the situation on the borders and at Genf.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern thank St. Gallen for the promise to help with a considerable sum in the event of war. They ask that the promise be kept secret. Since Bern must bear the war costs, they request St. Gallen to inform them in writing which sum would be available in an emergency against interest and bond, so that Bern may act accordingly.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the interrogation of three men detained in Konstanz (Hans Leander, Jörg Schmid, Michael) regarding stolen keys and break-ins in St. Gallen. The detainees deny the acts, but Schmid mentions a journeyman named Hans Reinhartler, who is described as a dangerous offender. In addition, a break-in at a Zolligckhofer's in the Rheintal is mentioned, which occurred a year and a half ago.
en.sender: The Administrator of the Captaincy, the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Glarus ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene in a protracted dispute between the widow of the deceased Burgomaster Rüland and the Tischen of Krietzlen. Glarus has already issued two different rulings, which were open to the parties' choice. Since the widow has again asked for support, Glarus wishes to settle the matter in St. Gallen and move the parties towards an amicable settlement.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern thank the Council of St. Gallen for the friendly offer to lend 10'000 gulden in case of emergency. They ask for forgiveness for a misunderstanding, as their envoy Dr. Wilhelm Fals had been not in St. Gallen, but with some citizens of St. Gallen. They ask to remain in this benevolent disposition, and promise in turn all honor and friendship.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Burgomaster and Council of Lindau to recognize the local citizen Lorenz Müller, son of the deceased Lorenz Müller, as their citizen and to issue him a credible certificate. The weavers' guild in St. Gallen will only admit him to the apprenticeship guild upon presentation of this document. St. Gallen requests Lindau for a written response.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help the advocate Jacob Ungmuot in the protracted legal dispute between the widow Dorothea Hüeterin and Bernhardin Huonrwadel from Schaffhausen. They ask for swift conduct of the proceedings and support, so that the widow receives compensation for her damage and finds peace.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Wil reply to a letter from the authorities of St. Gallen regarding the prisoner Hans Heer. They report that Heer had complained to them that his wife had been taken away from him. He had not been resident in St. Gallen, but in the Hofgericht. The Hofräte of St. Gallen had tried and punished him. His wife, as the daughter of an old citizen, had been admitted as a resident (Hintersasse) for a short time. Wil refers to the letter of the Hofräte for further details.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landshofmeister and Pfalzenzrat of Wil report to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on the case of the citizen Hans Here. He says that he was imprisoned and sentenced to a fine for adultery with the wife of Hans am Büel in Zofingen. Wil released him from custody upon request, with the condition that he refrain from the woman. They ask St. Gallen for further instructions, as Here has turned to the Wil authority.
en.sender: Landshofmeister and Pfalzenzrat of the princely monastery of St. Gallen in Wil
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Wil reply to an inquiry from St. Gallen regarding the imprisoned Hans Feeren. They have asked their citizens how much linen Feeren had bought in Wil. The citizens reported, based on signed slips, that the linen was stamped with Nuremberg staves and crosses and cut into twenty ells. Wil communicates this to St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Night Clerk and Statthalter of the St. Gallen monastery at Wil reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen concerning the prisoner Hans Geern. They report that Geern's property was confiscated by the authorities to satisfy his creditors. Geern himself was released, but his property was pledged. The Statthalter Jörg Elßner owes Geern 230 pounds. If this amount is not paid, the property is to be sold.
en.sender: Night Clerk and Statthalter of the St. Gallen monastery at Wil
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Glarus ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to receive their countryman Heinrich Bücher, who has settled in St. Gallen and is seeking a benefice, in a well-disposed manner as a Confederate. They request that they help him in obtaining a benefice according to their means and treat his applications as if he were acting in his own name or in the name of an entire friendship.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Church Council, the Elders and the Community of the Evangelical German Nation in Prag ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a generous contribution for the construction of churches and schools as well as for the maintenance of teachers and preachers. They refer to the free exercise of the Evangelical doctrine approved by the Emperor and ask for the donation to be entered in the book designated for this purpose.
en.sender: Church Council, Elders and Community of the Evangelical German Nation in Prag
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Solothurn request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Hans Schwaller. He has complained that his appointed factor Heinrich Zysar fled after settling the business and taking in a sum of money. Schwaller wants to pursue the assets and asks for support. Solothurn asks that he be assisted in all due matters.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Christoph Büchler, Ammann, and the judges of the city court of St. Gallen transmit to the Burgomaster and Council of Lindau an open edict. They ask that it be publicly proclaimed and posted in the usual places, so that the creditors of Tisani, including citizens of Lindau, can assert their rights.
en.sender: Christoph Büchler, Ammann, and the judges of the city court of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: Pfleger, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg reply to a letter from Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen concerning the St. Gallen citizen Jacob Bösch. They transmit the declaration of Matthäus Daxhofer and associates, which names the required documents and securities for the claim of Bösch’s wife on the inheritance of the brothers Hans and Elias Mair.
en.sender: Pfleger, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to an inquiry from the Council of Augsburg regarding the indemnification for the citizens of Augsburg Matthäus Dannhoffer and Zacharias Horenshüek. They state that they cannot provide the desired guarantee in the name of the city. However, they are willing for Dannhoffer et Consorti to pledge the house of the citizen of St. Gallen Jacob Hössli as security for the indemnification and to have a corresponding pledge letter issued with the town seal.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Council of Augsburg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen reject the request for remission of the fine for the citizen Jacob Wetzler. He says that he insulted the city's servants, slandered the authorities, and, by purchasing houses shortly before the passage of the Prussians, drove up the grain prices. Wetzler must pay the fine of 38 pounds Heller in full and behave more modestly in the future.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to pardon the banished Wolfgang Zosatz and to open the city to him again. Zosatz was banished for injuring another citizen, but he had behaved honestly in the war and was injured in the arm in the process, so that he can no longer work. The citizens of Zürich ask for help until he can go back into service.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Glarus ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to set a date for the heirs of the deceased Master Josef Wägler, namely Captain Thomas Schmidt and Ulrich Schüch. The heirs should be able to assert their claims to the inheritance as soon as possible, since the division of the inheritance is being delayed by the people of St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Glarus ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hear and advance the widow of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen, Vester Vogler, and the wife of the Glarus resident Fridli Zwik in an inheritance matter. The two women had turned to Glarus to assert their rights to the estate. Glarus requests the support of the Confederates.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to deliver the estate of their deceased sister Agnesa Hötzer to the citizens there, Bonaventura Willin, Madlena Hötzer, Ulrich and Jacob Hötzer. The Lindau authorities confirm the kinship and guardianship of the supplicants and ask for the fulfillment of the legal claim.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Albrecht Zukmantel von Brumatt and the Council of Straßburg ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hold the citizens of Straßburg, Hans Bus and Balthasar Caudolt, in favorable recommendation. They request that official measures be taken against the tailor Hans Schlatter so that he repays the amounts of 27 and 19 florins 9 batzen laid out for the deceased Ernst Schlatter.
en.sender: Hans Albrecht Zukmantel von Brumatt and the Council of Straßburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Glarus ask bailiff Caspar Brüning to present himself to them immediately in order to clarify the situation of the widow of the deceased burgomaster Kelter. It concerns the question of whether she has renounced the Landrecht or has again placed herself under the protection and the Burgrecht of St. Gallen. Glarus wishes to be able to answer St. Gallen accordingly.
en.recipient: Bailiff Caspar Brüning

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Glarus reply to a letter from St. Gallen concerning the widow of the deceased Burgomaster Keller. They ask for information on how and for what reasons the widow acquired the Glarus land law and later renounced it in order to return to the protection of St. Gallen. Since they had not learned any reasons from the widow herself, they call upon their countryman Caspar Stocker to present himself in Glarus in order to clarify the situation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist the Ulm citizen Joseph Schreiber in a matter concerning his deceased stepdaughter Anna Maria Kressin and her husband Anton Thalmann in Horschlein. They refer to the attached petition of Schreiber, in which he asks for the recognition of his son as a legitimate son and for the assumption of guardianship for the child.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen reply to the letter of 2 January concerning sunken linen. They report that the shipman Schnerzgais had sailed in strong weather against the ship regulations and had departed without a customs ticket. The fault lies with him, not with the other shipmen. Schnerzgais has been arrested and obliged to pay. Schaffhausen remains bound to St. Gallen in Confederate friendship.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans auf der Mur, Landvogt der freien Ämter des Ergaues, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the relatives of the deceased Webers Jacob Nägeli in Mülebach to take over and maintain his three children. Nägeli’s widow Magdalena Spilmanin has requested a letter of intercession, as she cannot feed the children.
en.sender: Hans auf der Mur, Landvogt der freien Ämter des Ergaues
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant a gracious support to the widow Anna Eilgeßin and her children out of Christian compassion. Their deceased husband, the citizen of St. Gallen Valten Felen, is said to have died of the plague after he had cared for the infected in St. Gallen. Kempten has already maintained her eldest son at its own expense.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landvogt Diethrich Reding von Schwyz asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to leave the two orphans of the deceased Jörg am Büel and his wife Elisabeth Messmerin in their inheritance right to the goods of the deceased Aunt N. Messmerin. He submits a certificate confirming the children's legitimate birth and the good reputation of the parents.
en.sender: Diethrich Reding von Schwyz, Landvogt of the County of Toggenburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landvogt Sebastian Wirtz in Turgau to resume the process between Hans Scheggern and the Vogtkind Gregorius Dolders of Pfinhausen. They ask him to announce a date to the parties for the 4th or 5th of February, so that the matter can be decided favorably and further delays avoided.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Sebastian Wirtz, Landvogt in Turgau

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Glarus ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their councilor and captain Niklaus Vogel in the settlement of the estate of the deceased Thomas Marti in St. Gallen. As they cannot appear in person due to bad weather and other business, they request support and friendly treatment of their envoy.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the Landvogt of Frauenfeld to reopen the law in a legal dispute between Hans Bisegger and the Vogtkind Gorius Dolder and to refer the matter to the lower bench for discussion. They refer to the fact that Bisegger did not specify the costs for legal representation and that his claim to be more closely related than the Vogtkind is not correct. They request a free judgment without prejudicial attachment, in order to avoid further costs and disputes.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt of Frauenfeld

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen to grant their citizen Appolonia Kenerknechtin, widow from Staufen, the assurance that she, as the next heir of the deceased Anna Kenerknechtin, wife of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Hans Ulrich Franckh, may take up the inheritance. They ask that the heir be favored without hindrance and with moderate deduction.
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Sebastian Wininger, Landvogt in Upper and Lower Thurgau, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to allow the sworn court bailiff Martin Tochha and his co-heirs to take possession of a divided inheritance in the city. Wininger promises in return to adhere to the Thurgau inheritance practice and to render service to St. Gallen.
en.sender: Sebastian Wininger, Landvogt in Upper and Lower Thurgau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ybbs ratify the settlement of the estate of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Hans Ulrich Krantz by their town bailiff Hans Spörker. They ask St. Gallen to pay out the remaining 50 florins to the widow Apollonia Knerknecht. Ybbs promises to transfer the amount by bill of exchange and thanks for the inheritance upon departure.
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Stadtrath and Council of Bregenz ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to conduct an inquisition and investigation into insults and abusive words that were allegedly made to the Bregenz citizen Hans Caspar Schmid by sons of Bregenz citizens in St. Gallen. They ask for written notification of the results in order to be able to proceed against the guilty parties.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to secure for their citizen Peter Herb, the weaver, the inheritances of his deceased sister-in-law Barbara Mößlinin that are due to him by right and local custom. They also request that Herb be allowed to pass through unimpeded, as he comes from the city where the plague is raging.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Christoph von Schwanbach and Hans Bruder, stewards of the court before Kreuzlingen, ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for help in a legal dispute. They complain about a judgment of the Landvogt of Güttingen, which obliges their vassal Georg Stähelin to bear all common burdens like an ordinary subject. This contradicts the old customs of their free court. They ask for a written explanation of how the judgment is to be understood.
en.sender: Christoph von Schwanbach and Hans Bruder, stewards of the court before Kreuzlingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Zürich report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, in response to their letter, they were unable to find the tailor's journeyman Peter Mafej von Abbenzell in the city and have no knowledge that he ever worked in Zürich. They assure them that they would hand him over or interrogate him, as desired, upon his future arrival or renewed inquiry.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Maximilian, Herzog in Obern und Nidern Bayern, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he has lifted the closure of the city and its surroundings imposed because of the plague. He says that he has instructed his officials not to hinder the St. Gallen citizens in the future and to let them pass freely.
en.sender: Maximilian, Herzog in Obern und Nidern Bayern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Landvogt Johann Ludwig Würtz to urge the heirs of the deceased town councillor Hans Zünd to hand over in writing to the widow of the deceased David Vögelin the requested account for the costs of care and burial of the deceased maid. Should this not happen, the heirs are to be summoned before the Council of St. Gallen on 15 April at 8 o'clock in the morning to negotiate the acknowledged claims.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Johann Ludwig Würtz, Landvogt of Rorschach

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to release the imprisoned Mathäus Kästlin, son of the Lindau Burgomaster Matthias Kästlin. They refer to the attached supplication of the father, who states that his son suffers from a natural defect that renders him incapable of action when consuming alcohol. Lindau requests that leniency be preferred over strictness, so that the punishment does not harm the son in honor and trade.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report to St. Gallen on the statement of the tailor's apprentice Peter Waffli, who was questioned under oath regarding the accusations against Barbara Hartmann. Waffli testifies that Hartmann claimed that her deceased brother Züger had not impregnated her, but rather a shoemaker's apprentice imprisoned in St. Gallen. Furthermore, Hartmann stated that she wanted to have her marriages drawn out of her body one after the other and had gifted Waffli clothing.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizen Wolfgang Baderen in an inheritance dispute concerning a property at Arbon. Baderen defends himself against the demand of his brothers-in-law to carry the property in high money, and demands its sale or fair distribution. Zürich requests St. Gallen to relieve Baderen and his co-guarantors from the burden and to secure his right.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help the citizens of St. Gallen Tobias Stüeler, Jacob Kleinhanß, Ulrich Stüeler and Daniel Stüeler. These are the heirs of the deceased St. Gallen bailiff of Burgl, Gall Maurer, and his wife Susanna Güsserin. They are to receive the inheritance due to them, as the estate is said to have already been touched and sold.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hand over the sum deposited with the St. Gallen Chancery, which the St. Gallen citizen Friedrich Schobinger owes to their citizen Hans Ludwig Schwartzenbach, to the heirs of Schwartzenbach. The heirs wish to settle the claims of the divorced wife and other creditors. Zürich undertakes to satisfy all claims.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Glarus request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hand over to the citizens of Glarus Michael Vogel and Kaspar Wyss an inventory of the property inherited by them from the deceased Johann Wattli. They are to hand over the property to the heirs after payment of the surety and to allow their departure without further notice.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the Chapter of Bischofszell. They are willing to seal the letters with the seal of the office of the lordship of Bürglen, since the former bailiff cannot be compelled. Regarding the fine, they propose that an Amtmann or another envoy of the monastery come to St. Gallen, so that the matter can be discussed by Council delegates.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Kustos, Seniores and Chapter of the Collegiate Church of St. Pelagius in Bischofszell

en.regest: The sender in Basel informs about the granting of a privilege to the goods carriers Annoni, Volpi and Lorenzi, who receive the exclusive right for 24 years to carry goods between the Netherlands and Italien. The family Gabalioni from Turin attempts to break this privilege and has turned to the Swiss envoy in Luzern. The envoy is now in Basel, where he is explained that the privilege applies only to the three named goods carriers and that other merchants could freely move their own goods.
en.recipient: Ehrenueste, fürnemme, insonders gönstige herren unnd fründt

en.regest: Burgomaster, Judges and Council of Graz request Judges and Council of St. Gallen to help the citizens there, Hans Staiger, Jacob Staiger and Georg Lämpl, the sons of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Hans Staiger, in the settlement of the inheritance of their aunt Barbara. Since the two sons from Graz cannot travel there, they request a power of attorney for Jacob Staiger, so that he can settle the inheritance and return to Graz quickly.
en.sender: Burgomaster, Judges and Council of Graz
en.recipient: Judges and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Glarus request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their countrymen Nicolaus Vogel and Fridli Aeble. These have received an inventory that was handed over to them by the Sekellmeister Schmidt and the master builder Schüch. They hope for a uniform copy without costs. Glarus asks St. Gallen to help the two countrymen so that they receive the inventory, their accounts, and a complete report, in order to know what is due to them.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen regarding the citizen of St. Gallen Katharina Nägin and a contract with her children. They state that Nägin wishes to pay 700 gulden to her legitimate children from the marriage with the deceased citizen of Konstanz Jacob Wüßerrei. They assure that they will not oppose it if the mother and the children receive this amount, and attach this as a receipt.
en.sender: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish an edict concerning a scheduled general debt court day for the departed citizen of Lindau, Joseph Rogels Müller zu Heimastetten, and his wife, so that the creditors can assert their rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg reply to a letter of 5 March. They state that Othmar Basthardt, the heir of the deceased Dorothea Basthardt, has been banished from Ravensburg for about eleven years on account of insults to honour and the resulting lawsuits. Since he has died, they cannot give any information about his person.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Duke Karl Emanuel von Savoyen asks the Lords of the City of St. Gallen to intervene with the Lords of Basel so that all his subjects can transport goods between Italien and Flandern via Basel, without individual carters hindering this under false pretences. In return, he promises to protect and maintain the four families of St. Gallen citizens in his city.
en.recipient: Lords of the City of St. Gallen

en.regest: Appollinaris Iten, Landvogt in the Rintal, thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for their congratulations. He asks for an excuse that he cannot extend his stay in St. Gallen, as he must arrive with his men in Ägeri the next day and reach the St. Gallen monastery on Friday evening.
en.sender: Appollinaris Iten, Landvogt in the Rintal
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Bregenz request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to take into custody the weaver Jeremias Miller there, who has violated the imperial privilege of the city of Bregenz. Miller says that he has bought up and removed yarn within the mile around Bregenz, which harms the toll rights of the city. Bregenz reserves the right to further negotiate the matter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about the receipt of an intercession letter for the citizen of St. Gallen Jeremias Miller, who is in a feud with the city of Kempten. They recommend that Miller settle amicably with Kempten and refrain from such encroachments in the future. Otherwise, Kempten will proceed legally. Furthermore, they set a court day for 17 July and allow Miller to have the upper Feldtmühle inspected.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Duke Karl Emanuel von Savoyen complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the St. Gallen merchants Christoph Scherer, Christoph Krom and their partners had defrauded the General Postmaster Don Ascanio Sandri of about two million ducats. He asks the city to provide redress so that Sandri may recover his money, in order to preserve the reputation of the St. Gallen merchants in his lands.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Duke Karl Emanuel von Savoyen reports to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the St. Gallen merchant Christoph Heinrich Scherer and his relatives, to whom his Council and chief clerk Ascanio Sandri had lent up to 5000 ducats, had transported their goods and withdrawn to their fatherland. He asks the city to help Sandri to his money, in order to avert future damage to his subjects.
en.recipient: Herrn der Stadt St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform the Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz that the Council of the city of Nürnberg has published a coinage ordinance. They learn that the Züger thick pennies and other coins of the same value have been set at 20 kreuzer. They ask for a written report on what measures Konstanz has taken in this matter.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: Abbot Heinrich of Kempten informs that the Burgomaster and Council of Kempten had complained about the citizen of Kempten Jeremias Müller. He is said to have used forbidden roads with goods from the market of Kempten, Dietmannsried, and to have evaded toll. The Abbot rejects the accusations, as the market is free and Kempten has no rights there. He asks St. Gallen not to give credence to the accusations, not to punish Müller, and to send him a copy of the letter from Kempten.
en.sender: Heinrich, Abbot of the Foundation of Kempten
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen demand from Statthalter and Council of the city of Zürich the repayment of 4000 Sonnenkronen with interest, which have been outstanding since 1622. They instruct their fellow citizen Christoph Sallenmüller to collect the debt and ask Zürich to support him in the claim and to make a substantial partial payment.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of the city of Zürich

en.regest: Several citizens of Kempten ask the Burgomaster and Council of Kempten to direct a letter of intercession to St. Gallen. They are creditors of the Scherrer and Krumen, who are insolvent in St. Gallen, and fear that the citizens of St. Gallen will satisfy their claims with priority. They refer to the case of the Zollighofer and ask for equal treatment of foreign creditors.
en.sender: Joseph König, Magdalena Paulus, Jacob Schüzer and others
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in a debt matter that is the subject of an accompanying supplication, to treat the Kempten supplicants justly. They refer to the fact that with them, in such cases, always the older debt instruments and the better right take precedence, and ask for the same treatment as they grant their own citizens in St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz reply to an inquiry from St. Gallen regarding the Zuger and Zürcher ducats. They state that the coinage ordinance of Nürnberg is not yet observed in Konstanz and that the ducats continue to circulate at 23 kreuzer. They ask St. Gallen to inform them if a new valuation is decided there.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to question their citizens Jeremias Ebnat and Lorenz Cuenz as well as the widow of the deceased Georg Strauben and to have them testify in writing whether they had seen a letter from the Kempten citizen Hans Greither, in which he is supposed to have guaranteed a wine purchase. The testimonies are to be transmitted at the expense of the Kempten side.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich reply to the request for prompt confirmation of the Confederates' privileges towards the new Empress. They report that the envoys of the cantons accepted the application at the Diet at Baden and postponed it to the next Diet in October. Since the time of the Imperial Diet is still uncertain, the matter can remain pending until then, without anything being lost.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen congratulate N. von Castilion on his appointment as French ambassador in the Confederation. They ask him to settle the outstanding peace money for the previous year and the current year, as they did not receive it from Mr. de Refuge. They request written notification of when they should send their messengers to collect the amounts.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: N. von Castilion, French ambassador

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen that they have appointed a peremptory court day against the citizens Christoph Heinrich Scheren, Christoph Kromen and co-relatives. Since citizens of Memmingen, in particular Hans Roth and Melchior Reutol, are also affected, they ask for the cause to be announced in Memmingen.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Hauptleute and Council of Trogen for information regarding the reputation and conduct of their fellow citizen Jerg Brüderer, who is detained in St. Gallen on suspicion of linen fraud. They wish to know whether he has a good or bad name, in order to be able to proceed with him more securely.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Hauptleute and Council of Trogen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of the Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene in a neighborly manner for their countryman Jag Bruederer, who is a prisoner in St. Gallen. They point out that he has always behaved honestly in Appenzell, and ask that he not be treated according to the strictness of the law.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen. It concerns the request of the King of Savoyen to obtain a pass for his subjects, who travel through Basel with goods. The Zürich councillors, who are already in Basel, were instructed to negotiate with the Baselers and to move them to a friendly decision. Zürich hopes for a soon positive solution.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform the Prelate that in the latest Baden annual account the Hanau and Hagenau thick pennies were fixed at 23 kreuzer. They ask why the Prelate had estimated these at 22 kreuzer, and request equal treatment so that no disadvantage arises for the Land.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Mr. Prelate of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to provide the widow Elisabeth Stadelmann, left behind by the deceased preacher Jakob Allgäuer, with a benefice in the hospital. She is to be treated like the other preachers' widows and included in the inscription, so that she may have her maintenance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Herr von Pappenheim that they cannot conclude the proposed grain purchase, as the payment is to be made immediately and in cash, whereas they do not have the necessary funds due to other civic complaints. They ask that this decision not be taken amiss, and thank him for the friendly treatment of their envoys.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Herr von Pappenheim

en.regest: Maximilian, Herzog zu Steiermark, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he had negotiated with their envoys regarding the sale of fruits. The proposed means are good for both sides, but were only accepted ad referendum, as the envoys were not sufficiently empowered. He asks for a quick response regarding the decision of the city.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen refer to the Baselers regarding an enclosed letter from Herr von der Tornetta, which concerns the conduct business in the name of the French King. They ask the Baselers to pass their still outstanding resolution soon and to direct it in such a way that no mutual complaints arise. They assure them that they will undertake nothing that could be to the detriment of the Baselers, and ask for a friendly reply.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Basel

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Frankfurt ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admit their citizens Johann du Fay and Johann de Famar in a debt matter against the departed citizen of St. Gallen Christoph Heinrich Scherer, Christoph Krumen and Consorts on equal terms with the citizens of St. Gallen. They refer to the fact that in Frankfurt there is no preference for locals over foreigners in personal actions, and ask for reciprocity.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Council of Nordhausen informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a devastating city fire on 21 August, which destroyed the greatest part of the city within the ring walls, both towers of the Oberpfarrkirche St. Nikolai, as well as grain stores. The damage is enormous. Since the affected citizens ask for support, the Nordhausen authorities request their St. Gallen colleagues for a helpful contribution to the reconstruction.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Landvogt Beat Jakob Frey in Thurgau to hear the complaint of their citizens Lorenz Kessel and Johannes Scheitermann against Caspar Speger willingly and to settle it with a swift process. They point to the danger of delays and evasions and have appointed the Stattschreiber Melchior Guldin as counsel for the plaintiffs.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Beat Jakob Frey, Landvogt in upper and lower Thurgau

en.regest: The Consuls and Senate of the Imperial City of Frankfurt am Main ask the Consuls and Senate of the City of St. Gallen to intervene for their citizens Johannes du Fay and Johannes de Famars. They request that the messenger Stephan de Famars, as the mandatories of the two citizens, be given credit by the authority of the St. Gallen authorities in the handing over of the money and in the settlement of the associated business.
en.sender: Consuls and Senate of the Imperial City of Frankfurt am Main
en.recipient: Consuls and Senate of the City of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in the debt matter of the citizen of St. Gallen Christoph Scherer, to spare his wife and children. Since the creditors would have seized the debtor's property, one fears that the innocent family may fall into misery. One requests that the wife and children be spared as far as possible, so that they may remain in their house and support themselves.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their fellow citizen Otilie Heelme, widow née von Vonbühl, in a dispute with her neighbor Hans Bartholomäus Schobinger. They refer to the attached supplication of the widow, in which she complains about structural changes and damages, and request a favorable consideration of their letter of intercession.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Köln confirm the receipt of a letter of 7. August concerning the departed citizen Christoph Hennßler Scherer as well as Christoph Kroomen and Unterländer as creditors. They have had the attached citation posted at the designated places. Since the Jacob Kräuter named therein has traveled to Frankfurt, the appointed deadline could not be communicated to him. This is to be made up upon his return. Since the specified time has almost elapsed, they ask St. Gallen to place Kräuter and the other parties under the protection of the Empire, so that no disadvantage may arise to them.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Köln
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Bernhard Burkhard, bailiff of the lordship of Grüningen, for support for their fellow citizen and butcher Jacob Appenzeller. He says that he bought a calf from Ammann Johann Heinrich von Tobel in Rapperswil, which was however defective. Tobel refuses compensation. The St. Gallen ask for a friendly mediation so that Tobel will make good the damage.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Bernhard Burkhard, Council of Zürich, bailiff of the lordship of Grüningen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Solothurn report that their citizen Hans Schneller was arrested in St. Gallen on account of an obligation against Christoph Heinrich and Christoph Thomas, and that his letters were confiscated. They ask St. Gallen to return the letters and securities to Schneller or to communicate the cause of the arrest.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the authorities of Schaffhausen. They have interrogated their citizen Ludwig König, the bookseller. He stated that the matter is of a different nature than it appears to the Schaffhausers. The St. Gallen ask the Schaffhausers to excuse König. Should the heirs of the deceased Doctor Lorenz Rotmund not be satisfied with the answer given so far, they may substantiate their claim more closely.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen

en.regest: Decastille reports that the envoys of St. Gallen had asked him in Baden for the payment of the pensions. Since the money has arrived, the envoys can be sent to Solothurn with their usual receipts to collect the peace and alliance money, where he will have it paid out.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Glarus ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their countryman Fridolin Zäsyer. He says that he bought the house and farm of Adam Tschudi in Rütten. Tschudi, however, declared that he does not want to honor the purchase, as he has a claim against the heir Ringler, which he wants to use to pay the purchase price. Glarus asks St. Gallen to forbid Tschudi from collecting his claim against Ringler until the purchase contract is fulfilled.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz answer an inquiry from the St. Gallen in the dispute between the creditors Christoph Heinrich and Christoph Thomas and the citizen of Konstanz Hans Schüin. They confirm that the items sent by Thomas to Schüin, as listed in the attached inventory, have already been returned. Schüin's wife has affirmed this under oath.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Solothurn ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hand over to their citizen Hans Schwallers the obligation of the St. Gallen citizens Schärer and to grant him justice before the St. Gallen court. Schwallers is represented by the Glarner Caspar Freulin. The Schärer had retained the obligation, although Schwallers pays the interest. Solothurn refers to the Confederation's legal aid and asks for prompt proceedings.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Hans Schmuck in the bankruptcy proceedings concerning the assets of the wife of the bankruptcy opponent in St. Gallen. They have issued him a document which he is to present. The men of St. Gallen are to let Schmuck obtain money not only from the citizens but also from the wife of the bankruptcy opponent.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish the edict concerning the appointed court day for the creditors of the deceased citizen and coppersmith of Lindau, Melchior Weber, so that no one be curtailed in his rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landvogt Dietrich Reding to issue the birth certificate of their citizen Heinrich Tobler's fiancée Elisabeth Baumgartner from the bailiwick. Tobler has learned that a document regarding his conduct is required from him beforehand. The St. Gallen authorities consider this a questionable innovation and ask Reding to comply with the request without delay or to communicate their concerns to them in writing.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Dietrich Reding, Landvogt of the County of Toggenburg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to amicably settle the disputes between the Lindau citizen Johannes Keller and the citizens of St. Gallen. Should a settlement not be reached, they request that the matter be handed over to the Lindau Council for decision. The letter refers to an attached supplication by Keller, who asks for support in the settlement of his mother-in-law's estate.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank for the letter and the enclosed coin types. They inform that they have forbidden the Mantuan thaler with shield and have instructed their merchants not to accept the transmitted types. They ask for information about the measures in Konstanz and promise to report on the reaction of the Prelate.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Solothurn request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to deliver the obligation of their citizen Hans Schwallern to a messenger without delay. They refer to a lawsuit against the citizens of St. Gallen Sebastian and Georg Schärer, who serve as sureties for Schwallern. Solothurn wishes to examine the obligation in order to protect Schwallern and expects a reply.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they are dissolving the arrest that their Landammann Konrad Tanner had imposed against the St. Gallen Balthasar Rotmund on account of a wine debt of Hans Agmüller. They ask St. Gallen to release the arrested person and to settle the debt. However, Appenzell reserves the right to continue pursuing the claim of the Landammann against Rotmund.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, because of the strong influx of thaler, Dickpfennigen and Dreikreuzer, which were being spent above their value, they would have to make a moderation or a prohibition. They ask the St. Gallen to tell their messenger how the payment and the coin types stand with them and whether an order has already been issued or resolved there.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Appenzell for the release of the citizen Balthasar Rotmund and Elisabeth Reutlingerin. However, they reject an arrest against Appenzellers who had bought hay and orally promised not to drive the cattle away before payment. Furthermore, they inform Appenzell about the ban on low-value coin denominations that were sent from Konstanz, and ask for compliance.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Ammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Lindau that they had amicably settled the dispute between the citizen of Lindau Johannes Veller and the widow of Gabriel Krämer. However, Veller reserved a claim of 160 gulden against the son of the deceased Anton Wolfen. As the widow disputed the debt and the son did not pay, St. Gallen could not impose compensation on the widow. The question of whether the son must pay for the father was referred to the imperial Kammergerichtskommission.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: A woman asks the Council of St. Gallen to intervene with Jacob Alther so that he honors her and the joint child. She explains that Alther promised her this, but she is poor and cannot acquire citizenship on her own. She asks for forgiveness for her behavior and for support so that Alther fulfills his promises.
en.sender: An unnamed woman (mother of the child of Jacob Alther)
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter of 14 and 18 January 1613, in which St. Gallen had requested assistance regarding the citizen Jacob Zilchenen and the Lindau citizen Barbara Messmerin, called Riedin. Lindau had summoned the Messmerin, who has now submitted a counter-report. This is handed over to St. Gallen for information. Lindau is of the opinion that, if the matter stands as Messmerin presents it, St. Gallen's request can be granted.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Barbara Wisererin, daughter of Urban Wiserer, asks the Council of Lindau for paternal mercy and grace. She describes herself as a humble, distressed, and deeply troubled citizen. The letter is a supplication regarding an intercession letter from the Council of St. Gallen for Jacob Altherr.
en.recipient: Council of Lindau

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Solothurn inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the St. Gallen merchant Hans Schwaller has died. They ask that the deadline for the appeal not be allowed to lapse, but that one first wait until a guardian for the heirs has been appointed. Furthermore, they request that the original obligation of the deceased be handed over for examination, so that the heirs can safeguard their rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Glarus request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hand over the still outstanding inheritance to the heirs of the deceased Josef Mathis. The Vögte of St. Gallen had initially seized the property in order to examine whether Wolfgang Mathis was still alive. Since he cannot be found, the Glarus authorities request the release of the property and offer a guarantee for the main estate.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Landvogt in the Rheintal. They say that they received it late and cannot give a complete Council. On the next Tuesday, the inspection of the bridge at Wadt will take place. They ask the Landvogt to be present at this hearing in person or through representatives, and promise an answer.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Appollinario Iten, Landvogt in the Rheintal

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Solothurn ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to provide them with a verbatim copy of an obligation, as the St. Gallen side would have refused the original. They wish to use this to continue the process concerning the estate of the deceased citizen of Solothurn, Hans Schwaller. Furthermore, they inform them that they will appoint an arbitrator with full power for this matter.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Solothurn
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen ask Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur to assist their town Ammann Christoph Bühler in clarifying the bankruptcy case of the St. Gallen citizen Christoph Heinrich Scherer. It concerns the determination of the property brought in by the wife Anna Hettlingerin. Winterthur is to make the necessary appointments with the persons concerned so that the report can be submitted in writing.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur

en.regest: Caspar Graf zu Hohen-Embs und Gallara replies to the letter from the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen regarding the detained persons. These are suspected of having broken into houses in St. Gallen, robbed them, and attacked the bleach. The Count promises to forward the statements and judgments of the prisoners after their interrogation, and declares himself ready for neighborly friendship.
en.sender: Caspar Graf zu Hohen-Embs und Gallara
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen confirm the receipt of a letter from Count Caspar von Hohenems und Galla as well as the attached settlements of the recently justified wrongdoers. They thank him for the neighborly good will and offer their services for the future.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Count Caspar zu Hohenems und Galla

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur reply to an inquiry from the Council of St. Gallen regarding a claim by the widow Anna Hegenerin against the Landschreiber Hegener. He says that he did not manage his sister's inheritance himself, but left it to his wife. After the death of the father, Hegener received 500 and 57 florins and collected the interest from the properties in the County of Kyburg in order to increase his capital. Winterthur asks St. Gallen to consider the widow and her children with favor.
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Caspar Graf zu Hohenems und Gallara sends the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the judgments concerning maleficium persons who were imprisoned in Hohenems and executed on the 29th of the previous month. He asks that the judgments be examined so that the rascals still at large can be arrested and punished according to their deserts.
en.sender: Caspar Graf zu Hohenems und Gallara
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from Landvogt Rippel. They declare themselves willing to support the proposal of the Landvogt in order to achieve an amicable settlement in the matter between Brünzhorn and the young men. The daughter will appear the following Tuesday morning with the previous assessors and bailiffs in Rineck, in order to await further amicable negotiations. They ask that the escort previously granted also be confirmed for this occasion.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt Rippel

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen that the embassy to the Empress, planned for the Imperial Diet at Regensburg to confirm the privileges of the Confederation, must be cancelled. Luzern has refused the mission because of the high costs and possible new obligations, particularly with regard to the Turkish aid. Schwyz and Unterwalden would join this opinion. They ask St. Gallen to discuss the further steps at the next meeting of the cantons.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admit the smith Michael Geibel as a citizen. His father Hans Geibel has committed to transferring 150 gulden in cash to him, so that he can meet the city's requirements for the admission to citizenship and marriage. Lindau requests the acceptance of the offer and promises reciprocity.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Solothurn ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in the process concerning the estate of the deceased citizen of Solothurn Hans Schmallen, to hand over the original bond to the authorized Council of St. Gallen Fridliß Glutzen. They request that further costs be spared and that Glutzen be granted his right, without a prejudicial judgment being issued against the debtor.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Solothurn
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Landvogt Beat Jakob Frey for the just finding of the judgment in favor of their fellow citizens Lorenz Stachelen and Johannes Schüchzren against Caspar Meyer. They ask him to carry out the execution of the judgment immediately and not to allow delays by the opponent, so that the law may take its course.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Beat Jakob Frey, Landvogt in Thurgau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur to convey to their fellow citizen N. Schellenberg, innkeeper at the Krone, that 26 July is the deadline for an amicable settlement with the St. Gallen goldsmith Gabriel Murer. Schellenberg ended his apprenticeship with Murer prematurely and, despite his oath, did not present himself for the settlement. In the event of a lack of settlement, Schellenberg should expect the due right.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Sebastian Horger to provide for the Kempten citizen Bartholomea Appolonia, whom he has impregnated. Horger has abandoned the child. Kempten asks St. Gallen to compel Horger to take over the child, to pay alimony, or to reach an amicable settlement.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Lindau to help their citizen Erasmus Abbenzeller. He says that he has handed over a house and a garden to his brother-in-law Mathias Bletscher, a citizen of Lindau, as security for an inheritance of less than twenty gulden. Bletscher, however, does not want to be content with this. St. Gallen requests Lindau to exert influence on Bletscher or to report in writing what is lacking, so that Abbenzeller is not detained any longer.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen, which concerned the release of a small inheritance to the citizen of Lindau Hans Abbenzeller by the citizen of St. Gallen Mathis Schlagharn. Lindau declares that, according to old custom, inheritances would only be released after 30 years without bail. However, since the property is small and Abbenzeller has provided a security on house and garden, they have instructed Schlagharn to hand over the property to Abbenzeller or his wife, whereby the tenth gulden is to be retained as a deduction and is to be guaranteed by Lindau.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen inform the Herr Official of Konstanz that they do not recognize his authority to cite their citizen Barbara Schlumpf before the marriage court of Konstanz. They refer to the jurisdiction of their own marriage court and of the cantons ruling in the Reintal. They ask the Official to suspend the proceedings against Georg Herr von Rinegg until the question of competence is clarified at the next Jarrechnung in Baden im Aargau, otherwise they protest against the citation and all further steps.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Herr Official of Konstanz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen declare a proceeding null and void. They reserve the right to proceed against the lawsuit in order to preserve their freedoms and overlordship, and refuse the execution of any potential judgment.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of the city of St. Gallen ask the Herr Official of Konstanz to give belief and hearing to their Statthalter Melchior Guldlin, who hands them a letter of protestation. They ask him to value this as an expression of their good opinion.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the city of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Herr Official of Konstanz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to release Caspar Hazenberg, son of Catharina Hazenbergin, who is accommodated in the Lindau hospital, who is detained there, upon the present supplication. They consider the reasons advanced not unreasonable and promise that Lindau will behave favorably towards St. Gallen in similar cases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell reply to an inquiry from the city of St. Gallen regarding Peter Nägeli, who is detained in Appenzell. Nägeli was sentenced in 1612 for begging and vagrancy and banished from the land. The accusation by Lukas Knechtli, who was executed in Bregenz in 1615, against Nägeli is false. Knechtli admitted shortly before his execution that he had falsely accused Nägeli. Appenzell leaves the further handling of the case to St. Gallen.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter from St. Gallen of 5 March regarding the St. Gallen citizen Jacob Alther and the woman of Lindau Barbara Messmer. They pass on the statement of Messmer and express doubt about her account, as Alther may have promised her a marriage. They leave the further assessment of the case to the Council of St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich reply to the letter of the Äussere Roden Appenzell and St. Gallen regarding the passage of foreign war troops through the land of the Gotteshaus St. Gallen. They support the recipients protesting with the abbot of the Gotteshaus St. Gallen. Should a further passage threaten, they wish to consult with other interested cantons in order to bring the complaints before the next Badische Jährrechnung.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Äussere Roden of the land of Appenzell, Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Glarus ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their Statthalter Adam Böniger in the taking over of the inheritance of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Jos Walther. Böniger has made himself available as guarantor for the heirs of the widow of the deceased bailiff Nicolaus Vogel. Glarus requests St. Gallen to hear Böniger amicably and to bring the matter to an amicable settlement.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Schultheiss and Council of Bern to remain unburdened by the Confederation and to offer their help to the citizens of St. Gallen. The background is a dispute over the inheritance of the wives of the citizens of St. Gallen Lorenz Teschler and Johannes Schaihemann, which Caspar Meier from the Thierhag is conducting. St. Gallen fears that a judgment of the Landvogt in the Reintal could lead to disadvantages for both sides, and wishes that the judgment of St. Gallen be taken into account by the envoys at Baden.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Bern

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to release the weaver Caspar Hazenberg, who is detained in St. Gallen. Hazenberg’s Vögte, Abraham Schlaipfer and Heinrich Sauter, had submitted a supplication in Lindau, in which they affirm Hazenberg’s innocence and request an intercession with the Council of St. Gallen. Lindau agrees to the request and asks St. Gallen to release Hazenberg so that he can answer for himself.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Mülhausen reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen dated 23 March regarding the estate of the deceased goldsmith Hans Rudolf Ritter. They report that Ritter died of the plague and that his mother Elisabeth Buchterin has taken over the inheritance. They have sold the weaving materials mentioned in the supplication to Baden in Aargau. They assure that they will maintain the friendship of the Confederates.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the eight cantons of the Reintal to adjudicate the innovation undertaken by Georg Heer von Rineck against them, so that they may remain unimpeded in their jurisdiction and their freedoms. They request that no precedent be made on the case of a young single man, which would be burdensome to them and to other cantons of the Confederation.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: The eight cantons of the Reintal

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Glarus request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to continue granting the annual reward to their town clerk Melchior Bell and his cousin Albrecht Vogel for the transmission of the Confederates' copies. This had been customary until now and is now requested again following the death of the former Councillor Joachim Vogel.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Kempten request Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen, after the creditors from the estate of the deceased court clerk and bailiff of Bürglen have been paid, to distribute to the Kempten relatives the share due to them. In particular, the Kempten councilor Jacob Kleinhans is to be repaid the 14 gulden and 15 kreuzer he advanced without remuneration.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Kempten
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen inform bailiff Luzen Riser that the marital dispute between Jörgen Heren and Barbara Schlumpf has been settled by a compromise.
