They ask Riser to ensure that Heren collects the awarded amount of 500 gulden and that the St. Gallen side issues a receipt. Furthermore, they annul the purchase of the farm at Thal by Heinrich Schlumpf for his daughters, as this was done without the consent of the authorities, and request a document.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Bailiff Luzen Riser, Landvogt in the Rhinthal

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have appointed a general court day for their citizen Jakob Egger and his wife Clara Haldlin. They ask the authorities of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish the attached edict, so that even naturalized or affiliated persons who might have claims against Egger may take notice of it.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Glarus confirm to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they will gladly fulfill the request of the deceased Landstatthalter Adam Böniger to grant the settlements and new allowances as before. They thank them for the special trust that St. Gallen has shown towards Böniger and promise to act benevolently in similar cases as well.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the granting of an arrest against the bankruptcy of Hans Heinrich Heining in Lyon for the benefit of their citizen Heinrich Schopfen. They ask for further support and favorable treatment so that Schopfen may successfully enforce his claim in the bankruptcy proceedings.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landvogt Appolinari Iten in the Rheintal to postpone the discussion of a legal dispute between Christoph Raa of Lindau and the heirs of the deceased Daniel Schirmann by two to three weeks. The guardian of the heirs, Johannes Schirmann, cannot appear due to a serious accident. A representative should be appointed who will help continue and conclude the proceedings with the plaintiff.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Appolinari Iten, Landvogt in the Rheintal

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Bern report on the dispute with the Bishop of Konstanz over the rights of the citizens of Bern in the Münstertal. They refer to old contracts and the reintroduction of the Burgrecht. Since the Bishop does not accept the new regulations and is raising troops, they ask St. Gallen for help and support to prevent an armed conflict.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The letter contains only the address lines to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, who are described as pious, provident, venerable, wise, special good friends and faithful dear Confederates. No letter text with substantive content is present.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the letter of the Council of Bern from 24 September. The latter had turned to St. Gallen because of the threatening unfriendliness of the Bishop of Basel towards the renewed citizen rights in the Münstertal. St. Gallen declares that the rights of the Münsterthaler are not affected by the Biel exchange. It promises to comfort the Münsterthaler, to look after them, and to defend them with all means if necessary.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Bern

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern thank St. Gallen for its friendly statement in the Münsterthaler affair. They report that the Bishop of Basel, through the mediation of the French ambassador, has dismissed the Maesspriester and closed the sacristy. However, the Bishop wishes to annul the old contracts and examine his powers. Bern has protested against this and demanded the reinstatement of the Münsterthaler to their status. Bern asks St. Gallen to remain persistent in the matter and to show its support in deed.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz reply to an intercession by the St. Gallen citizen Emanuel Weber, called Hilers, concerning the heirs of the deceased Konstanz citizen Bernhard Meier. They have informed the heirs of the content of the intercession and heard Weber. Since the heirs would have submitted a written counter-report, which is of considerable significance, they would have urged the parties to a friendly settlement and send the St. Gallen Council a copy of the counter-report.
en.sender: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Georg Graf zu Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen und Veringen, Herr zu Haigerloch und Wehrstein, Erbkämmerer des Heiligen Römischen Reichs, Rat Seiner Kaiserlichen Majestät und Präsident des Reichshofrats, answers the letter of the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen dated 22 October 1612. He confirms that he has received the petition of the citizens of St. Gallen Christoph Tannen, Georg Schöppler and co-relatives. He declares himself willing to ensure a swift resolution of the matter upon his return to the imperial court. In the meantime, he has issued the citizens a written patent that sets out their situation vis-à-vis the creditors and refers to the still pending imperial decision against the Jews in Pehem.
en.sender: Johann Georg Graf zu Hohenzollern-Sigmaringen und Veringen, Herr zu Haigerloch und Wehrstein, Erbkämmerer des Heiligen Römischen Reichs, Rat Seiner Kaiserlichen Majestät und Präsident des Reichshofrats
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Tirol government communicates that the plague has broken out in St. Gallen. It orders strict border controls, whereby persons and goods from infected areas may only enter after quarantine and with a certificate. Since many citizens of St. Gallen visit the Bozen market, it asks that they be prevented from doing so, as goods would otherwise be rejected.
en.sender: Prince Archduke Maximilian of Österreich, Vice-President, Regents and Councilors of the Land of Tirol
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the French ambassador, since the distribution of the shares has already taken place and other cantons have received their share, to name a date at which they could collect their portion.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Lords of Castiglione, royal Council and ambassador in the Confederation

en.regest: Innroden and Ußroden inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, due to the rising prices in the Empire, they had fixed the Reichstaler at 2 1/2 gulden. This was done with the opinion of the Prelate of St. Gallen. They had instructed their subjects not to increase other coin types, but to maintain their value, otherwise a fine would be threatened.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: The Austrian territorial lordships in Innsbruck confirm receipt of the letter of 16 December 1613 concerning the plague in St. Gallen. They report that the situation in St. Gallen is not entirely clean, and order that citizens of St. Gallen and their goods may pass through the territory only with valid certificates and an oath that they have not been in infected places.
en.sender: Vice-president, Regents and Councillors of the Austrian Lands
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich inform Inn- und Ausroden of the Land of Appenzell that they will follow the invitation to a Tagleistung in Baden by the seven cantons. They intend to participate in the assembly through their Council messenger and to act, to the best of their ability, for peace, quiet, and unity in the fatherland.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Inn- und Ausroden of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: The seven Catholic cantons request Zürich to participate in the general Confederate Diet on 16 February 1624 in Baden. They refer to the ongoing unrest and war preparations in the domestic and foreign spheres, which endanger the common peace. They ask Zürich to send an instructed delegation and to invite the other cantons to participate, in order to provide for the peace and security of the Confederation.
en.sender: Schultheiss, Landammann and Council of the seven Catholic cantons of the Confederation (Luzern, Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden ob- und nid dem Wald, Zug, Freiburg and Solothurn)
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of the city of St. Gallen ask Ammann Hans Engeler of Tägerwilen to intervene on behalf of their citizen Niklaus Zollikofer. The latter had demanded the repayment of a loaned sum plus interest from his deceased brother-in-law Jacob Engeler. Engeler had delayed the repayment and reduced the interest. Zollikofer fears that Engeler will not settle the claim and asks for support so that he receives his money.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the city of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Hans Engeler, Ammann of Tägerwilen

en.regest: Burgomaster, lesser and greater Council of the city of St. Gallen offer their services to the French ambassador von Castillon, as the King of Frankreich desires a departure and a number of troops of the Confederates. They ask that the accompanying Mitrat Jacob Rüttern and town clerk Melchior Guldin be received favorably, that they be given credit, and that they be dispatched again with as much willingness as possible.
en.sender: Burgomaster, lesser and greater Council of the city of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Herr von Castillon, secret councilor and ordinary ambassador of the King of Frankreich in the Confederation

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the town clerk and Council of Arbon to settle the dispute over outstanding old interest and profits of the boys' school. The school councils had turned to the town clerk of St. Gallen, who is tasked with achieving an amicable settlement. Should this fail, the St. Gallen side threatened legal steps and protested against the costs arising therefrom.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Town clerk and Council of Arbon

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Landammann and Council of Appenzell that the Zuger and Dickpfennige are being spent in the neighborhood at six batzen. They ask for Appenzell's opinion on whether these coins should also be set at this value in St. Gallen or whether a neighboring meeting should be held.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to an inquiry regarding an inherited neighbor. They report on the imprisoned Hans Weissenstein, who came from Melanch about twenty years ago, served in various wars, and was now found in St. Gallen. They ask to be informed whether he arrives in Appenzell, as he is to be questioned for blasphemy and other offenses.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request several neighboring cities for a written report on the current value and acceptance of certain coin types, in particular ducats, Philipps- and Reichstaler as well as Zürcher Dickpfennige. They wish to thereby better regulate the currency disorders in the region and establish equality with the neighbors.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz, Lindau, Überlingen, Rottweil, Memmingen, Kempten, Isny, Leutkirch, Ravensburg, Biberach, Ulm, Nürnberg and Augsburg

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Arbon ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform them whether the man imprisoned there, who resembles Christoph Weißhuot, who was arrested two years ago, knows him. They request an unburdened report on the name, appearance, and acquaintance of the prisoner with Weißhuot.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter of 7 April 1614, in which St. Gallen had asked for their opinion regarding the revaluation of various gold and silver coins. Lindau informs that the coins have for some time been issued and withdrawn at certain rates (e.g. ducats at 2 fl. 20 kr., gold gulden at 1 fl. 45 kr.). They will maintain this for the time being.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell reply to a letter from St. Gallen regarding the monetary situation and agree that the Dickhepfenninge are to be taken at six batzen, as in other Imperial cities. Furthermore, they ask St. Gallen not to obstruct their people from buying linen bales and not to pressure the merchants, as this would contradict the equality of neighbors.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Chur reply to a letter of 7 April and state that the heavy ducats at 35 batzen, the Philipsthaler at 23 batzen, the gulden at 19 batzen, the thick pfennigs or Zuger Örtlin at 6 batzen and the Reichstaler at 21 1/2 batzen are being issued.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Leutkirch answer an inquiry from St. Gallen regarding the current rates of the most important gold and silver coins. They report that the rates in Leutkirch have risen, for example ducats to 35 batzen and Reichstaler to 86 kreuzer, and that they must adjust themselves in this matter to the prices of their neighboring cities.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they had hitherto received and paid out ducats at 2 gulden 16 kreuzer, gold gulden at 1 gulden 45 kreuzer, Philippstaler at 1 gulden 32 kreuzer, Reichstaler at 1 gulden 24 kreuzer, gulden at 1 gulden 16 kreuzer, and Zuger Dicken at 24 kreuzer. Since in Nürnberg and Augsburg ducats now amount to 2 gulden 20 kreuzer and Reichstaler to 1 gulden 26 kreuzer, these sorts would no longer be seen so frequently in Kempten, and the silver and other Kronen had completely disappeared.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen reply to the letter of the St. Gallen of 7 April 1612, in which they had requested information about the exchange rates of the most important coin types. Memmingen states that they had so far oriented themselves to the rates of Augsburg and Nürnberg when valuing the coins. They name the current values for ducats, gold gulden, Spanish Philip thaler, silver crowns, King thaler, Reichstaler and Zug thick pennies.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to Schaffhausen on the matter of the St. Gallen citizen Konrad Stüdlin. They had presented the matter to the son and his brother Thomas Zwick. Both had declared that they had already earnestly admonished the son in October to present himself, and had also instructed their merchants at the market in Lyon to search for him. Since the merchants have not yet returned, they can report nothing yet. Should they learn that the son has entered into a marital obligation, they would not proceed against it, but let the matter take its course.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter of the 24th of the month, in which the Abbey of St. Gallen complains about the sale of Kegelwetter to citizens of St. Gallen. The city states that it initially knew nothing of the transaction, and declares that the parties involved had been punished with fines. The city reaffirms its friendly disposition.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Abbey of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen, in which the latter had asked about the value of the most important coin denominations in Ulm. Ulm reports that the coins are constantly rising in value and that this cannot be prevented. They attach a list giving the rate of ducats, gold gulden, silver crowns, thaler and pfennigs in kreuzer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and members of the High Court Churwies ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a voluntary donation for the construction of their own church in Mästrilserberg. The evangelical neighbors there could not bear the costs alone. They had already begun the construction but needed further support so as not to have to abandon the work.
en.sender: Landammann and members of the High Court Churwies
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg answer an inquiry from St. Gallen regarding the rate of coins such as ducats, Reichsthaler, and Sechspatzner. They refer to the agreed-upon rates of the three neighboring circles and ask St. Gallen to regulate or abolish the inflated rates of low-fine coins in their cities, in order to avoid trade disadvantages and imbalances.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Biberach reply to a letter of the 41st of the month, in which the rates of the most important coin types were asked for. They regret that the coinage order of the Empire is not observed, and name the current rates: ducats at 3 gulden 20 kreuzer, Philippstaler at 1 gulden 34 kreuzer, Reichstaler at 1 gulden 26 kreuzer and gulden at 1 gulden 12 kreuzer. They report that these coins are hardly in circulation and that instead three-pfennig pieces and small change are used.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have listed the gold and silver coin types in circulation there as well as their prices. They ask to be informed of any future changes to the coin types or rates in St. Gallen, and express their willingness to continue the neighboring correspondence.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Überlingen answer an inquiry from the Council of St. Gallen regarding the rising prices of coins. They state that in their grain house, ducats are taken and paid out at 35 batzen, Philippstaler at 23, Reichstaler at 21½, gulden at 19 batzen, German pfennigs at 6, French pfennigs with cross at 7, and Schreckhenberger at 3 batzen. They find this burdensome and would gladly align with the neighboring cities.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Überlingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann together with the church and Vatz of Zizers thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a donation of 321 gulden for the church building in Meienfeld. They assure that the money is used exclusively for the construction, and ask for God's blessing.
en.sender: Landammann together with the church and Vatz of Zizers
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Pflegere, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg reply to the letter of 7 April and send the report of their Deputies on the coinage regarding the current value of the most important coin types. These name the Ducat at 140 Kreuzer, the Königsthaler at 93, the Reichstaler at 84 and the Gulden at 75 Kreuzer. The Zuger Dickpfennige or Sechsbatzner are given at 24 Kreuzer. Since a meeting of the three united Circles to regulate the coinage is approaching, the outcome of these negotiations is awaited.
en.sender: Pflegere, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank for the letter of 23 April regarding the value of the coin types and the attached coin list. They confirm that they have ceased their coin minting until they learn of the decision of the upcoming Imperial Diet in Nürnberg. They ask that the decision of the Imperial Diet be sent without delay after its conclusion, so that they can coordinate with their neighboring superior authorities. They inform that they have also communicated the letter to the city of Zürich.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Council of Nürnberg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the information regarding the coinage. They request a copy of the specimens transmitted from Nürnberg for the coinage assessment and valuation, as these were not attached to the St. Gallen letter. They wish to be able to deal with the matter more thoroughly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send them in writing the recently issued grain and market ordinance as well as the orders to the grain merchants. They wish to follow the example of St. Gallen in regulating grain prices and trade.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Radolfzell transmit to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the statements of four citizens of Radolfzell. These testify that the St. Gallen merchant Scherer, in the winter of 1613/14, paid the usual carriage fee of six batzen and six denarii toll per sack for the transport of grain sacks across the frozen lake to Konstanz or Rottweil. This serves as evidence in the legal dispute between Ulrich Gschwendreuter and Scherer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the transmission of copies of the coinage edicts from Nürnberg. They send the printed edicts back and express the wish for a better and more durable order in such matters. Since the next Baden annual account may deal with this, they advise St. Gallen, if it is concerned with the renewal of the regalia, to send an embassy to the next Baden assembly to obtain counsel and information there.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jakob Frey, Landvogt in Thurgau, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist his subject and Fehner of Wegenhausen in asserting his inheritance right from the estate of his deceased aunt Elisabeth Büchelerin. He requests that, in recognition of his intercession, the Fehner and his co-heirs be given what is due to them according to law and equity, and that they be left in their right.
en.sender: Jakob Frey, Knight, Statthalter and Council member of Zug, Landvogt in upper and lower Thurgau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ludwig Heilig, bailiff of Bürglen, informs Josias Kessler, town clerk of St. Gallen, that he has received his letter from the blacksmith in Schwieberg. He will report to the gentlemen about it as soon as the court convenes. Furthermore, he transmits 11 thaler, which he has paid for the inheritance of the deceased Andreas Zilligen.
en.recipient: Josias Kessler, town clerk of St. Gallen

en.regest: Gabriel Zollikofer, citizen of St. Gallen, asks the Council of the Imperial City of Leutkirch for mediation in a dispute with his brothers Jeronimus and Bartholomäus Zollikofer over the settlement of common benefice properties. He requests Leutkirch to persuade the Council of St. Gallen to set a court day to clarify the matter.
en.recipient: Council of the Imperial City of Leutkirch

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Leutkirch request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to set a final court day in the dispute between Gabriel Zollikofer and his brothers Hieronimus and Bartholomäus Zollikofer over the Zollikofer alms and donation money. They ask that the parties be summoned to it and that Hieronimus Zollikofer be ordered to inquire in writing with Bartholomäus if the latter cannot appear, so that the matter may be heard without hindrance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The town clerk and Council of Feldkirch inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the appointment of a general court day for the joint creditors of their citizen Martin Schauris and his wife Katharina Konzetin. They ask the authorities of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish the edict at the usual places, so that no one is disadvantaged by ignorance.
en.sender: The town clerk and Council of Feldkirch
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to readmit the glazier Caspar Kutter, who is staying in Appenzell, into favor. Kutter has behaved honestly in Appenzell, which the community of Spycher confirms. Appenzell asks for forgiveness for Kutter's earlier mistake.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Domprobst, Dekan and Chapter of Chur inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the Chur six-batzen coins in the city of Chur have been devalued down to 21 kreuzer, although in assay and weight they corresponded to the other Confederate coins. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to let the Chur coin remain valid and unrestricted, otherwise they would complain to other cantons.
en.sender: Domprobst, Dekan and Chapter of Chur
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform the Ußeren Roden that they have discussed the matter of the passes and crossings of the Abbot of St. Gallen for the Madruzische Kriegsvolk in the annual accounts in Baden. They propose to send a message to Glarus to obtain its consent to a joint declaration, and ask for the opinion of the Ußeren Roden.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: The Ußeren Roden

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter from St. Gallen regarding an intended military expedition. They indicate that they know nothing of the mentioned military recruitment, except what the newspapers report. They have heard that Count von Emps has enlisted captains, but neither patents nor money have arrived. Soldiers have not arrived in Lindau. They promise to inform St. Gallen confidentially if they learn of anything of a warlike Wesen in the region.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ulrich Tschudi, Landvogt of the lower and upper Rhine Valley, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan of 200 gulden for one year, as the costs for the assumption of office of a Landvogt are high and the revenues are delayed until autumn. He offers to repay the money with interest and to bind himself in writing. The deposit is to take place with the former Landvogt of Zug.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Lindau for the information regarding the passage of the Madruser army under Captain Jacob Reichen. They report that they have jointly with the Äusseren Roden intervened with the Abbot of St. Gallen to have the troop movement conducted away from their borders. The Abbot has promised to enable the passage in an orderly manner and without damage. The permission is expected shortly.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that approximately 200 soldiers of Colonel von Madruzzo are to come into their Upper Reich. Since the pass for the Milanese territory is not yet open, they have instructed Captain Raitner to hold the soldiers back with borrowed money and to urge them to be patient. They ask to be informed of what St. Gallen hears in this matter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Wädenswil ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admit the citizen there, Caspar Spüler, who had lived in their land for over twenty years and behaved exemplarily, into their favor and grace. They confirm his good behavior and ask for support for his intention to settle in St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Glarus ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant a further deadline in the dispute over the estate of the deceased wife of the Glarus countryman Fridlin Weiss. The Glarus creditors had not assembled on the agreed day. Glarus asks that the matter be postponed until the inheritance is clarified, and furthermore recommends that, because of the growing burdens, a new statute be issued.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the Ammann and Council of Rheineck to assist their citizen Hans Melchior Schüble, goldsmith, in a debt claim matter. Schüble says that he delivered gold and silver work to the Rheineck subject Hans Jürg Löwen, worth 31 florins and a few kreuzer, which the latter has not paid despite multiple reminders. The Rheineck authority is to instruct Löwen to settle the claim.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Ammann and Council of Rheineck

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank for the letter of intercession in favor of the citizen of Schaffhausen Ulrich Merlin. They have instructed their citizens Sebastian and Thomas Zwickher to look into the matter. Since Thomas Zwickher is staying in Schaffhausen, he will report the state of affairs personally, as the young Merlin cannot present himself at the moment.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell report that their countryman Hermann Tobler, in St. Gallen, was insulted and beaten by the citizen of St. Gallen Jacob Wetter while buying grain. Tobler therefore wishes to proceed legally against Wetter. The Appenzellers ask the authorities of St. Gallen to treat Tobler favorably and to ensure that Wetter withdraws the insults or bears the costs.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Glarus ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to refer the widow of the deceased painter Fridli Taeli, who has retained six carts of heartwood in St. Gallen, to a specific date. They are to ask the St. Gallen authorities to set a date for the widow to appear and settle the matter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen confirm the receipt of a letter of 4 October regarding the widow Fridlin Aeblin. They would have wanted to set a date for the parties in St. Gallen, but must postpone this due to urgent business. They promise to determine a new date and to inform Glarus in writing in good time.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Land of Glarus

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Leutkirch ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene in the dispute of their citizen Gabriel Zollikofer with the St. Gallen citizens Jeronimus and Bartholomäus Zollikofer over the money of the Zollikofer poor. They request an amicable settlement or, if this fails, a quick legal decision in favor of the Leutkirch citizen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Schwyz report that their countrymen had bought a horse from the St. Gallen master Jacob Vogt, which proved to be subject to a belly ailment. They had annulled the purchase and sent the horse back, which Vogt had refused. They ask St. Gallen to instruct Vogt to accept the horse and refund the purchase price along with costs, otherwise Schwyz will proceed legally.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to the Council of Glarus about the complaint of Jos Pfendler, Jacob Tschudi, Rudolf Wichser and Esaias Kubli against the citizen of St. Gallen Jacob Rietman, called Vogt, concerning a purchased horse. Rietman has declared that he had warranted the horse as healthy for only four weeks. Since the deadline has expired without the animal being returned, he cannot be further compelled. The matter was referred to the St. Gallen city court, where the Glarners are to be given impartial justice.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Vogt and Council of Glarus

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Glarus ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to recognize and protect the widow of the deceased Dammes Lederer, a woman of Glarus, as an heir according to the St. Gallen city law. The St. Gallen town clerk had denied her the right of inheritance on the argument that women could not inherit under the city law. Glarus appeals to the federal articles, according to which inheritance cases are to be judged according to the law of the place of residence of the deceased.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Glarus about the inheritance of the deceased Samuel Zaiderers. The widow Fridli Aeblis and the St. Gallen town clerk Guldi are disputing the inheritance. Since both sides refer to the respective territorial law, the St. Gallen authorities ask Glarus for a certified copy of the Glarus law, in order to clarify whether the maternal grandmother is preferred over the paternal relatives. They set 16 January 1615 as the deadline for the submission.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Glarus

en.regest: The Schultheiss, Council and citizens of the city of Bern inform the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen about the situation of the Confederates in Frankreich. They complain about violations of the peace treaty, the non-payment of promised amounts, and the convocation of the French Estates on the occasion of the King's coming of age. Since Zürich has not answered their inquiry regarding a common Diet, they declare that they will take the necessary measures to promote the common concerns themselves, and ask St. Gallen to approve this.
en.sender: The Schultheiss, Council and citizens of the city of Bern
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich invite Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to a Diet of the Confederation in Baden. This takes place on Tuesday, the 17th or 27th of January, in the evening. The occasion is the war situations on the borders of the Confederation and France, the question of the Payments of the Confederates, and the violation of the Perpetual Peace. The St. Gallen are to appear through their Ratsbotschaft with full power and to deliberate.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Glarus that the court day scheduled for the Thursday after Epiphany regarding the inheritance dispute between the widow Fridlin Eblin and the town clerk is postponed to 26 January 1615. As the reason they cite other urgent business and the Confederate assembly in Baden. They ask Glarus to inform the Landsfrau of the postponement.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Glarus

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Leutkirch ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to name a date for the final clarification of the Zollikofer charitable foundation. The citizens of St. Gallen Hieronimus and Bartholomäus Zollikofer refuse to hand over the share of approximately 13'000 florins falling to Gabriel Zollikofer. Leutkirch threatens further costs, which would have to be borne from the foundation funds, if the Zollikofer do not pay or provide sufficient security.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Council envoys of the Confederates at the Diet at Baden to take up the matter of the citizens of St. Gallen Thüringer, Schindler and Werrer, who have gotten into difficulties in Piemont. They request that the delegated Council messengers Joachim Rüetlinger and Melchior Guldin as well as those affected be heard and that means be found to replace the damage, since the innocence of the citizens is evident.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Council envoys of the thirteen cantons and the Puntens at the Diet at Baden

en.regest: The Landvogt and Council of Glarus ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support Maria Madlin, the widow of the deceased Caspar Iblin. She is the closest blood relative of the Glarus town clerk Melchior Guldin and his siblings. Madlin expects to be admitted as the next heir according to the St. Gallen city and inheritance law. Glarus asks for a friendly recommendation to the St. Gallen authorities.
en.sender: The Landvogt and Council of Glarus
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their fellow citizens Wilhelm and Andreas im Hoff in the collection of a debt. They refer to an attached supplication and request that the necessary support and execution against the debtor be granted to the authorized attorney Caspar Koch or his deputy.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report that they have detained and interrogated Daniel Streng, who comes from Burgau, for a theft. He confesses that, years ago, at the fair in Altstätten, he stole a Kettlin containing knives, Pfriemen, and Engellseid from a St. Gallen cutler. Lindau asks St. Gallen to inquire among their cutlers whether anyone has lost the goods, and for a report on the results.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Confederates ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to consider their fellow citizens, the Schobbinger, Schindler and Schürer, who have traded in Piemont, with favor and to give them security from their creditors until their trade is settled. They promise to support St. Gallen in similar cases.
en.sender: Cities and Lands of the Dreizehn and the allied cantons
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Leutkirch point out that they had received no answer regarding their voluntary cession of the share in the Zollikofer Almosen to St. Gallen. Their citizen Gabriel Zollikofer had been summoned to court on 13 February. As this deadline was too short, they had ordered him not to proceed any further. They warn that they would take action against any detrimental measures.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen send to Heinrich Elmer, Landvogt in Thurgau, the statements of witnesses whom they have examined and sworn upon his request. The statements concern points that were disclosed to the witnesses and are intended to serve as information.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Heinrich Elmer, Landvogt in upper and lower Thurgau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to two letters from the Council of Lützel dated 22 January and 9 February 1615 concerning the claim of the Lützel citizen Gabriel Zolicofer against Bartholomäus and Hieronymus Zolicofer for an alms. They extend the deadline by eight days and summon Gabriel Zolicofer to the town hall on 27 February 1615 at 8 o'clock in the morning. Should this deadline be too short, a further date is set for 11 July 1615. They ask for an amicable settlement and promise impartial adjudication.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lützel

en.regest: De Castille confirms the receipt of the letters of the St. Gallen envoys to the King of Frankreich, in which the citizens of St. Gallen are recommended, who were badly treated by the Duke of Savoyen. He promises to continue his affection for the St. Gallen people and to forward the letters with his own, as favorable as possible, letters to the King.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Landammann and Council of Ausserrhoden about the impending march of 2000 Landsknechten. They ask that on the next Tuesday, Council members be sent to St. Gallen to consult together with the abbot on how to extricate themselves from this complaint.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Ausserrhoden

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Leutkirch reply to an inquiry from St. Gallen concerning a claim by their citizen Gabriel Zollikofer against the brothers Hieronimus and Bartholomäus Zollikofer. They complain about the delay and costs that Gabriel had incurred through the brothers, and reject their refusal to pay. They declare themselves willing to participate in an amicable settlement, and dispatch Gabriel Zollikofer as well as the town clerk Matthäus Schwarzen to examine the books and create a basis for a compromise.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that in a few days five Fähnleiner of warlike troops recruited in Österreich and Tirol will pass through and are to march into Italien. They report that a Colonel named de Schohobokh has received the pass into the Confederation. They ask for confidential information about the nature of the matter and the opening of the pass.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to an inquiry by Count Karl Ludwig von Sulz regarding the coin types they accept as imperial currency in their Seckelamt. They list the current rates for Hungarian ducats, Ziggini, Philippstaler, silver crowns, Reichstaler, and gold thaler in batzen. Furthermore, they explain that they make no distinction between the general payment types in the Seckelamt, but accept every type at the usual market value.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Karl Ludwig, Count of Sulz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform the French ambassador that they have ordered their fellow councilor Jacob Studern to collect the portion of the Abbenzell distribution due to the city together with the Abbenzell residents. This is done on the basis of a previous statement by the ambassador to the town clerk. The city reaffirms its loyalty to the King of Frankreich.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Petrus von Castille, French ambassador

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Wil report that the Kessler Wernhard Suter from Liegnenberg complained that new thaler had been withheld from him in St. Gallen by Jörg Effinger and his wife. Wil had admonished the Effingers to return the thaler, which they had promised to do. Wil asks St. Gallen to let the thaler be returned to the Kessler, in order to maintain good neighborly relations and avoid further disputes.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Obervogt Bernhard Bodmer of Arbon to enable an amicable settlement of the dispute between their schoolmasters and the Arbon Council as well as Martin Strauß at the castle on 10 or 20 May. Should this fail, they ask him to continue the legal proceedings already initiated against the Arbon Council and to inform the St. Gallen citizens of the judge as well as the time and place of the hearing.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Bernhard Bodmer, Obervogt of Arbon

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen that the seven cantons have approved an embassy to Frankreich regarding the privileges of merchants and complaints about customs duties. They ask St. Gallen to inquire of the merchants whether they wish to support this embassy, and for feedback.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The seven Catholic cantons declare to Zürich that they withdraw their consent to the embassy to Frankreich, because they were bypassed in the selection of the envoys. They demand that envoys be appointed from their cantons in equal number, otherwise they are not to be mentioned in the powers of attorney. They emphasize that this serves the rescue of their reputation and the preservation of unity.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: The administrator of the captaincy, the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have their citizen Laurentz Gsell appear before them on 23 May. Gsell is to hear the complaints of his business partners Johann Ludwig de Gall, Constantin Schanolts and Andreas Eliatz against the widow of Jacob Strauben concerning a partnership debt and to answer for himself, as he had previously appealed to the St. Gallen authority.
en.sender: The administrator of the captaincy, the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Stadtpfand, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz confirm the receipt of a letter from St. Gallen to their citizen Konrad Seiner. They have examined the matter and taken steps to move the step-siblings and brothers-in-law who are at enmity with him towards an amicable settlement. They hope that this will bring peace, and continue to offer neighborly assistance.
en.sender: Stadtpfand, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of a letter from the Solothurn messenger. They ask that the merchants trading in Frankreich be informed so that these may record their complaints and hand them over to the ambassador. They warn against refusing the handover, as this could hinder the interests of the merchants in the future.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Solothurn report that they have received an answer from the King regarding the complaints about the merchants operating in Frankreich. They assure of the King's good disposition to grant justice to the complainants, and request a memorial with the most important points of complaint in order to obtain a speedy resolution.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen remind Obervogt Bernhard Bodmer of the answer promised by his Seckelmeister Truss to their complaint against the Stadtammann and Council of Arbon concerning a fief. Since no answer has been received, they ask Bodmer to set the court day as soon as possible, to inform them of the time and place, and to formally notify the opposing party.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Bernhard Bodmer, Hauptmann, bishop's Constance Council and Obervogt of Arbon

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Wil request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Salome Köppin, wife of Jacob Schneider. She says that she lent money to her sister-in-law Ursel Bülin and gave her yarn, which the latter sold without performing the promised work. Since Köppin is poor and has children to support, the men of Wil request a favorable letter to the men of St. Gallen so that Köppin may get her money back.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report that fellow citizens Georg Zollikofer and brothers as well as Tobias Schöbinger, in the year 1608, when visiting the Easter Fair in Regensburg, wanted to send monies that they had received from debtors to Regensburg and further to St. Gallen. In the imperial German customs house at Enghards, the money was seized as contraband and brought to Wien. The St. Gallen ask Nürnberg and Ulm to question their relatives whether they may freely carry their earnings out of the country, whether they are aware of any prohibitions, and whether they feel secure in their freedom. Furthermore, they request assistance in the restitution of the money and the preservation of trade freedom.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Cities of Nürnberg and Ulm

en.regest: The administrator of the captaincy, the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Laurentz Stahell to present himself before them on 18 July. Stahell had refused to appear in the matter of the Pellische Gesellschaft and had justified his supplication with irrelevant motives. The people of Konstanz ask that Stahell be moved to fulfill his duties as a co-helper in the Steubisch debt matter.
en.sender: The administrator of the captaincy, the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Giovanni Battista Gabaleone informs the Schultheiss and Council of Luzern that he has instructed the merchants of St. Gallen in Casale Monferrato to name the names for the desired passes. He says that he will issue these separately for each family. He thanks them for the recommendation of the merchants and the dispatch of two envoys, but considers this unnecessary, as the Duchess of Savoyen is well-disposed. He promises to support the envoys, but announces that he has less time for the moment because of the dissolution of the armaments and his own duties.
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Luzern

en.regest: Joan. Baptista Gabaleone reports to the Schultheiss and Council of Luzern on his negotiations with the merchants of St. Gallen in Piemont. They ask for individual letters of safe-conduct for their envoys, which he is willing to grant. He confirms the receipt of their letter of 24 June and declares himself ready to support the envoys of St. Gallen and Zürich, although he is currently restricted because of the discharge of the troops and other tasks.
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Luzern

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have been informed by the city of Luzern of its answer to Herr Gabelleon. This concerns the merchants of St. Gallen and their trade with the Frankish County Savoyen. Zürich forwards to the Confederates the letter of Luzern along with a copy of Gabelleon's answer, so that St. Gallen may inform its merchants accordingly and they may behave accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Kämmerer, Burgomaster and Council of Wangen inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the citizen of St. Gallen Lorenz Stachel did not appear at the court day in Wangen due to a significant impediment. They set a new final court day for Saturday, the 22. August, and ask the St. Gallen authorities to detain Stachel so that he appears in person or is represented by proxy.
en.sender: Kämmerer, Burgomaster and Council of Wangen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Luzern inform the Burgomaster and Council of Zürich that, at the request of the merchants of St. Gallen, they had sent a letter to the Knight Gabaleon regarding his business in Savoyen. They send a copy of the received reply, from which it emerges that the matter will take a good turn. They ask Zürich to guide and instruct the merchants accordingly, and promise the support of the Confederates.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to the request for an opinion on the coinage rate of Baden. They communicate that the Landtschreiber Zidler proposes a meeting of the four Oberkeiten (Appenzell, Thurgau, St. Gallen, Zürich) to discuss the coinage rate. The meeting is set for 8 August 1615 at St. Gallen Castle. They ask Appenzell to attend the meeting through Ratsbotschaften.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to communicate to them in writing their opinion on a new Baden coinage ordinance and valuation. They themselves would not have wanted to undertake anything without the knowledge of the neighboring authorities and wished that no inequality regarding the coinage arise in the neighborhood.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Councils of the city of Augsburg ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Hans Weichser, linen weaver, to bring in the inheritance of his brother Alexander Weichser, who died in St. Gallen. They enclose a supplication in which Weichser proves his kinship by oath witnesses and appoints Jacob Widenman as his proxy. Augsburg asks that Widenman be treated courteously and that he be helped in the inheritance negotiation.
en.sender: Councils of the city of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell reply to the inquiry of St. Gallen regarding the Baden coinage ordinance. They explain that they could not separate themselves from the majority of the Confederates, as the ordinance had already been accepted by them and transmitted to Zürich. They ask that their absence from the meeting be excused in a neighborly manner.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform the Obervogt of Arbon that the Hospital Masters revoke the settlement agreed upon three months ago with Martin Strauß, as he has given no answer. They ask the bailiff to take back the copy of the settlement handed over to Strauß and to show the Hospital Masters a judge, so that they can obtain their rights against the town clerk and Council of Arbon regarding outstanding interest on the Mahrnmühle.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Bernhard Belman, Bishop's Councilor and Obervogt of Arbon

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to Appenzell on the negotiations of the recent meeting in the parish of St. Gallen regarding the coinage matter. They enclose copies of the resolutions adopted by the Lords' Envoys, the Prelate, and themselves. They ask Appenzell to inform them in writing whether these resolutions are also acceptable to them, so that the letter to Zürich indicated in the closing act can be handed over.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen send Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz a copy of the renewed coinage edict, which is to be published on 27 August or 6 September. This is done with regard to an earlier request by the people of Konstanz to participate in the coinage regulations without being burdened.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the transmission of the coinage ordinance and its coordination with the neighboring Oberbailiffs. They state that they agree with the content, but would have wished that the thick coins of Chur and Haldenstein had also been included. They agree that the Confederates are to be signed by the city of Zürich, and ask that they may also sign. They promise to hold their citizens to the observance of the ordinance, and ask for reciprocity.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz confirm the receipt of the new coinage ordinance of St. Gallen. They thank them for the neighborly good will and in turn offer their help in neighborly matters.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur report that the widow Sabina Freypuellerin, left behind by her deceased husband Christian Freypolt, has died of a fatal illness. She asks St. Gallen to transfer the boy she has left behind to his home city, so that he may be raised in honor by his relatives. Winterthur asks for the child's benevolent reception.
en.sender: The Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from Winterthur concerning the deceased Christian Huijpolts. They reject the request to take in his orphaned son, as the latter is no longer a citizen of St. Gallen. Huijpolts citizenship had been forfeited before the boy's birth. However, they had let two gulden be given to the child as a Zehrpfennig.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur

en.regest: The Stadtvogt and Council of Meilenfeld ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intercede for the citizen Hans Jakob Töber and his sister Anna. They say that they have been excluded from the inheritance of the deceased father Balthasar Töber by their siblings. The city of Meilenfeld requests the St. Gallen authorities to persuade the siblings to forgive and to hand over the maternal and paternal inheritance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Glarus ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their Confederate Ulrich Vogt to take back a sick horse that Peter Wirtz, the bailiff of Glarus, had bought from him, or to give an answer. If an amicable settlement is not possible, St. Gallen is to provide for a just court, so that Wirtz may return to his duties without costs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to question the servant of the St. Gallen citizen Christoph Altter, who was present during the wine bottling. Altter is said to have sold new wine mixed with old vinegar wine to the Schaffhausen citizen Jakob Krachen. Krachen denies this. Schaffhausen wants to clarify the truth about the alleged fraud.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The town clerk and Council of Rorschach ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to order their former town clerk Andreas Heer to collect the 200 gulden that his daughter has inherited from her sister Anna Maria, in the name of his son, from the guardians. Heer has come into legal dispute with the guardians.
en.sender: Town clerk and Council of Rorschach
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Meister and Council of the city of Straßburg inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have forwarded the complaint raised by the St. Gallen citizens Peter Felschen and his brothers against the widow Magdalena Hillerin and her representatives to the latter for accountability. They send the judicial declaration of the defendants and ask for good neighborhood.
en.sender: Georg Jacob Wormbser, Meister and Council of the city of Straßburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Luzern thank for the support of their citizens in Savoyen and promise to continue this. They explain that they had released their town clerk for a short time only exceptionally due to urgent business. Since the agreed deadline has expired, they ask for his prompt return, otherwise they could not do without him any longer.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Luzern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Leonhard Heuri, Stadtammann, and the judges and assessors of the city court of Kempten ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publish an open edict regarding the creditors of the St. Gallen woman Margaretha Lutzenbergerin. Since she is also indebted to citizens of St. Gallen, this should be done so that equity is preserved and no one can plead ignorance.
en.sender: Leonhard Heuri, Stadtammann, and the judges and assessors of the city court of Kempten
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Court of Thal ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant the young man Hans Kun the lapsed abbey fief at Buchbach. Kun has farmed the fief until now, but is young and has many children. The request is based on the fact that Kun wants to continue farming and developing the fief, which would benefit the abbey and the citizenry.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landvogt Heinrich Elmer informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Caspar Meyer has presented to him four votes of the cantons Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden and Zug as well as a judgment of 17 December 1615 between Johannes Schyschermann and Lorenz Schellen. Meyer asks to move Schyschermann to settle the accounts and to refrain from pursuing Schellen until the claims are liquidated. Elmer declares that he must enforce the judgments of the ruling cantons, but hopes that St. Gallen will resolve the matter wisely.
en.sender: Heinrich Elmer, Landvogt in the upper and lower Thurgau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landvogt Ulrich Tschudi in the Reintal to compel the vassal Hans Conrad Sizen to vacate the fief of Leonhard Zollikofer von Altenklingen immediately and without further legal proceedings. Sizen had taken leave himself and now nevertheless wishes to remain and refuses to do so. The St. Gallen authorities ask for support to prevent an undesirable innovation, whereby lords of a fief would have to file a legal claim first after leave had been taken by themselves.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Ulrich Tschudi, Landvogt in the Reintal

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Hans Rösslange, who is from St. Gallen and was active in Zürich as a cloth maker, stood before the marriage court because of a marriage promise to two women. Since he had recently left St. Gallen, the Zürich authorities ask for written information about the circumstances of his departure and possible marital entanglements in St. Gallen, in order to be able to continue the proceedings against Rösslange, who is in custody in Zürich.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from Landvogt Heinrich Elmer concerning Steffen Majer. They instruct their town clerk Melchior Goldin to clarify the matter. They request Elmer to ensure that Majer remains quiet or, if he has claims against the citizen of St. Gallen Johannes Scheürhemen, to assert them before the ordinary judge according to the custom of the Confederates.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Heinrich Elmer, Landvogt of the Landgrafschaft Thurgau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the appointment of a general court day for the creditors of the deceased citizen and coppersmith of Lindau, Jakob Weber. They ask that the edict be publicly posted and published in St. Gallen, so that interested parties residing there also receive notice of Webers' seized property and no one is deprived of their right.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to readmit Caspar Kutter, who is banished there. He says that he behaved honestly in Appenzell at the Speicher, but cannot live there with his craft. Appenzell confirms his good behavior in writing and asks for clemency, as Kutter will behave properly in the future.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Solothurn request Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen to send the heirs of the deceased Captain Hans Schwaller and his co-parties the judgment from a previous legal dispute against the citizens of St. Gallen Keller and Rodtmund, in which Jacob Keller had been excluded, under the chancery signature and, if possible, in the Latin language. The citizens of Solothurn needed the judgment for future claims.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Solothurn
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the French envoy Petrus de Castille to have their annual pension from the French Queen collected. They wish to have this done through their messengers dispatched to Baden, as the envoy will soon be proceeding to the Royal Court. They commend themselves to his grace and favor.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Petrus de Castille, French envoy

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Schultheiss and Council of Bern for the great help and friendship that the Confederates have shown to the citizens and merchants of St. Gallen in their dispute with the Duke of Savoyen. They report that the matter has been brought to a good end and the prisoners were released. They offer to repay this in the future.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Bern

en.regest: Statthalter, Ratsschultheiss and Council of the city of Luzern ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizen Hans Wägelin in the collection of a claim of around 600 gulden against the St. Gallen citizens Sebastian and Georg Scheren. Wägelin says that he lent the sum in good faith years ago and that an agreement has been set for 28 April. Luzern requests legal support so that Wägelin may be paid together with interest.
en.sender: Statthalter, Ratsschultheiss and Council of the city of Luzern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Landvogt Ulrich Tschudi for the friendly treatment of their fellow citizens Jacob Allgöwer and Josua Kessler. They send the requested receipt and ask that, if there is dissatisfaction, it be improved and sent back. Furthermore, they ask that the delegates Ulrich Ruchen and Joseph Wilden be allowed to take over the prisoners and be given good guidance. The expenses incurred have been given to the two.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Ulrich Tschudi, Landvogt in the Rheintal

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Peter Freudig, Landvogt of Aarberg, for information regarding the estate of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen, Mathias Moßburg of Brittnau, and his widow. They ask for written notification regarding the amount of the assets and the inheritance claims according to the local inheritance law. Furthermore, the heirs are to be instructed to suspend the process and the division until the claims of the heir of St. Gallen, Susanna Moßburgin, are taken into account.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Peter Freudig, Landvogt of Aarberg

en.regest: Reinhard Cysat der Jüngere, town clerk of Luzern, thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the words of thanks regarding his mediation activity with the Duke of Savoyen. He points out that the success is mainly attributable to the efforts of Hans Jörg Lützel. Furthermore, he asks for support for the joiner Hans Stähle, who has deposited his entire fortune with the Herren Schärer. Cysat requests that Stähle be protected in the settlement with the creditors so that he does not fall into poverty in old age.
en.sender: Reinhard Cysat der Jüngere, town clerk of Luzern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Peter Frütting, bailiff of Arbon, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for patience, as he, being the new office holder, has not yet any knowledge of the estate of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Mathias Moßburger. He promises to give justice to the widow Susana Moßburger and to initiate the process as soon as he has examined the documents.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to an inquiry from Karl Ludwig, Count zu Sulz, regarding the coin types in circulation in St. Gallen. They list the current rates for Hungarian ducats, Venetian zecchins, silver crowns, Philippstaler, Reichstaler, gold gulden, and gold gulden. They report that they are not aware of any higher rates for these types to date.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Karl Ludwig, Count zu Sulz

en.regest: Karl Ludwig Graf zu Sulz, Landgraf im Klettgau, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have a messenger confidentially inform him at what rate the city accepts and issues various coins such as Tugaten, Zeggis, Philipps- and Reichstaler, Silberkronen, gulden and Goldgulden.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ulrich Tschudi, Landvogt in the Nider- and Oberrheintal, asks Burgomaster Joachim Reutlinger of St. Gallen to request the St. Gallen citizen Ulrich Hochrüttner to go to Thal. There, a marriage promise had been concluded between his daughter and Hans Berlocher of Reineck. Tschudi hopes that a friendly settlement can be achieved through negotiations, otherwise other steps would have to be taken.
en.sender: Ulrich Tschudi, Landvogt in the Nider- and Oberrheintal
en.recipient: Joachim Reutlinger, Burgomaster of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Schultheiss and Council of Luzern that they had fully settled the claim of their citizen Hans Stähelin against the deceased Scherrer in cash. This was done at the request of the Luzerners, although other creditors of Scherrer received only a part of their claims immediately and granted the rest interest-free over seven years. St. Gallen hopes to have thereby satisfied Stähelin, and reaffirms the friendly relations of the Confederation.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Luzern

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Luzern thank for the answer regarding the sale of the inheritance of the deceased citizen of Luzern, Hans Täubelius, to citizens of St. Gallen. They ask that the inheritance be settled partly in cash and partly against a secure written instrument in St. Gallen or in the Land, so that the heir may retain his assets without damage.
en.sender: The Schultheiss and Council of Luzern
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The town clerk and judges of the city court of Lindau ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hear the witnesses Caspar Kuntz and Caspar Rötzen in a legal dispute between the heirs of the deceased Hans Hoer and the defendants Ulrich Rad and Amade Eggolt. They also request information from the St. Gallen council minutes regarding an oath that Kuntz is said to have sworn in 1609, and regarding his return to the city.
en.sender: The town clerk and judges of the city court of Lindau
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about rumors that two regiments of mercenaries of Count von Sulz are to march to Mailand via Lake Constance and the Gotthard. Since such troop movements had previously heavily burdened the city and district of Lindau, they ask to be informed whether the Confederation permits the troops to pass, in order to prepare in good time.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the city of Lindau to continue the neighborly relationship of trust and request that it inform them of what they have further learned in this matter. They commend themselves and Lindau to the protection of God.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Lindau

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the information regarding an impending march of Landsknechts to Italien. They confirm that rumors of such an intention on the part of Count Karl Ludwig von Sulz or his son were also circulating among them, but that no confirmed information was available. They ask St. Gallen to convey similar news to them, so that both cantons could jointly consult with the Confederates on the necessary precautions.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Appenzell reply to an inquiry from Lindau regarding an impending march of Landsknechte. They report that they had consulted Zürich and the Landvogt of Appenzell. The Landvogt had stated that the Madrid Regiment was to be reinforced in the Milanese territory and might march over the Gotthard. He had assured them that he would not touch the borders of Appenzell and would inform Lindau. Appenzell hopes that the march will not take place because of the peace negotiations between Österreich and Venedig.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about an imperial patent, according to which a regiment of German mercenaries is being recruited in Spanien under Colonel Count Carl Ludwig zu Sulz. The muster ground is Rorschach, St. Gallen and Chur, the inspection in the Milanese. They request confidential information on who the recruitment serves, how strong it is, and where the troops are to be led.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for forwarding the decision of the city of Zürich. Since nothing new has happened since then, they let the matter rest. They offer to promote everything that serves the welfare of the fatherland and the neighborhood, and promise to transmit news about the war matter confidentially.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that a Bavarian captain has been slain in Ravensburg and that servants have been recruited in the name of the Crown of Spanien. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to make corresponding arrangements in possible cases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about the request of the Spanish envoy for the passage of troops through the Confederation. They refer to the resolutions of the Diet of Baden and explain that they refuse the passage for security reasons. They ask St. Gallen to participate in the next Baden annual accounting in order to jointly act against such passages.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Lindau that they have learned from a letter from the city of Ravensburg that a Sulz commander has recruited soldiers there. The city of Ulm has informed them that the imperial patents explicitly state that the recruited soldiers are to be led via Rorschach and St. Gallen to Uri. The abbot, who is staying in Griesbach, knows nothing of these plans. St. Gallen shares this with Lindau as a neighbor.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform that they have already informed in a previous letter about the recruitment and the passage of foreign troops. They ask St. Gallen to inform the Appenzeller Confederates about the incidents in the Land Appenzell and to send them the corresponding letter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that a Swabian ensign arrived in Lindau the day before. He had requested the transfer but did not appear at the Council meeting and had moved on to Memmingen. Some servants had shown themselves in Lindau and wanted to cross to Rorschach, but had been detained.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Ulm thank Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen for the reply to their letter regarding the war application. They regret the criticism contained therein and offer to communicate trustfully in similar matters in the future. They ask St. Gallen to continue reporting news of war events to them.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Ulm
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to Burgomaster and Council of Ulm that the Sulzer Regiment and the soldiers who are to reinforce the Madruzer Regiment have been granted passage through Uri, Schwyz, and the land of the St. Gallen monastery. The march of 6000 men has already begun. They enclose a copy of a letter from Zürich.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Lindau about a Venetian Fendrich who was detained in St. Gallen with a patent. They refer to a letter from the previous day and its enclosures. Furthermore, they state that the Anpach has already taken several servants into service.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell Innerrhoden ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their fellow councillor and captain Kalchsuter in a legal dispute with Ulrich Rieders son. They request that Kalchsuter be treated amicably and that further harassment be refrained from, as he has lived peacefully. Furthermore, they ask that partial witnesses not be admitted.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of Appenzell Innerrhoden
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm thank St. Gallen for two letters of 6 and 13 June concerning the Sulzer recruitment, and ask for further communications. They report that the situation regarding the soldiers is still unclear. In Prag and Wien in Österreich, war recruitments are being carried out, but their goal and use are still unknown to them. Should written information arrive in the future, they will communicate it to St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Ammann and Court of Thal to protect and uphold the widow Margaretha Sandnerin in her inheritance right to one third of the estate of her deceased father.
