They refer to a previous decision and point out that such a judgment is final. They demand that the heiress be able to enforce her rights without resistance and with the necessary costs.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Ammann and Court of Thal

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Solothurn remind the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen of their earlier requests in favor of Captain Victor Byssen and the sons of the deceased Captain Hans Schwaller. They refer to the response of St. Gallen of 14 March regarding a document between the Solothurner Jacob Keller and the citizens of St. Gallen. They ask that the desired document now be sent without delay.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Solothurn
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Melchior Maag, Landvogt of the County of Kyburg, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the St. Gallen weaver Philipp Schowinger was detained in Altorf for blasphemy and disobedience. He asks the St. Gallen to inform him why Schowinger is wandering about in the land, whether he is mentally ill or who he actually is, so that he can continue the proceedings against him.
en.sender: Melchior Maag, Landvogt of the County of Kyburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten reply to a letter of 5 July, in which St. Gallen had requested an arrest at the Toana concerning a sum of money received in Piemont, regarding the Kempten citizen Magdalena Hoerin and her brother-in-law Daniel Stenglin. Kempten informs that they have communicated the matter to those concerned. They have agreed to provide a written statement. Kempten asks to await the reply.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Landvogt of Kyburg regarding the weaver Philipp Scheueringer detained there. They reject the claim that he is a citizen of St. Gallen, as they have no weaver of this name among their ranks. They refer to an earlier letter in which they had already rejected the details given by a carpenter named Hans Scheueringer as incorrect. They suspect that both persons are identical.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Melchior Maag, Landvogt of the County of Kyburg

en.regest: Magdalena Fehren, widow of the late Burgomaster Paulus Fehren, asks the Council of the city of Kempten to forward her apology and her offer to the Council of St. Gallen. She refuses consent to the Scherer-Accord, as it is unfair to creditors and insufficiently secured. She offers to remit a quarter or third of her claim if the remainder is paid in cash or with sufficient security within half a year. She asks Kempten to intervene with St. Gallen for her concerns.
en.recipient: Council of the city of Kempten

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about confidential warnings that war-troops, which are passing through the Confederation under the pretext of the pass to Italien, are to be kept together for other purposes. They ask for confidential information whether the troops have already crossed the Gotthard, how long the pass will remain open, and whether the imperial escort is being admitted.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Lindau for the information regarding the passage of Landsknechte. They state that the troops had already crossed the Gotthard. Whether the pass would remain open for another month or whether a return journey would be permitted is unknown to them. They ask Lindau to inform them of any information regarding this matter, and promise to report everything further to them without delay.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich answer an inquiry from St. Gallen regarding the passage of troops to Italien. They state that 6000 men had already passed through and were staying in Mailand. Whether the cantons would continue to open the pass is unclear. Zürich and the other Protestant cantons would write to the Confederates regarding the pass permits and passages. Furthermore, they report on the situation in Mailand, Savoyen and Venedig as well as on recruitments in Switzerland.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about rumors that Spanish war recruitment is taking place in Italien and around Lake Constance as well as in Straßburg. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to inform them confidentially if they receive credible news about such developments that could concern the Evangelical Confederates.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen send Burgomaster and Council of Lindau a copy of a reply from the city of Zürich as well as three further pieces of news from unknown sources. They share these with them to inform Lindau about the situation.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform the Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz about the measures permitted for the purchase and sale of linen goods in St. Gallen. When sending linen, the Leoner Stab and the Nuremberg ell are allowed, but no other foreign measures. The measuring instruments are not handed over to the merchants, but the goods must be measured by appointed officials. The measuring instruments are to be made available to the naturalized merchants and handed over upon request.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information on the local practice regarding the purchase and sale of linen. They ask whether foreign measures (Milanese, Leonese) are used alongside the town measures, who measures them, and whether the merchants themselves are allowed to apply foreign measures. In addition, they request the Milanese, Conic, and Venetian ells at their own expense.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the continued confidential correspondence. They state that there is currently nothing worthy of writing to report due to the war recruitments and the general silence in the highway. They ask for the continuation of the exchange and promise to henceforth report everything worthy of writing without concealment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Confederates of the 11th of the month, in which they reported on rumors regarding military recruitment and intentions against the evangelical estates in the fatherland. St. Gallen states that it knows nothing of such plans. The Landsknechte passing through the Confederation were not stopped but sent on and are already in Mailand. They are also unaware of any recruitment on Lake Constance or gatherings around Straßburg. They promise to report immediately upon receiving suspicious news and ask for reciprocity.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to provide for the widow Magdalena Liechtensteigerin. She says that she gave her deceased husband 100 gulden from her paternal and maternal inheritance for the acquisition of his estate. She asks for the reimbursement of this amount through the sale of the estate or through the granting of a credit of trust from her birth and freedom letters.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Bernhard Bodmer, Obervogt of Arbon, to act on behalf of the butcher Hans Tobler. Toblers Knecht Hans Scherr has impregnated his daughter Otilia, who has now given birth to a child. Since the mother cannot raise the child and the father is at war, Tobler asks for help to hand the child over to the father's parents or relatives. The St. Gallen authorities ask Bodmer to have this arranged by virtue of his office as Obervogt.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Bernhard Bodmer, Obervogt of Arbon

en.regest: The Landammann and Landrat of the Outer Rhoden of the Land of Appenzell reply to a complaint by the St. Gallen hospital almoners regarding the poor condition of the country road. They point out that the road in their land has never been in better condition and that the fault for the poor sections lies with St. Gallen and Altstätten. They offer to improve the road in their land if defects are found.
en.sender: Landammann and Landrat of the Outer Rhoden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Stadtmann and Council of Altstätten that the customary wine price for the current year could not be agreed upon. Since the estimates of the two parties differed, an honest man from the St. Gallen Council was appointed as arbitrator. He has set the wine price at seven gulden and seven batzen per Salm.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Stadtmann and Council of Altstätten

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Frankfurt request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to examine the supplication of the heirs of the deceased Noe du Fays and of the citizen of Frankfurt Johann de Famars. They ask for support in the collection of a debt claim against the citizens of St. Gallen Christoph Thanner, Georg Tobler, Burckhard and Jacob Spleiß. The claim is liquid and secured by mortgage. Frankfurt asks that the debtors be moved to pay together with interest and costs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The heirs of the deceased Noé du Fau and Joachim de Jamars ask E. E. and F. W. for a letter of recommendation to the Burgomaster and Council in St. Gallen. They are burdened with considerable debts by the citizens of St. Gallen Christoph Danner, Georg Kessler, Burkhard and Jakob Stähelin as well as co-partners, which these did not pay despite pledging and agreement on a deadline. The creditors demand the immediate payment of the capital with interest or the taking possession of the pledged goods by their proxy Matthäus Oettelin von Costnitz.
en.sender: Heirs of the deceased Noé du Fau and Joachim de Jamars
en.recipient: E. E. and F. W.

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information on whether the widow of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen, Hans Jakob Muralt, Barbara de Bononia, is provided for with her daughter Katharina, the widow of the deceased Anton Gysli of St. Gallen. The widow wishes to take her mother to St. Gallen and take care of her maintenance. Zürich wishes to know whether this can be done, so that the woman can be informed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Liechtenstein request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help the widow Elsa Bantlissen, daughter of the deceased citizen of Liechtenstein. She says that she married the citizen of St. Gallen Jakob Locher and spent from her inheritance for the joint household. After his death, nothing was repaid to her. Liechtenstein requests compensation from the estate of Locher so that the widow can provide for her livelihood.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Stadtschultheiss and Council of Feldkirch ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post the edict concerning the appointed general court day for the citizen of Feldkirch Hans Ulrich Gerber. Since citizens of St. Gallen are also creditors, this should ensure that no one is curtailed in their rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Sebastian Alther, Landvogt in Unter- und Oberrheintal, thanks Burgomaster Joachim Zölligkoffer of St. Gallen for the transmitted interrogations. He asks for permission that the executioner Hans comes to Rheineck on Saturday, the 2nd of January, to interrogate the prisoners.
en.sender: Sebastian Alther, Landvogt in Unter- und Oberrheintal
en.recipient: Joachim Zölligkoffer, Burgomaster of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landvogt Sebastian Alther informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the statements of the arrested thieves Balthasar Heider and Hans Hürte as well as their wives. He asks for permission to question the witness Master Hans, and announces that the court day is to take place on Tuesday, 7 January.
en.sender: Sebastian Alther, Landvogt in and out of Reineck
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Friedrich Graf zu Fürstenberg asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to recommend to the creditors of the St. Gallen merchants Georg Kessler and Christoph Sanner that they behave patiently until the execution of an imperial commission. The Jews in Mähren had delayed the merchants' claims for years, which had led to their debt burden. The Count promises to strive for St. Gallen in other matters.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of the city of Veltlin request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to transmit to them the files of a man arrested on Friday. The 33-year-old Jakob Wächter from the Markgräflerland, a hatter, had worked in St. Gallen for Balthasar Stauder and had stayed at the inn of Othmar Spieß. He had taught Adam Wecker the trade there. Veltlin requests the transmission of the complaint in order to clarify the truth.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the city of Veltlin
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Frankfurt request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene again with the citizens of St. Gallen Christoph Sommer, Marx Kessler and associates on behalf of the heirs of the deceased Noé du Fay as well as Johann de Famars. The creditors have declared their necessity and requested renewed intercession. Frankfurt requests that the debtors be instructed to pay, so that the citizens of Frankfurt receive their money.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Anna Fackhlerin, who comes from Issny, is detained in Lindau for theft. She claims to have served in St. Gallen and asks for information about her conduct and her reasons for leaving. Lindau asks for a reply via the dispatched messenger.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen declare to Barbara Klirin that they do not recognize her complaint against the citizen of St. Gallen Wolfgang Schobinger before the Consistory in Konstanz, as they have their own marriage court over their citizens. They protest against the proceedings there and summon Klirin peremptorily to three court days in April 1617 before their marriage court in the town hall. In case of absence, they threaten to treat her as a fugitive from justice and to release Schobinger from her claims.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Barbara Klirin

en.regest: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz answer an inquiry from the Council of St. Gallen regarding the St. Gallen woman Barbara Küoni. They explain that it is a marriage case that falls under the jurisdiction of the ecclesiastical court. Since the Bishop of Konstanz or his Vikar has already initiated proceedings, they cannot intervene. They ask that Küoni be allowed to return.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Emperor Matthias requests the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to postpone the executions pending against the St. Gallen merchants Christoph Danner, Georg Kessler and Consorts by their creditors until they have fully satisfied their claims against the Moravian Jews, against whom an imperial execution patent exists. He refers to the imperial resolutions and patents already issued.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report that, following an order from the Bishop of Konstanz, they had relied on the process against their citizen Barbara Schumpf being discontinued by Jörg Herren von Riggig. Since this has not happened and the process is to be continued, although they dispute the jurisdiction of the ecclesiastical court, they instruct their town clerk to communicate their decision to the Bishop's Official.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Johann Hausmann, bishop's official at Konstanz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist the widow of Jacob Wolfen in obtaining her share of the inheritance from the estate of Elsbeth Schmidin. This had been so stipulated in the testament of the deceased Ursula Huxin. The widow Wolfen had agreed that her share should follow the other creditors.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Glarus report to Burgomaster and Council of Zürich about the disputes between the Prelate of St. Gallen and the evangelical subjects in Toggenburg. They describe the failed mediation attempts and the appointment of a new Diet on 26 May in Rapperswil. The Toggenburgers refuse to participate until a Landsgemeinde clarifies their rights. Glarus asks Zürich to also urge the Toggenburgers towards a peaceful solution.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen that they have informed Glarus and Appenzell about the disputes between the St. Gallen prelates and the Evangelicals in Toggenburg. They advise the Toggenburgers to appear on the appointed day in Rapperswil before the envoys of Schwyz and Glarus, in order to avoid unrest. They ask St. Gallen for its opinion and promise to report on further developments.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich reply to letters from St. Gallen of 23 and 24 May 1617 concerning the Toggenburg matters. They report that the evangelical co-religionists in Toggenburg had complained and had been invited to a Diet in Rapperswil. Zürich has dispatched two Council envoys. Furthermore, they ask St. Gallen to order their Landvogt in the Rheintal to prevent Count von Ems from crossing the Rhine with troops, should an uprising occur.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Schultheiss and Council of Bern to kindly hear their city physician and fellow councilor Dr. Sebastian Schöbinger, who is pursuing the renewal of the regalia with the Roman Imperial Majesty, and to grant him as favorable a response as possible.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Bern

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Burgomaster and Council of Luzern to hear their city physician and fellow councillor Dr. Sebastian Schöbinger, who is pursuing the renewal of the regalia, and to grant him a favourable response.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Luzern

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen remind Burgomaster and Council of Basel about the renewal of the regalia with the Emperor. Since some cantons do not consent, it will be discussed at the next annual accounting day in Baden whether the confirmation should be attempted again through a joint embassy. St. Gallen asks Basel to consider the matter and to send an embassy to Baden. If an agreement with all cantons fails, the cantons for whom trade is particularly important should find a solution among themselves to avoid disadvantages.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Basel

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the intercession letter of the city of Frankfurt of 17 March 1617 concerning the claim of the heirs of Johann du Faimans against the citizens of St. Gallen Christoph Tanner and Georg Kessler. They refer to the submitted complaint and the appeal of the attorney Job Sätelis to the Council of the city of St. Gallen. Furthermore, they state that they had received an imperial instruction not to examine the matter any further, and they forward a copy of this letter.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Frankfurt

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Arboners of 6 June 1617 regarding a debt claim of the St. Gallen school. They confirm that the Schultheissen accept the declaration of the Arboners to be considered as debtors until the next Martini and to relieve the surety Leuz Mezger. This is done without deduction of the agreed 25 gulden and without impairment of the rights of the Schultheissen until full payment.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of Arbon

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to Count Caspar von Hohenems that the parish priest of Höchst is withholding from the hospital the half of the hemp and tithes, which it has possessed for over 200 years. The parish priest, after inspection of the documents, had indeed withdrawn, but the scribe had disputed the claims of the hospital. The city asks the Count, as overlord, to secure the peaceful enjoyment of the tithe for the hospital and to silence the scribe.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Caspar, Count of Hohenems and Gallera

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Chur ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Kaspar Frick in the collection of a claim of about 20 gulden against the heirs of the St. Gallen citizen Heinrich Grüter. Frick says that he lent money to Grüter, who was serving in the French war. Chur requests St. Gallen to use official authority to enforce the payment of the principal, interest, and costs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Hieremia Locher to pay the three received sums of money, along with the costs and damages incurred, to the widow Anna Maria Dondorferin, a citizen of Memmingen, through her agent Bartholomäus Schmid. The widow had turned to Memmingen because she lost her case in Zürich against the messenger of Zürich and now has to sue against the messenger of St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Statthalter and Council of the city of Feldkirch report to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on the instruction of a boy who has been handed over to them. They state that the father, the carpenter Mattheis Zebel, called Hüß, had obtained citizenship about ten years ago and had married an unmarried woman. After his expulsion from Feldkirch, he had begotten the boy in Bregenz with a woman from the Arlberg or Tirol. Since neither the father nor the mother was married, the boy cannot be punished as an offender against honor. Feldkirch refuses the punishment and hands the boy over to St. Gallen.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the city of Feldkirch
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Jacob Krebs in the collection of a claim from the estate of the deceased wife of Heinrich Zürr. They refer to an earlier letter of 19. September 1611, in which they had declared that foreigners are equally entitled in edicts. They ask for quick and inexpensive support.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell thank St. Gallen for its care for their Landammann Johann Schüssen in the dispute with the Prelate. They communicate that they have not yet found a final solution, but have received a letter from the Inner Roden. They report on a messenger from Switzerland in Appenzell and a warning by the Sekelmeister Martin Sutter of a possible war. They ask St. Gallen for confidential news and opinions.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell reject the accusations of the Appenzell Landrat, that they had promised help in the dispute between the Abbot of St. Gallen and his subjects in the Toggenburg. They declare that they know nothing of the sort and contradict the claim that their Amtmann Konrad Zellweger had acted in Wattwil, as he had never been there. They ask the Appenzell Council not to give credence to these false rumors and to defend them in the matter.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have learned of a dispute between the Abbot of St. Gallen and the subjects in the Turtal. They point out that they had not offered any help to the people of the Turtal, and ask the St. Gallen authorities to adhere to the existing contracts and not to suspect Appenzell of acting against the contracts.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to appoint their citizen Hans Jakob Büelinger, goldsmith, who has already cut coin dies for St. Gallen, as coin master or coin warden. They assure that Büelinger knows the coin matters and ask for a favorable answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen answer the inquiry of the St. Gallen corn master regarding the combating of weevils in grain. They state that their officials take the affected fruits out of the Dünni, let them stand empty for a while, sprinkle them with sweet water, and have the Muren cleaned before re-storing them. They know of no other means of prevention.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the town of Stein am Rhein inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have taken in a man in their hospital who gives his name as Hans Sailer, cooper. He is described in a wanted notice transmitted by St. Gallen as a possible murderer and member of an evil society. Stein asks St. Gallen for written information on whether the man is actually a citizen of St. Gallen and what his background is, so that they can proceed legally against him.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the town of Stein am Rhein
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the inquiry of the city of Stein am Rhein regarding the prisoner Hans Seyler there. They confirm that Seyler completed his apprenticeship with the St. Gallen furrier Jacob Knoblach. However, he did not subsequently pursue the trade, but begged and is ill-spoken of. St. Gallen suspects that Seyler is the person whom Benedict Bettlin, who was sentenced in St. Gallen, referred to as a fellow accomplice. They send an excerpt from Bettlin's statement and point out that Bettlin was also known as “Bene” or “der Wild”.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein report that they have strictly interrogated the imprisoned Hans Deyler. They were unable to prove either theft or murder. Deyler claims that the executed Balthasar falsely accused him. Stein sets Deyler free and offers St. Gallen to hand him over against a bond.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank the von Stein am Rhein for their offer to hand over the captive Hans Dörfflin against security for costs. Since the person of the captive is not of great importance to St. Gallen, they leave the further handling of the matter to the von Stein am Rhein.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: The von Stein am Rhein

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Count Caspar zu Hohenems to help their citizens in a debt matter against the heirs of the deceased Obervogt Georg von Rait zu Roschach. They request that the goods be restored and a court day be set, so that the creditors are treated according to the Inngoldtstättischen Landrecht. Furthermore, they ask for the settlement of an open debt of the city of 18 Florin 4 Kreuzer and 4 Heller.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Caspar Count zu Hohenems

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the administrators of the captaincy as well as Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz to help their citizen Jacob Zili in the collection of a debt owed to his brother-in-law Anton Schaurout. Zili appeals to the inheritance claims of his deceased wife Sophia Schauroutin as well as to a pledged estate. The St. Gallen authorities ask for support in the payment and for recognition of their intercession.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Administrators of the captaincy and Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: The Landammann and Council in the hinter Bregenzerwald ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the local bailiff to arrest or detain the persons Homen Michel, Jacob Jäger and Albrecht All, who come from the Au and are causing unrest in the Bregenzerwald. They ask for a reply.
en.sender: Landammann and Council in the hinter Bregenzerwald
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Count Caspar zu Hohenems, Glarus and Vaduz to grant a gracious audience to the heirs of the deceased citizens of St. Gallen, Georg and Philipp Zwicker, and to respond favorably to their humble petition. They refer to the detailed description by town clerk Melchior Guldin.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Count Caspar zu Hohenems, Glarus and Vaduz

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen whether the newly introduced Churer pfennigs, half-batzen and Tischpfennigs with the image of Saint Quirinus may be accepted and paid out. They ask for a neighborly answer. In the meantime, they have strictly instructed their subjects to refrain from importing these coin types until further notice, in order to avoid dispute and damage.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from Arbon regarding Martin Straussen and his debts to the St. Gallen school chest. They point out that the school trustees have become impatient and could not enter into any further agreements. Since Arbon had promised to fully compensate the school chest on Martini, they demand the payment of the outstanding amounts.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Arbon

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the impending march of the Greek war troops to Friuli. They attach a report from the neighborhood containing details on dates, quarters, and provisions. They ask for reciprocity in similar reports and for the continuation of the correspondence of the Confederation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Wil inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the case of a foreign woman who is supposed to have given birth to a child in Wil. The child is said to have been assigned to the shoemaker Caspar Widmer, who lives in Oberbarn, as the father. Widmer is said to have reached an agreement with the woman to pay the child's father Georg Weber 30 Rhenen, and the woman commits herself to raising the child at her own expense. Wil communicates this to St. Gallen, as the woman is not a citizen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen communicate to Burgomaster and Council of Lindau a message that has come to them from the city of Schaffhausen. They request mutual communication of similar messages and express their readiness for continued good neighborly correspondence.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the information regarding the warlike troops passing through Tirol and Friaul. They promise to maintain good neighborly correspondence in the future as well, and enclose further confidential communications from other cantons. In a postscript, it is reported that the two Councils of Österreich had ordered the Commander to hasten with the troops, which were to arrive in Kempten on the following Monday.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Councils of Archduke Maximilian zu Österreich inform the French envoy about the march of 2000 men under Colonel Moritz von Kriechingen. The infantry marches over the Black Forest to Schwaben and Kempten. The Councils assure that the soldiers carry their weapons themselves, the caution is provided by the Colonel, and the passage is soon to be undertaken.
en.sender: Secret and intimate Councils of Archduke Maximilian zu Österreich
en.recipient: Royal French Envoy Johann Ludwig Schultheiss von Adelhus zu Richenzell

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Glarus ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizens, the Herren Kelmündin, to pay the heirs of Hauptmann Schwerters in Wollenturn and to release Caspar Ströwli, who is liable as surety for them, from the surety. Ströwli is abroad, otherwise his wife would be harmed. Glarus threatens otherwise with serious measures.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Stadtschultheiss and Council of Feldkirch ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish the edict concerning the general court day appointed for their citizen Hans Schallend. Since Schallend may possibly be indebted to citizens of St. Gallen, this should prevent creditors from being disadvantaged by ignorance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Lindau to allow the heirs of the deceased citizen of Nürnberg, Caspar Forta, to arrest eight bales of jute leather. These are said to come from the estate of the bankrupt debtor and to be located in Lindau. The creditors of St. Gallen are interested in the payment and ask for official support.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Captain and Landvogt of Liechtenstein that Thias Krey of Baiermühle, who comes from the Toggenburg, was caught in St. Gallen stealing grain. Krey confesses that he had already been punished for theft in Weinfelden. The St. Gallen authorities ask for a copy of the trial and for information about Krey's conduct and reputation among his neighbors.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Captain and Landvogt of Liechtenstein

en.regest: Imperial Bailiff, Schultheiss and Council of Wil reply to the inquiry of the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen regarding Hans Küoni of Immensee, who is detained in St. Gallen. They state that Küoni stood before the Halsgericht in the year 1610 for theft and was punished. As an enclosure, they attach his confession and the judgment, according to which his nose was cut off and he was banished from the city.
en.sender: Imperial Bailiff, Schultheiss and Council of Wil
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landvogt Dietrich Reding von Schwyz informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about Theiss Krey, who is detained in St. Gallen. He says that he has behaved quietly since his arrest on 8 February 1608 in Liechtensteig. He stood before the High Court for theft, was sentenced to the pillory and fined 100 thaler. Some of Krey's neighbours had turned to the people of St. Gallen and asked for mercy for him.
en.sender: Captain Dietrich Reding von Schwyz, Landvogt of the County of Toggenburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Heinrich Zeller, who comes from Herisau and was employed in St. Gallen as a bleacher, has been insulted there. At Zeller's request, they confirm his good conduct in Appenzell. Zeller was previously accused of burglary and theft, but was not incriminated under torture. He merely admitted that he had invoked the devil at the house of the mother and the deceased cousin Jos Ramsauer, which he deeply regrets.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to Ammann and Court of Widnau and Haslach im Reintal that they had learned from their hospital officials and citizens that an increase had been made in the annual tax there. They ask that a place and day be determined for the coming week at which their dispatched Council messenger could negotiate orally, and request a written answer.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Ammann and Court of Widnau and Haslach im Reintal

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to Lindau that confusion has arisen in the city because of the rumor that the Churer Sechsbäzner have been recalled. Many refused to pay with this sort. They ask Lindau to provide information about the recalled sorts and the reasons.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter from St. Gallen regarding the Six- and Three-beiger coins that were prohibited and struck there. They confirm that the ring-containing sorts, which were trying to sneak in, were struck, but that the Churer were not affected as they were current. The Three-beiger were indeed struck, but can be distinguished by the table and continue to be issued and received promiscue.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Hauptmannschaft, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz reply to a letter of 24 March regarding the coin types. They communicate that the stamped four types of Dickpfennig or Sechsbätzner as well as one type of Dreibätzner are too light. To avoid damage, they had forbidden the circulation of these coins in Konstanz. They send the stamps with and offer their services.
en.sender: Administrator of the Hauptmannschaft, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern inform the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen that they are setting out the dispute with the Duke of Longueville and his relatives, which concerned the city of Neuenburg, in open printed form. They ask St. Gallen to read the enclosed copies and to defend, protect, and handle Bern in this matter, as Bern would do for St. Gallen.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the Landvogt in the Reintal, Basch Altherr, to investigate a wine contract between their citizen Sigmund Zolikofer and Thomas Siber in the Büren. It is claimed that the interest amounts to ten gulden per year. The city wishes to know whether this is true, in order to be able to act accordingly.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Basch Altherr, Landvogt in the Reintal

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kitzingen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the unmarried shoemaker's journeyman Hans Jakob Locher, son of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Daniel Locher, has fallen ill there. They ask that 12 or 14 gulden be paid out to the journeyman from his estate, which his cousin Felix Zübler administers, so that he may settle his debts and travel home.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from Altstetten, which had set a date for a negotiation on the coming Monday. As Monday does not suit them, they ask that the date be moved to the following Tuesday, 28 April. The envoys would arrive in Altstetten on Monday evening.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Altstetten

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to Lindau that Christoph Kobel from Feldkirch, who is in their custody, has stated that about five weeks ago in St. Gallen a malefactor referred to as «Rothlatz» was executed. As they do not trust this statement, they request Lindau for information on whether this happened, and in the affirmative case ask for the protocol as well as for notification on whether the condemned man had mentioned the prisoners.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter from St. Gallen, in which a young prisoner had claimed that an Appenzeller offender had been taken in and punished in Lindau five or six weeks ago. Lindau denies this and reports that only on the past Friday Hans Thanner vom Büchlin from the Lordship of Bregenz had been executed by hanging and burning, but that he had never mentioned the St. Gallen prisoner.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Stadtvogt and Council of Maienfeld ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene with the Princess of Solothurn on behalf of the widow Helena Lagin. She had lost her case in the appellate court of Liechtensteig against her guardians Heinrich Spießer and Rudolf Groben. The guardians had refused the requested accounting and imposed unjustified debts. Maienfeld requests that the guardians be compelled by decree to provide the accounting.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Wil answer the inquiry of the toll collector of St. Gallen regarding the weight and scale regulations at the Wil yarn market. They stipulate that Mengen under one pound are indicated on the small scale, while larger Mengen are weighed on the large scale with the Vierling or half pound. A fee of one Lichter Heller is charged for five pounds.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to issue a credible copy of the testament of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Jakob Viol, in which their citizen Hans Jakob Haderer is named as an heir. This is to be done so that Haderer and his co-heirs can take possession of their inheritance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Ludwig Holzhalb, Landvogt in the Upper and Lower Rhine Valley, reports to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about an investigation at the four lower courts. These deny seeking to go against the judgment on the speeches of Badener, and declare that they would comply with the judgment for four years. Holzhalb suspects that different things were said in Bad, and delivers the report with the St. Gallen town constable Heinrich Lutzen.
en.sender: Hans Ludwig Holzhalb, Landvogt in the Upper and Lower Rhine Valley
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen demand that Johann Staudern, former Landvogt in the Rheintal, settle the outstanding sum of 300 gulden. They refer to the fact that Staudern received 900 gulden for the Landvogtei Rheintal and, despite promises and extensions of the deadline, has not made the payment. They threaten that, in case of non-payment, they will call upon the Confederates for superior judicial assistance.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Johann Staudern, Council of Kyburg, former Landvogt in the lower and upper Rheintal

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the St. Gallen town constable not to collect tolls from the St. Gallen woman Elisabetha Meggelin, the wife of the deceased Appenzell Statthalter Konrad Schüpfen, for the purchase of goods and cloths. They consider this an unneighborly innovation and ask that the previous good customs be maintained.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss, Statthalter, Council and Deputies of the Evangelical Religion in Frauenfeld ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for tax support for the construction of a new parsonage. The existing building is dilapidated and must be demolished. Since the community is small and poor, they cannot finance the building without outside help. They refer to previous grants from St. Gallen and ask for another gift.
en.sender: Schultheiss, Statthalter, Council and Deputies of the Evangelical Religion in Frauenfeld
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss, Statthalter, Council and Deputies of the Evangelical Religion in Frauenfeld ask Kunkler of the Council of the city of St. Gallen, bailiff of the lordship of Bürglen, for a donation for the new construction of the parsonage at St. Johann. The old building is dilapidated and the community is poor, as it has been deprived of its temporal income by its fellow citizens of the Catholic religion.
en.sender: The Schultheiss, Statthalter, Council and Deputies of the Evangelical Religion in Frauenfeld
en.recipient: Kunkler of the Council of the city of St. Gallen, bailiff of the lordship of Bürglen

en.regest: Ammann and Council of Rheineck request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publish an edict concerning a scheduled general court day for the creditors of the deceased citizen of Rheineck, Jörg Heeren. They ask that the edict be posted in the usual places so that no one is disadvantaged by ignorance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Council of Arbon reply to a supplication by the citizen of St. Gallen Zacharias Studin. They state that they do not claim a deduction for the property that Studin brought from St. Gallen, as this would violate the neighborly agreement. For the property that Studin's ancestor Georg Riedtman brought as a citizen of Bischofzell, they reserve the deduction. This had not been carried out until now because Riedtman's wife Guldin Melligin had still had much property in St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich invite Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to a Confederate Diet on 26. Oktober 1618 in Baden. They request the dispatch of an authorized Council messenger to deliberate on current political tensions and rumors, to clarify misunderstandings, and to secure peace in the fatherland.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Richter, Statthalter, Council and Community of the Evangelical Religion of Krummenau thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the favorable approval of a strong tax penny on the purchased property of the Pfründhaus from the parish and preaching office of St. Johann. They ask for continued neighborly favor and commend themselves to divine care.
en.sender: Richter, Statthalter, Council and Community of the Evangelical Religion of Krummenau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen confirm to the evangelical community of Frauenfeld their consent to a tax for the construction of the Pfrundhaus at St. Johann. They have contributed a sum from the city treasury and collected further funds from wealthy citizens. The total amount amounts to 134 florins, of which 30 florins come from the gentlemen and 104 florins from the citizens.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss, Statthalter, Council and Community of the evangelical religion of Frauenfeld

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the Hauptmann, Schultheiss, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz to have their citizen Christoph Denner, who is threatened by his former journeyman Christoph Kreiser from Hessen, appear in St. Gallen to report on the dispute. In case of refusal, Kreiser is to be tried according to law on the charge of recklessness.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Hauptmann, Schultheiss, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help the widow of the deceased citizen of Lindau, Ulrich Eggen, to prevent her illegitimate son from using a letter of surety to plunge his mother into poverty. They request that the son return the letter of surety, in order to protect him and the creditors from harm.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Burgomaster and Council of Chur that they have learned of the judgment in the case of the former citizen of St. Gallen Otilia Essigin against Heinrich Blum. Since Essigin is no longer a citizen and her place of residence is unknown, they have sent a copy of the letter to her brother Bartholomäus Essigen, who remained in St. Gallen, so that he may forward it to his sister. It is not known whether she will appear at the court day.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Chur

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to take up the matter of Baschi Hälftenberger from Nieder Urnen. He says that he had settled with the citizen of St. Gallen Jeremias Locher over a loss of 120 gulden, whereby Locher would take over half. Since Locher has now retained 60 gulden along with a letter to Hans Heinrich Müller, Hälftenberger fears that he will also lose the remaining 80 gulden. Zürich asks St. Gallen to help Hälftenberger and to secure the repayment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz transmit to St. Gallen the statement of the widow Elisabeth Schoblerin in the legal dispute between the heirs of Ibelli and Michael Schobler. The witness reports that the mother of the deceased Michael Schobler had denied to her having a debt and had not asserted the claim during her son's lifetime.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on the inheritance matter of the St. Gallen woman Magdalena Huwiler. Since not all heirs of the Muralt family were present, the negotiation was postponed. The parties are to appear before the competent Councils at the Zürich fair after Whitsun. Zürich warns that Magdalena Huwiler has little to expect in view of the costs for the deceased Anna Muraltin.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the city of Luzern to treat their town clerk Melchior Guldin, who represents the heirs of the deceased Caspar Schlumpf, with goodwill in obtaining Promotorialen from various cantons. They refer to a previous similar request and thank in advance for the support of the Confederates.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Luzern

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter of the 5th of the month regarding shipping wages to Konstanz and Schaffhausen. They report that the wages for the Konstanz voyage have remained unchanged for years, only for wine they had been raised a few years ago from 6 to 30 kreuzer. For the Schaffhausen voyage, the wages had been set about five years ago, with the consent of the authorities and merchants, at 3 kreuzer per salt cask, 1 kreuzer per salt and 1 kreuzer per hundredweight of merchant goods. This increase was due to rising costs at high and low water as well as to the reduction of the ship's load to 30 salt casks per ship, which increased safety. The shipmen also had to return empty, as they had no return cargo.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen dated the 16th of the month. They communicate that Archduke Leopold von Österreich, as Governor of the County of Tirol and other frontier lands, is expected and should be asked for strong contributions. He is to come to Feldkirch within three weeks to hold a Landtag there with the four lordships before the Arlberg. His retinue is not to exceed 120 horses and 210 persons. After the Landtag, he will probably travel to Bregenz and from there by ship to Konstanz.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that in a few days 1000 horsemen recruited in the Netherlands will come into the upper Landrevier and pass through Neuenburg. Archduke Leopold of Österreich will arrive in Wolfegg on 4 April to receive the people and organize their further march. Lindau shares this upon request and remains ready for neighborly services.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Lindau for the report on the passage of 1000 Dutch horses and the arrival of Archduke Leopold. They ask for further communications and promise to do everything that serves the continuation of the good and trusting relationship.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Lindau

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Secret Council of Lindau inform St. Gallen about imperial letters that demand the passage of troops to Böhmen in the territories of both cities and in Wangen, Isny, Leutkirch, as well as with the nobility. They further report that twelve banners of Italian troops are to be quartered in Bludenz, Feldkirch, Bregenz, and the Landvogtei of Schwaben. Lindau asks St. Gallen to inquire about the pass over the Gotthard and to report whether the Confederates will grant passage to Italian troops. Furthermore, it is reported that 1000 horsemen from the Netherlands are to march through Elsass and Schwaben.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Secret Council of Lindau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Secret Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the town messenger Jacob Hildebrand was attacked and robbed of his money on the journey to Nürnberg between Neresheim and Öttingen. They ask to be informed how high the interests of the St. Gallen travellers are, and promise to investigate the case.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen that they are answering its inquiry regarding the passage of Dutch and other foreign troops. They report on the situation in Italien and Mailand, where troops were recruited, and on the quarters of the 1000 Dutch cuirassiers in Alsace. They refer to the upcoming day of the thirteen cantons on 25 April, at which the danger from foreign troops is to be discussed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist Bailiff Hans Holderegger in the settlement of the inheritance of the children of the deceased Stadler in Hundwil. They confirm the legitimate birth of the heirs and refer to the agreement that inheritance cases in St. Gallen are to be inherited according to the law of St. Gallen.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Lindau for the information regarding complaints from other cities. They report that troops have been recruited in Italien and Mailand, whose route of march to Germany is still unclear. They ask Lindau to help them clarify the situation and enclose a document concerning Dutch troops.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Lindau

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report that their sailors brought from Schaffhausen that the previous day a commotion had arisen at Steckborn, as about 1000 Welschen had invaded in the lower Thurgau and had killed a watch. Lindau suspects that it concerns troops from Stockach and the Donautal who had behaved badly. They ask St. Gallen to inform them what is known there about the war situation and the sought-after pass. Furthermore, it is reported that people marching from the Elsass are heading towards the Donautal and Ulm, whereupon great fear exists among the population.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report to St. Gallen on the situation in the war. They dismiss rumors of an incursion of 1000 Welschen into Unterthurgau as unfounded, as only a bell alarm had taken place. The Confederates had decided in Baden to deny the pass over the Gotthard to foreign troops. Approximately 700 men were lying in Feldkirch and the surrounding area, whose objective was unclear; an attack on St. Gallen had been feared for July 1. Lindau offers to notify St. Gallen immediately upon receiving new information.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a reply letter of 21 May and ask for confidential reports on further developments of the war. They inform that two regiments of the army marching from Alsace had arrived on Thursday in Wiblingen and Kirchberg near Ulm and were to be led down the Danube via Günzburg.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to postpone a hearing scheduled for the next day with delegated envoys, as urgent business prevents the elected Landammann Quorath Zällwegger from participating. They promise to convey their opinion on the following Saturday.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the Statthalter of Liechtenstein to instruct the scribe Martin Schmid in Höchst to recognize the tithe claims of the St. Gallen hospital on the Büchler in the lower Buchholz and not to contest them any further. They refer to previous customs and ask for the protection of the almshouse from Schmid's demands.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Statthalter of Liechtenstein

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Ulm for a letter of 13 June and ask for the continuation of the trusting exchange. They refer to an enclosed letter regarding new war levies. Furthermore, they report that soldiers and money had already arrived in Rorschach and that some persons had fled from the borders.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Council envoys of the thirteen cantons at the Diet of the annual accounts at Baden to advocate for the abolition of new toll increases in the Austrian lands. The merchants of St. Gallen are heavily burdened by these duties. The city refers to the existing hereditary agreement with the House of Österreich and asks that the complaints be remedied in order to promote trade.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Council envoys of the thirteen cantons at the Diet of the annual accounts at Baden

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Eberhard von Rappoltstein to determine the date for the division of the paternal and maternal inheritance of their fellow citizen, the widow of the late Herr Hundt. They refer to the fact that several months have passed since the father's death and request a prompt and inexpensive settlement.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Eberhard von Rappoltstein zu Hohenegg

en.regest: The judges of the city and Landsgemeinde of Zürich report that the St. Gallen day-labourer Jacob Höwberger had committed himself to a marriage with Anna Schuollerin, but had left her and returned to St. Gallen. Höwberger had taken an oath in Zürich to present himself again and to keep his promise. The judges of Zürich ask the authorities of St. Gallen to use their power to compel Höwberger to honour his engagement, or to inform them in writing whether he is already married in St. Gallen.
en.sender: Judges of the city and Landsgemeinde of Zürich
en.recipient: Kammerer and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report that Emperor Ferdinand II. has hired about 1000 French soldiers to lead them through the Confederation and the Landvogtei Schwaben to Böhmen. They request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform them as soon as possible what they know or could learn about the background of this troop movement.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a report on the state of war, which they received upon their request. They declare themselves willing to serve St. Gallen in similar cases and to continue the neighborly intimacy.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish an edict concerning the appointed general court day for the deceased citizen of Lindau, Balthasar Humbler. This is done so that creditors and relatives can assert their claims against the inventory of the deceased and no one be curtailed in their rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz remind the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of a promise by the St. Gallen citizen Lorenz Zschellen to deliver 25 to 30 centners of powder to the Konstanz citizen Cyrill Zimberling. Since the authorities have forbidden Zimberling to obtain powder from St. Gallen, the Konstanzer ask to allow Zimberling to collect the promised powder from Zschellen.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Caspar Graf zu Hohenems asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to allow his councilor and physician Dr. Sebastian Schöbinger to travel immediately to Hohenems and to remain there for up to eight days, as he himself is suffering from a serious illness and requires medical assistance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Schorno, Council of Schwyz and Landvogt of the County of Baden, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the customs officers in the County of Baden, lacking loading lists, had to break open the goods of the carriers in order to levy the duties. He asks the St. Gallen authorities to instruct their merchants to issue credible loading lists to the carriers in the future, in order to avoid such inconveniences.
en.sender: Johann Schorno, Council of Schwyz and Landvogt of the Grafschaft Baden
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Elector Friedrich von der Pfalz to provide Melchior Guldin, whom they have appointed as their proxy for the widow Adriana Francisca von der Hohen Sax, with a letter of recommendation to the General States of the Vereinigten Niederlande or the High Council of Holland, as well as to Prince Mauritz von Oranien, so that he can successfully assert the widow's inheritance claims in the Niederlande.
en.recipient: Friedrich, Pfalzgraf bei Rhein, Kurfürst und Herzog zu Bayern

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the five cantons would have granted permission for the passage of 6000 Italian Spanish troops. The infantry would march through Uri, Schwyz, the Mark, Sarganserland or Einsiedeln, Rapperswil to Tirol, the cavalry over Zug through the Ergoew to Alsace. They ask St. Gallen to be vigilant, to guard against danger and deceit, and to report any occurrences to them.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that 6000 Spanish soldiers are to march over the Gotthard to Rorschach and through the Toggenburg. The Austrian Vögte of the lordships before the Arlberg are to meet the next day in Dornbirn for a consultation regarding this passage. Lindau asks St. Gallen for immediate notification of what they have learned about it.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Lindau for the information that 6000 Spanish soldiers are to march over the Gotthard to Roschach. They say that they cannot yet confirm this, but promise to notify Lindau immediately upon receiving new information. They send an excerpt from a letter by a deceased fellow citizen and ask for the continuation of the confidential exchange.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Appenzell that a troop of 9000 men from the Milanese is to set out and place itself in the service of the territories. The five cantons together with Freiburg and Solothurn have decided to attack Bern if it does not yield. Preparations are being made in Luzern and other places. The abbot of St. Gallen has consulted with the lords of Muri and Wettingen. St. Gallen asks Appenzell to send envoys on the next Saturday or earlier to jointly consult on defense and to involve the abbot.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for confidential communications about war troops that are marching through the Confederation from Italien. They declare themselves ready to continue the confidential correspondence and the mutual informing about the current events.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the information regarding the impending passage of Spanish troops. They inform that the Spanish King intends to send 6000 men from the Milanese to Germany and to lead them through the Confederation. The departure is not yet determined, and the route will probably lead via Veltlin to Lake Constance. Zürich asks St. Gallen to take the necessary watch and security measures.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Hans Erleholz. Erleholz had handed over 100 gulden to the St. Gallen merchant Sebastian Küllner for a debt to the St. Gallen citizen Jacob Keufzig. Keufzig had not forwarded the money, however, but had spent it on grain. Erleholz is in custody and the grain has been seized in St. Gallen and Steinach. Überlingen requests that the grain be returned to Erleholz as his property.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Alfonso Casale informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he has gladly accepted the commission mentioned in their letter of the 14th or 24th of the month. He says that he has already written to His Excellency in their interest and expects a good outcome of the matter. He offers his services for further requests and hopes that the citizens of St. Gallen in the states of His Majesty will be treated equally well.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that approximately two thousand Italian and Spanish soldiers are already on the march. The first are to arrive in Lachen by next Monday and then march via Rapperswil through the County of Toggenburg and the land of the Abbot of St. Gallen. Zürich asks St. Gallen to behave accordingly and assures its own precautions.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rorschach ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their fellow citizen Johann Gabriel Blumegger, the Obervogt of Mündlingen, to collect a remaining amount of 149 florins and 48 kreuzer from Joachim Gmünder. Gmünder is said to have refused payment despite a reminder and to have fled. The Rorschach authorities ask for a written recommendation to the citizens of St. Gallen, in order to settle the arrears and to uphold market justice.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau thank for the communication of 3 October concerning the Italian war troops and report in turn that 7000 men have arrived in Cremona. These are to leave Mailand, march to Varese, and proceed to Germany in companies of 500 men each. The first troops could reach Rorschach within 14 days.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Lindau for the confidential report on the Italian and Spanish war troops. They state that these are to arrive in Rapperswil on 28 October according to the new style. Furthermore, the cantons of Uri, Schwyz and Unterwalden have established a supplementary force in Rapperswil, the purpose of which is still unknown to them. They promise to inform Lindau of further developments.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizen Caspar König in a debt matter. They refer to an attached petition and emphasize that debts written voluntarily and with good deliberation should be gratefully paid after long-standing surety. They request that the supplicant be viewed in a good light and that they contribute to the swift obtaining of his release.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Esslingen report that the widow Margaretha Freiberger, together with her children Joseph, David and Tobias Freiberger, and her son-in-law Matthäus Zell, have appeared before them. They wish to give their cousin Heinrich Wanner 200 gulden for the acquisition of a benefice and maintenance in the hospital. The widow requests a letter of intercession to St. Gallen. Esslingen promises to reimburse the 200 gulden and to establish a bond on the widow's assets with an annual interest of 10 gulden. They ask St. Gallen to accept this.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizens Konrad and Hans Jakob Fölcklin in the collection of an outstanding debt owed to the citizen of St. Gallen Jacob Breisig. They refer to the equal treatment of citizens and foreigners in matters of cession and gold court according to the custom of St. Gallen and ask for friendly neighborly help.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report that approximately 300 Spanish soldiers, including 100 on horseback, attempted the day before yesterday to pass through the land of Aebzell at the bridge in the Au. The watch posted there by the Lords of Aebzell threw down the bridge and raised the alarm. The country folk appeared in great numbers, whereupon the Spaniards withdrew. They promise to report immediately on any further developments.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: E. St. Wht.

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Basel for information regarding the validity of a letter of completion, which the in Basel trained Doctor Johannes Conrad Schöbinger received from his master Luca Gernler. In St. Gallen, the local apothecaries demand that Schöbinger, who wants to open an apothecary without the usual apprenticeship period, not be admitted. The St. Gallen ask the Basel for their opinion on whether the letter of completion allows Schöbinger to run his own pharmacy.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Basel

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the notification that the Italian and Spanish war troops have moved on. They ask to continue to keep an eye on this troop and to inform them immediately if it stops. Zürich offers to inform St. Gallen of its own findings. Furthermore, it is mentioned that a negotiation in Baden between Bern and Freiburg is taking place; the results will be communicated upon the return of the envoys.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau thank St. Gallen for the information regarding the Italian troops marching through the Confederation. They report that the people of Roschach to Fussach have already crossed via the Ruggsteig. The commissioners, together with the one from Reitnau and other Austrian officials, had been in Lindau. The people are moving on rapidly. Lindau asks for mutual warning and assures neighborly loyalty.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Privy Council of Lindau inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the strong presence of Italian troops in the Austrian territory of Bregenz, who are apparently taking up winter quarters. They fear inconveniences and price increases in the neighborhood and ask to be informed how things stand in the Confederation.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Privy Council of Lindau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Secretaries of the Council of Lindau thank for a letter of 12 November and report on the military situation. They receive the news that in the quarters of Scheidegg and Weiler the subjects were instructed to provide themselves with supplies, as troops are again coming from Bregenz. The people are moving into the Allgäu because of the blocked pass through Pünz and unrest in the Illertal. The Neapolitan troops behaved arrogantly. Through Pünz, 100 German horsemen came to Lindau, of whom 50 were detained by Count zu Ems, while the rest continued on.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Secretaries of the Council of Lindau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Secretaries of the Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the report on the Spanish war troops gathering around Bregenz. They consider it unlikely that this troop will proceed against the Confederation, as it must first still gather and equip itself. They ask St. Gallen to continue observing the situation and to inform them. Regarding the dispute between Bern and Freiburg, negotiations are still ongoing, and a result is still pending.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that their Burgomaster Hans Rudolf Rahn has heard rumors that he has behaved improperly in his office and has fallen into disgrace. They ask the St. Gallen authorities not to give credence to these untrue reports, to investigate the source, and to inform them of it, so that they can act accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the confidential report of 15 November concerning the Spanish war troops in Bregenz and their advance. They ask that they continue in this good foresight and continue to report to them in a confidentially trustworthy manner of the Confederation about all important and necessary occurrences. Zürich declares itself, for its part, ready to show St. Gallen all the loyalty and friendship of the Confederation.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Secret Council of Lindau report that the Nuremberg messenger Christoph Sprüder was insulted by a court bailiff at Obersilgäu. The latter threatened to raid Lindau if it sent more riders. Lindau asks St. Gallen to examine the messenger under oath and to transmit the statement sealed.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Secret Council of Lindau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ybbs inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that their citizen Hans Blum, Schlosser, who had complained to them about a child begotten in adultery, came to Ybbs upon summons and appeared there. He has declared himself willing to answer to all who assert claims and has sworn to the Amtsbürgermeister not to depart until the matter is clarified. Ybbs asks St. Gallen to instruct Ottilia Hässing to appear in the town hall on Friday, 15 January, at 8 in the morning, to bring her complaint against Blum and await the judgment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Bischofszell request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have their citizen Jacob Meurer comply with his sworn promise. Meurer had committed himself to provide for the children of his brother-in-law Jacob Löwen, as these live in poverty. Bischofszell had deprived Löwen of the church call and placed the children under guardianship, as the parents did not care for them. Meurer has not reacted so far.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the citizens of St. Gallen Jacob Hiltprandt and Hans Giller had been absent in Lindau. They have set a court day for Friday, the 18. Dezember, and request the St. Gallen to ensure their citizens attend at this date.
