en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report that the widow of the deceased merchant Christoph Freyberger and her son Jeremias Vanner had paid the demanded 200 gulden together with interest and costs in cash. They ask the recipients to admit Vanner to their hospital, and promise to pay the 200 gulden in cash as soon as they receive a report on the matter.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Council of Bischofszell regarding the engagement of their citizen Hans Maurer to a daughter of his brother-in-law Jacob Sturm. They have summoned Maurer and presented the matter to him. Maurer has agreed to travel to Bischofszell on the next Fyrtag to clarify the matter. St. Gallen continues to offer neighborly services.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Altschultheiss and Council of Bischofszell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to the letter of St. Gallen of 17 December regarding the estate of the deceased Reicha Hüblin. They state that the deceased is said to have a sister Ursula in Straßburg, who as the next heir would exclude other heirs. They have requested information from Straßburg and will not describe further heirs for the time being. They send copies of the codicil and the inventory.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Secretaries of the Council of Lindau thank the Burgomaster and Secretaries of the Council of St. Gallen for the communication of a sworn report by their citizen Christoph Gmünder regarding an encounter with a citizen of St. Gallen in the Landvogtei of Schwaben near Weingarten. They promise to reciprocate the neighborly goodwill.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and Secretaries of the Council of Lindau
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Secretaries of the Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Basel answers St. Gallen regarding its inquiry of 24 October concerning the dispute between the apothecary Hans Störli and Dr. Johann Heinrich Schidtlin. The Basel visitors report that, according to Basel order, apothecaries must not be physicians and physicians must not run apothecaries. The letter of apprenticeship for Schidtlin is invalid, as he did not serve the usual time as an apprentice. Basel has investigated against Schidtlin regarding the misconduct.
en.sender: Statthalter of the Mayor's Thumb and the Council of the City of Basel
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the City of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the city of Basel to settle the dispute between the local apothecaries and the St. Gallen Doctor Johann Heinrich Schöbinger. They refer to a previous request of 29 October and ask Basel to hand over to Schöbinger the rights and documents due to him, so that he can open his apothecary.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Basel

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich invite Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to a conference in Arbon. The occasion is the complaints about foreign troop movements through the Confederation, in particular by Italian and Spanish war troops, which raise the price of grain and require watch duties. It is expected that further troops will pass through in the spring. The conference is to take place on Wednesday, the 12. January, in Arbon, to deliberate on countermeasures and a general Diet.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Appenzellers, who wished to investigate the exchange of Chur pfennigs and hallers by their countrymen. The St. Gallen authorities report that they had already prohibited the circulation of these coins and established strict penalties to prevent the outflow of small change. They ask the Appenzellers to secretly investigate and report the guilty parties so that they can be punished.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: The Appenzellers

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to review the use of Kurrpfennigen and Hallers in the exchange and to discontinue it if necessary. They report that they had forbidden the coins among their people, but that this would only be effective jointly with St. Gallen. Appenzell inquires about the nature of the coin and asks for an answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Burgomaster and Council of Basel to support the widow Katharina Muraltin in her petition for the return of a French contract or its replacement. The contract is in the hands of the Basel citizen Melchior Obmüller. The widow offers indemnification.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Basel

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the citizen of Strasbourg Sebastian Wagner has taken over the inheritance of the deceased woman of St. Gallen Richa Hüeber. Since the deceased's biological sister is still alive, she alone is entitled to the inheritance. Lindau requests St. Gallen to inform the parties of the day set for 24 January. Proceedings will continue regardless of attendance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Sebastian Mezger, Ehevogt of Ursula Hueberin, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene with the Council of Lindau so that his wife may take up the inheritance of her deceased sister Tristran Hueberin. He offers his house at the Weierholztor as security for the required bail or asks for guarantors. The inheritance amounts to 350 florins after deduction of the bequests.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Secret Burgomasters and Councillors of the city of St. Gallen request the Burgomaster and Secret Council of the city of Lindau to make their Captain or Engineer available to them for a day or somewhat longer. They intend to better defend their city and need the advice of an experienced Engineer, as they fear a Spanish passage through in the coming spring.
en.sender: Secret Burgomasters and Councillors of the city of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Secret Council of the city of Lindau

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the city of Lindau to make an engineer available to them for a day or a few days, who could help in the defense of the city. They justify this with the difficult times and the hostile attitude of the Bishop.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich thank Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen for the confidential report on the situation in Lindau. They request that they remain in good repute amidst the pending and strange events and keep each other informed. They await the results of the Confederate Diet taking place in Baden next Sunday and ask God for protection against misfortune.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and secret Council of the city of Lindau reply to a letter from the St. Gallen, who wanted to appoint the Lindau Statthalter Matthias Polen for the defense of their city. Lindau instead proposes Captain Adam Strauß von Freudenberg, as Polen had come under suspicion due to earlier contacts with the Lords of Steinach and Count Friedrich von Solms. Strauß lives in the countryside, visits St. Gallen regularly, and is an experienced engineer.
en.sender: Burgomaster and secret Council of the city of Lindau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and secret Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a report on the former Seckelmeister Lienhardt Wygman. He has complained in Memmingen about St. Gallen. Memmingen wishes to know how Wygman lived in St. Gallen, why he left the city, and how he behaved towards his wife.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ysen reply to the letter of the St. Gallen town rider concerning the new weaver master Conrad Weißenmann. They have questioned four dyer masters, who confirm that Weißenmann learned the dyer and weaver trades in Ysen and has always behaved honestly and uprightly. He has taken a good farewell. Ysen wishes him all the best.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and secret Council of Lindau reply to a letter of the 9th of the month. They cannot dispatch their citizen Captain Adam Danuß vom Heuwdenberg, as he, being an Austrian Landsass with property in Kärnten and residence near the Lordship of Bregenz, risks losing his income through political activities. Lindau instead proposes to commission the engineer Valentin Friderich from Basel, who has already contributed to the fortification of Lindau.
en.sender: Burgomaster and secret Council of Lindau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and secret Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Brulart replies to a letter of 30 January and declares that he will gladly pay out to St. Gallen in future the pensions of the King granted to his allies. He asks that a receipt be given to the town messenger so that the latter may receive the pension for the current year. He regrets that he could not pay earlier due to the high expenses in Frankreich in the previous year, and hopes for understanding.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Basel answers the request of the St. Gallen citizen Katharina Muraltin, who had turned to Basel in order to obtain a Vidimus of a French contract deposited with the Basel Professor Melchior de Insula. Basel communicates that it had informed itself with de Insula about the state of affairs and forwards the answer to the supplicant.
en.sender: Statthalter of the Burgomaster's Office and Council of the City of Basel
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen reply to an inquiry from St. Gallen regarding a legal dispute between the Memmingen citizen Gerwer Maister and the resident Konrad Wäsmann. They report that Wäsmann had married the daughter of the Memmingen citizen Bartholomäus Ringelin in Memmingen about thirteen years ago. As he could not stay there, he had moved to Essingen and later to St. Gallen. His wife had remained in Memmingen with her father. Wäsmann now wishes to take her to himself. His good conduct in St. Gallen is attested by certificates.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Advocate of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz write to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the unbearable and rapid scarcity of money in gold and silver coins. They ask to be informed what measures St. Gallen is seeking against this burden, whether an ordinance or valuation has been established there, and how high gold and silver coins are current there.
en.sender: Advocate of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform the Councils and Authorities in the Rheintal about the unforeseen rise in money and the resulting danger. They communicate that they have re-assessed the gold and silver coins, but have not yet made this public. They ask the recipients to keep the coins at their previous value and not to issue them at a higher value, so as not to burden the neighborhood.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Councils and Authorities in the Rheintal

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Lindau about the strong depreciation of money and ask for information on whether a coin valuation has taken place there and at what rate thaler and silver coins were circulating there. Furthermore, they request Lindau to instruct a wine seller serving there, who is said to have seduced a citizen in St. Gallen, to answer for this in St. Gallen, so that the honor of the citizen may be preserved.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: The Statthalter of the Bürgermeisterthumb and the Council of the city of Basel inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they had graciously permitted the citizen of St. Gallen Ulrich and his governess to stay in Basel. They are convinced that Ulrich will conduct himself as well as his abilities allow.
en.sender: Statthalter of the Bürgermeisterthumb and the Council of the city of Basel
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish an edict concerning the appointed general court day for the citizen Conrad Hassen of Lindau and his wife Katharina Schulerin. This is to be done so that creditors may assert their claims and no one is disadvantaged through ignorance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Caspar Koenig in a dispute over a ring purchase and the wine rent intercession of the deceased Christoph Caspar Zollikoffer. They refer to the attached supplication and the Landgericht decision and ask for a written answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Miron informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he has paid out an annual annuity to Herr Studer, which the King has granted them. He regrets not being able to fulfill their request in full, as it arrived too late. However, he promises to transmit another annual annuity with the next dispatch around Easter, although this is intended for other purposes. He asks for understanding and assures his continued friendliness towards the interests of the King.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau thank for the letter of 25. February along with the coin tax. They explain that, owing to the general coin confusion in the Empire, they do not make their own assessment but adjust to the neighbors. They refer to an upcoming meeting of the Imperial cities to discuss the coinage. Regarding Barbara Wincklerin, called Wagnerin, they have granted her time for consideration but urge her to give a prompt answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Arbon ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to protect the children of the deceased Zacharias Rüeger in their inheritance rights. The children claim the portion of the estate due to them from the estate of their stepmother Dorothea Andresin, who had lived with the deceased in a second marriage. Arbon appeals to its own city law and the city tax books, according to which Dorothea Andresin had brought into the marriage an amount worth 1700 gulden. The children had inherited nothing from the first marriage. Arbon asks St. Gallen to uphold the counter-right, as Arbon has done until now.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Council envoys of the cities of Straßburg, Frankfurt, Augsburg, Nürnberg and Ulm inform St. Gallen about the problems in the coinage and ask for consent to a provisional edict for the regulation of trade. They refer to the upcoming Frankfurt Lenten Fair and hope that St. Gallen observes the regulation in order to maintain the common trade.
en.sender: Council envoys of the cities of Straßburg, Frankfurt, Augsburg, Nürnberg and Ulm
en.recipient: Schultheiss, Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen thank for the letter of 28. February 1620 concerning the devaluation of money and the coinage ordinance. They explain that they could not order a fixed coinage ordinance in their city, but that buyers and sellers at the grain and corn market must themselves negotiate the acceptance of the coins. Should they in the future publish a final coinage tax, they would communicate this to St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau communicate to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen a provisional coinage edict issued by the envoys of the cities of Straßburg, Frankfurt, Augsburg, Nürnberg, and Ulm regarding the valuation of gold and silver coins. They ask for the return of the copy after a duplicate has been made, as they do not wish to publish it for the time being, but rather to await the stance of other cities.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have approved the provisional coinage edict of the free and imperial cities to remedy the defects in the coinage system. They ask St. Gallen to publish and observe the edict, so that the grain buyers of St. Gallen can comply with it.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The bailiff and Council of the city of Bischofzell request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel their citizen Martin Maurer to take over his brother-in-law Jacob Kürbender's two children and provide for them properly. Kürbender has gone into military service and his children are in great poverty. Bischofzell threatens to award the children to the mother if Maurer does not comply.
en.sender: The bailiff and Council of the city of Bischofzell
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich communicate that they cannot yet give a final answer to the inquiry of the Confederates of Schaffhausen regarding the coinage, as they are waiting to see how the coin edict will turn out at the Frankfurt Lenten Fair. They ask St. Gallen to avoid any further increase in the money until a joint consultation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the flight of Anna Zuberlienderin, wife of the St. Gallen citizen Lorenz Rietmann. They report that she had remained disobedient despite two requests to leave and is now imprisoned. They ask St. Gallen to question Rietmann and report in writing how the matter is to be handled, as she has accepted the citizenship of St. Gallen.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Appenzell for the release of Anna Zuberbüelerin, the wife of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Lorenz Rietmann. They ask Appenzell to investigate with the Weigl why she had threatened the Zuberbüerin with a woman and a horse, and for a report on the facts of the matter.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Ausserrhoden of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Wangen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish an edict concerning the appointed general court day for the creditors of the citizen of Wangen, Balthasar Dollinger. Since citizens of St. Gallen might be interested in the debtor, this is to ensure that no one is curtailed in their rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Franz Wyss in the collection of a debt of 280 gulden plus interest from Andres Bönnikhofer. The latter is expected in the city on the next Thursday. Wyss is to have his property arrested and appraised until he has paid.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Confederates inform the Council of St. Gallen about a meeting in Baden, at which they discussed the claims of their former citizen Hans Halder. Since Halder, despite admonition and brief imprisonment, persists in his undertaking, he was banished from the city and the judicial district. The Confederates ask St. Gallen not to support Halder in his matters.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the Künerin in an inheritance dispute between Maria Magdalena Künerin and the children of Löwy Rotschachen. It concerns a child's share that her deceased husband Zacharias Küner had inherited from his first wife. The stepchildren claim a share, which the Künerin disputes. Zürich asks for support so that the Künerin remains protected under the inheritance law of St. Gallen and the claim of the stepchildren is rejected.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the widow Benigna Krafftin in the dispute over the testament of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Martin Schlumpf. The Schlumpf heirs demand that the widow's life annuity be covered from her own assets, which contradicts the testament. Ulm asks that the widow be maintained in the execution of the testament and that no concessions be forced upon her.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the St. Gallen Othmar Boumgarter was killed in their hospital by a journeyman with a stab wound. The perpetrator has not been identified. Bern sends the report and the pass of the deceased, so that St. Gallen can inform his heirs.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Rudolf Sonnenberg, Landvogt in Thurgau, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the citizen of St. Gallen Jacob Köchler to adhere to the contract concluded with his sister-in-law Margarethe Mayer. Therein Köchler has obligated himself to pay 1000 gulden and to settle the remaining claims. The citizen of St. Gallen Lorenz Zollikofer has obligated himself as guarantor. Sonnenberg requests that the guarantee be left untouched until the settlement.
en.sender: Hans Rudolf Sonnenberg, Landvogt in upper and lower Thurgau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: R. Vigorz informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he cannot currently fulfill their request for a pension. The money that recently arrived consists of remainders from the previous year and is intended for the payment of the remaining colonels and captains, who are still outstanding from the first transports for the pensions of the allies. Furthermore, the money is under the seal of the General Treasurer, who is on the way. He promises that with the next supply of money in the current year, St. Gallen will be among the first cities served, and asks for forgiveness.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Schultheiss and Council of Bern not to burden their citizen and butcher Konrad Reiner with the new levy of the Trachtengeld. Reiner has traded in livestock in Bern's territory for years and has only paid the usual toll and the Gleitgeld. The St. Gallen authorities request that he be left with the previous levies and that his goods be allowed to pass quietly.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Bern

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for their letter of the 12th of the month. They regret the hostile incursions of the Pündter into the Pündten, to Thurn and Tell, but rejoice that these have again been driven out of the land. Furthermore, they report that two companies of mercenaries, who have arrived on foot, have been stationed on Blumenberg and in Montafon.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen mourn the death of the citizen Kaspar Rainer, the brother of the recipient. They ask Melchior Rainer to send a proxy or to authorize one in writing, so that the inheritance of the deceased, which is partly located in St. Gallen, can be arranged and distributed. Otherwise, the heirs fear damages and suspicion.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Melchior Rainer, Stadtrichter zu Kaschau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the confidential report on incidents in the Pünzten. They ask that such information continue to be sent, as trade could unfortunately continue to decline and the neighbors must remain vigilant. Lindau declares itself ready to make similar reports.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Statthalter and Council of the Land of Glarus for their Confederate assurance to protect the County of Werdenberg. They offer, in turn, to assist Glarus with advice and action if needed. Since St. Gallen lies on the border and is itself endangered, they request that Glarus keep a watchful eye and provide help in an emergency.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of the Land of Glarus

en.regest: Leopold, Archduke of Österreich, President and Chamber Councillor, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to ensure that Hans Jakob and Ulrich Schlapperitz promptly settle the outstanding debt of 294 gulden and 43 kreuzer from the salt office to the former salt factor Georg Rauner.
en.sender: Leopold, Archduke of Österreich, President and Chamber Councillor
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Thomas Freiherr von Ehrenfels zu Haldenstein complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the attachment of a lien on his coins (Dicken and Halbdicken), which were seized under the pretext of being too light. He refers to his imperial minting privilege, according to which his coins are valid in the Empire, and asks for the lifting of the lien. He says that he has sent the nobleman Hartmann von Salis to St. Gallen to report on the circumstances, and hopes for an amicable settlement.
en.sender: Thomas Freiherr von Ehrenfels zu Haldenstein
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizen Bartholomäus Schöbinger, who inherits 4000 gulden from a testament of the widow Elisabeth Schirmerin, in the collection of the sum and the settlement of the inheritance. They request lenient treatment regarding taxation and duties, so that Schöbinger may feel the claim acutely.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Glarus ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their fellow citizen Susanne Altman in the inheritance dispute concerning the estate of her deceased brother. They request the St. Gallen authorities to support the fellow citizen Hans Jacob Hiltner, sent by Glarus, in this matter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Rorschach ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Peter Kessler. He has for a long time sold on the St. Gallen market on Saturdays, until the Smiths' Guild prevented him and took his little stool. Kessler wants to complain to St. Gallen. Rorschach requests that they help him to his right without payment and treat him not as a stranger, but as their resident (Hintersasse).
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report that three-batzen coins are frequently smuggled into their city, causing harm to the common people. They state that they had secured a number of such coins from a Bartholomäus Homona from the Milanese. As they cannot examine these themselves, they ask St. Gallen to test the coins for their authenticity and communicate the result, in order to counteract the abuse.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of the city of Lindau thank St. Gallen for the examination of Reichstaler-Dreikreuzer and the report of the coin administrator. Since new types of Sechsbatzner appear daily and the Savoyard pieces sent along are suspicious, they ask St. Gallen to have these also examined by their coin administrator and to send the report by this week. They promise to reimburse the expenses and to oblige themselves in other matters.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Lindau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the city of Lindau dated 2 September. They have instructed their coin officials to examine the Bavarian six-batzen coins. They send the result of the examination regarding fineness and value to the city of Lindau in an accompanying report.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Lindau

en.regest: The Council of the city of Bischofszell, at the request of the St. Gallen schoolmaster and citizen, confirms that the Rheineckerin Margaretha Lamparteri was lawfully begotten by the honest parents Michael Lamparteri and Anna née Bürgin. They report on the promised dowry of 200 gulden and ask St. Gallen to take the bride under its protection.
en.sender: Council of the city of Bischofszell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to the Landvogt of Frauenfeld about a dispute between Hans Jaelgen von Allmishausen and Jakob Schlatter von Rossrüti, which had begun in St. Gallen with insults. Schlatter says that he did not appear despite a court order, as he claims the protection of the von der Linden. The St. Gallen ask the Landvogt to hold the Diet scheduled for the last day of the month of October and to decide the matter.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt of Frauenfeld

en.regest: Hans Konrad von Roll, Landvogt in Thurgau, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a written report on the names and deeds of those persons whom Andreas Behamg von Lindau, who was tried in St. Gallen, is supposed to have named under torture as accomplices in crimes. He needs these details in order to be able to proceed against the accused as their superior officer.
en.sender: Hans Konrad von Roll, Landvogt in Upper and Lower Thurgau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter of the 9th of the same month. They state that they know nothing of winter quarters or approaching troops. They merely mention that last week about 60 persons on horseback and on foot passed through Vadensky to accompany the body of a young Prince of Lorraine who had been shot in Böhmen. They do not suspect that winter quarters are intended, but promise to make further inquiries and to report confidentially to Lindau.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Landvogt to waive the threatened penalty against Hospital Ammann Georg Stähelin and his co-witnesses for the witness examination in the case between Hans Jagkhen and Jacob Schlatter. They refer to the old custom that the subjects of the court of Allmensperg present themselves in St. Gallen for information, and emphasize that the examination does no harm to the Landvogt.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hand over a copy of the testament or inventory of the estate of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen, Hans Müller, to the citizen of Konstanz, Sebastian Schelpe. They promise to act in a neighborly manner in similar cases.
en.sender: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Emanuel von Roll, Landvogt in Upper and Lower Thurgau, transmits to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the statements of three witnesses regarding a dispute over household linen between Hans Juchsen von Almensberg and Jacob Schlatter von Fürstenrüti. The witnesses confirm that Schlatter had settled his accounts with his mother, and report on insults by the Wagner. Von Roll asks for peaceful restraint.
en.sender: Emanuel von Roll, Landvogt in Upper and Lower Thurgau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter of 13 November. They explain that they could not prevent the increase in coin rates, as this had become customary in the neighbourhood and in the Empire. They had therefore adapted to the neighbouring cantons and taxed certain coin types, while others could be traded freely. The rates are attached.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform them which gold and silver coins are current there and at what rate they are issued or withdrawn. They refer to a recently printed list, which is no longer up to date, and ask for a written statement of the values.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich write to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the coinage ordinance agreed upon in 1619 is not being observed and that the denominations are rising daily, which leads to great burden on the countryside. They ask for information on how St. Gallen is disposed in this regard, in order to jointly work towards a permanent tax ordinance and to prevent the increasing burden.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the intervention of the Landvogt in the Rheintal for the Jews Salomon and Elia in Rheineck. They recall that the Jews were expelled because of usury and the violation of the prohibition to show themselves in the city. They refer to the old statute not to tolerate Jews and adhere to it. They offer the Landvogt neighborly friendship in other matters.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Johann Zimmermann, Hauptmann and Council of the city of Luzern, Landvogt in the Rheintal

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Landvogt in Thurgau to remit the penalty imposed on the St. Gallen hospital amman Georg Stachelin. Stachelin had entered the jurisdiction of the court of Allmensberg despite a prohibition by the Landvogt, who had previously dismissed a complaint against Jacob Schlatter. The St. Gallen refer to the long-standing custom whereby citizens of both sides were permitted to stay in the jurisdiction of the other without being punished. They ask for leniency for the preservation of good neighborly relations.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt in Thurgau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have published the coin edict from the coin probation day in Augsburg and ordered their citizens to observe the established exchange rates for gold and silver coins. They ask for neighborly consideration and show themselves ready for further friendship.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landvogt Johann Zimmermann in the Rintal asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to treat the Jews Salomon and Elias in Rinegg, who have fallen into disgrace because of money-changing and were banished from the city, amicably. He requests that they be granted free passage, as they intend to conduct themselves properly in the future and submit to punishment in the event of complaints.
en.sender: Johann Zimmermann, Landvogt in the Rintal
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Schultheiss, Burgomaster and Council of Ogersheim about the death of their fellow citizen Kaspar Steiner. Since he left no legitimate heirs, a division of his estate is scheduled for 22 January 1621. They ask Ogersheim to report whether Elisabetha Scheifferin lives there and whether she is still alive. If she wishes to assert inheritance claims, she is to appear in St. Gallen by 20 January 1621.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss, Burgomaster and Council of Ogersheim

en.regest: Hans Rudolf Rahn asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant grace and forgiveness to his brother-in-law Christoph Scherrer. He says that the latter has suffered in exile for over eight years and is elderly and poor. Rahn requests that Scherrer be allowed to live in St. Gallen with his family, and asks the creditors for forbearance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern inform the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen about the rising devaluation of money and the import of inferior coins. To avert damage, they have decreed that in Bern only Confederate coins with the corresponding stamp are to be accepted and issued. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to leave their coins at their previous value and not to weaken them, so that they are not forced to take similar measures.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform the city of Winterthur about the death of their fellow citizen Caspar Nemitz and the division of his inheritance scheduled for 21 January. Since the citizens of Winterthur Jacob Schallenberg, Jacob Solzer and Magdalena Oettliugerij could be heirs, they ask Winterthur to inform them of the date. They are to appear with valid inheritance certificates, otherwise the division will be continued without them.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Winterthur

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a meeting with Luzern and Zug in Zug regarding the unsettled coinage. They request a written report on the coinage ordinance existing in St. Gallen as well as on its administration by the mint master and the Gwardin, in order to promote a common ordinance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report that, together with other cantons, they held a conference regarding the unequal coinage in Zug and agreed on a tax order for gold and silver coins. They send a copy of this agreement and ask St. Gallen for its opinion and decision, so that the order can be printed and published in the name of the assembled cantons, also including Schaffhausen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Beyer, Pfälzischer Amtsvogt des Amtes Neustadt, informs Jacob Preißer, Tuchschere zu Kuba, about an inquiry from the Council of St. Gallen. The Council had asked whether the children and grandchildren of the deceased Schultheiss Jacob Phlierer from Ögersheim are related to the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Caspar Reiner. Beyer states that Reiner could inherit if he proves his kinship. He asks Preißer to meet him in Neustadt to clarify the kinship and discuss the journey.
en.sender: Johann Beyer, Pfälzischer Amtsvogt des Amtes Neustadt
en.recipient: Jacob Preißer, Tuchschere zu Kuba

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish an edict concerning the appointed general court day for the creditors of the deceased citizen of Lindau Hans Peter Löwen and his widow Maria Zangmeisterin. They request this measure so that no one be curtailed in their rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Bern for the communication of the Confederates regarding the coinage question. They state that they have prohibited foreign coins by edicts in order to protect trade. Furthermore, they report that the thaler in St. Gallen already counts for 2 gulden 20 kreuzer, and ask Bern to take this into consideration. They wish Bern peace and prosperity.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Bern

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Frankfurt am Main inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the General Lieutenant of the Union, Joachim Ernst, Margrave of Brandenburg, at the request of Frankfurt, has guaranteed the safety of the merchants for the upcoming Lenten Fair. They enclose a copy of the corresponding order, according to which the imperial army is to allow the traders to pass freely from 10 March to 7 April.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of Frankfurt am Main
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Christof Scherer, who lives in Switzerland after a loss in Piemont. His wife and children are already in St. Gallen. They request that Scherer be supported in his return to St. Gallen and in the settlement of his debts, so that he may live with his family again.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Burgomaster and Council of Winterthur that the date set for the division of the estate of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen, Kaspar Kamms, could not take place because of disputing heirs. They ask Winterthur to refer their citizens Jakob Keltzen and Jakob Schellenberg, who are called as heirs, to 15 March and to cause them to appear the day before with a certified document regarding the inheritance right of the city or to send authorized lawyers. Otherwise, the division will be continued without them.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Winterthur

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich remind Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of the agreement reached in Zug regarding the value of the coinage as well as the content and weight of the coins. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to adhere to the agreed values when minting in St. Gallen, in order to avoid further complaints, and expect a reply.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The examiners appointed by Kempten report that citizens of Kempten brought old silver and silver tableware to St. Gallen in the last three to four years and had thaler struck there, which they then brought back to Kempten. There, they had these thaler melted down into inferior three-penny pieces and kreuzer. They ask St. Gallen for a list of the names, the quantities of silver delivered, and the numbers of thaler received, in order to clarify the matter.
en.sender: Martin Geiger, Jacob Kleinhanß and Zacharias Jenisch
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to Burgomaster and Council of Stuttgart that the son of the local goldsmith Hans Georg Kreutz, Daniel Kranich, is seriously ill. The Kranich family is poor and unable to bear the costs of care. St. Gallen has already granted 12 gulden from the hospital and asks Stuttgart to also help the sick man out of pity.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Stuttgart

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform the heir of the deceased Melchior Reinacher about the settlement of the estate. They name the assets taken over by the heir in the value of 3000 gulden as well as the assumption of a debt of 300 gulden. They ask for confirmation of the satisfaction of this claim.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Noble, Honorable Sir, Heir of the deceased Melchior Reinacher

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Secret Council of Lindau inform the Burgomaster and Secret Council of St. Gallen that they have learned that on the same evening a cavalry of 500 horses will march into Lindau and is to proceed to Bregenz and Feldkirch. They share this news out of neighborly friendship.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Secret Council of Lindau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Secret Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the transmitted information. They state that the Baden Tagleistung was cancelled because of the seven papal cantons. Instead, a meeting of the four evangelical cities and the Land of Appenzell has been set for next Monday in Aarau. They hope that the French envoy Montolon can clarify the Pünzter matter in Solothurn. The Burgomaster of Zürich, Hans Heinrich Holzhäuser, will report further to St. Gallen during his transit.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the information regarding the grain purchase prohibited by the Pünthers and the arrival of Archduke Leopold in Konstanz. They have requested the Archduke in writing to lift the prohibition. Zürich offers St. Gallen its support and asks for reciprocity.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Proconsul and Consuls of the city of Posen recommend Barbara Gerber, the widow of the seal engraver Valentin Rewelt, to the Proconsul and Consuls of the city of St. Gallen. Barbara is a woman of St. Gallen and the heir of her deceased parents. She is travelling with her husband to St. Gallen to receive her inheritance. The men of Posen ask that the couple be assisted in the recovery of the goods.
en.sender: Proconsul and Consuls of the city of Posen
en.recipient: Proconsul and Consuls of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Lindau, Konstanz, Überlingen, Memmingen and Wangen that they are cancelling the Pentecost market, which was to begin on 12 May, on account of moving causes. They ask the recipients to inform their citizens of this, so that they may arrange themselves accordingly.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Councils of Lindau, Konstanz, Überlingen, Memmingen and Wangen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the friendly support in the introduction of the new bailiff to Sax and Forstegg as well as for the benevolent answer to their request. They offer to return this and ask to persist in this good will of the Confederates and, in view of the current dangerous circumstances, to look after Zürich.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rottachzell reply to a letter from the St. Gallen, who, because of an imperial and grand-ducal order not to let grain and munition pass into the three Phünten of the Engadin, ask for tolerance in the purchase of grain. Rottachzell declares that they must obey the order literally and cannot make any exceptions. They ask St. Gallen to clarify the matter at higher places and promise to forward the answer to other interested parties.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the discovery of inferior coins in their territory. They report that the citizen of Zürich, Hans Jakob Füßlin, upon passing through on his way to Leipzig, had handed over 70 Spanish ducats to the St. Gallen resident Heinrich Zollikofer, for which he wanted to receive Dreibatzner or half Dickpfennige. Instead, inferior Haldensteinische coins had been delivered. Zürich asks St. Gallen to inquire with the persons mentioned and to report the result to the sent messenger, in order to prevent the evil.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have appointed a joint court day for their emigrated citizen Nikolaus Haberstock. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to publicly post and publish the edict, so that any creditors among the citizens of St. Gallen may assert their claims.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to Lindau on the discovery of bad coins in their city. Jakob Soler, who comes from Herisau, admitted to having obtained the coins from the Eppeleisch writing office in Lindau. The coins are too light. St. Gallen requests Lindau to inquire with the Eppeleisch writing office how long and on what basis they had traded with Soler, and asks for a report to the St. Gallen messenger.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report on the shortage of coinage. Amadeo Eggolt had exchanged Chur three-kreuzer pieces for thaler with Jacob Schoch from Herisau, without writing down the sums. Since the Confederate three-kreuzer pieces were lacking, Grienningen three-kreuzer pieces from Schwaben and Franconia had also been smuggled into Lindau. Lindau had not wanted to prevent this, so as not to affect St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the city of Zürich to refund to their citizen Konrad Steiner, butcher, the money confiscated by the bailiff of Wangen. Steiner says that he bought cattle in the bailiwick of Wangen and paid with coin current in St. Gallen, which he had received at the exchange. The bailiff says that he confiscated the money because he does not want to refund it without the consent of the authority. St. Gallen requests Zürich to issue a certificate to Steiner that the coin was acquired through exchange and not through bill exchange, and to act with the bailiff of Wangen for the repayment.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that a sum of money in three sorts of Dreibeiners has arrived in their city. Due to concern over possibly false coins, they have had them held. They request the St. Gallen authorities to have the two sorts examined by their coin warden at Lindau's expense and to report the result to them.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to Landvogt Leonhard Holzhalb that in the camps of Zürich at Maienfeld and Pfäffers rumors were circulating about an impending attack by the Leopoldians on the Bündner. They ask him for a written report on whether this is known to him and what the situation actually is.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Leonhard Holzhalb, Council of the city of Zürich and Landvogt of the lordship of Hochsax

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen dispatch their Council member and colleague Dr. Sebastian Schöbinger to the Council envoys of the cities of Zürich, Bern, Basel and Schaffhausen in Baden for a matter that is important to the city and citizenry. They request the envoys to hear Schöbinger and to respond favorably to his petition.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Council envoys of the cities of Zürich, Bern, Basel and Schaffhausen in Baden

en.regest: The thirteen cantons ask St. Gallen and Chur to accept and publish the coinage ordinance decided upon in Zug. This ordinance regulates the valuation of gold and silver coins, forbids foreign schillings and insufficient twoers and half-kreuzer, and suspends coins down to the batzen for three months. The ordinance enters into force on 1. August. Bern, Freiburg, Solothurn and Basel have referred the acceptance to their lords.
en.sender: Cities and lands of the thirteen cantons
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the Landammann and Council of the upper part of the Land of Appenzell to participate in a neighboring conference on 30 July 1621 on the Pfaffentz. The aim is to jointly consult on measures against the harmful coinage, in order to establish a uniform value for gold and silver coins, to keep good coins in the land and to abolish bad ones.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the upper part of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen invite Landammann and Council of Appenzell to a neighborly meeting on 11 July 1621 at 8 o'clock at the Pfalzentz. The occasion is the difficult coinage situation. They wish to consult on common measures to establish an equal value and tax for gold and silver coins within the borders, to keep good coins in the country, to abolish bad ones, and to prevent the harmful exchange. They ask for the dispatch of Council messengers with full authority and power.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen remind Genf of an outstanding debt of 4000 Sonnenkronen including interest. They have commissioned their fellow citizen Daniel Studern to collect the claim and ask the Genfer authorities to assist him in this.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Syndics, Burgomaster and Council of Genf

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report that they have received the letter of intercession from St. Gallen for the citizen Daniel Stauder there. They have presented Stauder's supplication to the widow and the heirs of the deceased Lindau Council member Thomas Schwarz. However, these refuse the support and do not ask Stauder for help. Lindau forwards the counter-report of the Schwarzs to St. Gallen, so that Stauder may take note of it.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and the five secret councillors of the city of Schaffhausen ask the Burgomaster and the secret councillors of the city of St. Gallen to report to them in writing how and with what order they arrange their mint, what they give the workers as wages, what these must earn from the mint work in their lease, and how it stands with the deduction for shot and other things.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and the five secret councillors of the city of Schaffhausen
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and the secret councillors of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Winterthur for its offer to move the citizen Christoph Steuffel there to the court day. Since Steuffel has not appeared until now, the St. Gallen authorities set a peremptory court day for Friday, the 9. October, in the town hall. They request Winterthur to notify Steuffel of the date and to cause him to appear personally or through authorized representatives, so that the long-standing dispute can be settled.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur

en.regest: Administrator of the Hauptmannschaft, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz reply to a letter of 21 July. They complain about the burdensome coinage and the ring-containing gold sorts and promise to strive for their improvement. Regarding the desired report on the Montweigen-Deubländer, they state that Council member Georg Dobelin is not currently at home, but is taking a spa cure, which is why the request cannot yet be handled.
en.sender: Administrator of the Hauptmannschaft, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen confirm the receipt of a reply from Winterthur regarding the excuse of the citizen Christoph Stäheli there. They have communicated the letter to their citizen Sebastian Kröung. Since the documents mentioned in the supplication have not yet been submitted, no decision could be given to the supplicant. St. Gallen asks Winterthur to order Stäheli to appear before the Council on 29 August to clarify the matter and submit the requested documents.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur

en.regest: Heinrich Hußmann, Substitut of the Chancery in Baden, answers town clerk Melchior Güldin of St. Gallen regarding his inquiry concerning the former bookkeeper Caspar Meyer. He says that Meyer laid down his office in the last annual account and transferred the guardianship over his children to Andreas Thoen and Christoph Beuchheller. The Lords Envoys confirmed this guardianship. Meyer is thereby bound in his actions.
en.recipient: Melchior Güldin

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur reply to a letter of 28 July. Their citizen Christoph Büchholzer has excused himself and taken the matter into his own hands. He has agreed with his brother-in-law Caspar Meyer on two important points and promoted the affair himself. Winterthur does not take up the matter, as it rests with Büchholzer himself.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene in a dispute between Adriana Francisca Freiin von der Hohen Sax, a citizen of St. Gallen, and the former town clerk of St. Gallen, Zülj. It concerns an account for the administration of inheritance in the Netherlands. The city of Zürich asks for an amicable settlement or, if necessary, for a just judgment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen answer an inquiry from the Confederates of Schaffhausen regarding the coinage ordinance. They set out the organization of the coinage administration, the duties of the administrators, the master of the mint and the workers, as well as the accounting. They explain that the mint was established not out of a desire for profit, but to ward off bad coins and to protect the linen trade.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen

en.regest: Caspar Müller von Schwyz, bailiff of Bischofzell, asks Burgomaster Joachim Reuter of St. Gallen to ensure that the orphan Elisabeth Brün, daughter of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Jakob Brün, does not stay with the widow of the deceased Gervin Jäcklin in St. Gallen. She went to St. Gallen without the knowledge of her guardian Heinrich Rietmann. Müller requests that the orphan be sent back to her guardian and that she be kept under the protection of the higher court in case of resistance.
en.sender: Caspar Müller von Schwyz, bailiff of Bischofzell
en.recipient: Joachim Reuter, Burgomaster of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their grain merchants and boatmen to register at the Konstanzer Kaufhaus when passing through the Untersee. This is done to comply with the orders of the authorities not to let any goods, supplies, or ammunition pass to the Bündner, and to avoid disturbances.
en.sender: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The bailiff and Council of Bischofzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to retrieve their citizen Elisabeth Thumann, who has eluded her guardian Heinrich Riedmann and is lodged with the widow of the deceased Darius Jägkann in St. Gallen. They request that Elisabeth be handed over to her guardian within eight to ten days or that she be given other suitable accommodation. They threaten to use the usual means against disobedience in case of further refusal.
en.sender: The bailiff and Council of Bischofzell
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the envoys of the eight cantons of the Confederation, who govern the Lordship of Rheintal, at the conference day in Lindau, to kindly hear their citizen and hospital clerk Johannes Zilli in his complaints against the people of Rheintal and to help him in his matter. Zilli wishes to present the matter in the annual accounts of Rheintal in Lindau.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Envoys of the eight cantons of the Confederation, who govern the Lordship of Rheintal, at the conference day in Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report that the Confederates in the Pünden are in danger because of the Spanish Milanese capitulation and wanted to raise three banners. They ask St. Gallen to help the Pünden with force and assistance in order to preserve the common freedom.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The sender reports on the interrogation of the city's Jews, in particular Helias, regarding a silver transaction. Helias stated that on Wednesday he had sold 22 Loth of silver at 16 batzen per Loth. Five days later, on Thursday, he had brought silver again, which after weighing weighed 31 Loth, whereupon the buyer accepted it as 24 Loth. Helias had accepted this and told his brother-in-law Salomon in Hebrew that he should pick up the money for 24 Loth by Sunday. The silver, which weighed 37 Loth, had been brought to the sender. The sender asks for further instructions.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, on the order of Archduke Leopold, they had prohibited the passage of victuals and munitions for the Pünzner. They report that the St. Gallen doctor Johann Heinrich Schädler had transported metal and grain to St. Gallen, although he claims to have bought them for the city. The grain is stored in Konstanz. The Konstanzer ask for a written explanation of whether Schädler bought the goods for the city and whether they are still in St. Gallen.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Caspar Graf zu Hohenems asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to release the town physician Sebastian Schöbinger there for a short time, so that he may stand by the Count in an advisory capacity regarding his health complaints. He promises to serve St. Gallen in similar cases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Landammann and Council of Appenzell. They declare themselves willing to participate in a meeting of the three neighboring authorities to discuss the problems with the coinage. They report that they had already decided in a conference with the Prelate of St. Gallen to rate the thaler 1½ and the Confederate coin 30 kreuzer higher and to prohibit inferior coins. They will send envoys to the discussed meeting.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell complain about the growing irregularities in the valuation of silver crowns and Reichsthaler, which lead to great disadvantages for the common man. They ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen whether it would be useful to summon the neighboring authorities to a new meeting in order to find a uniform currency valuation, or whether there is a common rate to which everyone could adhere. They request a written answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request their Confederates in Basel to compel the Professor Melchior de Insula to deposit a French contract with a Vidimus, which belongs to their citizen Katharina Werrettin, with the authorities and to have it read publicly. They ask that the document be kept safely in the Basel chancery until the conclusion of the legal dispute.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Basel

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from Appenzell Innerrhoden of 27 September 1632 concerning the coinage. They state that they had remained with the agreed coinage rate, had prohibited Churer half-talers and foreign three-batzen coins, and had set Basler half-gulden at 36 kreuzer. They ask Appenzell to continue the minting of smaller coins, so that the money remains in the country and is not exchanged by usurers. They have ordered their market managers to proceed against such traders.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell Innerrhoden

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell confirm the receipt of St. Gallen's response regarding the coinage. They declare their intention to observe the latest coinage ordinance, but request that the mint master continue with the minting of batzen and other lower denominations and that the coin buyers mint as good and correct money as possible, in order to support the poor man. Appenzell offers in return neighborly services.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a request by the citizen of St. Gallen Gregorius Tobler, who has a claim against the citizen of Lindau Michael Gurgel. Tobler had Gurgel arrested because the latter had not paid with bills of exchange of St. Gallen. Gurgel came out of custody. Lindau instructs Gurgel to either pay according to the handwriting or to submit himself to custody again.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau forward to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the written report of their citizen, the wife of Hans Michael Meügel. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to instruct their Appenzell citizen to settle with the Lindauers in the proposed manner and to pay.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to investigate the perpetrators of defamatory rumors concerning the Burgomaster of Zürich, Hans Rudolf Rahn, and to report the results to them in writing. Rahn wishes to defend himself against the slander. In the postscript of 16 November 1601, the Zürichers ask for news about the situation in the Pünden and for special attention to the lordship of Sax.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about the tense situation in the Pünden, where Leopoldic troops are stationed in the County of Sargans and violence threatens the Lordship of Sax. They ask St. Gallen to keep a watchful eye on the Lordship of Sax and to provide assistance in case of emergency. In the postscript, they thank them for the transmitted letters and ask for further reports.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur that they have set a court day for 29 November in the legal case of the Winterthur citizen Christoph Studheler against the St. Gallen Sebastian Krommen. They request Winterthur to inform Studheler of this date and to ensure that he appears unencumbered and with the necessary power of attorney.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur

en.regest: Ammann and Court of Kempten request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post an edict concerning a court day set for the St. Gallen citizen Thomas Haneraten. This is to be done so that any St. Gallen creditors who have claims against Haneraten may learn of it and assert their rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from Count von Hohenems concerning the apothecary Marx Haltmeier, who is held captive in Lustnaw. They report that Haltmeier, under oath, stated that the root collector Jacob Rüetmann had handed him wolfsbane to pound. Rüetmann later brought the root back mixed with sulfur, which Haltmeier noticed. He thereupon warned Rüetmann and withheld the root until Rüetmann brought the rest.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Caspar Graf zu Hohenems, Glarus und Vaduz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the letter of the Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Liechtenstein regarding the imprisoned citizen of St. Gallen, Marx Haltmeier. They report that Haltmeier, under oath, testified how he had sold wolfsbane to the Liechtenstein resident Hans Liebmann. Liebmann had ground the root and mixed it into his grain, which led to a complaint by the miller. Haltmeier had stated that he sold the root as harmless, as he himself did not possess any Stössel. The St. Gallen authorities ask for further inquiries.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Liechtenstein

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report on the complaints of the citizens of Wangen, Joachim and Kaspar Daniel Zollikofer, against the factor Mathias Ebneter. He had added excessive thaler on exchange bills in Bayern and Ingolstadt. The Zollikofer suspect that Ebneter wants to remit the coins to Venedig in order to evade the complaint there. St. Gallen declares that it will confiscate and coin secret coins within its jurisdiction, and offers to support the people of Wangen in similar cases.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Wangen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Wangen inform St. Gallen that their citizen Mathias Ebert has smuggled bad three-batzen coins into the city. Ebert claims that the coins came from the merchants Joachim, Lorenz and David Zolligkoffer in Augsburg via the Buroner to Wangen. Wangen asks St. Gallen to question the Zolligkoffer and report whether they had actually received the bad coins, in order to be able to punish Ebert if necessary.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz reply to a letter from the St. Gallen bookbinder, in which he reported on a recently committed excess by citizens of St. Gallen. They report that on the evening of St. Martin's Day, some relatives of St. Gallen had carried out fistfights in the inn. Since the perpetrators have already been punished and the penalty paid, they do not wish to pursue the matter further and ask that this be understood as well-meant.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Caspar Graf zu Hohen-Embs, Gallara und Vaduz asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to interrogate and examine under oath the Alsatian Ardeggen, whether he had given his subject Jacob Riedtman poisonous roots, without mentioning their poisonous nature. Riedtman had had the roots ground at the Holzmühle, whereby flour was poisoned and three persons were killed. The Count asks for a sealed answer.
en.sender: Caspar Graf zu Hohen-Embs, Gallara und Vaduz
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich invite Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to a Confederate assembly on 30. Dezember 1621 in Zürich. They warn of Spanish troops marching from Mailand into Switzerland, and ask for resolutions on common defense and mutual aid. In a postscript, they inform that an envoy of Archduke Leopold von Österreich has arrived, and refer to his letter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen share with the Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of the City of Zürich Appenzell a letter from the Governor and Parliament of Dole in the County of Burgundy concerning the Mansfeld troops. They confirm that they continue to feel bound by the hereditary union and the maintenance of peace.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of the City of Zürich Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich communicate to the Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell a letter from the Governor and Parliament of Dole in the County of Burgundy. This is addressed to the Confederation regarding the Mansfeld troops. Zürich declares that it has answered the Governor, stating that it will forward the letter to the Confederates and will continue to act in accordance with the settlement of the inheritance and strive for peace.
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rottach ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to urge their fellow citizen Johann Gabriel Bluenegger, the Obervogt of Liechtenstein, through his citizens, the brothers, to pay an outstanding balance for linen. Bluenegger had already asked for help a year and a half ago but was put off. Now he must submit his account to the lordship and urgently needs the money.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant their citizen Hieronymus Spengler the enjoyment of his share of the inheritance of Jacob Rambsauer, who died in St. Gallen. Spengler has registered as an heir and must now prove his kinship. Konstanz asks for a document stating that in St. Gallen, in cases of inheritance between citizens and strangers, no distinction is made.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the request of the Innern Rhoden to again accept whole and half Dicken of the Confederates. They explain that they had prohibited the new Schaffhauser Dicken because of their low silver content, in order to protect the common man. The old Schaffhauser Dicken would continue to be accepted, however with a deduction of nine kreuzer and one Pfennig. They ask for a confidential reply.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of the Innern Rhoden of the Land Abbenzell

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Appenzell request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to insist upon the mint officials that Confederate whole and half thaler be accepted at the agreed rate. This is to apply until a permanent agreement is reached among the neighboring authorities at the upcoming Confederate Diet in Baden or elsewhere.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Georg von Kirchberg to compensate their citizen Hans Melchior Heuwman for his unpaid expenses and services as well as for the damage from the undelivered grain delivery of 200 Metzen to Lindau. They refer to Heuwman's oral and written reports as well as to the report of the Mint Administrator Christoph Schlappritz.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Georg von Kirchberg

en.regest: The envoys of Archduke Leopold zu Österreich ask the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich to reduce the number of herbs purchased abroad and to issue a regulation to prevent the damage caused by the herb war. They further demand that the prices for patient care in the hospital be adjusted and that the buyers deliver the herbs at their place of residence. The envoys expect a reply.
en.sender: Director and secret councillors of Archduke Leopold zu Österreich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to refrain from further purchasing of grain for the city and the hospital. They justify this with the severe grain shortage in Schwaben and the danger that the supply to Lindau might cease. Lindau is being pressed by Österreich and the common man to take measures so that the grain is used for daily needs rather than for stocks.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel their citizen Hans Melchior Heinemann to fulfill his obligation towards the citizens of St. Gallen David and Nicolaus Güller. Heinemann had obligated himself to pay a debt or to return a horse, but did not appear despite reminders. Konstanz asks for official support.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich send Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen copies of the new coinage regulation, which was agreed upon at the latest Baden Diet. They ask for publication and strict adherence to the regulation, in order to maintain good order and to prevent further complaints.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Schultheiss and Council of Tuttlingen to notify their citizen Georg Stauder of the peremptory court day on 12 March and to compel him to appear in person or through an authorized representative. Stauder had not complied with two previous dates due to an arrest. In the event of further absence, judgment will be rendered based on the appearance of the opponent Hans Meger von Arbon.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Tuttlingen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to order their citizen Sebastian Höggern to either return a half piece of leek-green Lindau cloth to the citizen of Nürnberg Mauritz Buhle or to pay the amount of 107 ½ florins together with costs and damages. Buhle has complained in writing and requested intercession.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to summon the citizen of St. Gallen Heinrich Schritlin by authority. He has been awarded a fine for an offense committed in Konstanz, but has not paid it despite promises and admonitions. The people of Konstanz ask for neighborly help so that Schritlin pays the fine and keeps his promise.
en.sender: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Imperial Hereditary Duchy of Walburg Councils and Upper Offices at Scheer ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hear the accompanying Landtamman and Upper Church Warden Caspar Schantzen in his matters in a friendly manner and to grant him the due support. This is done in the absence of Dukes Wilhelm Heinrich and Friedrich.
