en.sender: Reichserbherzogliche Walburgische Räte und Oberämter zu Scheer
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Buchhorn reply to a letter from the St. Gallen, in which the latter had asked for permission to buy grain. They state that although they are in principle willing, they are bound to the side of Archduke Leopold by urgent letters and oral orders from the imperial chamber directors in Innsbruck. They ask St. Gallen to support them in this matter, as otherwise they would have to reckon with an imperial penalty for disobedience.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen report that they had the quality of the wax, which was complained about by merchants of St. Gallen, examined by their Veltliner residents. The result was positive. They ask St. Gallen to instruct its coin administrator to accept the usual wax fee in the future and not to complain about it.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the city of Überlingen to waive the punishment of the widow and her four children, who had unknowingly incurred a fine of 40 gulden. They request a mild punishment and refer to the fact that the family is poor and fatherless. Furthermore, they assure that the convicted person has paid the fine and will not commit anything more serious.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Stadt Überlingen

en.regest: The Hospital Masters of St. Gallen ask the Council of Lindau to permit their bailiff in the Reinthal, Lucas Studacher, to purchase 40 Malter of grain. Since the hospital has no grain of its own in Ringeck this year, the farmers in the Reinthal are to sell their customary grain loan in the form of grain to Lindau. The Hospital Masters request Lindau to grant the purchase favorably, so that the farmers can feed their animals.
en.recipient: Council of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen reply to an intercession of St. Gallen for their fellow citizen Daniel Wetter, who was caught with inferior coinage. They justify the confiscation, as Wetter had damaged the grain market with bad three-batzen coins. They ask St. Gallen to instruct its citizens and grain carriers to use only good coins in purchases and payments.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Bern request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to uphold the inheritance rights of the widow and children of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen, Sebastian Kromen. Kromen's brother-in-law, the town clerk of Bern, Johann Rudolf Bucher, has contested the bequest of his sister-in-law Margarete Meyer to Kromen. Bern requests St. Gallen to postpone the matter until Bucher has been informed and to grant him justice.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a report from Basel, according to which Austrian troops intend to march towards the Pünzte. They ask the St. Gallen to prepare for possible unrest and assure them of their Confederate friendship.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen that Austrian war troops are marching from the Alsace towards the Bündnerland. Furthermore, small groups of foreign soldiers are said to be marching through the Thurgau under the pretext that they have deserted. Zürich asks St. Gallen to keep an eye on such troops and, in case of danger, to notify the bailiff of the Lordship of Sax as well as the Landvogt of the County of Werdenberg.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern ask the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen to help their town clerk, who cannot appear in person due to other obligations, in the inheritance case concerning the estate of the deceased Kunigunde Tobler, wife of the St. Gallen citizen Sebastian Krumen. They recommend the claims of the heirs and ask for a friendly or legal decision.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to an intercession of the city of Konstanz for their citizen Ferdinand Felen. They deny the request to allow Felen to be represented by a lawyer, as this would contradict the city's statutes and personal presence is necessary for the clarification of the legal dispute with the St. Gallen citizen Haler. They have set a court day before the St. Gallen city court for 2 July 1622 and ask Konstanz to inform Felen of this day and to compel him to appear in person.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Mindelheim inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the prisoner Paulus Weauner was executed on the same Friday. They report that part of the stolen money was found, but no letters. Weauner had 16 Reichstaler, 4 ducats, 1 tenth and 1 gold gulden on his person. He had been willing to sign a receipt and provide bail. Mindelheim offers to hand over the money in St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the death of the citizen of St. Gallen Lienhart Gmünder in Lyon. Since his widow Anna Gmünderin, as the next of kin, would be the heiress under the law of Zürich, the men of Zürich ask that the widow be supported in the inheritance and that other more distant relatives be excluded.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the Landvogt of the Turgau to support the St. Gallen butcher Hans Altherr. He says that on 8 July he had a horse, which he had bought in the Argau, seized and held there upon passing through St. Peterszell, although he bears no guilt and has caused no damage. The St. Gallen request the release of the horse without payment and promise to sue the responsible parties for any possible damages.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt of the upper and lower Turgau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Schultheiss and Council of Bern to observe the prohibitions issued in the Bernese territory against the whitening of foreign cloths. They request the provision of a judgment that would allow the Bernese Ammann to buy meat freely in the city of St. Gallen, so that he may butcher the meat in St. Gallen. Furthermore, they ask for the resumption of the former agreements within the framework of the Confederation.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Bern

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg send Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen a letter of safe-conduct from Lieutenant General Johann Tserclaes Count von Tilly for the Frankfurt Autumn Fair. They ask that the patent be published in the necessary places and presented to the garrisons, so that the merchants can travel safely.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank for the report on their Burgomaster Hans Heinrich Holzhäuser. They ask St. Gallen to cooperate in the deployment of scouts and the transmission of news. Regarding the purchase of livestock, they state that they have newly issued a mandate against harmful livestock purchases, but permit the St. Gallen butchers to buy livestock in Zürich, provided that it is not resold elsewhere. They inform about a conference of the Catholic cantons and Glarus on 25 August and ask St. Gallen to take care of shipping on Lake Constance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Radolfzell ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to urge their fellow citizen Tobias Schömer, who has acted against the market regulations and fled before the decision, to settle the matter by 31 August.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen invite Landammann and Council of Appenzell to come to the city the next evening and to spend the night in the residence of the citizen Daniel Studer on the St. Leonhardsstrasse. They ask the Appenzellers to travel the way together with the Confederate envoys to Lindau, and promise them hospitality.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter of 14 September 1626, in which Überlingen asks for delivery at the St. Gallen weekly market due to a shortage of lard and unslicht. They refer to the fact that their own market is also weakened by the outflow of milk and cheese to foreign buyers. They offer to grant Überlingers free access to the St. Gallen market, provided they send their own people there.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizens and grain carriers to deliver lard, cheese, and tallow to the city of Überlingen in exchange for grain. Überlingen has hitherto granted the citizens of St. Gallen priority in the procurement of grain at the markets and wishes to continue to do so.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have the edict concerning the appointed general court day for the deceased citizen of Lindau Calixt Murgel publicly posted and published in St. Gallen. This is to be done so that any creditors among the citizens of St. Gallen may learn of the claim and no one be disadvantaged by ignorance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to provide legal assistance to their citizen Ulrich Stierli. The St. Gallen Sebastian Zwickher had promised Stierli's daughter Barbara in marriage, but had departed without farewell. Stierli wishes to follow Zwickher and force him to fulfill the promise. Schaffhausen requests St. Gallen to treat Zwickher accordingly, so that Stierli may feel the effect of the petition.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Bern report that butchers of St. Gallen purchased over six hundred head of cattle at the markets of Verlen and sold them to foreign butchers, although the ordinance allows only two oxen per week. They ask St. Gallen to warn the butchers to refrain from the pre-purchase in Bern, and promise to supply the cattle necessary for household use. Furthermore, they thank them for the hospitality shown to the Bernese envoys in Lindau.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the hospitable reception and hospitality of their envoys at the Confederate conference in Lindau. They declare themselves willing to serve St. Gallen in similar cases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Bern inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have granted their citizens Konrad Rainer and Hans Appenzeller permission to buy twenty head of cattle to alleviate the cattle shortage. They ask St. Gallen not to issue similar patents, as this could endanger the cattle trade. Rainer has admitted to having sold cattle to foreigners, which is why he has been instructed to refrain from doing so.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheissen, Landammann and Council of the seven Catholic cantons thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the hospitable reception, hospitality and gifts that their envoys received at the Lindau Conference. They promise to serve St. Gallen in similar cases with the same love and loyalty, and ask God for the preservation of friendship and unity.
en.sender: Schultheissen, Landammann and Council of the seven Catholic cantons
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Unterwalden ob dem Kernwald thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the kindness and benefits that have come to their envoy Johann Imfeld in Lindau. They offer their support as Confederates and mention that Bartholomäus and Hieronymus Zollikofer as well as Jakob Krenich Imfeld had also shown particular kindness.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of Unterwalden ob dem Kernwald
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Unterwalden thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the kindness and good deed that came to them through their envoy in Lindau. They offer themselves for mutual support and recommend themselves to the fatherly care of God.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council in the Boden of Uri thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the great friendliness and hospitality shown to their envoys at the last Landtag in Lindau. They ask for continued friendship and Confederation.
en.sender: Landammann and Council in the Boden of Uri
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Schwyz thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the special honor and friendship as well as the great costs that the latter have incurred for their envoys at the recent Lindau conference. In return, they offer Confederate friendship and services.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to newly settle the dispute between their citizen Othmar Appenzeller and the tanner Hans Schüßellberger over the purchase of calf skins. Schüßellberger has complained that the skins were valued too low. Zürich asks that the parties be summoned again and the skins be valued by appointed appraisers according to the oath, in order to achieve an amicable settlement and save further costs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich complain to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that butchers of St. Gallen, namely Konrad Thür and his servant Kaspar Appenzeller, buy up cattle from the Zürich countryside and sell it to outsiders, whereby prices rise. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to prevent their citizens from doing so, and otherwise threaten with penalties and the prohibition of buying Zürich cattle.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Stadtammann and Bannerherr Wolfgang Hasler in the name of the four courts in the Rheintal report to the Burgomaster of St. Gallen that they had recently been in St. Gallen regarding the wine levy. Since they could not reach an agreement, it was decided to tax the summer wine at 19 gulden and 3 shillings per measure of 9 kreuzer. This was confirmed by neighborly friendship.
en.sender: Stadtammann and Bannerherr Wolfgang Hasler in the name of the four courts in the Rheintal
en.recipient: Burgomaster of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Bern for the reply to their letters regarding the naturalized butchers Konrad Reiner and Hans Abbenzeller. They justify the issuance of certificates and intercessions for the cattle purchase, as not all city butchers had the necessary capital, and emphasize that the cattle must be slaughtered and sold in the city. They ask Bern to grant free passage to three citizens of the city who are traveling to the next market in Bern, so that they can buy cattle for the city's own consumption.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Bern

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to reopen the right of Tüferer Caspar Felix Meier against the citizen of St. Gallen Sebastian Krumen. Meier has complained about a dismissal, as the costs for the marriage process of his deceased wife Margaretha have not yet been discussed. Zürich asks for an amicable settlement.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a written report on the valuation of the pound of unpolished stones as well as on the quantity of solder needed for their processing.
en.sender: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Itel Reding, Landvogt in Thurgau, for support for their citizen and butcher Michel Herber. He says that he bought oxen from the Prelate of Villingen, but that they were seized by the subjects of the Landvogt. The St. Gallen ask that the purchase be allowed to stand without deduction, as they had not previously restricted free purchase in their city.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Itel Reding, Landvogt in Thurgau

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Glarus thank St. Gallen for the hospitable reception of their envoys in Lindau. They ask that the issued ordinance be observed, according to which cheese and the like may only be sold at the markets of the Confederates, and request that action be taken against Captain Jacob Meier, who comes from Toggenburg, and others who bring such goods to St. Gallen.
en.sender: Landammann and seated Council of Glarus
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann, Court and Community of Thal reply to the inquiry of the St. Gallen envoy regarding the deductions and seizures they have levied from the widow of Tuchsen. They ask for time to consider, as the officials of Mollach and Nall have presented their claims. They promise to conduct themselves according to the answer of the Council, and offer their services.
en.sender: Ammann, Court and Community of Thal
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report that the young journeyman Kaspar Hohl from Tüffen is in their custody and has confessed, among other things, to having stolen from the Appenzeller merchant Peter im Kilperg. They ask Landammann and Council of Appenzell to initiate an inquisition to clarify the circumstances and request that the result be communicated to their messenger.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Rottenschwil to help with a specific matter in a neighborly manner, so that the petitioner may obtain his right. They thank them for the support and promise to do the same for them in similar cases.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Rottenschwil

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the report on the gathering of foreign troops and war preparations on Lake Constance. They inform them that they have notified the other cantons of this matter as well as of a letter from the Austrian directors in Innsbruck, in which secret agreements with the Grisons are suspected. They request a joint Confederate assembly regarding the price increase, the hoarding of supplies, and the coinage, and ask for further reports.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen that the abbot had allowed Spanish troops to pass against Rapperswil. They ask for further reports on this. In addition, they state that Luzern had halved the coins, as Bern, Freiburg, and Solothurn had already done. They request St. Gallen's opinion on the concerns regarding the coin devaluation and the continuation of the coinage order.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rorschach ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have it investigated in the city whether the butcher Melchior Pfister, who was arrested in Rorschach and is supposed to have stolen 150 florins from a merchant of St. Gallen, committed further thefts there. They ask for a written answer in order to release the prisoner or to convict him.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the report on the approaching foreign warlike people. They ask that vigilance be maintained and that it be ascertained whether the people are gathering or moving on, and where they intend to go. Zürich has already informed Appenzell, the Landvogt of the Rheintal and Turgau, as well as the bailiff of Sax, and will in turn maintain the Confederate supervision.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Jeronimo Casale, Vice-envoy of the Spanish Queen, for support for their merchants Schobinger and Spindler. These are said to have been taken into arrest in Mailand with their cattle and money, although they had patents of the Governor. The city has sent an envoy to the Duke of Mailand and asks Casale to give this envoy credit and to ensure their release as well as future trade guarantees.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Jeronimo Casale, Vice-envoy of the Spanish Queen in the Confederation

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to give full faith to their councilor Jeremias Peyer, who is in St. Gallen together with Captain N. Zörnlin of Basel. They ask for his report and for an explanatory statement. Schaffhausen offers similar support in return.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the bailiff of Grüningen to enforce the decision already issued by Zürich in the grain purchase case between the St. Gallen butcher Othmar Abbenzeller and the Heltwiler Hans Schüffelberger. They report that Schüffelberger, despite his oath, did not appear, but only sent his brother Martin with two Council members of Zürich to have the goods appraised again, and then departed.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Bailiff of Grüningen, Hans Caspar Landeggen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen reply to an inquiry from St. Gallen regarding the Stathauptmann Hans Jakob Hünlis. They explain that they cannot dismiss Hünlis, as the city requires more soldiers due to the dangerous situation and Hünlis is praised for other tasks. They ask the Confederates to come to an understanding with Hünlis.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rottweil answer the inquiry of St. Gallen regarding Melchior Pfüsteren, who is detained in St. Gallen. They state that the citizen of Rottweil, Hans Ulrich Schuerz, who accuses Pfüsteren of thefts, has not been at home until now. His report, according to which Pfüsteren stole money from him and a merchant, is enclosed. They ask for further news.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Gemeiner Landrat of the Äusseren Roden of the Land of Appenzell inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the majority of the cantons of the Confederation had remained with the coinage department. They request a meeting the next day in St. Gallen with the abbot and the Landvogt im Rietthal, to deliberate on the promotion of the poor people and the equalization with other cantons.
en.sender: Landammann and Gemeiner Landrat of the Äusseren Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform about a shortage of beef and roast meat as well as demands by the butchers for higher prices. They ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to communicate how high the pound of meat is taxed there, how many Löt the pound weighs, and whether it is weighed in, in order to adjust the prices in their own city.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for its confidential communication and ask for continued vigilance and mutual information. They report that the Confederates in Baden had requested Archduke Leopold von Österreich to remove foreign troops and to secure the grain trade. Regarding the coinage, they state that they will maintain the suspension of the mint until the opinions of the other cantons are available, and ask St. Gallen to inform them of the results of the planned conference in St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank E. E. Fst. W. und Gst. for the favorable treatment of the citizens of St. Gallen Schobinger and Schindler by the envoy Dr. Sebastian Schobinger. They ask for the continuation of this friendship. Furthermore, they request that the Obrist von Erlach, who intends to travel to Mailand and Venedig, be persuaded to assist the St. Gallen citizens if needed. It would be desirable if the Obrist acted in the name of the Confederates with instructions and letters of credence.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: E. E. Fst. W. und Gst.

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report on a dispute between their citizen Anton Gerber and the Lindau goldsmith Johannes Gloggen. Gerber had wanted to offer Gloggen suspicious scrap silver, whereupon a physical altercation had occurred. Gerber had been held up at the gate and had had to return a cup to Gloggen. Both parties had complained. Lindau sends the silver to St. Gallen and asks for its return or disposal at the discretion of St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the letter regarding the coinage. They report that so far only Bern, Glarus, and Unterwalden had voted against the coin withdrawal, while the other cantons had not yet replied. Zürich will continue to publish and observe the coin withdrawal in its territory. They hope that the trades will continue to operate despite possible restrictions, and ask St. Gallen to behave accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Adam Cronus zum Zieglhaus in Lindau remits 25 gold ducats to the city of St. Gallen. He asks the authorities to distribute the money among the poor in the city who come from Veltolin, through their almoners, without naming the donor.
en.recipient: Amtsbürgermeister und Baumeister zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about the negotiations at the Baden Diet regarding the withdrawal of coinage. It was determined there that the Reichstaler minted in St. Gallen are lighter and of poorer quality than the other Confederate ones. To avoid misunderstandings and complaints, the Zürichers ask the St. Gallen authorities to henceforth mint Reichstaler according to the Imperial and Confederate standard.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Schultheiss and Council of Luzern for the support given so far to their citizens Schobinger and Schindelin in Montferrat and Novara. As the matter is still unresolved, they ask Luzern to issue a letter of recommendation to the Colonel of Beroldingen, so that he can intercede in Mailand and Mantua on behalf of the St. Gallen citizens for the Catholic cantons.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Luzern

en.regest: The Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen request Landvogt Sebastian Heinrich Trüeb to instruct the farmer David Ruchen of Thal to vacate the leasehold. The citizen of St. Gallen Leonhard Zollikofer has terminated the leasehold within the deadline and taken on a new tenant, but Ruchen refuses to move out. The city requests official assistance so that the new tenant can take possession of the leasehold.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Sebastian Heinrich Trüeb, Landvogt in the Upper and Lower Valley

en.regest: Egon Graf von Fürstenberg sends the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen some game from the hunt at Wildbrats. He thanks them for the quick and benevolent decision in the case of Daniel Schlumpf and offers further neighborly favors for the future.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to dissuade the heirs of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen, Caspar Schlumpf, from the intention to pay off a debt of 500 Kronen (converted to 866 gulden 40 kreuzer) plus interest in the local currency. The heirs are not forced to pay off the debt, but wish to settle the debt in another currency, which harms the creditors of Winterthur. Winterthur requests that the heirs be instructed to leave the principal debt with the usual interest or to make the payment in the agreed currency.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the letter of the Rorschach authorities regarding the imprisoned Melchior Pfister. They report that Hofmarschall Pfister had apologized, as he had not known what was going on in Rorschach. He had declared himself willing to present himself and give a report if they would hand over the chest to the Stiftsamt. St. Gallen promises to do this and asks Rorschach to request Pfister's statement again.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Rorschach

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish an edict concerning a newly appointed general court day for the absent citizen of Lindau, Georg Rosacher. They wish to ensure that creditors who have claims against Rosacher learn of this and that their rights are not curtailed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Radolfzell reply to a letter from St. Gallen of 18 November 1622, concerning the St. Gallen fellow citizen Jacob Abt, from whom Melchior Pfister is said to have stolen 130 florins. Since Abt has not pursued his complaint further, the Radolfzell authorities demand that Abt appear in person or be examined under oath in order to determine the truth. They ask to be informed how this matter will proceed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johannes Franz Reding invites the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to his wedding with Susanna von Pflumern, taking place on 26 October in Rorschach. He asks the gentlemen to arrive the evening before and to be present on the wedding day to adorn the celebration. He requests a reply.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Frankfurt inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have requested General Count von Tilly for a free pass for the upcoming Lenten Fair. Tilly has graciously granted it. The Frankfurt authorities forward the copy of the pass for information.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a detailed report on the local coinage regulation and its effects. They say that they did not join the St. Gallen withdrawal of the coins, as they lie on the border and must trade with the subjects there. They ask for an answer on the state of affairs in order to be able to hold further consultations.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information regarding the implementation of the coinage ordinance and the effects of the coin devaluation on the prices of foodstuffs and goods. They explain that they will not initially follow the devaluation, as they lie on the Imperial border and must deal in Imperial coins. They ask for a confidential and comprehensive answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen confirm the receipt of a letter of 25 November 1622 regarding the legal dispute between the Zürcher Ferdinand Holey and the St. Gallen Sebastian Zollikofer. They have set a new court day for the Monday after Judica and ask the authorities of Zürich to inform Holey of this date and to seriously obligate him to appear on time, in order to avoid further delays.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Schaffhauser of 7 September. They report that the coinage was halved and the thaler was devalued by half a pound by Baden's decision. This led to great inflation and a shortage of money, as the money had been driven out of the country. They ask the Schaffhauser to rectify the grievances and to calm the country.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen

en.regest: The bailiff and Council of Bischofszell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to revoke the banishment pronounced against their citizen Hans Koller, butcher. Koller says that he had fallen into disgrace with Landammann Schüß because of thoughtless words and had been arrested. He says that he is engaged to a woman of St. Gallen and wants to establish his household in St. Gallen. Koller hopes that Landammann Schüß himself will ask for grace. Bischofszell asks for neighborly help and promises reciprocity.
en.sender: The bailiff and Council of Bischofszell
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the bailiff of Neunkirch to assist their citizen Othmar Abbenzeller in a purchase dispute with Hans Schüffelberger of Bichswil. Schüffelberger says that he secretly counted the purchased cows and issued a false document regarding half of the property of Lorenz Abbenzeller. The St. Gallen authorities ask for judicial assistance so that the Bishop's judgment is enforced and Abbenzeller is reimbursed for the costs incurred.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Bailiff of Neunkirch

en.regest: Hans Kaspar Heidegger, bailiff of the lordship of Grüningen, reports to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the legal dispute between the St. Gallen butcher Othmar Appenzeller and the Sitterdorf gardener Hans Schüffelberger over a purchase of veal. The court has ruled that two impartial men should inspect and appraise the 44 disputed pieces. Appenzeller is to pay Schüffelberger the calculated value and pay him two Kronen for costs. Furthermore, Appenzeller is to produce the butcher from Rheineck as a witness to refute the accusation of bribery. The bailiff asks the St. Gallen authorities to release the messengers so that the matter can be settled.
en.sender: Hans Kaspar Heidegger, bailiff of the lordship of Grüningen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Michael Meyer genant Wanger, butcher at Stein am Rhein, publicly testifies that the Säckler Hans Schüßelberger in the Grünlinger Amt and the butcher Othmar Appenzeller at St. Gallen had concluded a purchase of calf skins. Meyer had stood as surety for Schüßelberger. Since Appenzeller does not keep his promises and thereby causes costs to Schüßelberger and Meyer, Meyer demands that Appenzeller bear the costs incurred.
en.sender: Michael Meyer genant Wanger, butcher at Stein am Rhein

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to lift the arrest imposed on their subject Hans Wiggli Haller von Lohningen. The citizens of St. Gallen Peter Feer and Hans Jakob Tanner had Haller arrested for 60 pounds and 15 pounds in court costs. Haller is innocent and complains about the measure. Schaffhausen asks for his release so that Haller may come to his right.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Decastille in Solothurn complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the change in the messenger system. The previous mounted messenger from the Gascogne had reliably brought him the needed goods from Lyon every two weeks on Thursday evening. The new foot messenger refuses to take over the shipments and does not stay to receive letters. Decastille asks that the old messenger be reinstated, as he has noticed no faults in him.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform that they will cancel the fair scheduled for the Friday and Saturday after Philippi and Jacobi this time. They ask the recipients to inform their citizens of this, so that they may avoid unnecessary costs.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: Bailiff Hans Caspar Heidegger of Grüningen apologizes to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the arrest of his subordinate Martin Schüffelberger. The latter had claimed in St. Gallen that the Bailiff had allowed Heinrich Deeler to arrest the butcher Jakob Appenzeller for a debt. Heidegger denies this and promises to punish Schüffelberger for the false accusation. He asks that the arrested persons be released and that their costs be reimbursed.
en.sender: Hans Caspar Heidegger, Bailiff of the Lordship of Grüningen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and the Deputies of the Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the citizen of St. Gallen Jakob Hiller on Saturday in the inn called zum Schäfli had slandered the Landammann and Bannerlord of Appenzell Johannes Schüss. They ask St. Gallen to call Hiller to account and to send a written answer. Furthermore, they reject the claim that citizens of St. Gallen have no access to the Landrechnung.
en.sender: The Landammann and the Deputies to the Landrechnung of the Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur inform that the son of the deceased citizen of Winterthur, Bonifaz Brenwald, namely Hans Heinrich Brenwald, has married the woman of St. Gallen, Elisabeth Nägeli. Since Brenwald requires written proof of his origin for the ecclesiastical confirmation of the marriage in St. Gallen, Winterthur requests its issuance. They confirm that Brenwald was born legitimate to Bonifaz Brenwald and Barbara Tünkhlerin and has always behaved honestly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the answer of their citizen Jakob Hyllers regarding the defamatory remarks against Landammann and Bannerlord Johann Füß. They ask that Hyllers be further questioned as to whether the statements came from Uolly Rechsteiner, called Jagglis Uolly, or Weijrathen Uolly, or from someone else, in order to be able to investigate the matter better.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: De Castille asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform him whether they had approved the change of the usual messenger between the cities or whether a reason for this change existed. He hopes that they will not deny him the requested convenience, as it brings them no disadvantage.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about impending attacks on the Evangelical cantons of the Confederation by the regiments of Sultz, Baldiron and Ladron as well as Austrian and Spanish troops. They ask the St. Gallen to be vigilant, to inform them immediately of any new developments, and to prepare for possible support, so that the fatherland may be saved.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and the Deputies of the Land of Appenzell report to St. Gallen that the Appenzell citizen Jakob Hiller denies his defamatory remarks against Landammann Schüsser. However, the witnesses Jos Frener and Hans Holderegger confirm that Hiller accused Schüsser of disgrace and claimed that he would lose his office. The Appenzell ask St. Gallen to appoint a specific court day for Hiller, so that Schüsser can avenge his honor.
en.sender: Landammann and the Deputies for the Land Audit of the Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen thank for the warning of 6 May regarding the presence of Austrian troops on the Rhine and rumors of an attack on the Confederation. They report that no muster was held in Stockach and no troops had arrived, as citizens of the town had reported. They promise to continue inquiring and to inform St. Gallen about everything concerning the fatherland.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann, Council and the country people of Glarus inform St. Gallen about an embassy of the Catholic cantons, which urges them to accept a Lucerne judgment against their Catholic fellow citizens. Glarus rejects this, as the judgment violates the Landbrief and treaties. They ask St. Gallen for help and support in an emergency and promise in turn their assistance.
en.sender: Landammann, Council and the common country people of the Evangelical religion of Glarus
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Glarners of 28 May, in which they had asked for help in a dispute with the Catholic countrymen. St. Gallen declares that the Confederation is only obliged to help in the case of attacks from outside, but only as a mediator in internal disputes. They will follow the Diet and ask the Glarners to rely on St. Gallen.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann, Statthalter and countrymen of the Evangelical religion of Glarus

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz that in the legal dispute pending between Ferdinand Heel and Joachim Zollikoffer, Heel has announced witnesses for the provision of evidence but has not yet produced them. Since he has excused himself and requested a new date, the St. Gallen authorities set the 15th of July 1623, 10 o'clock in the morning, at the Rathaus in St. Gallen for him and ask the Konstanzer to inform their representative of this date.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: The Statthalter and Council of the city of Zürich ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have their citizen Laurenz Schellen report on the state of a bill of exchange for 4000 gulden, which he concluded in 1621 with the citizen of Zürich Caspar Santij. They request written information on the manner of service and the deductions, in order to clarify a dispute between Santij and the citizen of Zürich Christoph Werdmüller.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to lend them 2000 gulden for the Landvogt Zillen or to transfer them to the bailiff to Sax. Zürich has already paid 2892 gulden to Zillen and promises to repay the sum within three months with interest. This is done to avoid further legal disputes and costs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Caspar Heidegger, bailiff of the lordship of Grüningen, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist his subject Jörg Pfenninger. Pfenninger says that he sold two cattle to the St. Gallen butcher Konrad Künz and remained in debt to him for 9.5 thaler. Künz promised payment but made it only partially and with insufficient coin. Heidegger asks that Künz be compelled to make full payment including costs.
en.sender: Hans Caspar Heidegger, bailiff of the lordship of Grüningen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Kaspar Heidegger, bailiff of the lordship of Neunforn, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he has instructed the steward Hans Schüffelberger to settle the claim of the Appenzeller. However, Schüffelberger refuses, as the calf was overvalued at the market purchase. He asks that the Appenzeller be instructed to keep the calf, or that Schüffelberger be given a calf of equal value, so that the matter may be settled.
en.sender: Hans Kaspar Heidegger, bailiff of the lordship of Neunforn
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to a complaint by the Schwyzers Caspar Hirten and Ulrich Sigendaler against the St. Gallen butchers Jacob and Hans Rietmann. The St. Gallen parties claim to have paid the purchase price in cash in dublons and Reichsthalers. They point out that the Schwyzers had taken the money by force and demand that the citizens of St. Gallen not be further harassed.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of Schwyz

en.regest: Bailiff Hans Joachim Krimm von Freylingen zu Stettlieben reports to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Clara Hillerin appeared before him after her return. She presented the divorce contract with Melchior Nef and applied to keep and raise the two children from her first marriage with Alexander Heron herself, as Nef does not uphold the contract. Krimm refuses this, as he fears that the children would be poorly raised with Hillerin, and hands the matter over to the gentlemen for decision. He hands them a certified copy of the contract.
en.sender: Hans Joachim Krimm von Freylingen, Bailiff zu Stettlieben
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Schwyz report that the St. Gallen butchers Jacob and Hans Weyeli owe their countrymen Caspar Spiler and Ulrich Gwerchscher 30 Kronen and 20 Schilling for purchased butcher's goods. Despite reminders, no money has been paid. The Schwyzers ask the St. Gallen to persuade the debtors to a friendly settlement, in order to avoid further costs and inconveniences. They promise, for their part, to help with claims of the St. Gallen against the Schwyzers.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the bailiff of Gottlieben concerning the children of the deceased Melchior Tiefel. They confirm that Tiefel had kept the contract, and ask the bailiff to present himself in person to receive the contract and the receipt and to hand over the money to the guardians of the children.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Hans Wernher Bruggmann zu Herblingen, bailiff of Gottlieben

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Schwyz summon the Confederates Jacob and Hans Rütimann, butchers, before the court. The background is a legal dispute between Rütimann and the St. Gallen Council member Caspar Giebel, bailiff of the hospital. The St. Gallen side wants to determine the truth through witnesses. Rütimann is requested to appear in Schwyz, otherwise the proceedings will continue without him.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Rudolf Reding von Bierberg, Count of Toggenburg, informs that on 15 April 1622 in Heimberg a lightning bolt struck the Turm and damaged the church, Turm, and bells. The church community asks for support for the reconstruction. Reding requests the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to provide a considerable aid out of Christian compassion and neighborly affection.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Joachim Brünisi, bailiff at Gottlieben, confirms the receipt of a letter from the St. Gallen. He reports that he has handed over the inheritance between the widow Anna Züllin and the children of the deceased Melchior Vren and Alexander Fromhus to Caspar Keuber. Since the widow had provided poorly for the children, he wishes to adhere to the inheritance and inform the children orally.
en.sender: Hans Joachim Brünisi von Herblingen, bailiff at Gottlieben
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich recommend to their Confederate circle of friends in St. Gallen the Councilor Michael Rosset, who wishes to approach them with particular business. They ask that Rosset be heard in his requests in a friendly and benevolent manner and that he be given a satisfactory answer, so that he may rejoice about it upon his return to Zürich.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Hofvogt Johann Klingern of Rorschach to take care of the upbringing and maintenance of the orphan Daniel Pfistermann. The boy, whose guardians are Lorenz Ruh and Melchior Lecher, is to attend school in Konstanz and afterwards learn the language in Italien. The St. Gallen ask Klingern to reach an agreement with the guardians regarding the costs, so that the boy can support himself in the future.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Johann Klingern, Fürstlich St. Gallischer Rat und Hofvogt zu Rorschach

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of the Äussere Roden of the Land of Appenzell inform St. Gallen that their countryman Thomas Lutz von Effriet has presented a Kompassbrief issued by St. Gallen, according to which he had bought a quarter of corn in the morning at 26 kreuzer and in the afternoon at 34 kreuzer from the St. Gallen citizen and corn merchant Balthasar Suter. Appenzell had commissioned the Confedrate Ulrich Züricher to inquire about the prices. He had sworn under oath that Suter had sold the corn on Saturday before noon at 26 kreuzer. Appenzell asks St. Gallen to examine the matter.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the Äussere Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant their citizen Caspar Oswald an arrest on the purchase price of a property named Katzensteig located in the County of Thurgau. Oswald has brought a testament before the court against the relatives of his deceased wife, who, however, asserted the jurisdiction of the Bischofszell court and had inheritance rights placed under arrest there. Since the property is said to have been sold to an unknown citizen of St. Gallen, Schaffhausen requests support in securing the purchase money.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the report on the defamatory remarks of the Milanese Ordinarius Hilprand Späler. They state that they do not wish to trouble St. Gallen further, as they will settle the matter otherwise. However, they request that the written information be transmitted in authentic form under the seal of St. Gallen, so that it can be used if needed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about reports that a strong army of Spanish troops on foot and horseback will shortly arrive at Füßach and reach the Grisons. They ask the Confederates to watch this people and, through their own scouts, to find out whether it will march further into Germany or winter there, and for notification of the results.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to waive the tenth-penny deduction for the widow Verena Scherbinin, wife of Schultheiss Georg Schmid. They refer to the fact that the citizens of St. Gallen had already been exempted from this deduction by the heirs of the deceased Anna Scherbinin, sister of the petitioner. Stein am Rhein asks for written confirmation of this favor.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich order the bailiff of Grüningen to detain the tanner Hans Schüßelbaur from Bichwil to compensate the butcher Otmar Appenzeller from St. Gallen for the purchase of calf skins. Appenzeller had received a judgment that condemned Schüßelbaur to pay two Kronen, which the latter had not fulfilled despite intercession. The bailiff is to force Schüßelbaur to pick up the animals and pay the purchase price along with costs.
en.recipient: bailiff of Grüningen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the report on the approaching Italian and Spanish troops. They state that they had received similar reports, according to which the troops were equipped with pickaxes and shovels in addition to weapons. They promise to conduct further inquiries and to inform St. Gallen immediately, and ask for mutual vigilance.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Zürich for the support of their citizen Othmar Zoberzeler in the legal dispute with the bailiff of Grüningen. They report that the defendant Hans Schübelberger did not appear, but only sent his cousin Martin Schübelberger with two witnesses, who wanted to inspect the properties without documents. Since Schübelberger has unexpectedly departed, the St. Gallen authorities ask Zürich to exert influence on Schübelberger so that he pays the purchase price along with costs and damages to Zoberzeler and the matter is finally settled.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the city of Altstätten. They point out that the levy of 7 1/2 pounds, 16 shillings and 6 denars per Müt at the customs office was done out of good will and not by right. They ask Altstätten not to raise any further complaints for the current year and to accept the existing customs duties. They promise, for their part, to admonish the customs duties and to act in a neighborly manner.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Town clerk and Council of Altstätten

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the reports on the approaching Spanish war troops. They ask the Confederates to continue their efforts and to explore through scouts whether the army will winter in the country or march on. Zürich promises to inform St. Gallen as well about all warnings and reports.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Town Schultheiss and Council of Altstätten, on behalf of the four courts of the Rhine Valley, communicate that they wish to conclude the wine purchase according to old custom for 1623. Since the courts cannot pay the 7 kreuzer 2 pfennig per measure demanded by St. Gallen, they have agreed on the price of 2 kreuzer per measure. They ask St. Gallen to accept this price in order to avoid greater disturbances.
en.sender: Town Schultheiss and Council of Altstätten
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel the citizen of St. Gallen Sebastian Zwickher to keep his marriage promise to the daughter of the Schaffhausen locksmith Ulrich Wirrin. Zwickher had impregnated the daughter but had departed for Ulm. Wirrin now wishes to bring the matter before the authorities in St. Gallen. Schaffhausen asks for support so that Zwickher enters into the marriage.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Landvogt of the County of Baden to help their citizen Sebastian Giger. The latter says that he delivered provisions to the citizen of Genf Amé Bonet, which are still unpaid. Bonet says that he committed himself to appear in St. Gallen, but failed to do so. The St. Gallen ask for a letter to the city of Genf, so that Bonet appears or pays.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Hans Gilgen auf der Maur, Landvogt of the County of Baden

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizen Hans Conrad Stierlin. He has a claim of 217 gulden against the St. Gallen citizen Jacob Aebt, which the latter settled by selling his house to Caspar Schüwlin. Schüwlin promised the payment, but the purchase fell to another. Schaffhausen requests that Schüwlin be instructed to pay the agreed amounts.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The town court of Lindau requests the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to examine the citizen of St. Gallen, Caspar Kürißamer, as a witness in a legal dispute between Anna Rietmännin and Johannes Hößlin over a wine debt. The parties are disputing the currency and the rate of the payment. Lindau asks that the witness be questioned under oath and that the statements be transmitted sealed.
en.sender: Town clerk and judges of the town court of Lindau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Zürich that they have heard the witnesses in the dispute between Othmar Appenzeller of St. Gallen and Hans Scheibelberger of Zürich. They transmit the statements and ask Zürich to support Appenzeller in the matter, so that the judgment of the court of Grüningen may be enforced and the dispute settled.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen transmit to the city of Zürich the statements of witnesses who were heard in the dispute between Hans Schüffelberger and Othmar von Altherr. They ask Zürich to serve the statements on the plaintiff Schüffelberger and to implement the amicable resolution already reached by the bailiff of Gossau, so that both parties may come to rest.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Zürich

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene on behalf of their countryman Hans Hügner. He says that eight days ago in Thurgau he was run over by a horse belonging to the St. Gallen subject Joachim Gnepper, so that the horse fell to the ground. The horse belongs to the Appenzeller Wälti Schregen, who wants to pay for the damage. Hügner accuses Gnepper because of insulting words. Appenzell asks for compensation without costs and for the restoration of honor.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the consent to the joint letter to the government of Ensisheim regarding the moneys drawn from the lands. They promise to send the letter after receiving the declaration of Schaffhausen. Furthermore, they thank them for the honorific envoys sent and offer their friendship and support in the current difficult times.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss, Burgomaster and Council of Frankfurt am Main describe the dire straits of their city following the siege by the Spaniards and the takeover by a garrison. They ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a mild tax for the needy citizenry and for intercession with the people of St. Gallen, as they themselves could no longer help.
en.sender: Schultheiss, Burgomaster and Council of Frankfurt am Main
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The letter contains only the salutation to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen. The sender, date, and content are missing.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: De Castille informs that the pension of the King cannot yet be paid out, as the cantons have priority over the allies. He promises that a transport will arrive in February, whereupon the payment is to take place.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about the response of the Confederates to the government of Einsiedeln. Schaffhausen had refused to join the common response and had issued its own declaration, while St. Gallen had agreed. The common response had been sent without Schaffhausen. Zürich communicates a complaint from Luzern and asks St. Gallen to explain itself to Luzern or to handle the matter at its own discretion.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to accept the sixteenth penny as a deduction for the relocation of the Schaffhausen citizen Friedrich Peyer and his wife. They explain that the sixth penny applies only to the deduction of inheritance by strangers who are not bound to the city. For the deduction with one's own property, the sixteenth penny applies. They refer to the mutual practice with Zürich and other Confederates.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform them how high the price for beef and roast meat is with them and what meat rates they had ordered their butchers to observe. They wish to improve their own butchers' ordinance and promise, in turn, to show the neighborhood the courtesy on the occasion.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Luzern reply to a letter from the Council of Zürich. They regret that the cities of Schaffhausen and St. Gallen do not want to give up or exchange the small Reichstaler. Since this burdens the Confederation, Luzern declares that, in the event of no remedy, it will devalue the Taler following the example of the neighbors. It is protested that damages are claimed against the mints, which are to exchange the Taler with good money.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the city of Konstanz dated 22 December 1623 concerning the meat price. They communicate that the meat had been estimated and inspected up to the Christmas holidays. Due to a shortage of meat, they had allowed the butcher to sell the meat at a higher price, which led to inconveniences. They ask Konstanz to communicate how high the meat price is there and what regulations apply with the butchers, in order to find a mutually agreeable solution.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Lindau for information on the local meat prices and the applicable regulations, as irregularities in the meat tax in St. Gallen are bothering the population. They wish to use the Lindau practice as a model for their own improvements and offer neighborly support in return.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the communication of the meat prices. They inform that in Konstanz a pound of beef has been set at 6 kreuzer and roast meat at 5 kreuzer. As the common man complains and the meat is cheaper elsewhere, they inquire with the neighbors. They promise to make a decision after receiving the answers and to inform St. Gallen.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Luzern confirm the receipt of the letter from St. Gallen of 20 January 1624 regarding the Imperial half. They declare that they will defer their further statement until a joint meeting in Baden, where the coinage and other occurrences are to be discussed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank them for the communication of the meat prices in Konstanz and in turn communicate the rates valid in St. Gallen for beef, veal, mutton, and goat meat. They instruct the butchers to strictly adhere to the prices and threaten penalties in case of violations. Furthermore, they ask for information about the night watch routes.
en.sender: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen
en.recipient: Verwalter der Lechenschaft Egnach und Rat der Stadt Konstanz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank for the communication of the meat prices in Konstanz and share their new rates: best ox meat 5½ to 6 kreuzer, other ox meat 5 kreuzer, best veal 16 pfennigs, bull meat 9 pfennigs. They instruct the assessors to adhere to these prices and threaten, in case of excess, a fine of 10 pounds pfennig or removal from the craft. They ask for the decision of Konstanz.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Deputies of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Luzern ask the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen to intervene in a debt matter in favor of the citizens of Luzern, Medler Nüss and Caspar Brunner. They say that these had lent 27 gulden to the St. Gallen Hans Müller, which he had not repaid. The Luzerners ask for official support so that the debtors receive their claim together with costs.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Luzern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to a request for a favor regarding the departure tax for the citizen of Schaffhausen Friedrich Hagend, who has married the widow of the deceased Burgomaster of St. Gallen Jacob Spengler. They refuse the levy of the sixteenth penny, as they had in the past levied the sixth penny. They offer to levy the sixteenth penny in the future for mutual arrivals with body and own property.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Schwyz ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their deceased fellow citizen Jeri Zwingen in a debt matter. Zwingen had bought an ox from the St. Gallen butchers Joch and Jacob Vogt and paid the money with a bill of exchange from Caspar Zwingen. The St. Gallen butchers had not accepted the money. The Schwyzers ask for support so that Zwingen can enforce his claim without high costs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Landvogt Itel Reding in Thurgau to look favorably upon Ulrich Hoeschen, who is detained for theft and has stolen a piece of piececloth, after his release and return to the city of St. Gallen. They request that he follow the petitioner and release the malefactor against the usual bond.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Itel Reding, Landvogt in Upper and Lower Thurgau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen confirm the receipt of the answer of 25 February 1624 in favor of Friedrich Huber and his wife Magdalena Schlaepferin. They ask for forgiveness that their letter of 3 February did not arrive in time. Furthermore, they request Schaffhausen to take consideration in the future regarding prohibitions against their citizens, as they themselves observe the same rules of neighborliness.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen

en.regest: Jost Ulrich, Landvogt in Ober- und Nidern Turgau, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he will hand over the prisoner Hans Wettern the next day on the border through his sworn servant Felix Engelin. He asks the St. Gallen to send their deputies to the border to receive the prisoner.
en.sender: Jost Ulrich, Landvogt in Ober- und Nidern Turgau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Luzern thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the swift handling of the complaints of Hans Müller and Jacob Schärman. They ask to be informed what further accusations the citizens of Luzern have against those of St. Gallen, as their citizens felt strongly aggrieved. They further offer the loyalty and friendship of the Confederates.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizens Christoph Werdmüller and Hans Jacob Löw in the collection of a debt from Peter Syner. The creditors had had goods from Syner seized at Pangraz Gerig in St. Gallen, which, however, had been lifted again at the request of Hans Süris of Solothurn. Zürich requests that the goods still present be newly arrested or that Syner and Heinrich be taken into custody until the creditors are satisfied.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Landvogt Itel Reding for the handover of a captured Brenner. They share his confession, according to which he had stolen on the Bleiche in Konstanz. They ask for the return of the stolen items or their value and for the communication of the statements of Hans Bloetschen and his wife, who are said to have given the perpetrator the opportunity.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Itel Reding, Landvogt of the upper and lower Turgau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Burgomaster and Council of Arbon for the transmission of information about the imprisoned Caspar Bronner. They ask the Arboners not to grant citizenship to Othmar Spoehl, who is considered an accomplice or assistant of Bronner, but to monitor him. Since the matter requires further clarification, they request Arbon to report on this.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Arbon

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank the Landvogt of Rorschach for his support in the case of Stephan Kramer. They share Kramer's statement that he had come under suspicion of murder because of accusations by a butcher who had been put to costs. They ask the Landvogt to clarify the matter with his superiors and to convey the opinion of the Rorschach people in order to reassure the Feldkirch people.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt of Rorschach

en.regest: Georg Langhans, servant of the Church in Bern, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to graciously accept the dedication of a Latin chronicle by his brother Jacob, clerk in Riggisberg, and to recommend him favorably.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to the request from Rorschach for the favoring of their citizen Ferdinand Holen in a legal dispute against Sebastian Zolikofer. They refer to the fact that Holen had revoked a concluded settlement, which caused the arrest and the delay. They announce that the court day will be held on 6 April at 8 o'clock in the town hall, and they reject the request for written copies of the witness testimonies, as this is not customary.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Rorschach

en.regest: Joell Reding, Landvogt in Thurgau, informs St. Gallen that, in response to their request, he did not personally question Thomas Studer and his wife Barbara Kollerin in Konstanz, but had them questioned by other witnesses. These stated that a man named Hans, who presented himself as a fever patient, spent the night with them and sold cloth. Reding asks St. Gallen to inform him what the accused might say under torture about these persons.
en.sender: Joell Reding, Landvogt in upper and lower Thurgau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Basel remind of the agreement of the three cities Basel, Schaffhausen and St. Gallen to redeem low-grade thaler. Since Schaffhausen and St. Gallen had not done this, the thaler of the three cities had been prohibited in Collmar. Basel asks St. Gallen to redeem the thaler still held in the city against other Reichstaler, in order to avoid a mutual prohibition.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Itel Reding confirms the receipt of a letter along with an arrest warrant. He informs them that he must postpone the interrogation of Thomas Klöckner and his wife because of the holy season and other business. He asks the citizens of St. Gallen to proceed further with the prisoner, and promises to make up for the interrogation at a later date and to report the result.
en.sender: Itel Reding, Council of Schwyz, Landvogt in the upper and lower Thurgau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to cite their citizen Sebastian Zwickher. He has not appeared despite an earlier letter and has not kept his marriage promise to the daughter of the St. Gallen Burgomaster Ulrich Risslin. The St. Gallen authorities are to summon Zwickher according to their custom so that he can defend himself.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur to send them one or two knowledgeable men who can inspect pits and excavations for the establishment of a new Zeholz in the city. If Winterthur has no such people, St. Gallen asks for help in procuring them or for the dispatch of people whom the St. Gallen could then pick up.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to the inquiry of the city of Konstanz regarding the citizen Ludwig Hager and his wife Magdalena Schlaipferin. They explain that during the joint residence of the spouses, the surviving spouse has the eternal Beschwörung. In the present case, the Abzug was paid and the Council was let out again. The wife received 6000 gulden in cash for the house and goods, in addition to 10000 gulden Leibgeding and her own property. Her own possessions, such as clothes and silverware, were excluded. They offer to continue future transactions equally.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: C. Kloeÿs informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a legal dispute between the pastor Georg Küenlin of Weilen and the heirs of the Zimmermann family from Weilen, which results from a testament. He asks the authorities of St. Gallen to patiently hear and promote the claims of the pastor's party, or else to mediate an amicable settlement between the friendly parties.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a conference in Zug, at which the Confederates, because of the unequal coinage and the harassment by foreign beggars, have decided to hold two foot patrols. They ask St. Gallen to take care in their land that the patrols take place on 4 and 14 June as planned, in order to abolish the beggar population jointly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Klöze reply to a letter of 15 April 1624 concerning the inheritance of the deceased Abraham Gmuender. They inform that his son Christoph and his mother Salomena are still alive. Due to the current danger of war, the inheritance cannot be collected. They ask St. Gallen to continue to keep the share safely until the heirs or their proxies can collect it.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the 13 cantons to take up the matter of their fellow citizens Zollikofer, Schobinger, Scheidtlin and Zili, to whom a considerable sum of money is being withheld in Mailand. They have sent the Council and Steuermann Dr. Sebastian Schobinger together with his agent as envoys to secure the repayment of the money.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: The 13 cantons

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich reply to the letter of St. Gallen regarding the Turgau withdrawal. They confirm that they carried out the withdrawal last year, but with the reservation that the release must be proven by legally valid letters and seals. They have instructed their envoys to the Baden annual accounts to hear the complainants. Zürich leaves it to St. Gallen to decide whether to join the other Turgau court lords or to send its own envoys to Baden, and assures of Confederate friendship.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizens trading in Lyon to restore the old order of the usual messengers. The French envoy Myron in Solothurn has applied for this, as the change harms the merchants. Schaffhausen will in turn hold its citizens to the observance of the old order and to the payment of letter fees.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Ammann and Court on the Tannenberg to detain their officials Uli Näff and his co-tenant in Lütisburg in order to enforce the judgment of the St. Gallen city court in the case against the weaver Sebastian Högger. Högger is to claim 100 gulden by obligation. The debtors had failed to make the payment despite the deadline. St. Gallen asks for payment including interest and costs.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Ammann and Court on the Tannenberg

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Luzern ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to prevent their citizens from disputing or refusing the Dugana in Piemont, which was granted to their Schultheiss and Stadtfendrich Sebastian Ritz. They refer to the payments already promised and Ritz's protestation in Baden. Furthermore, they ask that the citizen of St. Gallen Hans Lochler be cited to St. Gallen to examine a proper accounting of his administration, as the previous account is erroneous.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich remind St. Gallen of the request of the Confederates to cease minting smaller denominations, as this leads to inequality and inconvenience. They ask St. Gallen to refrain from minting until further notice and to align itself with the other cantons in order to avoid further disadvantages.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
