en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Confederate cities regarding the coinage question. They ask Zürich to inform them which coins are current there and how highly they are valued, as they themselves use only thaler for trade. They fear that the Chur coinage is being melted down in the neighborhood and converted into smaller coinage, which could lead to damage.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: The Ratsbotschaften of the seven Catholic cantons of the Confederation ask the Burgomaster and Council of Zürich, their lords and superiors, to admonish the cities of Basel and St. Gallen to conform with the other Confederates in matters of coinage. The continuation of coin minting by Basel and St. Gallen is burdensome to the Catholic cantons, as there is concern about the harmful withdrawal of coarser denominations. In the event of refusal, they would be compelled to resort to other means, which they, however, wished to avoid.
en.sender: Ratsbotschaften of the seven Catholic cantons of the Confederation
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich answer the inquiry of St. Gallen regarding coin minting. They state that they have ceased coin minting, and send an overview of the rates for common gold and silver coins. Furthermore, they report that they have prohibited new Bündner and Churer coins as well as new Haldensteinische coins due to quality defects.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Schwyz thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the special honor and friendship that has befallen their Landvogt in Rinthall. They assure them that they will not forget this for good and will serve St. Gallen in future cases, and recommend themselves to divine care.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to an inquiry from Appenzell as to whether the city had forbidden the half Konstanzer Örtlin. They deny this, as they were waiting for a conference with the Prelate of St. Gallen. However, they had instructed shopkeepers to report trade in these coins, as they were being smuggled in in large numbers and could lead to inconveniences. Furthermore, they had forbidden false Pfennige and would also forbid the Gwänder and Haldensteiner Örtlin.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Sebastian Zwickheren to compel his son to fulfill a promise. This concerns the daughter of the Schaffhausen citizen Ulrich Stierlin. If this is not observed, the son is to be punished according to city custom.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen answer the question of whether they would prohibit the collection of the half-Örtlin of Konstanz as well as Pfennige or Heller. They explain that they had not fundamentally prohibited the coins, but had merely instructed the merchants to report the mass introduction of these coins in order to avoid inconveniences. They further mention that they would also prohibit the coins forbidden by Zürich, and await the report of the Prelate of St. Gallen.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform them whether they have prohibited the new half Örtli and Pfennig. Appenzell has been informed that St. Gallen has done so. This contradicts the contract concluded a few years ago, according to which neither side may prohibit coins without the consent of the other.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant citizenship to their citizen Hans Rudolf Dumann, a joiner. Dumann has worked abroad for eighteen years and wishes to settle in St. Gallen, as he finds no opportunity in Zürich because of the many masters. The Zürich authorities request a favorable setting of the citizenship fee, as Dumann has a small fortune.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank the envoys of the 13 cantons for their earlier intervention with the Duke of Mailand in favor of the St. Gallen merchants Zolli, Schobinger, Schindlen and Zili. Since the envoy of the merchants has returned without an answer, the St. Gallen authorities ask the envoys to intervene again with the Duke so that the five little casks of money, which were confiscated by the royal ministers, are released.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Envoys of the 13 cantons to Baden

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about a goldsmith imprisoned in Zürich, who claims to be Philipp Rudolf von Erfurt and is said to have allegedly stolen in St. Gallen. They ask for information about the theft and the man. Furthermore, they report on troop movements of the Obristen von Lütisbach and Rinach in the Herrschaft Rötteln and ask St. Gallen to keep an eye on these troops and to inform them of further developments.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to treat the widow and children of the deceased St. Gallen church and school servant Ulrich Philipp Ochsner with goodwill upon their return to St. Gallen. They refer to Ochsner's thirteen years of loyal service as well as his low salary during the coinage increase and ask for support so that the family does not fall into oblivion.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen confirm the receipt of a letter concerning the grain merchants. They have admonished their merchants to observe the market regulations. Since a regulation prescribes that grain is to be procured from St. Gallen, they ask Überlingen to identify the citizens of St. Gallen as such, so that they can be distinguished from other grain merchants. They furthermore demand the punishment of those who do not adhere to the rules.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their grain merchants not to be too hasty in their purchases at the Überlingen market and not to drive up the prices. They refer to the market regulations, according to which purchases are to be made publicly and not agreed upon in inns, otherwise Überlingen will be forced to take countermeasures.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to pardon their citizen Christoph Schärer the Younger and to open the city and land to him again. Schärer has incurred debts because of the coinage crisis and must stay abroad. Zürich asks for an answer via the messenger to Zegringen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about the threat posed by a foreign military force around Basel and Müllhausen. They ask the Confederates to grant the four Evangelical cities a reinforcement of 300 to 400 men to support Müllhausen. Furthermore, they request St. Gallen to contribute to the costs of this reinforcement, as the Evangelical Wesen is in danger.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their Confederal Peter Wiser and his co-sureties. Wiser, who acts as guardian of the widow Maria Wäldlin, is owed 50 gulden by Johann Brunner from a settlement matter, which the latter has not paid despite an obligation. Zürich requests St. Gallen to instruct Brunner to settle the 50 gulden plus costs and to hand over the money as soon as possible to avoid further costs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Glarus thank St. Gallen for its long-standing support at the Confederates' Diets. As the Landammann has died, they ask St. Gallen to grant the vacant office of Landammann to their fellow councilor Albrecht Vogel. They refer to the fact that this office formerly came from the family Vogel and ask that other applicants be rejected. They promise to support St. Gallen in similar cases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Landammann and Council of the Inner and Outer Rode of the Land of Appenzell that on the same day they had received a letter from the French Queen from Field Marshal Haraucourt. In it, a pass through a Confederate canton towards the Bündner Lands is requested for a certain number of troops on horseback and on foot. Zürich informs Appenzell of the copies and offers its friendship.
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Inner and Outer Rode of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about the passage of 1200 French foot soldiers, several hundred horses, as well as Bernese and Valais regiments through their territory to support the French King. They request St. Gallen to protect the neighboring lordship of Sax from possible attacks or blockades by foreign aid and to defend it in case of emergency.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich invite Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to a meeting of the four Evangelical cities and the Outer Roden of Appenzell. This is to take place on 3 November in Zürich. The occasion is the occupation of Meilen and Steg by imperial troops and the danger of a new war. They wish to consult on how to defend themselves against a possible enemy and secure the passes.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform the Landammann and Council of the Inner and Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell that Archduke Leopold von Österreich again requests the withdrawal of the troops stationed in the Upper Margraviate of Baden. They send a copy of the Archduke's reply and ask Appenzell to comment on the matter if necessary. Zürich itself has already granted troops to the Queen of France.
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Inner and Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report that the citizen of St. Gallen Wolfgang Haller refuses to acknowledge the judgment of the great Council of St. Gallen in a debt matter with the citizen of St. Gallen Ulrich Rietmann. Haller claims that Rietmann did not demand the debt. Zürich asks St. Gallen to instruct Rietmann to pay Haller the accrued interest or to prove in writing that he had terminated the principal.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have appointed a general court day for their departed citizen Michael Albrecht and his wife Margarethe Dietrichin. They ask the authorities of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish the relevant edict according to their custom, so that no creditors are shorted.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to an inquiry by the Landvogt regarding the arrest of the Thal subject Christen Lutz for a debt to the St. Gallen woman Magdalena Werni. They refer to the neighboring treaties, according to which no mutual arrests are to be permitted, and object to the judgment of the court at Thal. Furthermore, they point out that the disputed debt did not belong to the deceased husband Jacob Tobel, but to his widow as free property. They request the Landvogt to lift the arrest and return the sold horses.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Johann Durler, Landvogt of the upper and lower Rhine Valley

en.regest: Leopold, Archduke of Österreich, confirms the observance of the inheritance union and asks the 13 cantons to demand the departure of unknown troops that have passed through their territory and established themselves on the Steig, or to dismiss their commanders. He warns of a danger to the peace and asks for an urgent answer.
en.recipient: Burgomasters, Schultheiss, Landammann and Councils of the 13 cantons

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Burgomaster and Council of Leutkirch about the state of the legal dispute between their citizen Sebastian Zollihofer and the Leutkirch innkeeper Hans Tischler. Since the statements of the witnesses are contradictory, they have suspended the proceedings for one month to allow room for further evidence. They ask Leutkirch to inform their kinsman of this.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Leutkirch

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel their citizen Jörg Hochreuter, shoemaker, to pay the outstanding debt to the Ulm citizen Claus Marcks, tanner. Marcks has been ill for a long time and is in urgent need of the money. The payment has already been overdue for a long time. Ulm asks for superior assistance so that Marcks is not further harassed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Secret Council of the city of Zürich inform the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen about the results of the latest Aargau meeting. They confirm the oral declaration of the envoys, according to which the Confederates in an emergency want to defend their freedoms with life, property, and blood and to support one another. Since they consider the written version of the draft to be questionable for certain reasons, they ask St. Gallen to be content with the oral report and this summary reminder.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Secret Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen address the Landvogt of the County of Thurgau. They have learned that the Landgerichtsknecht Felix Engeli from Sulgen had spoken to their citizen Hans Rietler in Kappel regarding the case of his deceased wife. They consider this a novelty, as their citizens, being free Confederates, were not subject to serfdom. They ask the Landvogt to mandate Engeli not to further harass Rietler, and expect a written reply.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt of the County of Thurgau

en.regest: Melchior Lussi, Landvogt in Thurgau, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their fellow citizen Hans Appenzeller to pay the fine of 29 florins 6½ schillings owed to him for the purchase of the inn Schwinlehen. Appenzeller had promised to make the payment within three weeks and is guaranteed by Sebastian Dober. Lussi requests payment in order to avoid further costs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johannes Büler, Landvogt im Ober- und Unterrheintal, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a report from the monastery of Thal. The latter complains about an arrest that the citizen of St. Gallen Andreas Herr has placed on 50 florins with Klaus Lützen in Thal. The monastery of Thal refers to old customs and rights vis-à-vis St. Gallen and claims that the debt belongs to the abbot's servant. Büler asks the St. Gallen authorities to hear the case patiently and to request Andreas Herr to justify himself.
en.sender: Johannes Büler, Landvogt im Ober- und Unterrheintal
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Zürich to support the heiress of the butcher Othmar Abbenzeller. She had pledged her own property for the legal disputes of her brother with Hans Schüffelberger from Hirtswilen. Her brother-in-law Zacharias Schmid had taken possession of the property and promised her 20 gulden, which he does not pay. The St. Gallen ask Zürich to instruct the bailiff of Grüningen to help the woman obtain her right.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Landvogt Melchior Lussi to refrain from the renewed summons of their citizen Hans Weiser to the Landgericht in Frauenfeld regarding a claim of his deceased wife. They refer to the fact that their citizens are not serfs and demand a written explanation of the facts.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Melchior Lussi, Landvogt of the lower and upper Thurgau

en.regest: The Richter and Council of Mels ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their neighbor Peter Müller in the collection of a debt owed to the citizen of St. Gallen Balthasar Schmid. Müller says that he sold oxen to Schmid, but the payment is still outstanding. Mels offers similar services in return.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen respond to the request of the St. Gallen to inquire into the origin of defamatory remarks. They state that they have investigated with their citizen and shipper, who had taken Jacob Schmidlin of Arbon across the sea. The latter stated that Jacob Abt had been taken prisoner in St. Gallen and that his head had been cut off on Friday night. Schmidlin had said nothing of an attack on the monastery. A misunderstanding had therefore arisen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the information regarding the recruitment of a regiment of Landsknechte by the Freiherr von Pappenheim. They state that they will endeavor to obtain further information. Due to the threat to the evangelical cantons by Spanish troops and the uncertainty regarding the intentions of the Confederates, they call for a joint assembly on 2. February in Zürich to deliberate on defense.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admit their resident, Joachim Zollikoffer, the tailor, as a citizen. Zollikoffer wishes to settle in St. Gallen and has already acquired a house there. In Zürich, he has behaved honestly and piously for the last seventeen years. The citizens of Zürich request a willing admission so that he may spend his twilight years there.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about the arrival of 6000 foot and 600 horse in Steckborn, who are to march across Lake Constance to Rorschach and Rinfelden. They ask St. Gallen to send out scouts to clarify the intentions of the army, and offer, in case of danger, 300 musketeers via the Vogt of Kyburg.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz forward the petitions of the citizens of St. Gallen Hans Öheli and Kaspar Reiner. They explain that the paternal and maternal property of the wife of Konrad Reiner is not blocked or retained, but has remained undivided due to pending legal disputes of the heirs until the matter is clarified. They ask the St. Gallen authorities not to impose any costs on the petitioners.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Konrad Stauder and Thomas Schobig ask the Administrator of the Hauptmannschaft, Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, to confirm to them in writing that the paternal and maternal inheritance of their sister-in-law Salome Oderlin is not being withheld by the city of St. Gallen. They fear that a false rumor about this might prevent their brother-in-law Konrad Winder from making a will in favor of his wife.
en.sender: Hans Konrad Stauder and Thomas Schobig
en.recipient: Administrator of the Hauptmannschaft, Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for reports on war troops that have arrived at Rorschach and the Enden and are marching against Rapperswil. They ask to continue watching the troops and to inform them at any time of further developments. Zürich declares itself ready to also watch the foreign troops, to keep itself in readiness, and to assist St. Gallen in case of emergency.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen confirm the receipt of a letter from Landvogt Melchior Lussi dated 26 January 1625, which concerns the Gwandtfall of the deceased wife of the St. Gallen citizen Hans Weiler. They ask for forgiveness that they cannot attend the day set for 26 January at Sulgen due to unforeseen business. They ask to be given a new date on which they wish to communicate their opinion and inform the Landvogt.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Melchior Lussi, Landvogt of the upper and lower Turgau

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the confidential news about the troops passing through at Rorschach. They offer their help again and have already sent out 300 men under the Landsschreiber Hans Ulrich Hegner the Younger, who are available at the first command.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Uri request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admonish their citizens, who trade in Italien, not to further threaten or harm the Uri Landvogt Hans Jacob Muheim. Muheim has not participated in the St. Gallen [affair]. Uri threatens countermeasures if Muheim suffers harm.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the report on the foreign war troop moving from Rorschach to Liechtensteig. They share that the troop has also been held up at Rapperswil and at the Gotthard, because the pass has been newly cut and the weather is bad. Furthermore, provisions are lacking. Zürich has sent messengers to explore the situation and will inform St. Gallen immediately. They know nothing about the pass for the Ländler. They ask for further reports and promise support from the Confederates.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about rumors that a regiment of 800 men from Lindau will march via Rheineck into the Rhine Valley and attempt a raid there, which Count Salm is to follow. They ask for clarification through scouts and for military support in the Rhine Valley and in Sax, should violence occur.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help the three brothers Jakob, Jörg and Thomas Thoma, the sons of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Joseph Oewe. They request that the inheritance of the three peasants of Appenzell be settled quickly and at low cost, so that they do not have to delay their affairs for long.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of the outer Rode of the Land of Appenzell inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the statements of several witnesses. These confirm that the miller's wife Ulrich Möttelis had uttered gross abusive words against the Landammann Konrad Zellweger. She claimed, among other things, that Zellweger had unlawfully taken the cattle of her brother-in-law Hans Kuhn and withheld her share from her. The Appenzellers ask for neighborly friendship.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the outer Rode of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report that they had previously kept deer in their city moat, but have now unfortunately lost the fawns and possess only two living deer. Since the Count is well provided with big game in his forests, they ask him to give them a pair of fawns in order to repopulate the city moat.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Hugo Graf von Montfort und Rottenfels

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Count Hugo zu Montfort for a pair of fawns for the town tower, as they have lost their game through misfortune. They refer to the Count's promise to supply them with big game and offer their services in return.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Hugo Count zu Montfort und Rottefelß

en.regest: Hans Graf zu Montfort informs that he has ordered his forester to procure a pair of young bucks for St. Gallen, which would then be delivered immediately. Furthermore, he requests written information regarding the settlement with his mint administrator Pietro Giovanni Fachinetto, in particular regarding the quantities of silver delivered between 1. November 1621 and the present time and the coins received for them.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to expedite the legal dispute between the Lochmannische Gesellschaft and Jacob Stueben. The plaintiffs Michael Wildinastern and Endreß Olern had already had themselves represented by a lawyer with power of attorney, but the proceedings are being delayed due to the negligence of the lawyer Caspar Maijer. The people of Konstanz ask that the trial be accelerated so that it comes to a final judgment.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Count Hugo zu Montfort for the sending of two Heinen for the restoration of the city moat. They report that their mint officials had never personally negotiated with Herr Fachineti, but that he may possibly have delivered silver to the mint through his factors. The officials have now drawn up a specification of the delivered silver vessels, which is presented to the Count.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Count Hugo zu Montfort

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank the Count for the assurance to provide further carriages for the restoration of the salt market. They report that the salt administrator had handed over a specification regarding silver deliveries to the mint by Herr Fachineti. As they had never negotiated directly with Fachineti, they ask the Count to verify the details and to transmit the specification to them.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Count von Toggenburg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the city of Konstanz. They report that beef and veal have hitherto been sold at the same prices. Since the cattle had been difficult to obtain and much of it came from Bayern, the best ox meat had been valued more highly. The pound of meat weighs forty Lot. They ask for neighborly consideration.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to an inquiry from the Landammänner and Council of Appenzell regarding the heirs of the deceased citizen and hospital pensioner Josef Küner. They report that they had examined Küner's estate and had a citizen detained, but had found nothing. A woman had owed Küner wages, but this was uncertain. Since the creditor Thurn owed more than he had redeemed, they ask Appenzell to provide for itself.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a written report on the meat prices there, in particular for beef and roast meat, as well as on the weight of the pound and the existing regulations for butchers. They wish to inquire of the citizens of St. Gallen in order to remedy their own deficiencies among their butchers.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Haug Graf zu Montfort confirms the receipt of a letter from the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen. He accedes to the wish for coinage, as soon as he has received it. He thanks them for the transmitted designation and promises to reciprocate accordingly.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist the widow Anna Murer, daughter of the late Doctor Hans Jakob Muralt, in an inheritance matter. It concerns the question of whether certain debts of her late brother Doctor Hector Muralt have already been settled. The widow Murer, according to a judgment in Zürich, was awarded only 763 gulden. Zürich requests St. Gallen to support the Murer in this matter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Frauenfeld report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a great shortage of butchery goods in their territory. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to inform their master butchers that they would be welcome in Frauenfeld, and promise to make similar efforts in return in similar cases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish an edict concerning a court day appointed for the creditors of the citizen of Lindau Hans Schöffler, so that no one be curtailed in their rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Obervogt Beat Jakob Segesser von Brunegg to compel his subject Wilhelm Haberlin to pay the citizen of St. Gallen Daniel Schlumpf 42 gulden 12 kreuzer as well as 5 gulden 40 kreuzer surety with interest. Schlumpf has repeatedly asserted the claim without success and asks for official support in order to be able to maintain his family.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Beat Jakob Segesser von Brunegg, Council and Obervogt of the Lordship of Arbon

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen remind Georg Ludwig von Freyberg of their request of 23. Mai 1625 concerning their citizen Hans Melchior Heinemann. As they have not yet received an answer, they ask him to grant them a gracious answer as soon as possible, so that the dispute may be settled and Heinemann may come to his right.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Georg Ludwig von Freyberg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to question their citizen Thomas Schirmer whether a chest seized in Zürich, which is marked with the sign of the merchant Carellen of Turin, belongs to him. The citizen of Zürich Caspar Sauter, to whom the property was originally attached due to a debt of 1000 florins, denies the ownership by Schirmer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their subject of the court, Balthasar Hasler, to obtain the 77 gulden owed to him by the citizen of St. Gallen, Bernhard Ziegler, for purchased salt. Hasler has so far been unable to obtain the payment despite repeated urging and is urgently in need of the outstanding amount.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen report that they have taken inventory of the estate of the deceased citizen Friedrich Heissen. As hardly any tanned goods were found and the widow reports only minor debts, open edicts are issued. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to assert their claims arising from the sale of three horses and from the estate before the city court of Memmingen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel their citizen Leonhart Laubacher, shoemaker, to pay a due installment of 35 gulden plus interest and costs to the Ulm citizen Wilhelm Rayel, tanner. Rayel has already granted Laubacher a grace period and delivered leather, but Laubacher wants to pay only upon renewed delivery. Ulm asks for official compulsion to avoid further efforts.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their countryman Heinrich Koller vom Espich. He says that he had amicably settled a dispute with a citizen of St. Gallen and had committed himself to 20 florins. Since the payment had not been made, Koller had filed a lawsuit. Appenzell requests the St. Gallen authorities to urge the citizen to pay in order to avoid further costs.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform them whether the deceased woman of St. Gallen, Barbara Kumin, had made a will. They request an inventory of her estate and the sending of copies, so that Zürich, as relatives, could provide for the orphan left behind by her.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Prince-Bishop of Konstanz answers the supplication of Johann Heinrich Scheitlin. Scheitlin had demanded the repayment of 830 gulden, which the Chamber had received from the sale of his grain purchases confiscated in Konstanz and Feldkirch. In addition, it concerned two fields in St. Gallen. The Prince-Bishop states that he has not yet decided, as Scheitlin has given him satisfaction. Scheitlin has stated that he has not engaged in smuggling and has transported the metal to Lindau, although he had brought it to St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Johann Heinrich Scheitlin

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Landvogt in Thurgau to exert influence on the debtors of the Leprosarium, Claus Andreas Steg and Andreas Koch. These are indebted to the Office for 141 florins of principal and 200 fuder of hay annually, but have not paid the interest. The Landvogt is to instruct the debtors to make the payments and to present themselves to the Office.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt in Thurgau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lütkirch remind Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of their letter of 25 October concerning the deceased Lütkirch citizen Barbara Dünnin. Since no answer has been received, they say that they have instructed their citizen Hans Wieblern to demand an inventory of the estate and to take the bequeathed goods to themselves. They request the St. Gallen authorities to grant Wieblern all favorable assistance in this matter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their fellow councillor and citizen Thomas Zwickher to enable the judicial service to his brother-in-law Ulrich Wirlin after the expiry of the agreed year. Wirlin has already postponed the matter several times because of his daughter, but now he needs a final decision. Schaffhausen asks for a reply.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information on whether the bakers there bake by weight or how the bread inspection is otherwise handled. The bakers of Lindau had complained about the practice there and claimed that in the neighborhood it is done differently. Lindau had already inquired with other cantons.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizen Johann Jäsele, who claims a remaining sum of 71 Reichsthaler, 1 Schilling and 15 Pfennig from Daniel Wetter and his mother Barbara Wetterin, in the payment. They refer to the dire straits of Jäsele and ask for a quick and just payment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Hoefele asks the Council of Memmingen for an intercession with the Magistracy of the city of St. Gallen. He says that he has a claim of 71 Reichsthaler, 1 gulden and 19 kreuzer against the widow Barbara Wetterin and her son Daniel Wetter. Since the father of the family has passed away and left an inheritance, he asks that the debtors be urged to pay the remaining amount.
en.recipient: Council of Memmingen

en.regest: The Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform that the dispute between the St. Gallen citizen Hans Melchior Haimmen and the resident of Konstanz Johann Cappitel has been settled. Haimmen has issued a receipt in which he waives all claims against Cappitel. The people of Konstanz send a copy of the receipt to St. Gallen, so that they can quiet Haimmen in the event of new complaints.
en.sender: Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Glarus ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Hans-Jakob Lapsi to return the cloak of the Glarus schoolmaster Johannes Richter. The latter had mistakenly taken the cloak of the St. Gallen citizen on 9 October 1625 at the Wilder Mann inn in Glarus. Glarus offers to return its own cloak unchanged, provided Lapsi covers any possible damages and costs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Lindau to intervene on behalf of their citizen Daniel Studer. He says that he cannot pay the withdrawal fee for an inheritance in Lindau, as his brothers-in-law had kept the best bonds. The St. Gallen ask Lindau to persuade the brothers-in-law to support Studer with 600 florin in cash or surety, or to accept the best bonds themselves.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: Johann Bueller, Landvogt in the lower and upper Rintal, asks Burgomaster Ambros Schlumpf of St. Gallen to send his appointed executioner Hans to Altstetten on the following Tuesday at 8 o'clock in the morning to perform his duty in a matter of inzeug. He offers the town constable three batzen as wages.
en.sender: Johann Bueller, Landvogt in the lower and upper Rintal
en.recipient: Ambros Schlumpf, Burgomaster of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Burgomaster and Council of Altdorf about the debt matter of Mathias Wanner. They have sent Christof Büchler and Heinrich Bodmer as proxies for the appointed day of negotiation. These are to set out in detail and liquidate the claims of the city of St. Gallen against Wanner. The St. Gallen ask Altdorf to give credence to the proxies, to support them in the matter, and, in the event that an amicable settlement does not come about, to hold swift justice and protect the St. Gallen claims.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Altdorf

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Georg Joachim Zollikofer to report to Hauptmann von Innöfres and deliver the promised soldiers, or to come to an agreement with him. Zollikofer had accepted the Fendrich position and committed himself to recruiting one hundred men, but did not appear. Zürich wishes to avoid the breach of military law and asks for mediation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ottilia Zollikofer, widow of the late Johann Lorenz Zollikofer, thanks Burgomaster Hans Heinrich Holtzhalb in Zürich for his efforts in the matter of her son Georg Joachim and a German youth. She considers the youth's claim unfounded and his attorney not sufficiently authorized. A relative will shortly travel to Zürich to give further instructions. She asks Holtzhalb to continue doing the best so that the merchant may come to certainty.
en.sender: Ottilia, widow of the late Johann Lorenz Zollikofer, née Zill, citizen of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Hans Heinrich Holtzhalb, Burgomaster of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg report on the interrogation of the witness Maria Blarerin in the dispute between Catharina Wetzelin and Maria Hagenbacherin. The witness denies having sewn clothes for Wetzelin or received fabrics, and confirms only having sewn bedding from barchent. Hagenbacherin did not appear for the hearing, whereupon the interrogation was nevertheless carried out.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The letter contains only the salutation to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen as special friends. The actual text is missing.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen about the circulation of false Reich thalers, which in their stamp are identical to the genuine ones but are lighter and consist of copper and tin. They send an enclosed specimen for warning and ask to inform their own subjects, to determine the origin of the coins, and to return the piece so that other cantons can also be warned.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen not to regard the engagement of their citizen Hans Heinrich Kläßer to the Schaffhausen woman Barbara Moser as a violation of the condition not to marry elsewhere. The engagement took place before the condition was imposed. They request that Kläßer be treated graciously and that his fiancée be admitted as a citizen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Chancery of St. Gallen informs that the community and service of the city of Frauenfeld, at their request, has collected a tax of six hundred Reichsthalers. This is to be distributed to the needy in Frauenfeld. Peter Koch, the eldest of the gentlemen, is commissioned to receive the money against receipt and to distribute it accordingly.
en.recipient: Peter Koch

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform that they have appointed a general court day for their departed citizen Jeronimus Dohmen. They ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish the edict, so that any creditors from St. Gallen may also register their claims and no one is curtailed in their rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss, Burgomaster and Council of Frankenthal thank St. Gallen for the donation of 600 Reichsthaler. They assure that the money will be distributed among the poor citizens and neighboring communities who have fallen into distress through the war. They ask for prayer and promise to keep St. Gallen in remembrance.
en.sender: Schultheiss, Burgomaster and Council of Frankenthal
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant the widow Salome Örtlin the withdrawal from the citizenship of St. Gallen. They refer to the power of attorney she has granted to her guardians and confirm that in Konstanz every citizen may freely withdraw with his property without additional tax or deduction. They ask for neighborly consideration and for a written confirmation of the free withdrawal.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The heirs of the deceased Kempten Master Builder and Privy Councillor Hans Zoller ask the Council of Kempten to intervene with the Council of St. Gallen. They demand the release of a principal obligation left by the deceased David Schobinger, as well as vidimated copies of obligations and accounts that Duchess Felicitas von Savoyen had given to the St. Gallen families Schobinger, Scherrer and Schlumpf.
en.sender: Heirs of the deceased Master Builder and Privy Councillor Hans Zoller of Kempten
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen not to prevent their citizens Heinrich Beyer and Alexander Ziegler from having linen purchased in St. Gallen collected by hired carriers. Merchants of St. Gallen had attempted to hold the goods and to obtain an official order. Schaffhausen refers to the fact that the carriers are contractually bound and threatens to grant official assistance in turn if damage is done to the goods of the citizens of St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Kempten request Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen to provide the heirs of the Seelischen with the desired copies free of charge and to effectively grant them the rights previously assigned to them. In return, Kempten offers equal and further friendly services.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Kempten
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to a complaint by the citizens of Schaffhausen Lorenz Feigen and Alexander Ziegler regarding alleged seizures of their goods. They reject the accusation and explain that they only act in legal disputes concerning muleteers and their animals. They ask Schaffhausen to settle future complaints in a Confederate manner, and warn of countermeasures in the event of attacks on goods of St. Gallen.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen

en.regest: Johann Beeler, Landvogt in the lower and upper Rintal at Rheineck, congratulates Burgomaster Lorenz Stauden on his new office and asks him to grant the executioner Hans permission to perform his duties in the Old Town on the coming Monday, the 18. May, at 9 o'clock, as he has fulfilled his own duties on that day.
en.sender: Johann Beeler, Landvogt in the lower and upper Rintal at Rheineck
en.recipient: Burgomaster Lorenz Stauden of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann, Baumeister and Council of the parish of Tüffen request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to readmit Ulrich Lindemann, who has fallen into disgrace there, into grace and to place him under their protection. Lindemann says that he behaved honestly as a guest in Tüffen and departed from there with good knowledge and will. The people of Tüffen ask for this favor in order to promote Lindemann's prosperity.
en.sender: Landammann, Baumeister and Small and Great Council of the parish of Tüffen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen reply to a letter of 20 April. They reject the complaint that their merchants had seized goods. They ask that the St. Gallen muleteers not be prevented from loading goods, and refer to the friendship of the Confederates.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Caspar Bueler, bailiff of Bischofszell, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, at the request of the Council of St. Gallen, he has taken the testimony of witnesses in a legal dispute between Christoph von Stein and the citizen of St. Gallen Catharina Muraltin. He transmits the sworn statements of the witnesses, which concern defamatory remarks made by Muraltin regarding the wife of Steins.
en.sender: Caspar Bueler von Schwyz, bailiff of Bischofszell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizen Gottfried Ganter in collecting a claim of 50 florins plus interest from the St. Gallen citizen Hans Halder. The debt is already due and Ganter has already made several unsuccessful demands. Lindau asks for sovereign assistance so that Ganter may receive his money without further delay.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the kindness, honour and hospitality shown to their Council members Hirtzel and Grebel during their recent stay in Sax. In return, they offer all services of the Confederates and friendship.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: A citizen of St. Gallen addresses the Burgomaster and Council, as the heirs of the deceased Hans Herlens of Kempten are demanding vidimized copies of accounts. The sender considers this a pretext to obtain reprisals against the city and its subjects through the Imperial Majesty. He refers to a settlement concluded two years ago, according to which the parties were to act jointly and not negotiate with third parties. He asks the Council to refuse the heirs the release of the copies, as he himself does not possess any further copies and does not wish to separate himself from the fellow citizens Schobinger and Spindler.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen forward to Burgomaster and Council of Kempten the answer of their citizens Schobinger, Schindleri and Scherer to the supplication of the Helische heirs. The citizens of St. Gallen adhere to the settlement of 1624 and ask Kempten to restrain its citizens from reprisals and to admonish them to patience. St. Gallen refuses the surrender of documents and protests against the intended legal steps of the Helische heirs.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz confirm to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the citizens of Konstanz, with their person and property, whether inherited or acquired, may move freely to St. Gallen or other places, free from Abzug and Nachsteuer. They ask for a certificate of this custom, so that the bailiff there, Salomo Zettlin, may present it.
en.sender: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Matthias Peyer im Hof, Statthalter and Council of the court of Yl, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to mandate the citizen of St. Gallen Sebastian Zwickher so that he presents himself in Yl. The woman of St. Gallen Barbara Wirtlin complains that Zwickher seduced her, fathered a child, and left her sitting without answer for four years. She asks for legal clarification of the marriage promises and the committed mistreatment.
en.sender: Matthias Peyer im Hof, Statthalter and Council of the court of Yl
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten reply to a declaration by the citizens of St. Gallen Schobinger, Knecht and Beyständer. They ask the citizens of St. Gallen not to neglect the redemption, as it concerns a small amount, and warn of the danger that the way to the Emperor may be blocked. They thank them for the withdrawal regarding Hans Ulrich Dorn and offer their services.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ples request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hand over the estate of the deceased goldsmith Abraham Gemünder, which is kept in St. Gallen, to his widow Salomena and her second husband Hans Froelich as the authorized representatives of their son Christoph Gemünder. They refer to previous correspondence and request the prompt fulfillment of the legal claim.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Landvogt Mußler to instruct the heirs of the deceased bailiff Caspar Zwyer, Felix Caspar Meyer and Christoph Stössel, to leave the citizen of St. Gallen Sebastian Krenn in peace. Krenn had already won a judgment against the heirs in 1622. However, the heirs had challenged the matter again. St. Gallen calls on Mußler to dismiss the heirs or refer them to the court of St. Gallen.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Hans Mußler, Landvogt of Upper and Lower Toggenburg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the Landvogt in the Rhine Valley regarding his letter concerning the wine trade of the farms St. Margretha, Thal, Untergraben and Lochbach. They refer to the settlement of 1618 and explain that they have always behaved peacefully. They ask the Landvogt to admonish the farms to accept the judgment. Otherwise, they are ready to hear the complaints themselves.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Balthasar von Ott, Landvogt in the lower and upper Rhine Valley

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen reply to a letter of 24 June concerning the heirs of Fehlen and the citizens of St. Gallen Nöringer, Schindler, Weren and Schreiner. They request the original or a certified copy of a letter which Othmar Schreiner is said to have addressed to Josua Fehlen on 29 April 1622. At the same time, they send a copy of the power of attorney granted to the heirs of Fehlen in relation to the Rheimer.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Exiled parish priests from the Palatinate tract Via Montana ask the Bishop and the Cathedral Chapter of St. Gallen for financial support. They describe their plight after being dismissed and expelled from their parishes by the Elector, the high cost of living in exile in Worms, and the confiscation of their property. They refer to the known generosity of the St. Gallen towards other needy persons and ask for help.
en.sender: Exiled parish priests from the Palatinate tract Via Montana (among others Johannes Adam Eckhet, Christoph Koecher, Johannes Sigismund, Philipp Parlen, Philipp Heußer, Christoph Andreae)
en.recipient: Bishop and Cathedral Chapter of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Johann Heinrich Schaidle to settle an outstanding debt with interest and costs to the Nürnberg gunsmith Michael Dolawer. Dolawer says that he handed pistols to Schaidle, which the latter did not return but gave away.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Administrator of the Hauptmannschaft, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they had moved the Kirchweihmarkt scheduled for September by a few days to 22 September 1626. They ask for this news to be passed on to the market participants.
en.sender: Administrator of the Hauptmannschaft, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Altstätten together with the estates Marbach and Bernang request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to allow the wine run before the Weni, as this would be beneficial for both the Rhine Valley and St. Gallen. They refer to the fact that they had recently been in St. Gallen to request this, but had not yet received a final answer. They hope for a favorable answer for the good of the city of St. Gallen.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of Altstätten together with the estates Marbach and Bernang
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Expelled Palatine pastors ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a tax for the expelled Palatines living in the Upper Palatinate and the Margraviate. They describe their distress caused by expulsion, plundering, and lack of salary. They promise to distribute the funds as needed and thank for previous support.
en.sender: Expelled Palatine pastors (among others Johannes Cüner and Georgius Summer)
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Kempten report that the Duke of Bayern had kept coins at too low a value, which was causing them a loss of over 20'000 gulden. As they could not raise the money, they ask St. Gallen for a loan of 8'000 or 10'000 gulden against security and interest.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Court of Goldach request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to examine the citizen of St. Gallen Michael Schreiber as a witness in a legal dispute between the heirs of Caspar Fromenweyler and the heirs of Jakob Lindemann. They ask that Schreiber be bound by the usual witness oath and that the testimony be transmitted in writing and sealed to the Court of Goldach.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Landammann and Council of Appenzell to give credit to their Councilor Dr. Sebastian Schöbinger. He is to communicate to them a complaint by the other court lords of the Hof concerning the Rheintal wine run, which violates old breaches and customs. They request neighborly compliance.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Council of Kempten dated the 7th of the month regarding a requested loan. They ask for forgiveness that they cannot comply with the request, as the city treasury is heavily burdened by high expenses in these difficult times. They offer their help for other matters.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask St. Gallen to suspend the negotiations with the Unter-Rheinische Gemeinden regarding the Wyülouff until the envoys of the Badische Järrächtnung in the Rheintal arrive. They propose to increase the number of assessors by four persons and to make the Wyülouff after eight days. The final decision is to be reserved for the future Badische Järrächtnung.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Stadtrichter and Council of Arbon ask the Amtsbürgermeister of St. Gallen to proceed against the violation of the prohibition on the trade in grapes. They report that some Arbon citizens would be selling grapes in St. Gallen. They request that the merchants be identified, that the grapes be taken from them without payment, and that the names be sent to Arbon so that they can be punished.
en.recipient: Amtsbürgermeister of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Landammann and Council of the Land of Appenzell to help the St. Gallen bleacher Anton Schowlin to recover his stolen linen. Anna Knorin, who was captured in Appenzell, had facilitated the theft by her husband. St. Gallen requests Appenzell to intervene with the Vogtin of the Knorin so that Schowlin is compensated. In return, St. Gallen promises to treat the prisoner kindly.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: The bailiff and Council of Bischofzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to exert influence on the citizen of St. Gallen Melchior Scherer. He has promised the widow Anna Scherbin, daughter of the deceased Burgomaster of St. Gallen Jakob Reutlinger, 300 gulden from her inheritance, which she needs for her livelihood and the improvement of her dwelling. Nothing has happened so far. Bischofzell requests that Scherer be moved to pay at least 200 gulden.
en.sender: The bailiff and Council of Bischofzell
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for their neighborly goodwill. They communicate that they will lower the Konstanz pfennigs, as proposed by St. Gallen, to half, namely thirty-two for one batzen, and intend to accept and pay them on Wednesday.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to give credence to their fellow councillor and Statthalter Michael Stür, who is arriving for business reasons, and to treat him in a neighborly manner. They promise to support St. Gallen in similar cases in a neighborly manner as well.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Landvogt Brandenberg to lift the complaint of the community of Wilen against Jacob Zwinger. They refer to the fact that the fiefs of Wartau and the lordship of Werdenberg are affected by the matter. They demand that the community of Wilen be instructed to conform to the old custom and to withdraw the complaint.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Niklaus Brandenberg, Landvogt in Lower and Upper Turgau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to postpone the division of the estate of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Thomas Reiner until a certain date. They request that the siblings of Elisabeth Reinerin, the wife of the citizen of Ravensburg Jürgen Bruggers, be persuaded to contribute their received dowries, so that Elisabeth as heir receives her share and equality among the siblings is established.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The community of Grüsch in the Vorderrheintal informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that their houses and churches were severely damaged by the Landstrafen. They ask for a contribution towards the restoration of the church and the purchase of bells. For this purpose, Hans Hartmann Gadiant and Michel Hutz were appointed as envoys.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask their Confederates in Basel to support the citizens of St. Gallen Felix Züblin, Hanns Flader and Jacob Flader. The citizen of Basel Manuel Wider owes them money for linen purchased, which has been due for a year and a half. As Wider is in negotiation with other creditors, the St. Gallen side asks for superior authority's help so that the claim is settled.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Basel

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Basel to instruct the Basel citizen Samuel Wider to pay or secure the 950 gulden 22 batzen 2 heller owed to them for linen to Felix Züblin, the heirs of Hans Ebneter and Jacob Cuentz. The creditors had long tolerated Wider, but he is now in negotiation with other creditors and has not informed them of anything.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Basel

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Basel reply to an intercession letter from St. Gallen regarding a claim against the Basel citizen Samuel Mida. Since Mida had declared himself willing to meet the creditors by a short deadline, they had not been able to press him further. They ask the St. Gallen to keep their citizens patient for a little longer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Samuel Midot declares to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he cannot pay his creditors due to missing books and the absence of his brother-in-law Israel Saltzman. He asks for patience until after Easter, in order to settle honestly and to protect his reputation.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg remind Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of their letter of 15 January 1627, in which they had intervened for their citizen Jürgen Büttzer and his wife Elisabeth Reinerin. Since no reply has yet been received, they ask again to move the Reiner children and heirs to make the due disposition and to help the Ravensburgers.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Amtleute of the Lordship of Rotenburg ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene on behalf of Barbara Baertschin of Deilingen. She has been excluded from the inheritance by the heirs of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen, Michael Haintzelman, the widow Juditha Stähelin and her sisters. The Amtleute request the St. Gallen authorities to support Barbara Baertschin in her rights.
en.sender: Amtleute of the Lordship of Rotenburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rottweil ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to restrain their Confederates Othmar Kunz and his co-parties to pay the Rottweil fellow citizens Johann Martin Weber and Johann Zobell for a contractually guaranteed performance. They refer to the existing Confederation and ask for prompt fulfillment to relieve the supplicants.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Landvogt Peter Bücher of Lenzburg that they have, upon the application of other creditors, inventoried and seized the assets of the St. Gallen citizen Lorenz Rohen, a hospital almoner. They set a court day for 23 April and ask Bücher to notify his officials Samuel Jebliher and Hans Löher of Egnach as well as other creditors of the Abbey of St. Gallen of this date and to have the proclamation made according to the custom of the land.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Peter Bücher, Landvogt of Lenzburg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ybbs ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Michel Barthen in a legal matter against the merchants Rietreithe and consorts. Barthen has filed a petition in which he requests the examination of witnesses and the submission of trade books to clarify a claim from the years 1599 to 1612. Ybbs asks St. Gallen to offer Barthen a helping hand so that he may come to his right.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Michael Sandt asks the Council of Yssny for a letter of intercession to the Council of St. Gallen. He is in dispute with the St. Gallen merchant companies Schobloch, Seeleben and Zollikoffer over unpaid linen deliveries from the years 1599 to 1612. Sandt demands the handover of the trade books and annual accounts in order to clarify the outstanding claims and settle the legal dispute.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Yssny

en.regest: Johannes Cuntz and Georg Summer, expelled members of the Palatine church, thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a donation of 1200 gulden transmitted by the Nuremberg messenger Andreas Weigelin. They report that the money is being distributed to the needy persons named in the enclosure, and they commend the donors to prayer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the heirs of the deceased Rosina Zollikoferin to pay Schultheiss Marx Schultzeis and his ward the 45 gulden due to them from the lease capital of 1500 gulden. The payment is owed according to the endowment deed and inheritance contract. Konstanz requests neighborly help to avoid a costly lawsuit.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the practice in creditors' matters. They explain that secured creditors are paid from their pledges. Unsecured creditors, whether citizens or foreigners, are included in the common mass without preference for the citizens. Each receives his share pro rata, insofar as the funds suffice.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Leopold, Archduke of Österreich, responds to an intercession by the citizen of St. Gallen Johann Conrad Schaublin. He points out that Schaublin had already been released in writing. He agrees to the return of the metal seized in Konstanz in 1621 only if Schaublin proves that he did not bring the metal into the mint, but delivered it to the city of St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Archduke to their citizen Johann Heinrich Schaitlin. They state that they never commissioned Schaitlin to deliver metal, and that they had only purchased and paid for the metal he brought. They had offered two pieces to the Teutonic Order for repayment. They ask the Archduke to be lenient towards their citizen.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Leopold, Archduke of Österreich

en.regest: The Stadtschultheiss and Council of Feldkirch reply to a letter of the 14th of the month, saying that they had dispatched a messenger to collect the documents in the said matter. As soon as the documents arrive in three days, a date will be set for the parties. They ask to be informed when this has been done.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landvogt Melchior Gisler to instruct the heirs of the deceased Caspar Meier, Felix Caspar Meier and Christoph Scheufel, to desist from the lawsuit against the citizen of St. Gallen Sebastian vom Schlüssel regarding a guardianship matter. The court of St. Gallen has already passed a judgment confirming the rights of vom Schlüssel. The heirs had disregarded this judgment and brought the matter again before the Hegiberg court. St. Gallen requests protection and support for vom Schlüssel.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Melchior Gisler, Landvogt of Upper and Lower Toggenburg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Chur ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist the widow of the deceased Burgomaster of Chur, Johann Lurer, Barbara Lurer, in the collection of a debt of 70 gulden owed to the citizen of St. Gallen, Bernhard Ziegler. The widow has already tried unsuccessfully several times to obtain the payment. Chur requests official support so that the creditor may collect her claim.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the citizens of St. Gallen Tobias Haffner, Jacob Hilybrandt, Lorenz Nayeheülte, Großhans St. Gallen, Meinhard Koch and Othmar Weübler von Weil had behaved contentiously in Konstanz. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to instruct the named citizens to appear before the court of Konstanz on Saturday, 11 July.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to the request of the Zürcher marriage judges to summon the citizen Andreas Frisig, copper-smith's journeyman, regarding a marriage case with Anna Schnidin. Frisig admitted to the mixture but denied the marriage promise. The judges of St. Gallen disclose that the plaintiff has the right before the St. Gallen marriage court and that Frisig was bound by oath not to leave the city.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Marriage judges of the city and district of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Biberach ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to return to their citizen Hans Bernhard Meyer the goods arrested there without charge. They refer to the fact that the Heimatschneiderische forbids the arrest and that the St. Gallen David Miller had previously not sought help with them. They request that Miller be left in his lawsuit before the first judge.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Bailiff Brünsmann of Gottlieben asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have their fellow citizen Lieutenant Colonel Bartholomäus Kunz suppress the complaints of soldiers against Friedrich Sebastian Kunz. These soldiers, whom Kunz had recruited on the Lieutenant Colonel's behalf, are demanding outstanding pay. Brünsmann requests intercession so that Kunz does not lose in the law, and offers reciprocity.
en.sender: Hans Joachim Brünsmann, Bailiff of Gottlieben
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Judges and Assessors of the City Court in Straßburg ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to examine the subject Peter Zech there as a witness in a legal dispute between Abraham Hassel and Jacob Brilon. They request that the witness be questioned under the usual oath and that the statements be returned sealed.
en.sender: The Judges and Assessors of the City Court in Straßburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizen Margaretha am Stein, widow of the deceased hospital master Konrad Hinderle, in an inheritance matter. They ask for sovereign assistance so that Margaretha am Stein receives what is due to her according to law and equity.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Rudolf Reding, Landvogt of the County of Thurgau, reports to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on the interrogation of the arrested Jörg Lenz from the Brägenzerwald. Lenz is said to have confessed to having stolen a linen cloth as a servant of the bleacher Jagkweil and sold it to the countryman Hans Seger in Rorschach. His fellow servant Georg von Hundwil is also said to have stolen a cloth. Further investigations are still pending.
en.sender: Johann Rudolf Reding, Landvogt of the County of Thurgau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Prince Eitel Friedrich zu Hohenzollern communicates that he has received the supplication of the Rottweiler citizen Jacob Vogler. Since the heirs of the deceased Esslingen merchant Conrad Zücher do not concede any claims and a settlement at the Rentmeisterei is still pending, Vogler's claim cannot currently be taken into consideration. Should a considerable amount remain open in the settlement and no agreement on the payment terms be reached, the law must decide.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Irlen, Ludwig Hoen and Johann Veiht thank the Schultheiss and Council of St. Gallen on behalf of Count Ludwig Heinrich von Nassau-Weilburg, the Council and the burnt citizenry of Herborn for the donation of thirty ducats for the restoration of the city and the Landesschulen after a fire.
en.sender: Johann Irlen, Ludwig Hoen and Johann Veiht
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The War Council of the city and district of Zürich asks the Council of St. Gallen to take care of the pregnancy of Barbara Kumber from Windisch. Her fellow countryman from St. Gallen, Leonhart Loberger, has impregnated her and left her. As she cannot support the child alone, she asks for help. The War Council requests the St. Gallen authorities to speak with Loberger or his relatives so that he provides for the mother and the child.
en.sender: War Council of the city and district of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the visit of the seal-bearer of the Patriarch of Konstantinopel, who wishes to explore the doctrine of the reformed churches. They report that the envoy has shown himself to be sincere, and ask St. Gallen to treat him accordingly. They send the town clerk Johann Jakob Ziegler as an escort for the envoy to St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the citizens of Zürich concerning the widow Anna Brandenburgerin. They point out that her deceased husband Hans Schwenzer had never been a citizen or resident (Hintersasse) of St. Gallen, but had lived in the territory of the Prelate of St. Gallen. He had been imprisoned a year and a half ago for an offense and dismissed from hospital service. Since he is no longer in the service of the hospital and is not a citizen of St. Gallen, they cannot set him tasks and have no opportunity to instruct him.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of Zürich

en.regest: The Statthalter and Council of the city of Zug request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their Confederate Jörg Kuhn Schwarz to take care of the maintenance of the four children of his deceased sister Anna Brandenbergin. Since the father died without children, Schwarz, as the next heir, is obliged to maintain the children. Zug threatens to send the children to him if he does not attend to the settlement of the inheritance within eight days.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the city of Zug
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen forward the envoys of the Patriarch of Konstantinopel, Herr Cyril, to Burgomaster and Council of Chur. They ask for a welcoming reception and support in his matters, as Chur had also done for Schaffhausen in similar cases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Chur

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the von Lindau not to settle their affairs on their own initiative and at their own risk, but to turn to the city. They promise, as the most prominent, to show good neighborliness to the Lindauers as well as to their own citizens, and refer to divine protection.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: the von Lindau

en.regest: The bailiff and Council of Bischofzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizen Georg Zwingen in a legal matter. Zwingen had sold linen cloths to Jacob Ruschler, on the condition that they should serve as a pledge for 120 florins and two debts. Daniel Ruschler nevertheless passed the cloths on to his brother. After the latter's death, Zwingen's claim was not recognized as trusted property in the estate. Bischofzell appeals to the authorities of St. Gallen to confirm Zwingen in his right.
en.sender: The bailiff and Council of Bischofzell
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Chur inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about an order of the Mailänder Regierung, according to which persons and goods from the plague-affected regions of Bavaria, Württemberg and Augsburg may no longer pass into Mailand. They ask the St. Gallen Confederates to take similar measures and to turn back suspicious persons, in order to protect the city from the plague.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
