en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish an edict concerning a scheduled general court day for the departed citizen of Lindau, Anton Eggert, and his wife Susanna Zellerin. This is to be done so that creditors can assert their claims and no one is disadvantaged by ignorance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The hereditary vassal of Hans Joachim Künsig, bailiff at Gottlieben, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the citizen of St. Gallen Anton Zilihen to assert his claims against Christoph Sebastian Krumb before the court of Gottlieben. He warns that Krumb is attempting to draw the matter before the Councils, which would be contrary to the jurisdiction of the Bishop of Konstanz.
en.sender: The hereditary vassal of Hans Joachim Künsig, bailiff at Gottlieben
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have appointed a general court day for the heirs of the deceased citizens Jeremias, Friedrich Peier and Jacob Hüeber as well as their creditors. Since citizens of St. Gallen are also involved in the trading companies, they ask the St. Gallen authorities to publicly post and publish the relevant edict in suitable places, so that no one is curtailed in their rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Salomon Hirzel, Council member of the city of Zürich and Landvogt of the lordship of Wilflingen, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to allow the inheritance to the deceased citizen Christoph Schlumpf from the Scheibenwergk. The widow and the children are in great poverty. He requests the St. Gallen authorities to secure for the widow and children the share of the house property that is due to them.
en.sender: Salomon Hirzel, Council member of the city of Zürich and Landvogt of the lordship of Wilflingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter of 16./24. June concerning the widow and children of the deceased Christoph Schläpfer. They report that Schläpfer's father had died about forty years ago and that the children had divided the inheritance. Christoph had received his share, but had married without the knowledge of the authorities and lost the right of citizenship. The widow asks for payment of the outstanding 24 and 14 florins. The St. Gallen authorities ask the Landvogt to support the widow and to promote the payment.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Johann Meier, Councilor of Zürich and Landvogt of the Lordship of Wädenswil

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the citizens of St. Gallen Jörg Francisco and Hans Jakob Zillig to pay the widow Sophia Sprünglin, née Zillig, and her son Heinrich Zillig the share of a claim against the Rotmunden that is due to them. The Zilligs had undertaken to pursue the claim jointly and to share the proceeds, which they had not done until now.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Gerold Escher, bailiff of the Lordship of Laufen, announces a legal matter to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen. Jeremias Peyer and his wife have been banished from Schaffhausen because of debts and have debts and property in Laufen. Escher has set a peremptory court day for Wednesday, the 20th of Hornung, at 8 o'clock in Hurlingen at the Golden Eagle. He asks the St. Gallen citizens, who are also interested, to appear in person or through proxies.
en.sender: Gerold Escher, bailiff of the Lordship of Laufen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich invite Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to a conference of the Protestant cantons on 11 February in Zürich, to deliberate on the defense against an approaching foreign military power. They request the dispatch of envoys with full power and the arrangement of scouts, in order to be informed of the enemy's movements.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Cristoff d'Annon, Notary, attests to the settlement between the buyers Pomier, Ziegler and others as plaintiffs and Hieronymus Müller as defendant. The parties agree that the plaintiffs shall provide sufficient surety to Müller for his claim of 15'000 gulden and send an authorized representative within six weeks to settle the matter amicably or legally. Müller undertakes to allow the goods to pass freely. The settlement was concluded in Basel.

Burgomaster and Council of Zürich invite Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to a Confederate conference on 2. March 1628 in Baden. They request the dispatch of a Council messenger to deliberate on the points mentioned in the Abschied and to preserve peace in the fatherland. The Zürich chancery asks the St. Gallen chancery to forward the letter to Landammann and Council of Appenzell.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the foreign military force remains in Swabia and is increasing. They ask the Confederates to have their envoys arrive for the Diet in Baden on the evening of 29 February, so that the final decisions and the negotiations with the other confessions can be discussed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Secret Council of St. Gallen for a quick answer as to whether St. Gallen or its citizens could support Zürich with a large sum of money on loan. This is necessary to prepare for a possible attack by a foreign military power on the borders. Zürich promises to advocate for St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Secret Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hieronymus Müller, citizen of Basel, protests against the witness testimony set by the St. Gallen merchants on 10 March. He declares the appointment null and void, as he can appear neither in person nor through a proxy, because the questions to be heard were not communicated to him. He asks the Council to convey his excuse and to intervene with the St. Gallen people so that they await the appointment and refrain from informal proceedings.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Basel report that their citizen Hieronimo Müller has submitted a protestation and a complaint. They ask the Confederates in St. Gallen not to rush Müller and to let the matter remain pending for the time being, as his objections contradict the settlement reached between him and the citizens of St. Gallen as well as the customary practices and the common law.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen invite Landammann zu Zellweger to participate in a meal for the honourable envoys of the Confederations of Zürich, Luzern, Schwyz and Glarus. They ask him to inform the envoys of their arrival and to appear at the meal himself.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann zu Zellweger

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen invite Landammann and Council of Appenzell to a meal held in honor of the envoys of the Confederates Zürich, Luzern, Schwyz and Glarus. These are deputed to a meeting in Thurgau. The St. Gallen ask the Appenzell to appear upon the arrival of the envoys, and promise to reciprocate on similar occasions.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen invite Bartholomä Blarer, Landvogt in Thurgau, to a meal in honor of the envoys of the cantons of Zürich, Luzern, Schwyz and Glarus, who have participated in the last Baden Diet in Thurgau. They ask him to participate in the meal upon the arrival of the envoys, which they will communicate to him.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Bartholomä Blarer, Landvogt in Thurgau and Oberrheintal

en.regest: Christoffel Lübbemann, citizen of Zürich and servant of the reformed church in Güttingen, asks his cousin, Captain and Councillor Christoffel Büffler in St. Gallen, to procure for him a halberd and a Baggenhuben from St. Gallen during the times of war. He promises to pay for the weapons in the autumn, as he cannot afford the transport from Zürich.
en.recipient: Christoffel Büffler

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that their parish priest Dr. Georg Zeaemann is falsely accused in a printed work by the Jesuits of having been involved in the publication of a treatise against Cardinal Bellarmin. They ask the authorities of St. Gallen to demand a report from Hans Philips Chunz, called Spieß, and his son, who are staying in St. Gallen, regarding the background of the treatise and to communicate this confidentially.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter of 21 March. They cannot determine who wrote the booklet directed against Cardinal Bellarmin, as the person named Spieß does not reside in their city. They report that Spieß recently passed through and spoke with a local book printer about the book. They recommend inquiring with their own citizen.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant an audience to their envoy Hans Wilhelm Eschbacher, who represents them in certain matters, and to give him full credence. They promise to support St. Gallen in the matters concerned as neighbors.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Wil to allow the St. Gallen citizen Lorenz Iseli to transport wheat to St. Gallen. The city of Wil had stopped the freight at the Thorhütung. St. Gallen assures that the grain will only be sold in the city and neighborhood, and asks for the friendship of the Confederates.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Wil

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the Zollikoferische Gesellschaft in the bankruptcy proceedings concerning the heirs of Jeremias Studerich and Jacob Huobers. They transmit a vidimierte copy of the Pfandobligation and ask that the envoys of the Gesellschaft be protected and handled at the next court day session.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to listen willingly and without prejudice to their councilor Johann Wilhelm Eschberger, whom they have delegated to the St. Gallens, and to give him credit. They promise to support the St. Gallens in similar cases in a neighborly manner.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich reply to an intercession of St. Gallen concerning a claim of 50 florins, which Anna Rordorff is supposed to have bequeathed to the St. Gallen woman Eva Künkin and her daughter. Zürich informs that the heirs of Rordorff refuse payment, as the will is formally defective and a later, younger disposition exists. Furthermore, the estate has already been distributed. Zürich asks St. Gallen to drop the claim in order to avoid further costs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jakob Brandenberg, Landvogt in the Upper and Lower Thurgau, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the citizen of St. Gallen Jeremias Müller had injured the Roggwil twill weaver Ulrich Blumen in his house with seven wounds to the neck, whereupon the latter had died after eight or nine days. Brandenberg accuses Müller as a manslayer before the free Thurgauian Landgericht and requests the St. Gallen authorities to have Müller appear at the Rathaus in Frauenfeld on 11 May 1620 at 8 o'clock in the morning to answer to the law.
en.sender: Jakob Brandenberg, Landvogt in the Upper and Lower Thurgau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Karl Gries, Statthauptmann, and the judges and verdict-givers of the city court of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post the attached edict. Therein, a general debt day is set for the deceased citizen Hans Breiten der Jüngere. The citizens of St. Gallen might be creditors and should be informed of the date.
en.sender: Karl Gries, Statthauptmann, and the judges and verdict-givers of the city court of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to receive the accompanying Caspar Leffler as their envoy in a friendly manner and to accord him full confidence. They ask for neighborly support in an emergency and promise to assist St. Gallen in similar situations to the best of their ability.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to the request of a neighbor for the purchase of a quantity of grain, which he had directed to them because of the shortage and high prices. They state that they cannot conclude the sale for significant reasons, and ask for understanding.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Noble, honorable, prudent and wise, especially dear Lords, Friends and Neighbors

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to transmit to their citizen Hans Eschwiler a copy of the marriage contract between the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Hans Leonhard Schöbinger and his wife Barbara Sauterin. Eschwiler, as the next blood relative, wishes to assert his share of the inheritance. The Zürich authorities also request written information on whether a spouse can make the property inherited from the parents their own and exclude the next heirs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizens Joachim, Laurentz and David Zollikofer to submit the original of an obligation. This had been handed over in the bankruptcy proceedings concerning the heirs of Jeremia, Friedrich Feyren and Jacob Hueber only as a private copy and transsumpt. Schaffhausen, as the ordinary judge, requires the original in order to examine the claim.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen confirm to Schaffhausen the receipt of a letter concerning the deceased gentlemen Joachim Lorenzen and David Zollikofer. They state that they handed the letter over to the persons concerned and collected the fee. The answer of the gentlemen will be communicated to Schaffhausen in writing. Since the reasons advanced should suffice as an excuse, they refrain from further measures.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen

en.regest: Niklaus Gmeiner, Hofschreiber zu St. Gallen, informs that the communities of Bernang, Balgach, Widnau and Hasslach agree to the contract granted the day before by his lords and the deposed lords on account of good neighborhood and the propagation thereof. He refers to the letter of the deceased dean and asks for indulgence, as the veneration soon passes to the successors.
en.sender: Niklaus Gmeiner, Hofschreiber zu St. Gallen
en.recipient: Hofschreiber

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have their citizens Joachim, Laurentz and David Zolligkoffer produce the original deed regarding their claims against the bankruptcy estate of Peyer and Huber. The St. Gallen party had retained the document without valid reason. Schaffhausen emphasizes that the production of the original is customary and promises to treat the matter amicably.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The five Catholic cantons inform St. Gallen that they do not wish to allow the passage of 80 German horsemen and foot soldiers into the inner cantons, as this would damage the reputation of the Confederation. They ask St. Gallen, as the foremost canton, to turn the troops back until the Princes and Superiors have been requested for permission to pass.
en.sender: Schultheiss, Landammann and Council of the five Catholic cantons of the Confederation
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter of 13 June, in which the five Catholic cantons communicated that foreign troops had been quartered in St. Gallen and marched through. St. Gallen contradicts this, as no such troops were seen or inquired about in the city or jurisdiction. They are near the border, but only accessible via the territory of the Abbot of St. Gallen. They assure that in similar occurrences they will inform the Confederates.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss, Landammann and Council of the five Catholic cantons of the Confederation

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Landvogt Rudolf Reding zu Liechtensteig that they had imprisoned the young man Hans Jakob Holenstein aus Wetzikon, because he had confessed to having stolen 30 pounds and a woman's dress in Teufen. They ask Reding to report in writing whether and why Holenstein had recently been a prisoner in Liechtensteig and how he had been released, in order to satisfy the justice.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt Rudolf Reding zu Liechtensteig

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to allow their bailiff of Bürglen to participate in the interrogation of the evangelical congregations in the Turgau. These congregations have filed complaints regarding the lack of preachers. The bailiff did not feel competent without an order from his superiors. The interrogations are to be recorded in writing for the Baden annual accounts.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish the edict concerning the general court day appointed for the citizen Christoph Egger and his wife Magdalena Heilgen. This is done so that creditors can assert their claims and no one is disadvantaged by ignorance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen inform that the citizens of St. Gallen Joachim, Laurentz and David Zollikofer had handed over to them their original obligation regarding a claim against the defaulted Peyer and Hüeber. Since a court day is set for 16 July, they request the authorities of St. Gallen to instruct the Zollikofer to appear personally or through authorized attorneys and to negotiate the matter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their fellow citizen Ferdinand Brandenburg. The St. Gallen merchant Gregorius Gerig had lent him 200 gulden and has not paid the annual interest of 10 gulden since 1627. Überlingen requests St. Gallen to compel Gerig to pay the outstanding interest and capital.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Heinrich Reding, Obervogt of Roschach, to have the grain shipment of their grain carriers Jacob Schlittberger and Conrad Ziegler, which has arrived in Roschach, unloaded immediately. The grain carriers had bought the grain in Konstanz and need the wagons for the return journey. The Council fears that the produce might be damaged by rainy weather, and asks for the release of the drivers.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Heinrich Reding, Obervogt of Roschach

en.regest: The Burgomaster of St. Gallen informs the Vogt and Council of Bischofzell that they had imprisoned the servant Jakob Arnold, who comes from the territory of Bischofzell, in the Wisli for theft. Arnold had confessed to two further robberies. Since his reputation is bad, the St. Gallen authorities ask for a written report on his behavior and his deeds in Bischofzell, in order to be able to proceed accordingly.
en.recipient: Vogt and Council of Bischofzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about an inheritance dispute concerning the estate of the deceased citizen of Schaffhausen, Daniel Schmid. Since citizens of St. Gallen claim as heirs to take possession of the property, Schaffhausen has set a court day for 5 October. The St. Gallen authorities are requested to notify the parties involved of this date and to compel them to appear, as well as to refrain from arresting or forbidding debts in St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen for support in an inheritance dispute. It concerns a life annuity that the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Daniel Schmid had established for his widow Sara Bidermann at 50 gulden. After the widow's death, the heirs dispute the payment of the capital. The St. Gallen side asks for an amicable settlement or legal assistance.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen

en.regest: Melchior Gallati, Landvogt in Thurgau, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to cite the citizen Jeremias Müller so that he appears on 31 August 1620 at 8 o'clock in the morning in the Rathaus in Frauenfeld before the Landgericht and answers for a manslaughter. If Müller is not present, his friends are to be informed whether they will represent him or take charge of him.
en.sender: Melchior Gallati, Landvogt in upper and lower Thurgau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizens Joachim, Laurenz and David Zollikofer as well as their lawyers in the case of the Peyer and Hüber claims to appear on 12 September before the Schaffhausen court in order to settle their claims amicably or legally.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Unterwalden thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the friendly reception and support of their Landvogt Bartholomäus Odermatt in the Rheintal during his term of office. They declare themselves ready to serve St. Gallen in future matters with the same zeal and good will.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Stadtmann and Council of Feldkirch inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they are cancelling their annual market on 26 November. They ask the St. Gallen to inform their citizens of this, so that unnecessary costs are avoided.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rottweil respond to an intercession of St. Gallen for Othmar Tanner against the Rottweil citizen Jacob Vogler. Vogler has stated that Tanner must contribute to the liquidation of the Hohenzollern pension. Since the co-interest holder Johann Klein asks for a postponement, they grant Tanner a little more time. He should initiate the liquidation in the meantime; otherwise, he may invoke coercive measures at Rottweil.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist the married couple Balthasar Schmalenberger and Ursula Zollihofer in their inheritance claims from the estate of the deceased Lorenz Zollihofer. The cousin Sigmund Zollihofer is withholding the one-sixth share that is due to them, although other heirs have already been paid. The family is in urgent need of the inheritance proceeds in the current inflation and war situation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Rottweil to help their citizen Othmar Tannern in the collection of a debt of 300 florins, inherited from his father, together with costs. Tannern has already turned to the debtor multiple times without success. St. Gallen refers to a similar assistance for Vogler and asks for superior support, so that the debtor be compelled to pay.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Rottweil

en.regest: Melchior Gallati, Landvogt in Thurgau, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Hans Heusser, who comes from Loemschwilen and is detained with his brother-in-law Hans Hueber, has confessed to having stolen a horse and other items about five years ago. He says that he has already suffered punishment for these acts. Gallati asks for a written report on whether Heusser has told the whole truth, so that he can decide on further proceedings.
en.sender: Melchior Gallati, Landvogt in upper and lower Thurgau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The bailiff and Council of the city of Bischofszell request the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen to cause their citizen Jacob Schind, butcher, to appear before the Bischofszell Council on 15 October at eight o'clock. Schind has not appeared in court in a purchase dispute with a Bischofszell weigher, although he had been summoned twice. Bischofszell asks for a legal response to the complaint.
en.sender: The bailiff and Council of the city of Bischofszell
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Arbon reply to a letter from the Council of Rorschach dated 20 September concerning the Rorschach citizen Balthasar Schmalenberg. They forward for information the letter of their citizen Sigmund Zollikofer Jung, who had only reported himself after the matter had been discussed, and declare themselves ready to render all agreeable services.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Rorschach

en.regest: Melchior Gallati, Council member and former Statthalter of Glarus as well as Landvogt in Thurgau, invites the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to his wedding on 26 November in Frauenfeld to the widow Verena Heini. He asks for their presence at the church procession and the subsequent meals and for a friendly reply.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Vratislaus, Graf zu Fürstenberg, informs the Haupt und Stände der Eidgenossenschaft of his engagement to Gräfin Luvinia Gonzaga von Novellara. He invites them to attend the marriage on 17. Dezember 1628 in Passau and asks for their presence.
en.recipient: Haupt und Stände der Eidgenossenschaft

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Mülhausen request Schultheiss and Council of Waldshut to support their citizen and merchant Balthasar Schlaipfer. He says that he has placed a lien of 300 florins on Zacharias and Ulrich Haelßer in Feldkirch, ahead of all other creditors of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Sebastian Hueber. Mülhausen requests Waldshut to have the liquidated debt of 43 1/2 florins, together with interest and costs, paid to Schlaipfer without further legal disputes.
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Waldshut

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizen Marx Christoph Schmidt in the collection of debts in St. Gallen. They request that the creditors of Schmids there, who have arrested his assets, not be given preference, but that the prohibition benefits all registered creditors, as is customary in Nürnberg.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Caspar Schindler asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a letter of recommendation for his proxy Stephan Bessler, so that he may collect his claims against debtors in St. Gallen. He asks for swift legal assistance to avoid costs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Christoph Wingk, Subdelegate of the imperial High Commissioner, asks Count Caspar von Hohenems to pay the outstanding and future weekly wages for the billeting to Amadeo Erolt, who resides in Lindau. He says that the latter has been authorized by the new High Commissioner Johann Stephan Schossi to collect them. Wingk promises to bring the payment to the attention of the Lieutenant General.
en.sender: Christoph Wingk, Subdelegate of the imperial High Commissioner
en.recipient: Caspar Count von und zu Hohenems

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to restrain their hospital servant, who is involved in a legal dispute with Hans Schachen from Kreuzlingen, from speaking law before Appenzell. Furthermore, they ask that the names of those who have stolen from the hospital wood be named, so that these may be punished.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the letter of the Überlingen from 7 November. They reject the proposal to purchase a piece of land to pay off the interest on a capital of 12'000 florins, as they do not wish to acquire an estate outside the Confederation. They request the Überlingen to give them a sum of money to pay off the annual interest. Otherwise, they will insist on the full repayment of interest and principal after the expiration of the deadline.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen

en.regest: The officials of the lordship of Sonnenberg ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their subordinate Barbara Bertschin von Reutigen. The citizen of St. Gallen Michel Künzle wishes to redeem the testamentary dispositions of his deceased wife Juditha Stachlin in favor of her nearest heirs, including Bertschin, with a named person. The officials request that Künzle stand still until the matter is clarified.
en.sender: Officials of the lordship of Sonnenberg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen confirm the receipt of a letter dated 25 November 1628, together with the report of the citizen of Nürnberg Christoph Hiller. They ask Nürnberg to request Hiller to liquidate his account under oath, as the creditors of the deceased Sebastian Hübers do not accept the accounts presented. Furthermore, they request that the 111 gulden, 1 schilling and 8 pfennig paid to Jörg Löchler after the bankruptcy be refunded to the creditors.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Hamburg request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizen Cordt Rautig in the bankruptcy of the St. Gallen citizen Sebastian Werber. Rautig has a claim of 628 Ratsgulden for purchased English cloth. Since Werber is insolvent, Rautig, as a foreigner, is disadvantaged compared to younger creditors. Hamburg refers to the right of equal treatment and requests that Rautig be treated accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and secret Council of the city of St. Gallen answer the petition of Count Caspar zu Hohenems for a loan for his subjects in the counties of Ems, Lustenau, Vaduz and Schellenberg. They refuse the request, as the city's finances are weakened by inflation, war and the plague in Piemont and Frankreich. They ask for forgiveness and promise to help in future possibilities.
en.sender: Burgomaster and secret Council of the city of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Count Caspar zu Hohenems

en.regest: Ammann and Secret Council of Feldkirch thank Count von Vaz for his letter and the oral transmission by the Hofmeister and Statthalter Hannibal Berna. They ask for patience in fulfilling the demands, as the city is in great distress due to the war and the plague and has hardly any means. They assure that they will pay the interest to the benefices at Konstanz, and ask for forgiveness for the delay.
en.sender: Ammann and Secret Council of Feldkirch
en.recipient: Count von Vaz

en.regest: Caspar Graf zu Hohenems asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant a loan of up to 6000 gulden to his subjects in Embs, Lustnau, Vaduz and Schellenberg. He says that this is necessary to pay the high war tax demanded by an imperial commissioner and to prevent a renewed quartering of troops. The Count sends his Councilor Jacob Hannibal Bernd to negotiate the conditions.
en.sender: Caspar Graf zu Hohenems, Gallara und Vaduz
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: The Altrat and Council of Bischofszell thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the presentation of the city coat of arms and two silver crowns for the newly built town hall. They promise to place the coat of arms in a fitting location and to show themselves in mutual neighborhood and friendship.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Statthalter and Council of Feldkirch inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the legal disputes concerning the properties of Georg Kössler in Winenburg and Balthasar Eisen in Rorschach. They have passed a judgment, which is to be published on 12 February. As the creditors of St. Gallen have announced that they will make themselves known, they ask for acknowledgment and remain well-disposed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Advocate, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz remind the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen of an agreement of 1587, according to which, upon the withdrawal of inheritances, only the tenth penny is to be paid. They ask to support the citizens of St. Gallen Daniel Strauß and his siblings in the claim for their share of the inheritance from the estate of the deceased Elisabetha Schlumpf and to hand over to them the property that is due to them.
en.sender: Advocate of the Hauptmannschaft, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Pangratz Zoller. He says that he sold 46 cloths to the under-guardianship Hans Rudolf Bruebler, who has not paid for the goods. The cloths have been arrested in St. Gallen. Memmingen considers the purchase void, as Bruebler was under guardianship, and requests St. Gallen to return the goods to Zoller.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizen Heinrich Weber in the collection of a claim of 90 francs against the heirs of the late citizen of St. Gallen Lorenz Schobinger, who died in Lyon. The sum is still outstanding according to a ruling issued in St. Gallen on 7 March 1625. Zürich asks for support so that Weber may receive his money.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report on the trial between Franz Kling and Hans Sumi of Solothurn against Gregor Speyung. The witness examination was initially postponed because the plaintiffs did not appear. Now the parties have been summoned again for the examination. Lindau transmits the statements of the witnesses and offers St. Gallen to promote the law and render neighborly services.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank a Count for a letter of 7 February as well as for a gifted stag. They assure him of their neighborly affection and offer to serve the Count in the future to the best of their ability.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Count

en.regest: Egon Graf zu Fürstenberg, Landgraf in Baar, Herr zu Hausen und Weitra, Ritter, Römisch-Kaiserlicher Rat, Kämmerer und bestellter Obrister, Generalleutnant des Schwäbischen Kreises, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he is having a live stag delivered to them, as he has learned that they have longed for one for a long time. He assures them of his good neighborliness and goodwill.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landvogt Hans Rudolf Lerber zu Interlaken asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene on behalf of the orphan Hans Bär. The boy's father, a carpenter from St. Gallen, has died. Since the boy has no relatives in Interlaken, Lerber asks the authorities of St. Gallen to intervene with the grandmother Lucia Schlaterin and other relatives so that the boy is raised and trained in a trade. Lerber offers to sell and remit the father's small estate.
en.sender: Hans Rudolf Lerber, Landvogt zu Interlaken
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish an edict concerning the appointed general court day of the widow Margaretha Kramerin, widow of the deceased citizen of Lindau Oswald Bellen. This is done so that any possible creditors of St. Gallen may assert their claims and no one be disadvantaged by ignorance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish an edict concerning a general court day for the creditors of the citizens of Lindau Ulrich Benzteng and Leonhardt Heussler, so that no one is disadvantaged through ignorance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The church and school officials of the County of Hanau thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a donation of 500 gulden, which was made before the Frankfurt Autumn Fair. They assure that the money has been distributed to the most needy according to their best knowledge and conscience, and ask for forgiveness for the delayed reply.
en.sender: Kirchen- und Schuldiener der Grafschaft Hanau
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen answer the inquiry regarding the prisoner Hans Kern, called the Huser. He was imprisoned in October 1626 on suspicion of having resold stolen yarn. After interrogation, he confessed only to the sale of war troops, fire, bows, bread, spoons, and six jugs in Morstetten. He was banished from the city and court for life.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Fromm, fürnemm, ersam und wiß, besonders liebe guete Fründt und Nachpurn

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Hamburg request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizen Curt Heutin in the collection of a debt of 628 Reichsthalers from the citizen of St. Gallen Bastian Gruber. Heutin says that despite multiple legal steps and earlier interventions, he has received nothing. Hamburg requests official support so that Heutin may receive his money.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to an intercession by the citizens of Zürich for the citizen of St. Gallen Melchior Guldin zu Bürglen. They reject the request, as Guldin did not conduct himself properly in the administration of the bailiwick and the dismissal is solely his fault. The bailiwick has already been handed over to a new, sworn bailiff, who will take office on 1 May. St. Gallen declares itself ready for other friendly gestures towards the Confederates.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen hand over to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen 2000 gulden with interest, which they had lent them. They ask for the return of the main bond, which they had handed over to the St. Gallen fellow citizen Jürgen Hildebrand. They thank them for the neighborly support and offer their services.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Imperial Bailiff, Schultheiss and Council of the city of Wil ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for written information about Hans Herrnsperger von Juchwill, who is detained in Wil. He was also involved in St. Gallen about ten years ago. The authorities of Wil want to know what he stated there and how he was punished, in order to determine the appropriate punishment in Wil.
en.sender: Imperial Bailiff, Schultheiss and Council of the city of Wil
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the information regarding the grain purchase. They inform about the increase of the war population in Schwaben and in the Upper Rhine Circle as well as the movement of troops against Basel and Müllhausen. Out of concern for the Evangelical cantons, they have convened an Evangelical Diet at Aarau. They offer their support and ask for further confidential information.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen once again for support for their citizen Pangratz Zollner. He says that he has not been able to assert his rights in a legal matter with Hans Rudolf Bruebler and others. Zollner has turned to Memmingen again and asked for further intercession. Memmingen asks St. Gallen to take Zollner's request into consideration.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The envoys of the Confederation inform St. Gallen about the delivery of the imperial edict for restitution to Müllhausen and warn of possible imperial execution. They ask the city to remain vigilant and to prepare for possible military interventions. Furthermore, they invite St. Gallen to the Confederate Diet on 17 May in Baden to deliberate on the defense against foreign military power and joint defense.
en.sender: Envoys of Zürich, Bern, Basel and Schaffhausen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in view of the dangerous situation and the threat from the Evangelical cantons, to send out scouts. They ask for daily reports on the strength, location, and route of the troops in Schwaben, as well as on other matters relevant to the Confederation, in order to be able to act in a timely manner against hostile intentions.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help the widow of the deceased Hans Nägeli from Tüffen and her seven children. The former miller Balthasar Schidli has left the service in the mill. The widow fears that she will not be able to make ends meet without help. Appenzell asks that Schidli be kept in the mill for a while longer, until Nägeli's son can learn the trade.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the information that grain is being bought up in Überlingen and elsewhere for the war troops in the Upper Rhine region. They promise to inform the Confederates in Zürich and to report on further developments. Appenzell offers St. Gallen mutual support in similar cases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank for the information regarding the march of the imperial armada. They assure St. Gallen of their help as Confederates in case of emergency and keep their people ready. They ask that the enclosed letter be transmitted without delay to the competent cantons.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The envoys of the three Pünfte to Chur thank the Confederates for their offer to negotiate with the imperial commanders regarding the entry of the army. They report that the imperial troops have already marched over the Steig into the country and have occupied the passes, bridges, and the city of Chur. The Obrist von Merode has promised to uphold the rights of the cantons and to maintain the garrison at the expense of the Emperor, in order to secure the passage to Italien.
en.sender: Heads and Council envoys of the three Pünfte to Chur
en.recipient: Burgomaster, Schultheissen, Landammann, Councils and envoys of the Confederation to Baden

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Hans Ulrich Rirtz, goldsmith. He says that he entrusted a sword hilt set with pearls to the citizen and apothecary of St. Gallen, Gabriel Krumben, for sale. Krumben did not return the item but demanded a silver knife sheath, which he had already paid for. Lindau requests St. Gallen to instruct Krumben to hand over the sword hilt immediately and intact.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich communicate to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen a response of the Drei Bünde to an inquiry. They report that the danger to the fatherland through the increasing war troops of the Reich does not diminish. The mentioned imperial letter to the Drei Bünde is word-for-word identical with the letter directed to the Dreizehn Orte. Zürich recommends itself further as faithful the Confederates.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about the threat by imperial troops in the Pündten and ask for consent to recruit cavalry and infantry together with the other Protestant cantons under the command of Colonel Schaferlitzki, in order to be able to defend themselves in good time.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the arrival of large foreign troops in the Bündner Lands and at the Comersee, as well as the march of General Wallenstein. They request an embassy to Baden, in order to consult together with the other cantons on the defense of the Confederates and the Bündner.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in view of the current situation, to deploy good scouts. They request that, in particular from Nürnberg and Ulm as well as their surroundings, it be learned whether and how much warlike force is in motion against the Confederate lands. Zürich offers to inform St. Gallen about the situation in and around Straßburg.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the transmitted news and ask them to continue informing them about everything worthy of report. They declare themselves ready to reply in turn and to show the Confederate friendship.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich send to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen a copy of a letter from Herr General von Eisen to the thirteen cantons of the Confederation. They ask the St. Gallen to instruct their next upcoming envoys to Baden accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Wolf Rüdiger von Ossa, Colonel and Commander of the imperial army in Pünden, warns the Council envoys of the thirteen cantons against foreign envoys who, with cunning and practices, disturb the common good and wanted to move the Lords to actions against the imperial people. He asks them to rely on the imperial Synchronisationschreiben and not to listen to the words of the foreign envoys, who only sought their own interest and unrest.
en.recipient: Council envoys of the City and Land of the thirteen cantons of the Confederation

en.regest: Ferdinand Erel and Wolfgang Jacob Sattler, heirs in Kempten, ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their relatives, the Herren Schobinger, Spindler and Scherrer, to transmit to them within three weeks the Austrian debt instrument together with the last settlement with the imperial chamber in authentic form. They threaten otherwise with other means.
en.sender: Ferdinand Erel and Wolfgang Jacob Sattler
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizens Schobinger, Scherer and Schindler to hand over the certified copies of the obligation of the Duke of Savoyen as well as the account to the heirs of the deceased Ottilie Hörlein. Otherwise, the heirs are to refrain from their claim. Kempten refers to the civic kinship and the great distress of the heirs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Zürich to intervene with the envoys of the other three Protestant cities so that the former town clerk of St. Gallen, Melchior Güldi, may come to a proper accountability. They refer to earlier cases in which the Superiors had consented out of consideration for the Protestant cities and to avoid inconveniences.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the city of Überlingen to help their citizens and grain buyers, who had provided 94 horses for the grain transport for the imperial commissioners in Pünzten, in bringing the animals back. The horses have not yet returned despite promises. In addition, they ask Überlingen to support the St. Gallen people in further grain purchases.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Überlingen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Burgomaster and Council of Kempten that they have received the letter of intercession for the citizen of Kempten Hans Schlaepfer. They have requested the interested parties of St. Gallen to submit their counterarguments. The reply will follow in a separate letter. St. Gallen asks Kempten to inform the Kempteners of this.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen answer the inquiry of the neighbors as to whether Archduke Ferdinand of Österreich intends to lead about 1000 men through the Confederation and the Landvogtei Rheintal into the Rheintal. They state that they have only heard that the King of Frankreich has detached two companies from Metz and that the Marquis de la Valette has dismissed his troops. They consider it unlikely that the Confederation will be attacked, and promise to inform immediately upon receiving new news.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen and Winterthur

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the city of Schaffhausen to help their citizens and merchants, who are involved in a dispute with Hieronymus Müller from Basel, in obtaining evidence from the Schaffhausen Council and court records regarding the bankruptcies of the Eger and Züblischen. The merchants of St. Gallen need these documents for the final settlement of the main dispute. The Council asks for friendly support.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Schaffhausen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a petition of intercession by the Landvogt of Frauenfeld for the widow of the deceased citizen Jeronimus Müller. They state that the widow has received nothing from the estate, and ask the Landvogt to protect the Müller family and to release the cloth seized from her, which is due to the son Ulrich Blumen.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt of Frauenfeld

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Radolfzell inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the outbreak of the plague in their city. They ask to refrain from allowing the Radolfzell grain merchants to visit the market of St. Gallen. If the situation improves, they are to send their grain merchants to St. Gallen with a certificate. Alternatively, merchants of St. Gallen or healthy persons from healthy cantons could be commissioned to buy grain and ship it by water.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Council of the village and bailiwick of Zug request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to move their citizen Wolfgang Schowinger to pay a debt of 84 mint gulden and 27 schillings to the widow Barbara Moser. Schowinger had promised the payment but did not keep it. Zug asks for friendly intervention so that the creditor receives settlement of her claim.
en.sender: Ammann and Council of the village and bailiwick of Zug
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen express their sorrow over the plague raging in St. Gallen and ask for intercession with God. They request the authorities of St. Gallen to order that no one with contagious sores leaves the Überlingen corn market, but that business transactions are handled by proxies who have not been in infected places within a month. Überlingen offers neighborly support.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Melchior Gallati, Landvogt in Thurgau, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to settle the heirs of Vlerich Blumen called Zwingerer, who was murdered in St. Gallen. The murderer Jeremias Müller died in Frankreich. The widow of the murdered man asked Gallati for help to settle her costs and damages. Gallati requests the St. Gallen authorities to move the heirs of Müller to a fair settlement in order to avoid further lawsuits.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Advocate of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they are cancelling the Kirchweihmarkt planned for 29 September because of the danger of the plague. They ask for understanding and commend themselves to divine protection.
en.sender: Advocate of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Schultheiss and Council of Solothurn about the results of the Diet of the Confederates, which had taken place in Solothurn. They confirm that the 6000 men decided upon are intended only for defense. St. Gallen declares itself willing to agree to the unanimous resolution and reaffirms its loyalty to the Confederation.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Solothurn

en.regest: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the danger posed by Italian and Spanish troops. They ask that the envoys appointed to St. Gallen appear the next morning at eight o'clock to negotiate on common interests.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform the recipient that the city of Zürich has informed them of the impending Spanish passage. They ask the recipient to continue to pay attention to the dangerous situation in the fatherland, as before.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Ußroden

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the special honor, manifold kindness, and neighborly friendliness that their envoys received at the marksmanship in St. Gallen. They offer to serve the St. Gallen in a similar manner and hope for the continuation of the good neighborly friendship.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Barbara Brunnerin, gravely ill, dictates her last will in Zürich. She disposes of her clothing and personal items, among them a gilded goat figurine for the daughter of the brother Zacharias and a small silver cup for the brother-in-law Hans Jacob. She thanks her children David and Magdalena for their care and leaves them 100 gulden each. The doctors and apothecaries are to be paid. The rest of the clothing goes to the sister Maria Magdalena. The niece Ester receives certain garments. The barber Hans Caspar Koller attests to the correctness of the record.
en.recipient: Siblings

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the forwarding of confidential news and ask for further reports. They explain that they take the information seriously and will remain vigilant. In case of emergency, they promise to lend St. Gallen assistance to the best of their ability and to behave as loyal Confederates.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request the Council of St. Gallen to grant citizenship to the stonemason Tobias Kreißer of Flaach. Kreißer has worked for years in the Zürich quarries and behaved honestly. Zürich recommends him on account of his good origin and his professional knowledge. St. Gallen answers on 19 November 1629 that the citizenship will be postponed until the next Candlemas because of the plague and the good supply of the quarries.
en.recipient: Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish the edict concerning the general court day for the creditors of the deceased Hans Zünne Papiers of Niederreusslingen, so that any claims of St. Gallen may also be taken into account.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizens Michael Stündlin called Haug and his sister Katharina. These have asked for intercession so that they can assert their right to the estate of their sister Magdalena Kündlin called Häugin, who died in St. Gallen, and of their brother-in-law Nicolaus Gastel.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizen Hans Jakob Essner and his wife in the dispute over the paternal inheritance of the deceased Barbara Rönigerin. The siblings of the deceased refused to hand over the share, although the marriage contract secured the inheritance rights and, according to the law of Zürich, half-sisters on the father's side inherit. Zürich requests support so that Essner receives his share.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to include the wife of their citizen Hans Jakob Sessler in the paternal property of their deceased sister Barbara Bäuerin pro rata. Should this not happen, they request that the distribution of the estate be withheld until the settlement of the testament signed in the deceased's own hand.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to a request from Caspar Wiesenberger, the Amtmann of Peter Dreymach, for help for his sister Katharina Hürgemans and her two children, who were raised by Jacob Lüberher. They point out that Lüberher has lost the citizenship of St. Gallen and no longer allows himself to be considered a citizen. Since he resides in Graffenried, it is the responsibility of the authorities there to take charge of the children. St. Gallen is not responsible.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Johann Rudolf Reding, Prince-Abbot's Councilor of St. Gallen and Landvogt of the County of Thurgau

en.regest: Johann Rudolf Reding, Landvogt of the County of Toggenburg, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene with the brothers of the deceased St. Gallen citizen Jakob Rüeger. These refused to take over one of the two orphaned children of their deceased sister Katharina Heppenmoserin. Reding requests the St. Gallen authorities to urge the brothers to take over the children or to come to an agreement with the uncle, as the latter himself lives in poverty.
en.sender: Johann Rudolf Reding, Landvogt of the County of Toggenburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen not to confirm the testament of the widow Magdalena Schürmerin. Her son has received half of the estate, while the sister, the wife of the Schaffhausen citizen Ludwig Ziegler, receives only a small share. The Schaffhausen authorities ask that the matter be left untouched and that the siblings be allowed to come to an equal inheritance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to an inquiry by the citizen of Schaffhausen Ludwig Ziegler. They explain that the introduction of a town clerk in St. Gallen is unusual and dishonorable. They point out that in marital cases they only approve what is due to them. They ask Schaffhausen to proceed against such injustice, and further promise continued friendship of the Confederates.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rottweil ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene on behalf of their citizen Hans Jacob Weigel. The latter has employed the St. Gallen journeyman tailor Hans Rederer, who, under the pretext of possessing a considerable fortune, has incurred debts. Weigel and his creditors ask for support so that the creditors can be satisfied.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen that Schaffhausen has been asked by imperial commissioners for a pass for 18'000 centners of ammunition and war weapons, which are to be sent to Alsace. As the city of Zürich considers the transit dangerous, they request St. Gallen to find out how the ammunition in Lindau is situated and whether additional war troops are marching against the Confederation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their countryman Konrad Signer in asserting his inheritance right to the estate of his deceased sister Anna Signerin. They recommend him with a letter of intercession and request superior assistance so that he may obtain his right.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant their countryman Ulrich Schefer of Tüffen the seat in the mill of the St. Gallen citizen Caspar Schlumpf. Schefer has been staying in St. Gallen for 28 years and has behaved honestly. The Appenzellers ask for a friendly answer.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The expelled church and school officials of the Kurpfalz congratulate the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on the end of the plague. They praise the Christian charity of the citizens of St. Gallen during the epidemic and ask for renewed support, as their distress has increased further due to the expulsion and the plague.
en.sender: Georg Summer, Ambrosius Bohner und Jonas Liebing
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Council of Bernau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help the bailiff and guardian Michael Heusser, so that the inheritance of the deceased Maria Wildfauss, an orphan of the deceased Hans Nägeli, may be assigned to him. The brothers of the deceased had refused Heusser the accounting. Bernau testifies that Maria and her brother are the only heirs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Stadtschultheiss and Council of Rineck ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to urge their citizens to a friendly settlement in the inheritance case of the deceased Joachim Eggmann. The citizen of Rineck, Jacob Berlocher, guardian of the deceased's niece, has refused to participate in the division, as he fears that the inheritance will remain under the law of St. Gallen. Rineck wishes to settle the matter, as the inheritance rights of both places are different.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Council of Rorschach concerning the citizen Hans Jakob Stolz, who has appealed against a judgment regarding the inheritance of the widow of the deceased Jost Zügg and the child's portion of his stepdaughter. They set the court day for Monday, the 6. February, and ask Rorschach to inform Stolz of this, so that he may appear in good time and the matter can be settled amicably.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of Rorschach

en.regest: Francisc Reding, bailiff of Rorschach, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to award the inheritance of his deceased sister-in-law Elisabeth Dänlerin to his subordinate Jacob Locher. Locher is the lawful heir as the nearest relative. A distant relative is improperly interfering in the inheritance. Reding requests the St. Gallen authorities to put Locher in possession of the estate without further effort and to prevent unjustified interference.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Gallus Hoffmann der Ältere reports that his lord held court on the same day. He asks them to continue to trust and serve him, and assures them that he gratefully offers himself for any service.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send a copy of the testament of the deceased wife of the St. Gallen citizen Andreas Fehren to their citizen Konrad Füßlin, the guardian of the three children of the deceased Johannes Engen. Füßlin has requested the support of Lindau, as he suspects that the children are provided for in the testament.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Bassompierre, who comes to St. Gallen as an extraordinary envoy of the King of Frankreich to consult on the security of the Confederation, announces that he will convene a Landsgemeinde in Solothurn on 3 March 1630 new style. He asks the St. Gallen to send envoys with full power to hear the King's proposals and to decide on the raising of troops.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform the Council of Rheineck that the amicable settlement between the St. Gallen citizens Niclaus Ebnethaller and Heinrich Eggmann on the one hand and the Rheineck citizens Hans Jakob Stoltz and the heirs of the deceased Joachim Eggmann on the other hand regarding the inheritance has failed. They ask Rheineck to name 25 February as the date for the final adjudication of the inheritance and to instruct the heirs to appear. Otherwise, St. Gallen will divide the inheritance according to the city's inheritance law.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Stattammann and Council of Rheineck

en.regest: The bailiff and Council of Bischofzell request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, on behalf of the St. Gallen citizen Margaretha Bombgartnerin, to examine the estate of her deceased husband Balthasar Müller. They wish to interrogate five citizens of Bischofzell as witnesses and send their statements sealed to St. Gallen, so that the widow may receive her inheritance.
en.sender: The bailiff and Council of Bischofzell
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they had deputed their councilor Conrad Enderlin for a matter to be communicated orally. They request an audience and that Enderlin be given the same trust as themselves. They expect a neighborly answer that serves the welfare of the city, and offer reciprocity.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg to call their citizens Christoph Schnürfer and Christoph Hiller to order. They are to deliver the tauberischen effects to the creditors of the St. Gallen citizen Sebastian Haerbers and to prevent Hiller from further legal disputes. St. Gallen refers to earlier concessions in similar cases.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the friendly promise to provide Stathauptmann Spitzel with counsel for three years. They transmit the agreed obligation, which is kept by their fellow citizen Jacob Gildbrandt, and ask that the guarantee be duly observed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizen Balthasar Schmalenberg in the claim for his inheritance. Schmalenberg had registered, in the name of his wife Ursula Zollighoferin and his brother-in-law Loth Schnell, for the inheritance portion from the estate of the Zollighofer in St. Gallen. The city of St. Gallen had granted them three years of patience, as a brother lived abroad. This deadline has expired. Schmalenberg now asks for an intercession with the Council of St. Gallen, so that the inheritance portion of his son Jacob can be invested.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The administrator of the Hauptmannschaft, also the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz, ask the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen to assist their citizen Paul Wünsch in a legal matter. They refer to a submitted supplication and ask that Wünsch be granted what right and equity might give him.
en.sender: The administrator of the Hauptmannschaft, also the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the heirs of the deceased Appenzeller woman Maria Schlaepferin. They had been refused in St. Gallen when claiming the estate of their sister and cousin, as the latter had made different testamentary provisions. Appenzell maintains the view that the land law of the deceased has not been forfeited and that the natural heirs must not be bypassed. They ask for an amicable arrangement so that the heirs' share is granted to them without resistance.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landvogt Melcher Haller in Thurgau to allow the widow of the deceased Junker Wernhart von Wathstetten, who wishes to move into the St. Gallen hospital, to pass through with her inheritance without deduction or back tax. They refer to an old agreement between St. Gallen and Thurgau, according to which persons who move between the territories are to be treated freely and without deduction.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Melcher Haller, Landvogt in Thurgau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report that the deceased Appenzell Landwaibel Jost Jacoben was settled in Trogen and the creditors of St. Gallen were dismissed. They point out that Jacoben had embezzled 34 gulden and 40 kreuzer in church interest. They ask the Appenzell to not subordinate the trusted church property to other debts, and threaten countermeasures otherwise.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen that they have ratified the Solothurn Abschied concerning the mobilization and have turned to the two envoys. They declare themselves willing to contribute to the restoration of peace in the event of a failed peace negotiation. Since the five Catholic cantons and the Valais do not agree to the mobilization and the troop contingents have already been distributed, they ask whether Zürich can withdraw its declaration. They ask for information on how they should behave towards the French Crown, should they be threatened with reprisals.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen that, in response to an answer from Marshal Bassompierre and reports from the Catholic cantons, they have decided to grant their own captains permission to publicly recruit for 600 men. They ask for an answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the reply to their latest letter and the transmitted news. They request the St. Gallen to continue informing them about everything that comes to them in writing, and promise to serve them in similar cases in a Confederate manner.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Meister and Council of Straßburg request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to accede to the inheritance claim of their citizen Hans Paul Winckenberger against the heirs of the deceased St. Galler Caspar Reiner. Winckenberger has attached a document and attestation from Straßburg, which proves his descent from Jacob Pfeiffer. Straßburg requests that the share of the inheritance be delivered without further delay.
en.sender: Bernhard von Kageneck, Meister and Council of Straßburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizens Caspar and Jacob Bowman in the inheritance dispute over the estate of the deceased Johannes Brunner. The Bowman have a claim to the estate and ask for favorable treatment without great costs and a long process.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help the widow Susanna Weinin, daughter of the deceased citizen of Stein am Rhein Georg Weinin, in the enforcement of her inheritance rights. She is a co-heir in place of her deceased child. The city of Stein asks for support in the legal proceedings.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Pflege, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant full faith to their trading servant Matthäus Hirschen, who was sent to St. Gallen on behalf of the heirs of the deceased Hans Österreicher, in a legal dispute with the heirs of the family Cuenz, and to grant him all official support, so that their factor Jacob Cuenz in Genua may receive a just judgment.
en.sender: Pflege, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to enable their citizen Joachim Im Thurn to purchase tents. Im Thurn has acquired the tents from his lieutenant and now wishes to sell them to Council members of St. Gallen. Schaffhausen asks that Im Thurn be given priority in the event of a shortage of tents in St. Gallen and that the goods be purchased from him at a reasonable price.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant an audience to their envoy Johann Wilhelm Escher, who represents them in an urgent matter, and to believe his statements. They expect a neighborly and benevolent answer, as the city and the citizenry are in the greatest distress.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen thank St. Gallen for the promised aid of 1000 Reichsthaler to cope with the imperial soldiery. They transmit a draft of the bond and ask that the payment date be fixed. The money is to be returned to Jacob Hildbrandt by 5 June so that the original can be issued.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help the women of St. Gallen Ursula, widow of the deceased Ulrich Hulgen, and her daughter Anna, wife of the watchmaster Jergen Schmidt, to their right in an inheritance case that has arisen in St. Gallen. They request superior care so that the two receive their inheritance, and a copy of the testament.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen that Basel has informed them about the quartering of the Wallenstein army in the neighboring lands of Further Austria. They ask St. Gallen to make inquiries in Memmingen, where General Wallstein, Archduke Leopold, and other war leaders are coming together to decide on the further war plan.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have taken note of the dispute between Schaffhauser Heinrich Scheucher and St. Galler Ludwig Ziegler over a testament of the deceased Magdalena Fuchs. They set a court day for 26 July and request the St. Gallen to notify Scheucher so that he appears punctually in the Schaffhausen town hall and can present his claim.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the letter of 21 June and the accompanying news. They ask that the previous trusting communication be continued, and promise that they will not leave anything undone on their part. They ask for the forwarding of the received news to other Confederates and recommend themselves mutually to divine care.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support a supplication of their citizens Wilhelm and Hans Philipp Geuder as well as Anton and Konrad Tucher. These have obtained an arrest on the goods and wares of the St. Gallen man Konrad Schiltlen and request further assistance to obtain what belongs to them without hindrance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
