en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg answer an intercession of E. F. for Jacob Christoph Schlappritz and co. in a bill of exchange case against Wilhelm im Hoff. They have heard the defendants and find that the payment was made before the date fixed in the bill of exchange. They ask E. F. to side with the plaintiffs, to be content with the payment made, and to refrain from unnecessary prolixity.
en.recipient: E. F. (Eure Fürstlichkeit)

en.regest: Listing of the distribution of a collection of 1000 gulden donated by the city and church of St. Gallen to various persons, including parish priests, schoolteachers, widows, orphans, and political figures, with detailed amounts in gulden and kreuzer.

The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen congratulate the French envoy on his appointment and ask him to support the pensions of the city of St. Gallen to be distributed by the Confederation. They recommend their envoy Daniel Studer, who is to present the toll grievances of the merchants, and instruct him to collect the city's pension in the name of the city.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: N. du Vialart, Royal Councillor and ordinary envoy in the Confederation

en.regest: The persons Georg Summer, Ambrosius Tolner, Gebhardt Agricola and Jonas Liebing, resident in Nürnberg and appointed to the ecclesiastical collection work, confirm to the Council of St. Gallen that they were paid 1000 gulden by Andreas Wegelin for the expelled Palatine church and school ministers. They assure that they have distributed the money as needed to the exiles, widows and orphans as well as needy political persons, and promise to present the corresponding receipts.
en.sender: Georg Summer, Ambrosius Tolner, Gebhardt Agricola, Jonas Liebing
en.recipient: Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The expelled Upper Palatinate church and school officials thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the two collection drives in favor of the exiles. The city collected 1000 gulden in Reich currency and handed them over through the Nuremberg postman Andreas Wegelin. The donors ask for prayer and promise to always praise the generosity of the city of St. Gallen.
en.sender: Expelled Upper Palatinate church and school officials
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to detain their citizen Georg Stähelin, the stonemason, to make him take back and support his wife Anna Luggbrunnerin, whom he has left. Furthermore, Stähelin is to reimburse the costs for the child's care up to now as well as the wedding costs, since the mother has fallen into poverty.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landvogt Werdenberg asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to return the stolen horse to his subject Hans Schlutter. Schlutter says that he discovered the animal in St. Gallen with a citizen there. The horse is castrated, dun, has a glass eye and an ear cut off at the top. The Landvogt promises reciprocity in services to the Confederation.
en.sender: Hans Gabriel Elmer, Landvogt of the County of Werdenberg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The town clerk of Altstätten and the other officials of the Upper and Lower Reinthal report to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on the latest negotiation regarding the wine tax. Since no one had been willing to take on the matter alone, they had decided to carry out the assessment. They ask that the wine tax be left at 2 Pfennig and 2 Heller, so that the farmers can offset their losses, and promise to promote the matter in their communities.
en.sender: Town clerk of Altstätten and other officials of the courts of the Upper and Lower Reinthal
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Frauenfeld inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a complaint by the Zürich schoolmaster Heinrich Mösslin against the St. Gallen citizen Joachim Friedrich. Mösslin says that he had Friedrich's money arrested in Frauenfeld, as it had belonged to his deceased wife, Friedrich's mother. Since Friedrich is away, the Frauenfeld authorities say that they confirmed the arrest and gave Friedrich eight days to state the reasons for the arrest, otherwise it would be lifted.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in view of the dangerous situation in the Rheintal, to establish a postal connection via the innkeeper at the Krone at Elggkouw. They request that letters to the co-religionists in the Rheintal and the replies to Zürich be transmitted without delay by fresh foot messengers, in order to be able to provide the subjects with advice and help.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen send Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen a copy of their goldsmiths' ordinance. This is done at the request of the St. Gallen, who want to use the ordinance for the reformation and better establishment of their own craft. Schaffhausen emphasizes its willingness to support St. Gallen in such and other matters.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich send, upon request, a copy of their Goldsmiths' Ordinance to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen. The copy explains how in Zürich the assay, the stamp, and the penalties towards the goldsmiths are handled.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel their citizen Jacob Luchsse to pay immediately the outstanding balance of 41 gulden and 10 kreuzer for purchased leather to the Ulm citizen and tanner Claus Marckh. Marckh has turned to Ulm, as he urgently needs the money as a craftsman and Luchsse delays payment despite multiple reminders and surety.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about the influx of imperial and Austrian troops to Konstanz, Thun, and Lindau, as well as about the war preparations of the Abbot of St. Gallen. They ask for information regarding the intentions of these troops and of the Abbot, as well as for vigilance towards the co-religionists in the Rhine Valley. They will deliberate on the matter at the Diet in Baden.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Lorenz Klee and his business partner to pay the heirs of the deceased Schaffhausen citizen Felix Moser 142 gulden plus interest and costs. The sum is owed from a settled agency and has been due since 1629. Schaffhausen requests prompt payment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Advocate, Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz hand over to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the last ordinance issued by their goldsmith. They ask for forgiveness for the delayed copy due to other chancery business and declare themselves ready for further neighborly service.
en.sender: Advocate, Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Stadtammann, Burgomaster and Council of Meersburg request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly publish and post the edict concerning the weekly market in Meersburg, which was granted to them by the Emperor and the Bishop of Konstanz, at its usual place, so that the market visitors may learn of it.
en.sender: Stadtammann, Burgomaster and Council of Meersburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Pflege, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for support in the legal dispute between their trading servant Jacob Kunz and the heirs of the deceased St. Gallen merchants Ludwig and Othmar Kunz. The heirs had attempted, through the lawyer Ludwig Oswald, to overturn an already issued judgment of the arbitrators and to examine the books again. Augsburg asks that Oswald be prevented from such delays and that Kunz be helped to a just judgment.
en.sender: Pflege, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Jakob Schobinger to hand over the 150 florins deposited with him, together with interest, to Lucretia Mingardina. She acts on behalf of the heirs of the deceased Maria Mingardina and presents a letter of attorney. The heirs were driven out because of the evangelical doctrine and are staying in Zürich.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant their countryman Daniel Knechtle admission to the city. Knechtle wishes to settle in St. Gallen and place himself under the protection of the city. The Appenzellers request that he be tried for one year, as he wishes to administer the inheritance of the deceased Jörg Allgöwer until his children come of age. Knechtle commits himself to live piously and honestly.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Duke Julius Friedrich asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help his subject Hans Schauber, citizen and merchant of Calw, in the collection of a claim of 200 gulden against the citizen of St. Gallen Caspar Schlumpf. He refers to the right to grant priority to creditors with a proven claim and asks for assistance in obtaining payment.
en.sender: Julius Friedrich, Duke of Württemberg and Teck, Count of Mümpelgart, Lord of Haydenheim, Guardian and Administrator
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to seriously instruct their citizens, the trading relatives of the family Zolliker, from the side of the supreme court, to pay the heirs of the deceased citizen of Schaffhausen Felix Moser the still outstanding balance of 103 florins. The debtors had so far only settled 80 florins and dangerously postponed the rest.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Altschultheiss and Council of the city of Solothurn inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the ongoing disputes between Zürich and the five Catholic cantons regarding the collations in the Rhine Valley and the marriage jurisdiction. They request the dispatch of empowered envoys to a Confederate Diet on 12 May 1621 in Baden, in order to achieve a peaceful settlement.
en.sender: Altschultheiss and Council of the city of Solothurn
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the communication regarding the victory of the evangelical Church. They praise God for the relief of the Church and ask to overthrow the pride of the Antichrist. They thank them for the confidential communication, offer their friendship, and recommend themselves to each other's divine care.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich thank the Council of St. Gallen for the detailed reports recently received. They ask that such good advices continue to be transmitted and that they also be kept informed of written news concerning the Pünkten and the neighboring Tütschlanden.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank the Bishop of Konstanz for the communication of an imperial commission regarding their absent citizen Melchior Guldin. Since the matter concerns the Confederation, they say that they have already forwarded it to the Confederates. They ask the Bishop to communicate the letter to the Confederates and to recommend the business in neighborly friendship.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Bishop of Konstanz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Bishop Johann of Konstanz for the communication of an imperial commission concerning the departed citizen Melchior Guldin. Since the matter concerns the Confederation, the Confederates have already taken note. The St. Gallen ask the Bishop to recommend and leave the business to them. They promise to be neighborly and well-disposed to the Bishop in all things.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Johann, Bishop of Konstanz

en.regest: Bishop Johann of Konstanz asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant his physician Sebastian Schobinger a medical license. He says that he has had good experiences with Schobinger and wishes to avail himself of his services.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizen Loth Schnell in asserting his inheritance right to the estate of his mother-in-law Agnes Zollikoferin. Schnell says that he had himself enrolled in St. Gallen in order to claim the share of the inheritance due to him and his wife. Lindau requests that the matter be expedited so that Schnell may come to his inheritance without hindrance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen that the conference scheduled for the Sunday after Aarau regarding the conference desired by Bern could not take place because of certain causes. They ask the St. Gallen to withdraw their sent envoys and for the time being to send no one to Aarau.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to participate in the conference scheduled for 29 August in Aarau. The occasion is the refusal of the Abbot of St. Gallen to recognize the two preachers who have arrived in the Rheintal for the vacant parishes. Zürich wants to proceed jointly with the evangelical cantons against the Catholic cantons and the Abbot in order to preserve religious freedom.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Bern inform that the French envoy Broussard will not come to Solothurn. As time is pressing, they invite the Protestant cantons to a meeting next Sunday in Aarau to discuss further steps. They ask Zürich to inform the other Protestant cantons.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report to St. Gallen that they were informed by a trusted person that the Bishop of Konstanz and the abbot had issued threats and made unusual preparations. In particular, the Rorschach ships were seized and ammunition was secretly purchased in St. Gallen. Zürich asks St. Gallen to inform it by messenger what has been learned in this matter, in order to jointly protect the fatherland.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz reply to the letter of intercession for the citizen of St. Gallen Johann Rainsperg. They say that they had urged the evangelical heirs to pay the remaining legacy. These say that they had excused the delay so far. Since little time has elapsed and the legacy is running with interest, they ask St. Gallen to instruct Rainsperg to exercise further patience.
en.sender: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have received an answer from the French King to a complaint transmitted by the thirteen cantons at the last Baden Diet regarding the tolls in Valence. They enclose a copy of the letter in order to inform the Confederates about it.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan, as they are compelled by imperial commissioners to pay 30'000 gulden and 1'560 florins monthly to the imperial war chest, otherwise a further 13 companies would be billeted. They send their Council member Caspar Löffler, who is to negotiate the amount of the loan.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to forward a letter to the Roman Emperor to a citizen of Zürich in the vicinity of Wien. They request that the letter be delivered in the name of the city of Zürich and that a reply be obtained, as the five cantons were seeking help from foreign princes against Zürich and Zürich wished to make an apology.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten thank St. Gallen for the promised loan sum of 3000 gulden. Since the money has not yet arrived in Lindau, they send their Oberbaumeister Johann Meier to St. Gallen to collect it and to agree on the obligation. They promise to remember the help with gratitude.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich send Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen a letter to the Roman Empress, which they should hand over personally to their citizen Jeremias Vögelin, who is staying in Wien, for better form and certainty. They ask that Vögelin be granted an unencumbered escort with the next Zug to Wien, as they had already offered to do so in this regard.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Maximilian, Landgraf zu Stielingen, announces that he is compelled to seize 2000 or 1500 fruits for one gulden. He asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send a man who will inspect the goods and grains and confer with him.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Glarus ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their countryman Friedrich Fluri, who has become speechless after a stroke and asks for support. They request the St. Gallen authorities to persuade Fluri's sister Anna Flurin, a citizen of St. Gallen, to grant her brother a maintenance payment. Should she refuse, they will send the brother to St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Council of St. Gallen instructs the Councilors Joachim Schitlin and Hans Krommen to go to Engen to inspect the offered fruits. They are to agree with the Landgrave on a purchase of up to fifty Fuder if the goods are of good quality. The goods are to be delivered duty-free or with a share of the duty. The Councilors are to reserve the right of loading and report on the condition of the Bruchhüter.
en.recipient: Maximilian von Pappenheim

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from Maximilian von Pappenheim dated 16 October. They report that the envoys sent by him, the St. Gallen Council member Lünghart Scherer and the fellow citizen Caspar Deggen, were informed about the purchase of the small town. They declare themselves ready to ratify the contract as soon as the conditions are met, and ask for the consent of the hereditary lord.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Maximilian von Pappenheim

en.regest: Emperor Ferdinand II. reminds the Counts of Pontresina of the agreement to close the passes again after the end of the Italian unrest. He warns them against a French envoy who wants to persuade them to open the passes on the Steig, which would harm the Empire and the Archducal House. The Emperor declares that he will nevertheless keep his promise to certify the passes, and asks the Counts to remain in devotion to the Empire and not to enter into new alliances.
en.recipient: The three Counts of Pontresina

en.regest: Othmar Hiller, a dyer in St. Gallen, replies to a letter from the Landamt and Council of Glarus. He states that he and his wife Anna Florin had learned of the deplorable condition of their brother-in-law and brother Friedrich Jakob Florin. Hiller rejects the accusations, as his wife had acquired her property herself and it belonged to her husband and children. He offers that his wife give her brother-in-law temporal sustenance, but refers to the law of St. Gallen, according to which a wife must surrender her property for necessity and the maintenance of her husband.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter of 29 June concerning the Glarus countryman Friedrich Jacob Blum. They have instructed his sister Anna Blum and her husband Othmar Zillern to treat the Glarus man in a friendly manner. Since Blum has fallen into poverty, they refer to the St. Gallen city law, according to which citizens are not obliged to support one another, but the authorities provide for those in need in almshouses or hospitals. Moreover, Anna Blum's children have already received support in the hospital. They ask Glarus to provide the necessary help for Blum himself, as the federal decrees stipulate that each authority provides for its own.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Glarus

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to ensure that the children of the deceased Magdalena Schwarz, daughter of the deceased citizen of Lindau Thomas Schwarz, are safely handed over and have managed their maternal inheritance in St. Gallen. They refer to an enclosed letter from the heirs, which describes the circumstances.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The children and heirs of the deceased Thomann Schwarzen direct a humble request for intercession to the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Lindau.
en.sender: The children and heirs left behind by the late Thomann Schwarzen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Lindau

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to pay out 200 of 700 florins lying in St. Gallen to the citizen of Konstanz Konrad Weltinger and his wife Elisabetha Hüglin. Weltinger wishes to buy the fishery in Lindau from the widow of the deceased Konrad Schreiber and leave it to his son Bartholomäus Schreiber. The payment serves to promote the purchase and the welfare of the son.
en.sender: The Administrator of the Captaincy, also Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Maximilian, Landgrave of Stühlingen, and the envoys of the city of St. Gallen agree on a grain purchase. The city can choose between 250 Malter of wheat and 50 Malter of oats at 3 gulden 45 kreuzer or 200 Malter of wheat and 100 Malter of oats at 4 gulden. It pays 600 gulden immediately and 350 gulden in Nürnberg. The Landgrave delivers weekly to Zell, where the goods are measured. The city may take about 30 Malter for trial after eight days.
en.recipient: City of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nördlingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Hans Seltzner, tanner, in the collection of a debt of 44 gulden. Seltzner has a bill of exchange debt from Jacob Hagelstein, called Thomas Burger, from Rottenburg, which the latter has assigned to his brother Hans Albrecht Thomas in St. Gallen for payment. Nördlingen requests support so that Seltzner receives his money.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizen Konrad Waser, a joiner, in his complaints against his brothers-in-law and sister-in-law. Waser had promised 300 gulden for the marriage with Juditha Niethin, which he could not raise. Furthermore, the in-laws had divided up his household goods and movable property behind his back. Waser wishes to present himself in person in St. Gallen to obtain information about the situation and to request the due payment. The Zürich authorities ask for official assistance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern inform the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen about the Diet of the neutral and allied cantons set for 29 November in Baden. This is to settle the disputes between the five Catholic cantons and Zürich regarding the Thurgau and Rheintal collation, matrimonial, and land peace matters. Bern requests St. Gallen to attend the Diet through authorized envoys and to contribute to peace.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about the request of the three Pünfte to be allowed to recruit soldiers in the Confederation and for support. They ask St. Gallen to equip the envoys for the Diet taking place in Bern on 29 November with full power, so that the concerns of the Pünfte can be discussed jointly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Christoph Krolth zu Meissenburg informs the Pünzischen envoys in Unterengadin that the subjects of Archduke Leopold zu Österreich in the region are being forced to take a new oath. He requests the envoys to investigate this and, in the other case, to protest, so that no actions are taken against the rights of the Archduke.
en.recipient: Pünzischen Abgesandten im Unterengadin

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen inform Burgomaster and Council of Zürich that a Spanish people is marching over the Gotthard and is to be quartered in Konstanz. Furthermore, citizens from the Schwarzwald have reported that the Oberste von Ossa there had asked for quarters for about 100 horsemen and other people, and that some horsemen had already arrived in Engen. They ask God for help for the distressed evangelical churches.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform that they have learned of the advance of Spanish troops and their quartering in Konstanz. Although they do not yet believe the report, they ask St. Gallen to inquire and report to them on the situation, as it is an important matter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Burgomaster and Council of Schweinfurt that their citizen and town clerk Melchior Guldin has published a pamphlet against the city and its freedoms. They ask the Schweinfurt authorities to inquire with the local printers whether the work was printed in Schweinfurt, and if so, to proceed against Guldin and to transmit some copies.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schweinfurt

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Frankfurt send to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen copies of a royal patent of the Swedish Majesty. This patent concerns the local fairs, the continuation of trade, and the safety of the roads. The Frankfurters ask that the printed copies be brought to the attention of the citizens and merchants of the city who attend the fairs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen declare to Hereditary Steward Wilhelm Heinrich von Waldburg that they grant permission to his wife and young household to reside in the city for six months. Should the war in the Empire not cease, an extension will be granted upon further request. The relatives and the household staff are subject to the jurisdiction of the Council during this time.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Wilhelm Heinrich von Waldburg

en.regest: The envoys of the three Bünde of Chur thank for the friendly answer to their petition. They report that Archduke Leopold of Österreich is recruiting troops and having them quartered in Lindau, Konstanz and Tirol, which is interpreted as a threat to Switzerland. They request the Confederates to provide active assistance in case of emergency, and ask to be informed on what support they can rely.
en.sender: Heads and Council envoys of the three Bünde of Chur
en.recipient: The 13 and associated cantons of the Confederation

en.regest: Wilhelm Heinrich von Waldburg, hereditary marshal of the Holy Roman Empire, sends his son and court master Blasius Gapani to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen. He asks that Gapani be heard favorably as his envoy, that he be given credit, and that they declare themselves favorably towards him in accordance with the state of affairs. He promises to oblige St. Gallen in similar cases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they had received a letter from the three Pünfte to all the cantons, in which they are requested to state their opinion on a matter. They make St. Gallen a party to it by means of a copy and offer themselves for the services of the Confederates.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss, Vögte, Council and citizens of the city of Thun ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help the widow Magdalena Marti. She says that she raised her two deceased children, who died without heirs, with great effort and expense during the plague. They request the St. Gallen authorities to grant her a part of the inheritance of her children, and ask for a written answer.
en.sender: Schultheiss, Vögte, Council and citizens of the city of Thun
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Christoph Finckh zu Kacisenburg, as Commissioner of Archduke Leopold von Österreich for the Unterengadin, refers to his letter of 23 January. He explains that the preparation of war troops without his exclusion is detrimental to the Archduke in the Unterengadin. He commands that no one is to go to war service without his knowledge, under threat of loss of body, honour and property. He demands the publication of this command in the community and a written answer.
en.recipient: Judges, Gschworne, Dorfmeister and communities of Ramüß

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the Evangelical Religion in Glarus ask the Confederates for support in the bailiwick dispute with Schwyz over Uznach and Gaster. They threaten that, if no agreement is reached by May, they will defend the occupation of the Landvogt of Werdenberg by all means. They request the cantons for Confederate help or for better advice.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Evangelical Religion in Glarus
en.recipient: Burgomaster, Schultheiss, Landammann and Council of the cantons Zürich, Bern, Basel, Schaffhausen, St. Gallen and Appenzell

en.regest: Wilhelm Heinrich zu Waldburg thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the hospitality shown to his envoy Blasius Gazer as well as for the offer to take his family into the city. He accepts the offer, but explains that he will initially place his wife and children with his in-laws in Überlingen because of the bad winter roads. He assures that he will maintain the offer for the future.
en.sender: Wilhelm Heinrich, Reichserbtruchsess, Freiherr zu Waldburg
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Melchior Guldin, former town clerk of St. Gallen, protests to the Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz against the intention to transmit his recently printed treatise to Archduke Leopold in order to obtain his judgment on the demands of St. Gallen. He refers to his imperial commission and the ongoing deliberation in the Reichshofrat. Guldin asks that the transmission be refrained from and that he be given time to complain to the Emperor.
en.recipient: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of a letter from the Evangelical cantons to Glarus. It concerns the period of bailiwick (Bevogtungsspanne) that Glarus still maintains towards its countrymen of another religion. Zürich asks St. Gallen to declare itself in the name of the Confederation whether Glarus should maintain or give this up.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of a letter from the French ambassador to the Confederates. They send a copy of this letter to inform the St. Gallen thereof.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Kessler, town clerk, reports to the Landvogt that he has received his letter. He asks for leniency for the delayed reply, as he had previously been prevented from doing so because of a breach of the peace and a lack of money. He assures him of his loyal and obedient attitude.
en.recipient: Landvogt

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landvogt Adam Ziegler of Bregenz to hand over Thomas Küen, who is imprisoned in Bregenz, to St. Gallen without cost. They justify this by stating that Küen gave false testimony in the matter of Jörg Degenbach and should be strictly interrogated and punished in St. Gallen in order to clear innocent people from suspicion.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt of Bregenz

en.regest: Adrian Ziegler, bailiff of Sax and Vorstegg, confirms the receipt of a letter dated 16 February 1632. In it, he was asked to interrogate Anna Gontzebachin in order to clarify the committed errors and to protect the innocent from suspicion. Ziegler declares himself willing to serve the Justitia. He reports that Gontzebachin had been disturbed in head and mind by Herr Georg Zwickre and Heinrich Zollikumer. As a priest, he had taken her in, as she had invoked the freedom of the castle. After daily visits by the parish priest and medical treatment, she had regained her mind and voluntarily left the freedom. Ziegler does not doubt that she will tell the truth.
en.sender: Adrian Ziegler, bailiff of Sax and Vorstegg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Heinrich von Rohan, appointed by the King as extraordinary envoy to the Confederation and to Upper Germany, informs the Confederate cantons that he has postponed his journey until the arrival of an ordinary envoy, in order to then give them the desired satisfaction. He expects an answer in the first days to the request for 4000 kreuzer, which is based on the alliance with the King.
en.recipient: Burgomaster, Schultheiss, Landammann and Council of the 13 and affiliated cantons of the Confederation

en.regest: Johann Escher, Council member and Captain of the City Banner of Zürich as well as Landvogt in Thurgau, confirms to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the receipt of their letter. He states that he is content with the punishment of his citizen Michael Krütterer for abusive words and demands no further compensation. He regrets the inconveniences for the people of St. Gallen and offers his services.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Rudolf Reding, Landvogt in Toggenburg, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the citizen of St. Gallen Jost Hanenberger, called Moseli, is in custody for theft. He was married to Anna Riedlingerin, who had previously been in custody in St. Gallen and had made statements. Reding asks for these statements to be communicated to him so that he may examine them, and offers reciprocal service.
en.sender: Johann Rudolf Reding, Landvogt in Toggenburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Archduke Leopold rejects the accusations of the Confederates that he is preparing a raid. He claims that the Confederates, through their war preparations and violations of the inheritance agreement of 1621, provoked his countermeasures. He declares that he will take no further steps as long as the Confederates do not further pressure him, and expects that they remain loyal towards him.
en.recipient: Confederate cantons

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to the intervention of Lindau for their citizen Anna Mellin and her bailiff against the butcher Bernhart Ziegler. They state that they have communicated the accusations to Ziegler and enclose his reply. They request Lindau to, if it continues to pursue the lifting of the arrest, to hear the case before them within one month, otherwise Ziegler will not be given any further answer.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Chur inform that they will henceforth manage the coinage business themselves and have appointed a master of the mint. They ask St. Gallen to declare the six batzen, which are struck in Chur, valid in their city and jurisdiction alongside other Confederate coins. Chur assures that the coins conform to the imperial standard of weight and fineness and are not struck in excess.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to treat the family Aniorgen of Genf, who is applying for the citizenship of St. Gallen, favorably. The Aniorgens have been recommended by the Genfern, and Zürich wishes to support this recommendation in order to preserve the friendship of the Confederates.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the letter of the Confederates of Chur, who have reformed their coins and ask that they be readmitted in St. Gallen. St. Gallen declares that it cannot decide this alone, as the neighboring authorities had prohibited the Chur coins because of their low value. However, they will endeavor to support the request of the Chur people when the opportunity arises.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Chur

en.regest: The three Bünde answer a letter from Archduke Leopold to the Confederates, in which they are accused of having forcibly entered the Habsburg territories. They reject the accusations, emphasize their innocence, and justify their defensive measures against the invasions. They refer to the Italian peace settlement and the inheritance agreement, which they had not violated. They ask the Confederates to maintain their resolution and to provide them with assistance in case of emergency.
en.recipient: Burgomasters, Schultheissen, Landammänner and Councils of the thirteen cantons and allied territories of the Confederation

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report that they have received a letter from the Confederates in the Grey Points, addressed to 13 cantons and allied Confederates. They report this to the Council of St. Gallen in copy and commend themselves to its divine preservation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Emperor Ferdinand II. answers the letter of the thirteen cantons of the Confederation of 12 February 1632. He revokes the imperial commission issued between Melchior Guldin and the city of St. Gallen and leaves the matter to the jurisdiction of the Confederates. He asks that Guldin be given impartial justice and that the inheritance settlement be observed.
en.recipient: The thirteen cantons of the Confederation

en.regest: The Council of the city of Bischofszell informs that the prelate of the St. Gallen collegiate church intends to levy a new tax on the farms and properties of the city and the hospital in the County of Toggenburg. Since Bischofszell itself was asked for a statement, the Council asks the St. Gallen for written information on how they stand towards the planned burden or whether they have already received an answer.
en.sender: Council of the city of Bischofszell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz send their councillors and chancery administrators Nicolaus Teuchern and Johann Harder to the recipients. They ask for a gracious audience and that full faith be given to the envoys in their oral communications, and that they act favourably. Konstanz offers the same support in return.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: King Gustav II. Adolf of Schweden requests the Confederates to maintain their neutrality and good understanding with him. He warns against granting the Spanish King the pass for his troops advancing from Italien, as this would harm the common peace and the freedom of the Confederates. Should the Confederation comply with this request, he would be compelled to act against the enemy, which would result in a war in their land. He assures them of his royal friendship and Huld.
en.sender: Gustav II. Adolf, King of Schweden
en.recipient: Burgomasters, Schultheissen, Landammänner and Common Councils of the thirteen and allied cantons of the Confederation

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz thank for the good reception of their envoys. They ask for support for the bailiff Bernhard Pforzhammer, who has to represent the inheritance of the deceased St. Gallen woman Barbara Kobsamin for the four children of the deceased Caspar Kobsam. They request the St. Gallen authorities to help the bailiff with the payment of the inheritance share.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the information regarding the intentions of the King of Schweden to take the pass over the Bischofsbrücke or other Confederate passes. They do not believe that the King has anything hostile in mind against St. Gallen or Zürich. Should they, however, learn of anything, they promise to notify St. Gallen immediately and ask for mutual notification.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich invite Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to a Confederate Diet on 16 May 1632 in Baden. The reason is the approach of foreign war powers to the Rhine and Lake Constance. They ask for sent envoys with full power to deliberate on the defense against the danger and the joint declaration of 23 March 1632.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Landammann and Council of the upper Roda of the Land of Appenzell about the death of the St. Gallen citizen Johann Endres Züricher, who is said to have died from a stone injury after a quarrel with an Appenzeller miller. The St. Gallen authorities have examined the witnesses and detained and questioned the suspected perpetrator, a young journeyman. He denies that the death was directly caused by the throw. St. Gallen sets a day to negotiate the matter.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the upper Roda of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich communicate to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen a copy of a letter from the Königin von Schweden to the Confederation. They ask that the corresponding declarations be made on the occasion of the next Diet in Baden.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The expelled pastors of the County of Solms-Braunfels thank the St. Gallen congregation for the donation of 300 gulden, which they received through the Frankfurt pastor Matthäus Tournemain. They state that the money was distributed among the exiles as needed, and name the individual recipients as well as the amounts. They ask for prayer and wish the St. Gallen congregation peace and blessing.
en.sender: Jonas Pistor, Theodor Damphius and Johannes Pithan, expelled pastors of the County of Solms-Braunfels
en.recipient: Preachers, Elders and Deacons of the Christian congregation in St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the transmitted news of the Confederates and ask for prayers for the Swedish Queen. They thank for the support of the Zürich envoy in Baden and state that their Statthalter in Innsbruck will now join St. Gallen in order to travel from there to Innsbruck.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen invite Landammann and Council of the Inner Rhoden of the Land of Appenzell to introduce the newly elected Landvogt of the Rheintal to his office. They ask the Appenzellers to take the way over St. Gallen and to stay there for lunch. Furthermore, they request a written answer as to whether the mentioned horse ride will take place on St. Wolfgang's Day.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Inner Rhoden of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the receipt of a letter with enclosures. They ask that they also be informed immediately of any future matters of concern, and offer themselves for mutual services.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan of 5000 or 6000 gulden for the war costs of the city, against annual interest and bond. In a postscript they furthermore request that the requested opinion in the legal dispute between Balthasar Hanoldt and the heirs of the deceased Michael Guldinast be sent immediately.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hippolyt Kambly, who was elected Landvogt of the Rheintal for two years, thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the invitation to his inauguration on 24 June. He asks them to attend and honour his wedding on 23 June in the house of the Ratshausmeister Anton Spelter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen congratulate the Abbot of St. Gallen on the assumption of the Landvogtei and ask the Innerrhoder Councilor Hans Buhler to grant the Abbot protection and help in all cases. They also ask for forgiveness for the delayed reply to an earlier letter and promise to continue the neighborly relations.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Hans Buhler, Buwherr of the Council of the Innern Rhoden, Landvogt to Rorschach

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the invitation to lunch with the new Landvogt of the Rheintal. They ask the St. Gallen to attend the farewell of the new Landvogt on 24 June to adorn the procession. They promise to reciprocate this if possible.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Leopold, Archduke of Österreich, confirms the receipt of a letter from the Confederates of 22 May concerning the delivery of the writings of Melchior Guldin. He informs them that he has again ordered his captain and the city of Konstanz to comply with the imperial resolution and the inheritance agreement, should Guldin be there. He asks the Confederates to make the necessary notification in Konstanz.
en.recipient: Councils and envoys of the Confederation in Baden

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the approved loan of 2000 or 3000 gulden. They send a copy of the obligation, which was issued in their usual style, and ask that any concerns be communicated before the final execution. They promise to reciprocate this neighborly favor in future cases.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz inform that they have appointed their coin administrator Hans Badler together with Andreas Schwaib to collect the approved loan. They ask St. Gallen to pay out 2000 gulden upon delivery of the interest bond.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the petition of the bailiff of Kyburg for a loan of several thousand gulden. They regret that they cannot comply due to their own war costs and the empty city treasury. They refer to the difficult situation of the neighboring German Imperial cities and ask for understanding.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Caspar Schlüchter, bailiff of the County of Kyburg

en.regest: The Committee of the Citizenry of Biberach requests the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a credit of several thousand gulden, as the city is financially exhausted by war pressures and the accommodation of royal soldiers. As security, pledged villages in the Franche-Comté are offered. The obligation is to be made under the town seal.
en.sender: Committee of the Citizenry of Biberach
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in view of the approaching Swedish troops, to continue sending out trustworthy scouts. They request that the exact nature of the troops be investigated and that Zürich be informed of all incoming reports.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Jacob von Waldburg zu Zeil asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant him residence in the city for a time, in view of the unrest in Schwaben, which led to billeting and levies. He refers to the fact that his cousin Wilhelm Heinrich von Waldburg zu Scheer has already been received in St. Gallen, and promises to return the service in the future.
en.sender: Johann Jacob von Waldburg zu Zeil
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Archduke Leopold states that he has no jurisdiction over Oeningen, as this territory is subject to the Bishop of Konstanz. He has, however, ordered his officials in the Landgrafschaft Nellenburg to arrest Melchior Guldin there and to carry out the extradition in accordance with the inheritance agreement, should the latter enter his territory.
en.recipient: Councils and envoys of the thirteen cantons of the Confederation

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen reply to a letter from Duke Heinrich de Rohan dated 3 August. Since they had not received the aforementioned earlier letter and the new one contains no clear demand, they cannot reply. They declare themselves ready for further service.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Heinrich Duke de Rohan

en.regest: Heinrich von Rohan asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant him the request made in an earlier letter of 3 August. He assures them that the Prince he serves is not to be harmed by the haste of his envoy, and hopes, through the fulfillment of his request, to show the Republic of Venedig that he stands in their esteem.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to administer the inheritance of the deceased widow and daughter of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Jakob Zili. They ask that the heirs, including the citizens of Lindau Melchior Riedermann and Ulrich Egger, receive their share. Lindau requests an impartial disposition so that the heirs receive their right.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Bern report to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on the attack on fifty Bernese soldiers in the Klus in the territory of Solothurn. They ask for trust in the attached account and for support in the case of further measures. They complain about the murderous treatment of their soldiers and the arrest of a subject by Solothurners.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Schultheiss and Council of Bern for their communication and promise of support regarding the tragic incident that recently befell the Schultheiss of St. Gallen in the Schlösserei. They declare themselves ready to do everything that befits good friends and the Confederates if necessary, and hope that the dispatched envoys will contribute to an amicable settlement and the preservation of peace.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Bern

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report that it has come to their ears that the abbot of St. Gallen has supported public recruitments in the Inneren Roden of Appenzell, which are intended for Colonel König to Lindau. They ask St. Gallen to report to them in writing whether this is true, so that they can better prepare for the upcoming Baden meeting.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann, Statthalter, Hauptleute and Council of Herisau congratulate the newly elected Burgomaster of St. Gallen. They declare that they approve of the timber purchase by the citizens of St. Gallen in Stürzenegg and will no longer object to it. Furthermore, they inform about a Diet of the Confederates in Baden on 14 January, which was convened because of the conflict between Solothurn and Bern.
en.sender: Landammann, Statthalter, Hauptleute and Council of Herisau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz confirm the receipt of a letter of intercession for the wife of the citizen of Memmingen Sebastian Eblin. They communicate that the complaint of the arrestant Leonhard Lindauer against Eblin's wife is set for 13 January. The intercession will be taken into good consideration, insofar as this does not contradict justice.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report that a large number of the Confederates is said to have been recruited in Lindau for the five Catholic cantons Uri, Schwyz, Unterwalden and others. They request St. Gallen to inquire about the number, the truth, and the names of the leaders and to submit a confidential report to them.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the willing response to their request concerning the five-cantonal recruitment and the passage through the land of the Prelate of St. Gallen to Lindau. They ask that, in view of the adverse circumstances that are showing themselves, they remain vigilant and report everything worthy of writing without delay.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank for the information about the situation in Memmingen and Kempten as well as about the billeting. They have forwarded the information to their envoys in Baden, in order to consult with the envoys of the five Catholic cantons. Furthermore, they report that 200 Italian soldiers had marched through the Ämter of Freien and Mellingen, and announce protest to the five cantons.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the information regarding the billeting in the Upper Swabian towns. They report that Italian war troops have arrived in Veltlin and intend to march into Tirol via the Wormser Joch. They ask St. Gallen to continue sending trustworthy scouts and to report daily on the situation, so that the envoys may be informed and consult together.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz report to St. Gallen that the Swissman Leonhard Lindauer had informed them that he had learned from the St. Gallen court lords that he had not applied for an arrest against a debt of a citizen of St. Gallen. Konstanz rejects this and asks Lindauer to be content with a decision on the matter. Furthermore, they report on an arrest they had imposed on the goods of the housewife of Sebastian Eblin von Mentzingen, and ask for good neighborhood.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the transmitted news and share with them an excerpt from their own reports. They ask that the correspondence be continued and that the approaching troops be observed at the border. They cannot believe the news that 140 French horsemen under the Freiherr von Saint-André had been defeated, as a messenger had arrived in Zürich the previous evening who knew nothing of it. They confirm the recapture of Memmingen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to release the Schaffhausen citizen Hans Georg Oswald, who is detained in St. Gallen. Oswald was arrested by the Lindau stonemason Hans Jakob Kürtzer over a claim for millstones. Schaffhausen asks that Oswald be released and referred to his ordinary judge, should Kürtzer still assert claims.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Christoph Näff in the collection of a claim of 243 gulden, 46 kreuzer and 6 heller. Näff says that this amount was owed to him by Sebastian Scherer and Jeremias Loher as heirs of the bailiff Ludwig Kunz, according to a settlement, until 2 December 1631. Näff says that he has not received the payment despite multiple reminders and asks Lindau for an intercession with St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg request the named Swiss cities for a loan of 100'000 Reichsthalers. They justify this with the high war burden, the siege by imperial troops, and the danger that the Protestant Imperial Estates might lose the city, which would endanger the entire Protestant cause. They promise repayment as soon as possible.
en.recipient: Schultheiss, Landammann, Burgomaster and Council of Zürich, Bern, Basel, Schaffhausen and St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rinegk ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for help. They say that they have fallen into distress and have asked for fire and war aid. The Obrist of Ossa threatens to lead away citizens if 30,000 gulden ransom or at least 9,000 gulden Imperial Contribution are not paid. Rinegk asks St. Gallen to lend or promise them 10,000 gulden to preserve the city from ruin.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Esslingen thank St. Gallen for a fire tax and ask for further help. They describe their dire situation after the fire and the burdens caused by imperial contributions and billeting. They request a loan of 3000 or 4000 gulden, the interest on which they wish to pay annually or have deducted from the linen tax, and offer to repay the capital after a few years.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich communicate to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen a letter from Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg, which is addressed to them and the other Protestant cities. They expect a meeting of the Protestant cantons, at which a common response is to be discussed and compared.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Wil ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to communicate to them the existing order for the weekly market, in particular for the trade in fruits and grain in the Kaufhaus. They wish thereby to treat the merchants in St. Gallen and Wil equally and to avoid inconveniences.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter of 4 June, which concerned duty-free goods and the purchase of grain in Rorschach. They ask the neighbors to discuss the matter among themselves, so that the duty be considered in a neighborly manner not only for consumption but also for the citizens of the city of St. Gallen. They point out that their grain merchants use the market and ask that the place be left to them.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein

en.regest: Wilhelm Heinrich von Waldburg asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to take the crates and bales lying in the residence of Dr. Schobinger into their official custody, as Schobinger has moved.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Council envoys of the Confederation at the annual Diet at Baden to intervene with Emperor Ferdinand II. Merchants of St. Gallen in Österreich are being asked to join the Catholic religion or leave the country, and must pay a contribution. The city of St. Gallen appeals to the eternal hereditary union and asks for the maintenance of free trade or for a deadline to settle its business.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Council envoys of the XIII cantons at the annual Diet at Baden

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to return to Hüßli, in the estate of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Sebastian Käser, the cloths handed over to him by Hans Jakob Hüßli, Landvogt of the County of Baden, or the money obtained from them. Hüßli says that he sold these goods before Käser's death and has not yet received the prices. Zürich asks for support in enforcing this claim.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Council envoys of the Confederation of Zürich, Bern, Basel and Schaffhausen answer the petition of the city of Nürnberg for a loan of 500'000 Reichsthaler. They justify the delay with unforeseen obstacles. They declare themselves in principle ready to serve the common evangelical and free Wesen, but refer to the high war costs and the threat by foreign troops, which burden their finances. They ask that the refusal of the petition be written down on these grounds.
en.sender: Council envoys of the Confederation of Zürich, Bern, Basel and Schaffhausen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg

en.regest: The Syndics and Council of Genf communicate that they have admitted the son of Herr Schobinger, as requested in a petition of the 16th of the current month, into their newly established House of Discipline. They await the further intention of the St. Gallen and of Herr Schobinger and offer their services.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have replied to the letter of the city of Nürnberg of 6 March concerning the granting of a sum of money. They ask St. Gallen to send the sealed copy to the competent place and to act towards Nürnberg accordingly on their part.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rottweil ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admit their citizen Wolfgang Fischer den Älteren in the bankruptcy proceedings concerning the estate of the St. Gallen citizen Leon Gruber. Fischer has a claim of 38 gulden 26 kreuzer. Rottweil refers to the fact that at their city court, foreign creditors are treated equally with domestic ones.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Nürnberg request Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen again for a loan of 100'000 Reichsthaler or, if this is not possible, for a smaller amount in gulden. They justify this with the high costs for the defense of the city against the papal camp and the associated entertainments. They promise to repay the loan with interest and to keep the help in memory.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Nürnberg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The envoy of the city of Kempten reminds the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of the request for help for the citizens of Kempten detained in St. Gallen. He urgently requests a small sum of money for the release of the prisoners, as they would otherwise be exposed to the death penalty by the enemy. Kempten promises to repay the help.
en.sender: Envoy of the city of Kempten
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish an edict concerning a general court day appointed for the creditors of the deceased citizen of Lindau, Christoph Aman, shoemaker in Reutin, so that no one be curtailed in his rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Count Vratislaus von Fürstenberg in Konstanz has requested a safe-conduct and escort for his couriers in their territory. They report that one of their messengers in Neuenburg had a letter with the St. Gallen seal taken from him by imperial riders. They ask for the return of the letter and for the prevention of such encroachments. They transmit to the Council of St. Gallen a letter from Colonel Ossa as well as three safe-conducts for the messengers of St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about the raids of Gustav Horn's army on Steinach and the Thurgau as well as the planned meeting of the 13 cantons in Baden. They ask St. Gallen to watch over the imperial troop movements at Arbon or Rosshach and to report to them about them.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the information regarding the reasons for the Baden contingent and the situation in the territory of the Prelate. They promise to watch over St. Gallen and to inform them of the intentions of the five cantons. They ask St. Gallen to observe the situation, to send out scouts, and to investigate whether there is a secret agreement between the Emperor, the Spaniards, the Abbot of St. Gallen, and the five cantons to grant the people the pass through the upper Toggenburg to Konstanz. They demand that all news be transmitted by foot messenger.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to appoint their Councilor and Landvogt Hans Jakob Büchi, who is prevented from attending a court day in St. Gallen, to entrust his deputy Hans Conrad Wüsten. They request that Wüsten be given credit and that he be supported in his proceedings.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on the negotiations in Baden, at which the five cantons promised a truce and agreed on a meeting with the Bishop of Konstanz. They inform about the unexpected departure of the Confederates, the movement of troops to Rapperswil and the planned march into Toggenburg. They ask for vigilance and mutual information.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen complain to Landammann and Council of Appenzell Innerrhoden about the claim that they had lured the Swedish army into the country and supplied ammunition. They reject the accusations as untrue and ask Appenzell to investigate the instigators, name them, and put an end to the bad neighborliness.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell Innerrhoden

en.regest: Hans Heinrich Holzhalb and Salomon Hirzel report to the Burgomaster and Council of Zürich regarding the excuses of the envoys of Schwyz, Uri, and Unterwalden concerning an extract. They stated that the appointed deadline had been too short, and emphasized that it concerned the preservation of the general estate, not an intention against Zürich. They suspect that the extract serves the protection of the Abbot of St. Gallen, and ask for understanding.
en.sender: Hans Heinrich Holzhalb and Salomon Hirzel
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of the city of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen about the negotiations in Baden. They report that the Duke of Rohan had traveled to Baden to deliver a letter to the Confederates of five cantons in the name of the King, which was to reverse the departure that had already taken place. Furthermore, they state that the troops of Schwyz, Uri and Unterwalden were standing at Rapperswil and Lachen, while Zürich and Zug were ready. They ask St. Gallen to pay attention to the behavior of the Innerrhoder and the preparations in the Abtischen Land and to inform them of the march of the Confederate people into Toggenburg.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of the city of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the march of 4000 Confederate soldiers to Toggenburg. They assure their support in case of emergency and ask to call the Appenzellers to help. Furthermore, they request a report on the situation by scouts.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in view of the arrival of imperial troops in Appenzell and the departure of the five cantons, to send out attentive scouts. They promise, for their part, to neglect nothing, and ask for an urgent written reply to Herisau.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the warning about the departure of the General and ask for support to avert the impending war. They report that Field Marshal Horn had promised to come to the aid of the neighboring Protestant estates in case of threat with 500 to 1000 or more horses.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Statthalter and Council of the city of Zürich inform the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen that they have received a message from the Duke of Rohan addressed to the citizens of St. Gallen. They ask for a reply and inform that 2000 Swiss with ammunition have marched into Wil and that others are encamped in Rickenbach and Schwarzenbach. They ask for the secure delivery of the message to their captain Hans Jacob Steiner in Rorschach.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell reply to a letter from the St. Gallen, in which it was claimed that Appenzell countrymen had spread improper talk about St. Gallen. Appenzell rejects this, gives no credence to such rumors, and reaffirms its friendly disposition and neighborliness toward St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich reply to the concern of St. Gallen regarding the siege of Konstanz by the Swedish Field Marshal Gustav Horn. They assure their support and send Captain Hans Zobel as a messenger to inform St. Gallen about the situation after the Baden Diet and to consult on the preservation of the city.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Secret Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about the gathering of the imperial, old-imperial, and Spanish war troops at Überlingen as well as about the threat from Catholic Confederates. Since Zürich must station troops on the borders, it asks St. Gallen for information on how much money it could lend at appropriate interest rates to cover the costs.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Secret Council of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Secret Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Henri de Rohan asks the Council of St. Gallen to inform the Council of Zürich that he has declared himself ready to support St. Gallen and Appenzell in preventing the passage of the Spanish army. He recommends sending out scouts to determine the route of the Spaniards and to transmit the information simultaneously to Zürich and to the camp of Marshal Horn.
en.recipient: Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Bern invite Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to a meeting of the thirteen cantons and the allied territories on 23 October in Baden. The occasion is the tensions following the siege of Konstanz and the withdrawal of troops of the Catholic cantons and Zürich. Bern requests the dispatch of authorized envoys for the preservation of peace and the clarification of the situation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Bishop Johannes zu Konstanz informs that during the siege of Konstanz, stolen items, including church ornaments and letters, had reached St. Gallen. He asks Burgomaster Sebastian Schobinger to dispose on the part of the authorities that buyers or holders of such Swedish booty must report the items and keep them unchanged until the ownership is clarified.
en.recipient: Sebastian Schobinger, Burgomaster zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Felix Bernburer, Landvogt of the Rhine Valley, for support for the citizens of St. Gallen, Bacher. These have a claim secured by pledge against Albrecht Eisenrat, who comes from Algovia and has left the land. Bernburer has seized Eisenrat's estate. The citizens of St. Gallen ask that the secured claim be favored over other debts and that Bacher be enabled to redeem it.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Felix Bernburer, Council of Zürich and Landvogt of the lower and upper Rhine Valley

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Landvogt Andreas Brugger to help the widow Helena Klösin, née Rigin, in an inheritance matter with the heirs of her deceased husband Konrad Adam. They refer to a previous approval by the city to pay out 200 gulden from the paternal estate and request the Landvogt to grant sovereign assistance so that the plaintiff may obtain her right.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Andreas Brugger, Obrist and Knight, Landvogt of the Lordship of Meilen

en.regest: The Stadtammann and the Stadtgericht of Memmingen ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly cite the creditors of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen, Johann Müller. They request that the summons be made known and posted so that the creditors can assert their claims.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Bishop Johann of Konstanz thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the inquiries into items stolen from a ship, which were found at St. Gallen. As he does not have at hand the persons needed for identification, he asks that the specified items as well as any other finds be kept in custody for a few more days until he sends someone to collect them.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Bishop Johann of Konstanz informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he has sent his Councilor Dr. Georg Dietrich to them. He asks that the envoy be given credit and that they accede to his requests. He assures them that he will behave in a neighborly manner and treat St. Gallen in a neighborly manner.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a request from the Council of St. Gallen for support for the brothers Melchior and Kaspar Schiller in an inheritance matter. They state that they know nothing of the estate of the widow Katharina Zueblin, née Schacher. Should claims of the Schiller arise, they will help them. Lindau remains friendly to St. Gallen in such cases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Elders of the reformed Bohemian and Moravian Brotherhood in Lyße in Poland ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send them the approved Christian collection. They report on their plight in exile and thank them for the support so far.
en.sender: Elders of the reformed Bohemian and Moravian Brotherhood
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Eisenach urgently request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan of 1000 gulden or rose nobles. The money is needed to maintain the Swedish garrison and to pay high contributions. As security, they offer an obligation of the city, of individual wealthy citizens, or of all seven guilds. They promise to repay the good deed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Commander of Lindau to provide their messenger Caspar Gmünder with a safe-conduct and to release him to Ravensburg. There he is to intercede for the release of the imprisoned Niklaus von Deuring, who was taken into custody by the Swedish Field Marshal Gustav Horn.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Commander of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the request for a loan of several thousand gulden for the garrison and contributions. They state that, due to inflation, billeting, and high expenses, they are unable to fulfill the request, and ask for forgiveness. They offer to serve in other matters in the future, and wish peace in the Empire.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Biberach

en.regest: Gustaf Horn answers the petition of the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for Lucas von Deining. He explains that Deining is being held as a war councilor and Statthalter in Ravensburg, as one must secure oneself against suspicious persons. However, he assures that Deining is being treated in his detention in such a way that he feels the benefit of the intercession.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Field Marshal Gustav Horn for the release of Niklaus von Deuring and his relatives. They ask again for the complete release of Deuring or at least of his wife and children and promise their friendship and support in return.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Gustav Horn
