en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to award the seven pieces of merchandise, which belonged to Christoph Endressen and Ludwig Rothhaupt and were sequestered by the creditors Alexander and Leonhard Braun, the heirs of Albrecht Heinzel, Edward Becker and Georg Christoph Pfenning, to the sequestrators according to the law of St. Gallen. The creditors had agreed among themselves on the order of satisfaction.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz respond to the request for a waiver of the departure tax or the succession tax for the widow Elisabeth Kobler. They refer to a regulation of the deceased Archduke Leopold, according to which citizens moving out of the city are to pay the tenth penny of their assets. They cannot contradict this territorial lord's order, but maintain the previous agreements regarding the inheritance.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur transmit to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the letters requested by their town clerk Hans Ulrich Hegner, which are designated as false and fraudulent. These are to help the citizens of St. Gallen defend themselves in a legal dispute against the citizens of Winterthur Peter Hofer and Hans Jakob Tanner, who have fallen into serious legal proceedings because of these documents.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant their citizen Wolfgang Schöbinger peace and stay of proceedings against his creditors. Schöbinger has asked them to help him in settling an old legal dispute with Arbon and in paying the costs. Zürich will write to the Bishop of Konstanz to have Schöbinger released or to demand an answer, and otherwise threatens arrest.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the newly arrived French ambassador has asked them to notify his arrival and mission to the other cantons as well. They announce that they will send an envoy to the ambassador after Easter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Jacob Truchsess, Graf zu Zeil, sends his Councilor and Steward Johann Reichart Öftringer to St. Gallen. He asks the Burgomaster and Council to grant him a favorable audience, to give credit to his presentations, and to show him goodwill. He promises to reciprocate this on every occasion.
en.sender: Johann Jacob Truchsess, Graf zu Zeil
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Vialar, who arrived in Solothurn on the eve as an envoy of the King in all the cantons, informs the Burgomaster and Council of Zürich of this. He asks them to pass the message on to the other cantons so that he can soon be received by them. He promises to hand over to them the general and the specific letters of the King, and offers his services.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the request of Heinrich, Count zu Wolfegg, for admission of him and his wife into the city. They declare themselves willing to grant him a lodging, provided this is possible without harm to the city. Further details they have discussed orally with the envoy of the Count.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Heinrich, Count zu Wolfegg

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Colonel and Commander of Lindau to release again the chests he had seized, together with the money of the citizens of St. Gallen contained therein. The citizens had sent the money to their factor Amadeo Eggolt in Lindau, but the pot was held back on the order of the Commander. The Council, at the request of the citizens, confirms that the money belongs to them and asks for its return.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Colonel and Commander of Lindau

en.regest: Heinrich Dietrich von Altenschweil auf Walthausen informs that, owing to an enemy incursion, he is staying with his family at various places and now has to withdraw from service. He asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant him and his relatives accommodation in the city and to take his small movable goods under protection. He promises to support the city in similar cases and asks for a reply.
en.sender: Heinrich Dietrich von Altenschweil auf Walthausen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Prince zu Fürstenberg asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to take the estate of his deceased wife into custody in an empty vault. He justifies this by his trust in the citizens of St. Gallen and asks for this favor, as he would otherwise not wish to trouble them.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Paulus Scaepscovius, envoy of the Glogau churches, informs Christoph Hoffmann, Primarius of St. Gallen, about the delivery of a collection of 800 Reichs thaler endowed by the city of St. Gallen. He says that he received the amount from Caspar Schlumpf and Georg Thoma in Zürich and assures that the money will benefit exclusively the designated communities.
en.recipient: Christoph Hoffmann

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Kempten inform about the capture of the city by the Swedish Field Marshal Gustav Horn on 21 March and request a Christian collection for the reconstruction of the city, in particular of the burnt-down chancery. They promise to paint the names and coats of arms of the donors and to distribute the surplus to the poor citizenry.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Field Marshal Gustav Horn for the release of Herr von Caimung and his family. They ask him to approve the complete release of Herr von Caimung, his wife and children and to let them travel safely to St. Gallen.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Gustav Horn

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg report that the citizen of St. Gallen Hans Schlumpf was released from arrest after providing bail, but that he absconded without permission and threatened the citizen of Nürnberg Hans Heinrich Pilger the Younger. They ask St. Gallen to compel Schlumpf, upon his return, to provide real bail or to submit to a juratorial binding, and to prevent him from bringing claims against Pilger in Nürnberg.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Bernhard Schaffalitzki, Knight, accuses the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, saying that citizens and residents from St. Gallen, Schaffhausen, Diessenhofen and Stein buy large Mengen of fruit in these places and bring it to St. Gallen, where they sell it in the market square to Lindauers, Constance people and other enemies of the common evangelical confession. He asks the city to prohibit this trade in order to avert damage and to show his well-disposed attitude.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz thank the Council of St. Gallen for the special kindness that their councilors and chancery administrators experienced at the castle of Bürglen through the bailiff there. They express their good neighborly will and offer to reciprocate this in any situation and to continue the neighborly relations that have been maintained well until now.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter of 14 May, which is directed against the corn shipments of the St. Gallen to Überlingen, Rottweil and Zell. They justify the trade in grain and other goods, as they do not practice agriculture and are dependent on the free market. They reject accusations of usury and ask the Generalmajor to continue to treat the St. Gallen favorably.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Bernhard Schaffelitzky von Muckenthal

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a complaint by Colonel Bernhard Schaffelitzky von Muckenthal of 24 May, according to which St. Gallen grain merchants had resold fruits purchased in Schaffhausen, Stein and Diessenhofen to other places. They reject the accusation, as their citizens are obliged to bring grain to the St. Gallen market. They explain that the markets in Überlingen and Zell have ceased and that the merchants therefore bring less grain. They emphasize their neutrality and ask for the maintenance of good relations.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Bernhard Schaffelitzky von Muckenthal

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Gustav Horn for his efforts regarding the release of Herr von Dantzwings and his family. They ask him, on their intercession, to allow Herr von Dantzwings and his kin to return to their house.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Gustav Horn

en.regest: The Secret Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich ask the Burgomaster and Secret Council of the city of St. Gallen to have their citizen Hans Christoph Schärer refrain from selling the powder intended for the Swedish Field Marshal Gustav Horn. They fear that the powder might fall into the hands of hostile powers, and ask for its storage until Horn's return or for the purchase of the powder by St. Gallen.
en.sender: Secret Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Secret Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Secret Council of Zürich request the Burgomaster and Secret Council of St. Gallen to prevent the private pre-sale of saltpeter. They fear that through the actions of private individuals the price of saltpeter rises and the authorities later have to bear higher costs. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to permit the sale only to the persons designated by them and to prohibit the pre-sale for the others.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Secret Council of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Secret Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that their boatmen Heinrich Schalch, Kaspar Trippel and consorts, who were transporting 71 heavy and 54 light sacks of grain for the citizens of St. Gallen Leonhard Ehratzeller, Konrad Ziegler and Othmar Schermess to Inn in Thurgau, were attacked by a band of Swiss soldiers at Stiegen. The soldiers forced the boatmen to drive to Stein, where they loaded half of the grain onto four wagons and brought it to Zell. The other half was left on the ship in Biberach.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen for their letter regarding the seizure of grain by French soldiers. They promise to return the friendship in similar cases.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request E. Wt. to hand over the fruits of the city mint that have been taken. They refer to an enclosed letter and promise to advocate for E. Wt.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: E. Wt.

en.regest: Johann Buntener, Knight, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he has received their letter of 14 June. He asks for an excuse for the absence of Ulrich Kammlis' heir at the appointed court day and requests an extension of four weeks. He proposes to settle the dispute through amicable mediation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The governing cantons of the Thurgau send to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen a coinage ordinance and tariff adopted on 10 June. They ask the Confederates to examine the ordinance and to communicate whether it is to be accepted, published, and observed in their land, so that the work of public benefit may be brought into permanent execution.
en.sender: Von Stetten und Ländern der Zächen des Thurgaus regierenden Orten
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Colonel of Schaffhausen to return to the St. Gallen linen weavers Conrad Ziegler, Leohard Hoegger, Conrad Zwickhen and Othmar Scherer the linen taken from them by a soldier under his command near Konstanz on the water, or to refund the purchase price. The merchants had brought the goods to Zell and possess valid receipts.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Colonel of Schaffhausen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen inform St. Gallen of the statements of their envoys, who observed the course of the shipwreck at Stein. The witnesses report that the ships of St. Gallen were stopped, threatened, and forced to turn back by soldiers at Stein. They describe the refusal to allow passage despite the presentation of the toll tickets and the threat of fire. Schaffhausen asks for acknowledgment of these events.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Leutkirch ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Hans Hafner, tanner. He complains that the St. Gallen Bartholomäus Hüeber owes him 93 gulden for cabbage and glue leather. Hüeber had incurred a debt of 186 gulden with Hans Heurstein in Isny, which Hafner had accepted only as a partial payment. Since Hüeber refuses to pay, the Leutkirch authorities request superior assistance for the payment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich warn Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a Spanish army of 20'000 men, which has gathered above Lake Constance and may possibly want to march through the Turgau and the jurisdictions of St. Gallen towards Konstanz or into the Waldstätten. They request the St. Gallen authorities to secure their passes, set up watchposts, and report on possible movements, in order to prevent damage to the Confederation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to the Landgrave of Stieeling that Swedish soldiers had taken grain from their citizens at Stein am Rhein. They say that they had caused an intervention to Generalmajor Schaffgotschy, but the messenger had been detained in Lindau, as the letter of the Landgrave was considered suspicious. They ask the Landgrave to communicate which further letters had been attached to his intervention, in order to be able to justify themselves.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Maximilian, Landgrave of Stieeling

en.regest: The almoners of the Brotherhood exiled from Böhmen and Mähren thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a donation of 800 Reichs thaler, which was handed over to the Leipzig Easter Market Collegium via Martin Humpoff. They promise to remember the benefaction in prayer and ask for continued favor.
en.sender: Almoners of the Brotherhood exiled from Böhmen and Mähren
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Maximilian, Landgraf zu Stühlingen, communicates that, at the request of a citizen of St. Gallen, he has directed an intercession to Generalmajor Vizthübel. He says that he wrote personally, as he does not possess a copy of the letter. The Governor in Lindau will report the content. He justifies his actions with the duty towards the Empire and the Protestant Estates, as the imperial actions violated the privileges.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg to restrain their citizen Hans Heinrich Bilgeren from harassing the citizen of St. Gallen Hans Schlaipfer with arrest or other inconveniences. Schlaipfer appeals to the Landrechnung, according to which differences are to be settled by amicable negotiation among merchants. St. Gallen requests intercession so that both parties would come to an agreement and disturbances would be avoided.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg

en.regest: The Viztum of Eckstätt informs that he had to intercept a letter from the Confederates to the Obrist Schauenburg, which was carried by Pappenheim, as it contained hostile content. He refers to the neutrality of the Confederates and criticizes that they continue to maintain correspondence with the enemy despite the siege of Konstanz and Überlingen. He announces that he will inform the Generalität of the incident and convey its instructions.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Viztum of Eckstätt declares to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that his earlier accusations concerned not the city of St. Gallen, but the Catholic cantons of the Confederation. He points out that the messenger detained in Lindau had received the suspicious hostile letters not from Pappenheim, but from merchants in St. Gallen. He cannot release the messenger without the instruction of the Obrist of Ossa, but will promote his release.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank the Council of St. Gallen for the friendliness shown to the Confederate envoys with the Abbot of St. Gallen. They request that attention be paid to the matters handed over to the Abbot, that the affected parties be supported, and that Zürich be informed of the outcome.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Glarus thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for their loyalty and support. They ask to accept a small gift, which they have had delivered by their envoys. They assure that they will continue to serve and help St. Gallen in the future, as far as it is in their power.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the voluntary gift of 1000 gulden, which St. Gallen bestowed upon the citizenry of Kempten, damaged by fire. They promise to use the donation for the benefit of the poor, and ask God for a blessing upon St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Chur report that their Chamberlain Jörg Schindler has heard rumors that St. Gallen is afflicted by the plague. This would hinder his journey, as travelers from affected places would not be admitted. They ask St. Gallen to examine the situation and to intervene with the Queen, so that Schindler may travel unharmed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Josua Friedrich, a citizen of St. Gallen, who is staying in Pünzt, complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about his dire straits. He says that he was deceived by a man from Filmerg, sold to Tirol, and forced into the Spanish army. There he suffered great famine and plague. After his flight and capture, he says that he was freed by a nobleman. He asks for permission to return home and to be admitted to the Schiltwacht, as his children are in distress and he cannot live without them.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Landammann and Council of Glarus for the receipt of Gambsthieren. They confirm their Confederate friendship and declare themselves ready to reciprocate this on the occasion. Furthermore, they mention the friendly treatment of the Glarner Landvogt Trümpf and his envoys in St. Gallen.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Glarus

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Altstätten ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to appear on 19 November 1634 for a joint wine valuation in the Rheintal. They hope for a good valuation, as the wine is good and the prices high, and expect that the St. Gallen will well remunerate their envoys.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the departure of their embassy to the French King. The French ambassador Vialar in Solothurn, despite oral requests and the hope for a better opinion, had not issued letters of introduction. The envoys had nevertheless departed in the name of God.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Dekes Vialar expresses his surprise at the decision of the protesting cantons and the allied cantons to send envoys to the King, although he has already forwarded their letter to His Majesty and advocated for them. He warns that this course of action will displease the King, and explains that he cannot render them any service in this matter, as he does not wish to advocate for a cause that is unpleasant to them themselves. In other matters, he offers his services.
en.recipient: Lords of the protesting cantons and the allied cantons

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizen Georg Kees in a legal matter. Kees says that he delivered linen to the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Caspar Betzen, called Schlumpfen, and in return was promised 3 centners of lard. The widow Schlumpfen did not deliver the lard. Kees asks for help so that the widow either delivers the lard or reimburses the 60 florins advanced as well as the costs incurred.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Chancery of Rorschach confirms that Jerg Ernst von Ravensburg and Jacob Hüeber have appeared before Ammann Jacob Heßler. Ernst complains that 39 weeks ago Caspar Schlempp, called Wetz, in St. Gallen sent him a festive piece of lard, to which he received no answer. He declares that he will do what he has to claim from Wetz or his people, and stand to Wetz for question and answer if needed.
en.recipient: Jerg Ernst von Ravensburg

en.regest: Ammann and Council of Feldkirch reply to a letter of 23 October. They declare themselves willing to allow goods and carriers, accompanied by proper Feldkirch letters of safe-conduct, to pass through unimpeded. Goods from Basel or other infected places are to be purified beforehand. Feldkirch asks St. Gallen to act likewise in similar cases and assures its support.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the request of the citizen of St. Gallen Wolfgang Schöbinger, who asks for support in the enforcement of an arrest against the Bishop of Konstanz. Zürich declares that, lacking support from other cantons and due to the difficult circumstances, it is currently unable to settle the claim. They ask St. Gallen to advise Schöbinger to be patient and to be well-disposed towards him and his family in all matters.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Henry de Rohan thanks the cantons of the Confederation for the trust they place in him. He regrets that he must depart because of a royal commission before he can perform the promised services for the cantons. He assures them that until his departure he will do everything possible for the negotiations and that even after his departure he will promote their interests within the limits of his possibilities.
en.recipient: Burgomaster, Schultheiss, Landammann and Council of the Evangelical cantons and places of the Confederation

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have received an answer from the Duke of Lothringen to a joint letter of the evangelical cities and cantons regarding a negotiation. They forward a copy of this answer for information and commend themselves to the care of God.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen to grant their citizen Wolfgang Schowinger, who is in an extreme state of distress, time and a deadline for payment towards his creditors. They refer to the distressed situation of the family with many children and ask for a friendly reception of this intercession.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank the city of Zürich for forwarding the answer of the Duke of Rohan to the letters of the evangelical cities. They rejoice in the benevolent disposition of the Duke towards the evangelical Wesen. Furthermore, they communicate that they recently received news from Frankreich, according to which a part of the Spanish power had suffered shipwreck, and forward this to Zürich.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report to St. Gallen, at its request, on the facts regarding Hans Balthasar Kunz. He says that he had behaved stubbornly as a student and pastor and had been dismissed from the pastoral office. He also says that he had shown himself careless as a teacher and had been dismissed. Furthermore, he says that he had behaved improperly in a dispute with the citizen of St. Gallen Hans Kamby. Zürich therefore banished him from the city and land for two years.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their new citizen Dorothea Meyerin, the wife of the tailor Caspar Geeren, to present herself again in Zürich. She has not honored an agreement with her stepsister Anna Landoltin, according to which she was to pay 100 pounds in cash and secure 200 pounds, and has fled from arrest. Furthermore, the St. Gallen authorities are to report on missing letters.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Basel asks St. Gallen to help the citizens Mathis and Jacob Engeler von Wattwil and Cosy to enforce their rights against the stepmother and stepfather Velten as well as their relatives. Basel promises that it would have acted on its own without this intervention, and asks for a friendly answer.
en.sender: Statthalter of the Burgomaster and the Council of the city of Basel
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jodokus Metzler asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to consider the matter between Hans Jakob Locher and Rutschmann Krüßle as settled. Krüßle had detained Locher in the courts of Itingen and Büren and caused unnecessary costs. Metzler had had the matter transferred back to St. Gallen. He requests the city to protect Locher in his rights and to dismiss Krüßle, as the matter had been settled and acknowledged three times before the assessors.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about the conviction of the naturalized Dorothea Meyer for false accusations against the wife of the tailor Caspar Hirten. The children of the deceased father offer to raise the children themselves after the expiration of the agreed period. Zürich rescinds the previous contract and asks St. Gallen to return the original contract along with the annex, so that the children are not further hindered.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster, Court and Council of Calw describe to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the destruction of their city by the Bavarian army after the Battle of Nördlingen. They ask for a voluntary contribution for the rebuilding of the church, school and town hall as well as for the care of the poor and the sick.
en.sender: Burgomaster, Court and Council of Calw
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Schultheiss and Council of Luzern to intervene with the papal Nuntius and the Spanish envoy in Mailand on behalf of the St. Gallen merchants Schobinger there. These had been hindered in their trade by the Inquisitor in Mailand. The St. Gallen Council sends the Council clerk Christoph Büffler as an envoy and asks Luzern to give him credit and to support him.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Luzern

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landammann and Council of the outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell to prevent their fellow citizens Josef König and Joachim Jäger in Trogen from redeeming an old perpetual annuity deed of the St. Gallen church for half the money. They refer to the fact that the annuity now serves the evangelical religion and the preachers, and appeal to neighborly friendship.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to an inquiry from Weiler regarding the detained Hans Christen Steiger. He had lived with the daughter of the curate, which led to rumors of a pregnancy. The mother had communicated the rumors to the man, whereupon he left the house at night to pick up the daughter. He had tried to break down the door but was not hit. St. Gallen considers the case not fully clarified and asks for further information.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Imperial Bailiff, Schultheiss and Council of Weiler

en.regest: The Imperial Bailiff, Schultheiss and Council of Wil report that Hans Lichtensteiger von Bernsthal, who had been a resident (Hintersasse) of the Lords of St. Gallen for twenty years, is accused of his daughter Magdalena having lived incontinently. This is the reason for the revocation of his rights and his flight. Since the accusations cannot be confirmed, they ask for written information on the cause of the accusation and the current results of the investigation, in order to be able to act accordingly.
en.sender: Imperial Bailiff, Schultheiss and Council of Wil
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Landammann and Council of the Land of Appenzell to enable their citizen Caspar Schirmer to purchase Holz worth 400 gulden in the Tuffner Rod. They request that the Holz be left standing and that Schirmer be permitted to transport it into the St. Gallen countryside, so that he may settle the purchase price from the city treasury.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich communicate to St. Gallen an imperial letter concerning the free Imperial knighthood on the Danube, in the Hegau, Allgäu, and on Lake Constance. They report on the presence of the Duke of Lothringen in Breisach and the movement of imperial and Spanish troops in the Elsass. In view of this situation, they invite St. Gallen to a conference on 16 February in Aarau to discuss the defense and the attitude towards the Bishop.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, after the death of the citizen of Zürich Hans Balthasar Rütten in St. Gallen, to search for a small chest with documents. It is said that it contains, among other things, letters from the deceased Colonel Zollikoffer and a letter of safe-conduct issued by Zürich. The citizens of Zürich request that these be transmitted to them.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Wilhelm Heinrich von Waldburg, Erbtuchsäss, imperial councillor and chamberlain, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he intends to travel to his estates. He requests the release of seven chests deposited with the citizens of St. Gallen. His rent master Matthias Klinge will collect them. He thanks them for the custody thus far and asks for official assistance in the safe transport.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Bishop Johann of Konstanz to support their fellow councillor Georg Schindler in the matter of a property in Thurgau, purchased from his grandfather Sebastian Zillinen and held as a fief from the Bishopric. They request the Bishop to hear Schindler amicably and grant him the enfeoffment in accordance with the old letter of enfeoffment.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Johann, Bishop of Konstanz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Landvogt Jost Püntiner, in the dispute between their hospital officer Vincenz Schoeholtzer of Istighofen and the Oberholzer over a small sum, to bring the matter to a swift conclusion at the next court day in Aistig. They request that the affair be settled without further delay, so that Schoeholtzer may find peace and the debtors of the city of St. Gallen can fulfill their obligations.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Jost Püntiner, Landvogt of the Lower and Upper Turgau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Bibrach ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to provide for their citizen Conrad Saumen, who, as guardian of the children of the deceased Daniel Schlumpf, has no means, in the hospital. They themselves cannot provide help, as they are burdened by war costs and hunger. They promise to settle future interest from the estate if the widow and the children agree.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to officially compel the heirs of the deceased citizens of St. Gallen, Georg and Daniel Zollicoffer, to provide the warranty and indemnification promised in the deed of sale. This concerns the purchase of the estate of Wilderen, which has fallen to the widow and children of the deceased Nicolaus Teutschen. The buyers refuse to make restitution despite repeated reminders.
en.sender: The Administrator of the Captaincy, also Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Schultheiss and Council of Bern to support their town clerk Heinrich Rotmundt and his brother, the St. Gallen citizen Johann Melchior Rotmundt, in a legal dispute with the Bernese subject Johann Rudolf Küchlin. Rotmundt has already obtained a judgment in favor of his brother, but cannot enforce it due to the opponent's delaying tactics. The St. Gallen authorities ask for support so that the brothers can again exercise their rights and their office.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Bern

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information about the local meat prices for oxen, cows, and calves, as well as about the method of weighing. They wish to orient their own butchers' prices, which these want to raise, on those of their neighbors.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Luzern for the support of their citizen Christoph Büchler, who was troubled by the Inquisition in Mailand. They ask Luzern to continue to help in the matter, in particular through intervention with the Nuntius in Rom and with Cardinal Barbarino, so that the licenses for trade in Germany are issued and Büchler can collect his debts.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Luzern

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen that the Duke of Rohan has ordered 6000 men on foot and 600 horses to cross the Rhine and march through the County of Kyburg to St. Gallen. They ask St. Gallen to send out scouts to gauge the mood of the imperial people on Lake Constance and to report daily.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the French ambassador Meliand has arrived in Solothurn. They ask that this news also be communicated to the other cantons of the Confederation, and enclose a copy of the ambassador's letter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen send to the Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz the meat price list in use there. They inform them that the butchers had applied for a surcharge on beef due to high fattening costs. St. Gallen had agreed to this for the fattened animals, which could be slaughtered at 5 1/2 kreuzer. For the remaining meat, the previous price list applies until further notice.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Administrator of the Captaincy as well as Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they had received a letter from the Hauptleute and Ratssendten of the three Pünkte, which was addressed to the thirteen cantons of the Confederation and concerned the recovery of the Feldlin. They make the St. Gallen party aware of it through a copy.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen transmit to the bailiff and Council of Bischofszell the meat price list customary in St. Gallen. They report that the butchers had applied the day before for an increase in the price of beef to 5½ kreuzer, because they had fattened expensive oxen in the autumn. This had been permitted only for the slaughter of these animals; until further regulation, the previous price list remains in force.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: bailiff and Council of Bischofszell

en.regest: The Verwalterhauptmann together with the Burgzunftmeister and Council of the city of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform them how high the meat is currently taxed and weighed in St. Gallen, since the butchers there are asking for an increase in the meat tax and Konstanz wishes to orient itself according to its neighbor.
en.sender: Verwalterhauptmann together with the Burgzunftmeister and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Henri de Rohan informs that, by order of the King, he will march with his army into the County of Graubünden. He asks the recipients to prepare everything necessary for the passage of the army, and sends Christoph Scherrer, who will convey the details.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the special honor and kindness they showed their countrymen during the French passage through the city. They offer to return this at an opportunity and ask God for peace and prosperity of the fatherland.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jost Püntner asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to decide on two points still in dispute between Ruotschman Trübler and Hans Jakob Locher. It concerns a supplementary payment for the improvement of the house at Dietingen and costs of 125 florins. Since Trübler seeks his fortune elsewhere, he asks for a prompt and just decision.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Hauptleute and Council envoys of the three Bünde at Chur request the Confederates, in view of the danger threatening their passes and lands, to fulfill their duties of oath and league and to support them in case of emergency with manly help. They ask for a rapid answer regarding the intentions of the cantons, so that they may act accordingly, and promise in turn to uphold the obligations of the alliance.
en.sender: Hauptleute and Council envoys of the three Bünde at Chur
en.recipient: The 13 cantons of the Confederation

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Schultheiss and Council of Bern for help in lifting an arrest imposed on three citizens of St. Gallen, the Zollikoffer people, in the Landvogtei Yfferten. They refer to the attached report and expect that Bern will grant the St. Gallen the usual support of the Confederates.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Bern

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich send Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen a copy of a letter from the Captain and the Council Assembly of the Three Points to the 13 cantons of the Confederation, to inform them of its content.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help the three daughters of the deceased citizen of Lindau, Hans Schüelin, namely Margaretha, Magdalena and Anna, in the collection of their inheritance from the estate of their sister Barbara Schirmers, who died in St. Gallen. The sisters had turned to Lindau, as they are in a state of need and depend on the inheritance. Lindau asks for a friendly facilitation of the inheritance collection.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Directors of the Imperial Knighthood in Schwaben ask the Confederates to help in the recovery of goods and documents stolen in Thurgau and elsewhere. They propose issuing an open edict ordering the surrender of the loot under threat of heavy penalties, and ask for an inquisition in Thurgau. Should this fail, they threaten to claim the damage from those responsible for opening the pass at Stein.
en.sender: His Roman Imperial Majesty, respectively the Council and the Free Imperial Knighthood and Nobility in the Land to Schwaben, of both quarters on the Thonau, also the appointed Directors, Committees and present members in the Hegau, Allgäu and on Lake Constance
en.recipient: Burgomaster, Schultheiss, Landammann and Councils of the cities and cantons of the Confederation: Zürich, Bern, Glarus, Basel, Schaffhausen, Appenzell and St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the intercession for the citizen of St. Gallen Johann Kunz. He has claims against the Sponholz heirs. Some of the heirs have declared themselves willing to pay the share of the bequest, while others have not yet declared themselves. Should Kunz turn to a lawyer to take legal action against the heirs, he will receive justice in Konstanz.
en.sender: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Statthalter and Council of the city of Zürich communicate to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the answer of the free Imperial knighthood in Schwaben to an earlier letter. They ask for support in the formulation of a common answer of the Evangelical cantons and promise to discuss their own side in such a way that the knighthood is satisfied.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to allow their executioner to appear in the morning in the Hauptfleck of Appenzell to interrogate a person detained there who has been subjected to the question.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Emperor Ferdinand II. informs the Confederation that Zürich had had 800 centners of powder, which had been ordered in the name of the Emperor, brought to itself upon the arrival of Rohan. He censures this as a violation of the Imperial rights and treaties with the House of Österreich and orders that the powder be delivered immediately to the Emperor's plenipotentiary.
en.recipient: Confederate cantons

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern thank the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen for the hospitable reception and the friendliness towards their envoys, who had negotiated with the Abbot of St. Gallen regarding the Toggenburg religious matter. They promise to serve St. Gallen in similar cases with the same zeal.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to the petition of the naturalized citizens Hans Heinrich Sigeren, Cornelius Leu and Georg Hof for support in the release of their goods seized in Nördlingen. They declare that the goods had never been their property, but had only been managed as factors. They ask the Emperor to examine the matter himself, as an attestation without further investigation could serve to their detriment.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Emperor Ferdinand II.

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of the city of Zürich send Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen a draft of a reply to the Swabian Imperial Knightage. They ask for a statement, so that the letter to the competent authorities can be drawn up.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to the Landvogt in Turgau that Leonhard Kreuz, who comes from Heiligenberg, stole a linen cloth in St. Gallen. He was put in the pillory, whipped, and banished from the city and court. Since he subsequently stole again in Bischofszell, the St. Gallen authorities ask to be informed if any further thefts become known.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Jost Püntner, Landvogt in Turgau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that some citizens of St. Gallen have recently sold a not insignificant amount of powder to the enemies of St. Gallen. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to investigate this and take the necessary measures.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Schultheiss and Council of Wil to spare their fellow councillor Hansmann Kech and his son in the matter of the Constance procurator Messler. Messler has attacked the honour of the women of St. Gallen and the chastity of the son. The St. Gallen ask to abide by the pronounced judgments and to desist from further prosecution.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Wil

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to a request by the citizens of Nürnberg Hans Heinrich Bilgerin, Camerlin and Jörg Ruchol for a certificate that goods seized in Nördlingen are their property. They refuse the certificate, as the citizens of Nürnberg had always declared to St. Gallen that they possessed the goods only as factors, and the citizens of St. Gallen are not willing to turn to the imperial officer.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Altstätten inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have received a letter from the other courts involved in the Wine Committee. Since they could not make a final decision without their consent, they forward the letter and ask for the opinion of the St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Altstetten remind Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of the promise to send an answer or resolution regarding the sale of wine. Since the St. Gallen citizens wished to present their opinion orally, the Altstetten authorities ask to hear their opinion in friendly neighborhood on 23 June or 2 July.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report that they had heard from their citizens that these had behaved improperly in the courts of the recipients. It had been reported that a considerable amount of thatch had been broken from two houses and the hurdles slashed. The recipients are to bring the matter to the village on the condition that the citizens are to be allowed to keep their household. A deadline for the settlement of the matter had been granted to the citizens.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: the Confederates

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of the city of Zürich report to Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen that they had received the answer of the St. Gallen naturalized citizens to the latest Zürich request for the sale of two guns. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to prevent the sale of such weapons as much as possible and to earnestly admonish the citizens who acquire guns not to endanger their own benefit and to sell the guns only where it is proper, or to refrain from doing so entirely.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of the city of Zürich inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the decisions of the Confederate envoys at the Baden Imperial Diet. They had explained to the Imperial Commissioner Count von Hohenems that the hereditary union with Frankreich had only taken place for the reinstatement of the Bündner in their lands and would otherwise be firmly maintained. The Count had however expressed concerns that the Imperial forces would now seek out the French and the passes. Furthermore, Imperial troops would come to Lindau and the Hungarian Queen would demand the pass through the Prelate of St. Gallen for 12'000 men. Zürich requests St. Gallen to send all necessary scouts to preserve the Confederation from harm.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform that the Imperial Majesty complains about them, because the Duke of Rhaun, in the name of the Confederates, withdrew troops from their territory. They reject the accusation, as they knew nothing of it, and ask St. Gallen for information whether this was done at the instigation of envious persons. They refer to their letter of 22 June and expect a reply.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich reject the imperial complaint, stating that they had withdrawn 600 centners of powder after the arrival of the Duke of Rohan. They declare that they know nothing of such a proceeding and ask the Emperor to consider them excused and to continue his grace.
en.recipient: Ferdinand II., Emperor

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to deliver a letter to the imperial majesty, which they recently received, via the nearest route, however outside Lindau, to the imperial court. They request this friendly assistance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jörg Dietrich Reding, bailiff of Rorschach, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a misstatement by the merchant Ludwig Bilger, who had claimed that linen bought in St. Gallen had been sold for 1 gulden per pound. In fact, he had sold the goods for 40 kreuzer per pound. Reding asks the people of St. Gallen not to punish the merchants of Rorschach for this unconsidered statement, but to treat them amicably.
en.sender: Jörg Dietrich Reding, bailiff of Rorschach
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Wangen to help the St. Gallen citizen Franz Engwiler to obtain the inheritance of his deceased daughter Anna Maria from the estate of her grandmother Maria Staingadmerin. Engwiler was the father of the daughter and thus the next heir. The St. Gallen ask for an authoritative disposition so that the inheritance may be transferred without hindrance.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Wangen

en.regest: The French envoy Meliand asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in the name of the French King, for the enlistment of 12'000 Swiss mercenaries. He requests the city to send authorized envoys to Solothurn, who are to participate in an assembly on 5 August and consent to the recruitment. The King promises the payment of the pensions and further advantages.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admonish their butchers not to sell the cattle across Lake Constance. This contradicts the resolution of the last annual accounts day in Baden and makes meat more expensive for the population. Zürich threatens severe punishment in case of non-compliance and asks for compliance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Moliand requests the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to supply Captain Striker from the canton of Uri with the weapons necessary for him, against payment. He refers to the good willingness shown by the St. Gallen envoy during the recruitment carried out by him in the name of the King of Frankreich, and promises that His Majesty and he personally will be grateful for this.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Syndics and Council of Genf reply to a letter of the 26th of the previous month, in which the payment of the interest and a part of the principal was demanded. They state that, due to great and continuing burdens in recent years, they are unable to provide everything, but promise to pay the interest to Herr André Morel as soon as possible. They ask for patience regarding the rest and express their friendship.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Confederates regarding the complaint of the nuns of Meggenkloster. They complain that Ulrich Hangkristen had bought up their oxen, which violates the monastery rules. The nuns had also received meat on several occasions, which they are not entitled to. St. Gallen asks the Confederates not to support the nuns in this manner any further, and promises to settle the matter internally.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Confederate cantons

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landammann and Council of Äusseren Rhoden of the Land of Appenzell to compel their countrymen Jacob and Peter Wetter, Hans List and Uli Hoffstetter, who had sworn as bleaching servants, to fulfill their period of service with the St. Gallen bleaching masters. The servants had allowed themselves to be poached into military service despite their oath, which caused damage to the masters.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Äusseren Rhoden of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to postpone the division of the estate of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen R. Weichmanin until the arrival of the marital bailiff Endres Stöffing or his proxy. Stöffing, who is in imperial military service, has a claim to his inheritance. Konstanz asks for an official order so that the heirs do not take possession of the inheritance before Stöffing has made himself known.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Ammann and Council of Unterwalden to compel the citizen Jacob Züblin there, guardian of the boy Hans Züen, to pay the outstanding costs for board and education to Bernhard Schopfer, rector of the St. Gallen Gymnasium. Furthermore, the boy is to be handed over to the rector, as the latter would otherwise have to apply coercive measures.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Ammann and Council of Unterwalden

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Basel request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel their citizens Hans Jakob Locher, Hans Ebner and the heirs of Felix Züblin to liquidate their claims against the estate of the deceased Basel citizen Samuel Misot within eight days. Since the creditors did not appear, the proceedings will be continued after the expiration of the deadline and no further claims will be considered.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of the city of St. Gallen inform the neighboring communities that the market scheduled for 17 October in St. Gallen is cancelled due to plague and enemy danger. They request the recipients to make this cancellation known to their people so that they avoid unnecessary costs for a journey.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the city of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Neighboring communities

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Altstätten inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the envoys of the courts of the Rhine Valley in Altstätten have deliberated on the wine committee. They have decided, despite the high prices in comparison to other foodstuffs, for reasons of neighborhood, to accept the price of 7 kreuzer and 2 pfennig, with the hope of enjoying this again in the future. The resolution was passed unanimously.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jonas Liebing and Michael Castner, in the name of the church and school servants, widows, and orphans driven out of the Upper Palatinate, ask for a charitable support. They justify this with the continuing state of distress, the rise in prices, and the approaching winter. They refer to earlier help from St. Gallen and ask for an answer.
en.sender: Jonas Liebing and Michael Castner, Deputies for the Administration of the Christian Upper Palatinate Collection Work
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Christoph Heinzel, Stadtammann, and the judges of Memmingen ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have the attached edict concerning the court day for debts for the deceased citizen of Memmingen, David Brümel, publicly posted among the citizens of St. Gallen. They suspect that citizens of St. Gallen may have claims on the arrested assets of Brümel and wish to safeguard their rights in this way.
en.sender: Christoph Heinzel, Stadtammann, and the judges of Memmingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Exiled Palatine clergy and pastors ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a charitable collection for the churches and school services in distress in the Inspection of Seltz as well as for other exiles in Straßburg and Weißenburg. They ask for distribution by a pious person or a deacon. The request was confirmed by citizens of Straßburg of the Reformed religion on 19 October 1635.
en.sender: Johannes Bicaeus, Fridericus Emmerich, M. Joannes Reinerus Erpff, Joannes Froschius, Johann Bernhardt Samman, Andreas Haan, Isaac Ostertag, Margretha Joannis Heinen, M. Nicolaus Johan von der Schichten, Georgius Melchior Geyer, Johannis Martius, Nicolaus Heschius
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to request information in the legal dispute between Hans Jakob Kössner and Hans Jakob Peyer from Schaffhausen. It concerns the dowry of the deceased woman of St. Gallen, Engal Krumbin, daughter of the deceased Christoph Krumb. The men of Zürich ask that the citizens of St. Gallen be questioned and that it be reported in writing what property and goods the Krumbin brought to Schaffhausen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizens Leutnant Scherrer and Ulrich Lacher to settle the outstanding Zehrgeld bill with costs to the Zürich innkeeper Hans Andre Küter. The two had committed in writing to remit the money but have not yet complied with the payment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Secret Council of the city of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the notification regarding the imminent transit of Spanish troops to Italien. They confirm their loyalty to the Confederation and give their bailiff at Kyburg the order to procure a specific number of musketeers, who are to march to St. Gallen immediately if needed. Furthermore, they write to their Landvogt in the Rhyntal to take the necessary precautions for the defense of the land.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Secret Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the Honorable Womanhood to assist the widow Barbara Hergin. An inheritance has fallen to Hergin from her deceased aunt Katharina Luzin, the widow of the locksmith Peter Braun. The city asks for support so that Hergin may receive her due inheritance in a timely manner.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Honorable Womanhood

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the appointment of a general court day for the creditors of the deceased citizen of Lindau, Abraham Schmelz. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to post and publish the edict according to their custom, so that any creditors of St. Gallen may also assert their claims.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Schmalz, Statthalter, and the judges and verdict-givers of the city court of Kempten request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish the attached edict. It concerns the estate of the deceased citizen and chandler of Kempten, Sebastian Wächelin. Creditors and interested parties are to be summoned for the inventory of the estate.
en.sender: Hans Schmalz, Statthalter, and the judges and verdict-givers of the city court of Kempten
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in the legal dispute between their fellow citizen Hans Jacob Kussmaul and Hans Jacob Hugen called Gwerbet of Schaffhausen, to investigate what Hugens wife Engel Kümmin of St. Gallen took with her to Schaffhausen. They request written information regarding the amount of the goods taken, as a hearing in Zürich has been scheduled.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to prohibit and hold in arrest the sum paid by the city of Sabioneta or by Herr Francesco Bevilacqua of Mantua for the imprisoned Italians, until Lindau and the creditors there are compensated for their expenses. They also request information on the prices and weights for ox, beef, and veal in St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Bonhoeffer asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hold a voluntary collection for his mother and sisters, who are in flight from Hanau, as well as for himself. He asks that the money be transmitted via the Swedish Council Josias Gläsen. He offers to repay the sum.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to an intercession by Lindau for the widow of the deceased Walther Margrath and Marx Lindner. They state that the Italian debtors had already repaid the money to Andrea Boßner and that the arrest had been lifted. Furthermore, they report on the meat prices in St. Gallen: veal is scarce and costs five kreuzer per pound, beef forty Lot per pound.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the upcoming imperial passage. They report that the Überwehr in Toggenburg and Oberthurgau has already been carried out. Out of concern for safety, they ask the St. Gallen authorities to send reliable scouts and to inform them immediately of any incoming news.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landvogt Heinrich Zürcher in the Sarganserland asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to award the inheritance of their deceased sister Elisabeth to his subject Mathias Wepf and his sister Anna from Weingarten. Zürcher explains that, according to Sarganser law, the children of the other deceased siblings could not inherit. He promises that the Wepf brothers and sisters will take care of the rights of the nieces and nephews and will not harass them.
en.sender: Heinrich Zürcher, Landvogt in the Sarganserland
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Deputies of the Ecclesiastical Upper Palatine Collection Work ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in the name of the expelled church and school officials, widows and orphans, for a voluntary tax for support. They justify this with the continuing state of distress, the rise in prices and the winter, as the hope for peace was destroyed by the peace between the Emperor and the Elector of Sachsen. They promise a fair accounting and thank for previous help.
en.sender: Jonas Liebing, Michael Casmar und Johannes Rath
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant their fellow councillor and baker Hans Schickhen the aid of the superior court, so that he may benefit from the St. Gallen jurisdiction. They promise to act in the same manner in similar cases in reverse.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Christoph Hainzel, Stadtammann and judge of Memmingen, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post the attached edict. Therein, the widow of the deceased citizen of Memmingen Christoph Stürcklin is requested to declare the goodwill of the creditors, as she cannot pay out the assets. Citizens of St. Gallen could be affected as creditors.
en.sender: Christoph Hainzel, Stadtammann and judge of Memmingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: President and Chamber Councillors of the Guardianship of the deceased heirs of Archduke Leopold of Österreich, of the Upper Austrian lands, reply to the letter of the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of 27 December. They communicate that the increase in tolls ordered in the Arlbergish lordship and in some offices in Schwaben has already been revoked again and that the officials have been instructed not to burden anyone any further.
en.sender: President and Chamber Councillors of the Guardianship of the deceased heirs of Archduke Leopold of Österreich, of the Upper Austrian lands
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Stadtammann, Burgomaster and Council of Mösskirch inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that in Mösskirch foreigners and natives have equal inheritance rights. They ask for support for their fellow citizen Hans Studmann, who has come into an inheritance, and for an authentic chancery certificate, so that he may, during the lifetime of his deceased wife Anna Vömmelin and in this inheritance case, proceed according to the statutes.
en.sender: Stadtammann, Burgomaster and Council of Mösskirch
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the death of Burgomaster Burkhard Hüßler. Since he left no direct heirs, but only nieces and nephews, they ask for the notification of any relatives. The heirs are to legitimize themselves within ten weeks so that the inheritance can be distributed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Neunkirch inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the death of Burckhardt Syeß. Since there are no heirs in the ascending or descending line, but only cousins and female cousins, they ask for information on whether any other relatives exist. They set a deadline of ten weeks for the legitimation of the heirs, after which the inheritance shall fall to those who have appeared.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Ernst Graf zu Hanau asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen again for help. He says that he is in distress and exile with his family, in particular his widowed mother, because of the war. He promises to repay the support received after he has regained his property.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter of 11 March 1636 (old style) from Mündelheim. They hand over the balances submitted by their citizens, who are interested in the Äbel inheritance, and ask Mündelheim to proceed further in the matter. They recommend the merchants of St. Gallen again and hope that Mündelheim will help them with their claim in the Äbel inheritance, in order to maintain trade and correspondence.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Guardians, Burgomaster and Council of Mündelheim

en.regest: Pfleger, Burgomaster and Council of Mündelheim reply to a letter of 14 January 1636 regarding the estate claims of Caspar Schlumpf, Anton Zill, the heirs of the deceased Christoph Schlaffer and of the deceased Hans Thomas against the deceased Burgomaster of St. Gallen Hans Knüppel. They ask that the creditors be instructed to submit their claims in writing. Furthermore, they remind the St. Gallen heirs of the deceased Hans Tischler of a debt of 134 gulden, 7 schilling and 6 pfennig from the Knüppel estate.
en.sender: Pfleger, Burgomaster and Council of Mündelheim
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the measures taken against the price increase and the shortage of fruits and grain. They have restricted free purchase, prohibited buying up and export, and ordered house searches to determine the stock. They ask the St. Gallen to take similar measures and to supply their own population. Zürich offers to sell grain to St. Gallen if needed, but continues to prohibit export.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Statthalter and Council of the Äussere Roden of the Land of Appenzell request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen not to allow anything to be concluded or pronounced to the detriment of Ulrich Zürcher, a citizen of Appenzell and tanner in Tüffen, on account of an inheritance case. They ask that the matter be left open until other pending inheritance disputes between the relatives of both sides are clarified.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the Äussere Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform the Abbot of Rorschach that the weaver Hans Fremde from Weiler, who is in service in St. Gallen, has been detained due to a debt matter. They ask the Abbot to engage in the matter, as Fremde is a member of the monastery. Should the judgment of the court of Konstanz prove to be valid and the spiritual woman be attacked, they will let Fremde be brought before the court.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Abbot of Rorschach

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the creditors of the widow of the deceased citizen of Lindau, Balthasar Hößlin, who are resident there, to accept the payment plan proposed by the administrators of the widow. This provides that the creditors settle half of their claims immediately with goods or money and receive the rest in three installments without interest. Lindau refers to the difficult economic situation and the danger that in a lawsuit the creditors would receive less.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rothenburg ob der Tauber ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Georg Setler, who has raised the child of the deceased St. Gallen citizen Jacob Segelstein, in the settlement of the inheritance. Setler has not yet received maintenance payments of 60 Reichstaler. The Rothenburgers ask for official assistance so that the child of Segelstein, whose whereabouts are unclear, may be handed over and put under guardianship.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of Rothenburg ob der Tauber
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform the city of Lindau that they have examined the claims of their naturalized creditors there against the widow of the deceased Balthasar Hoßlein. They ask Lindau, in a neighborly manner, to instruct their own citizens to agree to the proposed method of payment and to raise no further complaints.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen remind Genf of the outstanding interest on a principal sum of 1715 Sonnenkronen. They demand the payment of the two overdue interest payments for 1634 and 1635 as well as the repayment of the principal sum within 84 days, in order to avoid future reminders.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Syndics, Burgomaster and Council of Genf

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Wangen request Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post an edict concerning the appointed general court day for the heirs of the deceased citizen couple Jacob Scheuzelin and Barbara. This is to be done so that no one is curtailed in their rights and cannot plead ignorance.
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to an inquiry from the city of Konstanz regarding the cloth trade. Sechs master dyers report that the pound of blue yarn costs 20 to 24 kreuzer depending on quality. For Endig, which is used for dyeing, they paid 40 to 45 batzen. The smooth or Tafel-Endig is less suitable than the other.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Administrator of the Landvogtei, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: The administrator of the captaincy, the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information about the dyeing wages. They wish to know how high the wage for the pound of blue yarn in St. Gallen is and at what price the dyers there trade Endich. The inquiry serves the settlement of a dispute between the wool weavers and the dyers in Konstanz.
en.sender: The administrator of the captaincy, the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Syndics and Council of Genf regret that St. Gallen has written again about the interest, as they had already caused payment to Herr Morel to be made. They ask for forgiveness that they could not pay the capital, as this is impossible for them, and promise to value the patience of the St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Christoph Heinzel, Ammann and the judges of Memmingen, request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish the edict concerning the first court day for the creditors of the citizen of Memmingen Georg Friderich Serer, so that no one be curtailed in their rights.
en.sender: Christoph Heinzel, Ammann and the judges of Memmingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Ernst zu Hanau thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for their sympathy regarding the death of his father and for the support during his time in exile. He promises to repay the city's kindness in the future and commends the city and its citizens to the protection of God.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Empress-widow Claudia requests the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist the communities of the Lordship of Ehenberg in taking out a loan for the reconstruction and the sowing of fields. The communities had turned to her through their Oberbailiff Johann Pancratz Gantzen and asked for a recommendation to the St. Gallen authority.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen answer the inquiry of the Äussere Rhoden regarding the inheritance claims of the deceased Katharina Buchnerin and Barbara Buschorlerin. They state that the heirs may receive the assets acquired in St. Gallen. The 75 gulden that the Buchnerin had received from the St. Gallen woman Steinin could not be reclaimed. St. Gallen asserts the right to dispose of the property acquired in the city and refers to the practice to date.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Äussere Rhoden of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Wil request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene with the local Junker Thon von Lütkirch. Their servant Peter Hörnberger, a Bawamtsfahrer, lost his horse at the last St. Gallen day. Hörnberger suspects a servant from Elagkhuffen, who had been in an inn on the same evening. Thon had promised to cover damages caused by his Swabian servants. Wil requests that Thon be made to replace the damage or to hold the suspect accountable.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Palatine-Zweibrücken envoys and councillors describe the dire situation in the Principality of Zweibrücken as a result of the siege by imperial troops. They ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a Christian tax or collection for the impoverished pastors, schoolteachers, widows and orphans. The funds are to be brought to Basel via the town clerk Jacob Freiveln. The senders promise to praise the good deed of the St. Gallen people to the Regent Luise.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen have levied 175 Reichstaler for the distressed church and school services, along with widows and orphans, in the Duchy of Zweibrücken. The document lists the recipients in the offices of Zweibrücken, Meisenheim, Neustadt, and Liechtenberg, as well as the responsible distribution commission.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Church and school services in the Duchy of Zweibrücken

en.regest: Pflegere, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizens Bartholomäus Bayer and the widow Jacobina Millreiterin. The St. Gallen Tobias Schobinger had lent them 50 Reichstaler and received a pledge worth 50 Reichstaler, without making the agreed repayment. Augsburg requests St. Gallen to compel Schobinger or his parents to pay.
en.sender: Pflegere, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
