en.regest: Ammann and Council of the town and bailiwick of Zug request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their former citizen Jacob Zeigler, called Pucher, and his wife Anna Maria Küstlerin in the realization of an inheritance. Zeigler says that he inherited a benefice estate in the benefice of Thürer from his parents Jacob Küstler and Barbara Nussbömerin. Furthermore, he says that an inheritance share of 300 gulden fell to him through the death of his first wife Anna Steinerin. Zug asks for favorable treatment and assistance in enforcing these claims.
en.sender: Ammann and Council of the town and bailiwick of Zug
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Wil report to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that their fellow citizen Widlis has testified in court against Junker Hans. They submit the sworn statements of the witnesses Ulrich Wiser, Ernst Schlatter and Christoph Herzog. These confirm that Junker Hans had promised to identify the thief of a stolen horse. Wil asks St. Gallen to support Widlis within the framework of the law.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to properly inventory the estate of the deceased Mingardin von Mingardinis and to place it in official custody until further notice. They request the sending of a copy of the inventory or, if possible, of the entire estate to Zürich, as the parties there could be heard by the gentlemen Thomas Zwickher and his son, appointed by the opposing party of Rudolf Werdmüller.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The catalogue documents the distribution of 500 gulden in Reich currency, which the church of the city of St. Gallen levied in 1636 for the suffering Upper Palatine exiles. The sum is paid out to pastors, schoolmasters, collectors, widows, orphans, and those suffering politically. In addition, 100 gulden for exiles in the Lower Palatinate are transferred to Daniel Arnoldt, the church council secretary. The payment took place on 6 June 1636 in Nürnberg.
en.sender: Church of the city of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Upper Palatine exiles

en.regest: Jonas Liebing, Michael Castner and Johannes Rath thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on behalf of the Upper Palatinate exiles for the approved collection of 500 gulden. The money was exchanged and handed over through the citizen of St. Gallen Andreas Wegelin. They assure that they will pay out the funds as far as possible and deliver the receipts.
en.sender: Jonas Liebing, Michael Castner and Johannes Rath
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Commissioners for the Administration of the Christian Upper Palatine Collection in Nürnberg acknowledge receipt of 500 gulden in good gold and other current coin. The money was brought by Andreas Wegelin, who had collected it on behalf of the Council of St. Gallen at the Nürnberg Ordinance. The sum is intended for homeless Palatine co-religionists and is distributed accordingly.
en.sender: Jonas Libing, Michael Castner und Johannes Karg
en.recipient: Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landvogt Jost Pündener to inform them in writing for what reasons Jörg Teubacher of Lachen, who is detained in St. Gallen, recently sat in prison in Frauenfeld for theft and how he was released again. Teubacher claims to have been innocent and to have been released without compensation. St. Gallen wishes to know how it is to behave towards Teubacher.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Jost Pündener, Landvogt of the lower and upper Turgau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank the bailiff and Council of Bischofszell for the report on the interrogation of the St. Gallen prisoner. He denied the accusations and identified himself as Jörg Trautmann. The St. Gallen authorities ask to allow their own executioner to conduct further questioning and to report the result of the torture in writing.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Bailiff and Council of Bischofszell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Landvogt concerning the prisoner Jörg Löblacher. He has denied having gotten into a dispute over a horse, but states that he was arrested in Konstanz for the theft of his brother Veit and brought to Frauenfeld. In Frauenfeld, he had given his name as Jörg Trummer. St. Gallen asks the Landvogt to look into the books and report in writing who this imperial prisoner actually is.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Jost Püntner, Landvogt of the lower and upper Thurgau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report that they are holding in their custody a suspicious young fellow named Jörg Leblerßer von Luchen from the Thurgau. He was recently imprisoned in Arbon as well for theft. They request the Statthalter and Council of Arbon to inform them in writing for what reasons the man was detained there and under what conditions he was released, so that they can decide on further proceedings.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of Arbon

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Administrator of the Captaincy and Burgomaster of the city of Konstanz to inform them in writing whether a prisoner named Veit Trüebbachern of Lenzburg was detained there. It concerns the suspicion that he had stolen ducats from a nobleman in Konstanz. The St. Gallen prisoner Jörg Trüebbachern, the brother of the one in Konstanz, was detained in Ermishoffen and Frauenfeld for the same theft, but was released, as he was innocent. The St. Gallen ask for information about the case of the brother.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Administrator of the Captaincy and Burgomaster of the city of Konstanz

en.regest: The Kirchenrat of the Pfalz thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the reception of the delegated church officials and for the support in the blockade of Frankenthal. He informs that he has received a sum of over 363 Reichstaler as well as further donations from Switzerland, in order to provide for the starving church and school officials in the Pfalz and in Straßburg.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inform them in writing whether the deceased Anna Frenerin made a will and whether it was drawn up in due form before the authority or the court. The request comes from the siblings Balthasar and Magdalena Sraim, who, as the nearest heirs of the deceased, ask for a favor.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to a request from Feldkirch for information regarding the will of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen, Anna Zeigerin. They confirm that she had drawn up a valid will shortly before her death, in which 500 gulden were designated for the relatives from Feldkirch. They offer to be helpful in the collection of this sum.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Feldkirch

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Burgomaster and Council of Zell about a lawsuit by the citizen of Zell Michel Schrandorfer against the St. Gallen Tobias Hoffmen and Jörg Schrepfer for 20 ducats. The defendants deny the debt and refer to the fact that their goods were confiscated in Zell by the garrison without any compensation being made. St. Gallen refrains from a judgment for the time being and asks Zell to grant the St. Gallen compensation for the seized goods or to suspend the lawsuit until the situation is clarified.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Ammann and Court of Bernang to permit the payment of a Holzlin to their citizen Lorenz Appenzeller, gardener, which his deceased wife Anna Hiermaennerin left there. Appenzeller is the next natural heir as the father of the deceased child. The St. Gallen authorities ask for official support so that Appenzeller may sell and administer the property.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Ammann and Court of Bernang

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform the Landvogt of the Turgau that Jörg Trautmann, who is detained in the lordship of Schönburg ob Flachen, stated in his defense that his journeyman Mathes Herman, called Peustlin, of Blastenberg near Weildorf, had abducted Trautmann's wife. Peustlin is a great thief and had buried about 1000 gulden of stolen money in a tin pot in his house in Blastenberg. The Landvogt is requested to investigate this.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt of the lower and upper Turgau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the Pfleger, Burgomaster and Council of Mindelheim to intervene with the heirs of the Kranich family. The merchants of St. Gallen, who are involved in the inheritance, have already received a first intervention, which, however, led only to a partial payment. They ask for further support so that the heirs settle the remaining claims and the merchants of St. Gallen can continue their business in the city.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Pfleger, Burgomaster and Council of Mindelheim

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to request the Bishop of Konstanz once again for a final decision in the claim matter of the St. Gallen citizen Wolfgang Schobinger. Furthermore, they ask the St. Gallen authorities to persuade Schobinger's creditors to grant a postponement of the claims, so that he may hope for a payment from the Bishop.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The parish priest of Frauenfeld thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the communication granted and the congratulations on his new parish. He assures them in turn of good neighborhood and correspondence.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Electoral Palatine Chancery and the Councils present thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the transmitted tax of 400 gulden of Straßburg currency for the benefit of the suffering professors, church officials, as well as widows and orphans in the Principality of Zweibrücken. They promise to praise the benefaction publicly and privately and to thank God, and recommend themselves to the Council of St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The present Pfalz-Zweibrücken councillors acknowledge to the citizens of St. Gallen Peter, Hans Conrad Feltz and their brothers the handover of 400 gulden Straßburg currency. This amount was collected with the approval of the Magistrat of St. Gallen for the needy church and school servants of the Principality of Zweibrücken as well as their survivors. The councillors assure that they will distribute the funds according to need and custom.
en.recipient: Peter, Hans Conrad Feltz and brothers, citizens of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel their citizens to return Geldern that they had received through bills of exchange with the Zürcher Hans Jacob Werdmüller, Caspar Hesse and the heirs of Anton Gstaltner. The bills of exchange had been concluded before the announcement of the devaluation of money in the Empire. Zürich threatens legal steps and costs if the return does not take place.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The pastors of the Reformed congregations in Frankenthal ask the ministers of the churches of St. Gallen for a Christian tax. They describe the plight of the expelled and suffering citizens, widows and orphans in the city and hope for a charitable collection to alleviate their distress.
en.sender: Petrus Crugotus, Martinus Schramius und Jacobus Heusch
en.recipient: Ministers of the churches of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Vogt Jost Dietrich Reding of Rorschach to inquire with the tanners there whether Afra Stadlerin von Trostberg, who was taken into custody in St. Gallen, and a woman from Wolfhaggen had lost stolen linen about twelve weeks ago. They ask for information on the type of goods.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Jost Dietrich Reding von Schweitz zu Glattburg, Vogt of Rorschach

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to accompany the heirs of Hans Jakob Werdmüller, Kaspar Gossen and Anton Pestalozzi, who must appear before the court of St. Gallen on the coming Tuesday, with a letter of recommendation. They request that the citizens of St. Gallen treat the heirs amicably so that they can assert their rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to two letters from the Statthalter and Council of Wil. They report that a prisoner had confessed to having stolen two pieces of linen from the bleacher of Wil, that she had taken one of them with her, and that her husband has the other. They promise to further investigate the matter. Regarding the arrest of linen at the bleachery, laid by a citizen of Wil against the Lords Zollikofer, they request release, as the Lords Zollikofer had been notified. If Herr Hueber sues, St. Gallen will judge.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of Wil

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Jacob Bergmüller to pay the widow Elisabetha Mänzin 10 gulden and 30 kreuzer. The daughter of Mänzin had deposited the money with Bergmüller before her death and confirmed the claim. Bergmüller refuses the payment despite a demand by the Amtsbürgermeister.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Weiler ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their bailiff Ulrich Wiss, from whom stolen cloth was stolen. They request that the stolen goods, if still available, be recovered and that it be determined where and to whom the cloth was sold.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jörg Dietrich Reding, bailiff, replies to a letter concerning a woman imprisoned in St. Gallen. He reports that the local bleacher has recently had linen stolen from him on several occasions, including a piece of household cloth of about 40 ells, a piece of linen from which 30 ells of red had to be cut, as well as three further pieces of household cloth. He asks the authorities of St. Gallen to inform him whether anything can be recovered of the stolen linen or where it was given, so that the bleacher Ulrich may regain his loss.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Wil ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel the St. Gallen citizen Georg Hauer to keep his promises. Hauer had promised Mathis Hollezechtler to cover the loss of 20 gulden that the latter had suffered through Hauer. However, Hauer had brought the bale not to Wil, but to St. Gallen. Wil asks for help so that Hauer compensates the poor man.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to look in their registers how much the Mark of silver was worth in pounds, pfennig, heller or gulden 200 and 300 years ago. They ask for a non-binding piece of information, as they themselves would not have better evidence.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Landvogt of the Valley of Obertoggenburg to mediate in an inheritance dispute concerning an inheritance case in Adorf. The guardians of the son of the deceased Konrad Krennin, Johannes Spengler and Cyrill Hinderleuch, report that the deceased Hans Jakob Krennin did not exclude anyone in his testament. They ask the Landvogt to help the guardians so that their ward receives his inheritance.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schmid, Council of Schwyz, Landvogt of the Valley of Obertoggenburg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in the name of the interested parties of the Schmidesche inheritance, to set a date for an amicable settlement or a superior decision. They ask that Herr Ulin be instructed to appoint his fellow citizens with power of attorney and instruction, so that the matter can be settled quickly in these difficult times.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Mindelheim inform the creditors of the community of Anselmen that the heirs of the community had not reached an agreement as expected. They order the interested parties to appear on 21 September, in person or through authorized representatives, to reach an agreement with the creditors or to await the decision of the authorities.
en.recipient: Interested creditors of the community of Anselmen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ybbs inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the appointment of a general court day for the creditors of the deceased Ybbs citizen Georg Gschwander. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to publicly post and publish the edict, so that any claims of the citizens of St. Gallen may be taken into account.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to report to them in writing how the dispute between their countryman Ulrich Lengenacker and his wife Martha Walderin with the citizen of St. Gallen David Müller stands. The two had been expelled from St. Gallen. Appenzell wishes to know better about the further conduct of the persons.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen not to drive the creditors of their citizen Wolfgang Röbinger out of the city. Röbinger has fallen into hardship. Zürich had wanted to help him in the enforcement of a Baden judgment, but the matter is now differently situated. They ask St. Gallen to consider Röbinger out of supra-local clemency.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publish an edict concerning a scheduled court day for the creditors of the deceased citizen of Konstanz, Hans Hafner, the tanner. They ask that the edict be publicly posted according to local custom, so that no one be curtailed in their rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen send to the Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell, at their request, a verbatim copy from the St. Gallen town book. This contains the details regarding the misconduct and crimes of the Appenzell countryman Ulrich Langenegker and his wife Maria Walderin, who resided in St. Gallen for a time without permission.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Mülhausen for the quick setting of a date in the dispute over the Knaus estate. They ask that, if an amicable settlement fails, the goods of the heirs of the deceased Burgomaster Kraus be sequestered. The widow had bought goods from Mülhausen, which she had sold to a debtor. St. Gallen asks for official assistance so that the creditors are satisfied.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Mülhausen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Glarus request the Confederate envoys in Solothurn to intervene with the city of Eger for the release of the Glarus merchant Christoph Studer jun. He says that he was detained there because of a high contribution for a garrison. The Glarus request an amicable settlement of the dispute and the preservation of the Confederate privileges.
en.recipient: Envoys of the Confederate cantons in Solothurn

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to the Judge and Council of Kaschau regarding the inheritance dispute over the estate of the deceased Hans Albrecht Milch. They argue that the half-siblings (Scheuner) are to be excluded, as the full sister Verena Milch and her children are present. Furthermore, the nieces cannot inherit, as they are too far away. The city of St. Gallen asks for further communications and declares itself ready for an amicable settlement.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Judge and Council of Kaschau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to clarify and supplement the judgment in the legal dispute between the heirs of Hans Jakob Werdmüller, Caspar Hesse and Anton Pestalutz and citizens of St. Gallen. The heirs had understood the judgment to mean that, as factors, they had dropped their claim upon the oath performed, but not that their claim against the contractors had been taken away from them. They ask for an amended and increased document, which they are to hand over to a messenger.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Biberach inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have appointed a general gantmeisterische court day regarding the estate of the deceased, childless citizen Johann Waalen. They ask the St. Gallen to serve the edict on the creditors and to notify the court day.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Palatine Countess Louisa thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the support of 400 gulden for the distressed rectors, professors, and church property managers of the Gymnasium in Zweibrücken. She promises to pray for the well-being of the donors and to publicly thank them.
en.sender: Louisa, Pfalzgräfin bei Rhein, Herzogin in Bayern, Wittwe
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich complain to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that merchants of St. Gallen, with city export permits, export grain not for their own needs, but over the sea and elsewhere. This drives up prices and disrupts the proper supply. Zürich asks that the merchants be instructed to keep the grain in the country, and assures that it will deliver grain if needed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information on the current meat prices. They intend to lower the meat tax, as the butchers argue that meat is cheaper to be had in St. Gallen, Schaffhausen and other neighboring places. They ask to be informed of the prices for the pound of best, medium and worst beef and roast meat.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to examine their grain merchants under oath in order to learn their names and origin. The merchants had apologized to the citizens of Zürich for purchasing grain under the pretext of being of St. Gallen and transporting it abroad. Zürich wishes to better monitor the fraudsters at its tolls and passes.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Jacob Eberzhamer, Stattrichter zu Memmingen, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly publish the attached edict concerning the appointed court day for the creditors of the deceased citizen of Memmingen, Hans Elsner. This is done so that the citizens of St. Gallen, in particular Joachim and Lorenz Zollikofer, can assert their claims against the inheritance.
en.sender: Johann Jacob Eberzhamer, Stattrichter and Commissioner of the City Court of Memmingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Meliand asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support Herr Delaube in the purchase of powder in the city, in order to send it to Lyon for the service of the King of Frankreich. He promises to advocate for St. Gallen with the French Crown.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landammann and Council of the Äusseren Rhoden of the Land of Appenzell to detain their countryman Uli Stäffann von Hüttenwil and have him appear on 23 November at 12 o'clock in front of the Fleischbank in St. Gallen. Stäffann has violated guild regulations by bringing meat from calves and pigs into the city, and has failed to appear despite being summoned.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Äusseren Rhoden of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist the heirs of the deceased citizen of Zürich, Hans-Jakob Werdtmüller, in the collection of a bill of exchange sum of 1000 Kronen against the heirs of the St. Gallen Caspar Schlumpf and Daniel Zolicofer. The Werdtmüller heirs had deposited the money in St. Gallen but had not been able to receive the consideration in Lyon. Zürich requests superior help so that the heirs receive their money together with interest and costs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Feldkirch ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Elisabeth Wiererin in the claim for her father's share of the inheritance. They refer to her petition and ask that the heirs of the deceased German Reiner be compelled to make the due division of the inheritance and that the share of the inheritance be allowed without delay.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The princely-episcopal-constanzian officials at Reichenau inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that many citizens of the island of Reichenau have become impoverished due to the war burdens of the past years. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to publish an edict so that creditors can assert their claims.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant support to their citizen Andreas Oertli in the dispute over the inheritance of his deceased wife Susanna Wundin against Hans Jakob Kreuzen, Bernhard Miltner zu Weningen and Sebastian Bischof. They demand that the defendants appear on 27 February, otherwise a decision will be made on the claims of the plaintiff.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant sovereign aid to their countryman Hermann Jeggeren. Jeggeren has a legal dispute with the citizen of St. Gallen Jakob Ziegler. Appenzell asks that Jeggeren be satisfied with his rightful claim, including the costs and damages suffered, so that he may obtain his right without further expense.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Palatine Countess Louise thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the support of the suffering professors, church and school servants, as well as survivors from the Principality of Zweibrücken. She mentions that the citizens of St. Gallen would have transferred 400 Reichstaler to her councillors residing in Straßburg. She assures that her son, Duke Friedrich, will not forget this kindness, and commends the citizens of St. Gallen to divine care.
en.sender: Louise, Palatine Countess by the Rhine, Duchess in Bayern, widow
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to negotiate with their citizen David Müller so that he releases the Lindau citizen Johann Andre Hundt von Dettmeir from the lawsuit. This concerns a judgment and an execution in the process of the departed Lindauer Thomas Wellin. Lindau offers help and requests neighborly consideration.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Wilhelm Otto Graf zu Ysenburg und Büdingen reminds the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of the plundering of his county by imperial soldiers in 1634 and his expulsion by Landgrave Georg von Hessen. As he is in great distress in Frankfurt and peace in Regensburg is not in sight, he asks for a loan against strong obligation, in order to be able to endure his exile until his return to his land.
en.sender: Wilhelm Otto Graf zu Ysenburg und Büdingen
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Georg von Ysenburg asks St. Gallen for a credit, as he was plundered by imperial soldiery after the defeat of the Protestant Imperial Estates in 1634 and driven out by Landgrave Georg von Hessen-Darmstadt. He hopes for a speedy restitution but expects no peace from the Imperial Diet in Regensburg. He promises a secure obligation and gratitude.
en.recipient: St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Joachim Keller, bailiff, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help his subject Katharina Clattnerin to become the heir of her deceased brother Konrad Clattner. He says that the latter, about 15 years ago, as a soldier, placed his assets under the administration of a bailiff. Since Konrad is presumably dead, Katharina asks for support in asserting her inheritance rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel their citizen Jacob Locher Jung to pay an open claim of 45 gulden and 13 batzen to the Basel messenger Jacob Hardman. Hardman had agreed in Schaffhausen to settle the amount within eight days, which has not yet happened. Schaffhausen threatens legal steps otherwise.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Council envoys of the Confederation to Baden to intervene with the French Queen Mother and Cardinal Richelieu on behalf of the Confederate merchants. These are said to have been taxed again by the customs officials in Valence, despite an Arret issued in 1636 that confirmed their duty-free status. The envoys are to present the complaints to the French envoy de Melian and enforce the observance of the Arret.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Council envoys of the Confederation to Baden

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Landvogt Michael Schorno in Turgau to support the wife Katharina Glarerin of Nieder Glattberg in the confirmation of her last will and testament. Since the matter falls under the jurisdiction of the Landvogt, the St. Gallen authorities request an authoritative confirmation or a document regarding the Landvogt's consent, so that the city's ratification has full legal force.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Michael Schorno, Landvogt in Turgau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to restrain their citizen David Müller to pay the outstanding debt to their relative Hans Andre Finckh of Newstein. They refer to a previous intercession and ask for the conclusion of the legal dispute to avoid further trouble.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to award their citizen Johann Schmidt his inheritance from the estate of his deceased wife Sibilla Dorothea Bornedrin. The inheritance claims are said to be based on a testament and recognized by St. Gallen. The inheritance is in the hands of the St. Gallen citizen Tobias Zollikofer. Konstanz asks that Schmidt be granted his due share.
en.sender: Captain, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The parish priests Martinus Februarius, Petrus Crugot and Jacob Heusch thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on behalf of the community of Frankenthal for the transfer of 200 gulden (125 Reichsthaler) by the Basel rector Daniel Tossan. The money serves to help the citizenry, which is afflicted by war, inflation and hunger. They wish St. Gallen peace and health.
en.sender: Martinus Februarius, Petrus Crugot und Jacob Heusch
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan of 5000 to 6000 gulden, as the city is in great distress due to the quartering of soldiers and their demands for payment. They offer the city's assets as well as the personal obligations of Burgomasters Joachim Scherrer and Nicolaus von Düring as security. Fellow citizen Johann Stadler is authorized to negotiate the sum and the interest. In a postscript, Holz is requested.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg ask the St. Gallen Burgomaster Sebastian Schobinger to use his influence with the Council and citizens of the city of St. Gallen for a loan, as the city is in great distress. They have already sent the Syndic Maximilian Müller and Johann Müller to St. Gallen for this purpose. They promise to repay this.
en.recipient: Sebastian Schobinger

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg refer to their earlier letters regarding the quartering of troops and the raising of a loan. They ask St. Gallen to give full faith to their Syndicus Maximilian Müller and Johann Maerl and to grant them a loan of 1000 florins against mortgage and bond in their time of need. They promise repayment with interest and counter-service.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Schultheiss and Council of Bern to instruct their citizen Georg Tribeler to leave the citizens of St. Gallen in peace. Should Tribeler nevertheless cause damage, Bern may instruct him to assert the damage before the St. Gallen authority. St. Gallen will protect the citizens according to the Confederation treaties and grant them justice.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Bern

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Reutlingen thank St. Gallen for the willingness to grant a loan of 6000 gulden. In order to keep the matter secret, they have communicated a refusal to the Rittmeister and ask St. Gallen to issue a corresponding letter. They request that the approved sum be transferred within two to three days by bill of exchange at their expense. The mortgage is to be drawn up at the discretion of the creditors. The remaining amount is to remain provisionally with St. Gallen. Johann Morell has agreed to raise 1000 gulden himself, for which he receives a certificate.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Statthalter and Council of Konstanz not to withhold the tolls paid by the citizens of St. Gallen in Zell and to allow the annual revenues to be paid freely. They refer to the good neighborly relationship and the existing inheritance agreement. Furthermore, they wish a peaceful new year.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Statthalter and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Landvogt Michael Schorno to serve a citation on the St. Gallen citizen Ulrich Krämer, as the latter is resisting a judgment of the Zollikofferische Gesellschaft. They urge Schorno to compel Krämer to obedience and to deprive him of his citizenship if he does not submit. St. Gallen rejects Krämer's request for help.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Michael Schorno, Landvogt in Ober- and Untertoggenburg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to revise a submitted draft of an interest or debt description and to return it for the execution of the obligation. Citing pressing soldier costs, they demand 100 gulden and ask that this sum be handed over to their citizen Peter Kessler against a receipt. They consider the sum received and acknowledge it.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the French ambassador to grant them the same favor as other cantons in the payment of outstanding pensions by the Confederation. They refer to the fact that they have hitherto been forgotten. The St. Gallen envoy Sebastiano Zollikofer will report to the ambassador to clarify the payment.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Herr von Meliand, ambassador of the King of Frankreich in the Confederation

en.regest: The Syndics, the Council and the Republic of Genf recommend to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the Herr von Sebriz, who is on his way into their territory. They praise his abilities in fortification and his zeal for the public good. Genf has been greatly satisfied with his services to date and expects that he will continue to render useful services in the future.
en.sender: Syndics, Conseil de la ville et République de Genève
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Wilhelm Otto Graf zu Isenburg und Büdingen asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen again for a loan against obligation. He justifies this with his financial distress and the approaching winter season, as he has no more means for himself and his family. He refers to an earlier letter of 18 February and hopes for a prompt answer.
en.sender: Wilhelm Otto Graf zu Isenburg und Büdingen
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz reply to a letter from St. Gallen regarding the meat tax. They announce that they had previously sold beef and veal at 6 kreuzer and the best mutton at 5 kreuzer per pound. Their meat assessors have been instructed to assess beef and cow meat, depending on quality, down to 4 kreuzer and below.
en.sender: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich recommend to the Council of St. Gallen the French engineer de Serres, who has made himself available to the Evangelical cantons. They ask for the St. Gallen opinion to be communicated, so that a conference can be held to discuss his employment and the conditions.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Melchior Laeger, Landvogt of Werdenberg and Wartau, for a copy of the confession of a recently executed criminal. The prisoner Hans Heinzer of Unterwalden, who has six fingers on one hand, is suspected of being his accomplice. The St. Gallen authorities request a description of the complicity in order to clarify the case.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Melchior Laeger, Council of Glarus and Landvogt of the County of Werdenberg and the Lordship of Wartau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Landvogt Hans Bernhard Schmidt in Baden for a copy of the confession and the description of the companions of the thief executed in Baden. They have captured Hans Liegener, who comes from the Unterwalden area, who among other things has six fingers and toes on each hand and each foot. They want to examine whether he is in connection with the executed man or his accomplices.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Hans Bernhard Schmidt, Landvogt of the County of Baden

en.regest: Johann Joachim Haller, bailiff of the County of Eglofs, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen again for support for Moritz Angermann and his wife Katharina Blattnerin. It concerns the inheritance question of Katharina's deceased brother Conrad Blattner. Haller points out that Conrad has not been heard from for 19 years, and asks that the inheritance be awarded to Angermann against a deduction of 10 percent, so that he can settle his debts and provide for his children.
en.sender: Johann Joachim Haller, bailiff of the County of Eglofs
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report that they have agreed on a meat tax together with Ravensburg, Wangen, Isny, Leutkirch, and Bregenz. The butchers of Lindau complain about high cattle prices and refer to the higher meat tax in St. Gallen. Lindau asks St. Gallen for information on the current prices for ox, cow, and veal, as well as for notification of how the city intends to proceed in the future.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Stadtmann and Council of Altstätten inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the Rheintal estates will begin with Weingarten on 14 September. According to the latest Baden recess, the Rheintal estates are to negotiate with the city of St. Gallen regarding the wine run on the first wine day. The deputies of the estates will arrive in St. Gallen on Wednesday evening and negotiate on Thursday. Altstätten asks for acknowledgment so that the Rheintal estates are not treated unjustly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the communication of the meat prices. They inform about a man detained in St. Gallen, who had two linen cloths dyed in Appenzell. The man is said to be from Unterwalden and to have bought the cloth in Rorschach. The Appenzellers ask for further information.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank the Abbenzell people for their help in the arrest of a prisoner. He confesses to having broken open the alms box in the church of Zurzach with an accomplice. The St. Gallen authorities ask for an investigation into whether the robbery actually took place. In a postscript, they also ask for clarification on whether an apothecary named Jacob Herwartten in Abbenzell had handed over linen for dyeing.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: The people of Abbenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Rorschach to intervene amicably with the Thurgau millers, who concern themselves with the grain purchase and export. They are to urge the millers to agree to the higher prices or to settle with Lorenz Reut, until the prices for the remaining shots are known.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Rorschach

en.regest: The Vitzthumb of Lindau informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of an imperial decree of 12 August, which confirms an extraordinary war surcharge for the Swabian garrison in Lindau. He asks the St. Gallen citizens to instruct their merchants and relatives to pay this fee. He assures them that this surcharge is not directed against the eternal hereditary relationship between Österreich and the Confederates, and further offers friendship and support in trade.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jakob Hans Gerhart, Pfand of the Council of Breisach and Landvogt there, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, at their request of 7 September, he has ascertained the names of the villains executed in Baden and Walshut. He names, among others, Hans Künz, the Schössbubhauser, and Caspar Schmalzer, who had committed thefts together. He encloses a list of the names.
en.sender: Jakob Hans Gerhart, Pfand of the Council of Breisach and Landvogt there
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Meliand from Solothurn replies to a letter from the citizens of St. Gallen, concerning their pension. He assures them that he will act benevolently in all matters concerning their interest and will soon give them the opportunity to recognize his wish to contribute to their satisfaction. He asks Herr Solicoffre, their fellow citizen, who had reported to him on their behalf, to communicate this to them in more detail.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to a petition by Thomas Ungnemen, a subject of Eglosheim. They grant him, in addition to the 100 florins already approved, a further 50 florins from the estate of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Konrad Blatter, provided that he secures a surety from a citizen of St. Gallen. Ungnemen says that he was pleased with the approval and now wishes to wait and see.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Johann Joachim Keller, Council member and toll collector of Eglosheim

en.regest: The Pflegere, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to present Mathes Kenden, who is staying there, with the declaration of the Augsburg citizen Helena Stamlerin. They ask that Kenden be ordered by the authority to submit a written report by 14 November, and request feedback on the delivery that has taken place.
en.sender: Pflegere, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Administrators of the Landshauptmannschaft, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz, dated 6 October 1636, which concerns the meat tax. They send a copy of their ordinance of 25 August 1637, which came into force on 5 September. They point out that the butchers adhere to the set tax, but the meat remains free of charge. The heavy forty-lot pound is used for the weight.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Administrators of the Landshauptmannschaft, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: Hektor Zollikofer informs that the University of Basel has complained of medical negligence on his part in the Tanner legal case, as he had not called a barber-surgeon. He rejects the accusation, as the boy had no visible injuries and he had done his best. He asks the recipient to ensure that the treating doctors are heard by the Imperial Councillors, and threatens otherwise to defend himself before the Basel Faculty.
en.recipient: Junker and Herr (unknown)

en.regest: Johann Joachim Haller, guardian of the heirs of the deceased Archduke Leopold, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hand over to the young man Zaigeren, a subject, the inheritance in St. Gallen that was awarded to him. He offers Georg Langen, Schultheiss of the lower part of the County of Eglofs, as security, who guarantees the return of the inheritance. Haller asks for a written confirmation of the security.
en.sender: Johann Joachim Haller, guardian, bailiff and toll collector of the County of Eglofs
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Konstanz informs St. Gallen that Lindau and Wangen have agreed on a fixed meat tariff, and asks to join. Beforehand, Konstanz wants to know how high ox, beef, veal, and goat meat are taxed and weighed in St. Gallen, and asks for a detailed report.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask N. Lerchener, Council and bailiff of Mündelheim, to decide without delay on the Kranich inheritance case of Gundelfingen, which was referred to the merchants of St. Gallen, so that they may be paid. They also request the settlement of the Schmid debt case, in which the heirs of Caspar Schlumpf and the widow of Jacob Haneß are interested.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: N. Lerchener, Council and bailiff of Mündelheim

en.regest: The Councilors of the Count Palatine of Zweibrücken, who are in exile in Straßburg, ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a compassionate monetary contribution. They justify this with the high cost of living and the burdens of the garrison in Zweibrücken, which they can no longer bear. They ask for the amount to be transferred by bill of exchange to the citizen of Straßburg, Peter Tripouet.
en.sender: Councilors of the Count Palatine of Zweibrücken in exile
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Pflege, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to cause Mathäus Kremen, living in St. Gallen, on the order of their citizen Sebastian Hozzen, to declare in writing by Easter whether he accepts the assets assigned to him in the will of the deceased Agatha Martin. The declaration is to be sent back to Augsburg.
en.sender: Pflege, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Reinhardt Erpff, former rector of the Palatine schools at Sulz, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a position at the local Gymnasium. He justifies this with his status as a widower and the death of several children. He offers himself as a private or extraordinary teacher and promises to run the Gymnasium with the same diligence as he previously ran the Palatine schools.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Regent of Marseille ask the Council of St. Gallen to arrest the bankrupt Ulrich Krom, who lives in St. Gallen, and to confiscate his goods. Krom has left debts of 150'000 piastres in Egypt, which has caused damage of over 500'000 francs to the French merchants in Alexandria. The French have been forced to take up 200'000 francs to satisfy the Turkish creditors. Marseille promises to support St. Gallen in similar cases.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Regent of the city of Marseille
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to two letters from the Augsburg authorities regarding their citizen Mathes Henden, who is in service in St. Gallen. They state that a matter has already been settled and no further process is necessary. Regarding the inheritance matter, Henden has submitted his opinion and his counter-report in writing, which is enclosed. They ask that Henden be spared from further harassment.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Guardians, Burgomasters and Council of Augsburg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen remind the Landammann and Council of the Äusseren Rhoden of the Land of Appenzell of a letter of 17 November concerning the St. Gallen citizen Anna Zollerin. Since the Appenzeller Michel Hämerler has not answered for himself before St. Gallen, he is summoned for 4 January 1638 at 8 o'clock in the morning before the St. Gallen town hall. The Appenzeller authorities are requested to cause Hämerler to appear and answer for himself.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Äusseren Rhoden of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: Landvogt, Landschreiber and Council of the lordships of Rötteln and Sausenberg ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help Steffan Stein of Eichholz. Stein's wife, the widow of the St. Gallen citizen Heinrich Städtin, is to be involved in the inheritance of the deceased sisters Barbara and Judith Städtin as guardian of her stepdaughter Ursula. The authorities of St. Gallen are to offer Stein their hand so that he is admitted to the inheritance as marital guardian.
en.sender: Landvogt, Landschreiber and Council of the lordships of Rötteln and Sausenberg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of the Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell reply to a letter of 14 December 1637. Their countryman Michael Küster has admitted to having committed fornication with the woman of St. Gallen Anna Zydlerin and wants to pay the fine. Regarding the marriage, they refer to the town law of St. Gallen, which forbids foreigners from marrying without 200 gulden in assets, as well as to the land law of Appenzell. Küster disputes the marriage; Zydlerin has already sought justice in Appenzell, which is why the matter is to be discussed there.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell return to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the previously borrowed pulley blocks and ropes with which the new bells were hoisted into the Turm. They thank them for the friendly neighborly assistance and offer their own support in all cases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Feldkirch inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they must set a court day for the creditors of the deceased Feldkirch Verburgert Johann Whipfer on 25 November. They request the St. Gallen authorities to publish an edict so that no one can plead ignorance, in case St. Gallen Verburgerts have claims on Whipfer's estate.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the cities of Augsburg, Ulm and Konstanz to send their apothecary regulations and price lists, as they wish to moderate their own regulation due to prices being too high. They also ask for information on whether the apothecaries and journeymen in the aforementioned cities are sworn to the regulation.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Pfleger, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg; Burgomaster and Council of Ulm; Verwalter der Hauptmannschaft, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from Lindau of 12 January 1638 concerning the Lindau protégé Hans Andreas Senft. The St. Gallen citizen David Müller had complained that Senft had not recognized his right to the Hof Petto. St. Gallen had instructed Müller to reach an agreement with Senft within 14 days, so that both cities would not be further troubled.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm reply to a letter of the 10th of the month, in which St. Gallen had requested the apothecary ordinance and the drug price for the renewal of their own ordinance. Ulm transmits the requested documents and points out that apothecary journeymen and deputies in Ulm must swear an oath to the ordinance before the Deputies.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz reply to a letter of the 10th of the month, in which St. Gallen had requested the Apothecaries' Ordinance and the oath-taking of the apothecaries and journeymen. Konstanz informs that the physicians still had to revise the ordinance and the price list of the medicines. As soon as this had been done, they would send the copy of the ordinance and the requested report in a neighborly manner.
en.sender: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell send the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen a deer, which their game warden shot last Saturday, as thanks for favors shown. They ask that the gift be accepted in friendly neighborhood and consumed during the Carnival season.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johanna, Elisabeth and Maria Juliana Pletscherin ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for help. They report that their parents have died and that the fatherland has been severely damaged by the war, so that they no longer have any support. They beg the city to alleviate their misery and promise gratitude.
en.sender: Johanna, Elisabeth and Maria Juliana Pletscherin
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Pflegere, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg reply to a letter of 10 January 1600, in which St. Gallen had asked for the value of the medicinal drugs in the apothecary ordinance and for the oaths of the apothecaries and their journeymen. Augsburg sends the printed apothecary ordinance, the tariff of the simple and compound medicinal drugs with the added value, and a copy of the oaths.
en.sender: Pflegere, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johanna Christina und Elisabeth Maria Juliana Scherrin ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for help. They report that they have fallen into a distressed state through the death of their parents and lost their property through the war. They are compelled to ask for support again and promise to repay this with prayers.
en.sender: Johanna Christina und Elisabeth Maria Juliana Scherrin
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator, Captain, Statthalter, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz hand over to the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen the tariff of the transmitted medicines as well as the pharmacy regulations and the oath for apothecaries and journeymen. They point out that in some Imperial cities the journeymen also have to swear a bodily oath. They ask for forgiveness that they could not comply with the request for a messenger by next Saturday.
en.sender: Administrator, Captain, Statthalter, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Philipp Reinhard Graf zu Solms thanks the Burgomaster and Council of the free city of St. Gallen for the generous tax assistance in favor of the expelled pastors of the Amt Hohendolln. He asks God for protection against similar misfortunes and for peace for the fatherland, so that one may be able to help other communities in the future. He offers his services.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the free city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Wilhelm Freiherr zu Seens thanks the Burgomaster and Council of the Free City of St. Gallen for taking over the support of his parishioners, as he can no longer bear this due to the war. He promises to show them his friendship in the future and to make himself useful to them within his means.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the Free City of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the Ausserrhoden of the Land of Appenzell request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to release their countryman Michel Feuster, who is imprisoned because of a marital promise with a citizen of St. Gallen. They refer to the fact that in cases of offenses against morality only a fine should be demanded and that in cases of marital promises the plaintiff must prove the residence of the defendant.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Ausserrhoden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Heinrich Lochmann reports to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the receipt of their letter. He reports on the imprisonment of a man and a woman, the flight of an executed man and his statements about a large, dangerous gang of robbers that roams the country. He recommends strengthening the guards, as the gang is also active at night.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report that the Lindau guardian Hans Ulrich Huenoß von der Anewil is satisfied with the settlement by David Müller. Since Müller does not agree, Lindau asks St. Gallen to order Müller to make a reasonable will or to pay the outstanding interest. Lindau wishes to try to persuade Huenoß to accept the dwelling for the capital, in order to bring peace to all parties.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen refer to their citizen David Müller, who has not provided satisfaction to his godson Junker Andrea Hünlin von Lauffenegg, and ask Lindau for information on the recently decided coin reductions and the approved coin denominations, so that they can regulate circulation accordingly.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a voluntary monetary donation for the construction of a church on the lower Hirschberg. They justify this with the necessity of a divine service for the subjects there and promise to mention donors by name and to advocate for St. Gallen.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg not to apply the newly introduced duties on sold and passing goods to the merchants of St. Gallen. They refer to the duty exemptions that have existed between the two cities since time immemorial and request that the merchants of St. Gallen continue to be exempted from these levies.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg

en.regest: Michael Schorno, Landvogt in Ober- und Nidertoggenburg, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to stop the process of the guild master Joachim von Wyler against the heirs of the Ammann inheritance in Arbon. He refers to a previous settlement and the Thurgau inheritance law, which excludes the claim. Schorno warns against unnecessary costs and threatens to represent the matter before the Judikatur if the St. Gallen side does not yield.
en.sender: Michael Schorno, Landvogt in Ober- und Nidertoggenburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Palatine Louisa asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in view of the distress in the Principality of Zweibrücken caused by the war, to collect a Christian collection for the subjects there, church and school services, as well as their widows and orphans. She requests that the collected amounts be remitted through Peter Triponetten in Straßburg, and promises a just distribution of the gifts.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The letter contains only the salutation to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen. The content is missing.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Landammann and Council of Uri to listen friendly to their envoys Georg Schindler and Hans Anton Zili. These are to negotiate over the complaints of the St. Gallen citizens regarding the wine run of the Rheintaler and over the sale of properties. St. Gallen asks Uri to advocate for the St. Gallen citizens and to help that the neighborhood becomes trustworthy again.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Uri

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their countryman Hans Surer, who eight years ago sold two cattle to the St. Gallen butcher Hans Langlis but has received no payment to this day. They request official support so that Surer may receive his rightful balance without further effort.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report that they had opened and confiscated a package of money addressed to the St. Gallen Marx Zollikoffer. They suspect that the shipment originates from the Basel merchants Passavant, Socin and Rasser and violates the coin regulations. They request St. Gallen to examine the trade books of the aforementioned Basel merchants, to obtain the corresponding letters and to question Zollikoffer under oath as to where the gold comes from.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Franz Römer in Frankfurt to pay out 60 Reichstaler by bill of exchange to the three daughters of the deceased Count Albrecht von Hanau, Johanna, Elisabetha and Maria Juliana. The amount is intended as a Christian contribution for the exiles. The payment is to be made upon presentation of a receipt.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Franz Römer of Frankfurt

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Secret Council of the city of Kempten request the Burgomaster and Secret Council of the city of St. Gallen to interrogate the butcher's servant Endres Wegenstiel, who is supposed to be staying in St. Gallen. Wegenstiel is to testify under oath about an incident in which the Junker zum Weyer is supposed to have gone at night into the chamber of the wife of the Kempten citizen Sebastian Klüftinger. Kempten requests the transmission of the testimony.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Secret Council of the city of Kempten
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Secret Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Franz Römer asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant an annual contribution to the daughters of the deceased Count Albrecht von Hanau, as Zürich already does. He also requests support for two persons exiled in Meisenheim, the jurist Georg Pastor and the widow Jutta Maria von Castilion, who are not included in the official list of pastors and teachers from Zweibrücken, Simmern and Kreuznach to be supported. He asks that the contributions be sent to his brother-in-law Tossano via Basel.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Basel ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Georg Beyer, the bookseller, to pay the outstanding amount of 266 gulden and 1 schilling to the Basel citizen Ludwig König, the bookseller. König has already spent a lot of money on the claim. Basel asks for a quick payment so that König may be left without complaint.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hercules von Raitenau informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the widowed Archduchess Claudia zu Österreich has granted him the vacant bailiwick of Bregenz and Hohenegg. He asks the citizens of St. Gallen to be present in Bregenz on the morning of 6. July to accompany him during the immatriculation by the Commissioner Johann Georg von Königsegg and to adorn the act.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Chur declare to St. Gallen that the reduction of the tenths to nine kreuzer was not due to the inferiority of the coin, but due to the circulation of poorer coins in Tirol and Lindau. They offer to send their mint master to check the assay, and ask St. Gallen to continue to let the Chur coins circulate.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the coppersmith Georg Poern, who is detained in Lindau. He has admitted to having stolen four Reichstaler from the citizen of St. Gallen Hans Heinrich Bierkhamer. Furthermore, he has, together with an apprentice, stolen two cows from an unknown young gentleman and sold them in Wang. Lindau asks St. Gallen to conduct further investigations and to communicate the results.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen confirm to the widowed Palatine Countess on the Rhine, Louise, that, at her request, they have decreed a contribution of 300 gulden for the needy political, ecclesiastical, and school servants as well as their widows and orphans in the Duchy of Zweibrücken. The money is to be collected by Peter Crisonetten in Straßburg and distributed at their discretion, with the poorest, in particular ecclesiastical and school servants, receiving the largest share. The St. Gallen authorities ask for a report on the receipt and distribution.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Louisa, widowed Palatine Countess on the Rhine

en.regest: The Parliament at Dole apologises to the Confederates for the delayed transmission of the usual gratitude, as the war with Frankreich and the occupation of the passes had prevented this. It asks for renewed expressions of friendship, for military help to suppress the Franzosen, and for free passage for troops from Mailand. The envoy D'Acoste will explain this in more detail.
en.sender: Vice-President, Council and Commanders of the Parliament at Dole
en.recipient: The thirteen cantons of the Confederation

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen apologize to Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg for not being able to fulfill their request for a loan for the four evangelical cities. They justify this with the high costs of defense, the war in the vicinity, and the interruption of trade. They ask that this be considered excusable and offer their services for the future.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Radolfzell ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizens Conrad Hoffmann and Hans Georg Spengler to pay the Radolfzell butcher Michael Schorndorfer the outstanding 20 ducats plus costs and damages. The debtors had delayed the payment despite earlier promises, which weighed heavily on Schorndorfer in the current crisis.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The parishes of the Vorderen Grafschaft Sponheim thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the support of one hundred gulden, which they received during their flight from the Croats. They ask that the thanks be taken to heart, and wish the city peace, prosperity, and protection from misfortune.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for further patience regarding the repayment of a capital of 2000 gulden borrowed in 1626, together with interest. They justify their inability to pay with the burdens of war and promise to begin paying the outstanding pensions as soon as possible.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau answer the inquiry from St. Gallen regarding the price of meat. They send their current meat prices, which correspond to those of the neighboring cities, with the exception of a surcharge for veal due to shortage. The butchers must also pay a surcharge of two pfennig per pound of meat. Lindau expects no changes and asks St. Gallen to communicate the prices there.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Othon Count von Waldburg to return the stolen horse (a white grey) of their citizen and Nuremberg envoy Lorenz Rausch, who was ambushed and robbed by about twenty riders near Waldsee on his return journey from Courland. They ask for quick help and promise to serve the Count in similar cases.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Othon Count von Waldburg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter from St. Gallen regarding the price of meat. They state that their butchers had sold mutton at six kreuzer, as they had adopted the St. Gallen price. Lindau intends to maintain the price for the time being and asks St. Gallen to inform them how the price is handled there and what orders were issued.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Elisabeth Gräfin zu Hanau and Maria Juliana Freiin zu Hanau thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the tax assistance granted. They ask for God's blessing for the city and its rulers, recommend themselves to the steadfast kindness of the St. Gallen, and promise to repay the favor through intercessions.
en.sender: Elisabeth Gräfin zu Hanau and Maria Juliana Freiin zu Hanau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to an inquiry from the city of Lindau regarding the sale of meat. They communicate that they have instructed the butchers to sell the best meat at 6 kreuzer and the lesser meat at 5 kreuzer. Oxen that are not suitable for valuation are to be slaughtered according to their lower value. The city of Lindau is requested to observe this order.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Lindau

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur confirm the receipt of a letter from St. Gallen and send them the applicable meat prices as well as the regulations for butchers and poulterers. They declare themselves willing to serve St. Gallen in similar matters as neighbors.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Wangen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish an edict concerning a court day appointed for the creditors of the estate of the deceased citizen of Wangen, Mathes Vögelein. This is done so that no one is disadvantaged through ignorance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen reply to a letter of 19 July. They recall a loan for the city and the hospital of St. Gallen. Because of the war burdens and the siege, they cannot settle the debt immediately. They ask for a postponement until the next St. Martin's Day. By then, they intend, since viticulture is recovering, to pay the interest in money or wine.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz reply to the demand of St. Gallen for interest on a capital of 3000 florins lent in 1632. They point out that the interest for 1633 and 1634 has already been paid, and ask for a postponement of the repayment of the capital by one year due to high expenses. In a postscript, they communicate the current meat price.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Otto Erbtuchse, Freiherr zu Fridburg, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the citizen of St. Gallen, Lorenz Ruch, was attacked by riders on his return journey from Konstanz at Waldsee and robbed of his horse. He assures them that he does not tolerate such attacks and that he will return everything brought to his hands free of charge.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report that they were informed by Wangen and Isny that cattle at the upcoming markets would presumably be worth less and that the price of meat could therefore be lowered. They ask St. Gallen to communicate whether and what changes are planned there, in order to act accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information on the local custom in the butchers' trade. It concerns a dispute between the seller Victor Prüeller and the buyer Lorenz Labhart over an ox that died on the way into the city after the purchase. Prüeller claims that the animal had been healthy, Labhart appeals to the custom that the seller must deliver the livestock healthy into the stable. The parties ask for a report on the St. Gallen practice.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the citizens of Schaffhausen Bartholome Peyer and Caspar Degenfelder have renounced their property. They have set a final court day for the creditors on 29 October. They ask the authorities of St. Gallen to publish the attached edict in St. Gallen, so that no one can plead ignorance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report to the Landvogt in the upper and lower Rhyntal that Johann Jürgen Lienhart and Erhard Zollicoffer, who are citizens of St. Gallen, were forced by the ruling cantons to hand over their property on the Buchberg to Bartholomäus Dietzen and Ulrich Haller, despite letters of exemption. Since the property was purchased and exempted years ago, the Zürichers ask the Landvogt to help the Zollicoffers to possess their property in peace and to lift the arrest.
en.recipient: Landvogt in the upper and lower Rhyntal

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the complaints of the citizens of St. Gallen Georg Leonhart and Erasmus Zollikofer in the Rintal. They have informed the Landvogt in the Rintal as well as the city of Luzern about the incidents and ask St. Gallen to forward the letter to the Landvogt. They hope that the citizens of St. Gallen will remain unharmed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post an edict regarding the appointed general court day for the estate of the deceased citizen of Lindau, Hans Anderer Döller. They wish that the citizens of St. Gallen, who may have claims on the estate, also learn of this and be able to assert their rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: King Ludwig of Frankreich informs the Confederation of the birth of a son and assures that the Dauphin, when he is grown up, will bear special affection for the Republic and Nation. He refers to his envoy Meliand, who will provide further details, and asks for trust in his statements.
en.sender: Ludwig, King of Frankreich and Navarra
en.recipient: Common Confederation

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich communicate to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen a copy of a letter from the French King to the Confederates, which the French envoy Melliand had delivered to them. They ask for St. Gallen's advisory response.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they are sending them copies of letters addressed to the papal Nuncio in Luzern as well as to the Governor and Inquisitor in Mailand, in connection with the Baden Diet. These documents concern the trade of the Protestants with the Duchy of Mailand. Since St. Gallen is also involved in the trade transactions there, the documents are handed over for their information.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The church and school ministers of Zürich reply to the rejection of their intercession in the matter of Sabina and her husband Kunz. They defend their request by referring to documents from Nürnberg and St. Gallen as well as to the mercy of Christ.
