They reject the accusation of impudence and ask the St. Gallen authorities not to cast out the guilty without mercy, but to receive those who are penitent.
en.sender: Ministers of the Church and School of Zürich
en.recipient: Superiors and Ministers of the Church of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich recommend to the Council of St. Gallen the citizen of St. Gallen Hans Jakob Kunken and his wife. They ask for their readmission to citizenship, as they are being pressed in a matter that also concerns the church and school authorities. Kunken shall have incurred no guilt in a previous incident, and his wife shall have been in ignorance. Zürich asks for mercy and promises reciprocity.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Count Kaspar zu Hohenems forwards a supplication of the Jews residing in his County and Lordship of Schellenberg to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen. The Jews ask for permission to continue trading in cloths in St. Gallen, as they have been denied the pass. The Count describes the request as not unreasonable and asks the city, in a neighborly manner, to allow the Jews to trade.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich invite St. Gallen to a meeting on 24 October 1638 in Baden. It concerns the improvement of the coinage and a petition by a Burgundian envoy for the restoration of neutrality. Zürich asks St. Gallen to appear with empowered envoys. Furthermore, Zürich reminds St. Gallen of an earlier letter concerning Hans Jakob Kunz and his wife Sabina Schlumpf and asks for a prompt answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Steinach request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to take into custody Anna Maria Furtenbächin, widow of the deceased soldier Hans Friedrich Weinögler, who is sojourning in the city. She has separated herself with the movable property and debt books of her deceased brother-in-law Jacob Rastler. Steinach asks that she, together with the documents, be handed over immediately.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Caspar Rull, saddler, to obtain his share of the inheritance of his deceased aunt Katharina Rutschhuserin. Rull is the heir as the next relative in the second degree. The city of Stein recommends him and asks for superior support.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz. Anna Maria Furtenbachin von Leutkirch, who is in service in St. Gallen, says that she did not rely on the arrest made there, as she knew nothing of it, and handed over the money paid to her. St. Gallen has instructed her to present herself in Konstanz within the next quarter-term with the bonds and to give an answer.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: Five parish priests originating from the Principality of Zweibrücken thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a donation of 500 gulden to the churches and schools there. The funds were delivered by the envoys Johann Werner and Daniel Toussón. The parish priests pray for the welfare of the citizens of St. Gallen and promise to praise the benefaction in their parishes.
en.sender: Adolphus Langhans, Johann Nicolas Diepurgerus, Johann Wilhelm Rauschius, Johannes Christianus Neuhardus and Wilhelm Dessloch
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg reply to a complaint by St. Gallen regarding a surcharge of one-third of a percent on sold goods. They explain that this surcharge was introduced out of wartime necessity and is to be paid only by citizens of the city. Foreign sellers may add it to the purchase price. The existing duty-free status remains in effect.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish an edict concerning the appointed court day for the creditors of the deceased citizen of Konstanz, Georg Weigels, so that no one is disadvantaged through ignorance.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen confirm the receipt of a letter from Konstanz, which concerns the price of meat and the prices for butchers, lard, and candles. They communicate that they have set the prices for beef and roast meat, lard, and candles for their butchers, and present these in the attachment. They ask for mutual neighborly assistance.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz inquire of the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen whether they have accepted the resolution passed at the Diet in Baden regarding the Schid coins and have withdrawn the coins. They refer to the agreement of 1592, according to which no authority should make changes to the coins without the others, and ask for a prompt answer.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request information from the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, as their butchers are demanding an increase in the meat tax. They ask whether beef in St. Gallen is actually assessed at a higher rate than in Konstanz, and request notification of the current prices for beef and veal as well as for Centner of Vnschlitt and Liechter.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Palatine Louisa thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the taxes raised by the Confederation to support the co-religionists driven out of the Principality of Zweibrücken. She confirms the receipt of 500 gulden, reports on the distribution of the funds to political and ecclesiastical servants as well as house poor, and asks for prayers for the welfare of the donors.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich confirm the receipt of a letter from St. Gallen in favor of the widow Elisabeth Zöllikhoferin. They declare themselves ready to negotiate the dispute with the heirs of the deceased Melchior Mayer on the already determined court day. They promise the citizen of St. Gallen the best possible official help and support.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the city of Nürnberg dated 14 June. They reject Nürnberg's concerns regarding the new surcharge of one third per hundred and refer to the duty-free status existing between the two cities since 1387. They ask Nürnberg not to revoke the duty-free status, as this serves the trade of both cities and fosters the existing friendship.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Nürnberg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Landvogt of Frauenfeld to mediate in a dispute between the subject communities of Küttigen and Gitlen over grazing rights. They request him to take the inspection himself and to amicably reconcile the parties or to support the judgment of the bailiff of Bürglen, so that the neighborhood is restored.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt of Frauenfeld

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the heirs of Captain Ludwig Ziegler in an inheritance matter. The deceased Elisabetha Schlumpf had pledged herself to the St. Gallen hospital shortly before her death. However, the Ziegler granddaughters claim a part of the estate, as the grandmother had provided for them insufficiently. Schaffhausen appoints Captain Hans Jörg von Mandach as envoy to achieve an amicable settlement.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg answer a letter from St. Gallen of 20 December of the previous year. They justify the surcharge of 1 1/3 percent on sold goods and the transitum with the continuing state of distress. They point out that this does not contradict the existing contracts and imperial customs exemptions, as other cities also allowed this. They ask St. Gallen to compel their own merchants to pay the duties, and promise to revoke the surcharge when the situation improves.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The bailiff and Council of Koppigen ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have their fellow citizen Hans Jakob Dorn, butcher, protected in all his decent and fair matters and to grant him the effect of their letter of recommendation. Dorn wishes to collect a debt from Melcher Ricken in St. Gallen and fears being called to court because of the debt.
en.sender: The bailiff and Council of Koppigen
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Wangen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have appointed a general court day for their citizen Susanna Müllerin, widow of Hans Jacob Baaden. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to have the edict publicly posted and published, so that any creditors may assert their claims and no one is disadvantaged by ignorance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene with Bartlome Schabinger on behalf of his son Tobias. The citizen of St. Gallen Flori Heuss had nursed Tobias Schabinger in Paris during a severe illness and lent him 37 ducats from his own money. Tobias Schabinger had not repaid the money and had departed. Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request mediation so that Heuss may recover his money.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the information regarding the military arrangements of the Confederates. They communicate that they have posted sentries in Toggenburg and will consult with the Evangelical cantons as well as the three neighboring cities. They send a copy of the Recess of Baden as well as a copy of an imperial letter of credence for a new Resident, in order to assess the situation of the imperial recruitment efforts.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter of 26 March, in which help was requested in the collection of a debt of the son of Hans Bartholomäus Schowinger. They report that the father is in Wien and refuses to settle the debts of his disobedient son, as he is not liable for them according to city law. They ask Chur not to press the creditor Florian Geiss any further.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Chur

en.regest: The envoys of the Roman Imperial Majesty to the general Confederation inform the Confederates that the Freiherr von Schwarzenberg has been recalled as Resident. In his place, Marx Jakob von Schönau, guardian of the heirs of Archduke Leopold, Council and Waldvogt of the County of Hauenstein, is appointed. He is to remain in the Confederation in the name of the Emperor and to ensure good neighborhood as well as the observance of the hereditary treaties.
en.sender: Hannibal Graf zu Hohenems und Isaak Vollmar
en.recipient: Eidgenössische Stände

en.regest: Augustinus Rogg and Augustin Berlin report to the Burgomaster of Buchhorn about a dispute with the St. Gallen dyers Michel and Daniel Steinmann. They accuse the Steinmann of having defrauded them of 160 gulden, because the latter left the yarn in Buchhorn until it was sold by soldiers. The Steinmann had also insulted the Buchhorn dyer. Rogg and Berlin demand that the Steinmann restore their honor and pay, otherwise they will seize their goods and call upon the journeymen to stand still.
en.sender: Augustinus Rogg, pastor of Bregenz, and Augustin Berlin of Bregenz
en.recipient: Burgomaster of Buchhorn

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Altstätten inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the citizen of St. Gallen, Gerber, claims the opposite. However, both parties have sworn under oath that the dispute took place in the bathhouse in Altstätten. Since this falls under the jurisdiction of Altstätten, they ask St. Gallen to admonish their citizen as the instigator. They offer to let justice be done to the opposing party from Altstätten.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information about the current prices for beef and goat meat. The butchers in Konstanz had demanded a surcharge and referred to higher prices in other places. The people of Konstanz wanted to adjust their prices to those of the neighboring communities.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the authorities of Genf to support their merchants who trade in Frankreich and have been naturalized there. These merchants have been burdened with high duties by French officers against agreed-upon contracts and therefore wanted to move to Genf. St. Gallen requests Genf to grant the merchants the right to store their goods and to reside in the city.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Syndics, Burgomaster and Council of Genf

en.regest: The bailiff and Council of Trübschen confirm the receipt of a letter from the tanners of St. Gallen. They regret that the Dean of Berg has spoken sharply towards the citizens, and point out that they cannot issue orders to the Dean, as his superior is the Bishop of Konstanz. They ask the people of St. Gallen to assert their rights with the St. Vitus monastery. The dispute between the tanner and the Dean has been settled by a compromise of 50 florins.
en.sender: The bailiff and Council of Trübschen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to the Council envoys of the Confederates in Baden about the complaints of the merchants in Frankreich regarding tariff increases and a high levy, which violate the alliance and privileges. They ask for support and for the hearing of the delegated town councillors Sebastian Schobinger and Christoph Büfler, so that the complaints are remedied and the merchants are relieved.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Council envoys of the thirteen cantons at the Diet of the Yearly Account in Baden

en.regest: Landammann and Council of the Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help the country people of the parish of Unterhürstey with a tax and a contribution. They had built their own church to alleviate the hardships of the church journey. Appenzell asks for support out of neighborly and religious kinship.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Joseph Hochrütiner asks Amtsbürgermeister Amadeo Eckholt in Lindau not to censure his absence from the court, as the Obrist has forbidden him to come to Lindau. He thanks him for the confirmation of the arrest against his son and asks that his complaint be presented to an authority. He demands that his son be handed back to him and that his judgment be confirmed. He rejects the accusation that he wants to go to the Wiedertäufer and asks that the arrest against the son not be lifted, but that the child be allowed to leave the city.
en.recipient: Amadeo Eckholt, Amtsbürgermeister zu Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform the Statthalter of the Hauptmannschaft, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz, that a woman detained in St. Gallen has confessed to having stolen two Schetter from the dyer master Michel Steinmann and having sold them in Konstanz to an Anna in the Weberngasse. They request the authorities of Konstanz to investigate the matter and to report on the stolen pieces as well as the proceeds.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Statthalter of the Hauptmannschaft, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a copy of the apothecary tariff established there. They intend to create a reasonable price framework for their apothecaries to protect the population from being overcharged, and see the St. Gallen regulation as a useful model.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Statthalter and the judges of the city court of Lindau ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish an enclosed edict. It concerns a general debt court day against the cloth shearer Daniel Staenglin and his wife. Since citizens of St. Gallen could be creditors, these are to be informed through the publication.
en.sender: Statthalter and judges of the city court of Lindau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The administrator of the captaincy, the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to ensure the payment of an amount outstanding for 15 years to Margaretha Klaidhuein, widow of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Tobias Damer. They refer to an attached copy of the claim and ask for a swift settlement.
en.sender: The administrator of the captaincy, also the Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The General Officers of the united army warn the Confederates about the negotiations of the three cantons with Spanien regarding an eternal peace. They fear that the free passage of Spanish troops through Switzerland is allowed therein, which would endanger freedom and bring the war into the country. They ask the cantons to use their authority to prevent such advantageous treaties, and protest that they are not responsible for damages that arise from the disregard of this warning.
en.sender: General Officers and Colonels of the united army of the Allied Kronen and Estates (among others J. L. von Erlach, Wilhelm Otto Count zu Nassau)
en.recipient: The 13 cantons of the Confederation

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the tense situation in the Drei Bünden, where parts of the communities and governments do not agree with the peace negotiations with Mailand and raise protests. To prevent internal unrest and an escalation in the context of the Thirty Years' War, they invite to a Diet on 15. September 1639 in Baden. They ask St. Gallen to attend the day through a council messenger with full power.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen send Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen a copy of their newly established apothecary tariff for simple and compound medicines. They ask the Confederates to accept the tariff and declare themselves ready for further Confederate requests.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the communication of the recently renewed apothecary tariff. They assure that they, on their part, will always show true friendship and confederate love.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Meilenfeld confirm the receipt of a letter of 12 November, according to which the St. Gallen citizen-servant Salomon Heimann had been dismissed due to committed errors and mistreatment. They had arrested Heimann, but he had traveled to Feldkirch one hour earlier, after a letter from his father from St. Gallen had reached him. Statthalter and Council of Meilenfeld declare themselves willing to fulfill similar requests.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Council of Altstätten inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the Rheintal estates will arrive in St. Gallen on 30 October and on the following day wish to negotiate over the wine committee.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the Schultheiss and Council of Arbon to have the maid Rosanna Feurin, who is detained there, return a red coat and a pair of red stockings which she allegedly stole from the citizen of St. Gallen Sebastian Zollikoffer. They invoke the law of the Confederation, according to which stolen items must be returned free of charge.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Arbon

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen request Landammann and Council of Appenzell to order their resident Conrad Neuwiler to appear at the St. Gallen Town Hall on 7 November 1639 at 8 o'clock in the morning. The background is a complaint by the tiler Hans Kestenpaur against Neuwiler and the St. Gallen citizen Christoph Koller for defamatory words. The St. Gallen authorities ask for the presence of Neuwiler and his wife to clarify the matter.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Unterwalden ob dem Kernwald inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a legal dispute between their countryman Matheus von Flüe and the citizens of St. Gallen Daniel Zollikofer and partners. They state that the witness examination took place on 19 October and that the statements would be handed over to the judge. The court day in St. Gallen is set for 14 January.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of Unterwalden ob dem Kernwald
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nördlingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help the Nördlingen citizen Wolfgang Fischer the Younger in a legal matter against the citizens of St. Gallen Ochsner and Caspar Riedler. They refer to a submitted supplication and ask for an amicable decision.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nördlingen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Gottfried Lampen, a member of the city court, in the collection of a debt owed to the St. Gallen merchant Sebastian Fugger. The debt originates from the estate of the deceased David Broß. Nördlingen asks for helpful support so that Lampen may receive his balance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizen Hans Heinrich Ritter bester zum Storken in the collection of a fine of 96 francs pronounced in 1625 before the St. Gallen Steiger. The heirs of the deceased debtor Lorenz Begobinger have in the meantime means. Zürich asks that the St. Gallen parties be compelled to let Ritter have his right.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the message brought by their envoys concerning the high honor, loyalty, and friendship shown to them. They also thank them for the gift of 400 gulden in cash, which they have received for the new church building at the lower Heissteg. They promise to reciprocate this to the best of their ability.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Maria Magdalena, widow of the Counts of Ysenburg and Büdingen, recalls her letter of 12 November 1639, in which she had described her dire straits following the imperial cession of the county to Hessen-Darmstadt. As she has received no answer, she again requests a loan against obligation, in order to be able to survive until the peace.
en.sender: Maria Magdalena, née Countess of Nassau-Weilburg, Countess of Ysenburg and Büdingen, widow
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Archduchess Claudia to abolish the new customs increases at the Austrian customs posts. They refer to the eternal hereditary union and ask that the old customs pacts be observed again, in particular that goods from the Innerschweizerischen Lande pass duty-free and that only the old ordinary customs be levied on transit goods.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Archduchess Claudia

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to cause the citizen Hans Scherringer there to pay his servant Hans Jacob Bailbronnen and his wife the outstanding 250 gulden for carriage fare and provisions to Wien. The citizens of Ulm had advanced the money for the journey and the stay, but the father had refused the payment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Schultheiss, Council, Ammann and Court of Vaduz to allow the citizen of St. Gallen Hans Stüber to pursue the property inherited by his wife Catharina from his grandmother Catharina Schillerin into the Pünste without deduction. They refer to a similar case from Chur and ask for mutual consideration.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss, Council, Ammann and Court of Vaduz

en.regest: The Pflegerschaft and Amtleute of the hospital in Überlingen ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in view of crop failures, high levies, and the consequences of war, for a postponement of the due interest payments. They promise to settle the debt at the next opportunity and ask for patience.
en.sender: Pflegerschaft and Amtleute of the hospital in Überlingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nördlingen remind Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of their letter of 20 January 1640 concerning their citizen Gottfried Empen and his debtor Sebastian Höggern. Since no answer has yet been received, they ask that the debt be imposed on Höggern by authority.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to tolerate the request of the hospital master Konrad Fürstler to settle an interest before the bombardment until the end of the winter quarters. They say that they are prevented from paying the interest because of the high costs for the provisioning of the soldiery, which amount to 2400 florins monthly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Chur not to make any deduction from the withdrawal of the paternal and maternal inheritance from Chur for the widow of their deceased Council member Anton Klugi and his heirs. They refer to Confederate customs and previous cases in which citizens of St. Gallen had inherited without tax deduction, and request friendly approval.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Chur

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rorschach ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publish an edict according to civic custom, without burdening those affected. They wish to inform the residents and citizens whether they have claims against the persons mentioned or their property. Rorschach offers to serve St. Gallen in the same manner.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, in response to their letter of intercession, they have granted the citizen Jacob Weyermann there the release of the share of his wife Helena Geigerin in the estate of Conrad Küni. They request surety by citizens of St. Gallen, as Weyermann is absent, and assure that the surety will be properly taken up.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Wilhelm Heinrich, Graf zu Fürstenberg und Trauchburg, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about a nighttime break-in into the Liebfrauenkirche in Enandach on 1 May 1640. The perpetrators had ruined the altars and stolen church ornaments. He asks the St. Gallen authorities to secure the stolen items, which might be sold in St. Gallen, and to transmit them to Konstanz, as well as to identify the perpetrators and inform him.
en.sender: Wilhelm Heinrich, Graf zu Fürstenberg und Trauchburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Rheineck ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the weaver Spitzer. He had, as guardian of the daughters of Lienhart Giger, calculated their share in the estate settlement of their father. The daughters, married to citizens of St. Gallen, refused to pay. Spitzer sued in Jol and was instructed to seek out the daughters. They refused to have him drawn along. Rheineck asks that, in the event of refusal to pay, Spitzer be assisted by the authorities to obtain payment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Annweiler thank St. Gallen for the support through a donation of 100 Reichsthaler, which was granted by Countess Louisa of the Palatinate at the request of the Annweiler envoys. The money has been distributed among the plundered citizens, churches, and schools. They ask for God's blessing for St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster, Council, Church Officers, and Community of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Chancery of the city of St. Gallen confirms that a sealed, printed letter from Emperor Ferdinand III. of 26 May 1640 from Wien, concerning the convoked Imperial Diet, was delivered to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen by the Nuremberg ambassador Lorenz Rauschen. The present certificate serves as a receipt.
en.sender: Chancery of the city of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nördlingen reply to an inquiry from St. Gallen regarding a claim by the citizens of St. Gallen Othmar and Caspar Rüttmann against the citizen of Nördlingen Wolfgang Vischer. Vischer denies the debt and claims that he was forced by an arrest to sign an obligation. Nördlingen refuses to impose anything on Vischer without further examination, but offers to allow the claim of the Rüttmann to be properly brought and proven before them.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nördlingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to restrain their citizen Sebastian Höger to settle with the citizen of Nördlingen Gottfried Lempen and to make him free of complaint. They refer to two earlier, unanswered letters of intercession and ask for a written answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich confirm the receipt of a letter from the St. Gallen, concerning a citation of the Prelate of St. Gallen to the Imperial Diet in Regensburg. As it is unclear whether the citation is directed to the Confederates or to the Imperial Prince, they request further information regarding the form of previous replies and the intentions of the Prelate. They promise to discuss the matter at the Baden Diet and to answer St. Gallen upon receipt of the report.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Confederates report that in many places cattle are being stolen from the pastures. They ask St. Gallen to introduce border controls so that no one may pass with horses or cattle without showing a pass. They request that this be published by an open mandate and the butcher be informed, in order to prevent abuse.
en.sender: Estates and Landsgemeinde of the Confederation
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich invite Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to a conference of the Evangelical cantons on 19 July in Aarau. The occasion is the financial distress of the city of Basel. They ask for the deployment of envoys to deliberate on aid for Basel. Furthermore, they inform them of a letter from Wien, according to which imperial privileges could be confirmed at the Diet in Regensburg.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Landammann and Council of the Land of Appenzell Innerrhoden about a dispute between the St. Gallen citizen Lorenz Rech and the Appenzell countryman Wolfgang Schweg. Since Rech has not appeared despite multiple promises, the St. Gallen authorities, at the request of the Appenzell countryman, set a new court day for him on 4 August 1640 at 8 o'clock in the morning in the Rathaus in St. Gallen. They ask the Appenzell authorities to let their countryman remain unbound until then.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Land of Appenzell Innerrhoden

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for intercession on behalf of the tile-maker Conrad Nüwiller. He and his wife Magdalena Locheri have complained that a considerable sum, which is due to the wife as the inheritance of her father, has been in the custody of the St. Gallen people for years, without them deriving any benefit from it. Appenzell requests St. Gallen to ensure that Nüwiller receives the annual interest from the inheritance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landammann and Council of Uri to offer the right hand to their messenger Hans Ulrich, so that he may collect the debt of 490 florins including interest and costs from Captain Johann Strieffler. Strieffler had not paid the sum for the armor provided.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Uri

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Rottweil ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel the debtor Sebastian Höger to pay a clear debt to their citizen and court assessor. They refer to previous unsuccessful requests and lament Höger's refusal to answer the letters. Rottweil requests that the matter be mediated so that the creditor is paid without further delay.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Landammann and Council of Appenzell that the Appenzeller Lorenz Rechsteiner has not appeared at a scheduled court day in St. Gallen. The St. Gallen Wolfgang Laxen, however, has appeared. A new date has been set for 18 August 1620 at 9 o'clock in the town hall. The Appenzellers are requested to inform Rechsteiner of this and to instruct him to appear and to state his position on the incident.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: Emperor Ferdinand III. communicates that he had the complaints of the Confederates regarding the fortification of Konstanz by his envoy Schönau clarified. He proposes a conference in Waldshut on 20. September to preserve the old friendship and inheritance treaties and to dispel misunderstandings regarding Austrian or Spanish intentions.
en.recipient: Burgomaster, Schultheiss, Landammann and Council of the Confederation

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have designated 29 August as a common day of penance and prayer for the Evangelical Confederation at the Arbon Conference. They ask for acknowledgment and commend themselves to divine care.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Master and Council of the city of Straßburg request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in the legal dispute between the Halterns and Hans Conrad Haltern on the one hand and Balthasar Ludwig Küenzi and Leonhard Zollikofer on the other hand, to administer the oaths of perjury and malice (juramenta calumniae et malitiae) requested by both sides. They ask for documentary notification of whether and how the oaths were taken.
en.sender: Klaus Ludwig Wombser, Master and Council of the city of Straßburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich declare to St. Gallen that they can no longer help the St. Gallen citizen Wolfgang Schobinger, as the Pappenheim estate has passed to Count von Fürstenberg through a settlement with him. They ask St. Gallen to accompany Schobinger with a letter of intercession on his next visit to the Count, so that the latter will receive him amicably and provide means to satisfy his claims.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the repeated inquiries of the Council of Nördlingen regarding their citizen Sebastian Jäger. He says that he has apologized for his inactivity and submitted a counter-statement. If Nördlingen is not satisfied with this, Gottfried Lamp should legally assert his claim against Jäger before the St. Gallen authority.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Nördlingen

en.regest: Friedrich, Pfalzgraf bei Rhein, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to hear his councillor Josias Glaser, who is travelling in the Confederation, in his name and to give him credit. He wishes to inform them of his current condition and his intentions regarding the government of his Patrimonial Principality of Zweibrücken. He emphasizes the common religious kinship and asks for a benevolent reception.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The persons appointed in the Palatinate for the distribution of Christian aid thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the donation of 500 gulden (312 ½ Reichsthaler) to the distressed Palatines. They enclose a detailed account of the distribution to church and school officials as well as their dependents in the Lower and Upper Palatinate and in the Principality of Simmern, and ask for further support.
en.sender: Abraham Otgenius, Petrus Crugotius, Daniel Adam und Peter Seigert
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Elector Friedrich von der Pfalz informs that he has regained the Duchy of Zweibrücken. He asks the Protestant cantons of the Confederation for financial support, either for a loan of 5 percent interest or for a general collection. He promises to advocate for the Confederates and asks for a reply.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report that the Swedish councillor Josias Glaser, as envoy of Duke Friedrich von der Pfalz, has submitted a commission for the Protestant cities. As Glaser is ill, he asks for support. Zürich proposes a meeting in Aarau to collect opinions and to answer the Duke.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Pflegere, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizen Hans Jakob Heer in the claim of 200 florins of inheritance money against his cousin Daniel Heer in St. Gallen. Since the amicable settlement has failed, superior legal aid is invoked. Augsburg assures the return of the favor.
en.sender: Pflegere, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Confederates not to release the Cornet Carlo Cosio, who has been arrested in Mailand, from custody until he has made the surety Joachim Eckholt whole for a bill of exchange for 1000 Reichsgulden including interest and costs. Cosio fled with the money after his brother had not settled the bill of exchange.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Confederate cantons

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Chur reply to a letter from St. Gallen of 10 September 1639, which concerned the withdrawal of the assets of the deceased Seckelmeister Anton Clavigs by his widow. Chur refers to an older letter of 1620, which provided for mutual friendship in such cases, but emphasizes that this does not form a precedent for future cases. Since the old city rights of Chur provide for the withdrawal of the assets of outsiders, which were confirmed in 1628, they cannot comply with the request. They ask for forgiveness and promise to do everything possible that corresponds to equity.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jörg Dietrich Reding informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that his subject Balthasar Bomgarter refuses to appear in St. Gallen regarding a cattle purchase with Othmar Rietmann. Bomgarter claims that the oxen were forced upon him at a price of 67 florins, although he had only offered 60, and that he had been insulted. He wishes to prove this before his authority and refuses the jurisdiction of St. Gallen if he cannot do so.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Stamm and Council of Altstetten inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the delegates of the Rinthaler Höfe will appear before them in the morning to settle the matter of the Weingang.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the city of Konstanz dated 21 September 1640 concerning the departure of their Councillor and Seckelmeister Georg Schinder. They ask the Konstanzer to consider their request for intercession for Schinder and to grant him the promised friendship and Confederation, so that he may rely on it.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to cause their citizen Justina Schlitzin, the widow of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Eberhard Huber, to pay out to them and their siblings the inheritance share due to them from the father's estate. In the event of a refusal, the reasons are to be named.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Prince of Liechtenstein to intervene on behalf of their citizen Wolfgang Schobinger. Schobinger was defeated in a legal dispute with a Hauptmann and condemned to costs, which he has not yet fully paid. The widow of Schobinger threatens to sue before the Hofrat. The St. Gallen ask that the still outstanding war costs of eleven gulden and six schillings be settled and that further lawsuits be desisted from.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Prince of Liechtenstein

en.regest: Georg Dietrich Reding, Knight and bailiff of Rorschach, replies to a letter of 13 October, in which St. Gallen complains that he could not summon his subject Balthasar Bomgarter. He explains that this is not customary, and asks St. Gallen to specify the contracts and articles referred to, so that he may comply.
en.sender: Georg Dietrich Reding, Knight and bailiff of Rorschach
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Weiler ask Jacob Manßlin, Guild Master and Council member of St. Gallen, to report in writing how the butchers of St. Gallen sell their meat and lard and at what prices. They wish to know whether the old tariff still applies, in order to avoid misunderstandings, as the butchers of Weiler wish to follow the price of St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Jacob Manßlin, Guild Master and Council member of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the inheritance practice in Zürich: If a deceased person leaves behind full siblings and their children, the siblings' children are also admitted to the inheritance. Since the wife of the citizen of Zürich Heinrich Kerner, together with her siblings, was accepted as heirs by the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Lienhard Hüber and admitted without objection, the Zürichers request the St. Galleners to help grant Kerner his share of the surplus after deduction of the testament and legacies.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Basel ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the citizens of St. Gallen Jacob, Hieronymus and Balthasar Tischere (Schacher) in a legal matter. The three brothers have submitted a request for a letter of recommendation, as they claim 100 gulden from the inheritance of Jacob Heuberg and Anna Schneckhin as heirs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizen Hans Heinrich Uster, innkeeper at the Storch, in enforcing his claims against the children of the deceased Lorenz Schobinger. Since the children would have received a considerable inheritance after the death of the paternal grandmother, Uster asks for renewed support to assert his claims.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen recommend to the Council of St. Gallen Matthäus Muttis, who comes from Cyprus, has arrived there, and has presented his credentials. They ask the Confederates to receive the petitioner in their accustomed friendliness and to help him.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen about the death of the St. Gallen citizen and guild master Jacob Reiner. They have set a division of his estate for 21 March 1641. Since the Memmingen relatives Elias Kunzelin, Anna Röhrerin and Ursula Röhrerin could be heirs, they ask Memmingen to inform them of the date. They are to dispose of their inheritance right in writing and appear in person or through a proxy, otherwise the division will be continued without them.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Genfer of the 8th of the month, in which they request an extension of a court day for the deceased Jacob Steiner. Since the heirs have set a division for 2 March 1641, the St. Gallen cannot postpone the date any further. They grant the creditor Krüger, however, an extension until 18 February 1641. Furthermore, they urge the Genfer to settle the outstanding principal and the interest for the years 1636 to 1640.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Syndici, Burgomaster and Council of Genf

en.regest: The Masters and Council of the city of Straßburg inform the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen about the division of the estate of the deceased citizen and council member of Straßburg, Jacob Kunen. They ask that the citizen of St. Gallen, Hans Thomas Raitenberger, who claims to be an heir, be notified of the date set for 12 March. Raitenberger is to legitimize his kinship in writing or appear in person or through a proxy, otherwise the division will take place without him.
en.sender: The Masters and Council of the city of Straßburg
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich remind of their request of 11 September 1640 to support the Duke of Zweibrücken with a loan. Since a meeting in Aarau did not take place, they propose to replace the loan with a joint congratulation on the Restoration. They ask St. Gallen to communicate its opinion and the amount to be contributed, in order to draft a joint letter to Basel and Schaffhausen.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the newly appointed French ambassador, Herr von Commartin, will arrive in Solothurn on the last Sunday of the month of January and greet the Confederates. They ask that, if it suits their own situation, an honorary delegation be appointed for this occasion.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Burgomaster and Council of Lindau for a copy of their bread ordinance, in order to renew and improve their own ordinance. They assure them that they will use the copy without prejudice, and thank them for their efforts.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Bern inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they are releasing the citizen Hans Jakob Künker of St. Gallen, who had previously been admitted as a Landkind in Bern, from the obligation of federal subjects at his request. This is done against the surrender of the issued patents, so that Künker may seek his fortune in other places.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter of 11 February, in which St. Gallen had inquired about the local bread ordinance. They send a copy of the Lindau bread ordinance and declare themselves willing to render neighborly favors in similar and further matters.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss, Burgomaster and Council of Ogersheim thank them for the notification of the death of the St. Gallen Council member Jacob Reiner. They inform them that the widow Anna Reicheten, daughter of Clara Pfrister and Caspar Sunckhenheimer, is staying with her husband in Amsterdam and has not yet received the news. They ask that his share of the Reiner inheritance be kept in safekeeping until their return.
en.sender: Schultheiss, Burgomaster and Council of Ogersheim
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Appenzell thank for the letter concerning the hopeless child and ask for superior help for their tiler Konrad Küwiler. He is supposed to have received 700 florins of inheritance from his wife from her father, but is prevented from doing so. Appenzell requests St. Gallen to help the tiler so that he can obtain his property with little cost and quickly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Friedrich, Pfalzgraf bei Rhein, thanks the Confederates for the congratulations on the return of his lands and the gift of 2000 gulden. He assures them that he will maintain the friendly neighborhood with the evangelical Confederates and instruct his descendants to do the same.
en.sender: Friedrich, Pfalzgraf bei Rhein, Herzog in Bayern
en.recipient: Burgomaster, Schultheiss and Council of Zürich, Bern and St. Gallen

en.regest: Stadtammann and Council of Arbon ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant the local exile Isaak Jud access to apothecaries and herbs. Jud supports himself through the healing art and needs medicines, which are cheaper in St. Gallen. Since Jews are forbidden there, he asks for intercession. Arbon assures that Jud travels only for medical reasons.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jacob Hanibal Graf zu Hohenems, bailiff of the lordship of Feldkirch, thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the information regarding suspicious persons. He informs them that he has ordered his Austrian colleagues in Feldkirch as well as the Councils and Oberämtern of the lordship of Hohenems to keep an eye on the said bad fellows.
en.sender: Jacob Hanibal Graf zu Hohenems, Gallara and Vaduz, bailiff of the lordship of Feldkirch
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Reformed congregation in Frankfurt am Main asks the heads of the Reformed church and congregation in St. Gallen for financial support. It reports on the dire straits of the congregation, which is weakened by war, plague, and hunger. Furthermore, the small church in Bockenheim must be expanded, which costs over 2000 Reichstaler. The congregation is burdened with debts and asks for a voluntary tax for the church building and other needs.
en.sender: Lucas von der Straßent, Clemens Weitz, Daniel Flinß, Johannes Preuchius, Hendrick van der Borcht, Gerlach Beckh, Jost van Loen, Iohan De Gommer, Diederich Schoodt
en.recipient: Heads of the Reformed church and congregation in St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen recommend to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen Georg Clark, who comes from Schottland and has dedicated a treatise to the four Evangelical cities. Clark was recommended to them by Zürich and Basel and intends to travel to St. Gallen. Schaffhausen asks for admission and support.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Hauptleute and Rätesgesandten of the three Bünde at Chur answer an intercession by the merchants of St. Gallen in Italien. They reject the demand for a reduction of the toll from 52 to 40 kreuzer per piece at Chur, as the contract provides for payment in Chur currency. Regarding the double taxation in Chur and Latsch, they state that the payment had not been complained of during the occupation by the Graf von Tirol, and reserve the right to change or abolish the toll depending on circumstances.
en.sender: Hauptleute and Rätesgesandten of the three Bünde at Chur
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landammann and Council of Appenzell to tolerate the non-resident servants employed by the bleachers of St. Gallen for the current year. The masters had kept these servants expensively over the winter and depend on them. Furthermore, they request Appenzell not to prohibit the silk fabric (Schmuss) purchased in St. Gallen, but to allow its resale, so that the domestic linen weavers would not be harmed.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Burgomaster and Council of Kempten that they have received the letter of intercession concerning the claims of Kempten citizen Ferdinand Heelen against the late St. Gallen Sebastian Zollikofer the Younger. The guardian of the sons of Zollikofer has found no debts owed to Heelen in the books. St. Gallen has set a court day for 14 May at 8 o'clock in the morning and asks Kempten to have Heelen or a proxy attend this court day.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their countryman Conrad Ougsteren. He has to claim his earned wages from the St. Gallen Blochmeister Galle Schaitlin. Ougsteren wishes to give up the service for valid reasons and to comply with the Appenzell command. They ask that he be satisfied without further trouble and delay.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich invite Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to an assembly of the Reformed cantons to deliberate on the disputes between Zürich and Luzern. They ask that on 30 May 1641 an envoy with full power be sent to Aarau.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Landvogt in Ober- and Nidertoggenburg to protect the Prelate of Vispingen in his lawful purchase and to dissuade the unruly Gruebler from his plan. They refer to a supplication by the guardians of the daughter of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Jakob Locher and ask for support so that the Prelate and the guardians are not further harassed.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt in Ober- and Nidertoggenburg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from Conrad Reichert, which concerns the inheritance of the deceased Zunftherr Jacob Rainer. They communicate that they cannot recognize Reichert as an heir, as a line living in the city is more closely related and has already registered itself. They regret the situation and wish Reichert, who is staying in Amsterdam, God's grace.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Conrad Reichert, citizen and Council of Ogersheim

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request the Confederates' Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to protect Barbara Stockerin, the daughter of the citizen of Zürich Hans Bernhard Stocker, who resides in St. Gallen. They ask that the accused persons be taken into custody so that Barbara or her representative may be heard in court. The father had turned to Zürich with this request.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss, Council and the Two Hundred of the city of Bern thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the mediation assistance in the settlement of an internal unrest matter, which was resolved through the intervention of the Bernese honor envoys. They promise to reciprocate with friendship and service to Bern in similar cases, and recommend themselves mutually to the care of God.
en.sender: Schultheiss, Council and the Two Hundred of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to intervene with the Prelate of St. Gallen on behalf of the evangelical subjects in Hagenwil. These demand their own preacher or the retention of the previous portions of the benefice. Zürich offers to contribute to a solution, but first asks for mediation by St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel the citizen of St. Gallen Columban Gscheel to pay the citizen of Nürnberg Cornelius Leberun an outstanding amount of over 142 gulden. Gscheel has shown himself unreliable as Leberun's factor and has not settled the claim despite the account. Nürnberg requests official assistance to enforce the payment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen remind Lindau of a loan sum of 2000 gulden at five percent interest granted a few years ago. They complain that no further payments have been made since the first interest and that now the sixth interest along with the due principal is outstanding. They demand the settlement of the principal and interest or at least the payment of the last four annual interests, as well as clarification of how long the principal is to be kept at interest.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Lindau

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Wil ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizen Hans Strauss in an inheritance matter. Strauss, a distant relative of the deceased Sandholzer, had enriched their estate by about 100 marks. He had learned that the Sandholzer's will had been changed with the consent of the St. Gallen authorities. Wil requests the St. Gallen authorities to support Strauss and to decide the matter according to the statutes.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the deceased Winterthur butcher Hans Othmar Krüger was not able to satisfy his creditors. They ask the butchers of St. Gallen to assert their claims on Tuesday, the 17. August, at 8 o'clock in Winterthur, so that the debt can be shared and the matter discussed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Dorothea Meyerin to present to the citizen of Zürich Felix Amann a deed regarding the purchase of a half-house in Zürich. Amann had bought the house from his brother Jörg Amann and had considered it free, but it is allegedly still encumbered with 400 pounds. Zürich asks for the sending of the original or a vidimmed copy.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur report that the schoolmaster Georg Bastart complained to their Amtsschultheiss about insults by St. Gallen countrymen in Baden. Their citizen Jacob Sultzer, who was held out as a witness, testified that Bastart had only rejoiced in the bath over those present and heard nothing bad. Winterthur asks St. Gallen to make Bastart friendly and to avoid future requests.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to urge their citizen Georg Verstanden to settle the loyalty (Treueherzigkeit) provided by their citizen Bernhard Stöbel. Stöbel has complained about Verstanden, who, in the service of Nürnberg, did not pay him for hidden bookseller's goods. Nürnberg requests the swift satisfaction of Stöbel, so that he may be able to compensate his former master Wolfgang Endter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report that they cannot uphold the contract of 1634 between Dorothea Meyerin and her brother-in-law Jörg Amman. Since Amman is said to be impoverished and in care at the hospital, to have halved his estate, and the city law does not provide for a guarantee by the brother-in-law, a new settlement has become necessary. This was concluded by appointed council members to the mutual benefit of both parties. The copy is sent.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Georg Neithardt, der Jüngere, informs that he had stood before the Council because of an outstanding debt of 38.5 gulden. He promises to pay the sum in three installments at Christmas 1641, Whitsun 1642 and Gallistag 1642. Alternatively, he offers to transfer the debt with interest to Joachim Eggen in Lindau, if Ströbel accepts this.
en.sender: Georg Neithardt, der Jüngere, citizen of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Hans Bernhard Ströbel, innkeeper at the drei Kronen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to Schultheiss and Council of Luzern that their citizens trading in Frankreich have complaints in Lyon. The city authorities there demanded customs duties and a loan from them, which contradicted the privileges. St. Gallen asks Luzern to intervene jointly with Zürich in the name of the Confederate canton and to support the merchants.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Luzern

en.regest: Johann Ritter, Ammann of Altstetten, reminds the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of the wine run decided for 29 October. The officials of the Linthtaler towns and communities will appear in St. Gallen to carry out the run. Ritter asks the St. Gallen citizens to assemble with a small delegation to honour the run and to bear witness to the neighbourly friendship.
en.recipient: Haiminger, Doctor and Amtsbürgermeister of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Ritter, Ammann of Altstätten, informs the Burgomaster of St. Gallen about the wine run, which is to be opened in Altstätten on 1 November. He asks for the participation of representatives of St. Gallen in order to jointly make a decision. Ritter refers to earlier forms of cooperation and recommends himself to the neighborhood.
en.recipient: Burgomaster of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Ritter, Statthalter of Altstetten, informs the Burgomaster of St. Gallen that the man appointed in Laufen wishes to carry out the wine tasting for the coming Sunday, 13 November according to the new calendar, in Altstetten. He asks whether the Burgomaster wishes to be present on that day or to engage in some other manner, and commends himself to the neighborhood.
en.recipient: Burgomaster of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Rorschach ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly publish and post an edict regarding the appointed general court day for the creditors of the deceased Rorschach citizen Matthäus Nachbaur. They wish to ensure that any interested parties or heirs of Nachbars from St. Gallen are informed and that no one is curtailed in their rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ludwig Graf zu Eberstein describes to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the severe destruction of his lordship by the war, in which over 1000 people lost their lives. He says that he himself had to leave his ancestral home and must now pay a high ransom in order to be able to return. In his advanced age and in illness, he asks the Confederates for financial support, promises repayment after the peace, and commends himself to their favor.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Council of Arbon request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to proceed against the St. Gallen Caspar Zollikofer. He says that he bought from the Arbon feather-knife master Balthasar Vöth his knife forms and marks in order to have them copied in Frankreich. Vöth considers this to be imitation and a violation of his guild rights. Arbon requests St. Gallen to investigate the actions of Zollikofer and to protect the guild freedoms.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Winterthur inform the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen that the Winterthur citizen Magdalena Hublützelin, without the knowledge of the hospital administration, has left the hospital and has become a citizen in St. Gallen with her cousin Abraham Huber. They ask for written information about the property received by the aunt as well as for assistance with the inventory, in order to protect the heirs of both cities.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Winterthur
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Chur reply to a request from the citizens of St. Gallen regarding a withdrawal to the Seckelmeister Georg Schindler. They declare themselves willing to limit the withdrawal to 2.5 percent and to release the property located in Altstätten completely, although Schindler could have withdrawn a share of 20'000 there. They ask for reciprocity in future cases and refer to Schindler's relatives for the accounting.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen remind the Syndics, Burgomaster and Council of Genf of their answer of 14 September regarding the outstanding purchase goods and the overdue interest. They ask to pay the promised amount to the fellow citizen of St. Gallen together with interest or at least to make a partial payment. The rest is to be written on the principal bond until the interest is fully settled.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Syndics, Burgomaster and Council of Genf

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Burgomaster and Council of Genf to settle the outstanding interest on 2600 gulden, which was loaned two years ago at city currency. The last interest was due on the past St. John's Day. St. Gallen asks that the interest be paid with the first, as the principal is not yet to be redeemed.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Genf

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Confederates of Chur dated 3 December. They had levied a five percent deduction on the inheritance of the wife of the St. Gallen treasurer Hans Schindler. St. Gallen accepts this, citing the necessity of renewing the garrison in Chur. It is agreed that in future inheritance cases a five percent deduction will be levied on both sides. St. Gallen expects the final confirmation.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Chur

en.regest: Ammann and Council of Feldkirch ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their master builder and Council Bechtold Kuel von Bernstetten. Kuel has a claim to 300 gulden in interest and capital from Count Hugo von Königsegg, who has deposited the main obligation with Caspar Schlaipfer. Kuel needs a certified Vidimus of the obligation in order to receive the interest. Feldkirch asks St. Gallen to issue and certify a certified copy from the chancery.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from Feldkirch, which requests a Vidimus of a main obligation for Berchtold Kraelen von Freudenstein to Count Jürgen von Königsegg zu Hohenstaufen. Since the co-guarantor Caspar Schobinger does not reside in St. Gallen, the St. Gallen Curatores bonorum have no knowledge of the obligation. However, they have instructed the Curatores to search for Schobinger and have engaged in the enforcement pursuit. St. Gallen offers neighborly assistance.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Ammann and Council of Feldkirch

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Chur reply to a letter from St. Gallen of 14 December 1641. They regret that they could not comply with the wish of the St. Gallen Council member Georg Schindler regarding the deduction from inheritance, as this would contradict a new law. However, they agree that in future, in transactions of inheritance between the citizens of both cities, a deduction of five percent shall be levied. They ask that this be recorded in the rolls of grace or by a sealed letter.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Chur
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The creditors of the deceased Caspar Löffler ask the Burgomaster and Council of Kempten to intervene with the city of St. Gallen. The citizen of St. Gallen Caspar Schlumpf and his stepson Georg Löffler have, despite repeated reminders, not declared themselves willing to pay the inheritance debts. Schlumpf has furthermore interfered in the inheritance beyond the rights due to him. The creditors ask for a written recommendation to St. Gallen so that the debtors are compelled to pay.
en.sender: Creditors of the deceased Caspar Löffler
en.recipient: Burgomaster, Amtsvorsteher and Council of the city of Kempten

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to secure a friendly intervention for their citizens, who are creditors of Caspar Costler. They refer to an attached report and ask that the matter be treated not strictly according to the law, but according to equity, so that the petitioners may benefit from the intervention.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Maximilian Wilhelm, Erbtruchseß von Wolfegg, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to give credit to his lieutenant Georg Stöppel and to help him in the return of deserting soldiers from the company of the Obristleutnant Gerhard Blankenhans. These are to be detained in St. Gallen. He promises to send them a pardon.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the events in their city concerning a soldier who deserted from Lindau. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to support the envoy Eicher, sent by them, in this matter and to treat him in a neighborly manner, as the Chapter does not wish to settle the matter itself. Lindau is ready for an amicable settlement.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from Count von Wolfegg of 8 February 1647 regarding the bondman Hans Jerg Schueburger who fled from Lindau. They regret that the prisoner escaped through a mob from the city, although they had wanted to hand him over. They have identified and detained the perpetrators and ask for forgiveness for the incident.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Maximilian Willebaldo, Count zu Wolfegg, Governor of the Fortress Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from Count von Wolfegg of 8 February 1642, which concerns the servant Hans Jakob Rosenberger who fled from Lindau. They state that the improper actions of the servants, who wanted to take the man from their hands, had been unknown to them. They had arrested the ringleaders and handed them over to the watchmaster. Since the principal offender had fled into the territory of the neighboring authority, they had requested him to arrest him in order to give the Count satisfaction.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Count Maximilian Wilibald von Wolfegg, Governor of the Fortress of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen thank Appenzell for their efforts in the apprehension of the escaped soldier Hans Jacob Rosenburger. They request the Appenzellers to take the fugitive, in particular the main ringleader Jacob Rüschler von Hundwil, into custody upon renewed sighting in their territory and to take further steps to avoid further inconveniences.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council Appenzell

en.regest: Max Wilhelm Graf zu Wolfegg thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the willing arrest of a servant by a delegated Lieutenant. He asks the St. Gallen authorities to give full credit to his delegated Schultheiss and to hand over the servant, in order to promote military justice. He offers his services for all occurrences.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council in the Outer Rodes of the Land of Appenzell inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the soldier Hans Jakob Rothenburger, who fled from St. Gallen, and the young Passthart. They report that both arrived in Trogen on Tuesday evening and then departed in an unknown direction. They ask St. Gallen to name the Landammann who is said to have been involved in the deed, so that they can punish him.
en.sender: Landammann and Council in the Outer Rodes of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Landvogt of Frauenfeld to revoke the citation of their citizen Jacob Keller by Hans Melchior Oehlinger. Keller says that he was already sued by Oehlinger in St. Gallen in October 1641 and instructed to reach an amicable settlement through advisors. The St. Gallen authority demands that the proceedings be continued in St. Gallen as the first instance, and offers to let justice be done immediately in the event of a settlement.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt of Frauenfeld

en.regest: Maximilian, Graf zu Wolfegg, complains to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the treatment of his imperial Schultheiss Jacob Siesser by citizens of St. Gallen. They say that these had held an assembly of about 300 men, beaten down the servants of St. Gallen and insulted the Schultheiss. He demands that the city punish the ringleaders, otherwise he will protest publicly and will no longer guarantee the safety of the merchants of St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Maximilian Abbot zu Wolfegg asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to spare the widow Anna Zollikoffer, who stood before the court for insulting remarks towards a seamstress. He refers to her earlier melancholy and asks that she not be brought into further difficulties, but that she be granted good.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Hamburg request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizen Hermann Wachtmeister in the collection of a debt of 100 Reichsthaler including interest and costs against Gottfried Schobinger. Wachtmeister has received nothing despite multiple reminders. Hamburg requests legal support so that the debtor or his heirs are compelled to pay.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the City of Hamburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen report that their citizen Hans Jakob Seggler has filed a protestation before them in a legal dispute with Laurentz Zilli of St. Gallen. They request St. Gallen to confirm in writing how this protestation was issued before their Council, so that Seggler may make use of it legally.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Council of Arbon inform Heinrich Schaubinger that Maria Lärcherin, who was detained in Arbon, has fled. They ask him to appear on 13 March to deliberate on the items brought to her and to return his property to him. Furthermore, they request him to bring a sealed letter from his superiors so that future cases of confiscation are avoided. They inquire about the state of affairs in Feldkirch and ask that the enclosed letter be held back if no satisfaction has been given.
en.recipient: Heinrich Schaubinger, Doctor of Medicine, of St. Gallen

en.regest: The town clerk and Council of Feldkirch ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to request the Curatores bonorum of Caspar Schlumpf to hand over the vidimized copy of an obligation for 1000 gulden, which awards 300 gulden to Berchtold Köhlen von Sonnenstein. The St. Gallen authorities had previously stated that they had no knowledge of the Königseggische deed.
en.sender: The town clerk and Council of Feldkirch
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to lift the arrest of their countryman Michael Jäger. The citizen of St. Gallen Conrad Ziegler had arrested Jäger and prohibited a debt, which Appenzell considers unusual and contrary to the friendship of the Confederation. They ask that Jäger be satisfied in his lawful claims.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Martin von Rietenbach asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to postpone the arrival of their envoys, scheduled for the coming Tuesday regarding the merchants, to the following Thursday, as he must travel to Altstätten on Tuesday morning. Furthermore, he requests the appointment of lawyers for the final settlement of a dispute between his officials of Widnau and Haslach and the heirs of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen, Jacob Bleyner.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
