en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report that their butchers complain because they can no longer purchase cattle at the local rates due to the higher meat prices in the Confederation. They ask St. Gallen for information on how the best ox, ox-mass, cow, and calf meat is taxed and sold there, and whether a surcharge is levied, as well as how they intend to proceed in the future.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that much foreign people, in particular cavalry, are said to be gathering around Marchdorf and Feldkirch in order to attack the fortress Hohen-Twiel. They ask the Confederates to inquire about the strength and intentions of these troops and to communicate the results to them.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The parish priests of Hannover and the surrounding area ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a collection to support the city of Hannover, which has been afflicted by the war. They refer to a letter already sent to the Consistory, in which the dire situation was described, and promise that the aid will only be needed once. They commend the city of St. Gallen to divine care.
en.sender: Henricus Oraeus, Cunradus Henningg, Wendelinus Seipelius, Gilhelmus Christophorus Heimius, Carolus Snabelius, Johannes Hermannus, Georgius Benderus, Johannes Antonius Riccius, Johann Hartmann Palthenius
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Wil request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in the name of the bailiff Barbara Farrin, to question the witnesses of an ecclesiastical process in Konstanz who reside in St. Gallen. They ask that the statements be transmitted in writing and sealed to the bailiff, so that he can present them to the ecclesiastical judge.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Obervogt Ludwig Korber asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help his subject Hans Konrad Wink, innkeeper to the Lion in Langenrissen. The citizen of St. Gallen Jörg Basthart had lodged seven soldiers with Wink, promised to pick them up and pay for them, but has disappeared. Wink has spent over 20 gulden and demands payment. Korber requests the St. Gallen authorities to compel Basthart to pay.
en.sender: Ludwig Korber, Obervogt of the Lordship of Laufen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ammann and Council of Feldkirch ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to admonish the bailiff of Arbon to refund the purchase price for silverware to their citizen and goldsmith Joachim Frey. Frey had bought the silver from the thief Anna Maria Seülerin and handed it over to Dr. Heinrich Schobinger on the order of the authorities. The bailiff had, however, offset the purchase price with costs. Feldkirch points out that justice must be administered gratis and asks for support.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Basel reply to a request from St. Gallen to arrest the debtor Saurwasser. They point out that he often stays inconspicuously in the city and disappears when he is sought. They recommend having a private man set on him or turning to Solothurn if he is staying in Dornach.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, at the request of the Capuchin Laurentius von Unterwalden, to pardon Balthasar, Hartmann, Michael Steiner and Jakob Moler, who are detained there. The young men are imprisoned for mistreatment and, without intercession, threaten to meet their death. Appenzell requests mercy and release.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The chancery of the city of St. Gallen confirms the receipt of a sealed letter from the Lords Statthalter and Council of the canton of Unterwalden, which was handed over to the Amtsbürgermeister on 17 June 1642. The letter is submitted to the competent canton in Treuen and is therefore kept in custody insofar as the law permits. The messenger is dismissed from the inn with this receipt.
en.sender: Chancery of the city of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Lords Statthalter and Council of the canton of Unterwalden

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Unterwalden thank St. Gallen for the support in the pursuit of criminals. They ask for mercy for the young Balthasar Fanleman of Hergiswil, as they cannot confirm his deeds in their own land and he is young. Regarding the other persons mentioned, Michel Steiner of Hergiswil and Jacob Walen of Buchs, they cannot make any statements.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Rudolf Reding, Landvogt of Liechtenstein, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, in response to their inquiry, he had his officials search for the arrested Jaglin Walmen. Since much time had passed since the arrest and the land had been full of vagabonds, he had received no further news. He refers to the content of his earlier letter.
en.sender: Johann Rudolf Reding, Landvogt of Liechtenstein
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Rudolf Reding, Landvogt, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the boy Jögli Walen from Klingnau, who had come into captivity on 31 May 1640 with Christoph Dürlemann from the Lucerne region, was released after two days. He says that he was forced to board by the two older companions and was led astray by them. Nothing further is found in the protocol.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Unterwalden inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that several offenders, including three from Unterwalden, are in custody in St. Gallen. They ask for information on names and offenses as well as for a postponement of execution, in order to check whether anyone would take up the matter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Heinrich von Schönau, Landvogt of Grüningen, to release the subject Jakob Küntze of Krumenschwil, who is lying in the sick house in St. Gallen. He says that he urgently wished to return to his homeland. The St. Gallen offer to pick up the patient without chains or to hand him over on a cart.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Heinrich von Schönau, Landvogt of Grüningen

en.regest: Ammann and Council of Arbon inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they would hold court over a man detained with them until the coming Monday and cause the execution by the judge. Since the man still has waiting money, they ask the St. Gallen authorities to release him until then.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Konrad Widerholt responds to the request of the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the citizens Zacharias Schuggen and Sebastian Hoggeren in the release of goods from the recently confiscated enemy ship of Konstanz. He states that the claimed goods, including figures cast in Wachs, could not be considered the lawful property of the Confederates. However, should the two citizens prove that it is their paid-for property, he will reimburse them the due value.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ybbs ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to award their fellow citizen Agnes Kellerin, widow of the deceased Jakob Keller, her rightful share in the dispute over his inheritance. They refer to an attached excerpt from their statutes and ask for a rapid and inexpensive decision.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen express their regret over the fire in the city of Schwyz and ask God for the healing of the damages. They allocate 500 gulden from the city treasury and have collected 300 gulden from wealthy citizens, totaling 800 gulden. They ask the Confederates to distribute the money to the fire victims and promise to help in similar occasions as well.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: the Confederates

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen express their regret over the fire in Schwyz and ask for God's assistance. They allocate 500 gulden from the city treasury and ask the envoys to collect them. In addition, 300 gulden were collected from citizens, so that a total of 800 gulden are available. The city offers further friendship to the Confederates.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Schwyz

en.regest: The Elders and Heads of the High German community in Frankenthal ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a voluntary Christian contribution. They justify this with the impoverishment of the community caused by the war, which is no longer in a position to provide the necessary maintenance to its church and school servants, as all means of salary have been withdrawn from them by the authorities.
en.sender: Jacob Buda, Jacob Acker, Hans Zimmermann, Johann Ludwig, Hans Münch and Jacob Grammer, Elders and Heads of the High German community in Frankenthal
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that at the recent Baden Diet it was decided to maintain the coin valuation of 1638 and not to make any price increase for the gold and silver denominations. They request the St. Gallen to refrain from a planned revaluation in order to avoid disadvantages in the Confederation, and ask for notification of the reasons for their intention.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council of Schwyz thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the support after a fire in Schwyz. They confirm the receipt of a donation from the St. Gallen city chest and from private individuals and ask for the acceptance of this tribute. They promise to keep the gratitude in memory and wish St. Gallen protection from suffering.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau thank for the patient waiting time regarding outstanding interest payments to the Seckelmeister. They ask for further patience, as the war and garrison service would have exhausted their means. They promise to settle the debt at the first means.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Casparus Martinius and Maria, widow of the former court and town preacher Conrad Martini of Büdingen, thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the donation of 50 Reichstaler from the town treasury as well as for 8 Reichstaler from the clergy. They ask for God's blessing and promise to pray for the welfare of the city.
en.sender: Casparus Martinius and Maria, widow of Conrad Martini
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Appenzell that they have learned from their citizen Joachim Krommen, in the name of his sister Elsbeth Krommen, that Appenzell is allotting the inheritance to him and the other heirs of the deceased Anna Krommen and her husband Jakob Knaefler. Krommen was instructed to deposit his share in the St. Gallen chancery so that it is secured in case Anna Krommen or her children return.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhoden of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Biberach ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizen Joachim Stalzer, weaver, in a petition. Stalzer had turned to the Biberach authorities because he had found no redress in St. Gallen. He asks for a letter of intercession to the St. Gallen magistracy, so that the St. Gallen messenger Lorenz compensate him for the loss of 40 gulden.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm reply to a letter of the 15th of the month, in which the citizens of St. Gallen Albrecht Stiller and Elias Ritter, as curators of Hans Georg Stiller, who is staying in St. Gallen, have presented a counter-argument. Ulm declares that, had the matter been otherwise situated, they would have helped the citizen of St. Gallen Joachim Kunkler in accordance with his intercession. They express their willingness for friendly dealings.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Henricus Oraus, pastor and inspector at Hanau, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information about a collection that arrived in Frankfurt for the needy population in Hanau. He says that he has contacted the servant of Herr Halder, who has the funds before him but has no instruction as to whom they are to be handed over. Oraus asks for an explanation as to whom the funds are to be distributed.
en.sender: Henricus Oraus, pastor and inspector at Hanau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Henricus Oraus, pastor of Hanau and Inspector, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to let the blessing (donation) intended for the poor of Hanau go exclusively to the needy pastors, church and school officials there. He refers to the fact that these alone had asked for help and warns against involving other foreign churches, which had not requested anything, in it.
en.sender: Henricus Oraus, pastor of Hanau and Inspector
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen reply to a letter from St. Gallen of 29 September, in which the latter had requested the abolition of a renewed toll for merchants. They justify the levy with the high war costs as a border town and refer to the fact that merchants of St. Gallen are also subject to high levies in other places. They emphasize that they had treated the St. Gallen citizens favorably as Confederates until now, and remain well-disposed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen report that, owing to the favorable livestock supply until Easter, they have set a meat tax. They ask for information on how the meat tax and the weighing at the receivers are handled and how the livestock supply stands there.

Henricus Oraeus, pastor and inspector in Frankfurt am Main, acknowledges receipt of 500 gulden, which the Council of St. Gallen has designated for the evangelical churches, pastors, and their survivors in the Confederation. The money was handed over to him by the Frankfurt Council member Johann-Jacob Müller. Oraeus promises to distribute the sum to the recipients and to send a detailed receipt to the Council of St. Gallen.
en.sender: Henricus Oraeus, pastor and inspector in Frankfurt am Main
en.recipient: Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Solothurn ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to earnestly urge the miller Hans Ruch, who lives in St. Gallen at the inn of the Hecht, to report to his guardian in Solothurn in order to settle his debts. They also ask to have the innkeeper Joachim Rüetschler made to be patient with the collection of the debt.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Friedrich, Pfalzgraf bei Rhein, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a voluntary tax for the needy church and school servants as well as for widows and orphans in his lands. He justifies this with the impoverishment of the subjects through wars and asks for support to maintain the preaching office.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Council of Konstanz, which is considering a reduction of the meat tax and asks about the local prices. St. Gallen informs them that the best fattened and Vnger oxen meat costs at most 5 ½ kreuzer, the poorer 1–2 Pfennig, the best cow and calf meat 5 kreuzer, the best lamb meat 5 ½ kreuzer and the best pork 7 kreuzer. They ask for a reply.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz

en.regest: The Administrators of the Landmannschaften, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information on the level of meat prices for beef and veal in St. Gallen. They refer to an inquiry from the city of Schaffhausen regarding the meat tax and ask for a prompt report.
en.sender: The Administrators of the Landmannschaften, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kaufbeuren reply to the demand of the Ulm Council members Albrecht Müller and Elias Rütter, on behalf of their ward Hans Georg Müller, for the payment of arrears of interest. They refer to the state of war and their own financial difficulties. They state that Müller is willing to pay 100 to 150 gulden as a deduction from the capital, if this is possible.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm

en.regest: Landammann and Council in the Outer Rhoden of the Land of Appenzell request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to discharge Elsbetha Kellerin, who is from their region and has suffered a severe foot injury while serving as a servant in St. Gallen and is now unable to work, from the hospital. The family has no means to provide for her. They hope that the former masters or the city's cashiers would take over the costs of her care.
en.sender: Landammann and Council in the Outer Rhoden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the citizen of Ulm Hans Georg Müller, who had fled to St. Gallen, is being held by his wife, the wife of the citizen of St. Gallen Jost Runkler. The brothers-in-law have submitted a written declaration. Ulm asks St. Gallen to instruct the woman to release Müller and let him go to Ulm, so that he may settle his debt.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to treat their citizens Hans Felix Abegg and Heinrich Vögelin, the next of kin of the deceased Maria von Weilerin, favorably in her inheritance matters. They recommend the petitioners and ask for friendly support.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The assembled representatives of the 13 cantons of the Confederation in Baden ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to forbid and prevent the secret and public exchange of money and the abolition of the currency by their citizens, as this causes great damage to the Confederation.
en.sender: Cities and Lands of the 13 cantons of the Confederation
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Council and Elders of the Dutch and French Reformed Churches in Frankenthal ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a Christian tax. They justify this with the dire straits of the city and the congregations due to war burdens, plundering, and the lack of means to maintain the preaching office, as they would have to attract expensive preachers from outside in case of a pastor's absence. They refer to previous generous gifts of the Confederates and hope for renewed help.
en.sender: The Council and Elders of the Dutch and French Reformed Churches in Frankenthal
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Wangen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan of 1200 gulden. They say that they had been quartered by 150 cuirassiers of the Holy Regiment and had to pay for their provisions as well as a due monthly wage immediately, which was impossible for them. They promise to repay the sum with interest within two years and ask for a prompt answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the letter of the city of Kempten dated 17 December. They regret that Kempten has fallen into distress due to quartered horsemen, and declare that they cannot comply with the request for a loan of 1200 gulden. As a reason, they cite the high expenditures and the low income of their own city due to the ongoing war unrest. They ask that the refusal not be taken amiss.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Kempten

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich answer the request from Bern and Schaffhausen to abolish the new tolls in Morsee and St. Gallen, as these burden the merchants. They promise to take the necessary steps and to forward the answers.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to withhold the payment of the debt of their citizen Hans Jörg Müller, who is detained in St. Gallen, to the citizen of St. Gallen Joachim Künckler. The guardians of Müller have declared that they have no further means of payment. Ulm requests that the arrest be lifted and that Müller be allowed the way to Ulm, in order to avoid further unnecessary costs.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Stadttammann and Council of the city of Feldkirch request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to obtain their naturalized citizen Magdalena Weltin, who has entered the service of a butcher in St. Gallen without permission. They are to instruct her to appear in Feldkirch within eight days and report there, but not to be tolerated in St. Gallen until then.
en.sender: Stadttammann and Council of the city of Feldkirch
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Captains and Council envoys of the three Bündner cantons ask the Confederates, in view of the threat by the Habsburgers on Lake Constance, to Confederately observe the status of the Bündner and to support them. They assure that they will maintain the old hereditary union with Österreich, and ask for an answer.
en.sender: Captains and Council envoys of the three Bündner cantons
en.recipient: The 13 cantons of the Confederation

en.regest: Catharina Freiin von Hohenberg asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for help, as her sister, a widow, has lost her inheritance of 2000 gulden through intermediaries. She requests the city to send a messenger at the city's expense to Rattenstein to clarify the matter and to support the sister.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich communicate to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen a copy of a letter from the Captains and Council envoys of the three Bünde to the thirteen cantons and the allied territories from the Chur League Diet. They ask for the opinion and assessment of the St. Gallen regarding this letter.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform that, at the request of the Catholic cantons and the Prelate of St. Gallen, they have scheduled a general Confederate Diet on 20 February in Baden. They request St. Gallen to send envoys to Baden the day before, on 19 February, to coordinate the common position with the other Protestant cantons and the city of Biel.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to report on rumors that a tumult has taken place in St. Gallen, that the city has been set on fire, or that an engineer has been murdered. They request that the perpetrators of these lies be identified and arrested, or that their whereabouts be communicated, in order to protect the honor of the city of Zürich.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Catholic cantons ask the Council of St. Gallen to participate in an assembly at Baden in order to deliberate on the tense situation. They propose to send envoys to the French King and ask for consent to this step as well as to the answering of a letter addressed to some thirteen cantons.
en.sender: The Catholic cantons of the Confederation
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to order their citizen Melchior Müller to appear before them on 25 February. Müller has spoken impiously to Lorenz Nuwlin of St. Gallen at the town hall and must justify himself for this. Appenzell promises to let only the law and what is just befall him.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan of 3000 gulden, as they say that they could not afford the transport costs. As security they offer 300 casks of wine or the village of Sipnau situated on the lake. They promise to repay the debt in peaceful times.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Wilhelm Otto Graf zu Ysenburg und Büdingen informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the upcoming restitution of his lordships after an eight-year exile. Since the churches and schools in his territories are heavily damaged and he himself as well as his subjects are exhausted by the burdens of war, he asks the citizens of St. Gallen to also consider his lordships Ysenburg, Büdingen and others in the planned public collection for foreign churches and clergy and to grant a donation.
en.sender: Wilhelm Otto Graf zu Ysenburg und Büdingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Maximilian Willibald von Lindau asks Obristleutnant Johann Nussbaum to allow the citizen of St. Gallen Mainrad Fuchs to transport five pieces of cloth and 4.5 Schöffel of oats from Ravensburg to St. Gallen. He warns of possible consequences for the city of St. Gallen and Switzerland if the goods were to be confiscated, and promises gratitude.
en.recipient: Johann Nussbaum

en.regest: Hugo Graf zu Königsegg und Rottenfels asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help his subjects Endele, Bartholme and Michael Keller from Staufen to their right. Their deceased brother Sebastian Keller, a former St. Gallen black dyer, left a son Hanns, who has also died. The mother of the child wants to appropriate the assets of 300 Paarflorinen under the pretext of an invalid bequest. The Count requests that the Kellers be granted what is due to them according to law and local custom.
en.sender: Hugo Graf zu Königsegg und Rottenfels, Lord of Aulendorf and Staufen, Imperial Councillor and Chamberlain
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen thank St. Gallen for its sympathetic declaration and again ask for help in their distress. They request that they be lent 2000 or 3000 gulden, so that the city does not perish and may continue to be useful to the Confederation. The help will be gratefully repaid.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Bishop Johann of Konstanz to intervene on behalf of their citizen Caspar Schöbinger. He says that he had reached an agreement with the heirs of Hinob of Lindau regarding a debt, but is being stubbornly pressed by them. The city requests the Bishop to order the heirs to desist from using coercive measures and to grant Schöbinger a period of two months until his brother and the bailiff return. Furthermore, the city asks for permission to pledge the estate of his brother Daniel Studer in order to cover the costs.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Johann, Bishop of Konstanz

en.regest: The appointed Distributors of the Christian Collection in the name of the churches and schoolteachers of the Principality of Zweibrücken thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the renewed generous aid of 175 Reichsthalers for the suffering churches in the Principality. They commend the donors to their prayer and wish them God's blessing.
en.sender: The appointed Distributors of the Christian Collection in the name of the churches and schoolteachers of the Principality of Zweibrücken
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ursula Magdalena Schenk, née Herrschlin, declares to the Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg that she wishes to renounce and forgive her citizenship there for herself and her children, as she remains in St. Gallen with her husband. She requests an authentic certificate of the release and permission to retain her inheritance there along with the Fiftieth.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg to release the St. Gallen woman Anna Magdalena Schlumpfin and her children from the citizenship of Nürnberg and to issue them a corresponding certificate. The wife of the St. Gallen citizen Jacob Schlumpf wishes to renounce the citizenship of her own free will, as she can no longer remain in Nürnberg. St. Gallen also asks that her property in Nürnberg be left to her undamaged.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report that, owing to the recent Baden farewell, they were unable to hold a conference on the coinage disorder before the year's accounts. They have appointed a committee to advise on countermeasures and ask St. Gallen to also communicate their thoughts in writing in order to find a joint solution.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Captain and Bailiff Johann Müller zu Reineck asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to cause the St. Gallen Samuel Messmer to participate in a legal dispute before the Landammann and Council of Glarus. Messmer has been asked to serve as a witness or party. Müller requests a written answer to the Glarus authority.
en.sender: Captain and Bailiff Johann Müller zu Reineck
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to attend the meeting in Baden on 25. Juni 1643 to deliberate on the improvement of the coinage. They refer to the recent Baden Diet and ask for the dispatch of a messenger so that the business may be dealt with at the upcoming Diet.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell inform the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the incursion of the Weimarers into the Confederation at Rheinau. They invite the neighboring cantons to a consultation the next morning at 9 o'clock in the council house. In a postscript, they state that Landammann Zellweger reported that it was not an incursion, but only a stay of four hours at the Rheinau monastery. They ask whether the conference should take place and offer themselves for day and night.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Heilbronn request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to notify the creditors of the late Burgomaster Conrad Spölin living in the city, including the Schlumpfischen and Zollikouerischen as well as the brothers Golder and Jörg Jattstein. They are to appear before the acting Burgomaster on 28 August at seven o'clock to settle the estate matters.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Council and Elders of the three reformed congregations of Frankenthal thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the voluntary tax of 300 gulden. They assure that the money will be used for the maintenance of the ministry, the churches and schools, as well as for the poor, and offer their services.
en.sender: The Council and Elders of the three congregations of Frankenthal
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Biberach ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel Anna Huthlerin, living in the city, to settle a debt of 12 gulden to the widow of the deceased citizen of Biberach Hans Stuelmeister or to present herself. In case of refusal, she is to be expelled from the city.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to allow Hans Heinrich Muggensturm to instruct the son of the deceased Burgomaster Christen Mürckhen in musical instruments. Muggensturm has declared himself willing to teach the boy for payment, but cannot do so without the approval of the gentlemen, as he is employed by them and has other journeymen. Stein am Rhein refers to the good services of the father and asks for this favor.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report that they have forbidden the Mailänder residing in the city, in the guildhall, and in the district from staying any longer, as the Evangelical Confederates could not obtain free passage in Mailand. They request St. Gallen to issue the same penalty in the spirit of unity, so that the goal may be achieved more quickly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Ausserrhoden report that the old butcher Michel Tobler owes 45 gulden to their countryman Hans Schüss. Schüss is pressing for immediate payment, which would cost Tobler his citizenship. Tobler has proposed an installment plan of 2 gulden per month. The Ausserrhoden ask St. Gallen to persuade Schüss to let the old man remain in the city and to accept the installments.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the evangelical congregation of Frauenfeld and the associated places in the Landgrafschaft Thurgau, which intends to build its own church, with a mild contribution. Zürich has already given 1000 gulden from municipal funds and asks for support, as the congregation is in need of help.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish the edict concerning the general court day appointed for the departed citizen of Schaffhausen, Martin Ziller. This is done so that the creditors of St. Gallen as well may register their claims and no one be disadvantaged by ignorance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Abbot Romanus of Kempten asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the citizen of St. Gallen Caspar Giger to pay out the 60 ducats that he had received from the widow of the former Kempten watchman Peter Kaessers to her proxy Christoph Jacob Schielvogt. Giger had sold the horses, which had been bought with the money, in St. Gallen and retained the proceeds.
en.sender: Romanus, Abbot of the Foundation of Kempten
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: David Kunz and Sylvester Hiller, as guardians of the widow of the deceased Martin Diller, ask Obervogt Heinrich Escher of Weinfelden to dismiss the claims of Salomon Hirzel and other creditors against the widow and her children regarding the farm Eppenstein. They argue that the farm belongs to the widow, not to the deceased, and that she resides in St. Gallen, where a legal case is already pending.
en.recipient: Heinrich Escher

en.regest: The Amtleute of the Sindtscelis Gemeinde inform the Amtsbürgermeister of St. Gallen that they will make the wine run for the current year, as provided for in the old contracts, for 12 pounds to the Lords of the City and the Linthal. They ask for God's blessing and thank for the good neighborhood.
en.recipient: Amtsbürgermeister zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss, Council and the Evangelical community of Frauenfeld thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the transfer of 760 gulden as a contribution to the construction of a church. They ask for the maintenance of the friendly neighborhood and promise to remember St. Gallen in their prayers.
en.sender: Schultheiss, Council and the Evangelical community of Frauenfeld
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Ludwig Graf zu Ysenburg und Büdingen reports on the damages that have been caused to him and his subjects by the war with Hessen-Darmstadt. He asks the St. Gallen for a voluntary collection for the repair and reconstruction of the reformed church in Offenbach, as he himself has no more means.
en.sender: Johann Ludwig Graf zu Ysenburg und Büdingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The letter contains only two address formulas to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, both of which are designated as St. Gallen. No further text content is present.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Wilhelm Otto, Count zu Ysenburg und Büdingen, acknowledges receipt of 200 gulden in Frankfurt currency from Matthias Heuden, Solmischer Hofverwalter zu Frankfurt. The money was paid for the Swiss collection for the repair of the Ysenburg churches. The Count declares Heuden free, clear, and discharged thereby.
en.sender: Wilhelm Otto, Count zu Ysenburg und Büdingen
en.recipient: Matthias Heuden, Solmischer Hofverwalter zu Frankfurt

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Wangen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish the edict regarding the appointed deadline for the credit debtors of the deceased citizen Josef Messerschmidt, so that the creditors can assert their claims and no one be injured in their rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Abbot Romanus of Kempten asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to pay out to the widow of the deceased Wachtmeister Peter Wiss the money entrusted to her, which is with the Wegmann Georg Wegmann. He refers to the statement of the citizen of Kempten Christoph Heuler and to the fact that the money is due to the widow. He asks that the widow not be held liable for the debts of the Wegmann.
en.sender: Romanus, Abbot of the Stift Kempten
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hoffmann and Council of Bernau im Rintal ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to exert influence on the citizen Barbara Indermüller there. She has left her husband, the craftsman Bartholomäus Indermüller, and settled in St. Gallen. She has become very unruly and dangerous there. The Bernau authorities ask that she be brought to reason or sent back to her home.
en.sender: Hoffmann and Council of Bernau im Rintal
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kaufbeuren ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen not to lay an arrest on their Burgomaster and other citizens on account of a claim of 400 gulden assigned to Joachim Künckler. They refer to the fact that the underlying debt had arisen between subjects of the Empire and had not been secured on Swiss territory. They demand a written assurance and recommend that Künckler assert his claim before the guardians in Ulm.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report that Bavarian troops under General Werth and Mourj are entrenched near Schaffhausen and that further troops are being mobilized in Bayern, Zell and Konstanz. They fear an attack on the Protestant cantons. Therefore, they invite a meeting of all Protestant cities and cantons on 5. Februar 1644 in Arbon to discuss common defense. They request St. Gallen to participate in the meeting through a Ratsschultheiss.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Sebastian Bilgeri Zweyer von Effebach, Obrist, forwards the imperial order of 20. January 1644 to the four cities of Zürich, Bern, Basel and Schaffhausen. The Emperor complains that the enemy purchases horses and grain in Switzerland at the upper border, which contradicts the obligations of the Confederates. He earnestly urges the cantons not to assist the enemy and to punish the offenders.
en.recipient: The four cities of Zürich, Bern, Basel and Schaffhausen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they will give their envoys the message of the imperial agent Sebastian Zwyer, directed to the four Evangelical cities, to take with them to the upcoming conference in Aarau, in order to consult on a counter-response there. They inform the St. Gallen of this in order to keep them informed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen reply to a letter of 12 January 1643. It concerns the succession to a life annuity, which after the death of the widow Maria Vorweiler falls to the next heirs of the deceased Jacob Scipels. Schaffhausen declares that according to their law, the next blood relatives at the time of the inheritance are entitled, not the next at the time of the death of the entitled person. They ask St. Gallen to help their citizens in this matter with goodwill.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Hans Jakob Oswald in the collection of a claim. Oswald says that he has inherited debts from the estate of his brother-in-law Jacob Zschender von Waldenstein, which he has registered in St. Gallen. Since the debtors did not pay, the Schaffhausen authorities request the St. Gallen authorities to support Oswald from the official side, so that he may be paid without great expense.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg reply to a letter of 25 April of the previous year concerning Anna Magdalena Schlumpf. They state that they have not yet been able to complete the settlement of the war and succession taxes payable by her. They ask St. Gallen to request that Frau Schlumpf finally declare what property she possesses in Nürnberg and in St. Gallen, so that the settlement can be carried out.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan of 600 to 800 gulden for three or four years against obligation and interest. The money is needed to conduct proceedings before the imperial Kammergericht, as the suspended parish priest Johann Rudolf Schadten, with the support of unruly citizens, has committed acts of violence. Kempten also refers to the fief of Hans Lienhart Schobinger.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Kempten request Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen for a loan of 100 ducats. They justify this with the necessity to send a qualified envoy to other Protestant estates to seek counsel and help in their disputes with the Austrian Schultheiss. Kempten commits to repaying the loan within two or three years with interest.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Kempten
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich recommend to the Council of St. Gallen Samuel Leucherius, who comes from Neustadt in der Pfalz and who has stayed in Zürich for three years. Leucherius wishes to return to his homeland and asks for Christian support. The Zürichers ask the St. Galleners to hold the evangelical exile in good recommendation and to grant him mild assistance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen transmit to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the Confederate treaty letter concerning the deductions, which was agreed upon in conferences in 1670. They ask that the letter be examined, sealed with the seal of St. Gallen, and that their own copy be forwarded to the Landvogt of the Appenzell Land for sealing.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: David Wegerlin, Statthalteramtsverweser, and the judges of the Hauptgericht in Kempten ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publish an enclosed edict. Therein, a debt court day is set for the deceased Burgomaster Melchior Schmölz. Creditors are to be given the opportunity to make claims against his estate.
en.sender: David Wegerlin, Statthalteramtsverweser, and the judges of the Hauptgericht in Kempten
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in the inheritance case of the deceased Jakob Seiler, to admit the Schaffhausen citizens Hans Felix Abegg, Hans Martin Wolf and Hans Hauser together with their co-sureties as heirs. They refer to the fact that the St. Gallen naturalized daughters of Huldrichin have already been admitted, and ask for an amicable settlement.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to attest a power of attorney granted by them for the debt collection by Daniel Seytz in the Augsttal. The debtors refuse payment, as the Memmingen seal is unknown to them. Memmingen asks St. Gallen to confirm under its seal that the power of attorney and the seal of the city of Memmingen are known, so that the creditors can collect their claims.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Emanuel Steiger, Landvogt of Löwen, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to interrogate the citizens there, Leonhard and Burkhard Schallen, as well as Stefan Hilli, regarding the attached questions. Captain Jakob Steiger, agent of the Confederates in Mailand, wishes to defend himself against the insults by Lieutenant Christoph Schmid and his family. The statements are to be sent to the Landvogt.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Wangen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to officially seize and hand over, at the expense of the city of Wangen, the 24 pieces of linen lying with the heirs of the deceased Hans Kitter in St. Gallen, which the Wangen citizen Martin Holl had sold to Leonhard Dissen in Leutkirch. The pieces are to be subjected to the White Inspection to check the quality. Wangen assumes the costs and holds the parties harmless.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform the Stadtpfarrer and Council of Bregenz about the case of the St. Gallen butcher Hans Appenzeller. He says that he bought a sick horse from Hans Horn of Leutkirch under the condition that he could keep it and return it upon request. Horn was imprisoned because of the sale. The St. Gallen ask Bregenz to interrogate Appenzeller and the witnesses to the purchase and to issue them credible documents.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Stadtpfarrer and Council of Bregenz

en.regest: Johann Ludwig Graf zu Ysenburg und Büdingen asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help him with a voluntary collection and building tax for the restoration of the Reformed church in Offenbach. He refers to the poor condition of the church after the war and the dire straits of his county.
en.sender: Johann Ludwig Graf zu Ysenburg und Büdingen
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Appenzellers. They ask Landammann and Council of Appenzell to make their Landsknechte Othmar Tobler and Bernhard Daubenmann, who have a new court day on 14 or 24 May because of a dispute, unencumbered for this term and to attend it. In return, they offer similar services.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg remind St. Gallen of their earlier letters regarding the imprisonment of their Burgomaster Johann Walter Jung. He had been imprisoned because of a claim by the guardians of Hans Jürg Miller in Ulm against the Ravensburg citizen Joachim Runkher for 400 gulden. Since St. Gallen had given no answer, the Ravensburgers had to discontinue their trade relations. They request St. Gallen for a compliant decision, so that trade not be disturbed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen not to interpret the absence of the Appenzell countrymen Thomas Döbler and Bernhard Stübermann on 16 May at the legal proceedings concerning a committed outrage as a sign of ill will. They were obliged to attend the annual procession to Marbach on the same day. They request a new date.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Landvogt Johann Müller to protect the St. Gallen citizen Johannes Merz, shoemaker. Merz was attacked and threatened by a man from Zuckenriet between Rorschach and the Kluse. The city recommends Merz and his companion, the Council treasurer Sylvester Hiller, to the Landvogt and asks that the attacker be instructed to leave Merz in peace in the future.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Johann Müller, Landvogt of Rheineck and Upper Rhine Valley

en.regest: Georg Frölich, citizen in Floß, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a letter of intercession to the local authority there. He refers to a power of attorney for cession granted to his deceased father Johann Frölich in 1637 in Pleß, in order to assert an inheritance claim from the estate of the grandfather Jacob Gmünder in St. Gallen. Frölich intends to settle the claim personally and asks for support so that the inheritance be delivered without delay.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Duke of Schlesien requests the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist his subject Georg Fröhlich, a citizen in Pless, in the redemption of an inheritance in St. Gallen. This inheritance had been ceded by Christoph Gmünder to Fröhlich's deceased father Hans Fröhlich. The Duke asks for swift processing, as Fröhlich cannot be absent for long due to the difficult situation in Schlesien and the great distance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Ples request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their fellow citizen Georg Frölich in Floß. The latter claims an inheritance that had been judicially assigned to his deceased father by Christoph Gmünder. The Pleser request that Frölich be given what is his right without delay, so that he may set out on his journey.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Ples
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Joh Kemniz requests the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, on behalf of his subject George Froelich, citizen in Pleß, for the rapid settlement of an inheritance in St. Gallen. This inheritance had been ceded by Christoph Gmündern to the deceased father of Froelich. Kemniz asks for prompt completion so that Froelich may soon end his journey to St. Gallen, as time is pressing in Silesia and in his lordship.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to lift the arrest issued against their Burgomaster Johann Valler Jung and other citizens on account of a debt of the innkeeper at the Geist. Kempten is only responsible for the city's liabilities and offers the creditor annual installments of 100 florins without interest. Otherwise, Kempten will proceed with the same right regarding claims held by the citizens of St. Gallen in Kempten and other Imperial cities, which hinders trade.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to seek out their serf Hans Kochen von Geißlingen, who works for Salomon Zincken in St. Gallen. They ask that he be ordered to proceed immediately to Ulm to clarify the matter concerning the daughter of the goldsmith Matthäus Hochreiter, and that he not be allowed to work in St. Gallen any longer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jakob Langhans in Bern presents to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen a short summary of the history of the sword fight before Neuenegg, which he has compiled from the year book of the monastery of Königsfelden. He asks for the acceptance of the dedication and for a reply, which he would like to receive through the Professor of Zürich Johann Rudolf Stucki.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from Schaffhausen regarding the debt claim of the St. Gallen citizen Joachim Künckler, innkeeper at the Hecht. They forward Künckler's reply, in which he declares himself willing to settle the claim to Kaufbeuren in annual installments of 500 gulden without interest, and ask Schaffhausen to convey this offer to Kaufbeuren.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Landammann and Council of Appenzell that the prisoner Daniel Zollikofer and his wife have escaped from St. Gallen custody. They ask the Appenzell authorities to arrest the two, at the expense of St. Gallen, if they stay in the Appenzell land, and to notify St. Gallen of this.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen request Landammann and Council of the Land Appenzell to detain, on the costs of St. Gallen, by official arrest, Daniel Zollikoffer, who fled from their captivity on Sunday, and his wife, if they should be found in their land, and to notify them thereof.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Land Appenzell

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Arbon request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to lift the arrest imposed on the Jew Hirtzlin living in Arbon. Hirtzlin had been imprisoned in a dispute over a clock and a debt to citizens of St. Gallen. Arbon refers to existing treaties between the cities and requests that the citizens of St. Gallen be instructed to assert their claims in Arbon, where justice shall be done to the Jew.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Council and Elders of the three communities of Frankenthal thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the voluntary tax of 400 gulden received. They promise to use the money for the maintenance of the ministry, the churches and schools, as well as for the poor, and ask for forgiveness for the late sending of the letter of thanks.
en.sender: The Council and Elders of the three communities of Frankenthal
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council in the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their citizen Jakob Züblin to appear on 8 August at eight o'clock in the morning at the Holz at Obloch to settle a boundary dispute with Appenzell countrymen. They request that Züblin bring his documents and that the St. Gallen Burgomaster Weggen be present.
en.sender: Landammann and Council in the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landammann and Council of the County of Toggenburg to present the local man Bartholomäus Studach, who is said to have impregnated a citizen of St. Gallen out of wedlock, at the house of the Sunder in St. Gallen on the coming Monday at two o'clock. They demand that he justify himself against the accusation and have the child baptized.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the County of Toggenburg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landammann and Council of Ausserrhoden Appenzell to summon Bartholomäus Sonderegger, called Berlihan, to appear at a specific place in Linsebühl. He has impregnated the St. Gallen woman Katharina Heinimännin and fathered a child. Sonderegger is to baptize, acknowledge, and maintain the child. If he does not appear, the child will be buried in St. Gallen.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the City of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Ausserrhoden Appenzell

en.regest: Bishop Johann of Konstanz asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the creditors of the bankrupt Zollikhofer to refrain from their claim against Georg Guldinger. Guldinger, son of the widow Barbara Bischoffin, says that he had only been a servant and not a partner. The Bishop refers to the lack of evidence and asks for the acquittal of Guldinger as well as for the release of his seized movable property.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Richter und Rechtsprecher des Ehegerichts der Stadt Bern request the Burgomaster and Ammeisteren of the Chorgericht of the city of St. Gallen to summon the nail-maker and cutler Johann Stark, who is staying there, to appear before the Bern Marriage Court. The citizen of that city, Margarete Steiner, has filed a lawsuit against him regarding a marriage promise that he broke after he had left without being summoned.
en.sender: Richter und Rechtsprecher des Ehegerichts der Stadt Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Ammeisteren of the Chorgericht of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau report that they received a letter from E. Fst. dated the 17th of this month regarding the debt claim of the Lindau citizen Ulrich Loher against Lorenz Zilli or his estate. As they had no further information, they had informed Loher of the matter. He had handed them a written report on the 25th of this month. As they did not know what Zilli had conceded or denied to Loher, they could not commit to a position. They send the report to St. Gallen for information.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Graflicher Rat zu Hohenems confirms the receipt of a letter of the 12th of this month, which concerns an arrest imposed by Ammann Hans Schneider in Höchst or Füßach at the instigation of the Lindau citizen Ulrich Cäsers. Since the Ammann is subject to the Herrschaft Feldkirch, the Council refers the matter to the Graf von Hohenems as Vogt. He assures that the Graf will issue the necessary order to the Ammann.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant the community of Zurzach in the County of Baden financial support for the construction of a new parish and schoolhouse. Zurzach has no own funds and the community members are heavily burdened. Zürich has already approved 300 pounds and requests similar support from St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kaufbeuren thank for the offer to settle the 400-florin debt of the innkeeper Joachim Künckler in Ulm. They ask for a postponement because of war costs and debts. They instruct Künckler to pay 100 florins each on St. George's Day 1645 without interest, until the sum is settled. Künckler is to name a proxy who pays against receipt.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich report to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen on the conference in Frauenfeld with the five Catholic cantons. These had not considered the responsibility of the Zürichers for the church building in Utzwillen sufficient and had threatened further steps. Zürich declares that in the case of acts of violence against the evangelical subjects it must take up defense, and asks St. Gallen for support from the Confederates.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The community of the French church in Biberwier asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a voluntary donation for the maintenance of the pastor. The community has newly come into being under the leadership of Duke Christian von Burckenfels after a long dispersion. The Duchess and the brothers in Straßburg have already contributed to the rebuilding of the church. The long wars have plunged the community into poverty.
en.sender: Community of the French church in Biberwier
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Magdalene Katharina, Pfalzgräfin, asks the Burgomaster and Senators of the city and canton of St. Gallen to grant the subjects of the church in Bischöfliches a support for the maintenance of her minister, as they might otherwise fall into an even worse dispersion. She assures that this help will be well used, and asks for an answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Senators of the city and canton of St. Gallen

en.regest: Andreas Hindler von Glarus, Landvogt of the County of Werdenberg, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send a young man, who had stolen as a vagabond and was in his custody, to his castle Werdenberg. He says that he has received this order from his lords in Glarus.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of the city of Arbon reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen, which concerns the initiation of a legal dispute between the Arbon citizen Heitzlin Jud and the St. Gallen citizens Hans Martin Schobinger and Daniel Studer. Arbon orders the Jew to answer to the St. Gallen court and asks for the continuation of the proceedings in St. Gallen.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the city of Arbon
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to inquire in the hospital there how long Barbara Klandin, who served there, the wife of Matthäus Burgauer, a citizen of Lindau banished years ago, has conducted herself, whether her husband was with her, and how they have supported themselves. The couple recently returned to Lindau.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Schwyz thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the friendly reception of their envoys Caspar Küchli and Johann Heinrich Elmer in Altstätten. They praise the costly hospitality and gifts for the envoys and their servants. They offer their help in all matters.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Landammann and Council in the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to show mercy to their imprisoned Master Bernhart Högger and to spare him from captivity. Högger committed a breach of the peace after the damage to his daughter, but claims that the Brülischi did not adhere to the judgment. Högger wishes to do penance and submit to his authority.
en.sender: Landammann and Council in the outer Roden of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to a request from the Ausserrhoden regarding the disobedient citizen Leonhard Hegger. They state that they had previously offered clemency if Hegger would submit. Since he had remained disobedient despite admonitions, they ask the Ausserrhoden to admonish him to better behavior. Should he continue to remain disobedient, St. Gallen will employ other means.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Ausserrhoden of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter of 17 July. They communicate that their tin caster reported that from 100 pounds of the best Schlaggenwald tin, no more than 25 pounds of lead would be obtained. The reward per hundredweight amounts to 40 pounds, without wages for labor. They ask for neighborly services.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Wil

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the city of Augsburg to support their citizen Zacharias Rohn Wagner, who is engaged to the Augsburg woman Maria Walchhüsier. They request that the fiancée, together with her parents and her property, which is under bailiwick, along with a certificate of her birth and origin, be allowed to return to St. Gallen.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Guardians, Burgomasters and Council of Augsburg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg to release Anna Magdalena Schlumpfin, née Schwäbin, from their citizenship there and to accept the renunciation through her proxy Hans Schlumpf the Elder. They also ask for the payment of the inheritance still lying in the Lösungsstube, together with interest, since the woman cannot appear in person.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the honourable envoys of the eight cantons governing the Rhine Valley, who are holding a diet in Baden, to intercede for their executioner Lorenz Kunz. Kunz, as a judge in the Rhine Valley, earned 160 florins 40 kreuzer, of which 50 are owed to him by the former Landvogt and the rest by the new Landvogt. He has not yet received any payment and asks for superior assistance so that he may receive his wages.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Honourable envoys of the eight cantons governing the Rhine Valley in Baden

en.regest: Johann Kuoß, citizen and resident of St. Gallen, thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for their intercession. He asks them to approach the abbot so that the latter will repay him the 50 thaler that he had to pay as a fine for the mill Stolligen. Kuoß points out that the money is due to him and asks for a friendly reply.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that the envoys of the Evangelical cantons of the Confederation have decided at the Baden Diet to set a general day of fasting and prayer on Sunday Reminiscere, March 2. They ask St. Gallen to observe this day in a spirit of religious fellowship and hope for God's blessing and peace in the fatherland.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The chancery of the city of Konstanz informs Konrad Ziegler of St. Gallen that the city court has decided the case against Andreas Schmidt in his absence. Ziegler has been ordered to pay the counterclaim together with costs and damages.
en.sender: Chancery of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Konrad Ziegler of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the authority of Überlingen to assist their citizens Michel Reutmann and Hans Müller in the collection of a debt of 274 florins against the Überlingen citizen Hans Zubrin Meyer. A judgment ordering payment or an assessment already exists, but has not yet been executed. The St. Gallen authorities ask for official support to force the debtors to pay.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Administrator of the Burgomaster's Office, Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen

en.regest: Paulus Staeger reports that, on the order of the communities of Meyenfeld and Fläsch, he has rebuilt the burned inn on the Sankt-Lucis-Steig. He now plans to rebuild the also burned Sankt-Lucis-Kirche with the help of donations in order to make the Protestant service there possible again. He asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a Christian contribution and tax for this work.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Speyer ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the local Captain Daniel Studer von Rebstein to pay the 300 Reichstaler that his son, the Cornet Johann Jacob Studer, owes to the Speyer innkeeper Hans Maurer for provisions and medical treatment during an illness. Speyer refers to the innkeeper's dire straits and asks for swift assistance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post and publish the edict concerning the general court day appointed for their citizen Hans Adam Pfister, called Kreidenmann, according to their custom. This is done so that no one shall be deprived of their rights and so that no one can plead ignorance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Secret Council of Lindau request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to realize the pledge of the estate of the widow of the deceased Burgomaster of Lindau, Jacob Bensperg, with Albrecht Thomas Calß in St. Gallen. The Vögte of the widow and children ask for the support of Lindau, as the creditor threatens with coercive measures. Lindau considers the realization fair and requests St. Gallen to have this carried out according to the custom of the city.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Secret Council of Lindau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann-Nicolaus Zimmermann von Spennheim, Rector of the Palatine Pädagogium in Kreuznach, thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the transfer of twenty Reichsthalers. He reports that without this aid he would have had to give up his position, and asks for prayers for the city and its lords.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the request of the authorities of Speyer to persuade the St. Gallen captain Daniel Studer to pay 600 Reichsthaler for his delinquent son Hans Jakob. They reject the claim, as the statutes provide that a father is not liable for a delinquent son, and Studer has already complained about his son's behavior.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Speyer

en.regest: Burgomaster, Council and citizenry of Neuhäusen report that the Bavarian army on 7 October 1644 plundered their city, drove out the inhabitants and demolished the buildings. They ask the St. Gallen authorities for Christian help and aid to procure food and clothing for the impoverished families.
en.sender: Burgomaster, Council and citizenry of Neuhäusen
en.recipient: Kirchendiener, Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Basel request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to issue an attestation to the citizens of St. Gallen, the widow of Robert Mitz, Franz Braunweiler, and Daniel Mitz. The applicants had turned to Basel with a supplication to obtain this confirmation. Basel considers the statements credible and asks St. Gallen to grant the applicants the attestation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich recommend the evangelical co-religionists of Degerschen, who wish to establish a diaconate and a schoolmaster's position, to the Council of St. Gallen. They ask for generous support, as the means of the community are insufficient. Zürich refers to the previous donations of St. Gallen to co-religionists and the joint possessions in the region.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to officially compel their citizen Konrad Ziegler to pay the 8 florins awarded to the supplicant Andreas Schmidt von Stecklingen by the Konstanz city court without further delay.
en.sender: Administrator of the Hauptmann's Office, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Statthalter and Council of Schaffhausen transmit to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen two enclosures as well as the testament of Melchior Güldin, which his widow Elisabeth Eberhartin, née Güldin, has received from Amsterdam. They ask that the document be communicated to the bailiff Diethelm Hegner, so that he can inform himself about the inheritance of his brother Heinrich Güldin. Furthermore, they report that the widow Isaac Hattevier has authorized in Amsterdam to lift the arrest placed by Erasmus Schlumpf in Amsterdam on the Güldin properties and to collect the share of the inheritance. Schaffhausen will also send copies to the guardians of the children of Hans Joachim Güldin living in Bern.
en.sender: Statthalter and Council of the city of Schaffhausen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The citizens of St. Gallen, the widow of the late Robert Mitz, Franz Brunsweiler and Daniel Mitz, ask E. G. St. F. E. W. once again to request the city of St. Gallen in the name of the Confederation to issue a written attestation. This is to confirm that the heirs of the deceased Caspar Schlumpf in the bankruptcy of Schlumpf and Zollikofen are no longer creditors and that all creditors of St. Gallen had accepted the settlement signed by twelve gentlemen.
en.sender: the widow of the late Robert Mitz, Franz Brunsweiler and Daniel Mitz
en.recipient: E. G. St. F. E. W.

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Basel remind Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen of their request of 24 May 1645. They ask again to grant the desired attestation to the widows and heirs of Robert Mitzen, Franz Deinhusen and Daniel Mitzen, in order to expedite their trade matters.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Basel
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Kempten ask Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen for a contribution of 1000 gulden for the costs of an imperial commission, which was appointed to settle the unrest in Kempten caused by Johann and Christoph Künoch. Kempten promises to repay the loan with interest, and asks for a reply.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Kempten
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Friedrich, Pfalzgraf bei Rhein, asks the Burgomaster, Schultheiss and Council of the cities of Zürich, Bern and St. Gallen for help for his Kirchenschaffner Friedrich Adam Schwebell. He says that he has become impoverished through billeting during the war and can no longer support his two sons in their studies. The Pfalzgraf himself cannot provide help and requests the Confederates for supportive assistance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster, Schultheiss and Council of the cities of Zürich, Bern and St. Gallen

en.regest: The Obrister and Ratshauptmann, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information on meat prices. They want to lower the price of veal and beef, but the butchers resist. Konstanz wishes to know how high the prices are in St. Gallen, whether heads, feet, and offal are weighed together, and how heavy the pound of meat is.
en.sender: The Obrister and Ratshauptmann, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen Elsbetha Stockerin, née Ruedin. The citizen of St. Gallen Erasmus Schlumpf is maintaining an arrest, although he should have asserted his claims against the deceased father of Elsbetha. Elsbetha is the heir of her brother Georg Ruedin, who died in Amsterdam, and she left the inheritance to the father. Schaffhausen requests St. Gallen to urge Schlumpf to desist from the arrest and to hand over Elsbetha's property to her.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen and former advisor Zundowen in the collection of a claim against the Schobinger brothers in Wil. Zundowen has a claim of 168 Kronen, of which 78 have already been paid. Since Lorentz Schobinger died without children, Zundowen asks to move the heirs or the brother Hans Melchior to pay the remaining 90 Kronen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen refer to their letter of 3 June 1645 concerning the estate of the deceased glassmaker Melchior Wüldin. Since the heirs of Caspar Schlumpf lift the arrest against the estate, the St. Gallen authorities ask Amsterdam to deliver the estate to St. Gallen. Wüldin had been a citizen of St. Gallen until his death, his son is the lawful heir, which is why the inheritance is to be decided in St. Gallen.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss, Burgomaster and Council of Amsterdam

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Council of Zürich dated 2 August 1645. It concerns a claim by the citizen of Zürich David Kunz, the guardian of the children of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Lorenz Schobinger, against the heirs of the citizen of Zürich zum Storchen. St. Gallen points out that the children of Schobinger need not be liable for his debts. They ask Zürich to calm down their own citizen and to leave the children in peace. In a postscript, reference is made to a letter dated 13 August 1645 concerning the creditors of the Werdmüller family.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich communicate that Elector Friedrich von der Pfalz has intervened with them to obtain a stipend for the son of the churchwarden and Neukastellan Friedrich Adam Schwäbeli. Zürich declares itself willing, out of religious affinity, to contribute 20 gulden annually, and asks St. Gallen for its opinion on this request.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen confirm the receipt of a letter of 23. August, in which Elector Friedrich von der Pfalz asks for support for the parish priest Friedrich Adam Schwebel and his sons. They remit 15 ducats from the town treasury to the parish priest and ask the Elector to hand these over to the recipient and to obtain a receipt.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Elector Friedrich von der Pfalz

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to examine Theophil Lützelbulher residing there and his wife. The background is a dispute between the citizens of Winterthur Lorenz Goldschmidt and Hans Rudolf Schöller. Schöller claims that Lützelbulher ordered him to deliver goods to Goldschmidt. However, Lützelbulher demands more money than Schöller received. Winterthur asks for written communication of the statements.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
