en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz thank St. Gallen for the communication of the local meat prices. They in turn send their own meat ordinance and ask for mutual observance.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The parish priests of the Hanau district ask the church leadership of St. Gallen again for financial support. They refer to the fact that they had sought help a year ago but had received neither money nor an answer. They describe their extreme distress caused by the wars and earnestly ask for assistance.
en.sender: Parish priests of the Hanau district (Friedrich Schlemmer, Johannes Cressius, Johannes Antonius Riccius)
en.recipient: Antistites and Presbyters of the Church of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Jakob Stocker, former Landvogt and State Secretary, thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the payment of 100 gulden. This sum was assigned to him as compensation for his trouble in the chapel and gold negotiation. He assures his further willingness to serve and commends himself to the grace of the city.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Ludwig Philipp, Count Palatine of the Rhine, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the city of Kreuznach, which is heavily burdened by the war. He recommends the city and its citizens and asks for a voluntary tax or contribution so that the inhabitants can better bear their burdens and do not have to leave the city.
en.sender: Ludwig Philipp, Count Palatine of the Rhine, Duke in Bayern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Mindelheim ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their fellow citizen Gregorius Castol, who was damaged by spoliation and costs, in his claim against the Herren Zilller and co-relatives. They hope that Castol will be left with his offer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The officials of the Rinthelischen Gemeinden report to Amtsbürgermeister David Hildbrand that they had not reached an agreement in St. Gallen on the previous Tuesday because of the Weinausschlag. The Rinthelischen Gemeinden had agreed to give the St. Gallen citizens 16 denars, provided that the delegates do not challenge the assessment. They ask Hildbrand to grant the Gemeinwein the next day, and assure him that this is done according to old custom.
en.recipient: David Hildbrand, Amtsbürgermeister of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to release their citizen's daughter Katharina Schwyzers, who is imprisoned for disloyalty towards her uncle. The father Hans Jörg Schwyzers assures that he will provide for her in the future so that no further disadvantage arises for anyone. Zürich requests that the proceedings be conducted according to mercy and not according to strictness.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the petition of the city of Zürich of 18 October 1645 for the imprisoned citizen Hans Jörg Schreiber and his daughter Katharina. They state that the matter has not yet been clarified, as the person who is supposed to have taken the money was only arrested on the same day. Both prisoners must be questioned in order to find out the truth and to help the damaged citizen of St. Gallen. They promise to consult and report at the next opportunity.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the Lords Preachers of the Reformed Evangelical Religion in the City and County of Hanau to grant them, out of Christian compassion, 300 gulden in Frankfurt currency for a tax and contribution. They ask that the money be paid out through the pastors Friedrich Schlemmer in Kesselstatt, Johann Crefsio in Hochstadt, and Johann Anton Hiccio in Bruchköbel, and that a signed account be sent back.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Lords Preachers of the Reformed Evangelical Religion in the City and County of Hanau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to Burgomaster and Council of Zürich on the case of the imprisoned daughter of the St. Gallen citizen Hans Jörg Scheibler. The person who is supposed to have confessed to the attack on the Scheiblerin, despite interrogation and the Sevenfold Inquiry, has not confessed to being guilty. Since no further findings are available, the Scheiblerin must remain in custody until the truth comes to light.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen transmit to Burgomaster and Council of Basel the requested attestation. This confirms that the heirs of the deceased Caspar Schlumpf do not appear as creditors in the bankruptcy of Schlumpf and Zollikoffer and are also not included in the accord of 23. August 1644. The heirs were paid in Botzheim. The St. Gallen ask that the delay in sending not be taken amiss.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Basel

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern ask the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen to prevent their citizen Erasmus Schlumpf from imposing an arrest against the heirs of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen Joachim Güldin in Amsterdam. They refer to the contracts of the Confederation, according to which disputes are to be adjudicated at the residence of the defendant. Bern offers to deposit the inheritance goods in Zürich until the matter is judicially clarified.
en.sender: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The pastors and widows of the Duchy of Braunschweig-Lüneburg thank the Council of St. Gallen for the donation of 200 Reichsthalers delivered on 7 September 1645 by the citizen of Frankfurt Johann de Fay. They ask the Council to encourage the brothers of the churches of Schaffhausen to further works of Christian love and support.
en.sender: Pastors and widows of the Duchy of Braunschweig-Lüneburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen remind St. Gallen of their request of 25 July 1645 to lift the arrest issued by Erasmus Schlumpf against the widow Elisabeth Störckharter, née Sulzer. They refer to the fact that Bern had also demanded this and that the arrest contradicts the Confederates' pünden. As the widow is ill and dependent on the inheritance, they request again that the lifting of the arrest and the handover of the inheritance share be ordered.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The impoverished exiles from the Oberpfalz ask the clergy of St. Gallen to forward their petition to the Council and to advocate for it publicly. They ask for a favorable recommendation and for renewed support through a collection, as their distress continues. They enclose a list of the previous recipients of the St. Gallen collection.
en.recipient: Reverendi, Clarissimi, Doctissimique Viri (parsons and clergy of St. Gallen)

en.regest: Upper Palatine exiles in Nürnberg ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for renewed financial support, as they have fallen into extreme distress due to the long exile and the cessation of previous collections. They promise to distribute the donations fairly and to render an account thereof. Attached is a receipt for 100 Reichstaler, which the Council of St. Gallen had already contributed.
en.sender: Upper Palatine exiles (Jonas Liebing, Michael Castner, Wolfgang Francus Amberg)
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jacob Welcker, a citizen delegated by the city of Kreuznach, introduces himself to the Lords Burgomasters and several members of the Council of the city of St. Gallen. He hands over a letter from Elector Ludwig Philipp and asks, in the name of the city of Kreuznach, which is suffering from the burdens of war, for Christian aid. Since the Council is not fully assembled, they cannot make a decision. They promise to think of Kreuznach after their own business is concluded and to transmit the aid through the merchants Peter and Hans Conrad Fess and Brothers, who are resident in Frankfurt.
en.sender: Chancery of the city of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Jacob Welcker

en.regest: Georg Spindler and Daniel Kuntz report on the journey of the envoys to Schaffhausen. There, they say that on Friday before the impartial Council, an unfavorable judgment was handed down to them, which they could not appeal. They say that they returned to Zürich on Saturday evening. Spindler and Kuntz ask for further instructions and refer to the attached copy of the judgment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Council of Kreuznach informs the Burgomasters of Weil about an approved tax and contribution of 300 gulden, which was granted at the request of Count Palatine Ludwig Philipp. The Burgomasters are to enter the amount in the appropriate place and obtain the remainder for the currency fulfillment from the Seckelmeister.
en.recipient: Burgomasters of Weil

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Chur recommend their citizen Jacob Schmidt, who, as the nephew of the deceased woman of St. Gallen Wybli Schlappritzin, claims an inheritance share of 1500 florins that was withheld from him by a testament. They ask St. Gallen to treat the old and poor man paternally and to award him his rightful share according to the inheritance law of St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hoffmann and Council of Thalheim ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen not to sell the vines and properties, which were pledged to them from the inheritance of the deceased Lucia Schobel and which lie in their farm Thalheim. They offer to lease, cultivate, and issue the lease for the properties, and ask for a friendly reply.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jakob Hannibal Graf von Hohenems, Gallarata und Vaduz informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he is sending them a piece of game from his game park. He recalls a stag that the Obrist Truchsäss in Lindau had ceded to the citizens of St. Gallen, and offers to supply them with another piece of game in the spring or autumn.
en.sender: Jakob Hannibal Graf von Hohenems, Gallarata und Vaduz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Frankfurt reply to a letter of 26 January, in which St. Gallen had appealed against a threatened seizure of goods by the Generalmajor and Governor of Breisach, von Erlach. Frankfurt declares that it will not permit any arrest on goods of St. Gallen, neither on account of the free commercial rights nor on account of the dangerous consequences. It expects at the same time that St. Gallen will not prevent the creditors of St. Gallen in the said bankruptcy cases from enforcing their rights.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask their Confederates in St. Gallen to treat the imprisoned Katharina Schwytzerin, daughter of the citizen of Zürich Hans Jörg Schwytzer, leniently. They request that she be spared public disgrace and not punished severely, as her parents had humbly requested this.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Kempten request Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen for a neighborly aid of 2000 gulden. They refer to the high costs of the imperial commission for the settlement of their internal unrest and to an earlier promise of St. Gallen to assist in case of emergency. The envoys Jacob Stettmüller, Tobias Königen, Caspar Zollern and Hans Wepplin are to be heard. Kempten promises repayment with interest and a commitment of the city and guilds.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Kempten
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank the French ambassador for his recovery from a serious illness. They also thank him for his mediation, which led to the release of their envoys from the fortress of Hohentwiel. They ask him to continue to take the city under his protection.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Jacob Le Fevre, Lord of Caumartin, French ambassador

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to use their influence so that the St. Gallen Gordian Zollikoffer repays 60 Reichsthaler to the deceased Ulm butcher Hans Jacob Lützelmann. The amount is due according to the obligation and should be paid out to the creditors pro rata.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jonas Liebing, Michael Castner and Wolfgang Heinrich Salmuth thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the donation of 100 Reichsthaler to the exiles. They present an account of the distribution of 150 Reichsthaler to pastors, schoolmasters, widows, orphans and other needy persons. They ask for further support and assure that the funds were used for their intended purpose.
en.sender: Jonas Liebing, Michael Castner und Wolfgang Heinrich Salmuth
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Bregenz thank St. Gallen for the support through a delegated co-councillor. They ask for a loan of 1000 gulden in order to send an envoy to the Imperial court, who is to present the negotiations of the Imperial commission and their own defense. This serves the restoration of peace. Bregenz offers interest and obligation.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council, together with the dependents of the court and community of the city of Bregenz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Burgomaster and Council of Zürich about the case of the woman of Zürich, Katharina Schirmerin, who was detained in St. Gallen for theft. They report that, after interrogation and torture, Schirmerin named a Bernese carpenter's apprentice as an accomplice. Despite the serious offense and the false accusation of an innocent woman, they refrained from a harsher punishment at the request of the parents and because of the friendship of the Confederates. Schirmerin was released from custody and handed over to her mother, with the condition that she be kept under guard in the future.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Miners and parishioners of St. Luzi on the Steig ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a generous donation of 72 gulden for the construction of the St. Luzi church. They thank them in advance and wish the city peace, pious government, and blessing.
en.sender: Miners and parishioners of St. Luzi on the Steig
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss, Burgomaster and Council of Kreuznach thank St. Gallen for the granted audience and the intercession for their delegate Jacob Waldern. They explain that they are forced to take such steps only out of the greatest necessity, and wish St. Gallen good fortune and protection from similar conditions.
en.sender: Schultheiss, Burgomaster and Council of Kreuznach
en.recipient: Schultheiss, Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jacob Waelter, citizen of Augsburg, confirms that he received 300 gulden in Frankfurt from Herr Eltzen, Hans Conrad Eltzen and brothers on behalf of the Council of the city of St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Caumartin asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to treat Burgomaster Ziegler and his sons well in their affairs, as they have fallen into ruinous dealings due to the bad credit of foreign people. He regrets the renewed anger between the family of Erlach and some residents of St. Gallen and asks that the matter be settled amicably, so that the innocent do not have to suffer with the guilty. He promises, in the name of the King, to support them in all occurrences.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Bern request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct the heirs of the deceased Caspar Schlumpf to lift the arrest placed in Amsterdam against the estate of the citizen of that city, Johann Joachim Guldin. Bern refers to the fact that the deceased Melchior Guldin renounced the citizenship of St. Gallen and that the heirs reside in Bern. Bern rejects reprisals and expects a reply.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to participate in the conference of the Evangelical cantons taking place in Aarau on 28 April. This was convened on the occasion of a conference in Baden regarding the still unresolved Turgau affair. They request St. Gallen to appear through an authorized embassy in order to jointly deliberate on the promotion of the Evangelium and the commonwealth.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen forward a request from Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz to St. Gallen. Konstanz proposes that the cities of St. Gallen, Schaffhausen, Zürich, Winterthur, Stein and Frauenfeld meet for a neighborhood gathering to discuss the taxation and pricing of meat. Schaffhausen asks St. Gallen whether it considers this gathering appropriate and requests a reply.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the town of Buchs thank for the answer of 8 September and again request a loan of 1000 gulden. They refer to their difficult situation and the necessity of a delegation to the Imperial Diet. They assure that they will secure the loan by sufficient obligation and compensate as far as possible.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the town of Buchs
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the town of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that a request for support regarding their dire situation has reached them from the evangelical church and school ministers in the Palatinate. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to instruct their envoys for the upcoming Augsburg Conference accordingly, so that they can reach an understanding of the situation there and support those affected.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Council of Bern dated 4 October 1645 concerning the estate of the deceased Melchior Wildi. They state that they have informed the heirs of Caspar Schlempfen, who have substantiated their claim in writing. Since Wildi never formally renounced his citizenship in St. Gallen and his son was born there, they ask Bern to allow the inheritance to devolve to St. Gallen and to have the Schlempf debt claim discussed there. They offer to lift the arrest established in Amsterdam if Bern takes the matter upon itself, and ask Bern to support their citizens in this affair.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Bern

en.regest: Lefevre Caumartin confirms to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the receipt of Herr Studer, who had delivered them a commission. He declares his willingness to serve to the best of his ability in the discussed matters and refers for the rest to the report of Studers.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern thank the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen for the friendly explanation regarding the claims of the Schlumpf heirs to the inheritance of the widow of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen, Joachim Guldin, in Amsterdam. They request that the lifting of the arrest there actually be carried out and a certified certificate thereof be issued, so that the Guldin widow can claim the inheritance. In return, they offer to settle claims of the Bernese against the citizens of St. Gallen amicably or through swift justice.
en.sender: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Bern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen hand over to Elector Maximilian the supplication of their citizen Hans Bartholomäus Schober and ask him to continue to help the petitioner in the matter. They refer to grace already shown and request support in the reimbursement of the costs incurred, the interest on delay, and the conceded harmful Ämter, so that the citizen does not fall into further pledge.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Maximilian, Elector of the Palatinate

en.regest: Johann Bartholomä Schobinger, citizen and Ammann of St. Gallen, asks the Council for renewed intercession with the Elector of Bayern. The guardians of the heirs of the deceased Ott Heinrich Schobinger, despite electoral decrees and mandates, had refused the agreed payment of 300 gulden annually and had sold the pledged house in the Rosengasse without paying the proceeds to Schobinger. He demands the payment of the principal sum, the interest, and the costs incurred.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the citizens there, Alexander Ziegler and David Peyer. Three weeks ago, they had sent ducats to St. Gallen, which were not allowed to be spent there as foreign currency. The citizens of St. Gallen, Schlaepfer and Studer, refused to return them, although they themselves spent foreign coins. Schaffhausen requests that the ducats be handed over immediately to Peyer, who is staying in St. Gallen for this purpose.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Council of Zürich. The latter had reported that new tin castings, which did not have the proper hold, came from citizens of St. Gallen, and had requested an inquiry. St. Gallen had detained the citizen of St. Gallen Alexander Ziegler and the servant Jacob Schlaprizi to clarify the matter. However, since Schaffhausen had interceded, the two had been released again. St. Gallen assures that its citizens will no longer bring such tin castings into the country in the future.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform the Schultheiss and Council of Luzern about the ongoing disputes with Schaffhausen over a debt transport of the Ziegler. Despite a Schaffhausen judgment that obligated the Ziegler to withdraw the transport, it had not been executed. St. Gallen therefore resolves to bring its case before the Confederation at the Baden annual court day in order to preserve its freedoms. The Luzern envoys are requested to inform the Catholic cantons about this matter and to support St. Gallen.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and the small and great Councils of St. Gallen
en.recipient: The Schultheiss and Council of Luzern

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report that the heirs of Caspar Schlumpf have lifted the arrest on the estate of the deceased Melchior Wildi in Amsterdam. The citizen of St. Gallen Heinrich Wildi asks for support in the collection of his inheritance. The St. Gallen authorities ask Schaffhausen to participate in a friendly conference of the Wildi heirs in order to accelerate the distribution of the estate and save costs.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen

en.regest: Burgomaster, Council and Elders of the three communities of Frankenthal ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a further Christian contribution for the maintenance of the church and school servants. They report that the city has fallen into extreme poverty due to war burdens and damage to the crops by the French army. They hope that this is the last request, and thank for the help so far.
en.sender: Burgomaster, Council and Elders of the three communities of Frankenthal
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The pastors of the Reformed congregations around Meisenheim ask the Swiss church leaders and the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for financial support. They describe the distress caused by war, hunger, and flight, which also affects many clergy. They assure that the funds are used sparingly, and thank for previous help.
en.sender: Friedrich Exterus, Adolf Langhans, Christophorus Montanus, Georgius Fridericus Schwebel, Wilhelm Rießbach, Martinus Faber, Johann Caspar Herman, Johannes Christianus Neuhard
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau answer an inquiry from St. Gallen regarding the imprisoned Hans Boeliger. They describe the theft of 34 Spanish doubloons from an inn, in which Boeliger was involved as an inn servant. He says that he handed the key to the chamber over to a soldier. After the act was uncovered, Boeliger was banished from the city for one year.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten report that the internal disturbances have been settled by imperial commissioners and the city government restored. As the commissioners and about 300 soldiers will remain in the city for a few more weeks, they ask St. Gallen for a loan of 1500 gulden to cover the costs. They promise repayment with interest and thank them for the support.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Administrator of the Captaincy and the Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz reply to a letter of 22 July, in which the repayment of 2000 gulden capital and overdue interest was demanded. They regret that, for lack of money, they cannot pay, but promise to service the debt with two interests and, if possible, more. They ask for patience until better times.
en.sender: The Administrator of the Captaincy and the Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to the letter of St. Gallen of 7. August regarding the payment of outstanding interest. They ask for patience, as they are exhausted by general lack of funds, contributions, and garrison provisions. They promise that, as soon as they have recovered, they will promote the payment, and ask St. Gallen to let the claim rest until then.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Arbon request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen once again for a loan of 1000 Reichs thaler. They refer to the fact that the request previously had to be submitted to the Great Council, which led to delays. Arbon has achieved an amicable settlement and the calming of the city through the help of neighboring cantons. They ask for the approval of the loan against sufficient obligation, in order to settle still outstanding items and heavy debts.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Prag ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan of 1000 ducats or 1500 gulden until Martini. They justify this with the costs of hospitality during the Confessions and the necessity to put the community back in order. They assure repayment and offer an obligation.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the authority of Amsterdam to support the heirs of the deceased Melchior Goldast. Since the administrator Elias Sataimer possesses the estate, he is to be compelled through an official inventory process to provide a precise accounting. The inventory, the testament, and further documents are to be sent to the citizen of St. Gallen Zacharias Schinzer, so that the heirs, including orphans, can assert their rights.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss, Burgomaster and Council of Amsterdam

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich thank St. Gallen for the envoy sent, who informed himself about the Uelischwyl matter and contributed to the reconciliation. They promise to support St. Gallen in similar cases. Furthermore, they report that the hospital in Uelischwyl was expelled from the land and the people dismissed, and ask for prayer for peace in the fatherland.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Genevans of 21 August. They declare that they will for the time being tolerate the repayment of the principal of 6000 gulden borrowed in 1595, but request the payment of the five outstanding interests. They have commissioned the citizen and merchant Heinrich Hueber to collect the interests and to issue a receipt to the Genevans.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Syndics, Burgomaster and Council of Genf

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council as well as the Elders of the three communities of Frankenthal thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the delivery of 60 Reichsthaler for the maintenance of the church and school servants. They ask God to reward this generous contribution and recommend the St. Gallen citizens in God's fatherhood.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council as well as Elders of the three communities of Frankenthal
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Confederates dated the 24th of the month. The latter had requested a two-year extension for their countrymen, who had lent 6000 gulden to Ammann Johann Küchlin in Oberriedt. St. Gallen agrees to this at the request of the Confederates, but reserves the letters and guarantees and expects payment after the expiration of the term.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Schwyz

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the resolutions of a Confederate conference in Zürich. It has resolved that the Burgomaster of Basel, Johann Rudolf Wettstein, should travel to Münster in the name of the Confederation to ask the French envoys there to support the complaints of the Confederates against the Spärische Kammergericht. The city of Bern and the envoy in Solothurn have agreed to this. Zürich asks St. Gallen to approve this resolution as well.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report that their linen merchants complained about insufficient weight in large purchases when buying in Wil. They ask Schultheiss and Council of Wil to order an inspection of weights and scales at the linen market to remedy the deficiency, as otherwise the merchants of St. Gallen would avoid the market.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Wil

en.regest: The town preachers, schoolteachers, widows and orphans of the County of Hanau thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the transfer of 200 gulden, which were received on 27 October 1646 through the merchant of Frankfurt Jean du Fay. They report that the money has been distributed fairly among the needy, and ask for prayers.
en.sender: Town preachers, schoolteachers, widows and orphans of the County of Hanau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Dießenhofen reply to a letter of intercession from St. Gallen concerning the St. Gallen citizen Heinrich Biller the Younger and his request for the arrest of Jacob Müller von Lindau. They have questioned the innkeeper of the Sonne, who says that Müller is not on the premises but expects his imminent return. Dießenhofen will arrest Müller upon his arrival and inform the St. Gallen in writing.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report that they have received a letter from the city of Zürich, which has already been read out by Landammann Johann Tanner. They forward the copy for better information. They declare themselves ready to do everything that serves the common good, and expect the same behavior from Appenzell.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rhodes of the Land of Appenzell

en.regest: The Council of the Monastery as well as the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report that the city of Konstanz marched into Bregenz the day before with storming hand. This puts the borders of the Confederation in danger, as great force must be expected against St. Gallen. They ask the Confederates to avert the danger through an embassy or to contribute with troops for defense.
en.sender: Council of the Monastery, Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Confederate cantons

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Field Marshal Karl Gustav Wrangel for his friendly attitude towards the city and its citizens as well as for the assured neutrality. They send him two casks of Rhine wine and ask for further benevolent reception. The city promises to faithfully maintain the neutrality and to render Wrangel all possible services.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Karl Gustav Wrangel

en.regest: Carl Gustav Wrangel thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the declaration to the Confederate envoys as well as for the provision of two casks of Rheintaler wine. He assures that he will do everything that serves the preservation of the city and the unhindered continuation of trade, and asks for mutual support.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: C. G. Wrangel asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to recommend the Swedish Obristleutnant Döring, so that he may receive a ration owed to him. This had not been paid out to him during the taking of the St. Gallen Schreck through the city, as Döring had not been present.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The judges of the city court of Augsburg ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to interrogate the former citizen and merchant of Augsburg, Elias Schreckh, who is staying in St. Gallen, regarding the attached questions. They request the issuance of requisitions so that Schreckh's statements can be written down and sent back to Augsburg.
en.sender: Judges of the city court of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The pastors Göller, Wetzler and Seubert thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a donation of 60 Reichsthaler (90 gulden) to the church and school servants of the Principality of Zweibrücken. They assure that they have distributed the money according to need, and ask for the continuation of this Christian charity.
en.sender: Friedrich Göller, pastor and inspector at Meisenheim, Wilhelm Wetzler, pastor at Glan-Odernheim, Johann Christian Seubert, pastor at Lettweiler
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: C. G. Wrangell thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for their answer of 11 February 1647 regarding the fugitive Elias Schwarzen. Since the Obristleutnant Döring as well as other persons from Nördlingen make claims against Schwarzen, Wrangell asks that the delinquent be held until these are satisfied. He promises to hand Schwarzen over again after the claims have been fulfilled.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg to help their citizens Hans Jakob and Christoph Schlaprizi, Daniel Studer, Jacob Hochreütener and co-relatives in the enforcement of a judgment against Friedrich Isebrandt, who died in 1643. The Nürnberg city court has so far postponed the enforcement for unknown reasons. The St. Gallen side asks for an intervention so that the creditors can collect their claim.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich communicate to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen a copy of a letter they have received from the Obrist and Statthalter as well as Burgomaster and Council of the city of Lübeck. This letter was addressed to the envoys of the thirteen cantons of the Confederation assembled in Baden.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The city of Konstanz reports that, after the fall of Breisach and during the siege of Lindau, Mengen of grain are flowing into enemy territory via the customs of Rheinegg and Rorschach. The city has detained two of five ships and asks the Confederates to prohibit trade with the enemy in order to break the siege and protect its own population from price increases.
en.sender: Statthalter, Stadthauptmann, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: The 13 cantons of the Confederation, the Honorary Envoys assembled at Baden

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter of 14 February, in which 200 muskets and 30 measures of linseed oil for the garrison of Überlingen had been requested. They communicate that neither weapons nor oil are available, as the muskets were consumed during the last alarm and the oil is scarce. Furthermore, they urge the repayment of a loan with interest from the year 1646, as no answer has yet been received.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the Commandant of the island of Mainau to enable their citizen Caspar Schibener to obtain the release of 20 ash casks, which were deposited there by the shipman Hans Wucher from Steinach. They ask that either the casks be transferred or that Wucher be given a free and safe pass to collect them.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Commandant of the island of Mainau

en.regest: The Richter and Statthalter of the Burgomaster's office and Council of the city of Konstanz reply to an intercession letter from St. Gallen. They justify the temporary withholding of grain ships with the threat from the enemy in Bregenz and Lindau as well as the concern for the supply of the Confederation. They confirm that free commerce with the Confederation remains preserved, and request St. Gallen to admonish its citizens not to make excessive deliveries to the enemy.
en.sender: Richter and Statthalter of the Burgomaster's office and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform that their citizen Sigmund Roffenzweig has answered the complaint filed by St. Gallen on behalf of their citizen Willer. They ask St. Gallen to communicate this answer to their citizen and to point out to him that, if he is not in agreement, he may bring his complaint before the court of Konstanz, where a decision will then be made promptly.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Yssny thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the reception of their citizens, the shelter granted to them, the help rendered, and the mercy shown. They ask for God's blessing for St. Gallen and its citizens and promise not to forget the benefits received and to repay them.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The appointed judges of the City Court of Augsburg request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to release the seizures placed on the assets of the bankruptcy estate of Elias Schreck. They refer to the fact that seizures do not establish a preferential right and threaten otherwise to apply the Jus retorsionis to safeguard the interests of their citizens against the creditors from St. Gallen and Zürich.
en.sender: Appointed judges of the City Court of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the establishment of a general day of fasting, penance, and prayer for the Evangelical Confederation, decided upon at the conference in Aarau. This is to take place on Thursday, the 9th of May. They ask the St. Gallen to also observe this day, and commend themselves to divine protection.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg answer a request for help in collecting the claims of the citizens of Nürnberg Jacob Christoph Schlapritzi, Daniel Studer, Jacob Hochrüetiner and relatives against the citizen of St. Gallen Friedrich Hiltebrand. They have ordered Hiltebrand to pay, taken his movable goods into custody and given him a deadline of six weeks. They attribute the delayed answer to the burdens of war.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Felix Dunust asks the Burgomaster and Guild Masters, Secret Councillors of St. Gallen, to inform him how many Zürcher thaler were contained in a sum of 30 gulden sent to St. Gallen on 7 March 1646. He refers to a dispute with the mint master and asks for a written statement or a copy of the mint master's letter, as he needs this for his case.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Guild Masters, Secret Councillors of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Heinrich Ziegler, Münzmeister, asks Marx Thäubel, Goldfeind, to hand over 253 gulden 7 batzen, as he has become indebted to Hans Jakob Witter am Markt. He also asks for information about the rate of the 800 gulden sent to St. Gallen and whether they are Zürcher or other thaler, as he is concerned about possible inequality.
en.recipient: Marx Thäubel, Goldfeind

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, in the dispute between their mintmaster Heinrich Seiler and the late town clerk Conrad Stab, to obtain the testimony of the St. Gallen Marx Tübel. Tübel is to report how many Reichs- or Zürcher thaler he received from Seiler in March 1646. Furthermore, the St. Gallen are to transmit the corresponding letters from Seiler to Tübel to Zürich in a faithful copy of the originals.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landvogt Leodegar Pfeiffer in Toggenburg not to harass the St. Gallen citizen Heinrich Zillig on account of the Abzug. Zillig is disturbed because the Landvogt has placed under arrest the properties he inherited from his deceased mother-in-law Anna Künzin. The city of St. Gallen appeals to old contracts and the decision of Baden 1520, according to which no Abzug tax shall be levied between St. Gallen and Toggenburg. They request that the old custom be maintained.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Leodegar Pfeiffer, Landvogt in Upper and Lower Toggenburg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm reply to a letter of 13 April. They have examined the complaint of the citizen of St. Gallen against Hans Jacob Schuhmacher, residing in Germany, and have not confirmed it. They lift the defamatory remarks exchanged between the parties ex officio and compensate the costs incurred mutually.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizens Hans Martin Thurn and Elisabeth Schinnerin in the inheritance matter in St. Gallen. The two are said to be natural heirs of N. Schinnerin and her deceased cousin. They ask for support in asserting their share of the inheritance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jacob Schlumpf informs David Heyssenn that he has received his letter. He contradicts the claim of Johannes Müller to have received the disputed 100 bundles of ribbon. The Horner Schiffermann has always denied having received the goods. Schlumpf offers to make the payment if Müller produces an honest witness for the receipt of the ribbons. He asks Heyssenn to present this to the city court.
en.recipient: David Heyssenn

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to the Swedish Colonel Johann Volckmar that their fellow citizen Hans Melchior Schobinger, on the journey from Wien, was attacked and plundered by two soldiers at Wangen. They point out that this violates the confirmed neutrality, and request an investigation as well as the punishment of the perpetrators and the return of the stolen pillows.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Johann Volckmar, Colonel and Commander at Überlingen and on Lake Constance

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to lift the arrest on goods that were imposed on the St. Gallen heirs of the Schobinger in Feldkirch. The goods belonged to the Venetian merchant Innocenz Tomasini, who had had them sent via the Zürich councilor Hans Jakob Löwen. Zürich requests the lifting of the arrest so that Tomasini can receive his payment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Schilplin der Ältere instructs the town clerk to send out four letters to the clerks and Ammänner of Berngau, St. Margrethen, Rinegg and Thal. They are to report whether anything has changed regarding the tax since 1644, whether new divisions have taken place, which properties are tax-exempt and in what state the lord is who exempted the properties. The clerk of Berngau is also to report on the court of Balgach.
en.recipient: town clerk

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg to provide the support they had promised in the claim of Jacob Spieß, Daniel Studer, Jacob Hochrüetiner and co-relatives against the citizen of Nürnberg Friedrich Hiltebrand. Since the set deadline for payment has expired, they request that the movable property under arrest be delivered to the creditors and that the execution not be further delayed.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg

en.regest: Samuel Mosbach, Franciscus Romanus and the Council of Leipzig, as commissioners appointed by Elector Johann Georg von Sachsen, request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to notify the debtors Heinrich Knaejebach and co-relatives as well as the heirs of the deceased Caspar Schlumpf. These are to appear on 2 November at 14:00 in the town hall to negotiate a partial payment. The commissioners ask for a certified confirmation of the delivery.
en.sender: Samuel Mosbach, Franciscus Romanus and the Council of Leipzig
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the Obervogt Ammann and Court of Dägerswil to support the widow Benigna Zücherin and her Vogt Friedrich Buchser. They refer to a testimony that Buchser had provided for the widow and her children during her husband's military service. They ask that no payments be imposed on the widow to Casimir Roggwiler, as the estate of her deceased husband is not available, and that she be released from the obligation to pay.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Obervogt Ammann and Court of Dägerswil

en.regest: Burgomaster, Judges and Council of the imperial capital Linz reply to a letter of 29 July. They justify the quartering in the dwellings of the Herren Schindler and Friedrich with the great distress and point out that the expenses would be reimbursed. They assure their friendship, as long as the Herren do not violate their freedoms and remain in Linz. Should they settle in other places outside the landesfürstlichen cities, no transactions could be permitted to them outside the market days.
en.sender: Burgomaster, Judges and Council of the imperial capital Linz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Sulzbach thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the approved tax assistance in a time of need. They ask God to richly reward the good deed and commend the authorities of St. Gallen along with the community to the protection of God.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Bludenz inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the usual livestock market in Bludenz. They report that livestock plagues have broken out in the parishes of Schagun and Vandau as well as in the Au Mauris. Therefore, all animals from the affected areas have been quarantined and guards have been posted to prevent the introduction of sick animals. The market will take place on the following Wednesday, the 2. Oktober.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Max Christoph Freiherr von Welden zu Wolfegg recommends to the Burgomaster, Ammann and Council of St. Gallen the local founder Theodosius Ernst. He says that Ernst has hitherto done him good work. He asks the authorities of St. Gallen to consider Ernst before others for the execution of small casting works and to grant him the work.
en.sender: Max Christoph Freiherr von Welden zu Wolfegg
en.recipient: Burgomaster, Ammann and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Georg Graf zu Königsegg thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the kindness received during his exile. He informs them that Archduke Ferdinand Karl has appointed him General Commissioner in the Arlberg territories. He assures them that he wishes to be useful to the city of St. Gallen and the land, and asks for the opportunity to prove this.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank Count Johann Georg zu Königsegg und Rotenfels for his stay in the city and for the offer to act for them as General Commissioner of Archduke Ferdinand Karl in the Austrian circles. They ask him to continue to hold the city and its citizens in favor and, in particular, to kindly assist the merchants of the city in their trade transactions in his lands.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Johann Georg Count zu Königsegg und Rotenfels

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Landvogt of the Rhine Valley to support their city physician Dr. Hans Peter Rotmund in a legal dispute with the subject Konrad Tobler of Thal. Rotmund had delivered bad wine, which had not been properly understood before the court in Thal. The witnesses confirmed that the cask had been good. The St. Gallen ask for an amicable solution and for compensation for the damage and the costs.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt of the Upper and Lower Rhine Valley in Glarus

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich forward a request from the Evangelicals in Schretz in Mähren to St. Gallen. Approximately 600 expelled co-religionists, partly noble lords, ask for a donation for the construction of an auditorium, a school, and a parsonage. The Estates of Mähren have granted them free religious practice. Zürich requests a benevolent response and support from St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ensisheim and Breisach remind St. Gallen of a letter of 22 June 1646 and ask again for a reply. It concerns outstanding interest since 1635 on a capital of 1500 gulden of the city as well as interest since 1632 on a hospital capital of 1000 gulden. They request payment so that the interest does not continue to grow, and promise to tolerate further claims upon payment.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of Ensisheim and Breisach
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the Zürichers of 19 October 1647 concerning the Protestant exiles staying in Skalitz in Ungarn. They declare themselves willing to contribute 200 gulden for the construction of a church and school. They ask Zürich for information on whether the contributions of the Protestant cantons are to be collected or remitted individually, and leave the decision to the discretion of the Zürichers.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for information regarding the claims of the noble secular women's convent of Lindau. This convent claims that the city wall and the city gate belonged to the monastery of St. Gallen, that the right of high justice (Blutbannrecht) lay with the convent and not with the city, and that old silver hallers of the convent existed. Lindau asks whether these statements are correct, whether coins or stamps are present in the monastery, and offers reciprocal service.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen reply to the reminder from the city of St. Gallen regarding overdue interest. They explain that, due to their financial situation, which has been exacerbated by poor harvests and general hardship, they are unable to make a payment. They ask Spindler for further patience until their means improve.
en.recipient: Hans Spindler, Council and Seckelmeister of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau reply to a letter from the Council of St. Gallen dated the 12th of the month, in which the latter had requested information on several matters. Lindau states that the city wall, the Blutbann and the Malefizobrigkeit in the area of the monastery have belonged to the monastery since 1566, after these rights had been transferred in exchange for other privileges. They have not yet received any information regarding the keeper of the silver plate.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Commander Valckenhan of Überlingen to be helpful to their citizen Hans Melchior Schöbinger in his matter. They refer to a letter of 26 July and the willingness of the Commander of 4 August to help the supplicant. They request the granting and application of all useful means, in accordance with the neutrality of the Confederation and good neighborliness.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Commander Valckenhan of Überlingen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Memmingen report on the heavy siege by imperial and Bavarian troops and the resulting damage to the city and the citizenry. They ask Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich for a loan of 2000 to 3000 gulden, in order to repair the ruins and to support the population. Memmingen offers an interest of five to six percent and the repayment of the capital.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Memmingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen describe the severe siege of their city by imperial and Bavarian troops in the autumn of 1647 and the resulting damages. They ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan of 2000 to 3000 gulden for the restoration of the city and to relieve the citizenry. The repayment of the capital along with an annual pension is assured.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the Imperial City of Memmingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich answer a petition of St. Gallen for Martin Linderer, holder of the estate of the deceased Dorothea Forrerin, widow of the former German schoolmaster Hans Heinrich Mössli. They report that Linderer had paid the deceased approximately 1000 gulden in cash after her return from St. Gallen and Hochfelden. Furthermore, she had purchased a house at St. Jakob for 550 gulden. Linderer will soon render a proper account before the Schirmvögte and liquidate the estate.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Volckmar confirms the receipt of a letter of 8 December, according to which, upon the report of Johannes Marxen, fruits of Herr Melchior Rietburger had been found in St. Gallen. He offers that the citizens of St. Gallen send a representative to clarify the matter. He promises to impose punishment if misconduct is established, in order to satisfy the neighbors and deter others.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Burgomaster and Council of Hamburg to pay the creditors of the deceased Lorenz Felixe the money due to them together with interest. The creditors had already turned to the Confederates, the three Estates, and Schaffhausen on multiple occasions. St. Gallen asks for a final clarification of the matter to spare the creditors further damage.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Hamburg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen regret the siege of Schaffhausen by imperial and Bavarian troops. They refuse the request for a loan of 2000 to 3000 gulden for the repair of the city walls and for the support of the poor citizenry. As a reason, they cite the poor economic situation, the standstill of the linen weaving, several bankruptcies, high costs for border watches, and the resulting financial burden on the city.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform that they will support Memmingen after the siege not with a loan, but with a one-time grant. They inform St. Gallen of this intention and ask for its consent, so that the Confederates can act in unison.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz reply to an intercession letter from St. Gallen for the naturalized citizens Heinrich and Sebastian Schindler. They communicate that they have examined Martin Ziegler under oath on the same day. The statement of Ziegler, who reports on a purchase of damask and Daffetbendeln by a Marquartenter, is attached.
en.sender: Administrator of the Captaincy, Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform that the bailiff Hans Heinrich Lindinger has rendered an account before the Schirmvögte regarding the estate of the deceased Dorothea Hämerin, widow of Hans Heinrich Nüsslin. The Schirmvögte have approved the account and fixed the bailiff's fee, but are awaiting the answer of the heirs as to whether they agree or wish to appear themselves or through an attorney. Zürich asks St. Gallen to inform the heirs and to request an answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen thank St. Gallen for its answer of the 19th of the month. Since St. Gallen refuses a loan of 2000 to 3000 gulden with interest due to its own difficulties, the Memmingers now ask for a voluntary, gratuitous contribution to alleviate their distress. They promise to express their gratitude and to repay with service when their situation improves.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Konstanz inform St. Gallen that the citizen of St. Gallen Jacob Mauchen had paid a debt to the Konstanzer Thomas Zwicker, but in doing so had paid 28 thaler too much. Mauchen had complained to the Amtsbürgermeister because a payment receipt had been denied to him. The Amtsbürgermeister had thereupon requested the Konstanzer Bernhard Mauchlin to inform the citizens of Zürich in order to protect Mauchen. The citizens of Zürich had subsequently provided the receipt and paid the remainder. Konstanz declares that the Amtsbürgermeister had only wanted to seek justice, and asks St. Gallen to understand this accordingly.
en.sender: Administrator of the Hauptmannschaft, Burgomaster and Council of the city of Konstanz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur report that Georg Stäheli, a citizen of St. Gallen and master of the Stüver, has requested them in writing to inform him whether any children have been harmed in the city ditch in St. Gallen. They assure that this has not happened and ask that this be communicated to Stäheli. They recommend themselves to further gracious neighborhood.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Radolfzell wish the envoys of the city of St. Gallen a healthy new year. They assure that the merchants of the city in Radolfzell will continue to be received and supported in a friendly manner. Regarding earlier complaints about the Swedish garrison, which had taken away cloths, it is explained that this no longer happens and that the St. Gallen are not hindered in their businesses. Radolfzell offers security against all adversities.
en.recipient: Envoys of the Lords St. Gallen, Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen, assembled at Wil

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to earnestly compel their citizen Jacob Glinz, furrier, to release the Lindau citizen Conrad Zaffner, cooper, from the obligations he has assumed and to pay the expenses incurred for him. Lindau offers friendly assistance in return.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Memmingen ask Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen for a compassionate contribution. Since no answer has been received to their request of 4 January, they say that they have dispatched the Mitrat and hospital almoner Christian Teücher to personally present the city's dire straits. They ask for a willing answer.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Memmingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen confirm to Burgomaster and Council of Preßburg that Magdalena Rothin and Susanna Rothin, as daughters of the deceased Caspar Ruchen, are his heirs. They ask the Preßburg authorities to assist the two women in asserting their inheritance rights to 50 Reichstaler from the estate of the widow Anna Ruchen in Preßburg.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Preßburg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the arrival of the French envoy de la Barde in Solothurn. They communicate that the 13 cantons have set an audience for 9 February, and ask St. Gallen to proceed accordingly.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizen Hans Jakob von Rüstingen. He has obtained an obligation for 1600 gulden, which is owed to him by Hans Jörg Müller of Ulm. Since Müller is insolvent, the Zürich authorities request official assistance and an arrest on the person and property of the debtor, so that Rüstingen can collect his claim.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Lindau to help their citizen Jacob Klein, the church warden. He says that five years ago he bought 600 Hölzli from Johannes Müller, called Schiffeli, which he never received. Lindau should instruct Müller to name the boatman to whom the Hölzli were handed over, so that Klein can collect his damages from him.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Reutlingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to recommend and support the three Reutlinger citizens Ferdinand Bäuerin, Jerg Mayr and Balthasar Finck, who are collecting a fire tax because of the destruction of the city by Bavarian troops in the year 1647. They ask for a written answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Hauptmann to return to the citizens of St. Gallen, the heirs of Hans Schobinger, Jakob Schlumpf and Daniel Haimen, the goods taken from them by Schweden troops between Isny and Lindau. The city appeals to the existing neutrality between Schweden and the Confederation, which forbids hostile actions, and promises the Hauptmann neighboring support in similar cases.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Hauptmann

en.regest: C. J. Volckmar informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, at the request of his lords, he has had the goods seized by the St. Gallen citizens restored. He complains that the merchants are traveling without a pass and warns against smuggling foreign goods (such as salt) under the guise of Confederate goods, otherwise he will take revenge on another neighboring ship.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Obrister to order the commander in Langenargen to immediately and without compensation return the goods of the St. Gallen citizens, the heirs of Hans Schobinger, Hans Schlumpf, and Daniel Heiman, which were intercepted on the way from Eisenach to Lindau by a Swedish party. They refer to the existing neutrality.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Obrister

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the Landgericht Appenzell request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to summon the St. Gallen citizen, the wife of Schwarzen Stöcklis, as well as the daughter of the Zunftherr Othmar Schenk and others, who know of the accusation against the Appenzellerin Barbara Gmünderin, in the absence of the Appenzellers. They are to be sworn in and questioned according to the customs of the city of St. Gallen, as the Gmünderin is accused of the theft of cords and a bag. The statements are to be sent in writing to Appenzell.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Landgericht Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank the Colonel for the return of goods that had been taken from merchants of St. Gallen by a Swedish party. They inform him that their merchants will henceforth accompany their goods with authentic passes, and request the Colonel to ensure with the Swedish soldiery that these goods are allowed to pass unhindered upon presentation of the passes. Furthermore, they point out that a Steinower ship with 99 sacks of grain had passed through to Lindau under the pretext of Confederate goods; they admonished their citizens to refrain from such actions that contradict neutrality.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Colonel

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen to instruct their shipping people and order them not to smuggle foreign goods under Confederate goods when crossing Lake Constance. This is done at the request of the merchants naturalized in St. Gallen, who complain about the complaints of the Obrist of Überlingen. St. Gallen wishes to thus preserve the security of trade and shipping.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Appenzell ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to allow their principal officers Peter Bildstein and Carolus Jacobus Wyssen to recruit soldiers in St. Gallen for the service of the French Queen. They refer to the fact that this has already happened several times in St. Gallen, and promise gratitude as well as reciprocity.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Volckmar confirms that he allows the merchants of St. Gallen to export their goods with authentic credentials from their authorities. He recommends applying for a pass at the Generality, as armies may approach. In the meantime, he accompanies the goods with a pass, a certified copy of which the citizens of St. Gallen can use.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Colonel and Commander of the city of Überlingen requests the Swedish officers and soldiers to allow the carters of the city of St. Gallen, who are equipped with passes of the Confederates, to pass freely, safely, and unimpeded. These carters transport goods into and out of the Empire and possess the necessary permissions of General and Field Marshal Wrangel.
en.sender: Colonel and Commander of the city of Überlingen
en.recipient: Royal Swedish officers and soldiers

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen confirm that they have instructed their shipping people not to load or depart with foreign goods, in particular from Lindau. They assure that they had already done this previously, and offer St. Gallen their support as Confederates.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Volckmer, Obrist and Governor of Überlingen, informs Landvogt Jost Zweifeln that, upon the latter's intervention, he has lifted the arrest of his subject Heinrich Wasser. He hands Wasser over to the Landvogt so that the latter may punish him for the recently uttered insulting words against the Obrist, and instructs him to henceforth leave honest men in their respect. The reason for the arrest is evident from the attached protocol of 9./19. March.
en.sender: Johann Volckmer, Obrist and Governor of Überlingen
en.recipient: Landvogt Jost Zweifeln in the lower and upper Rhine Valley

en.regest: Jost Zwüffell complains that the citizen of St. Gallen Caspar Haltmayer has falsely accused the Winteseer Heinrich Gasser in Überlingen of defamation against the Colonel Wolkmar. Gasser has been imprisoned unjustly and incurred costs. Zwüffell requests the Council of St. Gallen to proceed against Haltmayer and to take him into custody until the matter is settled, in order to maintain the Confederation's neighborhood.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to the complaint of the Landvogt against their citizen Caspar Haltmeyer regarding alleged insult of the subject Heinrich Meyer. Haltmeyer denies the accusations and appeals to witnesses. The city asks the Landvogt to settle the matter amicably and declares that Haltmeyer must leave the city until the conclusion of the proceedings.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt of the upper and lower Rhine Valley

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to restrain their citizen Jacob Küntz to reimburse the costs suffered by the Lindau citizen Hans Conrad Hafner and to release him from the surety entered into for him.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jost Zwyffel, Oberkeit zu Rynegg, reports to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen about the dispute between his subject Heinrich Saßer and the citizen of St. Gallen Caspar Haltmeier. Saßer has declared himself innocent and denied the accusations. Zwyffel asks the St. Gallen authorities to instruct Haltmeier to refrain from acting until the legally binding judgment of the case, so that his subject is not further harassed.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Michael Franck, cashier in Überlingen, informs Caspar Huldreich in St. Gallen that Heinrich Bärter had to appear before the authority because of insulting words against the commander. Franck sends him the interrogations of the auditor and the letter of the Landvogt of Reineck in the original, so that Huldreich can prove Bärter's speech and the commander can support him in the law. He asks that the documents be returned after submission to the authority.
en.recipient: Caspar Huldreich, merchant citizen in St. Gallen

en.regest: Landvogt Hans Josef Kochlin answers the letter of the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen dated the 18th of the month regarding the subject Heinrich Endres and the citizen of St. Gallen Caspar Haltmeier. He reports that he has read the summons to Haltmeier and received his written statement. Since Haltmeier appeals to the law of the Confederation, according to which the defendant is to be sued at his residence, he cannot refer him to the Landvogt. He asks for news so that Endres may legally pursue Haltmeier in St. Gallen.
en.sender: Hans Josef Kochlin, Landvogt of the upper and lower Rhine Valley
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen recommend to the Colonel and Commander in Überlingen, Johann Volckmar, their citizens and master painters Jacob Christoph Scherer and Christoph Locher. These intend to carry out painting work in Überlingen and Langenargen for Swedish officers. The city asks for protection and favor so that the painters can travel safely and conduct their business.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Johann Volckmar, Colonel and Commander in Überlingen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the Imperial City of Memmingen thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the approved aid of 100 ducats. They promise to repay the amount after overcoming their distress, and recommend themselves further to the goodwill of the St. Gallen.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the Imperial City of Memmingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel the heirs of Margaretha Bodin, who died in St. Gallen, to settle the outstanding costs for the doctor, the pharmacy, and the burial from her inheritance. The guardians of the deceased in Lindau have no means to pay the debts.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Wil transmit to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen the testament of the St. Gallen woman Maria Pünderi, wife of David Marti. The document was drawn up in the presence of council members and the town clerk. The people of Wil ask the people of St. Gallen to ratify the testament.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask St. Gallen to communicate its opinion on the costs of the French embassy at the Salutation in Solothurn. Furthermore, they inform that the 200 gulden intended for the reformed community of Wald in the Ur canton have been collected and will be transferred together with other cantons. They request St. Gallen to also transfer its share.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Count Maximilian Wilibald, Gubernator of Lindau, for support for their citizen Gabriel Krum. Krum has been damaged in his wood near Lindau by the Schanzmeister of the Count. The two oaks already approved are to be handed over to him, and it is to be prevented that further damage to wood and meadows is inflicted on him in the future.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Maximilian Wilibald, Count of Wolfegg, Gubernator of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur to deliver one or two pieces of deer from the Graben to their citizen Wolfgang Müller against payment. The citizens of St. Gallen are dependent on hunting in their own Graben and thanked for the previous favorable promise.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen thank Schultheiss and Council of the city of Winterthur for the delivery of pieces of game from the city moat. They mention that the game, although somewhat damaged and in poor condition upon arrival, is gratefully received for the great favor. They offer to repay this in the future with other services.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of the city of Winterthur

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the request made by von Rheineck for a contribution to a new auxiliary benefice. This benefice serves youth education and divine service. Zürich has already approved 520 gulden and asks St. Gallen for a corresponding contribution to bear witness to the religious neighborhood.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landvogt Jost Zweiffel not to burden their citizens, who possess their own Trägen and Törggel in the courts of Rheineck and Thal, with new letters. The citizens had inherited their rights from their ancestors and wished to be allowed to remain with the old customs. They implore the Landvogt to grant them this.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Jost Zweiffel, Landvogt of the upper and lower Rhine Valley

en.regest: Landvogt and town clerk of the Rheintal answer an inquiry from the city of St. Gallen. They explain that they do not intend to abolish the Dörgel rights, but only to examine them in order to prevent abuses in the administration of the tithe. They intend to have new documentary letters with the sovereign's seal issued by those who cannot present documents. Otherwise, the Dörgel will be closed in the autumn.
en.sender: Jost Zwiffer, Landvogt, and Hans Albrecht Tanner, town clerk, of the Rheintal
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen confirm to Landvogt Jost Zweifel the receipt of a letter of 14 May. They communicate that they will inform the other interested parties of the statement contained therein by the Lord regarding the confirmation of the village right and the summons to those who have not yet collected their rights to assert their rights in Thurgau. As soon as they have received their answer, they will reply to the Landvogt without delay.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt Jost Zweifel

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to the request of Landvogt Jost Zweifel to certify and renew the toll rights of the citizens of St. Gallen in the Rheintal. They state that most citizens can already prove their rights with old, sealed letters and do not require a renewal. They ask the Landvogt to stick to the old letters and let the rights of the citizens stand, as this was also customary in the past.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Jost Zweifel, Landvogt of the upper and lower Rheintal

en.regest: Johann Konrad Meyer, Landvogt of Appenzell Ausserrhoden, reports to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he has questioned the wife of the preacher Jacob Maurer, Dorothea Frey, in Herisau. She says that she has refused to reconcile with her husband, as he has impregnated a woman in Sursee. Meyer confirms this in writing.
