An attached testimony from the former Schultheiss of Sursee, Ambrosi Schüpp, certifies that no complaint regarding this claim is known to him.
en.sender: Johann Konrad Meyer, Landvogt of Appenzell Ausserrhoden
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Burgomaster and Council of Lindau to instruct their citizen Conrad Lechner to cease the defamatory accusations against the St. Gallen furrier Jacob Schlinz. Schlinz had turned to Lechner in a legal dispute concerning 100 feet of land. The St. Gallen authorities consider it unusual to use insults during a pending legal dispute and offer that Schlinz give Lechner the due answer.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Commander in Überlingen to continue to grant the St. Gallen corn carriers free passage on Lake Constance. The people of Überlingen had refused passage due to suspicion of smuggling fruit to the enemies. The St. Gallen authorities point out that their citizens, according to old law, may not carry corn to foreign places, and refer to the cooperation with Schaffhausen and Stein am Rhein to prevent abuses by sailors.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Commander in Überlingen

en.regest: J. Volckman sends a pass to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for their grain merchants. He informs them that he will no longer permit the grain market in Stein, but will relocate it to Überlingen again according to the old custom. He asks the St. Gallen authorities to instruct their grain merchants to visit the market only in Überlingen and nowhere else.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Volckmar, Colonel and Commander of Überlingen, grants a pass to the grain merchants of St. Gallen. These are permitted to transport a quantity of grain, which they have bought in Schaffhausen and Stein, by ships to Rorschach. The subordinates of the Commander are to let the merchants pass freely upon presentation of the pass and a confirmation from their authority. Enemy property is prohibited, otherwise the goods and ships will be confiscated.
en.sender: Johann Volckmar, Colonel and Commander of Überlingen
en.recipient: The subordinates of the Commander of Überlingen

en.regest: Burgomaster and War Council of St. Gallen ask Landvogt Anton Arnold to refrain from the auction of the goods of the Almshouse of Linsbühl on the coming Tuesday. The Almshouse had offered Schmid the redemption of his claim together with costs, but he is waiting for the decision of the Court of Appeal of Konstanz. The city wants to prevent the Almshouse from being harmed by the sale.
en.sender: Burgomaster and War Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Anton Arnold, Landvogt of the upper and lower Thurgau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen complain to the Commander at Überlingen that their grain merchants, despite a pass issued on 24 June, were stopped on Lake Constance and forced to pay a so-called knight's tax. They ask that the merchants be spared this unusual levy and that they be granted free passage.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Herr Commander at Überlingen

en.regest: The Schultheiss, Burgomaster, Council and subjects of the cities of Sobernheim, Böckelheim and Nußbaum thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the generous support through a Christian alms tax, which they had granted at the request of Elector Ludwig Philipp von der Pfalz. They ask for further help and promise reciprocity.
en.sender: The Schultheiss, Burgomaster, Council and subjects of the cities of Sobernheim, Böckelheim and Nußbaum
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Jerg Ludwig von der See informs that he will only release the fruit from Schaffhausen and Stein, which was purchased by St. Gallen but detained in Konstanz, once the Confederates fulfil their obligations. He refers to the violation of the right of passage through the seizure of ships and fruit. Should St. Gallen provide a guarantee that nothing will fall into the hands of the enemy, the fruit will be dispatched immediately.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The city of Sobernheim confirms that it has handed over 50 gulden to the Council and Hospital Master Hans Jakob Kralt of St. Gallen as a Christian tax for the distressed communities of Sobernheim, Böckelheim and Nußbaum in the Lower Palatinate. The payment was made through Jost von Hilden of Frankfurt.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to tolerate for a short time the interest, outstanding for years, on a capital of 4000 gulden for the St. Gallen Hospital. They refer to the damages caused by the Swedish army and assure that the Hospital is secured by the pledged properties. In case of peace, interest and capital would be repaid.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nördlingen thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a generous contribution of 50 Reichsthaler for their burned citizens. They report that the donation has already been distributed, and wish St. Gallen divine blessing for this Christian mercy.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to restrain their citizen Jacob Schlumpf to keep his vow. Schlumpf is to clarify the dispute with Johann Müller and to release and hold harmless the citizen of Lindau Conrad Jochner, who had not participated in the matter. Lindau has already imposed penalties against Jochner.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and Council of Lindau
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report that the Commander in Langenargen on the last Saturday pursued ships with merchants' goods from Lindau to Rorschach on Lake Constance and brought them to Langenargen. The local merchants ask for the return of their goods. The city recommends the envoys Hans Zollikofer and David Studer and requests the Commander to grant them an audience and return the goods, which would correspond to the neutrality of the Confederation.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Johann Wolfgang von Ley, Colonel and Commander of the Fortress of Überlingen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Captain Johann Horey in Langenargen to hear the merchants Hans Schirmer and Jakob Rieder sent by them. These are to demand back the goods from Lindau seized by Horey. The city of St. Gallen refers to neutrality and asks for the return of the goods without payment.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Johann Horey, Captain and Commander of Langenargen

en.regest: A. Volckmar informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that, at their intercession, he has again released the confiscated goods of the Schläpfer family and other interested parties in the Endrische Schiff. However, he urges them to refrain from hostile goods in the future and to use only their own ships, otherwise he will proceed according to law.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Volkmar informs that he will continue not to hinder the ships of the Confederates, as long as they do not transport hostile goods for the Crown of Schweden. He refers to the case of a ship of Lindau, which was attacked at Rheineck with merchants of St. Gallen and brought to Langenargen. He asks the Confederates to prevent their subjects from such actions, otherwise he must search the ships and is freed from the consequences.
en.recipient: The 13 cantons of the Confederation

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen thank the Obrester of Überlingen for the issuance of charters of freedom to their corn merchants. However, they ask that the merchants continue to be allowed to land in Steinach or Rorschach as before, since the transfer to Arbon is very burdensome for them because of the laws, the bad roads, and the lack of protection from the weather. They promise to repay the Obrester for this in other matters.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Obrester and Commander of Überlingen

en.regest: A. Volckmar responds to complaints by the St. Gallen grain buyers regarding landing in Arbon. He allows the merchants to land in Steinach and requires passes and certificates for this, in order to exclude enemy goods. He justifies the relocation of the Rorschach market to Arbon with the necessity of better monitoring the enemy, and assures that the Confederates with valid papers would not be hindered.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have received a reply from the Commander of Überlingen to the letter of the thirteen cantons regarding navigation on Lake Constance. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to communicate their opinion on this matter to them.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Imperial Bailiff Sebastian Schobinger to use his influence with the Magistrate of the city of St. Gallen for an urgently needed loan. The city is impoverished by war costs and contributions and must pay the Emperor a high sum. They ask for a loan against the guarantee of the entire citizenry and all assets and hope for Schobinger's intercession.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Sebastian Schobinger, Imperial Bailiff of St. Gallen

en.regest: Friedrich, Pfalzgraf bei Rhein, thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the mild tax of fifty Reich thaler for the re-establishment and restoration of the destroyed school in Hornbach. He praises their Christian zeal and asks God to richly reward them for this good deed.
en.sender: Friedrich, Pfalzgraf bei Rhein, Herzog in Bayern, Jülich, Kleve und Berg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Leukirch ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan of two to three thousand gulden at ordinary interest and sufficient security. They justify this by the necessity to pay the Imperial contributions assigned for the Swedish military satisfaction, as the city is strongly exhausted by the war and the disturbed trade situation. They promise the punctual payment of interest and the repayment of the capital.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen forward a copy of a letter to Stein am Rhein, in which the Colonel and Commander of the fortress of Überlingen reports on the incidents with the St. Gallen corn carriers. They have instructed their naturalized corn carriers to adhere to the Swedish passes. They ask Stein am Rhein to order his sailors not to transport Confederate enemy cargo, but only to safely bring the goods purchased in Stein am Rhein back to Stein am Rhein.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Stein am Rhein

en.regest: The Vorsteher and Ältesten of the reformed Gemeinde in Skalitz in Ungarn thank the Council of Zürich for its letter of 13 May 1648. They confirm the acceptance of the voluntary contribution of 1950 gulden approved by the Confederation, which is to be used exclusively for churches and schools. They ask for God's blessing upon the Confederation and the Council.
en.sender: Vorsteher and Ältesten of the reformed Gemeinde in Skalitz
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen beg Archduke Ferdinand Karl von Österreich to prohibit the seizure of horses by the Pfennigmeister of Feldkirch. They refer to the eternal hereditary union with the Confederation, which guaranteed free trade and traffic. They request the Archduke to instruct his officials so that the citizens of St. Gallen can pass through unimpeded in the future.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Archduke Ferdinand Karl von Österreich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from Wil of the 15th of the month, in which the dyers' tariff was inquired about. They state that there is no special tariff in St. Gallen, as the dyers compared themselves with the people. However, they will try in the future to prescribe a specific measure, which will likely be difficult due to the changes in dyeing materials.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Wil

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Wil request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send them a written list of the dyers' wages customary in St. Gallen. They wish that their citizens and craftsmen, in particular the dyers, conform to the customs of their neighbors when determining their wages.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Richter, Hansel, Stadtammann und Richter zu Memmingen ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to publicly post the attached edict concerning the open debt court days of the Memmingen citizen Hans Jacob Büchlein. Since citizens of St. Gallen, in particular the wife of Jacob Hirtopf and the heirs of Hans Zoller, are interested as creditors, the posting should ensure that no one can plead ignorance.
en.sender: Richter, Hansel, Stadtammann und Richter zu Memmingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm send Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen an edict concerning the inventory and the edictal process regarding the estate of the deceased citizen of Ulm, Nicolaus von der Bank, cloth cutter. They ask that the edict be published in the usual places according to the custom of St. Gallen, so that any interested parties may take notice of it.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich inform the Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen that the evangelical congregation in Skalitz in Ungarn has gratefully accepted the gifts conveyed by the evangelical cities and cantons of the Confederation for the construction of an auditorium, a church, and a school. They ask for friendly-Confederate understanding for this communication.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to permit their citizen Andreas Zechelmaier, who has married a citizen's daughter in St. Gallen, to stay with his in-laws and to sell his trade goods at the weekly markets. Zechelmaier had previously worked as a bookkeeper in St. Gallen. Nürnberg refers to the good relations between the cities and the equal treatment of the citizens of Nürnberg in St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Leutkirch ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen again for a loan of 3000 gulden against interest and security. The money is necessary for the military satisfaction within the framework of the Imperial Peace. They promise repayment and ask for a rapid answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of Glarus ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the fellow citizens there, Jacob Märts and Jacob Zellweger, in recruiting soldiers for the company of their son Johann Zellweger in the French Feld. They request that the men who volunteer be accepted quietly and not publicly, as has been done in other recruitments in St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Lorenz Tschuschin, postmaster, replies to a letter dated the 20th of the month. He justifies his actions towards the St. Gallen Sebastian Riet, who had complained to the Imperial Steward in Tirol about an insult and the seizure of a horse. Tschuschin explains that citizens of St. Gallen had attacked the posts on the roads and cut off the postmasters of the Arlberg. He had released the horse again after it had been held in custody and had reached an agreement with the St. Gallens that they would no longer hinder the posts in the future. He asks for understanding for his measures to protect the postal service.
en.recipient: Wilhelm Freiherr von Taxis

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Kempten ask Dr. Sebastian Schobinger, Council member of St. Gallen, to use his influence with Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan of 3000 gulden. Kempten is said to be greatly exhausted by the war costs and the compensation payments within the framework of the Imperial Peace. They offer sufficient obligation and security and promise to repay the favor in other matters.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Kempten
en.recipient: Dr. Sebastian Schobinger, Council member of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Kempten ask Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen for a loan of three thousand gulden. They justify this with the necessity to pay their share of the contribution for the removal of the Swedish army after the Imperial Peace. Kempten offers a sufficient obligation and security for interest payment and repayment and promises to repay the goodwill in future opportunities.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Kempten
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ferdinand Karl, Archduke of Österreich, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he has examined the postmaster of Bludenz regarding his breach towards Sebastian Kunz and co-interested parties. He sends the copy of the complaint and considers it to be in conformity with the general postal regulations.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hektor Zollikofer reports to the Landvogt about his negotiation with the canon Johann Jakob Schmied of Bischofszell. Schmied refused the handover of a rent deed and the payment for the hospital, as he had not yet completed the purchase. Zollikofer asks the Landvogt to settle the parties and annul the purchase, so that the hospital can receive the rent deed.
en.sender: Hektor Zollikofer, councilor of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, at the request of their citizen Caspar Haltmeier, confirm that he is an honest and truthful man. Haltmeier has been slandered by people, who claim that he sold grain, which he had bought in Überlingen, to foreign places against neutrality and the city's statutes. The city confirms that he sold the grain to citizens of St. Gallen, and asks the Kommandant to protect Haltmeier.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Kommandant of Überlingen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Leutkirch ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to lend them 3000 gulden. They justify this with the ongoing contributions and a new high assignment, which exceeds their satisfaction contingent. They promise the repayment of the capital with interest.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen ask St. Gallen for a loan of 2000 to 3000 gulden for two to three years. They justify this with the high costs of the siege and the payment to the Swedish soldiery as a result of the Imperial Peace. They assure repayment and offer securities.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the Imperial City of Memmingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Leutkirch urgently request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan of 3000 gulden. They refer to the urgent demand of the imperial envoys to pay the agreed peace contributions immediately in order to avoid further damage from the war. Leutkirch asks for a prompt answer, as time is pressing.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Wangen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan of 8000 gulden to satisfy the soldiery after the Peace of Westphalia. They justify the request with the distress caused by war, a mouse plague, and crop failure, and refer to the existing friendship and neighborhood. They offer security for capital and interest and promise gratitude.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the letter of 9. November 1648 concerning the quota for a common war tax loan. They refer to the fact that the small Council may not borrow money from the city treasury without the consent of the great Council. The letter will be presented to the next great Council, which will then reply. Due to the lack of money caused by the standstill of the trade, fulfilling all wishes is difficult.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen

en.regest: Johannes Senftmeyer, town clerk of St. Gallen, confirms to the Landvogt the receipt of his answer to the request for the restitution of the Lenggghager inheritance goods. He hands over to the Landvogt the deed of sale between Dr. Schmid and the purchasers as well as the final account. He asks the Landvogt to move Dr. Schmid to the handover of the deed, whereby his interest is to be compensated to him, in order to settle the protracted dispute.
en.sender: Johannes Senftmeyer, town clerk of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Biberach grant Laurenz Ruesch of St. Gallen full power, for the city, in the context of the Imperial contribution payment to Schweden, to borrow five to fifteen thousand gulden on the estates of the St. Gallen Abbey or to acquire a village or market town.
en.recipient: Laurenz Ruesch of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Hauptleute and Council envoys of the three Bünde report to the four Evangelical cities that they had heard rumors that the peace settlement between Frankreich and Spanien could lead to their disadvantage and the abolition of their freedoms. They ask the cities for information about possible agreements, particularly regarding the Veltlin and the religion, and request them to use their authority to act against harmful provisions.
en.sender: Hauptleute and Council envoys of the three Bünde
en.recipient: The four Evangelical cities of the Confederation

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich communicate to Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen two letters from the captains and councils of the thirteen cantons. These demand that the Feldlin be handed over to the Pope as a deposit. Zürich declares that it knows nothing yet of such a breach, but will inquire and advocate with the other cantons that nothing harmful befalls the Peace of Religion and the prosperity of the cantons.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen confirm the receipt of a letter from the Landvogt in Thurgau dated the 15th of the month regarding the tithes at Egnach. They state that the aforementioned citizen Marx Feierabend is currently in Chur. As soon as he returns, they will summon him, read the letter to him, and communicate his counter-response to the Landvogt. They ask that this letter be accepted as an acknowledgment of receipt.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landvogt in Thurgau

en.regest: Karl Friedrich von Hohenems asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for support in procuring 1200 gulden, which his County of Hohenems must pay as an imperial quota to the imperial treasury. He refers to the financial distress and asks for a loan against sufficient securities, since St. Gallen has granted similar loans in the past.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landvogt in Thurgau reports that the Jew Elias of Emmishofen has complained that the citizen of St. Gallen Marx Weubler stole a gold chain and bracelets from him without judicial proceedings. He asks the Council of St. Gallen to instruct Weubler to return the property to the Jew and to assert his claims in Thurgau through the courts. He promises the Jew an impartial court.
en.sender: Johannes Anton Arnold, Landvogt in Thurgau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Wilhelm Graf zu Königsegg und Rotenfels asks the Ammann of Utzwil to help him and his subjects of the lordships of Königsegg and Aulendorf, who were damaged by the Swedish soldiery, in the payment of a claim of about 1000 florins. He sends his Ammann and two village bailiffs as authorized representatives, who deliver a written obligation. The Count promises to keep the sum and to show his gratitude.
en.sender: Johann Wilhelm Graf zu Königsegg und Rotenfels
en.recipient: Ammann of Utzwil

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Essingen thank for the fire tax aid of 1631. They report that they lost and were driven out of almost everything through the Thirty Years' War and raids. Now they ask for a loan of 1200 to 1300 gulden for the payment of the Swedish contingent. They promise good pledges, a written obligation, and repayment with interest.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan of a few thousand gulden. They refer to their earlier request of 20 September and to the fact that they want to repay the money quickly. They appeal to good neighborliness and ask for a positive answer.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the Imperial City of Memmingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Karl Friedrich Graf zu Hohenems asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to allow the creditors of his Ammann Hans Dietrich von Oberriet, who owe him 4000 gulden, to deduct this amount from a debt of the Hospital of St. Gallen in the amount of 6000 florins. He offers three vineyards in the Rhine Valley as security and promises repayment with interest.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Biberach ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant a gracious audience to the Council friends and citizens Johann Laij and Friderich Huebermann, whom they have deputed, and to be favorable to their request. They refer to the oral presentation of the envoys and emphasize the special trust they place in the St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten ask Councilor Sebastian Schobinger in St. Gallen to help in obtaining a loan of 3000 gulden for the Swedish Satisfaction. Kempten has sent its envoy Christoph Ludwig Lober to the Abbey of St. Gallen. They ask Schobinger to grant the envoy all support and to move the city of St. Gallen to cooperate, in order to avert a threatened execution.
en.recipient: Sebastian Schobinger, Councilor of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Kempten thank St. Gallen for the financial aid provided 15 years ago after a storm. They ask again for support in the form of a loan of 3000 gulden, as the city is ruined by war burdens. Kempten promises to accommodate citizens of St. Gallen in the linen trade, and instructs its envoys to negotiate the conditions.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Kempten
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Wilhelm von Königsegg asks Amtmann Daniel Diethelm of Uttwil to intervene with the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan of at least 1000 ducats. He refers to the urgent necessity to pay the Swedish military satisfaction and offers as security, among other things, vineyards near Markdorf. He asks for a prompt answer.
en.recipient: Daniel Diethelm, Amtmann of Uttwil

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Biberach thank St. Gallen for the audience and the trusting resolution towards their envoys Johann Taugen and Friedrich Biedermann. They urgently request a loan of 3000 or 4000 gulden for the payment of Swedish satisfaction money, as the city's assets would otherwise be ruined. As security, they offer the property of the hospital or the citizenry and ask for written assurance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Wilhelm zu Königsegg asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan of 5000 Reichsthaler, in order to settle the quartering of Swedish and imperial troops in his lordship of Wulldorf. He offers his vineyards near Markdorf as pledge and promises to have the obligation sealed by the Count zu Königsegg und Rotenfels.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hektor Zollikofer, town clerk, informs the Landammann that the communities of Küntenschwil and Jonschwil have received a neighboring contribution of 200 gulden for the new church building. As the Seckelmeister was ill, the money was delayed. It is now being brought by a runner. Zollikofer asks the Landammann to pass the money on to the responsible parties.
en.recipient: Landammann

en.regest: Abbot Placidus von Fischingen recalls his request for 3000 gulden for the city of Überlingen and complains about their refusal to settle or secure the claim. He asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to have the goods of the city of Überlingen, which were purchased in St. Gallen and stored there, seized, in order to reach a satisfaction.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the Land of Appenzell der äußeren Roden thank the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the grant provided for the construction of a new church in Tschäntal. They assure that the money will be used to the honor of God and the donors will be recorded in writings. They express their neighborly affection and ask for God's blessing.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Land of Appenzell der äußeren Roden
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Speyer ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen and innkeeper Johann Maurer in the collection of a debt of 350 Reichsthalers. The debt was acknowledged by Hans Jakob Studer, son of the deceased St. Gallen Statthalter Daniel Studer, for cost and care in Speyer. Since the Studer family has refused payment, the Speyer authorities request support in enforcing the claim from the Studer inheritance.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Kempten ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen again for an urgently needed loan to pay the Swedish satisfaction money. They assure that they will repay the debt after the payment of the satisfaction, and ask for a quick answer. In a postscript they inform that Swedish regiments have been quartered in the Estates, and request that the troops be withdrawn from the Empire.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Kempten
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the Imperial City of Memmingen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen once again for a loan of three or at least two thousand gulden for three or four years. The money is to be used exclusively for the payment of the satisfaction money for the Swedish army. Memmingen assures that it will only call in the loan when peace is secured, and asks for a prompt answer.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the Imperial City of Memmingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Biberach ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant them a profitable loan in the vicinity of the imperial execution commission. They request a written communication of how much St. Gallen is willing to lend.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: De la Barde asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to postpone the judgment in a lawsuit of the St. Gallen citizen Studer until his return. Studer had had to remain in Frankreich for a longer period because of an insolvency in Lyon and is now about to return home in order to take part in the decision of his lawsuit. He fears that his opponent will take advantage of his absence.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Leutkirch request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen once again for an urgently needed loan. They justify this with the high costs of the peace implementation, in particular the payment of satisfaction money and the provisioning of the quartered troops before their withdrawal. They promise the repayment of the capital with annual interest and ask for a favorable answer.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Landvogt Johann Kaspar Arnold von Spiringen to excuse their citizen Hans Schlumpf the Elder, who was cited in Frauenfeld for allegedly speaking words contrary to the Landfrieden. Schlumpf had merely wanted to collect an old debt owed by a citizen of Frauenfeld and had behaved modestly in doing so. The city of St. Gallen requests the Landvogt to treat Schlumpf leniently.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Johann Kaspar Arnold von Spiringen, Landvogt of Upper and Lower Toggenburg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Biberach urgently request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan of at least 3000 gulden for the payment of the Swedish militia satisfaction, as they are being pressed by the Swabian princes to pay their share. They promise to secure the sum and to pay interest on it annually.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Wilhelm Graf zu Königsegg asks Amtmann David Birtchen zu Feldkirch to further recommend his request for a loan of 5000 gulden for the payment of the satisfaction money to the Magistrat of the city of St. Gallen. He refers to the delayed answer and the impending ruin. He offers to repay the loan, or asks, in case of rejection of the credit, to help him with 1000 or 1200 gulden. His Ammann Hans Schuffmann will present the matter orally.
en.recipient: David Birtchen, Amtmann zu Feldkirch

en.regest: Johann Wilhelm Graf zu Königsegg informs that the originally planned loan of 3000 gulden was reduced to 200 ducats. He asks the St. Gallen to lend him an additional 1500 or 1000 gulden. Otherwise, he will instruct his Ammann Hans Kaufmann and the Council clerk Walch Hornstein to collect the 200 ducats before Easter. The obligation is sent.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to the neighborly request of Lindau for a credit for the Swedish military satisfaction. They declare themselves ready to fulfill the already outstanding principal debt of 5000 gulden together with interest and to consolidate everything into a single obligation. As soon as the original is executed and handed over, they would order the payment.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Lindau

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Wangen remind Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of their earlier requests for financial assistance. Since the peace has been concluded, they must make the cash payment. They have dispatched their fellow burgomaster Conrad Ruggen for this purpose and ask St. Gallen to receive him courteously upon his arrival and to assist them in their distress.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Jakob Truchsessen, Freiherr zu Walburg, Graf zu Zeil, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan of 4000 gulden for four or six years, as his subjects are not in a position to pay the satisfaction money due to war damages. He offers the town of Wangen with all rights and Gossau together with the weaving trade as security and promises repayment with interest in St. Gallen currency.
en.sender: Johann Jakob Truchsessen, Freiherr zu Walburg, Graf zu Zeil
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the willing granting of a loan of 300 ducats in a time of need. They promise repayment with interest and offer future services. The desired obligation has been issued in the chancery according to the transmitted concept.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Vitt Laist, carpenter, invites the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to the wedding of his daughter with the widow Barbara Laist. The ceremony takes place on Tuesday, the 13. April, in the parish church, followed by a wedding meal in the house of the groom. He asks the authorities to send themselves or a representative to attend the ceremony and the feast.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist their citizen Hans Heinrich Schmuelz in a commercial matter with the citizen of St. Gallen Hans Zidler. Schmuelz has requested a petition so that he may be granted just judgment and helped to his own. Nürnberg asks for a regulation among the citizens of St. Gallen so that Schmuelz or his attorney may be quickly helped in his right.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Hans Heinrich Schneck, merchant, asks the authorities for intercessions with the Burgomaster and Council in St. Gallen. He is involved in the bankruptcy of the St. Gallen merchant Hans Riedler and co-relatives and has bills of exchange and claims there. As he cannot travel to St. Gallen personally, he has authorized Hans Schlumpf. He asks for support so that his claims against Riedler and co-relatives are settled quickly and legally.
en.recipient: E. E. und Herrlgt.

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen remind Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen of their earlier requests for a loan. Since the discharge of the Swedish troops is to take place proportionally according to the securities provided, and Memmingen would come into great inconvenience if it failed to meet its quota, they request once again for a certain and willing answer regarding the sought loan.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Wangen thank the Amtsbürgermeister of St. Gallen for the promise to lend the city of Wangen 200 ducats interest-free for three years. They transmit the obligation signed by their councilor Daniel Küenzi and promise to repay the debt with interest on time.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the letter of the Memmingen authorities of 29 March 1649 regarding a desired loan. They communicate that the Great Council has approved the lending of 300 ducats for five years against a written obligation. They ask that the attached draft be executed in original form and that the money be collected upon delivery.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Biberach thank Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for the payment of 200 gulden to the Swedish Satisfaction. They ask that the sum be handed over to their former Burgomaster Matthäus Locher against the surrender of the main bond.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to swiftly administer justice to their citizen Johann Heinrich Schuncken in a bill of exchange matter with Georg Fidler and co-relatives. They refer to an earlier letter of 27 March and to the fact that the matter does not allow for delay. They request a favorable regulation so that Schuncken be treated like the citizens of St. Gallen in similar cases.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to grant a gracious audience to their Amtsbürgermeister Doctor Johann Heinrich von Pflaumern, who represents them to the St. Gallen, and to give unquestioning belief to his report. They ask for a compliant handling of the attached affairs according to their nature.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Masters and Council of the city of Straßburg reply to a letter from the citizen of St. Gallen Georg Sebastian Zolliker dated 26 September. They explain the situation of the Wambold capital, which was invested in 1622 at 7000 florins and reduced to 1909 florins after the coin devaluation. They refuse a redemption, as this lies within their discretion and the difficult situation in the Empire does not permit such payments.
en.sender: The Masters and Council of the city of Straßburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Wil inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have seized the assets of their citizen Georg Erhart due to numerous creditor claims. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to notify creditors such as Zacharias König, Sebastian Zwigger, Hans Jakob and Daniel Locher, David Kunz, Hans Jakob Gmünd and Hans Jakob or Sebastian Höger, so that these may appear on the 28th or 18th of the month and assert their claims.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Memmingen thank St. Gallen for the promise of a loan of 300 ducats. They hand over the corresponding bond in the original and promise the repayment of the capital as well as the annual interest payment. The co-lord Jacob Wachter is commissioned to confirm the receipt of the loan.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen reply to the letter of 26. September 1648 regarding a loan for the Swedish Satisfaction. They refer to existing claims of 8250 gulden and offer to increase these to 10000 gulden. Half is to be paid in wine on Lake Constance, the other half in cash. They request a bond and promise delivery after receipt of the original.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the Imperial City of Überlingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Jacob, Reichserbtruchseß und Fürst zu Waldburg, informs the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that he has dispatched his Councilor and Untervogt Reichle with full power and instructions for negotiations. He asks the citizens of St. Gallen to listen favorably to the envoys and to accede to his request, as it concerns the urgent necessity of his subjects. He offers reciprocity and commends himself to their care.
en.sender: Johann Jacob, Reichserbtruchseß und Fürst zu Waldburg
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen thank them for the friendly reception of their Amtsbürgermeister. They ask St. Gallen to explain itself regarding the intended measure, and request that the journey of their judicial relative Johann Schneider not be interpreted with ill will.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen confirm the receipt of the reply from Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen of 26 May, New Style, regarding the loan for the Swedish peace money. They regret that Überlingen feels burdened by the interest on the old principal debts contained in the draft of the bond. St. Gallen asks that Überlingen not continue to feel this as a burden, approve the loan, and deliver the promised wine.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the city of Überlingen. They reject the demand to increase the borrowed capital by 4000 gulden and to extend the redemption deadlines to five years, as this would unduly burden the municipal fisc. They adhere to their previous declaration. Regarding the wine offered, they point out that it had not been offered, as the Burgomaster of Überlingen himself had demanded payment in money.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Überlingen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen thank St. Gallen for the financial aid granted and the approval of a new loan for the settlement of the Swedish contribution. They consider the capitalization of the accrued interest required in the bond to be too burdensome and ask for a manageable arrangement for the repayment. Überlingen will send a hospital master to St. Gallen to negotiate this.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Pfullendorf ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan of 2000 gulden. They justify this with the necessity to dismiss the Swedish militia, which was imposed on them by the Peace of Westphalia. They assure that they will repay the capital with interest, and offer future services.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter from the city of Pfäffikon dated the 8th of the month, in which the latter requests a loan of 12'000 gulden for the satisfaction of the Swedish militia. They state that they have already lent considerable sums to other cantons for the sake of the peace and therefore cannot burden their treasury any further. They ask for forgiveness and for the gracious acceptance of their refusal.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: City of Pfäffikon

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter of 11 May, in which Abbot Thomas von Salem asks for a loan for the Swedish contingent money. They refuse the loan, as the city treasury is exhausted by the collection of the peace money in the Swabian Quarter. However, they assure their willingness to render further service according to their abilities.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Abbot Thomas von Salem

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen declare to Überlingen that the citizenry is not willing to share the debts of the hospital. Since the hospital belongs to the city, the citizens must bear the burden themselves. St. Gallen is ready to pay the remaining amount in cash without grain, provided Überlingen waives the written obligation.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ulm object to the demand of St. Gallen to merge outstanding interest with the capital and to interest it. They refer to the lack of proportion between the loaned capital and the high interest. Ulm offers to pay the interest without interest if St. Gallen increases the new loan to 4000 gulden and allows the repayment in two installments of 2000 gulden each over six years. Furthermore, they ask for the delivery of old money instead of new and propose to regulate the soldier's provisioning via a bill of exchange to Ulm.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Abbot Thomas and Prior Balthasar Hornstein of Salem ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a loan to pay the Swabian contingent for the Swedish militia. The billeted Douglas regiments caused higher costs than the assigned contingent, whereby the means for the satisfaction were lacking. Without payment by 24 August, the troops would have to remain in quarters. They assure repayment with interest and refer to the delegated councilor Leonhard Wappenkhauser.
en.sender: Thomas, Abbot of Salem, and Prior Balthasar Hornstein
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Eberhard von Rom asks Marx Spindler that the city of St. Gallen should pay money of the same amount instead of the promised wine delivery, as the wine price is too high. He also asks that the debts of the city and the hospital be separated, so that the citizens only guarantee the city debt. He thanks for the honor shown to him.
en.recipient: Marx Spindler, Council and Seckelmeister of St. Gallen

en.regest: The parish priests and elders of the churches in the Piedmontese valleys thank the Reformed churches of Switzerland for financial support that they have received in a time of great distress. They assure that they will manage the funds sparingly and faithfully, and ask for prayer. The letter was drafted at a synod in St. Johann im Luzerner Tal.
en.sender: Parish priests and elders of the churches of Christ in the Piedmontese valleys
en.recipient: Ministers, elders, pastors and professors of the Evangelical churches in Zürich, Bern, Glarus, Basel, Schaffhausen, Appenzell, St. Gallen, Biel and Müllhausen
en.place: Church in St. Johann im Luzerner Tal

en.regest: The pastors and elders of the Reformed churches in the valleys of Piedmont thank the Swiss church authorities for the generous support during a famine. They promise to manage the funds conscientiously and report that, due to the snow conditions and the many poor, they could only barely cover the public church expenses. They ask for prayers and a blessed effect.
en.sender: Pastors and elders of the Reformed churches in the valleys of Piedmont (Luserna, Perosa, Sammartino)
en.recipient: Church authorities of Switzerland (Zürich, Bern, Glarus, Basel, Schaffhausen, St. Gallen, Biel, Mülhausen)

en.regest: The reformed parishes and elders in the valleys of the Piedmont confirm that they have received 200 Rhenish gulden from Antoine Leger as the fruit of the charity of the St. Gallen church. They acknowledge the sum, thank for the support of the families living in extreme poverty, and wish the givers divine blessings.
en.sender: Parishes and Elders of the reformed churches in the valleys of the Piedmont
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform St. Gallen about a Confederate beggar hunt from 11 to 13 June. Domestic beggars are to stay at home, foreign honest travellers may pass, others are to be led out of the country. Useless persons are to be handed over to the Republic of Venedig for galley punishment. Zürich asks St. Gallen to make similar arrangements and not to admit the useless people.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Ludwig Philipp, Pfalzgraf bei Rhein und Herzog in Bayern, thanks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for their earlier support of his subjects. He asks them again to help the impoverished people in his office, as these are earnestly pleading for assistance. He assures them that he will strive for their well-being.
en.sender: Ludwig Philipp, Pfalzgraf bei Rhein und Herzog in Bayern
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen report to Landammann and Council of the Land of Abbenzell that the deceased Barbara Wattachin had kept an illegitimate child by Hans Müller, the Krommer, of Hundwil with her, although she would have had to hand the child over after a punishment in 1647. They ask the Abbenzell authorities to see to it that Müller or his friends take over and provide for the child, so that St. Gallen does not have to bear the costs any longer.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Land of Abbenzell

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Wangen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support their citizen Georg Hümlin. He says that he gave the St. Gallen butcher Silvester N. more than a year ago 10 gulden 12 kreuzer for 1.5 centners of lard, for which he received a goods debt of 1.5 centners. Since the butcher did not deliver the goods, Hümlin has already been taken to court six times. There are still 5 gulden 6 kreuzer outstanding. Wangen requests St. Gallen to compel the butcher to pay the debt including costs and to enforce execution.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Pappenheim officials of the lordship of Rotenstein ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a building levy for the reconstruction of the reformed hospital church in Grönenbach. They refer to the imperial commission signature of 1649, which granted them the right of patronage and the right to practice the reformed religion, as well as to the destruction of the churches by the war.
en.sender: Pappenheim officials of the lordship of Rotenstein
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to letters from the Council of Nürnberg of 17 March and 10 April 1649 concerning the citizen of Nürnberg Johann Heinrich Schmaichen. He accuses the citizens of St. Gallen Thomas Zwiercher and son of having made him blind bills of exchange before the bankruptcy of Sittler. Zwiercher rejects the accusations and has had the bills of exchange money in his hands placed in official sequestration. St. Gallen requests Nürnberg to release the goods only after an honourable reparation by Schmaichen.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Hans Georg von Closen to maintain the arrests laid by David Erhardt in Rain in Bavaria on the goods of Hans Lautergäber, who went bankrupt in Augsburg. They refer to the request of their citizens, including Jacob Schitlin, and thank him for the measure already granted.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Hans Georg von Closen, Freiherr zu Arnstorf und Pyra, Rat und Kämmerer der Kurfürstlichen Durchlaucht in Bayern

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen inform Schultheiss and Council of Frauenfeld that the citizen of St. Gallen Hans Jacob Leß has married the citizen of Frauenfeld Barbara Nörlin. They have approved the marriage and admitted the couple to the citizenship of St. Gallen. They request Frauenfeld to deliver the bride along with her brought-in property to the groom.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Frauenfeld

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg report that their citizen Johann Heinrich Schmecken has declared that he had written nothing offensive to the St. Gallen interested parties, but only honest and good things. They ask St. Gallen to pay out the funds deposited in the chancery to Schmecken.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich report that the goldsmith Ulrich von der Burre is a prisoner in Zug because he has issued false gold coins. He claims to have received these from the priest Jörg Tschan in Dertzen in the Prince-Bishopric, originally from Baden. Zürich requests information from St. Gallen as to whether Tschan stayed in St. Gallen about 18 or 19 years ago and whether similar incidents with counterfeit gold occurred there.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Zürich
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Speyer ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizen and innkeeper Johann Maurer in his claim against the heirs of the family Studer. They refer to earlier intercessions of 28 March 1645 and 21 February 1646, to which St. Gallen has not yet replied. Maurer has again asked for support, whereupon Speyer complies with him and requests legal help from the city of St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask Landvogt Reding to support the citizens of St. Gallen Anton Milchtasch, the heirs of Othmar Schauen, and Paulus Riet in a legal dispute against the widow of the deceased Josef Eppenberg on Oberglatt. The creditors had lent the deceased 400 gulden for the takeover of an inn. The debt court of Maggenau dismissed their claim. The St. Gallen authorities ask for payment from the house or from the estate of the widow, as she had co-promised.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Hans Rudolf Reding von Biberegg, Landvogt of the County of Toggenburg

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the Government of Innsbruck to order the Landtrichter Dr. Christoph Keller in Rankweil to pay the 200 gulden demanded by the St. Gallen citizens Thomas Zwier and son, together with costs. The St. Gallen citizens had advanced the money at Keller's request, who refuses to repay it despite court orders and promises.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Government of Innsbruck

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Wangen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen again for a loan of 2000 gulden. They say that they are pressed by the Estates of the Holy Roman Empire to pay the Swedish militia satisfaction. Without this payment, danger and inconveniences threaten them. They promise to repay the money and to gratefully repay the help.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Council of Ravensburg to exempt their citizen Schlapperitz and co-relatives from a tax of 15 pounds on properties located in Ravensburg. The citizens of St. Gallen had already cleared the properties and redeemed the co-heirs of Ravensburg with cash. They refer to a receipt in which no taxes are mentioned and ask for relief.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Council of Ravensburg

en.regest: J. Maurer, who fell into disgrace in Biel because of a feud with the Boltzen and an alleged poisoning of his wife and was banished by Bern, turns to the Council of St. Gallen. He asks for access to the banishment document of the Berner Grossweibel in order to defend himself. Furthermore, he demands that his wife, who is staying with a goldsmith in St. Gallen, be summoned and questioned, or that she present a divorce certificate. He hopes for a free pass and justice.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Karl Fugger von Kirchberg und Weissenhorn, Vizedom and imperial councillor, informs that the estate Yhetzing, left behind by Michael Ferdinand Klein and his wife, has been ruined by the enemy incursion. Since the creditors could not be satisfied, he says that they are determined to proceed against the estate with an edict and summary process. He asks the Council of St. Gallen to publicly post the attached proclamation and to report on it.
en.sender: Karl Fugger von Kirchberg und Weissenhorn, Vizedom and imperial councillor
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Leutkirch thank St. Gallen for a loan of 300 ducats and ask for further help of 500 ducats. They say that they are pressed by the burden of billeting and a serious threat from the Swabian Circle to pay for troop withdrawals and assignments, otherwise execution is threatened. They promise to issue a bond and to pay off the annual pension as well as the capital.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send their fellow councillor Heinrich Holtzhalb an authentic, vidimated balance sheet of the Zillierische creditors and debtors. Holtzhalb has agreed to let the claims of the creditors presented to him rest for the time being, but needs the balance sheet for verification. The Zürich authority requests the fulfillment of this wish in order to promote the business and to reassure both authorities.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Landammann and Council of the Outer Rode of the Land of Appenzell request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to proceed against the St. Gallen woman Anna Schiedlerin. She had showered her fellow countrywoman Anna Schüssin, who had lent her money, with defamatory and shameful words. Schiedlerin had furthermore claimed that Schüssin committed fornication with her brothers. The Appenzellers ask for the punishment of the liar.
en.sender: Landammann and Council of the Outer Rode of the Land of Appenzell
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Lindau ask Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen to lend a neighborly hand to the Lords of Überlingen in obtaining a loan for the withdrawal of the garrisons from Überlingen and Lindau. The funds are necessary to dismiss the troops and clear the cities, which would also benefit Lindau.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Lindau
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Count Karl Fugger and the Government of Landshut to maintain the arrest placed in Evra by the St. Gallen citizens Jacob and Georg Fels as well as Heinrich and Laurenz Schlaepfer against the departed Augsburg merchant Jos Laidegärber. They refer to the usual practice in bankruptcy cases and request protection against the lifting of the arrest by the Bavarian Government in favor of the Augsburg creditors.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Karl Fugger, Count of Kirchberg and Weissenhorn, Vicedom and Council of the Government of Landshut

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request the High Princely Government of Landshut for support in an arrest case against the younger Johann Ledergerber. They refer to the reports of the judges of Dorn and ask that the existing arrest be protected and the recusal action prevented, so that the seized goods do not pass to the family of the bankrupt.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: High Princely Government of Landshut

en.regest: Burgomaster, Council and citizens of Überlingen grant full power to the Amtsbürgermeister Johann Heinrich von Pfauern to raise funds for the payment of the Swedish contribution. They undertake, as security, to pledge all municipal and hospital property as well as claims against third parties and, in case of payment default, to satisfy the creditors, also through the realization of the pledges or the retention of revenues.
en.sender: Burgomaster, Council and citizens of Überlingen

en.regest: The electing Princes of the Swabian Circle, Franz Johann Bishop of Konstanz and Eberhard Duke of Württemberg, remind the city of Esslingen of its payment obligation for the fourth million of the Swedish satisfaction money. They urge the city to pay its share of 430 gulden as well as any outstanding balances from previous claims in cash into the Legstätte by the third deadline, in order to accelerate the evacuation of the occupied places and the peace. In case of default, they disclaim responsibility for possible damages, attributing it to the city.
en.sender: Franz Johann Bishop of Konstanz, Lord of Reichenau and Oehningen, and Eberhard Duke of Württemberg and Teck, Count of Mömpelgard, Lord of Haidenheim
en.recipient: City of Esslingen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to allow the Steinach boatmen access to the Überlingen weekly market. The St. Gallen Pfisterzunft, which wishes to visit the market, has appointed the two boatmen as agents to transport the purchased goods. Überlingen refers to the previous practice and the consent of the neighbors at Stein am Rhein.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Überlingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landammann and Council of the Land of Appenzell of the outer Rhoden to help the St. Gallen physician Johann Kwellner to obtain his healing costs and fees from the Appenzell peasant who had injured and damaged Anna Weberin, who comes from Küssnacht, during the night. The woman had been treated in the St. Gallen almshouse. The costs are to be imposed on the perpetrator.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Land of Appenzell of the outer Rhoden

en.regest: The city of Überlingen acknowledges a debt of 12'000 St. Gallen gulden to the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen, bearing interest of 600 gulden annually. After three years, 3'000 gulden annually plus interest on the remaining principal are to be paid. The revenues of the city and the property of its citizens serve as security. The sum also includes older, unpaid debts of the city and the hospital from the years 1628 and 1630.
en.recipient: Bürgermeister und Rat zu St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster, Council and all citizens of the city of Überlingen acknowledge that they owe the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen 600 gulden annual interest on 12,000 gulden. The interest is to be paid on the feast day of Matthäus. Überlingen reserves the right to buy back the capital after three years with a half-year notice period. St. Gallen can also demand the return of the capital after three years, in which case Überlingen is to pay it off in annual installments of 3,000 gulden.
en.sender: Burgomaster, Council and all citizens of the city of Überlingen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Karl August, Graf zu Kirchberg und Weißenhorn, Vizedom und Rat der kurfürstlichen Regierung, answers the letter of 30. August 1648. It concerns the continuation of an arrest against the Augsburg cloth merchant Herrmann den Jüngeren, which the citizens of St. Gallen Schlaprizi, Hochenrüter and Zolli had requested. Since a dispute between Augsburg and the Graf von Closen is pending before the court, the arrest cannot be lifted without a judicial decision. The kurfürstliche Regierung will examine the intercession of the citizens of St. Gallen.
en.sender: Karl August, Graf zu Kirchberg und Weißenhorn, Vizedom und Rat der kurfürstlichen Regierung
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Überlingen confirm the receipt of a letter from St. Gallen to the local ship and trade merchants Esaias and Lauritz Hörlinger. They ask for brief patience, as they cannot yet reply due to evacuation matters and the absence of their lease tenant. They promise to decide after the situation has been clarified and to show neighborly friendliness.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Johann Christoph, Provost of Kreuzlingen, asks the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for support in obtaining 5000 gulden, which his monastery owes for the provisioning of troops as a result of the peace settlement. He says that he has already inquired about loans from the Landrichter of Ulm, the Ammann of Wattwil, and the pastor of Thalberg. He asks for help to avoid the impending executions.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to instruct their messenger N. Locher to reimburse the Winterthur citizen Benedikt Reuchlin four Barentaler, which the latter had sent by letter to his son in Leipzig, but which did not arrive. Reuchlin had requested reimbursement from Locher multiple times, but the latter had refused. Winterthur asks for neighborly help.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landammann and Council of the Land of Glarus to help the citizens and merchants there, who have engaged with Hans Rudolf Elmern, in the collection of their claims. St. Gallen refers to the fact that it has hitherto proceeded towards foreigners according to the principle of reciprocity, and asks for support from the Confederates.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Land of Glarus

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Court of Hall ask the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen for a Christian fire tax for the rebuilding of their churches and schools, which burned down in 1634. They refer to their dire straits after the war and ask for a contribution at their free discretion in order to be able to finance the bell casting work.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and Court of Hall
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Burgomaster and Council of the city of Esslingen thank St. Gallen for a loan of 300 ducats. They ask for a further loan of 2000 gulden, as they would have to pay the fourth million for the Swedish military satisfaction in cash and their citizenry had been impoverished by the Thirty Years' War and fires. They assure the repayment with interest.
en.sender: The Burgomaster and Council of the city of Esslingen
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of the city of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to compel the heirs of the deceased citizen of St. Gallen, Caspar, to pay their citizen Heinrich Kaiser, a joiner, the owed sum of 248 pounds including annual interest. Kaiser has asserted the claim multiple times without success and asks for support, as he urgently needs the payment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen respond to a claim by the Winterthur citizen Jeremias Büchli against the St. Gallen messenger Tobias Lohr. Lohr denies having received a sealed letter with money, as such letters may only be handed to messengers upon special recommendation. He offers to replace the damage if Büchli can prove that the house servant had recommended the letter with a note regarding the money content. Otherwise, Lohr relies on the customary messenger's right.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Winterthur

en.regest: Augsburg informs St. Gallen about the evacuation of the city by Swedish troops and the return of the keys. Since Augsburg still owes a high remaining sum for the Swedish satisfaction payments and the coffers are empty, it asks St. Gallen for a loan of at least 10.000 Reichsthaler. Augsburg offers interest and securities for this and promises to support St. Gallen in the future.
en.sender: Pflege, Burgomaster and Council of the Imperial City Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Stadtammann and Council of Rheineck ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to send them light and heavy weights, from one quintl to ten pounds, with the St. Gallen town standard, for the upcoming inspection of all weights in their city. They promise to return the weights after use and to pay for their cost.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Karl Ludwig, Pfalzgraf bei Rhein und Kurfürst, informs the Evangelical Confederates that, in accordance with the Peace of Westphalia and the imperial restitution commission, he has returned to his Palatine lands and to Heidelberg. He recalls the good neighborhood and asks for the continuation of the friendly relations.
en.sender: Karl Ludwig, Pfalzgraf bei Rhein und Kurfürst
en.recipient: Evangelische Eidgenossen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Augsburg respond to the request for a loan of ten thousand Reichsthaler. They justify their refusal with the exhaustion of the city treasury due to high expenditures and the poor economic situation. In addition, such loans must be submitted to the higher authority, the Great Councils. They offer to assist St. Gallen in other matters.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the city of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the letter of 12 October, in which they were asked for a credit of 2000 gulden for the fourth million of the Swedish satisfaction. They refer to the low revenues and high expenditures of the city as well as to the exhausted finances and ask for understanding that they cannot comply with the request. However, they declare themselves ready for other services.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Ysen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that Elector Karl Ludwig von der Pfalz asks the Evangelical Confederation for support in the restoration of his Palatine lands and wishes to continue the existing correspondence. They forward the Elector's letter and request the opinion of the St. Gallen.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Nürnberg ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to seriously urge their citizen Bernhard Schapfer the Younger to settle the outstanding debt of 38 ½ gulden plus interest to the Nürnberg innkeeper Hans Bernhard Strübel. Strübel has already turned unsuccessfully to the St. Gallen authority on multiple occasions, as Schapfer does not pay despite promised deadlines.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Wangen inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have summoned the citizens of Wangen who have fallen into debt, Christoph zum Stäg and Martin Kunz, and have inventoried their goods and wares. In order to satisfy the creditors, they invite them to a Diet on 13 November 1650 at 8 o'clock in the morning in the town hall to liquidate the claims. They ask the St. Gallen authorities to inform their citizens and trading partners, including the heirs of Joachim Zollikofer, Sebastian Högger, Hans Heinrich Gebrüder, Caspar Schlumpf, Daniel Zollikofer, Sebastian Zwischer, Hans Heinrich Loher and Zacharias Zünger.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Landammann and Council of the Land of Appenzell der Ausserrhoden to restrain the debtor Anna Schüßin, widow of Hans Zeller, in order to compel her to pay the claim of 30 gulden together with interest and costs to the minor children of Anna Schifflin. The debtor allegedly deposited the money in Appenzell. St. Gallen offers to cover the costs of a dispute over an insult if the debt is settled.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of the Land of Appenzell der Ausserrhoden

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Schultheiss and Council of Baden to support their citizen and merchant Hans Schlumpf the elder in his claim against the deceased citizen of Baden Ambrosius Falch. Schlumpf had obtained a judgment against Falch, which was not settled after the latter's death. The St. Gallen authorities request that Schlumpf be allowed to retain his rights so that he can collect his claim without further costs.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Schultheiss and Council of Baden

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen confirm the receipt of a letter from Kempten dated 14 November, which concerns the citizens Christoph Frießtag and Martin Küßner. The citizen of St. Gallen Zacharias Zümpfer has thereupon submitted a supplication. St. Gallen asks Kempten to treat Zümpfer favorably and to help him with his claim to kinship property, so that he may obtain his right without damage.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to a letter of 14 September 1649. They communicate that the Appenzeller Joseph Brülisauer was accused before them of a theft. The witness Johannes Haldner had withdrawn his testimony, as Brülisauer had not appeared. Since the accusations took place within the jurisdiction of St. Gallen and Brülisauer must answer to them, they had let the proceedings rest until he presents himself personally.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Landammann and Council of Appenzell

en.regest: Statthalter and Council of Appenzell inform Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen that they have imprisoned Joseph Brulysauwer, who is accused of theft in St. Gallen and had pledged there to appear for justification on a coming Wednesday or Thursday. They request the St. Gallen authorities to transmit the corresponding witnesses in writing, so that they can conduct the proceedings against Brulysauwer and assign him the deserved punishment.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Veltlin ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to assist the citizens of St. Gallen Bartholomäus and David Studer in collecting a debt from the heirs of Michael Schanzens in Thalwil. The debt has been due since October of the previous year, and a court day in May has not yet brought satisfaction. The creditors refer to a house that has not yet been sold and ask for prompt resolution.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen request Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg to permit their citizen Johannes Klapriß to manage the properties in the city of Ravensburg that fell to him and his co-heirs from Jörg Bernhard Eberle himself. Klapriß has committed himself to causing no harm to anyone and to keeping quiet. The St. Gallen ask for a favorable answer.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg

en.regest: The Schultheiss and Council of Baden reply to the request for assistance in the payment of the St. Gallen citizen Hans Schlumpf. They state that the creditors of the deceased Halben Huet are content with the available means. They ask St. Gallen to instruct Schlumpf to satisfy the creditors equally. Otherwise, they will proceed to stricter legal protection to secure the claims of the relatives in the amount of 5000 gulden against the demands of foreign creditors.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Pflegere, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg thank St. Gallen for the special honour shown to their citizen David Erhardt. They ask again for a loan, now in the amount of 3000 Reichstaler, since St. Gallen had not responded to a previous request for 10 000 Reichstaler. They promise repayment under usual conditions and wish a happy new year.
en.sender: Pflegere, Burgomaster and Council of Augsburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Confederates Burgomaster and Council of Zürich to help their citizen Heinrich Hiller jun. in ecclesiastical jurisdiction, so that he may obtain his arrears. They refer to the attached document, according to which he is to claim a sum of money from Felix Burkhardt, councillor and town bailiff of Zürich. Hiller has proceeded rightly, as he does not deny the debt, but refers to the Herren Tübler, who allegedly still have claims against his father. Hiller disputes this and asks for support.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of Zürich

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Schaffhausen ask Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to help their citizens Christoph and Heinrich Ziegler in the execution of an arrest. The Ziegler have a claim against the Venetian merchants Otti arising from bills of exchange. Since the Otti do not pay, the Ziegler have had a share of the bankruptcy estate of Lorenz Zillis in St. Gallen arrested. The Ziegler send their servant Philipp Adam Kloeber to St. Gallen to settle the matter. Schaffhausen asks for support so that the Ziegler may receive the arrested property.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Ravensburg confirm the receipt of a letter dated 16 December 1629. They grant the St. Gallen citizen Johann Schlieren, who legitimizes himself with powers of attorney from his co-heirs, the status of resident (Hintersasse) in their city for one year, so that he can manage the property inherited from his deceased uncle Burkhard Wüster and collect debts. Schlieren must refrain from trade.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of the Imperial City of Ravensburg
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: The Masters and Council of the Imperial City of Colmar request the Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to examine under oath Anna Reichin, widow of the Wangen draper Hans Jakob Gottlieb, who is detained in Colmar. She is to state whether and how much money she had deposited with Anna Reichin, widow of a carpenter in St. Gallen, and whether she had taken it with her. Colmar requests confirmation of the statement in order to release the prisoner.
en.sender: The Masters and Council of the Imperial City of Colmar
en.recipient: The Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen ask the Glarus authorities to treat their citizens, who have an interest in the bankruptcy estate of the former Glarus countryman Rudolf Elmenreich, equally within the framework of counter-rights and to admit them to pro-rata payment. They refer to the mutual equal treatment in bankruptcies and inform about the insolvency of the St. Gallen butcher Othmar Rietmann, whose debts exceed the available means.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council, Landammann and Council of the Land of Glarus

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen reply to the letter of 24 January, in which Colmar had requested the sworn examination of Anna Kraessin, widow of a carpenter. They report that they had not found any person of this name in the city or in the territory. The Prefect also had not been able to provide any information. They ask for forgiveness that they cannot be of further assistance.
en.sender: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen
en.recipient: Master and Council of the Imperial City of Colmar

en.regest: The Hauptschultheissen, Stadtmeister and subjects of the Oberamt Kreuznach thank the Burgomaster, Council and Vorsteher of St. Gallen for a considerable tax which they have received in their distress. They assure that the funds are used according to the King's instructions, and ask for prayer for protection against enemy violence and for peace.
en.sender: Hauptschultheissen, Stadtmeister and subjects of the Oberamt Kreuznach
en.recipient: Burgomaster, Council and Vorsteher of St. Gallen

en.regest: Burgomaster and Council of Kempten request Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen to support the widow of the deceased Kempten Council member Tobias Schwizer in a debt matter. They ask that the citizens of St. Gallen, Christoph and Tobias Stauder, be instructed to accept the widow's offer and settle the claim.
en.recipient: Burgomaster and Council of St. Gallen

en.regest: Magdalena Schücher, widow of the late Tobias Schücher, asks the addressees to intervene with the Magistracy of St. Gallen. The family Stauder claims 500 florins from the weaving debts of her late husband. Her son-in-law Andreas Haunstein had offered 450 florins (100 in cash, 100 annually without interest), but the Stauder demanded 475 florins with interest and a shorter term. She asks that the Stauder be persuaded to accept the offer and to avoid further costs.
en.recipient: E. V. F. E. W.
